Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Account Overview Report in Recruit CRM gives a complete overview/pictorial representation of the candidate pipeline and deals pipeline for the entire account. It is designed to help you quickly understand how candidates and deals are distributed across different stages. You can use this feature when: You need a quick, visual overview of candidate distribution across hiring stages. You want to see how many deals sit in each stage of your deals pipeline by volume. You want to understand the distribution of deals based on the deal value of deals in different stages. Note: This report is available to Account Owners, Admins, and Users with relevant custom role permissions on the Business plan and above. Step-by-step instructions In Recruit CRM, the Account Overview Report has 3 segments: Total Candidate Pipeline graph. Total Deals by Volume graph. Total Deals by Value graph. To view the Account Overview report: 1. Click on the Reports section and select the Account Overview Report : 2. The "Total Candidate Pipeline" graph shows the percentage distribution of the candidates across various hiring stages: 3. The "Total Deal by Volume" graph shows the percentage of deals in different deal stages: 4. The "Total Deals by Value" graph shows the distribution of deals based on the deal value of deals in different stages: You can also choose to export the graphs generated. On any of the graphs, locate the three lines icon at the top right of the graph to open the export options. Choose your preferred export option to download or export the graph. Troubleshooting Problem: The Account Overview Report is not visible in the Reports section. Likely cause: The user role is not Account Owner, Admin, or Users with relevant custom role permissions What to check: Confirm your role in Recruit CRM. Resolution path: Only Account Owners and Admins, and Users with relevant custom role permissions can access the Account Overview Report. If needed, have the Account Owner update your role. 🤔FAQs Does the Account Overview Report show data for individual users only? No. The Account Overview Report provides an overview for the entire account, not just for a single user. Conclusion: The Account Overview Report in Recruit CRM gives account owners and admins a clear, visual summary of candidate and deal pipelines across the entire account. Use it regularly to monitor stage distribution, identify bottlenecks, and export visual insights for your team or stakeholders. s: You can customize the company's default industry field to suit your needs!
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

Delete a custom industry option

b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM offers a feature that allows users to customize default industry fields for companies. You have the flexibility to add as many custom industries as you'd like to align with your diverse work portfolio! You can also delete custom industry options you no longer need, while keeping the built-in default options intact. You can use this feature when: You need industry options that are not available in the default Company Industry list. You work across niche or specialized markets and want the industry field to reflect them. You need to clean up or remove outdated custom industry options. Adding a custom industry Simply follow these steps to create custom industries for companies: While creating a new company or editing an existing one in Recruit CRM, you'll have the option to fill in the company's industry field. Locate the Company Industry field, and you can choose from a default list of industries or create your own custom industry. If the industry you need is not in the default list, type the desired industry name into the search box of the Company Industry field. Click the Add button that appears to create this as a new custom industry option. Once added, you will find it from the User Added section within the Company Industry field. After selecting the custom industry, click the Submit button to save the company with that custom industry selected. You can also add a new custom industry directly from the "Company Industry" field on the company main profile page: Delete a custom industry option Go to a company record and edit the company. Click on the Company Industry drop-down field to view all available options, including any you have added. Find the custom industry option you want to remove. Click the small trash bin icon next to that custom industry option to delete it. After clicking on it, you'll receive a confirmation message indicating that you've successfully deleted the custom industry option: You can also delete the custom company industry from the company details page: Please note that the default industry options cannot be deleted. Troubleshooting Problem: Cannot find a newly added custom industry Likely cause: The custom industry was not saved or not selected from the User Added section. What to check: Open the Company Industry field and look under the User Added section. Confirm that you clicked the Add button after typing the new industry name. Resolution: If the custom industry is not listed, type the name again and click the Add button, then select it from the User Added section and save the company. Problem: Unable to delete an industry option Likely cause: You are trying to delete a default industry option. What to check: Look for the trash bin icon next to the industry option. Default industry options do not show a trash bin icon and cannot be removed. Resolution: Only delete options that display the trash bin icon. If you do not see the icon, the option is a default industry and cannot be deleted FAQs Can I add more than one custom industry? Yes. You can add as many custom industries as you would like to align with your diverse work portfolio. Conclusion: Custom company industries in Recruit CRM give you the flexibility to match the Company Industry field to your real markets and internal terminology. By adding, selecting, and deleting custom options directly from the Company Industry field, you can keep your data accurate, relevant, and easy for your team to work with. t: Adding a data add-on to your subscription
s: This article will guide you on buying a data add-on for your account to store additional records.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Step-by-step instructions to add the Data Add-On
Troubleshooting
FAQs
Q1: What is an additional records limit in Recruit CRM?
Q2: Do I need to buy an extra user to increase storage?
Q3: How is the payment for the add-on calculated?
Q4: Where do I go to manage or add more additional records limits?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? An Additional Records Limit is a monthly add-on that increases your Recruit CRM account's storage capacity without requiring you to purchase an additional user. Each add-on expands your account limit by 10,000 candidates, 10,000 contacts, and 10,000 company records , and the additional capacity is available across the entire account. Use this feature when: You've reached, or are close to reaching, your account's maximum record limit. You want to increase your storage capacity without paying for an additional user. You need to expand your account's record limit for the entire team. Please note: Additional Records Limits are applied at the account level , not per user. For example, purchasing one add-on increases your account capacity by 10,000 candidates, 10,000 contacts, and 10,000 company records for everyone using the account. Step-by-step instructions to add the Data Add-On Follow these steps to purchase an additional records limit for your account: Go to Admin Settings in your Recruit CRM account and under Account Management , click Plans and Billing . ​ Click Edit Current Plan . ​ Scroll down to the Additional Records Limit section. Now, select the number of add-ons you want to purchase. ​ Once you've chosen this, you can click on the ' Review Order ' button on the right side of the screen, under the 'Bill Summary', to proceed with the payment. ​ On the order review page, select the required checkbox and click Update Plan and Pay to complete your purchase. The prorated amount is calculated automatically based on your Recruit CRM subscription renewal date. Once the payment is complete, the additional records limit is applied immediately to your account. Troubleshooting Problem: Applicants cannot submit job applications, or new candidates and records cannot be added through the Recruit CRM Chrome Extension because a limit reached error is displayed. Likely cause: Your account has reached its maximum records limit for candidates, contacts, or companies. What to check: Go to Admin Settings → Account and review your account's current records usage to confirm whether the record limit has been exhausted. Resolution: Purchase an Additional Records Limit add-on to increase your account's capacity. Once the add-on is applied, applicants will be able to submit new applications again, and records can be added through the Recruit CRM Chrome Extension and other record creation methods without encountering the limit reached error. FAQs Q1: What is an additional records limit in Recruit CRM? An additional records limit is a monthly data add-on that increases your account’s storage by 10,000 candidates, 10,000 contacts, and 10,000 company records per add-on. Q2: Do I need to buy an extra user to increase storage? No. The add-on applies at the account level, not per user, so your whole team benefits from the extra capacity without anyone purchasing an additional seat. Q3: How is the payment for the add-on calculated? When you click Update Plan and Pay , Recruit CRM automatically calculates a prorated amount based on when your current subscription renews. Q4: Where do I go to manage or add more additional records limits? Go to Admin settings , then open Plans and Billing under Account Management , click the green button to edit your current plan, and scroll to the Additional records limit box Conclusion: Purchasing a data add-on (additional records limit) in Recruit CRM is a simple way to expand your account’s capacity for candidates, contacts, and companies without adding extra users. If you need more help with billing or plan changes, contact Recruit CRM support channel for further assistance. This data is useful for improving your campaigns and understanding your audience better. 🖥️ What is Google Tag Manager? t: Adding and Managing Call logs (New UI)
s: This article will help you understand how you can add call logs in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Step-by-Step Instructions
Method 1: Add a Call Log from the Record
Method 2: Add a Call Log from the Global Add Menu
Method 3: Add a Call Log on Mobile
Accessing and Reviewing Call Logs
Viewing Call Logs on a Record
Searching and Filtering Call Logs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Call logs in Recruit CRM help you record and manage phone conversations directly against candidate, contact, or company records. They create a searchable and organized history of call activity, making it easier to track conversations, review outcomes, and collaborate with your team. Each call log can include: • Notes summarizing the conversation • Call start time and duration • Collaborators who participated in the call • An associated record • A contact number • A customizable call type to match your workflow This feature is especially useful when you want to: • Record important candidate or contact conversations • Build a searchable call history on records • Categorize calls and track outcomes over time • Add and manage call logs while working on mobile devices Step-by-Step Instructions Method 1: Add a Call Log from the Record Open the Candidate, Contact, or Company record you want to log the call against. In the right-hand activity panel, click the call log icon to open the call log form. ​ Fill in the Add Call Log form. The Related to field will be auto-filled based on the record you are on. You can also add: Call notes: Use this field to capture the key points and outcomes of the conversation. Collaborators: Add any teammates who were part of the call. Call duration and start time: Record how long the call lasted and when it began. Related to: If the call log is linked to a record, you can add that record in the Related to field. Contact number: This field is optional. Select a number from standard or custom phone fields stored on the record, or enter a new number manually. ​ 4. Click the green Submit button to save the call log. It will appear in the record's activity section immediately. Tip: Always fill in Call Notes to capture the highlights of the conversation. This makes the log useful for future follow-ups and keeps your team aligned. Method 2: Add a Call Log from the Global Add Menu Click the blue plus (+) button at the top right of any screen in Recruit CRM. Select Call Log from the activity options. A form will appear on the right side of the screen. In the Related to field, search for and select the Candidate, Contact, or Company the call log should be attached to. This field is not auto-filled when using this method, so selecting the correct record is essential. Fill in all remaining details such as call notes, collaborators, call duration, start time, and contact number. Click Submit to save the call log. 📌 Please Note : If you forget to fill in the Related to field, the call log may not appear where you expect it. Always verify the correct record is selected before submitting. Method 3: Add a Call Log on Mobile Open the Recruit CRM mobile app and navigate to the Candidate, Contact, or Company record you want to log the call against. Tap the floater button at the bottom right corner of the profile page. Fill in the call log details in the form that appears. Tap Save to add the call log to the record. Accessing and Reviewing Call Logs Viewing Call Logs on a Record Open the record and go to the Activities tab and select the Notes and Calls section to see all call logs. Each call log card displays the contact number associated with the call, making it easier to identify the caller at a glance without opening the log. Click View More of any call log to expand it for a detailed view. The date and time when the call log is added appear at the bottom right of the call log card beside the clock icon. Searching and Filtering Call Logs To expand the full activity view, click and move the bar to adjust the size of the section as needed. Use the search bar to find specific call logs by keyword. Use the filter options to narrow results by activity type, call type, date range, or collaborator, giving you a focused view of the call history you need. Accessing the Call Logs List View In addition to viewing call logs from individual records, you can access a centralized list of call logs from different areas of Recruit CRM. ​ From Admin Settings Go to Admin Settings and open Phone Calling and SMS Settings . Click Account Credits and Usage . Scroll down to the Call Logs list to view the detailed list of call logs. Use the available options to choose which call logs you want to view: All Incoming Outgoing Missed You can also filter call logs by: To Number – Filter calls made to a specific number. From Number – Filter calls made from a specific number. User – View call logs associated with a specific user. Call Type – Filter calls based on their call type. Call Outcome – Filter calls based on their outcome. Related To – Filter call logs associated with a specific Candidate, Contact, or Company . ​ From the Mailbox Open the Mailbox from the left navigation menu. Scroll down and select Call Logs to open the detailed call logs list. Use the available options to choose which call logs you want to view: All Incoming Outgoing Missed You can further filter the call logs by: To Number – Filter calls made to a specific number. From Number – Filter calls made from a specific number. User – View call logs associated with a specific user. Call Type – Filter calls based on their call type. Call Outcome – Filter calls based on their outcome. Related To – Filter call logs associated with a specific Candidate, Contact, or Company . ​ How to delete call logs? Please note: System-generated call logs associated with phone calling credits cannot be deleted by any user. This restriction helps maintain accurate Phone Calling credit usage and prevents discrepancies in credit reporting. Manually created call logs can still be deleted by users such as Account Owners, Admins, and users on custom roles with the appropriate permissions to delete call logs. To delete manually added call logs, click on the 3 dots icon on the call log and select the 'Delete' option. Click on 'Yes' in the delete call log pop-up. Customizing Call Types You can create custom call types to tag each call log with a specific category, such as Intro Call, Follow-up, or Client Update. This makes it easier to filter and report on call activity across your team. Go to Admin Settings and click Call Type Customization under CRM Process Customization. Click Customize and then Add New Status to create a new call type. Enter a name of up to 50 characters and click Save Status. The new call type will appear in the Call Type dropdown when adding call logs. Note: You can add up to 100 custom types for Call Logs, Notes, and Meetings. Troubleshooting Problem: The Related to field is empty when creating a call log. Likely cause: You are using the global Add method to add the call log, which does not auto-fill this field. ​ ​ What to check: Verify that you opened the call log from the global Add icon instead of from within a record. ​ ​ Resolution path: Manually select the correct candidate, contact, or company in the Related to field before submitting. Problem: You cannot see certain call logs on a record. Likely cause: Filters are applied in the activity panel. ​ ​ What to check: Review the activity filters to ensure Call or All activities are selected. ​ ​ Resolution path: Clear or update filters to reveal all visible call logs. FAQs Where do call logs appear after I create them? Call logs appear in the activity section of the related candidate, contact, or company record, under the Notes and Call section. ​ Can I log calls that were not made through Recruit CRM? Yes. You can manually create call logs for any phone conversation by entering notes, duration, and other details, even if the call took place outside Recruit CRM. ​ Can I categorize my call logs? Yes. You can use call types to categorize your call logs and make them easier to filter and review. Conclusion: By using call logs in Recruit CRM, you can maintain a complete, structured history of all phone interactions with candidates, contacts, and companies. s: This article will help you give feedback on candidate lists sent directly to you through Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

Conclusion
b: Note: This article is designed for Hiring Managers & Executives that receive candidates from recruiters using Recruit CRM. What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows hiring managers and clients to review candidates submitted by recruiters through an Online Candidate List link. You can view candidate profiles, update hiring stages (where permitted), and leave remarks or interview feedback, all of which are instantly shared with your recruiter. This feature is useful when you want to: Review candidates submitted for a job. Update a candidate's hiring stage. Leave interview feedback or remarks for candidates. Share feedback directly with your recruiter. Review candidates and submit feedback Open the email sent by your recruiter and click the candidate list link. The link opens the list of candidates submitted for the job. You can review candidates in either List View or Kanban View . To provide feedback, update the candidate's Hiring Stage and add your remarks. You can also leave remarks without changing the hiring stage. In List View , click the candidate's Hiring Stage to change the stage and add your remarks. In Kanban View , open the candidate's profile for more details or simply drag and drop the candidate to a new hiring stage and add your feedback. Once submitted, your feedback is immediately available to your recruiter. Please note: If you see "Not Available" in any field, it means that no information has been added for that field. Troubleshooting Problem: I can't update the hiring stage. Likely Cause: The recruiter hasn't enabled client access for that hiring stage. What to Check: Verify whether the required hiring stage is available in the dropdown. Resolution: Contact your recruiter if you need access to additional hiring stages. FAQs 1. Can I leave feedback without changing the hiring stage? Yes. You can add remarks without updating the hiring stage. Conclusion The online candidate link makes it easy to review shortlisted candidates, provide interview feedback, and update hiring stages in one place. Your feedback is instantly shared with your recruiter, helping keep the hiring process moving efficiently. t: Adding Files & Creating Folders (New UI)
s: Add files related to any candidate, job or contact.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to access the Files tab on the Record Profile
Uploading a File
Renaming a File
Creating and Managing Folders
Create a Folder
Rename or Delete a Folder
Attaching a Saved File to a Field
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM provides a dedicated Files section for every Candidate, Contact, Company, and Job record, allowing you to upload, organize, and manage documents directly within the platform. You can create folders, rename files, reuse saved files by attaching them to file-type fields or emails, and access everything without needing to re-upload them from your device. File size limit: Each individual file must be 8 MB or smaller. You can use this feature when: • You need to store candidate, contact, company, or job-related documents in one place. • You want to organize files into folders within a record. • You frequently reuse the same documents in fields or emails and don’t want to re-upload them. How to access the Files tab on the Record Profile Accessing the Files Tab: Every record in Recruit CRM has a Files tab where files can be stored and accessed. To open the Files tab: Open any Candidate, Contact, Company, or Job record. Click the Files tab in the horizontal navigation bar, located below the record's information overview. ​ From here, you can view, download, upload, and organize all files linked to that record. Uploading a File You can add files to a record in two ways: Click the upload area or the Upload button, then select a file from your computer. Drag a file from your desktop and drop it directly into the Files section. Renaming a File You can also rename files stored in the Files section to keep them organized and make them easier to identify. Locate the file you want to rename in the Files Tab. Click the three-dot menu (⋯) next to the file. Select Rename . Enter the new file name and click Save . ​ Creating and Managing Folders Folders help you keep documents organized within a record's Files section, for example, separating resumes from offer letters. Create a Folder Click the Create Folder button on the right side of the Files section. Enter a name for the folder in the pop-up dialog. Click Save. Once the folder is created, you can click into it to upload files directly, or drag and drop files into the folder. Rename or Delete a Folder Click the three-dot menu (⋯) next to any folder to access the Rename or Delete options. Attaching a Saved File to a Field If a record has file-type fields (for example, a Resume field on a Candidate), you can populate those fields directly from the record's Files section, no need to re-upload a file from your computer. This works for Candidates, Contacts, Companies, and Jobs. Steps Click the pencil (edit) icon next to the file-type field you want to fill. Click the dropdown arrow next to the upload button and select Select From Saved Files . A list of files already uploaded to that record will appear. Select the file you want. Click Save. Please Note Clicking a file name opens a preview before you confirm the selection. Only files uploaded to the record you are currently editing appear in the list, keeping the selection clean and secure. You can still choose Upload File from the same dropdown to upload a new file directly from your computer. This feature works in both the Edit form and directly on the file fields visible on the record page. Attaching Saved Files to an Email When composing an email inside Recruit CRM, you can attach files that are already saved on any record, no need to download them to your computer first. Steps In the email composer, click the dropdown arrow next to the Upload From Device button. Select Select From Saved Files . The panel shows up to 15 recently used files for quick access. To find files from a specific record, use the search bar to look up the record name, then click Search. All files linked to that record will appear. Click a file name to preview it before selecting. ​ Click Add Files to add your selections. You can search across multiple records to gather files from different profiles. Once you have selected everything, click Done . The files will be attached to your email. Troubleshooting Problem: I can’t see the Files tab on a record. Likely cause: You may not have scrolled to the right section of the Widgets tab or it is hidden. What to check: Confirm you are on a candidate, contact, company, or job profile and scroll down to the Widgets section and scroll right to locate the Files tab. Also make sure that the Files tab is not hidden within the Customize Widgets option. ​ Resolution path: Adjust your scroll to locate the Files tab. If still missing, check the visibilty of the Files tab by clicking on the 3 dots and going to the Customize Widgets. FAQs What is the maximum file size I can upload? No. The dropdown only shows files uploaded to the specific record you are currently editing. How many recently used files appear in the email attachment panel? Up to 15 recently used files appear by default. Use the search bar to find files from any other record. Can I rename files after uploading them? Yes. Open the Files section of the record, click the three-dot menu (⋯) next to the file, select Rename , enter the new name, and click Save . Conclusion: By using the Files section and Saved Files in Recruit CRM, you can centralize documents, organize them into folders, and quickly reuse them in fields and emails. t: Adding job requisitions on the Hiring Manager Portal
s: Learn how to make job requisitions for your recruitment team!
h: 1. Pending 🟡
2. Approved status ✅
3. Declined status ❌
b: How to make job requisitions on the Hiring Manager Portal? 1. Navigate to your job's list page and click on the blue 'Job Requisition' button. 2. Provide all necessary job details in the respective fields and then proceed by clicking on the 'Save' button to submit your requisition. Different status of your job requisition! 🪜 1. Pending 🟡 After you've submitted your job requisition, it enters the 'Pending' status, indicating that it's awaiting review and processing. Simultaneously, your designated recruiter will be promptly notified via email about the new requisition you've initiated. 2. Approved status ✅ Following approval by your recruiter, your job requisition transitions to the 'Approved' stage, signifying readiness for the subsequent phases of the hiring process. Click on the approved job to access the 'Candidate Pipeline', providing visibility into the candidates being considered, as your recruiters work on filling the position. 3. Declined status ❌ If your job requisition gets declined by your recruitment team, it will be categorized under the 'Rejected' status, and on the 'All Jobs' page, you'll have access to view the remarks provided by your recruiter regarding the decline of that specific job. With this information at hand, you can then refine and enhance your job requisition, ensuring a better chance of approval upon resubmission. You will get an in-app as well as email notification whenever your job requisition undergoes approval or is declined by your assigned recruiter. We hope this helps! FAQs

Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Interested in growing your team in Recruit CRM? t: Adding notes and customizing note type (New UI)
s: Add/writing notes to Candidates, Companies, Jobs and Contacts.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before You Begin:
Step-by-Step Instructions
Add a Note to a Record
Bulk Add Notes to Multiple Candidates
Mention Teammates in a Note
Pin, Edit, and Delete Notes
Associate a Note With Multiple Records
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Notes in Recruit CRM help you log conversations, updates, and activities directly on candidates, companies, jobs, or contacts. You can also use them to keep your team aligned, especially when working across multiple records or collaborating on the same candidates or clients. From the Notes section, you can: • Add notes to individual records or multiple records at once • Mention teammates to notify them via email with a link to the record • Pin important notes so they stay visible at the top • Edit or delete notes as information changes • Associate a single note with multiple records • Customize note types for better organization and reporting • Search and filter notes to quickly find relevant information This is especially useful when you want to standardize note tracking, maintain clear communication across your team, and easily review important updates whenever needed. Before You Begin: Notes can be added to Candidate, Contact, Company, Job, and Deal records. Bulk note actions are available from the Candidates and Contacts list page. Customizing note types is restricted to users with access to the Admin Settings on the Business plan and above, or users with the Admin role on the Pro plan. The total of customised note types, call types, and meeting types which can be created is 30. Step-by-Step Instructions Add a Note to a Record Open the specific record you want to add a note to. You can navigate to Candidates , Companies , Contacts , Jobs , or Deals from the main navigation. On the record's profile/details page, click the Note icon on the right-hand side Activities panel. It is the first icon in the activity section. Type your note in the text area. Optionally, select a note type from the Select Note Type dropdown to categorize the note. Click Add to save. The note will be attached to that record immediately. Bulk Add Notes to Multiple Candidates If you need to log the same note for several candidates or contacts at once, use the bulk note action from the list page. Go to the Candidates or Contacts list page. Select the records you want to add the note to by checking the box next to each name. Click Add Note from the action bar that appears at the top of the list. Enter the note text and click Add Note . The same note will be added to all selected record profiles. 📌 Note: Bulk adding a note applies the same text and note type to every selected record. It is best suited for common updates, not personalized feedback. Mention Teammates in a Note You can notify a teammate about a record directly from the Notes section. This is useful when you need someone to review a profile or take action on a specific record. While typing a note, enter the @ symbol followed by your teammate's name. Select the teammate from the suggestions dropdown that appears. When you save the note, the teammate receives an email notification containing a direct link to that record. ​ Pin, Edit, and Delete Notes Keep the most important notes visible and up to date using the options available on each saved note. To pin a note , click the three-dot menu, then select Pin. The note will move to the top of the Notes section so it is always visible first. To edit a note , click on the three-dot menu, then select Edit. Make your changes and save. To delete a note , open the three-dot menu, then select Delete. Deleting a note that is associated with multiple records will remove it from all of those records. ⚠️ Please note: Pinned notes are visible to all users who have access to that record. Avoid including sensitive or confidential information in pinned notes unless it is appropriate for all viewers. Associate a Note With Multiple Records A single note can be linked to more than one record at the same time. This is useful when a conversation or update is relevant across a candidate or contact profile, a job, and a company simultaneously. While adding a note, click Create Associations below the note text area. Search for and select the additional records you want to link to this note. Save the note. It will now appear on every record you associated it with. Access and Filter Existing Notes All notes saved on a record are available in the Activities section, where you can search and filter them to quickly find specific entries. Open the record → go to the Activities section on the right to view all the entries. Use the search bar to find notes using keywords OR Apply filters from the Activities section to narrow results by: • Owner • Type • Created Date • Association This makes it easier to locate the most relevant notes without scrolling through all activities. Customize Note Types Note types allow you to tag each note with a category such as Interview Feedback, Client Call, or Internal Review. This makes it easier to filter, report on, and organize notes across your team. 🔒 Access required: Only users with access to the CRM Process Customization in the Admin Settings on the Business plan and above, or users with the Admin role on the Pro plan, can create and edit custom note types, or set default note types. To add a custom note type, follow these steps: Go to Admin Settings and click Note Type Customization under CRM Process Customization. Click the Customize button at the top of the page. Click Add New Status and enter a name for the note type. Names can be up to 50 characters long. To make this the default note type that is pre-selected each time a new note is added, check the box next to the new type. Click Save Status to finalize the new note type. It will immediately appear in the Select Note Type dropdown when adding notes. 📌 Note: The number of available call types, meeting types, and note types is 100. Troubleshooting Problem: You cannot create a new note type. Likely cause: You have reached the limit of 30 combined note types, call types, and meeting types. What to check: Review existing note, call, and meeting types in the customization settings. Resolution path: Remove or consolidate unused types to free up space, then try adding the new note type again. FAQs Can I add notes to all record types in Recruit CRM? Yes. You can add notes to Candidate, Contact, Company, Job, and Deal records. You can also associate a single note with multiple related records so it appears across all of them. Will my teammates be notified when I mention them in a note? Yes. When you type @ followed by a teammate's name and select them from the suggestions dropdown, they receive an email notification with a direct link to that record. Can I change or delete a note after it has been saved? Yes. Hover over the note and use the three-dot menu to edit its content or delete it. Keep in mind that deleting a note that is associated with multiple records will remove it from all of those records. What is the difference between adding a note and associating a note? Adding a note creates a new entry on a specific record. Associating a note links that same note to additional records so it appears on all of them. You do not need to create separate notes for each record when the information is the same. Conclusion: Using notes effectively in Recruit CRM helps you centralize information, keep your team aligned, and maintain a clear history of every interaction across records. By adding, associating, pinning, and customizing notes, and by taking advantage of filters and bulk actions, you can manage your workflows more efficiently and find key information whenever you need it. If you have questions about adding notes or customizing note types, use the chat icon at the bottom right of the screen to reach the support team. Related Articles How to Add Notes and Customize Note Types in Recruit CRM Assigning Owners To Records (New UI) Bulk Updating Records (New UI) How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM (New UI) Adding Files & Creating Folders (New UI)

t: Adding records in Recruit CRM
s: Adding records in Recruit CRM
h: What this feature does & when to use it?
Before you begin:
Step-by-step instructions
Method 1 – Global Add icon
Method 2 – List View
Method 3 – Chrome Extension
Link Companies When Adding Jobs
Standardized Location Fields
b: What this feature does & when to use it? This feature allows you to quickly add and manage records in Recruit CRM using multiple options, including the Global Add menu, List view, or Chrome Extension. It also helps link companies while creating jobs, and makes adding location details easier with address suggestions and auto-fill. The method for adding candidates, companies, contacts & jobs is the same. You can use this when you want to manually add the records in RecruitCRM. Before you begin: Please Note: When adding a job, you must associate it with a company using the Company Name field. Your ability to add or edit records may depend on your role and permissions set by your Recruit CRM admin. The Chrome extension is an additional option and requires separate installation and setup. Step-by-step instructions Method 1 – Global Add icon 1. Click on the Plus (Global Add) button at the top right of your Recruit CRM window to open the global add menu. 2. From the dropdown menu, select Company . Here we have taken the example of a company. Fill in the company form with all relevant details, then click Submit to add the new company record. Method 2 – List View 1. Click on the Companies tab on the left side of the screen to open the companies list view. 2. In the Companies list view, click on the Add Company button. 3. Fill in the details related to the company and, if applicable, its primary contact . Click Submit to save the new company record. Method 3 – Chrome Extension Another method for adding candidates, contacts, or companies is by using the Recruit CRM Chrome extension . Install and open the Chrome extension, then follow the prompts to capture and add records directly from your browser. For detailed instructions, refer to the dedicated help article linked within Recruit CRM. Recruit CRM Chrome Extension Link Companies When Adding Jobs When adding a job , the Company Name field is mandatory because every job must be associated with a company. The company dropdown does not show options immediately. Start typing the name of the company you previously created; as you type, the dropdown will display possible matches or allow you to create a new company if it does not already exist. Standardized Location Fields 1. Added a Postal Code field: We have added a ' Postal Code ' field alongside the Full Address, Locality, City, State, and Country fields. 2. Auto Suggestions: You can also search using a Street Address, City, State, or Postal Code for auto-suggestions while adding the candidate, contact, company and job. 3. Auto-fill via Postal Code: When a Postal Code is entered, the system automatically fills in the City, State, and Country using geo-coding services and can edit any location field if needed Note: The address suggestion feature is available on external pages and on the Chrome Extension. Troubleshooting Problem: The company you expect does not appear in the dropdown when adding a job Likely cause: The company has not been created yet or the name is being typed differently. What to check: Check the spelling and try typing more characters of the company name. Resolution path: If no match appears, use the option offered in the dropdown to create a new company record, then associate it with the job. Conclusion: By using the global add menu, the List view, or the Chrome extension, you can quickly add records manually in Recruit CRM. Related Articles Recruit CRM Chrome Extension Adding Candidates in Recruit CRM Default Fields in Recruit CRM Bulk Importing Jobs into Recruit CRM Adding records in Recruit CRM (New UI)

t: Adding Work & Education History in Candidate Profiles
s: This article will guide you on how to add work and education details to your candidate profiles.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
How to Add Work & Education History in Candidate Profiles 📗
How to View Saved Work and Education History in the Candidate Profile? 👀
How to Add Additional Work Experience or Education Entries? 📚
How to Delete Work or Education History Entries? ❌
Troubleshooting
Problem: Work or education details are not visible in the candidate profile
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The Work and Education History feature lets you store candidates' work or education details as separate categories in their profiles. You can easily add work and education history while adding a candidate by scrolling down the Add Candidate form. You can use this when: You are adding a new candidate and want to capture their work and education history immediately. You want to view all saved work and education details in a single place in the candidate profile. You need to add additional work experience or education entries to an existing candidate. You want to clean up a profile by deleting outdated or incorrect work or education records. Before you begin Please note: You should have access to add and edit candidate records in your account. Have the candidate’s work experience and education details ready (job titles, companies, dates, institutions, degrees, etc.). Remember that work and education details are stored as separate categories under the Work and Education History feature. How to Add Work & Education History in Candidate Profiles 📗 1. Click on the Global Add plus icon in the top-right corner of the screen. This opens the main menu to create a new record. 2. From the dropdown menu, select Candidate to open the Add Candidate form. 3. In the Work History and Education History sections, enter all the required details for the candidate’s work experience and education. These two sections here store candidates' work or education details as separate categories with the Work and Education History feature. 4. When finished, click the Submit button to save the candidate record. How to View Saved Work and Education History in the Candidate Profile? 👀 Once the details are added and the record is saved, open the candidate’s profile. Within the All Details area, locate the Work History and Education History categories. You can easily expand the collapsible section from the categories to move across the fields and view more information by clicking on this. Use the expanded view to review or scroll through all stored fields for each entry. How to Add Additional Work Experience or Education Entries? 📚 1. In the same Details section, click Add Experience to add more work history entries, or Add Education to add additional education records. How to Delete Work or Education History Entries? ❌ 1. Deleting work or education history from a candidate profile is easy. 2. To delete an existing work or education entry, click on the trash icon against the field that you no longer require. 3. A confirmation pop-up menu will appear. 4. When the confirmation pop-up appears, click Sure to confirm deletion and remove the entry from the candidate’s profile. Troubleshooting Problem: Work or education details are not visible in the candidate profile Likely cause: The sections were not filled out or the record was not saved. What to check: Confirm you scrolled down the Add Candidate form, entered the details in Work History and Education History, and clicked Submit. Resolution path: Edit the candidate, add the missing details in the Work History and Education History sections, and save again. Problem: Cannot find the Work History or Education History sections Likely cause: You are not looking under the All Details section or the categories are collapsed. What to check: Open the candidate profile and go to All Details. Check under Details for Work History and Education History and see if they are collapsed. Resolution path: Expand the collapsible section from the categories by clicking on it and then drag or scroll to move across the fields. Conclusion: Managing work and education history in candidate profiles is straightforward: add details while creating the candidate, review and expand them under All Details, and use Add Experience, Add Education, and the trash icon to keep records accurate. I Hope this helps. t: Additional Pages Included in the Recruit CRM UI Revamp
s: This article provides an overview of the pages and pop-ups included in the Recruit CRM UI revamp between July 22, 2026, and August 31, 2026.
h: List of Pages Being Revamped
b: , and August 31, 2026 . The rollout will take place in phases, with different pages being revamped throughout this period. This article provides an overview of each page included in the rollout, each section includes a short GIF highlighting where to access the page or pop-up in the current interface, making it easier to identify what is being revamped. The pages and GIFs in this article highlight selected locations where the updated interface will be available. For instance, the Assign Candidates to Job pop-up is shown below only in a few sections for reference. t: Advanced Analytics - Dashboard Filters and Parameters
s: In this article, we’ll explore how to add and configure filters and parameters in Advanced Analytics.
h: Step-by-step instructions on how to add a filter or parameter
Filter and parameter types
Date picker filters:
Time grouping parameter
Location filters:
ID filter:
Number filter:
Text or category filter:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? If you ever find yourself in a situation where you need to create nearly identical copies of the same dashboard, with just one different variable, there’s a better solution. Instead of creating multiple copies of the same dashboard, you can add filter or parameters. These let users change the data shown on dashboard cards themselves, without needing a separate dashboard for each variation. Step-by-step instructions on how to add a filter or parameter 1. Click the pencil icon to enter the dashboard editing mode. 2. Click the filter icon that appears in the top right to add a filter. 3. Select a filter type 4 . Connect your filter to dashboard cards to one or more dashboard cards on any or all tabs. 5. Save your changes. Advanced Analytics will display the filter only if the filter is connected to a card on the current dashboard tab. Filter and parameter types The type of filter or parameter widget you choose will determine how the widget works, as well as which fields you’ll be able to filter your cards by: Filter widgets: Date picker Location ID Number Text or category Boolean Parameter widgets: Time grouping Date picker filters: When picking a Time filter, Advanced Analytics will prompt you to pick a specific type of date picker widget: Month and Year Quarter and Year Single Date Date Range Relative Date All Options Single Date and Date Range will provide a calendar widget, while the other options all provide slightly different dropdown interfaces for picking values. To get a widget that’s just like the time filter in the query builder, choose All options. Time grouping parameter You can add a time grouping filter to a dashboard to change how charts are grouped by time. For example, you may want to look at the time series charts grouped by month by default, but give people the option to view the results by other groupings: by week, by quarter, and so on. Time grouping parameter widget can only be connected to questions built with the graphical query builder . This widget doesn’t filter data in the charts; the widget just changes the time granularity for any cards that have a datetime field connected to the widget. You can group by: Minute (or minute of hour) Hour (or hour of day) Day (or day of week, month, or year) Week (or week of year) Month (or month of year) Quarter (or quarter of year) Year Location filters: There are four types of Location filters to choose from: City State ZIP or Postal Code Country ID filter: The ID filter provides a simple input box where you can type the ID of a Owner, deal name etc. Number filter: You can choose from: Equal to Not equal to Between Greater than or equal to Less than or equal to Text or category filter: A flexible filter type that will let you create either a dropdown menu or an input box to filter on any category field in your cards. Options include: Is . Select one or more values from a list or search box. Is not . Exclude one or more specific values. Contains . Match values that contain the entered text. Does not contain . Filter out values that contain the entered text. Starts with . Match values that begin with the entered text. Ends with . Match values that end with the entered text. How to connect a filter or parameter widget to dashboard cards? Dashboard widgets apply across all dashboard tabs , though they’ll only be displayed when a tab has cards connected to the widget. Steps to connect a filter to a dashboard card: Click on the dropdown menu of the card you want to filter. Select the field that the widget should filter on. Here we’ve wired up a Date Picker filter to the “Deal Value Closed over Time” card, telling Advanced Analytics that the column to filter on should be the Deals Close Date field: How does auto-connecting filters to cards work? If other cards on your dashboard have the same field as the one you selected, Advanced Analytics will automatically connect the filter to those cards, including relevant cards on other tabs. How can I undo auto-connected filters? Click on the toast notification that appears when Advanced Analytics auto-connects the cards. Manually disconnect the cards by clicking the “X” next to the connected field. Wiring up dashboard filters to text cards You can even wire up filters to text cards, but only if the text card includes a variable . Requiring a filter or parameter: You can tell Advanced Analytics to require a filter so that people must filter the dashboard by a certain column on a card. If you require a filter, you’ll also need to supply a default value for that filter. When should I require a filter? If your dashboard pulls a large amount of data, making it slow or difficult to interpret without filtering. If your dashboard is meant to show data for a specific customer, project, or category instead of all available data. Editing a filter: To edit a filter’s settings: Click the pencil icon to enter dashboard editing mode. Click directly on the filter widget you want to edit. A settings sidebar will open on the right. From this filter editing view, you can wire up dashboard cards to the filter, or use the filter settings sidebar to: Rename a dashboard widget Change widget type Change filter operator Set filter input type Make a multi-select filter Change a filter’s selectable values Set a default filter value Make a filter required Move a filter Remove a filter How to Rename a Filter? In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. Change the label text. Renaming the filter only affects the filter’s display; the label has no effect on filtering logic. How to Change filter or parameter type? In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. In the sidebar, change the Filter or parameter type dropdown. Reconnect the widget to the relevant columns on each card. If you change the type by mistake, click Cancel to exit edit mode without saving. How to Change filter operator? In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. In the sidebar, use the Filter operator dropdown to select the desired operator. How to set filter input type? In dashboard edit mode, click your filter’s widget to open the settings sidebar. From the filter settings sidebar, set How should people filter on this column? : Dropdown list – Displays all possible values with checkboxes (best for predefined lists). Search box – Suggests values as users type (default for columns with <100 unique values). Input box – Allows manual text input (default for columns with >100 unique values). How to make a multi-select filter? In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. From the sidebar, find People can pick and select 'Multiple values'. How to Change a filter’s selectable values? In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. From the sidebar, find How should users filter on this column?. Select 'Dropdown list'.* Click Edit (to the right of 'Dropdown list') to specify where the values should come from: From connected fields From another model or question Custom list If you don't see 'Dropdown list' as an option, go to Filter widgets: Dropdown list for more info. If you don’t see “Dropdown list” as an option, go to Filter widgets: Dropdown list for more info. How to set a default filter value? In dashboard edit mode, Click on the filter you want to make required. A filter sidebar should pop up on the right side. From the sidebar, choose a value from the Default value input field. For example, you might want to set a default filter value like “Active”, so that when people load your dashboard, they only see data for “Active” records (not “Inactive”, “Cancelled”, etc). How to Make a Filter Required? In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. Scroll to the Always require a value toggle and turn it on. Set a default value for the filter. How to Move a Filter? In dashboard edit mode, click the filter widget to open the settings sidebar. Click the Move filter. Select a card, heading, or Top of the page to make it a dashboard-wide filter. Reconnect the widget to the correct columns after moving. How to remove a filter? In dashboard edit mode, click the filter you want to edit. From the sidebar, click Remove . Accidentally removed a filter? Click Cancel in the top-right to exit edit mode without saving changes. How to reorder filters? In dashboard edit mode, click on the grabber handle (six dots) on the right side of a filter widget, then drag the widget to a different position. Linking filters You can also link filters so that a child filter knows to limit its choices based on the activation of a parent filter. Say you have two filters, one to filter by state, the other to filter by city. You can link the city filter to the state filter so that when someone filters by California, the city filter will “know” to only show cities in California. In this case, state is th

t: Advanced analytics with Recruit CRM
s: Create advanced analytics and view account statistics in Recruit CRM, while building interactive dashboards for data visualization.
h: Step-by-step instructions on how to use Advanced Analytics
Creating custom reports and advanced queries✏️
Create your own custom Dashboards to organize your reports

Conclusion:
b: What is Advanced Analytics? Recruit CRM’s Advanced Analytics is an embedded analytics solution designed to help users create custom reports, visualize key metrics through interactive dashboards, and easily share insights with teams and external stakeholders. Advanced Analytics is an Enterprise plan feature which can also be added at an additional cost to the Pro or Business plan subscriptions. Step-by-step instructions on how to use Advanced Analytics Once you've subscribed to the Advanced Analytics add-on for your Recruit CRM account, you can start using the feature immediately from the Reports section . 1. You'll find a section on the Reports page called 'Advanced Analytics.' Clicking on it will take you to the Homepage , where you can find the available collections. Select the respective collection to explore it. You will have a default dashboard in the with some pre-built charts. 2. You can also personalize the default dashboard to fit your needs. Edit it to move tables, rearrange reports across different tabs, adjust visualization options, and more! 3. This, as an interactive dashboard, lets you visualize all the information from various statistics tables and see exactly which records (candidates, contacts, deals, jobs, call logs) the system is referencing. Simply click on the data you want to explore for a detailed view. Creating custom reports and advanced queries✏️ Create your own custom Dashboards to organize your reports To start adding and organizing reports in the same view, you first need to create a dashboard. This will allow you to add your statistics and reports, saving them in a single, interactive view where they can be easily accessed and connected with each other. To create your own new dashboard, click on the "+ New" button located at the top right of your advanced analytics screen and then click on "Dashboard" . Add a name, and a description to the new collection you create, save it anywhere in your library, and then click on "Create". This will allow you to start organizing and saving your reports in any custom dashboard you create. Having explored the default and custom dashboards in Recruit CRM, you should know that you can also create custom reports, tables, and statistics, and organize them into your own personalized dashboards. 1. To create custom queries and reports, click the "+ New" button, then select "Question" to create a specific report. You'll then be able to select the entity you want to generate the report from: 2. Once you've selected an entity for your report, you can choose various aspects and filters related to that entity. For instance, if you select "Candidates," you can specify which candidate fields you want to include in the generated report by clicking on the little arrow next to the title of the entity: 3. You can apply filters to refine your report or analysis, allowing you to obtain results that are precisely tailored to your needs. For instance, you can filter records to include only those with a current salary above a certain amount. 4. You can enhance your report by summarizing the data using various metrics, such as "Average", "Max of", "Min of" or "Sum". Additionally, you have the option to group the summarized results by any field in the records, providing a clearer and more organized view of the information. 5. Once you've made all the necessary customizations to your report, click on "Visualize" to generate the final, customized report. This will apply all your adjustments, allowing you to see the data exactly as you've configured it. Create your own collections to save your reports📘 In the advanced analytics feature, you can create your own collections or libraries to save all the dashboards you build. This makes it easy to access and manage your work, ensuring that all your reports and dashboards are organized and stored in one convenient place. To create your own collection, click on the "+ New" button located at the top right of your advanced analytics screen and then click on "Collection" . Add a name, and a description to the new collection you create, save it anywhere in your library, and then click on "Create". This will allow you to start organizing and saving your dashboards in a custom library. Actions you can perform once the report is generated 🤔 1. After generating the report, you can still make adjustments and refine your search. This includes applying additional filters based on entity fields, summarizing the results using metrics, and grouping data by specific fields. You can also open the search editor to modify your search criteria, refresh the results, and save the updated report to any collection or dashboard you've created. 2. You can also interact with each column or field in the report by clicking on the title. This allows you to apply filters to specific columns, adjust the data distribution, sort the column in ascending or descending order, or even merge it with another column. These options give you greater flexibility in customizing and analyzing your report. 3. You can make your report easier to read by adding extra details and turning it from a plain table into a chart or graph.. For example, instead of keeping the data in a table, you could include variables such as the number of years of experience for each record or who added the record. Then, you can transform this data into a graph (or any other option from the list of visualizations), making it more visually engaging and easier to interpret. To do this, simply click on the "Visualization" button to change how the table is displayed. 4. Once you've made all the changes and customizations to your report, you can save it by adding a title and description. You can store the report in any collection you've created within your account. Additionally, you have the option to add the generated graph or report to a previously created dashboard, or even the default dashboard, where you can arrange it for optimal and personalized visualization. Play with your dashboard 🎉 Now that you've created all the reports you need to track your workflow in a more specific and tailored way, you can save and organize them within your dashboard. The dashboard functionality allows you to further customize your reports and manage all this interactive information within a single, unified view. Explore all the features available in your dashboard to maximize its potential and learn how to efficiently manage and interact with the reports you've built. 1. You can further customize your dashboard by adding headings, creating new sections, including any new reports you've created but haven't added yet, and making a variety of other adjustments. This flexibility allows you to tailor your dashboard precisely to your needs, making it a powerful and personalized tool for managing and visualizing your data. 2. You can arrange and prioritize the reports in your dashboard by simply dragging and dropping them into the desired sections. Additionally, you can change the visualization options of the reports directly from the dashboard. This flexibility allows you to organize and display your reports in a way that best suits your workflow and highlights the most important information. Share your dashboards with anyone 👥 Once your dashboards are fully created and finalized, the next step is to share them with decision-makers or anyone interested in the statistics you've compiled. This ensures that relevant stakeholders have access to the insights and data you've organized. To share the dashboards you've created, click on the "Share Dashboards Link" button. Once you click on the "Share Dashboards Link" button, a new window will open displaying all the dashboards created in your account. To share a specific dashboard, simply turn on the toggle next to its name. This will generate a link that you can share with anyone. When someone clicks on the link, they will be redirected to the specific dashboard you chose to share. You can set your shared dashboard to auto-refresh, ensuring it stays up-to-date without needing to resend it every time the data changes. To enable this, select a refresh timeframe while editing the dashboard, before sharing it with others. Navigate to the Dashboard editing window and click on the small clock icon labeled "Auto-refresh". From there, you can select a timeframe for how often the dashboard will automatically refresh. Once you select a timeframe, a ticking clock icon will appear, indicating when the dashboard will auto-refresh. And that's it! You've successfully built detailed advanced analytics reports and created interactive dashboards using Recruit CRM and the data from your account. Congratulations! 🥳 Conclusion: From viewing the default dashboard to building custom reports, organizing them into personalized dashboards, and sharing auto-refreshing links with stakeholders, Advanced Analytics gives you a complete toolkit for turning your account data into actionable insights. t: Advanced Analytics — MCP (Model Context Protocol)
s: An article on connecting Advanced Analytics to Claude or ChatGPT.
h: Advanced Analytics MCP Server:
Who Is This For?
Before you begin:
Step-by-step instructions on how to connect Advanced Analytics MCP via Claude
Step-by-step instructions on how to connect Advanced Analytics MCP via ChatGPT
Enabling Connectors After Configuration
What This Can Do For You?
Currently Supported Actions on Advanced Analytics through MCP
b: Advanced Analytics MCP Server: Connect your Advanced Analytics data to Claude or ChatGPT and ask questions in plain English, instead of building a report manually every time. It works through either platform (Claude or ChatGPT) . Just connect whichever platform you frequently use, following the matching section later in this article. 📊 Scope of this connection: This connector is scoped only to Advanced Analytics. It's a separate connection from any other Recruit CRM integrations or connectors you may have set up. This feature is only available if your account has an active Advanced Analytics subscription. Advanced Analytics is an Enterprise plan feature, and can also be added at an additional cost to the Pro or Business plan subscriptions. Who Is This For? This is intended for Advanced Analytics Users who want to connect their data to an AI assistant like Claude or ChatGPT via MCP (Model Context Protocol). Advanced Analytics itself is Recruit CRM's reporting and dashboard add-on, giving you custom reports, forecasts, and insights built from your recruitment data. Read More About Advanced Analytics Before you begin: Make sure you have: Either Claude (Desktop app or a claude.ai account) or a ChatGPT plan that supports custom connectors. Access to log in to Recruit CRM, this is where authorization takes place for the MCP connection. Step-by-step instructions on how to connect Advanced Analytics MCP via Claude Behind the scenes, Advanced Analytics is built on Metabase, and that's the name you'll see in Claude. You'll use it during setup, and it's what Claude will respond to when you ask about your data. 1. Login into your Recruit CRM account on your default browser, or any browser where you're running your agent. 2. Go to the Advanced Analytics tab (inside the Reports section). This is the session that authorizes the connection later in the setup. Please note: Do not use this connector for general Recruit CRM actions (candidates, jobs, pipeline updates, etc.). This connection is scoped to Advanced Analytics only, and is separate from other Recruit CRM connections. 3. On Claude (Desktop app or claude.ai), go to Customize → Connectors . Click on Browse and search for Metabase, then click "+". ​ Click on 'Connect to Claude'. 4. Enter the server URL: https://analytics.recruitcrm.io/api/metabase-mcp and click ‘Connect’. 5. Since you're already logged into Recruit CRM's Advanced Analytics screen, you'll see an authorization prompt. On the authentication page that opens, click "Authorize" to connect. 6. Return to Claude. The connector should now show as "Connected." You're ready to ask Metabase (Advanced Analytics) questions. Note: If the Metabase connector is not visible as "Connected", please try to quit and restart Claude. Click here to watch a quick tutorial on how to connect Recruit CRM to Advanced Analytics to Claude. Step-by-step instructions on how to connect Advanced Analytics MCP via ChatGPT 1. Login into your Recruit CRM account on your default browser, or any browser where you're running your agent. 2. Go to the Advanced Analytics tab (inside the Reports section). This is the session that authorizes the connection later in the setup. 3. Open ChatGPT Settings, navigate to Security and login, then scroll down to enable Developer mode . Please note: Remote MCP connectors require Developer Mode on ChatGPT. 4. Go to Plugins and click on the "+" icon. 5. Enter the name of the connection such as Advanced Analytics and paste the MCP server URL: https://analytics.recruitcrm.io/api/metabase-mcp under the 'Connection' field. 4. Upload a logo (optional) and select Authentication: OAuth (if not selected by default) 5. Check the 'I understand and want to continue' checkbox and click on the "Create" button. 6. Click ' Sign in with Advanced Analytics ' when prompted to connect MCP to ChatGPT as shown below: 7. Since you're already logged into Recruit CRM's Advanced Analytics screen, you'll see an authorization prompt (not a login page). Click "Authorize" to connect. 8. Return to ChatGPT. The Advanced Analytics connector should now show as "Connected" under Settings → Plugins. You're ready to ask Advanced Analytics questions. Click here to watch a quick tutorial on how to connect Recruit CRM Advanced Analytics to ChatGPT. Enabling Connectors After Configuration You can enable connectors for individual conversations via the "+" button on the lower left of your chat interface, then "Connectors." You'll see your configured connectors with toggles allowing you to enable or disable them per conversation. What This Can Do For You? Once connected, you can ask your AI assistant questions like: "How many candidates did we add last month?" "Which recruiter placed the most candidates this quarter?" "Show me a chart with placements over the last 6 months" "Which companies have the most open jobs right now?" "Build a bar chart comparing placements by recruiter for this year" "Create a dashboard called 'Monthly Overview' with charts for candidates, contacts, and companies added per month" "Add my existing 'Monthly Candidates' chart to a new dashboard called 'Team Weekly Review'" "Update my recruiter performance chart to show this quarter instead of this year" “Top 10 companies by deal value” Currently Supported Actions on Advanced Analytics through MCP Capability What It Does Getting Answers Ask plain-English questions about your candidates, contacts, companies, jobs, deals, placements, and more — get a straight answer, a number, or a quick comparison. Building Charts Turn any question into a visual — trends over time, comparisons, breakdowns by category, top performers. Charts render right inside your chat. Building Dashboards Bundle related charts together into a dashboard so you or your team can check them anytime. Already have charts built? Just ask for them to be gathered into a dashboard rather than starting from scratch. Updating & Fixing Go back and change the time range, the grouping, the look, or the numbers being shown on any existing chart or dashboard — just describe the change. Organizing Your Work Save charts and dashboards into collections so they're easy to find later. Finding Existing Reports Search across your saved charts, dashboards, and reports using keywords or plain language, so you're not rebuilding something that already exists. A Couple of Tips Before You Start: Always refer to it by name. Ask your assistant about "Metabase (For Claude) /Advanced Analytics (For ChatGPT)" specifically, rather than "the connector," "the tool," or "MCP." This makes sure your assistant knows exactly which capability you're pointing it toward, especially if you have other connectors set up too. At the start of every chat , confirm the connector is active and get a quick view of what's available: "Are you connected to Metabase/Advanced Analytics?" "What tables can you see?" Since each new chat starts fresh, this only takes a moment and helps your assistant answer questions better. Ask it to check with you first. For anything unclear, a metric definition, a grouping, which fields to use, tell your assistant not to assume and finalize on its own. Ask it to share its suggestions and any clarifying questions before building the chart or query, so you can confirm the logic first. Be specific about formulas and definitions. If a metric could be calculated in more than one way (e.g., "placements," "time-to-fill," "active candidates"), tell your assistant which fields and logic to use, or ask it to show you the options before building anything. Don't assume it'll guess your definition right. Permissions & Security: Access through this connector is exactly the same as your own access in Advanced Analytics — nothing more, nothing less. If your role restricts you from certain reports or data in Advanced Analytics, the AI assistant you connect (Claude or ChatGPT) will be restricted from that same data. Data Privacy — Please Read Carefully ⚠️ What gets shared when you use this connection When you ask a question through this connector, the relevant Advanced Analytics data needed to answer it is sent to the AI provider you're using — Anthropic (Claude) or OpenAI (ChatGPT) — for processing. This can include candidate details (names, emails, phone numbers, job history, hiring stage), company and contact records, deal and pipeline data, notes, call logs, and meeting data — depending on what you ask. The AI provider processes this data on their own servers, in line with its own privacy and data retention policies. What to Check Before Using This Connector? Review the relevant provider's data retention and privacy policy directly — retention periods and handling can vary by plan: Claude (Anthropic): anthropic.com/privacy ChatGPT (OpenAI): openai.com/policies/privacy-policy If your organization has data residency, GDPR, or other compliance requirements, confirm that using an AI assistant with live recruitment data is permitted. Use good judgment about what you ask — only que

t: Advertise your jobs through Recruit CRM's Job Marketplace
s: Sponsor your jobs on multiple job boards directly from the system.
h: 1. From inside the Job
2. From the Admin Settings
b: It's always a struggle to find the right job boards to post your jobs and ensure you get the right applications to fill positions quickly. Recruit CRM helps you streamline your job posting process and publish job ads in an easy and targeted way. You can have access to more than 3,000 channels to advertise and market your jobs. Job advertising is available for all accounts with a paid Recruit CRM subscription. If you’re on the free plan (in the beta phase), you won’t be able to post jobs, but you can still explore the job board marketplace. Once you upgrade to a paid plan, you’ll experience a 3-day verification period . ​ Let's see how you can do this! How to advertise a job Only the account owners, admins, and users on custom roles have permission to advertise jobs. 1. From inside the Job 1. Open the job you wish to sponsor and click on the blue button at the top to advertise the job. ​ 2. A pop-up will appear prompting you to fill in the basic information for the job campaign. These fields are: Job Name Search for an existing job in your database Campaign Name Give your job advertising a name for future tracking Job Function Role and responsibilities of the job Location Where the opportunity is situated Industries The job's general industry P.S. The job function, location, and industry tag will only be used to offer you job board recommendations. Jobs that have the status : "on hold", "closed" or "canceled" cannot be advertised. 3. After filling in the details, you'll be redirected to a page where you can manage your existing contracts or buy job campaigns. Click on the second tab to access the Job Board Marketplace. ​ 4. Here you'll have a list with more than 3000 job board options to choose from, including LinkedIn, Monster, Facebook, SEEK and many more! SEEK is available on the Job Board Marketplace! You can now publish your jobs directly to SEEK through the Recruit CRM Marketplace. Simply navigate to the Job Board Marketplace section, select SEEK, and follow the prompts to post your job. You can also sort the options from newest to oldest and apply filters based on the location, industry and job function: 5. After choosing the job board(s) you wish to advertise in, click on "Add to Campaign" to proceed. ​ While advertising you can select all the required job boards in your cart and proceed to post the job i.e, you can post to multiple job boards in a single campaign. You can click on "More Information" to learn more about the job board and the advertising details (cost, campaign processing time, location, duration, etc). 6. On the right side of the screen you'll be able to see your bill summary. Select "Continue to Review Details" to go ahead with the purchase. ​ You can remove the job boards selected by clicking on "Remove from Campaign". 7. On the next page you'll need to fill in all the campaign's posting details like description, working location, organization's details, target group, etc. 8. You'll now be redirected to the check-out page. Before being able to purchase the job board ad, you'll first need to update your billing information on VONQ's Stripe account. ​ You'll only need to update your billing information once. 9. t: AI Assist for Notes and Call Logs in Recruit CRM
s: Discover how AI-Assisted notes and call logs streamline management, providing summaries and key point extraction for enhanced efficiency.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin:
Access AI Assist for notes
Use default prompts on notes
Apply AI-generated content (Replace, Copy, Regenerate)
Use AI Assist for call logs
Create and save a custom prompt
