b: What does this feature do & when to use it? AI Assist for notes and call logs in Recruit CRM uses AI to help you manage and improve written information in notes and call logs across all major entities (candidates, companies, contacts, jobs, and deals). You can use this feature when you want to: Turn long, unstructured notes into short, readable summaries. Extract key points from a conversation or call into bullet points. Improve the clarity and tone of your notes before saving them. Standardize note-taking across your team with shared, reusable prompts. Before you begin: Please note: AI Assist is available while adding notes and call logs on entities such as candidates, companies, contacts, jobs, and deals. You access AI Assist by clicking the AI Assist icon in the note or call log area. You can only delete prompts that you have created yourself. Prompts created by teammates must be deleted by those teammates. Access AI Assist for notes Open the relevant record (candidate, company, contact, job, or deal). Go to the detail view of the record. Start adding a note in the notes area. Click the AI Assist icon within the note editor to open the AI Assist panel. Use default prompts on notes In the AI Assist panel, choose one of the three default prompts : Summarize : to simplify and shorten the text you entered. Extract key points : to turn the main information into bullet points. Improve it : to refine and enhance the existing note. Wait for AI Assist to generate the output based on the selected prompt. Review the generated text. Apply AI-generated content (Replace, Copy, Regenerate) To update your note with the AI version, click Replace to overwrite the original content. To keep your original note but reuse the AI content elsewhere, click Copy to copy the AI output. If you are not satisfied with the AI result, click Regenerate to produce a new version. Once you are happy with the content, save your note as usual. Use AI Assist for call logs Open the record where you are logging a call . Go to the Call Log section. Start adding a call log entry. Click the AI Assist icon or open the AI notes area within the Call Log section. From the dropdown menu, choose one of the prompts: Summarize, Extract key points & Improve it. Review the AI-generated notes and use Replace , Copy , or Regenerate as needed. Save the call log with the improved content. Create and save a custom prompt While in the AI Assist interface (for a note or call log), type your custom instruction in the prompt input field (for example, “Write a summary in thirty words.”). Click the Save Prompt button. ​ When prompted, name your prompt clearly so you can recognize it later. Choose whether to share the prompt with your teammates or keep it private. ​ Confirm to save the prompt. It will appear under the Saved Prompts section. ​ Use saved prompts (including pinned prompts) Open AI Assist from a note or call log. Click on Saved Prompts . Locate the prompt you want to use from the list. If you have pinned prompts, they will appear at the top for quick access. Click the desired prompt to apply it to the current text. Review and then use Replace , Copy , or Regenerate as appropriate. Pin and Unpin Saved Prompts Open the Saved Prompts section in AI Assist. Find the prompt you want to pin. Click the pin icon to pin that prompt for quicker access. To unpin it, click the unpin icon to remove it from the pinned area. Delete your saved prompts Open the Saved Prompts section in AI Assist. Go to the My Prompts tab. Hover over the prompt you want to delete. Click the Delete icon. Confirm deletion if prompted. Remember: You can only delete prompts that you have created. If a prompt was created by a teammate, you will not see the delete option. The teammate who created it must delete it from their end. FAQs Is there a limit to the use of this feature? Yes, the AI-Assist feature has monthly token limits that vary based on your plan. Token usage includes both input and output, and may vary depending on the language and content. Monthly token limits per user: • Free Plan – 50K tokens • Pro Plan – 5 million tokens • Business Plan – 10 million tokens • Enterprise Plan – 20 million tokens These limits apply to the following AI features: • Generate Note Summary • Generate Call Log Summary • Generate Email Template • Generate Email • Generate Email Sequence • Email Reply Suggestion • Generate Candidate Summary • Generate Job Description Note: These token limits currently do not apply to AI Sourcing and AI Boolean Search . Is there any limit to the number of prompts I can save? The limit for prompts that can be saved is 50. How many prompts can be pinned? You can pin up to 50 prompts. What happens if I reach the token limit? If you reach the token limit, the AI-assist features will stop generating new content until the next monthly cycle begins. Users also get this error: ​​ "Oops! It seems you have exhausted your 2 million token limit for this month. It will be restored on {date in this format 20 May 2023}" What languages does the AI-Assist feature support? Currently, the AI-Assist feature officially supports English. However, OpenAI is capable of understanding and generating text in several other languages, including French, Spanish, German, Italian, Dutch, and others. Please note that the quality of AI output may vary across languages. When selecting a language in the AI-Assist settings, language options are displayed in their native form along with their ISO language codes (for example, Suomi (fi), Italiano (it), Nederlands (nl) ). This format is shown consistently in the language dropdown and the selected state , and a checkmark indicator appears next to the currently selected language to make identification easier. Conclusion: AI Assist for notes and call logs in Recruit CRM helps you turn raw text into clear, structured, and reusable information across candidates, companies, contacts, jobs, and deals. s: Automatically generate transcriptions when recording calls.
h: Generating call transcripts
Navigating and consuming the transcript

Is there a duration limit for the call transcription?

b: Call Transcript Generator provides a seamless method to record, transcribe, and analyze conversations based on the transcription of calls. Generating call transcripts 1. While making a call , turn the toggle ON for the "Record Call" option, and select the "Generate call transcript" checkbox. 2. Once your call wraps up, you'll find the recording in the "Notes & Calls" module on the right-hand side of the profile page. To obtain the transcription, click on the “ View Transcript” option right next to the call recording. 3. In case you have a previously recorded call in the system, just head to the call recording, click on the "Call Transcript" button, and choose to generate the transcript by clicking on the “Generate Transcript” option on the pop-up that appears. Navigating and consuming the transcript 1. By clicking on the “ View Transcript” , you will get a pop-up with access to the complete call transcript, and you can also run a search for specific words or timecodes within it. 2. You also have the option to copy the entire transcript or export it as a .txt file. At times, call transcripts may appear in the wrong language due to AI hallucination. When this happens, you can use the ' Regenerate' option to generate a corrected/accurate version. ​ After clicking on Regenerate , a confirmation message will appear. This message includes a checkbox labeled ' Update Call Notes' . When selected, the call notes will be updated automatically once the new transcript is generated. ​ Your last choice for this checkbox will be remembered, so you do not need to select it every time. This helps keep your call transcripts accurate, clear, and easy to manage without any manual fixes. Searching through transcripts from Boolean Search You can also search through these transcripts directly from the Boolean Search you use. This makes it easier to quickly find conversations containing specific keywords across all your transcribed calls and trace the records accordingly. ​ To do this, follow along: Go to the Boolean Search and type the phrase you are looking for. 2. Select the Call Logs box to enable the Boolean Search to look through call logs. 3. Click on Apply Search . And now, you will see the list of records that have the phrase mentioned in their call transcript. This way, you can instantly locate the right conversations and save time while reviewing important call details. Enhancing the call transcript with AI 1. You can click on the AI Assist Button to: Extract key points of the transcript; Summarise it; Improve it; Generate custom prompts to tailor the generated results to your specific requirements. 2. Once the generation process of the prompt is complete, you will be presented with the following three options: Copy the generated result; Replace it with the call log added to the system; Regenerate the result to make additional refinements. FAQs related to the AI-Call transcript feature Is there a duration limit for the call transcription? The feature accommodates calls of varying lengths, with the only constraint being the size of the audio file, which should not exceed 25 MB (which equals 1 to 1.5 hours of call duration). This ensures a smooth and efficient transcription process. What languages are supported by the transcription feature? The transcription feature supports a wide array of languages, including but not limited to English, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Arabic, Hindi, and many more. Here is the complete list: Afrikaans, Arabic, Armenian, Azerbaijani, Belarusian, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Catalan, Chinese, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, Galician, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Kazakh, Korean, Latvian, Lithuanian, Macedonian, Malay, Marathi, Maori, Nepali, Norwegian, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tagalog, Tamil, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Urdu, Vietnamese, and Welsh. Can I transcribe the calls recorded in the past? Absolutely! You can generate transcripts for past calls from the call logs, making sure you always have access to the information you need, whenever you need it. How accurate is the transcription? The Whisper ASR system is trained on a substantial amount of data, ensuring a high level of accuracy in transcription. However, the accuracy might vary based on the clarity of the audio and the language spoken. Is there a limit to the use of this feature? The AI-Assist feature has a monthly token limit of 3000 minutes of call transcription. After the call ends, open the Notes and Calls tab on the relevant candidate, contact, or company record and locate the call log entry for the completed call and click View Transcript to open the transcript pop-up. ​ Note: If the Record Call toggle or the Generate Call Transcript checkbox was not enabled before the call, no transcript will be created for that call. If you want the associated call notes to be updated automatically once the new transcript is generated, select the Update Call Notes checkbox. Confirm the regeneration. The results will show all records whose call transcripts contain the searched phrase, allowing you to trace and review the relevant conversations directly. ​ Enhance a Call Transcript Using AI Assist Once a call transcript is open, AI Assist lets you process and act on the content without manually reviewing every line. Open the call transcript using the View Transcript option on the call log. Click the AI Assist button at the bottom of the transcript area. Saved Prompts: Use your own saved instructions to tailor the generated output to a specific requirement, such as drafting a follow-up email based on the call. 4. Replace: Replace the current call notes or summary in the system with the AI-generated content. Regenerate: Run the prompt again to refine or adjust the output if the first result is not satisfactory. ​ Troubleshooting Problem - The call transcript is missing or not generated. Existing calls with recording can be transcribed by clicking on the Generate Transcribe button when opening the Call Transcript. ​ Problem - Boolean search is not returning the expected call transcript results. The system considers up to the last five messages in the email thread when generating the AI suggestion. If fewer than five messages exist, all available messages are used. s: In this article, we will tell you how you can use AI matching to find the most suitable candidates for your job listings.

b: What does this feature do and when to use it? AI Job Candidate Matching helps you find and rank candidates for a specific job using AI. You can search either from your existing Recruit CRM database (My Database) or Recruit CRM's Global Database , which contains 800 million+ external candidate profiles . Recruit CRM extracts relevant Search Filters from your query or Job Description and uses the Matching Criteria to evaluate candidates. Each candidate is ranked and scored from 0–100 based on how closely they match the defined criteria, with reasoning provided for each score. You can review and customize the Matching Criteria before running the search. When matching against My Database, recent notes and call logs can be used as additional context when ranking candidates and generating the reasoning for their match score, alongside information from their resume or profile. Use this feature when you want to: Get an AI-ranked shortlist of candidates already available in your database for an open job. Search the Global Database directly using the job description. Run an AI match from a job Use AI Job Candidate Matching from a job to find candidates who best match the role. You can search either your own candidate database or Recruit CRM's Global Database, review and customize the search parameters, and then use AI-powered Matching Criteria to evaluate and rank the results. Open the specific job for which you want to find and match candidates. Please note: The job must have a Job Description for AI Job Candidate Matching to generate the Search Filters and Matching Criteria. If the selected job does not have a Job Description, Recruit CRM will prompt you to add one before you can continue with the search Click the star icon at the top of the job to open AI Job Candidate Matching . ​ Select the database you want to search: My Database – Finds candidates from your own candidate database in Recruit CRM. Global Database – Finds candidates from Recruit CRM's global candidate database. ​ After selecting your preferred database, you will be presented with AI Clarifying Questions . Recruit CRM reviews the Job Description and asks for additional information when something is ambiguous, incomplete, or needs clarification before the search can be generated. ​ For example, the questions may ask you to clarify a missing work location, an unclear requirement, or whether a particular skill should be considered mandatory. You can select one or more available answers, provide additional information in free text where applicable, or skip the questions if you do not want to provide the suggested information. Clarifying the requirement helps produce more relevant results. ​ Once you have provided the required details, click Continue . You will then have the option to review the Search Filters and Matching Criteria that Recruit CRM has generated for the search. These define the parameters Recruit CRM will use to find, evaluate, and rank candidates. ​ Search Filters determine which candidates enter the search pool, while Matching Criteria determine how candidates within that pool are evaluated and ranked. To make changes to the Search Filters, click Edit Filters . The Filters panel will open on the right, where you can configure filters such as Employment Information, Skills and Keywords, Location, and Education . You can also add other filters based on your requirements using the option at the bottom of the panel. For Job Title and Company , you can enable the Current Only toggle to limit the search to candidates whose current job title or company matches the entered filters. Once you have configured the filters, click Save . Next, review the Matching Criteria generated from your query. These criteria are separate from the Search Filters and are used to evaluate how closely each candidate matches the requirements of the role. Each criterion contributes to the candidate's overall match score out of 100 . Recruit CRM assigns each criterion a suggested weight from 1 to 10 , where 10 is the highest importance . Criteria with a higher weight have a greater influence on the candidate's final ranking. You can change these weights based on the priorities of the role. You can also add, edit, or delete Matching Criteria based on your requirements. To add a new criterion, click Add Criterion , enter the requirement Recruit CRM should consider, and assign a weight based on its importance to the role. How the match score works ​ Each candidate receives a 0–100 match score based on how they perform against the Matching Criteria and the weights assigned to those criteria. A criterion with a higher weight has more influence on the final score than a criterion with a lower weight. ​ For example, if relevant experience is given a weight of 10 and a nice-to-have certification is given a weight of 2, performance against the experience criterion will have a much greater effect on the candidate's overall score. While you are configuring the filters and Matching Criteria, you will see the total number of candidates matching your Search Filters at the bottom of the page. This live count helps you understand the size of your candidate pool before running the AI match. Click Find Candidates to run the search. The search usually takes 2–3 minutes to complete. ​ Once the search is complete, Recruit CRM displays up to 100 candidates per page . You can review the matched candidates and take action directly from the results page: Select individual candidates or use the bulk selection option to select multiple candidates. Add the selected candidates to your Recruit CRM database. Assign selected candidates to a job. Add candidates to a hotlist. Add a note to the selected candidates. Please note: When My Database is selected, the results include up to 100 candidates on a single page . When you select a candidate, the panel on the right provides a detailed view of the candidate's profile , along with the Matching Criteria that contributed to their match score. This helps you understand why the candidate was ranked for the search and how closely their profile matches the requirements of the role. ​ Understand Search Filters and Matching Criteria Search Filters and Matching Criteria work together, but they serve different purposes. Search Filters: Search Filters are the initial criteria used to determine which candidates enter the search pool. For example, you can filter candidates based on their title, experience, skills, or location. Matching Criteria: Matching Criteria are applied after the candidate pool has been created. They help evaluate and rank candidates based on how well their profiles match the job. Each criterion has a weight that contributes to the candidate's overall match score out of 100. For example, suppose you're hiring for a Customer Success role and want candidates with at least five years of total work experience. You could use a Total Experience filter to require candidates to have at least five years of experience. You could then use a Matching Criterion to evaluate how much of that experience is specifically relevant to Customer Success. A candidate with five years of experience may meet the filter, but if only one of those years were spent in Customer Success, they may receive a lower match score than a candidate whose five years of experience are primarily in Customer Success. Search Filter fields: Field How it works Title Title searches the candidate’s current role and previous roles they have held in the past. To search for only the current roles, you need to enable/turn on the 'Current Only' toggle. Total Experience Set a minimum and/or maximum number of years of experience. Skills Searches for skills across the candidate’s entire profile rather than a single field. Mark specific skills as Must-have to make them require, or leave them as Good-to-have to improve ranking without making them mandatory. Language Skills Set the required proficiency level and optionally mark a language as Must-have . Location Matches any of the locations you enter. You can enter a city, locality, state, or country. Location matching is based on the candidate's current profile location rather than their employer's location. Recruit CRM can recognize known location synonyms in natural-language searches. Keywords Use Boolean search operators such as AND, OR, and NOT , including grouped searches, across the candidate’s full profile. University, Graduation Year, Degree, Name These fields are also available for searching. Current Only Limits results to candidates who currently hold the searched Job Title or currently work at the selected Company , rather than candidates who held the title or worked at the company in the past. Recruit CRM may automatically enable this option when it is relevant to the search. 📌 Please note: When matching against My Database , you can also filter and use Boolean search across custom fields, notes, and calls, using the same Boolean search functionality availabl

You can search this database using either a natural-language description or manually selected search filters, without requiring the candidates to already exist in your Recruit CRM database. Recruit CRM first narrows the Global Database using Search Filters and then, for AI Search, evaluates and ranks the resulting candidates using AI-generated Matching Criteria. This allows you to either describe the candidates you need in natural language or start from a Job Description and let Recruit CRM generate the search requirements for you. You can use this feature when you want to: Find candidates who are not already in your database. Get an AI-ranked shortlist based on a natural-language description. Quickly find a list of candidates using specific filters. Search a large external candidate pool instead of only your existing records. Ways to start a search in AI Sourcing: You can start an AI Sourcing search in several ways: - Natural-language Search : Describe the type of candidate you are looking for in plain language. - Job-based Search : Select a recent job and use its Job Description as the basis for the search. - Filter Search : Manually configure search filters to find candidates from the Global Database without AI ranking. Search for candidates using AI Sourcing 1. Natural Language AI Search: Natural-language search allows you to describe the type of candidate you are looking for using a plain-language description. Recruit CRM uses the information in your query to create relevant search filters and rank the resulting candidates. Go to the Candidates list page and click on the AI Sourcing button at the top. In the Search tab, describe the type of candidate you are looking for using natural language. Include details such as the job title, skills, experience, location, and any other requirements that are important for the role. ​ You can also start the search using the Job Description from a recent job . Select a recent job to use its Job Description as the basis for the search. Recruit CRM will extract relevant Search Filters and Matching Criteria from the description. 2.Job-Based AI Search: When you start an AI Sourcing search from a Job, Recruit CRM uses the job description from the selected job to generate the search requirements. The job-selection screen displays your most recently added jobs, and you can search for additional jobs by job name, company name, city, or Job ID. Only jobs you have permission to view are available for selection. Please note: The jobs that are on the 'Closed' job status will not be visible for selection. If the selected job does not have a Job Description, you will be prompted to add one before continuing. Review the AI Clarifying Questions displayed after you enter your search. Recruit CRM uses these questions to identify missing or ambiguous information that could affect the search results. For example, it may ask you to clarify an experience range, location, or another requirement. Clarifying the requirement helps produce more relevant results. You can select from the available answers, provide additional information where applicable, or skip the questions if you do not want to provide the suggested information. ​ Click Continue to proceed to the Search Filters and Matching Criteria. Review the Search Filters and Matching Criteria to see the parameters Recruit CRM will use to search and evaluate candidates. To make changes to the search filters, click Edit Filters . The Filters panel will open on the right, where you can configure filters such as Employment Information, Skills and Keywords, Location, and Education . You can also add other filters based on your requirements using the option at the bottom of the panel. For Job Title and Company , you can enable the Current Only toggle to limit the search to candidates whose current job title or company matches the selected criteria. Once these filters are configured, click on Save. Next, review the Matching Criteria generated from your query. These criteria help evaluate and rank candidates based on how well their profiles match the requirements of the role. Each criterion contributes to the candidate’s overall match score. You can adjust the weight of each criterion based on its importance to the role. Criteria with a higher weight will have a greater influence on the ranking, helping the most suitable candidates appear higher in the results. You can also add a new criterion based on your requirements by clicking Add Criterion . Enter the criterion you want Recruit CRM to consider, then adjust its weight according to its importance in the search. ​ As you adjust the filters, a live count of the total matching candidates will be displayed at the bottom of the page. This count updates based on the filters currently applied, helping you understand the size of the matching candidate pool before running the search. Click Find Candidates to run the search. The search usually takes 2–3 minutes to complete. Once the search results are available, Recruit CRM displays 100 candidates per page . From the results page, you can review the matched candidates and take action directly such as: Add the selected candidates to your Recruit CRM database. Assign selected candidates to a job. Add candidates to a hotlist. Add a note to the selected candidates. Select individual candidates or use the bulk selection option to select multiple candidates. Bulk selection is limited to 100 candidates at a time , corresponding to one full page of results. When you select a candidate, the panel on the right provides a detailed view of the candidate’s profile , along with the Matching Criteria that contributed to the candidate’s match score. This helps you understand why the candidate was ranked for the search and how well their profile matches the requirements. ​ ​ How the search works? Recruit CRM extracts relevant Search Filters from your query or Job Description and uses the Matching Criteria to evaluate candidates. Each candidate is ranked and scored from 0–100 based on how closely they match the defined criteria, with reasoning provided for each score. You can review and customize the Matching Criteria before running the search. ​ Search for candidates using filters from the Filter Search section in AI Sourcing Filter search allows you to manually define the criteria used to search the Global Database . Go to the Candidates list page and click AI Sourcing at the top. Select Filter Search . Enter the values for the fields you want to use as search criteria. Review the selected filters and click Search . Search filter fields: Field How it works Title Title searches the candidate’s current role and previous roles they have held in the past. To search for only the current roles, you need to enable/turn on the 'Current Only' toggle. Total Experience Set a minimum and/or maximum number of years of experience. Skills Searches for skills across the candidate’s entire profile rather than a single field. Mark specific skills as Must-have to make them require, or leave them as Good-to-have to improve ranking without making them mandatory. Language Skills Set the required proficiency level and optionally mark a language as Must-have . Location Matches any of the locations you enter. You can enter a city, locality, state, or country. Location matching is based on the candidate's current profile location rather than their employer's location. Recruit CRM can recognize known location synonyms in natural-language searches. Keywords Use Boolean search operators such as AND, OR, and NOT , including grouped searches, across the candidate’s full profile. University, Graduation Year, Degree, Name These fields are also available for searching. Current Only Limits results to candidates who currently hold the searched Job Title or currently work at the selected Company , rather than candidates who held the title or worked at the company in the past. Recruit CRM may automatically enable this option when it is relevant to the search. Please note: Only Skills and Language Skills allow Must-have and Good-to-have values to be combined in the same search. Other fields match any of the values entered by default. For stricter matching, use Boolean search with AND logic. When using Filter Search, Recruit CRM does not automatically treat different names for the same location, such as Los Angeles and LA , as equivalent. However, when a location is included in a natural-language query or job description, Recruit CRM may automatically recognize and add known synonyms to the filters. Filter Search returns candidates who match the selected filters but does not rank them based on suitability. No AI scoring is applied, so the order of the results does not represent a best-to-worst ranking. For most fields, selecting multiple values return

t: All Contractors Page / Timesheets in Recruit CRM
s: This article explains how the All Contractors page works and how users can view and manage contractors who have timesheets enabled.
h: How to Access the Contractors Page
Viewing All Contractors in One Place
Contractor Status
Review Job Name and Duration
Reviewing contractor information
Filtering Contractors
Bulk Actions for Contractors
Troubleshooting
b: The Contractors page is available under the Pay and Bill entity and provides a centralized view of all candidates who are working as contractors. This page helps agency users track contractor availability, active and future assignments, job duration, and related job and deal information from one place. ​ Only candidates who have timesheets enabled for at least one job are shown on this page. Note: Currently, this feature is in beta and can be enabled upon request. Please feel free to reach out to your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. How to Access the Contractors Page To access the Contractors page: Go to Pay and Bill in Recruit CRM Click on the Contractors tab You will see a list of all contractors that you have access to, based on your roles and permissions. Viewing All Contractors in One Place Open the Contractors page from the Pay and Bill entity. Review the list of contractors displayed in a single list view. Remember that a candidate appears here only if: They are assigned to at least one job where timesheets are enabled. You have permission to view that candidate’s record. Note: If you do not have permission to view a candidate, you will not be able to see that candidate listed as a contractor on the Contractors page. Contractor Status Look at the status column for each contractor. Note that the contractor status is automatically determined by the system and cannot be manually edited. Interpret the status values as follows: Assigned : The contractor is either currently working on an active job or is assigned to a future job that has not started yet. Green Assigned: The contractor has an active job. Yellow Assigned: The contractor has a future job that has not started yet. Available : The contractor is not working on any active jobs. All previously assigned jobs have passed their job duration (their start and end dates have ended). Review Job Name and Duration The Job Name and Job Duration columns provide an at-a-glance view of the contractor's current and upcoming assignments. The Job Name column displays all relevant jobs assigned to the contractor, including future job assignments. If a contractor has both active and future assignments, all relevant job names are displayed. The Job Duration column shows: For active jobs , the number of days remaining along with the job's end date. For future jobs , Yet to Start along with the relevant job's end date. If a contractor has multiple jobs, the Job Duration column displays the active job with the highest number of days remaining . Hover over the Job Duration value to view details of all relevant jobs, including: Job name Job duration Total duration Days remaining for active jobs Yet to Start status for future jobs ​ The remaining days are calculated based on the account's timezone . Job Duration Color Coding The Job Duration value is color-coded based on the percentage of the total assignment duration remaining: Green: More than 50% remaining Orange: 30%–50% remaining Red: Less than 30% remaining For example, for a 100-day assignment, 50 days remaining is shown in orange , while fewer than 30 days remaining is shown in red . Reviewing contractor information You can choose which fields are displayed on the Contractors page and arrange them to suit your workflow. On the Contractors page, click Show/Hide Columns in the top right corner. Select the fields you want to display or clear the ones you want to hide. Drag and drop the selected fields to arrange them in your preferred order. Click Save to apply your changes. ​ Your selected columns and their order will be reflected on the Contractors page, making it easier to view the information most relevant to your workflow. Filtering Contractors The Contractors page allows you to filter the list to quickly find specific contractors. To add filters: On the Contractors page, go to the top right corner of the page. Click Add filters to open the filtering options. Select a field from the Contractors field list to filter by Status, Job Name, or Deal Name. Choose the required filter values to refine the results. Apply the selected filters to quickly find specific contractors based on their status, the jobs they are assigned to, or the deals associated with those jobs. You can filter contractors using the following fields: Name Job Name Job Duration Portal Status Status Deal Name Bulk Actions for Contractors You can select multiple contractors at once and perform bulk actions on the selected records. On the Contractors page, select contractors individually by clicking the checkbox next to each contractor. To select contractors in bulk, click the checkbox at the top of the list, which selects 50 contractors at a time . Continue scrolling down the list to select additional contractors until the desired number is selected. You can select up to 3,000 contractors at a time for bulk actions by clicking on Select All. Once the desired contractors are selected, a bulk action bar will appear at the top of the list with options such as Assign to Job, Request Updated Profile, Pitch Candidate, Add to Hotlist, Enroll in Sequence, Compose Email, Add Note, Mark as Off-Limits, Update Field, Export, Enable Portal Access, Disable Portal Access, and Delete Candidate . Click More to view additional bulk action options. Select from the Bulk Action bar the action that you want to perform. Please Note Assign to Job: When Assign to Job is selected as a bulk action, the job selection is automatically limited to Contract and Contract-to-Perm jobs. Contractor Portal: Upto 200 contractors can be enabled or disabled for the Contractor Portal through bulk actions. When enabling the portal, eligibility is checked automatically. Contractors are excluded if: Their portal is already enabled. Their email address is missing. A portal already exists with the same email address. They have reached the daily invitation limit. If you would like to learn more about this feature, you can book a quick call with our team through this link . Troubleshooting Problem: A contractor you expect to see is missing from the Contractors page Likely cause: The candidate does not have timesheets enabled for any job, or you do not have permission to view that candidate. What to check: Confirm that the candidate is assigned to at least one job where timesheets are enabled. Confirm that your user permissions allow you to view that candidate’s record. Resolution: Enable timesheets for at least one job for that candidate if required. Ask an administrator to review and update your permissions if you should have access to that candidate. Problem: You cannot change a contractor’s status Likely cause: Contractor status is system-generated. What to check: Review the contractor's active and future jobs and their dates to understand how the status is being set. Resolution: Adjust job assignments or job dates if the status should change based on the contractor's actual assignments, rather than trying to edit the status field directly. FAQs Who appears on the Contractors page? Only candidates who are assigned to at least one job with timesheets enabled appear on the Contractors page. What happens if a contractor is unassigned from all jobs? If a contractor is unassigned from all jobs where timesheets are enabled: They are automatically removed from the Contractors page Their candidate record remains unchanged If the contractor is reassigned to a job with timesheets enabled, they will appear again on the Contractors page. Do deleted candidates appear on the Contractors page? No. Deleted candidates do not appear on the Contractors page. However, their historical timesheets remain accessible on the All Timesheets page. What does the Job Duration column show? For active jobs, it shows the number of days remaining and the job's end date. For future jobs, it shows Yet to Start and the job's end date. What happens to the Job Duration column if a contractor has multiple jobs? The Job Duration column shows the active job with the highest number of days remaining. Hover over the value to see details for all relevant active and future jobs. What happens when a contractor has only future assignments? The contractor is shown as Assigned in yellow, and the Job Duration column shows Yet to Start . When is a contractor shown as Available? A contractor is shown as Available only when they have no active jobs and no future job assignments. Conclusion The All Contractors page in Recruit CRM gives you a clear, centralized way to track contractors with timesheets, their availability, active jobs, and related deals. If you need this beta feature enabled or have questions about access and visibility, contact your account manager for further assistance. Related Articles How to Create and Manage Timesheets? t: All Timesheets Page in Recruit CRM
s: This article explains how the All Timesheets page in Recruit CRM works and how users can view, filter, and manage contractor timesheets from a single page.
h: Use this feature when:
Accessing the All Timesheets Page
Viewing All Timesheets in One Place
Understanding Timesheet Information
Filtering Timesheets
Taking Action on Timesheets
Timesheets for Deleted or Unassigned Records
Creating Timesheets in Bulk
b: The All Timesheets page, available under the Pay & Bill section , provides a centralized view of all contractor timesheets across your Recruit CRM account. Instead of navigating to individual candidates, jobs, companies, or deals, you can view, filter, manage, and take action on timesheets from a single location, improving visibility and streamlining timesheet management. Use this feature when: • You need a centralized view of contractor timesheets across candidates, jobs, companies, and deals. • You want to quickly locate timesheets by filtering them based on period, status, company, job, or deal. • You regularly submit, approve, reject, or update timesheets and want to perform these actions without opening individual records. • You need to create timesheets in bulk for multiple contractors and contract jobs. • You want to perform bulk actions such as creating invoices, updating time entries, exporting, deleting timesheets, or sending reminder emails. The All Timesheets page displays all timesheets available to you based on your role and permissions, along with their associated candidate, job, company, and deal information. It supports both individual and bulk actions directly from the list view, helping you manage contractor timesheets more efficiently. Timesheets are also retained even if their associated candidates, jobs, companies, or deals are deleted or merged, ensuring historical records remain available with appropriate labels such as Deleted or Unassigned . Note Currently, this feature is in beta and can be enabled upon request. Please feel free to reach out to your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. Accessing the All Timesheets Page You can access the All Timesheets page by: 1. Navigate to Pay & Bill from the left-hand navigation panel. 2. In the Pay & Bill section, click the Timesheets tab . ​ The All Timesheets page will open, displaying all contractor timesheets available to you based on your role and permissions. From here, you can view, filter, and manage timesheets without navigating to individual candidate, job, company, or deal records. ​ Viewing All Timesheets in One Place All contractor timesheets are displayed together in a single list on this page. By default, timesheets are automatically sorted by: Timesheet period (latest first) Company name Job ID This sorting helps you quickly find recent and relevant timesheets. Understanding Timesheet Information Each timesheet row displays both entity-related and timesheet-related details, including: Candidate Name Job Name Company Name Deal Name Relevant timesheet fields If a timesheet has no logged time, it displays “No hours logged.” Zero-hour timesheets also show an indicator next to their status. Hover over the indicator to see the tooltip “No hours logged in this timesheet.” ​ You can click on any related entity record to open its details in a new tab. Filtering Timesheets The All Timesheets page allows you to filter timesheets to quickly find the records you need. ​ To add filters: Click Add Filters at the top-right corner of the page. Select a field from the Timesheet Fields list. Choose the required filter values to refine the results. You can filter timesheets using the following fields: Timesheet Period Timesheet Status Company Name Job Name Deal Name Taking Action on Timesheets From the All Timesheets page, you can: Add time to open timesheets Submit timesheets Approve submitted timesheets Reject submitted timesheets All actions can be completed directly from this page. Timesheets for Deleted or Unassigned Records Timesheets are retained even if: A candidate is deleted A job, company, or deal is deleted A candidate is unassigned from a job Labels such as Deleted or Unassigned are shown next to the relevant record. You can still submit, edit, approve, or reject timesheets as applicable. Note: If a candidate has been deleted, the timesheets will still be available, but their Contractor Details page will no longer be accessible. ​ If a candidate is unassigned from a job, the timesheets will still be available and the Contractor Details page can still be viewed, but timesheet settings cannot be modified, and no new timesheets can be added. Creating Timesheets in Bulk Go to Pay and Bill , click on the Timesheets tab, and then click the Add Timesheet option from the top-left corner of the screen. A timesheet pop-up will appear, where you can select multiple contractors and contract jobs. Choose the timesheet period. Only time periods that are common across the selected contractors will be available and click Add to generate the timesheets. ​ This allows you to quickly create timesheets for multiple contractors at the same time. Using Bulk Actions The All Timesheets page allows you to perform actions on multiple timesheets at the same time. ​ To use bulk actions: Select one or more timesheets using the checkboxes on the left. Once selected, the bulk action options appear at the top of the page. From here, you can perform the following actions (depending on the timesheet status): Create Invoice Bulk Update Time Entries Email Reminder Export Delete The number of selected records is shown at the top-right of the page, allowing you to quickly confirm how many timesheets the action will apply to. Note: The limit for bulk selection is upto a 100 records. ​ How Timesheet Notifications & Email Reminders works in Recruit CRM Timesheets and Merged Records When candidates or jobs are merged, the secondary merged records the original records are removed, but their associated timesheets are retained and continue to appear on the All Timesheets page. If you would like to learn more about this feature, you can book a quick call with our team through this link . Troubleshooting Problem: You cannot see the All Timesheets page under Pay & Bill Likely cause: The All Timesheets feature is in beta and not enabled for your account. What to check: Confirm whether the Pay & Bill entity and Timesheets tab are visible in your left side panel. Resolution: Contact your account manager and request to have the All Timesheets feature enabled for your account. Problem: Bulk action options do not appear Likely cause: No timesheets have been selected. What to check: Confirm that you have checked at least one timesheet checkbox on the left side of the list. Resolution: Select one or more timesheets. Once selected, the bulk action bar should appear at the top of the page, allowing you to choose actions like bulk invoice, bulk update, export, delete, or set email reminders. Problem: You cannot apply bulk actions to all the timesheets you selected Likely cause : The bulk action limit has been reached. What to check: Look at the count of selected records at the top right of the page. Resolution: Ensure that you are selecting no more than 100 timesheets at a time. If needed, run multiple bulk actions in batches of up to 100 records each. FAQs How do roles and permissions work on the All Timesheets page? Access follows the same rules as the existing Timesheets module. Permissions are determined by the candidate access rules configured in Roles and Permissions . What happens if a candidate is deleted? If a candidate is deleted and no owner is available: Users with view everything access can still view and manage the timesheets. Users with limited access cannot view or act on deleted timesheets. Does the Timesheet Period filter include overlapping date ranges? Yes. Any timesheet whose date range overlaps with the selected period will be included, even if it does not fall entirely within that range. ​ Conclusion The All Timesheets page in Recruit CRM centralizes contractor timesheet management, making it easier to view, filter, and act on records from a single place, even when related entities change or are removed. If you need help enabling or using this beta feature, please contact your account manager or your usual Recruit CRM support channel. t: Assigning a candidate to a job
s: This article will teach you how to shortlist candidates by assigning them to specific positions.
h: What this feature does & when to use it?
Before you begin:
1. Assign a candidate from the candidate list page:
Emailing the contacts of the selected jobs
2. Assign a candidate from the candidate profile
3. Assign candidates from within a job profile
4. Using the Chrome Extension

b: What this feature does & when to use it? Assigning candidates to jobs lets you assign people to specific open roles directly from the candidate list page, candidate profile page, job profile page, or while creating a new candidate. You can use this when: You want to assign one or more candidates to open jobs. You need to email primary job contacts at the same time as assigning candidates. You’re viewing a job profile and need to assign existing or new candidates. You’re parsing resumes or using the Chrome extension and want to assign candidates immediately. Before you begin: Please note: Ensure job records have primary contacts with valid email addresses if you plan to email them. Have your candidate resumes and attachments ready if you plan to share files. 1. Assign a candidate from the candidate list page: From the candidate list page, select the candidate(s) you want to assign by clicking the checkbox beside each candidate’s name. At the top of the list, you will see new action options appear, including the option to assign the selected candidates to a job. ​ Use the assignment options to either create a new job or select one of the existing jobs in your database. During this process, you can also choose to immediately update the hiring stage of the candidate for the selected job. If the candidate is already assigned to that specific job, the system will alert you with a pop‑up so you do not create duplicate assignments. The system will alert you with a pop-up if the candidate is already assigned to that specific job. Emailing the contacts of the selected jobs While assigning candidates to jobs from the candidate list, you can choose to directly email the primary contacts of the selected jobs. This allows you to assign candidates and share their details with job contacts in a single workflow. In the job assignment window, click the Email Contacts button at the bottom. Then complete the assignment by clicking Assign or Assign and Update Stage , as required. If you have selected candidates who are already assigned to the job, the system will skip reassigning them, but they will still be included in the email that is sent to job contacts. A pop‑up will appear where you can select which candidate fields and files to share (for example, resume, summary, or other attachments). Once you have made your selections, click Generate Email . If any of the selected job contacts are missing an email address, a validation box will appear listing those records. You can review the highlighted records in the validation box and then click Continue to proceed with the valid contacts only. After continuing, you will be redirected to the Compose Email screen. Here, the email will be pre‑filled with: Recipients (only primary contacts linked to the selected jobs) A subject line The default Pitch candidate template The candidate details and files you selected Review the email content and simply click Send to share the candidates with the selected job contacts. 2. Assign a candidate from the candidate profile To assign a candidate from the candidate profile/details page, scroll down to the candidate’s job section and click the Assigned Jobs tab. There, you will be able to see all the jobs the candidate is currently assigned to and assign them to a new job by clicking on Assign to Jobs . Jobs that the candidate is already assigned to will be pre-selected and will not be selectable again, and you will have the option to view unassigned jobs for easier selection. 3. Assign candidates from within a job profile From inside a job profile, use the Assign Candidates option to add existing candidates to that job. If a candidate does not yet exist in your database, you can parse their resume and assign them to the job as part of the same flow. 4. Using the Chrome Extension The assignment can also be performed via the Chrome extension. After saving a new candidate, click on the 'Assign to Job' option on the Chrome Extension, and you will have the option to assign the candidate to the job: If a candidate exists in your database, click on the 'Assign to Job' option as shown below, and you will have the option to assign the candidate to the required job: Click here to learn more about Chrome Extension 5. Using the Resume Parser You can also assign the candidate to a job using our Resume Parser Feature. Click on the 'Assign to Job' option as shown below: Click here to learn more about the Resume Parser FAQs How many candidates can be included in the email to the job contacts? Only the first twenty candidates, sorted by last updated date, will be included in the email sent to job contacts, even if you assign more than twenty in the same action. Which contacts receive the email when I use Email Contacts? Only primary contacts linked to the selected jobs will receive the email. Other contacts on the job who are not marked as primary will not be included. Conclusion: Assigning candidates to jobs helps you keep pipelines accurate, share profiles with job contacts, and streamline your recruiting workflow from multiple entry points. b: When a new contact is added in Recruit CRM, you will need to assign that contact to their respective company or multiple organizations with which the person is associated (in case the contact has multiple partnerships). Here's how you can assign a contact to a Company in Recruit CRM. 1. Go to your list of contacts and choose a contact from the list that you wish to assign to a company. 2. Open the contact's profile and click on the pencil icon to edit the form. 3. Type the company name in the "Company" section and select the company from the list. ​ Don't forget to hit Submit to save the changes! We also give you the option to assign multiple companies to a contact. Here's how you can do it: To know who is the company of contact you will find it under the company field: On the company profile, it will be in the "contacts section": There is no limit to the number of contacts that can be linked/assigned/added to a company. How to add/remove existing Contacts of a Company? This feature helps you to seamlessly add or remove existing contacts of a company making it easier to manage your contact database efficiently. Before you proceed make sure that the 'Select Existing Contacts' field is visible in the ' Company Fields ' section under 'Admin Settings' To Add existing Contacts to a Company 1. From the Company Profile: Click on the Pencil icon in the Company Profile. You can search for the existing contacts in your database and add them from the drop-down list. ​ 2. From the list view: You can select a specific company or multiple companies on the list page and click on the 'Update Field' option. t: Assigning Contact To A Company (New UI)
s: This article will help you link a contact to a company or multiple companies.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
Step-by-step instructions
Link a contact to a company
Link a contact to multiple companies
Add existing contacts to the company from the company profile
Add contacts to companies in bulk
Remove contacts from a company
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows you to link contacts with one or multiple companies, helping you maintain accurate relationships between people and organizations. This creates a two-way association: • View all companies linked to a contact from the contact profile. • View all contacts linked to a company from the company profile. You can manage these relationships individually or in bulk, ensuring your database stays organized and easy to navigate. Use this feature when: • You want to link a contact to one or more companies. • You need to add or remove contacts from a company profile. • You need visibility into which companies have associated contacts. Before you begin: • Ensure you have permission to edit Contacts and Companies. • Confirm that both contacts and companies already exist in the system • Check that the Select Existing Contacts field is enabled (if managing from the company side). Step-by-step instructions Link a contact to a company Open the contact profile → click Edit, which is the pencil icon on top of the Contact profile. In the Company field, search and select the company. Click Submit to save. The contact is now linked to the selected company. Link a contact to multiple companies Open the contact profile → click Edit which is the pencil icon on top of the Contact profile. In the Company section of the form, type and select the company names you want this contact to be linked to. After making your changes, click Submit to save. • All linked companies will appear in the contact profile • The same contact will also be visible in each company’s profile Add existing contacts to the company from the company profile Make sure the Select Existing Contacts field's visibility is toggled on in the Comany's Custom Fields settings. ​ Open the company profile → click Edit which is the pencil icon on top of the Company profile. Use the Select Existing Contacts field to search and select contacts to link Click Submit to save ​ The selected contacts will now be associated with the company. Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Create Associations feature allows you to link a note, call log, task, or meeting to multiple records, such as candidates, contacts, companies, jobs, and deals. This eliminates the need to duplicate activities across records. This feature is useful when you want to: Link an activity to multiple records. Keep related records updated with the same information. Avoid creating duplicate notes, tasks, meetings, or call logs. View the same activity across all associated records. Maintain a centralized activity history. Create associations for activities While creating a Note , Call Log , Task , or Meeting , click Create Associations . Use the search bar to find and select the records you want to associate with the activity. You can link candidates, contacts, companies, jobs, and deals. Finally hit the Add button to save the changes. Once it's created, the associated records will be displayed under Associations . The same note, call log, task, or meeting will also appear on every associated record. For example, if you create a note on a contact's profile and associate it with a candidate, the note will automatically be visible on both records without needing to create it again. Note: If you link them it will automatically update the Updated On field of this action on the linked record as well. If a record is deleted, all the Notes/Call logs/Tasks/Meetings added to that specific record will also be deleted. When Notes/Call logs/Tasks/Meetings on a record is associated with any other record(s) under “Create Associations”, and if this primary record is deleted, all the linked associations will also be deleted. Troubleshooting Problem: I can't find a record while creating an association. Likely Cause: The record may not exist or may not match your search criteria. What to Check: Verify that the record has already been created and confirm you're searching with the correct name. Resolution : Create the record first if it doesn't exist, or refine your search to locate it. FAQs What happens if a linked record is deleted? If a record is deleted, all the Notes/Call logs/Tasks/Meetings added to that specific record will also be deleted. When Notes/Call logs/Tasks/Meetings on a record is associated with any other record(s) under “Create Associations”, and if this primary record is deleted, all the linked associations will also be deleted. Conclusion: The Create Associations feature helps you keep related records connected by allowing a single note, call log, task, or meeting to appear across multiple records. This improves collaboration, reduces duplicate work, and ensures everyone has access to the same activity history. Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Audit Log in Recruit CRM lets you keep a log of actions performed by you and your team on Recruit CRM. t: Backdoor Hire/Lost Fee Report
s: This article will guide you on how to use the Backdoor Hire/Lost Fee Report
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
How is a potential backdoor hire detected?
What Happens on Update?
Reviewing and unlocking records
Removing an alert
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Backdoor Hire/Lost Fee Report detection builds directly on top of the Job Change Alert Report . Whenever Recruit CRM detects that a candidate has changed jobs, it takes one extra step and checks whether the candidate's new company matches any job the candidate was previously assigned to (Jobs created in the last 365 days) and where they were never marked as Placed. If the system finds a match, it marks it as a potential backdoor hire, since it suggests the candidate may have joined that company on their own, outside the placement you were working on. Backdoor Hiring Alerts are useful whenever you want to: Catch cases where a candidate you sourced or submitted for a role may have been hired directly by the client. Track and resolve these cases with a clear status workflow, instead of managing them over email or spreadsheets. Log recovered fees against a record once a backdoor hire situation has been resolved commercially, so you have a record of the outcome. Please note: This feature is currently in beta and will be live for all users in the coming weeks. Before you begin: Please Note: Backdoor Hire/Lost Fee Report is available only on the paid plans (Pro, Business and Enterprise). Users with view access to a specific candidate or contact records will be able to view only those records in this report. You need Edit access to a record to update the candidate profile or dismiss its job change alert. If you don't have edit access and try to click Update, you'll see a "No access" screen instead. On the Free plan, detection doesn't run at all, and you'll still see the Backdoor Hire/Lost Fee Report, but it will remain empty. If you later upgrade to a paid plan, detection for your account begins from the next monthly detection cycle. One Backdoor Hire record unlock consumes 5 Recruit CRM credits per candidate. How is a potential backdoor hire detected? There are 2 ways of accessing the potential backdoor hire that is detected: From the Reports section. From the Candidate Details Page. Please note: This check only looks at jobs created within the last 365 days, and only jobs the candidate is currently assigned to at the time of the check. If you later unassign the candidate from that job, it's no longer considered for backdoor hire detection going forward. From the Reports section: 1. Go to Reports → Backdoor Hiring Report , where you can review, unlock, and track it. 2. From here, you can: Apply Filters. Search by the record's name or company to find a specific record quickly. 3. Backdoor Status: You can assign a status to each record to track resolution. The default status is Backdoor Hire . Updating status does not remove the record from the report. When Recovered is selected, a pop-up allows entry of the recovered fee (in the Job's currency); this appears in the Recovered Amount column and can be edited by selecting Recovered again. From within the Update Status option, you can also add a task directly against a record, so you don't lose track of what still needs resolving. 4. Total Recovered Amount is shown at the top right. Amounts are shown at two levels: The Recovered Amount column for an individual record is shown in that job's currency. The Total Recovered Amount shown at the top right of the report is shown in your account's currency, and it recalculates automatically whenever you apply filters — so it always reflects the total for whatever subset of records you're currently viewing. Bulk Actions: You will be able to update Status and Update Profile. When updating status in bulk, an option to simultaneously update profiles is shown. Selecting Recovered in bulk applies the entered fee to each candidate separately. Records already at the chosen status or already updated are skipped. Sort & Filters: Column-level sorting; filters for New Organization, Assigned Job, Hiring Stage, Start Date, and Status; search by candidate name and company name. From the Candidate Details Page: When a potential backdoor hire is detected, a Backdoor Hire Detected badge appears on the candidate's profile: Note: If a candidate has both a pending Job Change Alert and a Backdoor Hire Detected alert at the same time, only the Backdoor Hire Detected badge is shown on their profile as it takes precedence, since it's the more significant of the two. You can still update the candidate's profile directly from this badge. The badge stays until you click on ' Update Profile' or ' Dismiss' , or a newer job change is detected. Dismissing removes the alert from both the profile and the report, and the same alert won't reappear in future cycles, but a new one will appear if the candidate moves jobs again. What Happens on Update? The system updates the Current Organization and Current Title/Position of the candidate. Creates a new work history entry with the detected job details. If the previous work history entry had "Currently working in this role" toggled on, its End Date is set using the publicly available data (left blank if unavailable). If the candidate has reached the maximum number of work history entries, the oldest is removed to make room. If the new employer doesn't exist as a company record, it is stored as plain text and no company record is auto-created. Note: When a work history entry is created via the job change alert update, mandatory work history field validation is bypassed. If mandatory fields configured in your account are not available from the publicly available data, those fields will remain empty in the new entry. Reviewing and unlocking records Under the Backdoor Hire/ Lost Fee Report, each record shows: - Candidate Name - New Organization & Title - Assigned Job - Hiring Stage (along with its history) - Start Date of the candidate's new role - Job Contact's Phone Number - Recovered Amount Please note: The first 2 records in your report are unlocked for free. Every record after that stays blurred until you unlock it, which costs 5 Recruit CRM Credits per candidate. You can use 'Unlock All' to unlock everything at once. If you don't have enough credits to unlock every blurred record, unlocking proceeds in order, starting with the oldest detected record, until your credits run out. By default, the report is sorted by when the matching job was created — the older the job, the earlier it appears in the list; the more recently the job was created, the later it appears. If the same candidate happens to match more than one job at the same company, this is still only treated as one alert, and only costs you one unlock. Removing an alert You can clear an alert from a candidate's profile in one of two ways: change their Backdoor Status away from the default "Backdoor Hire" to any other status, or dismiss the alert directly from the badge on the candidate's Details Page. Note: If you delete a candidate record, it's removed from both the Backdoor Hiring Report and the Job Change Alert Report. If you merge two candidate records where either one had a pending alert, the detection checks rerun on the resulting merged profile, and any relevant alerts are surfaced again on that profile and in both reports. Conclusion: Backdoor Hiring Alerts give you visibility into candidates who may have joined a company outside your placement, without needing to track it manually. Review such records in the Backdoor Hiring Report, unlock the ones you need, and use the status and recovered amount fields to keep track of how each case is resolved. t: Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM
s: Learn the basic elements to get started with Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM
h: Connections
Recipe
Triggers
Actions
Assets
Projects
Jobs
Tasks
b: New to automation? Let's take this one step at a time. Connections Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM connects to apps to build recipes, with each connection reusable across multiple recipes. Think of a connection like a key that allows it to unlock and communicate with another tool or app (like Recruit CRM, Outlook, Slack, etc). It's a way for Workflow Automation to securely access and retrieve information from the connected tool. Recipe Now, imagine a recipe as a set of instructions or a cooking recipe. It's a series of steps that guides the workflow on what to do with the information it gets from Recruit CRM (or any other connected tool). Recipes allow you to create automated workflows, like moving data from one tool to another without manual effort. So, in simple terms, a connection is like the key to open the door to another tool, and a recipe is the set of instructions for what to do once that door is open! Triggers Triggers serve as events or conditions that kickstart the execution of a workflow. They determine when the automation begins by responding to changes or activities within connected applications. Trigger events are activated within specific apps (like Recruit CRM, Gmail, etc.) upon the occurrence of certain events, such as the addition or update of a candidate or the receipt of an email. Additionally, triggers can be initiated by actions like adding a new line to a file, scheduled occurrences, or firing at predetermined times or intervals. Actions Actions represent the specific steps or tasks performed in response to a trigger. These are the operations that interact with connected applications and manipulate data. Actions encapsulate the specific functionalities and operations required to achieve the desired outcome of the workflow. For example, in the context of a recruitment workflow, an Action could involve creating a Deal when triggered by the creation of a Job in Recruit CRM. The Action step defines the details of this creation process, specifying the fields to be filled, data mappings, and any other relevant parameters. Assets Assets within Workflow Automation are a comprehensive list encompassing all the Connections and Recipes associated with your account. These pivotal elements form the foundation of your workflow structure, providing the necessary components to drive automation. When you navigate to the Assets tab, you'll find a comprehensive overview of every recipe and connection that you and your team have created. This organized hub allows you to efficiently manage and access all the automation components. Whether you are working on intricate workflows or establishing connections with external applications, the Assets tab provides a consolidated space for overseeing and editing all the essential elements of your automation ecosystem. Projects A project serves as a repository for your integration assets. Within a project, you can organize and store a cohesive set of assets related to your integrations, encompassing recipes, connections, and sub-folders. Projects help users maintain a logical and organized workflow within their work environment. Organize the projects in your workspace by department, use case, or project. For example: Jobs Jobs represent the instances or executions of your workflows or recipes. When you trigger a recipe, whether manually or through an automated event, a job is initiated to execute that particular recipe. Jobs serve as tangible records of the workflow execution, capturing details such as start time, end time, and any associated outcomes. Every time a recipe runs, it generates a job that can be tracked and reviewed in the Jobs tab. This allows users to monitor the status, details, and results of each workflow execution. Whether a job is completed successfully or encounters errors, the Jobs section provides valuable insights into the performance and outcomes of your automation processes. Tasks A task represents a singular unit of work carried out whenever a recipe undertakes an action demanding computing resources. Each time a recipe utilizes an action offered by a connector, it registers as one task. A job within a recipe may encompass numerous tasks, with the total tasks executed in a job being contingent on the data associated with the trigger event and the logic embedded in the recipe. Task counting: The following table shows a breakdown of how tasks are counted with the different recipe steps: Action Count Trigger Will not be counted as a Task Trigger conditions Will not be counted as a Task Search/Create/Update/Get/Upsert/Lookup etc. The Task is incremented by 1 for each of these Actions Actions in repeat (for each loop) The Task is incremented by 1 for every Action in the loop Control statement (If, Error monitor, stop) Will not be counted as a Task Batch/bulk operations The Task is incremented by 1 Note: All users, regardless of their plan, receive 50 free tasks per month to test and explore automation features. The free tasks are account-specific and not user-specific. Learn more about tasks here. Workflow Automation is an Enterprise plan feature which can also be added at an additional cost to Pro or Business plan subscriptions. t: Billing and Revenue Report
s: The Billing and Revenue Report in Recruit CRM helps you analyze billing, payable amounts, revenue, and profitability across Companies, Jobs, and Contractors based on approved timesheets.
h: What this feature does and when to use it
Generate and Analyze the Billing and Revenue Report
View the Report
Export the Report
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it The Billing and Revenue Report helps you track key financial metrics related to contract staffing and understand your overall billing and profitability. Use this report when: You want to track Billable Hours and Payable Hours based on approved timesheets. You need to review Billable Amount, Payable Amount, Gross Profit, and Margin Percentage . You want to analyze billing and profitability for specific Companies, Jobs, or Contractors . You want to export report data or charts for further analysis. Note: The report includes data from approved timesheets within the selected date range. All amounts are displayed in the account currency. Permissions: Report access follows your existing permissions for Companies, Jobs, Contractors, and Timesheets. Users can only select and view records permitted by their existing access levels, including Owned Only or Team Only permissions. A dedicated permission for the report is also available under Reports in Roles & Permissions . Generate and Analyze the Billing and Revenue Report 1. Navigate to the Reports section from the left-hand navigation menu and open the Billing and Revenue Report . 2. Use the Report Based On dropdown to choose how you want to analyze the report. You can select: Overall, Company, Job, Contractor. When selecting Company , Job , or Contractor , choose the specific records you want to include in the report. 3. Open the KPIs dropdown and select the metrics you want to analyze: Total Billable & Payable Hours, Total Billable Amount, Total Payable Amount, Gross Profit, and Margin Percentage. The Total Billable & Payable Hours KPI is calculated using approved billable and payable hours. Gross Profit is calculated as: Billable Amount − Payable Amount. 4. Choose the required date range from the dropdown. You can select a predefined date range or specify a custom date range to analyze billing and revenue for a specific period. 5. Click Generate Report to run the report. If you want to save the same configuration for future use, click Save & Generate Report . Once generated, the report displays the selected KPIs along with a chart and detailed table. View the Report Once the report is generated, it displays key metrics for the selected Company, Job, or Contractor , including: Total Billable Amount, Total Payable Amount, Gross Profit, Margin Percentage. The charts vary based on the selected KPI. The Overall report also includes monthly revenue and margin trends and current-year vs. previous-year comparisons where applicable. The overall report provides an account-level view of billing and profitability. The summary table below the charts can be expanded for applicable report types to view the records contributing to the reported billing and profitability figures. This expansion is available only for reports generated based on Company and Job. Report data can be exported for further analysis. Click any chart bar to view the related Timesheet records, where you can use available filters, search, export, column customization, and other Timesheet actions. Export the Report You can export the Billing and Revenue Report in multiple ways: Click Export Report to CSV to download the detailed report data in CSV format. Use the Export option on the chart to download the chart as an image in PNG, JPG, or SVG format. Additionally, when viewing the related Timesheet listing, you can use the standard Export option to download the Timesheet data for further analysis. This allows you to use the report data for further analysis or share the visual representation of your billing and revenue performance. Important Notes Approved Timesheets: The report includes data from approved timesheets within the selected date range. Timesheets that have not been approved are not included in the report. Account Currency: All financial amounts are shown in the account currency . If a Timesheet uses a different currency, its financial values are converted to the account currency when the Timesheet is approved, using the exchange rate available at that time. Pay Amount, Bill Amount, and Gross Profit are then stored in the account currency. Until approval, these values appear as Not Available . Future exchange-rate changes do not affect the stored historical values. Report Types: You can generate the report based on Overall, Company, Job, or Contractor , allowing you to analyze billing and profitability at different levels depending on your reporting needs. Timesheets Spanning Multiple Periods: If a Timesheet overlaps with the selected reporting period, the entire Timesheet is included in the report, including its hours, billable amount, payable amount, and gross profit. Conclusion: The Billing and Revenue Report gives you a clear view of your billing and profitability based on approved timesheets, helping you analyze performance across Companies, Jobs, and Contractors over a selected period.
