b: . ​ Number Fields greater than : Searches for profiles where the value is greater than a given number. ​ Example: Years of Experience greater than "5" ​ Result: Retrieves profiles of candidates with more than 5 years of experience. between : Retrieves results within a specific numerical range. ​ Example: Salary between "50000" and "100000" ​ Result: Retrieves profiles with salaries between 50,000 and 100,000. ​ Group Filters 1. Filter Candidates by Call Type and Date Added On Objective : Identify candidates who have had a specific type of call within a defined time frame. Action : Select call type (e.g., "Phone Screening"). Add a group filter for call log added on is "Last Month" using the 'AND' condition between them as shown in the image below: Expected Outcome : Results displayed will include candidates who had a "Phone Screening" call, added in the last month. 2. Combine Call Type and Note Type Filters Objective : Search for candidates that meet multiple criteria for call and note types. Action : Select call type (e.g., "Phone Screening"). Add a group filter for call log added on is "Last Month" using the 'AND' condition between them. Add another group filter for note type (e.g., "Screening Notes") 'AND' for note added on is "This Week" as shown in the image below: Expected Outcome : Results displayed will include candidates who had a "Phone Screening" call, added in the last month, and "Screening Notes" added in the current week. Activity Fields Filter You can filter based on activities like notes, call logs, tasks, or meetings. ​ Here are some examples of how to apply filters based on activity fields: Example 1: ​ Filter: Task added by "John Doe" ​ Result: Retrieves all records for which tasks are created by John Doe. If you are on the candidate list page , it will return all candidates' records matching the search criteria, and it will be similar for other record types such as contacts, companies, etc. Example 2: ​ Filter: Call Outcome is "Positive" ​ Result: Retrieves all records where a call resulted in a positive outcome. Example 3: ​ Filter: Note Type is "Follow-up" Result: Retrieves all records where notes are categorized as “Follow-ups." Example 4: Filter: Meeting Type is "Sales Presentation" Result: Retrieves all records where scheduled meetings are classified as sales presentations. Cross-Entity Search Cross Entity Search allows you to retrieve records using fields from associated entities while keeping the primary entity view focused. ​ Example: You can search contacts based on their associated company fields . Currently supported for: • Contacts • Companies • Deals • Candidates You can perform the Search on the 'Kanban View' as well. ​ 📌 Saving, Applying, and Resetting Searches Recruit CRM allows you to save search queries for future use , making it easier to revisit commonly used searches without rebuilding the filters each time. Saved searches can also be shared with specific teammates, teams, or all users , helping maintain consistency when multiple users need access to the same search criteria. Once saved, these searches can be quickly accessed from the List Page Quick View , allowing you to run them instantly. ​ When working with filters or Boolean searches, it is important to apply your changes correctly so the updated results are displayed. After adding or modifying any filters, click the Apply button for the changes to take effect. Alternatively, you can press Enter to run the newly added filters without clicking Apply. However, if you remove an existing filter, pressing Enter will not apply the change; you must click Apply Filters to update the results. For changes made inside the Boolean Search field, you can execute the search by clicking Search or pressing Enter . ​ To make the process faster, Recruit CRM also supports keyboard shortcuts: • Mac: Command + Return • Windows: Control + Enter You can also duplicate existing filters to quickly recreate similar filter conditions without starting from scratch. Resetting and Persisting Searches If you want to clear all the applied filters and start over, you can use the Reset option. This will remove all currently applied filters and return the list to its default state. ​ Recruit CRM also supports persisting filters , which means your applied filters remain active even if you: • Navigate to another tab • Refresh the page • Log out and log back into the system This behavior ensures that your search context is preserved, allowing you to continue working with the same filtered results without needing to rebuild your search every time. Known Limitation Boolean Search Keywords Highlighting : While running a Boolean search, keywords won't get highlighted on the Resume file and in Notes. 👀 FAQs Can I use multiple filters on the same field? Yes, you can apply multiple filter conditions to the same field and use Boolean operators to create more refined searches. What are stopwords , and how do they affect my search? Stopwords are common words (e.g., “the”, “and”, “is”) that are excluded from search queries. This means that these words will not affect your search results. For more details, refer to the official stopwords documentation . Stopwords : a, an, and, are, as, at, be, but, by, for, if, in, into, is, it, no, not, of, on, or, such, that, the, their, then, there, these, they, this, to, was, will, with Wh y can’t I combine both AND and OR conditions in the same filter search? At the moment, filters support only one condition type within a filter group, either AND or OR . Mixing both in the same search can create ambiguity and lead to unpredictable results. For example: Title = Product AND Title = Manager OR Title = Lead This query can be interpreted in two different ways: • (Product AND Manager) OR Lead • Product AND (Manager OR Lead) Both produce very different results. In many cases, one query may return only “Lead” records, while the other may return no results at all. Since the system cannot reliably determine the intended grouping automatically, Recruit CRM currently supports only one condition type per filter group to ensure consistent and predictable search results. Can I search within candidate attachments other than the default resume? Yes. Select the Files option in Boolean Search to search the contents of a candidate's attached PDF , DOC , and DOCX files. The search includes up to the 10 most recent supported attachments for each candidate and excludes the default resume, which is searched under Candidates . What's the difference between the Candidates and Files search options? Candidates searches candidate fields (default and custom) and the resume stored in the default Resume field. Files searches other supported candidate attachments (PDF, DOC, and DOCX). You can select either option individually or use both together, depending on where you want Boolean Search to look. Hope this helps! 😄 Related Articles How to run a search in Recruit CRM Filter types for Advanced Search How to Run a Search in Recruit CRM (New UI) Filter types for Advanced Search (New UI) How to use the Global Search Bar in Recruit CRM

t: Build your own XML feed for job boards
s: This article will help you with the step-by-step process to build your own XML feed for job boards.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Why XML feed?
Here's how you can create your job feed:
Click here to know how to find the Job Slug
Here's an example of how you can create the XML feed for Xing
Here's an example to create the XML feed for Jooble
How to post jobs using the XML feed
How to check if your job is visible in the custom XML Feed
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Job Board XML Feed feature allows you to automate job postings to external job boards and receive applicants directly into Recruit CRM. While Recruit CRM offers native integrations with select job boards , XML feeds provide the flexibility to connect with additional job boards that support XML-based job imports. Use this feature when: • You want to automate posting jobs to job boards that do not have a native Recruit CRM integration. • You manage multiple job boards and need a standardized way to distribute jobs. • You want applicants from external job boards to be captured directly in Recruit CRM. • You need more control over the XML structure required by a specific job board. • You want to reduce manual job posting efforts and minimize data entry errors. The XML feed is generated dynamically using your job data and configured placeholders, ensuring that job information stays up to date automatically whenever changes are made within Recruit CRM. 1. By default, only the Account Owners and Admins can create XML feeds. You can also grant access to build XML feed to users on custom roles. 2. You can only create 10 XML feeds at a time on the Business Plan. On the Pro plan, you can only build 1 XML feed. 3. Only available on the Pro, Business and Enterprise Plan. Why XML feed? An XML feed is a structured data format used to distribute job listings across different platforms, including job boards. It provides a standardized and machine-readable way to share job-related information. The XML feed follows a specific format organizing details like job titles, descriptions, locations, requirements, and application instructions. Job boards consume the feed to display job listings consistently on their platforms. With the automatic transfer of applicant information, this functionality saves time and reduces errors. Here's how you can create your job feed: 1. Head over to Admin Settings >> Job Settings >> Build Job Feed XML >> click on the " Create Your XML Feed " button to get started. 2. Add a name to your feed to identify the feed and to track candidates, as it also serves as the ' Source ' of the applicants applying from the job board. Thus, an ideal choice would be to use the name of the job board itself. 3. Add XML header: The XML header is the static component of the XML feed and remains consistent across all jobs, as it is used to define the structure and formatting of the XML file. You will find it in the XML documentation provided by the job board you wish to integrate with. You can use the "Last updated on" placeholder in the XML header to allow job boards to fetch the time at which the XML was updated. Ensure that you include the XML body before closing the tags in the XML header. The XML body contains variable information that requires placeholders. To easily add these placeholders, utilize the ' Add XML Body Placeholder ' button located at the top right of the window. 4. Add XML body: The XML body is the main content of the XML feed as it contains It includes the actual job posting details, such as job title, description, location, requirements, job slug and application instructions. Click here to know how to find the Job Slug A slug is a unique code that Recruit CRM uses to identify each record. Here’s how you can find it for a job: Open the job profile. Look at the web address (URL) at the top of your browser. The text that comes after the last “/” in the URL is the slug. For example: For example, if your job URL is https://app.recruitcrm.io/jobs/12345 , then 12345 is the job slug. The image below will give you more clarity on the same: ​ To add the content under the ' XML Body ', you can refer to the sample code provided by the job board in their documentation. Input the required data for a single job here, and the system will automatically regenerate it for the remaining jobs. Only utilize fields in the XML that correspond to the available job data. For instance, if the XML includes a field named <Post Code>, but your job posting does not have this information, you should exclude the postcode field from the XML. Replace the sample data or empty spaces in the XML feed with the appropriate placeholders. By doing so, the XML feed will dynamically incorporate the relevant details from Recruit CRM for each job, eliminating the need for manual entry. When replacing values in the XML feed with placeholders, only replace the pre-filled values with the corresponding placeholders. This ensures that the dynamically populated job data from Recruit CRM is correctly integrated while retaining any other existing values or content in the XML feed. You can also add the Job's company logo to the custom XML feed. By adding the logo URL to the feed, the jobs will appear with the company logo on job boards. 5. Please ensure the XML body has been set up accurately, as the syntactical errors can be identified, however, errors in missing data or fields are not identifiable. 6. You can preview the XML feed to ensure that it meets all the requirements in terms of structure, content, and overall appearance. 7. Once you have set up your XML content, proceed to generate the feed by using the 'Submit' button. The generated XML feed once saved, allows you to make edits or updates as necessary through the Admin Settings. Here's an example of how you can create the XML feed for Xing To access the documentation for the Xing e-recruiting feed, please visit the following link: https://dev.xing.com/partners/job_integration/feed_docs#parameter-country 1. Navigate to the example feed and locate the static part, which encompasses the feed's format, structure, and type. Paste this static component into the header section of your feed. 2. The XML header encompasses the content from the beginning of the feed until the opening tag <postings> is encountered. It concludes with the closing tag </postings> and is followed by the closing tag </feed> to finalize the feed structure. 3. Ensure that you place the 'XML Body Placeholder' between the opening tag <postings> and the closing tag </postings>. This will indicate the specific section where the dynamic content will be inserted within the XML header. <?xml version="1.0"?> <feed xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="https://dev.xing.com/jobs/xsd"> <postings> {xml_body} </postings> </feed> 4. The XML body, which contains the variable information related to individual jobs, begins with the opening tag <posting>. Within this tag, you will find various job details that can be customized for each specific job entry. 5. You can find out which of the fields are necessary for job postings in Xing, and create your feed in accordance with that. 6. Here, some data can be static, that you want to keep contact for all jobs, others could be dynamic which are to be replaced by placeholders. 7. In this example, the value associated with CDATA is to be replaced by placeholders in the parentheses is to be replaced by placeholders to dynamically generate these values from job profiles and post them on the job board. 8. Once all the relevant data is added, do not forget to close the tag on the posting. The XML body will identify any errors in the syntax. However, if the error is an error in the posting or anything else other than the syntactical error, it will not be identified. 9. You can refer to the image below for more notes by Xing: Here's an example to create the XML feed for Jooble To access the documentation for the Jooble XML feed, please visit the following link: https://jooble.org/files/XML-feed/EN/jooble-xml-4job.pdf 1. Add the static component of the feed as reflected below: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> <jobs> {xml_body} </jobs> 2. The beginning of the variable component that is to be added to the XML body is signified by the <jobs> tag. Remember to close the tags after filling in the job details. This is what it would look like: <job id=" "> <link><![CDATA[{job_application_url}]]></link> <name><![CDATA[{job_title}]]></name> <region><![CDATA[{job_locality}]]></region> <description><![CDATA[{job_description}]]></description> <company><![CDATA[]]></company> <pubdate>...</pubdate> </job> 3. In the XML body, replace the sample data with placeholders from the drop-down menu on the top right of the window. 4. It is important to note that not all data requires CDATA. When replacing the 'Pubdate' field with a placeholder, ensure that the placeholder is in the correct format specified for the field. ​ How to post jobs using the XML feed In order for the jobs to be visible on the XML feed you have created, certain criteria need to be fulfilled first: Please note that it's not necessary to fill the fields with the message "Required To Post On Partner Job Boards" (City, State, Country, Maximum Salary, Job Description, Currency, Salary Type) for the jobs to be posted in the custom XML feed. However, if you’re posting to Free Job Boards , all fields m

b: Your careers page is often the first impression candidates have of your company. With Recruit Craft’s Website Editor , you can easily design and customize a page that reflects your brand and helps attract the right talent. ​ The editor allows you to mix and match templates, preview your design on different devices, and control how job listings appear, all without needing any technical skills. Let’s explore how you can make the most of it. 1. Choose a Template That Fits Your Brand 🎨 Start by selecting a pre-designed template that best represents your company’s look and feel. Each template provides a strong foundation, making it easy to create a polished, well-structured careers page. 2. Customize Each Section with Ease ✏️ After choosing a template, you can start personalizing every section of your careers page. The modular structure of the editor gives you complete control over each element, allowing you to create a page that looks and feels exactly the way you want it to. When you open the editor, you’ll notice that the workspace is divided into two main parts. The left panel is where you navigate between different components on your page, while the right panel is where you make all your edits and adjustments. This layout keeps everything organized, so you can easily move through your page and make changes without switching screens. The Elements panel on the left displays all the components that make up your selected page. This is where you’ll find sections like the navigation bar, hero banner, job cards, and more. When you click on a specific element, the panel will automatically show you the available settings and configuration options for that section. Each element has its own unique configuration settings, so it’s normal if one section offers certain options that others do not. For instance, one component might allow you to add a background image, while another might let you upload an SVG or adjust layout properties. To start making changes, simply hover over the element and click Edit. This opens a detailed view where you can modify that specific component. Within the right panel, you’ll find two main tabs that help you organize your work - The Configure tab lets you control how the element functions, such as field mappings, visibility, or content settings. The Design tab focuses on how the element looks, allowing you to adjust the layout, font styles, colors, and backgrounds. This clean, intuitive setup ensures that you can easily locate every tool and option you need, making it simple to fine-tune each part of your careers page until it perfectly represents your brand. Here’s what you can customize: 🔑 Navigation Bar Add your company logo to the navigation bar and customize the sign-up button to align with your brand’s style. You can adjust the colors, fonts, and layout to ensure it blends seamlessly with the rest of your website. ​ You can also change the height of the navigation bar using a simple slider. The height can be adjusted from 72 px up to 82 px; this helps achieve a more balanced and visually appealing header layout. As you adjust the navigation bar height, the logo automatically resizes as well, ensuring it looks more prominent while keeping the layout clean and well balanced. You can also make the company logo in the navigation bar clickable by adding a custom link to it. This allows you to direct candidates to a specific destination, such as your company website or a social page, when they click on the logo. The link can be updated at any time, giving you flexibility to change where the logo redirects without altering the design of the navigation bar. While uploading the logo, you can zoom in or out, rotate, and crop it as needed. This makes it easier to fit the logo correctly and match your branding requirements without having to edit the image elsewhere. ​ ✨ Hero Section Choose the perfect top section for your careers page from multiple layout options. You can mix and match designs from different templates to create your dream page. Adjust the font and color scheme to reflect your brand identity and make a strong first impression. ​ 🎯 Job Filters Decide how you want your job filters to appear on the page. You can set their color, font, and position to make the filtering process smooth and visually appealing for visitors. ​ You can also enable additional filtering options to help candidates find relevant roles faster. For example, a Salary Range filter allows candidates to set a minimum and/or maximum salary range while browsing jobs on the career page. This filter appears only if the Salary field is mapped in the filter configuration . When a salary filter is applied, jobs that do not have salary information will be excluded from the results. Click here to know more about how you can add this. Select Job Listing Page from the dropdown at the top and navigate to Filters . ​ ​ Select the Golden Groove filter and click Edit . ​ Choose the Dropdown option and open the Configure tab. ​ Click the + icon to add a new mapping. ​ Select the Salary field from the list and click Save to apply the filter. Note: The Salary Range filter is currently available through the Golden Groove filter template . However, it is not restricted to the Golden Groove career page template. You can apply the Golden Groove filter configuration to any career page template if you want to enable the Salary Range filter. 💼 Job Cards Control how your open job listings are displayed. You can modify the layout, font, and color of job cards to make them stand out while maintaining a clean and professional look. ​ You can also choose to display salary information on job cards to give candidates clearer visibility into compensation details. The salary values are automatically formatted for better readability and follow the appropriate numbering format based on the currency used. How salary is displayed on job cards If the minimum and maximum salary are equal → a single value is displayed (e.g., $5,000/month). If a salary range exists → it appears as a range (e.g., $5,000 – $8,000/month). If only the maximum salary is available → it is displayed as Up to $8,000/month . If no salary information is available → the salary will not appear on the job card. Salary values automatically include separators for better readability (for example, 700000 → 700,000 ). Indian currency values follow the Indian numbering format (for example, 700000 → 7,00,000 ). The salary frequency shown on the job card reflects the actual pay frequency configured in Recruit CRM , such as: • Hourly • Monthly • Yearly Controlling salary visibility You can enable or disable salary visibility using the Salary Range toggle in the editor. ​ Here is how you can do it Select Job Listing Page from the dropdown at the top and navigate to Job Cards . ​ Select the desired job card template and click Edit . ​ Choose the Additional Information option from the list. ​ Click on Salary Range , then open the Configure tab. ​ Turn the Visibility toggle ON . ​ Click Save to apply the changes.​ Job ID Display You can choose to display the Job ID on your job description pages by enabling the Show Job ID toggle in the Job Description page settings. Once enabled, the Job ID appears on the job description page, making it easier to reference specific job openings. 🔢 Job Count display You can display the total number of available jobs on your Job Listing page. When enabled, candidates will see a count such as “Showing 25 jobs.” The count updates automatically when candidates apply a search or filters, so they can immediately see how many roles match their criteria. ​ 📌 Please note: The Job Count setting is off by default for both new and existing templates. ​ Here’s how you can enable it: Open the Project where you want to enable the job count display. Select Job Listing Page from the dropdown at the top. From the left panel, go to Sections and select Job Cards . In the right panel, enable the Job Count toggle. You may need to scroll down to find this setting. You can also customize the text color and the text that appears before and after the job count. ⚙️ Job Description Page Header Customize the top section of your job description page just like the hero section. You can select from different layouts, mix and match styles, and personalize fonts and colors to keep your careers page consistent across every section. ​ This modular approach gives you full creative freedom to design a page that perfectly matches your brand and helps candidates navigate easily. 3. Real-Time Preview as You Edit 👀 The editor lets you see your changes instantly through a real-time preview feature. You can also toggle to Mobile Preview to check how your careers page looks on mobile devices, ensuring a great experience for all visitors. s: This article will guide you on how to bulk add time in Timesheets.
h: Adding Bulk Time from the Contractor Details Page
Adding Bulk Time from the Deals Page
FAQs
b: The Bulk Add Time feature makes it easy to add, edit, and submit time entries across multiple timesheets at once. Instead of opening each timesheet individually, you can save time by handling them all in one go. ​ This functionality is available in both: Contractor Details Page → bulk manage timesheets for a single contractor Timesheet Tab under Deals → bulk manage timesheets across multiple contractors Note Currently, this feature is in beta version and can be enabled upon request. Please feel free to reach out to your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. Adding Bulk Time from the Contractor Details Page 1. Open the Job, then select the contractor from the pipeline whose timesheet you want to update. ​ 2. Bulk select the timesheets to update, then click " Bulk Update Time Entries" . ​ 3. In the modal, enter work hours, break hours, and remarks. Use Copy to All or Copy to This Period if you want to replicate values and Click on it to apply changes across all selected timesheets. ​ ​4. If you are the designated approver, you can also directly submit and approve all the timesheets at once. Note: The Copy to All and Copy to Period actions will only apply hours to working days, not to days off. If needed, time for days off can be added manually. When you bulk update, the system checks the first valid timesheet (a non-approved timesheet is considered valid) to find errors. Some timesheets may not proceed. For example: “Method for logging work hours is different” → means the selected timesheets use different logging methods. “Timesheet is approved” → means approved timesheets cannot be updated. You can still continue with the valid timesheets by clicking Proceed. ​ Adding Bulk Time from the Deals Page 1. Open the Deal details page Go to the Timesheets tab . ​ 2. Bulk select the timesheets to update, then click " Bulk Update Time Entries" ​ 3. Enter the hours, breaks, and any remarks as required, then click Submit to save your changes and update the selected timesheets. ​ Errors: The first valid timesheet is always taken as the reference. After that, any errors are added based on the following conditions: Approved timesheets are excluded. Timesheets with different periods are excluded. Timesheets with different settings (workdays or method of logging hours) are excluded. Timesheets from different jobs are excluded. Timesheets where the user does not have edit access are excluded. Roles and Permissions: Based on edit access for the candidate, you can edit their timesheets. This includes bulk adding time, approving, and rejecting entries. ​ If you would like to learn more about this feature, you can book a quick call with our team through this link . FAQs Can I add different time entries for different contractors at once? Yes. Each contractor is listed with their respective timesheet period in the bulk entry modal. You can update individually or use Copy to All for consistency. Is overtime shown when adding time? Can I also add a remark Yes. Overtime is automatically displayed based on the rule template that was applied when the timesheet was created. You can also add remarks while entering or updating time. ​ What happens if a submitted or rejected timesheet is selected, and it already has values? The values from those timesheets will be pre-populated, and you can edit or update them as needed before resubmitting. If any remarks are added, those also will be populated. Can I submit timesheets in bulk if no time has been filled for any period? No. For all the selected periods, at least one day must have a time entry. If no entries exist, the timesheets cannot be submitted. Hope this helps! Related Articles How to Create and Manage Timesheets? b: Sending emails one by one can become very time-consuming. To help you save time we've built a simple bulk email feature :) 📧 How to bulk email candidates/contacts? 1. Navigate to the candidates / contacts list page and select the candidates/contacts to whom you want to send an email. 2. Select ' Email ' from the available options on the header bar. 3. Compose your email, you can also use email templates and add placeholders to make the email more personalized. You can add attachments, save drafts and schedule emails to be sent out later: ​ You can also send bulk emails directly from a hotlist, just like you would with other bulk options. Simply access the hotlist you wish to use , select the records you want to email, and you’ll see the options for bulk emailing them. Attach files to emails from Recruit CRM's "Saved Files" section: Click here to learn how to save files in the Files section To add files from the "Saved Files" section, you can click on the arrow button beside the 'Upload From Device' option and then click on the 'Select From Saved Files' option. You will be able to see up to 15 recently used files. You can search for the specific record(s) by using the search bar and then select the record(s). After that click on the 'Search' button. You'll be able to see all the files related to that specific record. You can also preview the files by clicking on the file name. You can select the desired files by clicking on the 'Add Files' option. You can search files from multiple profiles to add to your email. Once you select all the files, click on 'Done'. Now your selected files will be added to the email :) ​ Click here to learn how to create email templates You can give the recipients the option to be excluded from future email communications by enabling the opt-out/unsubscribe link. 2. Inside the candidate/contact profile Click on the name of any record on the candidate/contact list page: ​ Once the profile opens, click on the Email ID and the compose email pop-up will immediately appear. ​ ​ You can also store additional Email IDs on records by creating a custom field with the field type "Email ID". Once you click on the secondary ID, you'll also be redirected to the compose email pop-up. ​ Attach files to emails from your local device or from Recruit CRM's "Saved Files" section: 1. From your local device: You can click on the 'Upload from Device' button to directly upload files from your local device. After adding the files, you can see them at the bottom of the email 2. From Recruit CRM's "Saved Files" section: To add files from the "Saved Files" section, you can click on the arrow button beside the 'Upload From Device' option and then click on the 'Select From Saved Files' option. You will be able to see up to 15 recently used files. You can search for the specific record(s) by using the search bar and select the record(s). After that click on the 'Search' button. Then you can see all the files related to that specific record. Note : You can also preview the files by clicking on the file name Now you can select the desired files and then click on the 'Add Files' option. You can search for other profiles as well and once you select all the required files from various profiles click on 'Done'. By default, you will be taken to the Kanban view but you can switch between the Kanban view and the list view . 4. Select the desired candidates and click on the 'Compose Email' option from the available options on the header bar: 5. Compose your email and click 'Send'. 🤖 Use AI to compose emails You can use Recruit CRM's AI assist to draft emails and replies to your candidates and clients. Whether you're starting a new email or responding to one, our AI tool helps you communicate effectively and efficiently. 👉 Here's how you can do this: Open the pop-up to compose an email. In it, you'll see an option called "AI Assist". Once you click on it, you'll have different possibilities to use the AI to compose an email. Let's go through all of them: You can select from one of our ready-made suggestions to immediately draft an email: ​ You can type in a prompt to indicate the topics you wish the AI to write about: ​ You can also use voice commands to speak your prompt by clicking on the microphone icon. You can select from one of our nine supported languages. You can select the tone of the email from formal, casual, friendly or neutral. ​ Users can include placeholders in the emails, however, we recommend replacing the AI-generated placeholders with the placeholder from the dropdown to avoid potential errors. Please refer to the video for more context. After inserting your prompt, you can save it by clicking the "Save" icon. You will be asked to name your prompt and you can decide whether you want to share it with your teammates or not. Don't forget to hit "Save"! The prompts will be stored in the "Saved Prompts" section, which will help you save time writing manual prompts for specific needs. By clicking on "Saved Prompts", you'll also be able to pin and unpin the prompts you have saved. AI Assist FAQs What languages does this feature support? The AI-Assisted Email Template Creation feature currently supports the following languages: English Deutsch Français Dutch Español Português Japanese Finnish Is there any limit to the number of prompts I can save? The limit of prompts that can be saved is 50. How many prompts can be pinned? You can pin up to 10 prompts. Is there any limit on this feature? The AI-Assist feature has a monthly token limit. Users on the free plan will get 50k/user/month, while users on a paid subscription get 2 million/user/month. What happens if I reach the token limit? If users reach the token limit, the AI-assist features will stop generating new content until the next monthly cycle begins. If that happens, you will get this error: Oops! It seems you have exhausted your 2 million token limit for this month. It will be restored on {date} Why do placeholders need to be updated by the user? Recruit CRM placeholders have a specific format, like {candidate_name}, {candidate_city}, etc. However, AI may generate different results in terms of placeholders, such as [candidate_fullname], or , etc. ​ Therefore, users are advised to update the placeholders using the placeholder dropdown to avoid issues. If placeholders are incorrectly added, they will not work. 🔍 How many bulk emails can be sent at a time? While Recruit CRM allows you to send an email shot to 500 candidates/contacts at a time, it is important to understand that most email service providers (like Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, etc.) impose certain restrictions on the number or volume of emails that can be sent in a single batch AND/OR within a day . It's advisable to keep your email batches relatively small, typically no more than 30 to 50 emails at a time, based on the restrictions set by your email service providers. After sending each batch, we recommend waiting for a 20 to 30-minute interval before dispatching the next set of emails. This strategy can lower the risk of your email account being flagged by your service provider, thus reducing the chances of these emails landing in the spam folder of your candidates or contacts. Click here to know more about it! If your emails are still going to the SPAM/JUNK folder of your recipients, please turn Off the Email Tracking Pixel from the Profile Settings . b: What this feature does & when to use it? The bulk email feature in Recruit CRM lets you send personalised emails to multiple candidates or contacts at once, with each recipient receiving an individual email. You can use templates, placeholders, attachments, scheduling, AI Assist, and saved prompts to streamline your communication. Use this feature when you want to: Email multiple recipients about a job or an update. Reach candidates linked to a job or hotlist Note: When sending bulk emails from Recruit CRM, each recipient receives an individual, personalized email. Recipients cannot see each other’s email addresses, ensuring complete privacy. While drafting the email, you may see all names listed together, but each email is sent separately as a blind email to each recipient. 📧 How to bulk email candidates/contacts? To send a bulk email, navigate to the Candidates or Contacts list page and select the records you want to email. Once selected, click on Compose Email from the header bar. If any of the selected records are missing an email address, a validation box will appear highlighting those records. To add an email address, hover over the “Not Available” tag, click the pencil icon, enter the correct email, and save it. Please note that any email added here will also be saved as the record’s primary email. If you prefer, you can click Continue to proceed without adding missing emails. Once all required emails are added, you will be redirected to the Compose Email screen. If all selected records already have email addresses, you will be taken directly to the Compose Email screen. Here, you can draft your email, use templates, and add placeholders to personalise your message. You can also add attachments, save the email as a draft, or schedule it to be sent later. Additionally, you can send bulk emails from a hotlist by opening the desired hotlist, selecting the records, and choosing the bulk email option. You also have the option to enable the opt-out/unsubscribe link , allowing recipients to opt out of future communications. Click here to learn how to create email templates 2. Send an Email from an Individual Candidate/Contact Profile From the Candidate/Contact list, click the name of a record to open their profile. Click on the Email ID field; the Compose Email pop-up will open immediately for that specific contact. You can store additional email addresses by creating a custom field of type Email ID . When you click a secondary email ID, you will also be redirected to the Compose Email pop-up for that address. 3. Attach Files from Your Local Device or Recruit CRM's "Saved Files" section When composing an email, you can attach files stored on your local device. Click Upload from Device to select and upload files. After uploading, the attached files will appear at the bottom of the email. Attach files from the Recruit CRM Saved Files. To attach files already stored in Recruit CRM, click the arrow next to Upload from Device and select Select from Saved Files . You will see up to 15 recently used files. You can: Search for specific records using the search bar Click Search to list files related to that record Then: You will see all files associated with that record. You can preview any file by clicking its name. Select the desired files and click Add Files . You can repeat this process for other profiles. Once you have selected all required files, click Done . All chosen files will be attached to your email. Note : You can also preview the files by clicking on the file name. When composing an email, select which connected email account you want to send from. Note: Connecting multiple mailboxes and choosing the “From” account is only available for users on the Business plan. After confirming your content, attachments, and sender address, click Send . The system sends a separate email to each recipient in the To section, ensuring that no recipient can see any other recipient’s email address. 4. Bulk Email Candidates for a Specific Job Navigate to your Jobs list page and click on the job you’re interested in. Under the Candidate Pipeline tab, click View All . By default, you will see the Kanban view, but you can switch between Kanban and List views as needed. Select the candidates you want to email and click Compose Email from the header bar. Compose your email and click Send to bulk email candidates associated with that job. 5. Use AI Assist to Compose Emails You can use Recruit CRM’s AI assistant to draft new emails or replies to candidates and clients. Once you open the Compose Email pop-up, click AI Assist to open AI options. You can then: Choose from ready-made AI suggestions to instantly draft an email. Type a prompt describing what you want the AI to write. Use voice commands by clicking the microphone icon and speaking your prompt. Choose from nine supported languages. Select the tone: formal, casual, friendly, or neutral. You can include placeholders in AI-generated content, but it is recommended to replace AI-generated placeholders with official placeholders from the dropdown to avoid errors. After entering your prompt in AI Assist, you can save it for future use by clicking the Save icon. You will be prompted to name your prompt and choose whether to share it with your teammates. Saved prompts appear in the Saved Prompts section, helping you avoid rewriting prompts for recurring needs. By clicking on saved prompts, you can also pin or unpin them for quicker access. Click here to know more about it! If your emails are still going to the SPAM/JUNK folder of your recipients, please turn off the Email Tracking Pixel from the Profile Settings . Troubleshooting Problem: Some selected candidates/contacts did not receive the bulk email. Likely cause: Their records were missing email IDs at the time of sending. ​What to check: Whether those records appeared in the validation box for missing emails. If you clicked Continue without adding email IDs. ​Resolution path: Update the missing email IDs in the relevant records. Re-run the bulk email to include those updated records. Problem: AI Assist output includes placeholders that do not work correctly. ​Likely cause: AI-generated placeholder text does not match Recruit CRM’s official placeholder format. ​What to check: The placeholders used in the AI-generated email body. ​Resolution path: Replace AI-generated placeholders with default placeholders from the dropdown menu in the email composer. Re-run AI Assist if needed and then manually insert default placeholders. FAQs 1. How many bulk emails can be sent at a time? While Recruit CRM allows you to send an email shot to 500 candidates/contacts at a time, it is important to understand that most email service providers (like Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, etc.) impose certain restrictions on the number or volume of emails that can be sent in a single batch AND/OR within a day . It's advisable to keep your email batches relatively small, typically no more than 30 to 50 emails at a time, based on the restrictions set by your email service providers. After sending each batch, we recommend waiting for a 20 to 30-minute interval before dispatching the next set of emails. This strategy can lower the risk of your email account being flagged by your service provider, thus reducing the chances of these emails landing in the spam folder of your candidates or contacts. Conclusion: Bulk emailing in Recruit CRM helps you communicate quickly with multiple candidates and contacts while keeping each message personalized. b: What this feature does & when to use it? The bulk export candidate files feature allows you to export/download files for multiple candidates at once from the Candidate List page. You can export all files, only resumes, job-associated documents, or specific custom file fields. The export runs in the background, and you’ll be notified in-app and via email once it’s ready. Use this when you need to download resumes in bulk, export job-related documents, create a backup of candidate files, or extract file data for reporting or sharing. Step-by-step instructions 1. To begin the export process, navigate to the candidate list page. Use the checkboxes to the left to bulk-select the records you wish to export. 2. Once you've made your selections, click on Export button from the top bar. 3. Scroll to the bottom of the export pop-up to locate the file fields section, where you can choose the specific files you want to export. Export All Files: Select All Files to export every file stored in the candidate's profile, including resumes, job-associated documents, custom file fields, and profile pictures. Export Only Resume Files: Selecting Resume will export all files currently under the default resume field for the candidate. Export Job-Associated Files: Select this option to export files submitted through the job application form, such as cover letters and other job-specific file fields. Export Individual Custom File Fields: Besides the fields already mentioned, you can access all the file-type custom fields here so you can export them selectively. 4. When ready, click the Export button. A confirmation message will pop up. 5. After initiating the export, you will receive an in-app notification once the files are ready for download. 6. Additionally, an email will be sent to you from support@recruitcrm.io when your data files are prepared. The process may take a few minutes, depending on the file size. Note: Please note that the download link for the exported file expires in three days. Ensure you download your files before they expire. You can export files for up to 1,000 candidates at a time. If you attempt to export files for more than a thousand records, only the first thousand candidates' files will be processed. Troubleshooting Problem: The export email has not arrived. Likely cause: Processing is still ongoing, or the email is filtered. What to check: Check the in-app notification center to see if the export is completed. Check your spam/junk folder for emails from support@recruitcrm.io . Resolution path: Wait a few more minutes for large exports. Whitelist support@recruitcrm.io in your email system if needed and retry the export. Problem: Not all selected candidates’ files are included in the export. Likely cause: More than 1,000 candidates were selected. What to check: check how many candidate records were selected on the Candidate List. Resolution path: Re-run the export with a maximum of 1,000 candidates at a time. If needed, split your selection into multiple exports. Problem: The download link in the email no longer works. Likely cause: The link has expired. What to check: Confirm whether it has been more than three days since you received the email. Resolution path: Repeat the bulk export from the Candidate List to generate a new file and a fresh link. FAQs Q1. Can I export files for more than 1,000 candidates at once? No. You can export up to 1,000 candidate files at a time. If you select more than 1,000 records, only the first 1,000 candidates’ files will be processed. Run multiple exports if you need more. Q2. How long does the bulk export take? The process may take a few minutes, depending on the file size and number of candidates. You will receive both an in-app notification and an email from support@recruitcrm.io when the export is ready. Conclusion: Bulk exporting candidate files lets you quickly download resumes, job-associated documents, custom field files, or all files for up to 1,000 candidates at once. t: Bulk Importing Jobs into Recruit CRM
s: This article will help you import job records to Recruit CRM from a CSV/XLS file.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin:
How to import your spreadsheet to Recruit CRM?
Map your columns to Recruit CRM fields
Use mapping templates (edit or delete)
Key mapping rules and options
Finalize the import (Add to Hot List or Import Now):
How does the Contact & Company matching work?
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The bulk job import feature lets you upload a CSV or XLS file with job data in Recruit CRM to create multiple job records at once. You can use this feature when: Migrating data from another ATS or CRM into Recruit CRM. You want to upload a large number of jobs at once instead of creating them manually. Before you begin: If you have a file in XLSX format, you'll first need to convert it into XLS. ​ Here's how you can do this Before you import a file, please make sure it has column headers . If your spreadsheet has additional columns that are not available in Recruit CRM, you first need to create custom fields to map those columns into the system. Special characters like "<,>, & OR;" present in the file, crash the code for import. You need to remove these before importing the file. We do not have the option to import profile pictures into the CRM. You can add up to 500 jobs in one go. Ensure that the date fields follow the DD/MM/YYYY format. 🗒️ How to import your spreadsheet to Recruit CRM? Navigate to the Jobs section in Recruit CRM. ​ Locate the Add Job button. ​ Click the dropdown arrow on the right side of the Add Job button. ​ From the dropdown menu, select Import CSV/XLS . ​ In the file upload dialog, choose the CSV or XLS file that contains your job data and upload it. Map your columns to Recruit CRM fields After the file is uploaded, proceed to the field mapping screen. ​ For each column in your spreadsheet, select the corresponding Recruit CRM field from the dropdown list. Mapping your Recruit CRM fields with the columns in your CSV/XLS file is crucial to make sure that the information in those columns is correctly saved in Recruit CRM. ​ When you upload a file and reach the field mapping stage, ensure that after completing the mapping process, you click on the "Save Mapping" button: It will allow you to save the mapping fields as a template. This way, you can easily select it each time you upload a file, eliminating the need to manually map the fields every time. Use mapping templates (edit or delete) On the mapping screen, hover your cursor over the mapping template you want to update. ​ To edit a template, click the pencil (edit) icon. ​ To delete a template, click the trash can (delete) icon. ​ Only the creator of a mapping template can edit or delete that template. Key mapping rules and options If there are columns in your spreadsheet that you do not want to import, select Don’t Import This Column from the field dropdown for those specific columns. Once a Recruit CRM field has been mapped to a column, it will no longer appear as an option in the dropdown for other columns, preventing duplicate mapping. Always verify that the data type of the column (text, number, date) matches the data type of the Recruit CRM field you select. If needed, revisit your custom fields in Recruit CRM and create new ones before attempting to map unmatched columns again. If you choose the "Include First (Header) Row of CSV or XLS file" option, you won't be able to save the template. This is because selecting this option indicates that there are no columns (column names) available for mapping, rendering the template unable to identify which columns to map. Finalize the import (Add to Hot List or Import Now): After completing all field mappings, proceed to the final step of the import process. ​ Choose Add to Hotlist if you want to tag the imported records into a specific hot list immediately after import. On the Hotlist page, you can select from existing hotlists in your account or create a new hotlist. ​ Choose Import Now if you want to directly import all records into Recruit CRM without assigning them to a hot list. 🗒️ How does the Contact & Company matching work? IF THEN If the Company Name matches exactly with an existing Company The Job is linked to that Company . If the Company Name does not match any existing Company A new Company is created and linked to the Job . If the Contact's Email is provided and matches an existing Contact’s Email The Job is linked to that Contact . If the Contact's Email is not provided The system searches for the Contact by First and Last Name (only under the mentioned Company ). If a matching Contact is found based on First and Last name The Job is linked to that Contact . If a matching Contact is found by Email but that isn’t linked to the mentioned Company The Contact is linked to the mentioned Company , and then linked to the Job. If no matching Contact is found based on Email/First and Last name A new Contact is created and linked to the Job . Troubleshooting Problem: Import fails or “crashes” Likely cause: The file contains unsupported special characters or formatting issues. What to check: Look for special characters such as less than (<), greater than (>), and “and/or” symbols in the data. Confirm that date fields follow the DD/MM/YYYY format. Resolution: Remove or replace the problematic special characters in the spreadsheet. Correct any dates that do not follow the required format and re-import the file. Problem: A column cannot be mapped to any existing field Likely cause: There is no standard Recruit CRM field that matches the data in that column. What to check: Review available standard fields on the mapping screen. Resolution: Create a custom field in Recruit CRM that matches the data type and purpose of the column. Return to the import process and map the column to the new custom field. FAQs Can I import profile pictures with my job records? No, importing profile pictures into the CRM is not supported via the bulk import process. Conclusion: Bulk importing jobs into Recruit CRM allows you to migrate and manage large volumes of job data quickly, as long as your file is clean, correctly formatted, and carefully mapped. s: This article will help you import candidates/contacts/companies records to Recruit CRM from a CSV/XLS file.
h: What this feature does and when to use this feature?
Before you begin:
Step-by-step instructions
Troubleshooting

FAQs
Can I import more than 10,000 records at once?
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use this feature? The bulk import feature allows you to create or update multiple records at once, helping you standardize data and reduce manual effort. You can use this feature: When you’re migrating data from another ATS/ CRM tool or from a spreadsheet. When you need to add candidates/contacts/companies at once in bulk. When you’re cleaning and re-importing data with updated information. Before you begin: If you have a file in XLSX format, you'll first need to convert it into XLS. ​ Here's how you can do this Before you import a file, please make sure it has column headers . If your spreadsheet has additional columns that are not available in Recruit CRM, you first need to create custom fields to map those columns into the system. Special characters like "<,>, & OR;" present in the file, crash the code for import. You need to remove these before importing the file. We do not have the option to import profile pictures into the CRM. 📋 Step-by-step instructions The process to import candidates/companies/contacts is the same. Here, we have taken the example of the Candidates Entity. 1. In Recruit CRM, navigate to the ' Candidates ' entity. 2. Click the arrow icon next to the Add Candidate button and select the 'Import CSV/XLS' option. 3. Click on the Upload File button and select your file that contains the data that needs to be imported. Note: Up to 10,000 records can be imported in a single upload. To download a sample CSV file before your import so you can format your data for easier matching, click here: 4. The next step is to map file columns to Recruit CRM fields. Mapping your Recruit CRM fields with the columns in your CSV/XLS file is crucial to make sure that the information in those columns is correctly saved in Recruit CRM. 1. After the file is uploaded, the mapping template window appears. 2. On the left side, you will see the column headers from your CSV/XLS file. On the right side, you will be able to see the available Recruit CRM fields. 3. For each column, select the most accurate corresponding Recruit CRM field to ensure data is stored correctly. 5. To make this process easier for you, we've implemented a feature that covers this step by creating mapping templates. This means you won't have to map the fields manually every single time you upload a file by having your mapping track saved in a template. To save a mapping template, follow the next steps: 1. Once all columns are mapped, you can save this configuration as a mapping template by clicking the 'Save Mapping' option. 2. Enter a name for the mapping template. If you want to share this mapping template with your teammates, turn on the sharing toggle and click the Save button to save the template. This stored template lets you apply the same field mappings to future files without redoing the mapping manually. Important: If you select the option Include first header row of CSV or XLS file , you will not be able to save a mapping template. This setting indicates there are no column names available for mapping, so the template cannot identify which columns to associate with which fields. After confirming all mappings, click Import Candidates to proceed. 6. You will now see options to merge duplicate records during the import. Recruit CRM lets you merge duplicates based on any one of the unique parameters for each entity. Those unique identifiers are: Candidates: Email ID, LinkedIn URL, or Contact Number Contacts: Contact Number Companies: Company Name, Website URL, or LinkedIn URL 1. When you click Merge Duplicates , the system prompts you to select one unique parameter to use for detecting duplicates. During import, duplicates will be merged based on the selected parameter. 2. The 'Override Data' toggle provided below allows you to choose whether imported data should override existing records in the database. Enabling the override option ensures that duplicate records in the database are updated with the latest information from the imported spreadsheet. If information is not present in the spreadsheet, existing data will remain unaffected. When the toggle is set to 'OFF', merging duplicates won't override any existing data in Recruit CRM; instead, it will solely update the empty fields on the record with new information present in the CSV. After configuring these options, click Confirm Merge . 7. After confirming merge settings, you will see two options: Add to Hotlist or Import Now . If you do not want to add the records to a Hotlist, select No, Import Now . If you choose the “ Add to Hotlist ” option, you will see all existing Hotlists in your account and will have the option to create a new one as well. 8. Click the Import button to begin importing all records. Depending on the size of your file, the import may take a few minutes. 9. When completed, look for an Import Successful notification to confirm success. You have the flexibility to include both companies and their corresponding contacts within the same CSV/XLS sheet. This allows for the seamless import of both company details and the associated contacts working within those companies into your database in one go. When bulk importing companies, it's important to understand even if you opt for the 'Do Not Merge' option, the system automatically merges the companies from the backend based on unique parameters i.e. Name, Website URL, and LinkedIn URL. Opting for the 'Merge Duplicates' option enables you to merge the contacts being imported along with the companies, based on the unique parameters i.e. Email ID or LinkedIn URL . Troubleshooting Problem: Import fails or shows “Import Failed” / “Import Unsuccessful” message. Likely cause: File formatting issues or unsupported characters. Here is what to check: Confirm the file is CSV or XLS (not XLSX) and is under 10,000 records. Look for special characters, merged cells, or formulas in the file. Ensure the first row is a header row, not data. Resolution path: Clean the file (remove special characters, merged cells, and formulas). Re-save as CSV or XLS. Try the import again. 🤔FAQs Can I import more than 10,000 records at once? No. A single import supports up to 10,000 records. For larger datasets, split your file into multiple smaller files and run separate imports. Conclusion: Bulk importing records from CSV or XLS into Recruit CRM lets you quickly populate and update your database while controlling field mapping and duplicate handling. By preparing your file carefully and following the steps in this guide, you can complete reliable imports that keep your data accurate and usable. If you need help at any stage, reach out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance. Special characters like "<,>, & OR;" present in the file, crash the code for import. You need to remove these before importing the file. We do not have the option to import profile pictures into the CRM. 📋 Step-by-step instructions The process to import candidates/companies/contacts is the same. Here, we have taken the example of the Candidates Entity. 1. In Recruit CRM, navigate to the ' Candidates ' entity. 2. Click the arrow icon next to the Add Candidate button and select the 'Import CSV/XLS' option. 3. Click on the Upload File button and select your file that contains the data that needs to be imported. Note: Up to 10,000 records can be imported in a single upload. To download a sample CSV file before your import so you can format your data for easier matching, click here: 5. The next step is to map file columns to Recruit CRM fields. Mapping your Recruit CRM fields with the columns in your CSV/XLS file is crucial to make sure that the information in those columns is correctly saved in Recruit CRM. 1. After the file is uploaded, the mapping template window appears. 2. On the left side, you will see the column headers from your CSV/XLS file. On the right side, you will be able to see the available Recruit CRM fields. 3. For each column, select the most accurate corresponding Recruit CRM field to ensure data is stored correctly. 6. To make this process easier for you, we've implemented a feature that covers this step by creating mapping templates. This means you won't have to map the fields manually every single time you upload a file by having your mapping track saved in a template. To save a mapping template, follow the next steps: Once all columns are mapped, you can save this configuration as a mapping template by clicking the 'Save Mapping' option. 2. Enter a name for the mapping template. If you want to share this mapping template with your teammates, turn on the sharing toggle and click the Save button to save the template. This stored template lets you apply the same field mappings to future files without redoing the mapping manually. Important: If you select the option Include first header row of CSV or XLS file , you will not be able to save a mapping template. This setting indicates there are no column names available for mapping, so the template cannot identify which columns to associate with which fields. After confirming all mappings, click Import Candidates to proceed. 8. You will now see options to merge duplicate records during the import. Recruit CRM lets you merge duplicates based on any one of the unique parameters for each entity. Those unique identifiers are: Candidates: Email ID, LinkedIn URL, or Contact Number Contacts: Contact Number Companies: Company Name, Website URL, or LinkedIn URL 1. When you click Merge Duplicates , the system prompts you to select one unique parameter to use for detecting duplicates. During import, duplicates will be merged based on the selected parameter. 2. The 'Override Data' toggle provided below allows you to choose whether imported data should override existing records in the database. Enabling the override option ensures that duplicate records in the database are updated with the latest information from the imported spreadsheet. If information is not present in the spreadsheet, existing data will remain unaffected. When the toggle is set to 'OFF', merging duplicates won't override any existing data in Recruit CRM; instead, it will solely update the empty fields on the record with new information present in the CSV. After configuring these options, click Confirm Merge . 9. After confirming merge settings, you will see two options: Add to Hotlist or Import Now . If you do not want to add the records to a Hotlist, select No, Import Now . If you choose the “ Add to Hotlist ” option, you will see all existing Hotlists in your account and will have the option to create a new one as well. 10. Click the Import button to begin importing all records. Depending on the size of your file, the import may take a few minutes. 11. When completed, look for an Import Successful notification to confirm success. You have the flexibility to include both companies and their corresponding contacts within the same CSV/XLS sheet. This allows for the seamless import of both company details and the associated contacts working within those companies into your database in one go. When bulk importing companies, it's important to understand even if you opt for the 'Do Not Merge' option, the system automatically merges the companies from the backend based on unique parameters i.e. Name, Website URL, and LinkedIn URL. Opting for the 'Merge Duplicates' option enables you to merge the contacts being imported along with the companies, based on the unique parameters i.e. Email ID or LinkedIn URL . Troubleshooting Problem: Import fails or shows “Import Failed” / “Import Unsuccessful.” message. Likely cause: File formatting issues or unsupported characters. Here is what to check: Confirm the file is CSV or XLS (not XLSX) and is under 10,000 records. Look for special characters, merged cells, or formulas in the file. Ensure the first row is a header row, not data. Resolution path: Clean the file (remove special characters, merged cells, and formulas). Re-save as CSV or XLS. Try the import again. 🤔FAQs Can I import more than 10,000 records at once? No. A single import supports up to 10,000 records. For larger datasets, split your file into multiple smaller files and run separate imports. Conclusion: Bulk importing records from CSV or XLS into Recruit CRM lets you quickly populate and update your database while controlling field mapping and duplicate handling. By preparing your file carefully and following the steps in this guide, you can complete reliable imports that keep your data accurate and usable. If you need help at any stage, reach out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance. s: Learn how to send bulk texts to candidates and contacts.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
Step-by-step instructions
Troubleshooting
FAQs
Conclusion:
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Bulk texting in Recruit CRM lets you send a single SMS message to multiple selected candidates or contacts at once. The feature supports up to 300 words per bulk text, allows you to use SMS templates and placeholders, and lets you include opt-out text and create follow-up tasks as part of the workflow. You can use this when: You want to quickly reach multiple candidates with the same update or reminder. You need to send bulk messages to contacts for coordination or follow-ups. You are running campaigns that require simple, short, text-based communication. Before you begin Bulk texting is available on all paid Recruit CRM plans: Pro, Business, and Enterprise. All users from the US must obtain consent from each prospect before texting them. Ensure that the candidates or contacts you want to message have valid phone numbers. Confirm that the phone numbers are in countries where texting is allowed. Make sure you have sufficient phone calling and SMS credits, as bulk texting will be charged according to Twilio’s volume pricing. Click here to learn more about Texting Cost Overview. Step-by-step instructions Go to the candidate or contact list page where your target records are listed. ​ Select the candidates or contacts you want to send bulk text messages to. ​ Click on the message icon to open the messaging options. ​ From the three options that appear, choose whether to send SMS, request consent via SMS, or request consent via mail. ​ Check for any errors in the phone numbers and verify that they are valid numbers in countries where texting is allowed. ​ Click on the “Continue with the Candidates” option to proceed with the selected recipients. ​ Recruit CRM now checks for SMS consent when sending messages in bulk. Candidates/Contacts without recorded consent will show an “SMS consent pending” validation and must have their consent recorded before they can receive bulk SMS messages. 7. Write the body of the text message, keeping in mind that you can text up to 300 words in bulk at a time. ​ 8. Insert existing SMS templates into your message if you want to reuse saved content. Create new SMS templates if you need reusable content for future bulk messages. Use placeholders to personalize your SMS content with dynamic fields such as candidate or contact details. ​ 9. Choose whether to include an opt-out option in the text message so recipients can stop receiving further texts. ​ 10. Select the option to create a follow-up task related to the bulk SMS if you want to track next steps. ​ 11. Click the “Send SMS” button to send your bulk text. ​ 12. Review the pop-up that appears, which states that you will be charged 0.05 for each unique recipient per month and that this will be deducted from your phone calling and SMS credits according to Twilio’s volume pricing. ​ 13. After sending, note that you will also be charged for failed messages, and these will be visible under the message logs. Troubleshooting Problem: Bulk SMS fails for multiple recipients and shows as failed in message logs. Likely cause: Issues with phone number validity, carrier restrictions, or insufficient credits. ​ What to check: Look at the message logs to see which messages failed and confirm your current phone calling and SMS credit balance. ​ Resolution: Fix invalid numbers where possible, confirm that the destination countries allow texting, top up your credits if needed, and attempt sending again. FAQs Q1. How many words can I send in a single bulk SMS? You can send up to 300 words in bulk at a time. Conclusion: Bulk texting in Recruit CRM makes it easy to reach many candidates and contacts at once while staying within plan limits and consent requirements. It expands Recruit CRM's core functionality with features that help streamline recruiting workflows, improve collaboration, enhance reporting, and integrate with external tools. Use this plan when: You need to store and manage larger volumes of candidate, contact, and company records. You want advanced customization for roles, teams, pipelines, and custom fields. You need additional security features such as IP whitelisting and Single Sign-On (SSO). Our "Business Plan" has: ​ 1. Record and Entity limit The business plan allows you to add up to 20,000 records for candidates, contacts, and companies each. This ensures that you can independently manage large datasets across different categories without overlapping constraints. 2. CV/Resume Formatting Effortlessly customize and brand your resumes/CVs with our CV formatting tool, featuring personalized headers, footers, watermarks, and text redaction 3. Posting directly to job boards without having to create an account with them (job marketplace). 22. Create and access templates for notes, call logs, and tasks: You can create and customize upto 100 activity templates for notes, call logs and tasks. 26. Data Enrichment : The Data Enrichment feature helps users find missing email addresses and phone numbers for candidates or contacts using their LinkedIn profiles. t: Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM
s: This article will give you guidelines about what you'll need to consider before recording calls
h: United States (U.S.)
United Kingdom (U.K.)
Ireland
Canada
Rest of the world
Conclusion:
b: The call recording feature in Recruit CRM allows you to keep track of calls with candidates and contacts, making follow-ups easier and helping your team stay up to date. Before recording calls, it is important to understand the consent requirements that may apply based on the location of the people involved. Some countries or states require consent from more than one party before a call can be recorded. If a candidate or contact is associated with a region where more than one party’s consent is required, Recruit CRM automatically disables call recording. When you click the Record button, a dialog box will appear to remind you to obtain consent. You must inform the candidate/contact that you'll be recording this call, then click "I have taken consent" to continue recording the call. This guide is useful when: You plan to record calls with candidates or contacts. You need to understand when consent may be required before recording a call. You are calling candidates or contacts who may be located in different countries or states. You want to understand why call recording may be unavailable for certain contacts or regions. Country-wise requirements: United States (U.S.) In the majority of U.S. states, you'll only need consent from one of the persons participating in a call in order to record it (this is often referred to as "one-party consent"). Since you're opting to record the call you're placing, and presumably, you consent to your own recording of the call, you won't need to do anything else to comply with the laws of those types of states. However, approximately 13 states have chosen to require all parties' consent (sometimes called "two-party consent") in order to record the call. These states are currently California, Connecticut, Delaware*, Florida, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, Nevada, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania, Vermont*, and Washington State. For more general information on the subject, refer to Wikipedia's page on telephone recording laws on the basics of state recording laws. *Recruit CRM has chosen to include Delaware and Vermont on this list because they're tricky cases: Delaware has some conflicting laws about how many parties need to consent, and Vermont doesn't have specific laws on the subject but, does have some relevant court cases. United Kingdom (U.K.) Several laws govern the practice of recording calls in the United Kingdom (U.K.). Unless you can guarantee that the call won't be shared with any third parties and is being recorded to either gather evidence, ensure regulatory compliance, or prevent crime, it's best to think of the U.K. as an "all-parties' consent" jurisdiction. Read more about the U.K.'s approach to call recording by referring to Wikipedia's page on telephone recording laws , Ofcom's page for the regulations , or VanillaIP's quick summary on the subject. Ireland Irish law is clear: to record calls, you must obtain consent, so Ireland joins the U.K. and 13 U.S. states as an "all-parties' consent" jurisdiction. Irish law makes clear that the purpose of the recording should be explained in detail, so the parties participating can give informed consent. Read more about Ireland's approach to call recording at the end of the Data Protection Commissioner's FAQ page. Canada Like Ireland, Canada has established a single set of rules for call recording, built into its electronic privacy law (PIPEDA). Joining the other countries and states mentioned above, Canada has adopted an "all-parties consent" approach: to record a call, you need to obtain informed consent by notifying others on the call (1) that you intend to record the conversation, (2) any purposes the recording will be used for, and (3) that the call may only be recorded with each person's consent. Read more about Canada's approach to call recording by referring to the Privacy Commissioner's Guidelines for Recording Customer Calls. Rest of the world While this article has chosen to highlight certain countries above, it's by no means an exhaustive list. Since Recruit CRM doesn't know and can't enforce all international calling legal restrictions, Recruit CRM opts to display this consent message for all international calls except for Sweden and New Zealand. Before making a call to a new country, Recruit CRM recommends making sure that you and your legal team have an understanding of any regulations there, and always obtain consent if you're in doubt. The countries above were chosen for informational purposes; Recruit CRM doesn't guarantee that you can use the system to call any or all of these countries. This article has provided information about the law designed to help Recruit CRM's users better understand the legal issues surrounding call recording. Legal information is not the same as legal advice, the application of the law to an individual's specific circumstances. Recruit CRM insists that you consult a lawyer if you want professional assurance that our information, and your interpretation of it, is accurate. You may not rely upon this information as legal advice nor as a recommendation or endorsement of any particular legal understanding, and you should instead regard this article as intended for informational purposes only. Conclusion: Using call recording in Recruit CRM can make follow-ups and team collaboration easier, but it must always be done in line with applicable call recording laws and consent requirements.
