t: Call Recording Permissions in Recruit CRM
s: This article explains how call recording works in Recruit CRM and how role-based permissions control access to recording features.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
Configure call recording permissions in a custom role
1. Open Users and Roles to Create or Edit a Custom Role
Configure Calling and Call Recording Permissions in the Custom Role
Change Default Call Recording from Call Settings (User Level)
How to Make a Call & Add Call Logs? 📞
How to Access the Call Logs? 🎯
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Call recording permissions in Recruit CRM control which users can: Access phone calling and recording settings. Buy calling credits . Have their calls recorded by default . Choose which calls to record . Download call recordings. You can use this feature when: You are an Account Owner setting up call recording permissions for your team. You are creating or editing a custom role and need to control who can record or download calls. You want to understand how default call recording works at the role and user level. You need to know where to find call recordings and call notes for candidates or contacts. Before you begin 1. Calling and call recording must be enabled in your Recruit CRM account. 2. Only Account Owners, Admins, and users with relevant custom role permissions can configure calling and call recording settings. Configure call recording permissions in a custom role 1. Open Users and Roles to Create or Edit a Custom Role Go to the Users section in your Recruit CRM account to manage user roles. While creating a new custom role or editing an existing one, you will be able to configure specific calling and call recording permissions for that role. ​ Configure Calling and Call Recording Permissions in the Custom Role Within the custom role permissions, locate the Calling Settings. Configure the following permissions for users with this role: 🎯Phone calling and recording : A user with this permission will be able to access the Calling Integration & Credits page to buy calling credits and manage the call recording settings. 🎯Start recording calls by default : If enabled, if a user has this permission, the recording toggle inside a record will always be enabled by default. 🎯Allow user to choose which calls to record : If enabled, the user can turn the recording toggle on or off for each call in the phone calls section. ​ 🎯Allow user to download recordings : If enabled, the user can download call recordings from the system. If a user has Start recording calls by default but does not have Allow user to choose which calls to record , the recording toggle will be on by default, and the user will not be able to turn it off. Change Default Call Recording from Call Settings (User Level) A user can also manage their default call recording behaviour from their own Call Settings page: 1. Go to Phone Calling and SMS Settings . 2. Open the Call Settings page. 3. Enable or disable the default call recording toggle as needed. ​ Please Note: Only Account Owners , Admins , and users with appropriate custom roles can access this settings page. This setting is at the user level and does not affect recording settings for the entire account. The toggle in Call Settings will override the role-based Start recording calls by default permission. Example: If a user’s role has “Start recording calls by default” enabled, but the user has access to Call Settings, they can turn the default recording toggle off there and override that permission. Click here to learn more about call recording laws that may apply to your calls. How to Make a Call & Add Call Logs? 📞 1. When you initiate a call from a record, you will hear a calling tone, and the phone will start ringing. During the call, you can take call notes on the screen . These notes will be automatically added to the Notes and Calls section in the record once saved. ​ 2. Once the call ends, a post-call screen will appear where you can: Add more details about the call (e.g., call type). Create a follow-up task if needed. Review and add to the call notes (the notes from the live call screen will already be visible here). ​ How to Access the Call Logs? 🎯 Open the relevant Candidate or Contact profile. ​ Go to the Activity section. ​ Click on the Notes and Calls tab to view call recordings (subject to your download/view permissions). All notes associated with those calls. ​ Within this area, use the Notes and Calls tab to see the full history of call activity and access the recordings. 📋 How to transcribe calls in Recruit CRM? Click here to learn how to transcribe the calls 📲 How to use the native dialer to call from the system? Click here to learn to use your native dialler for calling! Troubleshooting Problem: I can’t see the Call Settings page Likely cause: Your role does not have permission to access Phone Calling and SMS Settings. What to check: Confirm if you are an Account Owner, Admin, or have a custom role that allows access to calling settings. Resolution path: Ask an Account Owner or Admin to review your role under Users and ensure you have the correct calling permissions. Problem: Calls are recording by default, and I can’t turn them off Likely cause: Your role has Start recording calls by default enabled but does not have allow user to choose which calls to record. What to check: Ask an admin to confirm your role’s settings for: Start recording calls by default Allow user to choose which calls to record Resolution path: If appropriate, the admin can update your custom role to grant Allow user to choose which calls to record, or grant you access to Call Settings so you can override the default. Problem: I can’t download call recordings Likely cause: The Allow user to download recordings permission is not enabled for your role. What to check: In your role configuration, verify if Allow user to download recordings is turned on. Resolution path: Ask an Account Owner or Admin to edit your custom role and enable Allow user to download recordings if it aligns with your organization’s policy. Conclusion: Call recording permissions in Recruit CRM’s new UI give you fine-grained control over who can record, manage, and download calls, as well as how default recording behaves for each user. By configuring custom roles correctly and understanding user-level Call Settings, your team can capture the right call data while staying aligned with your organization’s policies. s: This article will guide you on how to customize the call type in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows you to customize call types to better match your team's workflows and communication processes. By creating personalized call type statuses, you can tag, organize, and categorize calls more effectively, making it easier to track different types of conversations, improve reporting, and streamline follow-up activities. Use this feature when: • You want to create call types that reflect your team's specific workflows. • You need a clearer way to categorize and organize calls. • You want to improve call tracking, reporting, and follow-up processes. 📌 Important: Call type customization can only be performed by users with access to the Admin Settings. On the Pro Plan , this includes the Account Owner and users with the Admin role. On the Business Plan and above , access can also be granted to custom roles. Step-by-step instructions Follow along to add custom tags for your call types: ​ 1. Go to Admin Settings > Click on Call Type Customization under CRM Process Customization. 2. Click on the " Customize" button. 3. Click Add New Status . In the blank box that appears at the bottom of the list, enter the name of your new call type (up to 50 characters). 4. You can make it your default call type by checking the box next to it. 5. Click on the "Save Status" button. Please Note - Recruit CRM allows you to have up to 30 Call Types. This offers more flexibility and options to efficiently organize and manage your communication, allowing for better categorization and streamlining of your workflow. ​ Additionally, on the Business plan, you can grant access to the "Call Type Customization" option to your team members on custom roles as well. Here's how you can do this: 1. Go to your User Management settings in the admin settings . ​ 2. Go to the " Roles & Permissions " section and click on the pencil icon next to the role you want to grant access to. 3. Now, scroll down and turn ON the toggle for "Call Type Customization" and hit the " Save Role " button. Troubleshooting Problem: Unable to see the Call Types Customization option in Admin Settings Likely cause: Your user role does not have permission to access call type customization. What to check: Confirm whether you are an account owner, admin, or a user on a custom role with call type customization enabled. Resolution: If you are not an admin or account owner, contact someone with admin access to update your role or adjust permissions. On the Business Plan, ask an admin to enable the call type customization toggle for your custom role in the Roles and Permissions section. Problem: Cannot add more call types Likely cause: The maximum number of call types has been reached. What to check: Review the total number of call types currently listed in Call Types Customization. Resolution: Remove or consolidate unused call types to free up space, then add new ones. Recruit CRM allows a maximum of thirty call types. FAQs What is the maximum number of call types I can create? Recruit CRM allows up to thirty call types. Who can customize call types on the Pro Plan? On the Pro Plan, only account owners and users with the admin role can customize call types. Who can customize call types on the Business Plan? On the Business Plan, users with access to the Admin Settings can customize call types. Additionally, Account Owners can grant call type customization access to users on custom roles. Can I set a default call type? Yes. When you add or edit a call type, you can check the box next to it to make it your default call type. Can I allow only specific team members to manage call types? Yes. On the Business Plan, you can enable the call type customization permission for selected custom roles in the Roles and Permissions section. Conclusion: Call type customization in Recruit CRM helps you better organize and categorize your calls so your team can work more efficiently. If you need further assistance with permissions or setup, contact your account admin or reach out to Recruit CRM support. t: Canceling your subscription and permanently deactivating the Recruit CRM account
s: This article will help you with the steps to cancel your subscription and deactivate the account.
h: Exporting All Your Data
Canceling Recruit CRM subscription
Deactivating the Recruit CRM account
Pausing or freezing your subscription
FAQs ❓
b: This article explains how to cancel your Recruit CRM subscription, deactivate your account, and what happens to your data at each step. You’ll also learn how you can pause your subscription instead of canceling it if you’d like to keep your data safe for future use. Exporting All Your Data Before canceling or deactivating your account, it’s important to export all your data to avoid any potential data loss. Go to admin settings and Click on " Account " ​ Choose the type of export required: To know more you can go to the article - Exporting All Data For Recruit CRM Account Owners The first step to deactivate your Recruit CRM account is to cancel the paid subscription. Note: If you have more than 10 active seats, deactivate the other users and reduce your paid licenses to see the option to cancel your subscription and deactivate the account. Canceling Recruit CRM subscription 1. Go to the admin settings and click on Account . 2. Scroll down, and click on "cancel subscription". Please make sure you don't have any pending invoices to be able to cancel the subscription. In case you have a combination of annual and monthly seats on your subscription, both subscriptions will be set to cancel on the respective renewal dates. Once you proceed to cancel your subscription, you will still have complete access to your account and all data until the end of your current subscription period. The system will also show you the date until when the subscription remains active. ​ However, after the expiry of this period, you will not be able to access any data from your account. No retrieval or management of data will be possible after this date unless you reactivate your subscription. However, after the expiry of this period, you will not be able to access any data from your account. Once you successfully cancel the subscription, your subscription for the next upcoming renewal billing will be scheduled to cancel so that you will not be charged on your next billing cycle. You can still edit your subscription after it is scheduled to cancel. You'll receive a pop-up message asking if you would like to revoke the cancellation or simply edit the subscription while it's still active: ​ You still have the option to undo your cancellation. If you’d like to continue using Recruit CRM, you can revoke the cancellation or reactivate your subscription. ​ Click the link below to learn how to revoke your subscription cancellation or reactivate your account. ​ Revoking the subscription cancelation or reactivating the subscription Deactivating the Recruit CRM account Deactivating your Recruit CRM account is easy! ​ 1. Go to the admin settings and click on Account . 2. Scroll down, and click on "Deactivate Account". Note : You can only initiate the deactivation process after your subscription has expired. For instance, if your subscription renews on 30 October of the current year but you cancel your subscription on 20 October of the current year, you will only be able to proceed with the steps to deactivate the account after the subscription expiry period i.e. on 30 October of the current year. Once you deactivate the account, your data will be stored on our servers for up to 2 months after which it will be deleted permanently. Within these 14 days, you have the option to revoke the deactivation request. Once the request is canceled, you can restart the subscription anytime! WARNING: PLEASE READ CAREFULLY BEFORE YOU PROCEED Deactivating your Recruit CRM Account will cause permanent data loss . Once you click on the deactivate button, it'll be impossible for us or for anyone to retrieve your data. Everything will be deleted from Recruit CRM such as your records, emails, resumes, notes, & any uploaded files. This action is irreversible . Whereas, canceling your subscription will store your data in the cloud servers till the time you deactivate the account. Pausing or freezing your subscription If you wish to temporarily pause your subscription instead of canceling it, please reach out to Recruit CRM Support via the chatbox. During a paused subscription period: Your data remains secure. You can access it again once you reactivate. This is ideal if you plan to return to using Recruit CRM in the near future. FAQs ❓ What happens if I decide to reactivate after cancelation or pausing? If you reactivate your subscription within the retention period (up to 2 months after the subscription ends), you can restore access to your account and data. Can I retrieve my data after the retention period? No, data retrieval is not possible once the retention period lapses. To safeguard your information, we strongly recommend exporting your data before pausing or canceling. Hope this helps! t: Candidate Lifecycle Report in Recruit CRM
s: This report will give you the complete history of candidates for any given time period.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Generate and Analyze the Candidate Lifecycle Report
Export the Report
View Candidate Details:
Review Stage Ratios:
Troubleshooting
Problem: The numbers in the Candidate Lifecycle Report do not match the current dashboard counts.
Problem: A specific stage does not appear in the Candidate Lifecycle Report.
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Candidate Lifecycle Report helps you track the complete journey/lifecycle of candidates in your Recruit CRM database over a selected time period. It provides visibility into every stage transition a candidate has gone through, making it easier to analyze hiring progress, monitor pipeline performance, and identify trends across your recruitment process. The report displays candidate movement across both Hiring Stages (for candidates assigned to jobs) and Pitch Candidate Stages (for candidates pitched directly to clients). It also includes visual charts, stage-wise candidate counts, candidate-to-stage ratios, and detailed drill-down lists that can be filtered, customized, exported, or saved for future reference. Use this feature when: • You want to track the complete lifecycle of candidates over a specific date range. • You need to analyze how many candidates progressed through each hiring or pitch stage. • You want to save frequently used report configurations for quick access in the future. Generate and Analyze the Candidate Lifecycle Report Open the Candidate Lifecycle Report from the Reports section in Recruit CRM. Select the stages you want to include in the report from the KPI dropdown option. You can choose from: • Hiring Stages – Used to analyze candidates who have been assigned to jobs. • Pitch Candidate Stages – Used to analyze candidates who have been pitched directly to clients/contacts. Select the required date range for the report. You can choose one of the predefined ranges or specify a custom date range. Click Generate Report . Once the report is generated, you'll see: • A bar chart showing the number of candidates in each selected stage. • A summary table displaying the numerical count for every stage included in the report. Export the Report You can export the report in multiple ways: • Click Export Report to CSV below the chart to download the stage-wise summary table as a CSV file. • Click the Export icon in the top-right corner of the bar chart to download the chart as an image in PNG, JPG, or SVG format. • Click any bar in the chart to open the detailed candidate list for that stage, then select Export Report to CSV to download the detailed candidate report as a CSV file. View Candidate Details: Each bar in the chart is clickable. Click any bar to open a detailed list of the candidates associated with that stage for the selected time period. ​ Within the detailed report, you can: • Review the candidate records for that stage. • Sort the data by clicking any column header. • Customize the displayed information using Edit Columns . • Apply additional filters to narrow down the results. • Perform a Boolean Search to quickly find specific records, especially when working with larger datasets. • Export the detailed candidate list to a CSV file after applying the desired filters and selecting the required columns. Review Stage Ratios: The Candidate Lifecycle Report also displays the Ratio of Candidates Assigned for each stage. ​ The ratio is calculated as: (Number of candidates in a particular stage ÷ Total number of candidates across all selected stages for the chosen time period) × 100 📌 Note: The Candidate Lifecycle Report is based on historical stage transitions for the selected date range. As a result, the figures shown in the report may differ from the current candidate counts displayed elsewhere in Recruit CRM, such as your Dashboard statistics. Troubleshooting Problem: The numbers in the Candidate Lifecycle Report do not match the current dashboard counts. Likely cause: The Candidate Lifecycle Report shows historical data based on the selected time period, while the dashboard shows current, real-time counts. ​ What to check: Confirm the date range selected in the report and compare it to the time frame represented on the dashboard. ​ Resolution: Adjust the report’s date range to match the period you want to compare, and remember that the report reflects historical transitions, not only current stage assignments. Problem: A specific stage does not appear in the Candidate Lifecycle Report. Likely cause: The stage is not selected in the stages dropdown for the report. ​ What to check: Open the Candidate Lifecycle Report and review the list of hiring stages and pitch candidate stages you have selected under the KPI section. ​ Resolution: Add the missing stage to your selection and regenerate the report. Problem: The exported CSV does not contain all the fields you expected. Likely cause: Not all desired fields were selected before exporting. ​ What to check: In the detailed list view, verify which fields are selected for export. ​ Resolution: Choose the fields again during export and generate a new CSV. FAQs What is the difference between hiring stages and pitch candidate stages in this report? Hiring stages are used when candidates are assigned to a job, while pitch candidate stages are used when candidates are pitched directly to a client without assigning them to a job. How is the ratio of candidates assigned for each stage calculated? The ratio of assigned is the number of candidates in the particular hiring stage for the time period selected/Total number of candidates across all hiring stages for the time period selected *100. Can I edit which fields appear in the detailed candidate list? Yes. In the detailed list view that opens when you click a bar, you can click Edit Columns and select the fields you want to display, and those fields will then appear in the list. In what formats can I export data from the Candidate Lifecycle Report? You can export the table as a CSV file and export the bar chart as a PNG, JPG, or SVG image. You can also export detailed candidate lists as CSV files. Conclusion: By using the Candidate Lifecycle Report , you can gain a clear understanding of how candidates progress through your recruitment pipeline over time. Whether you're reviewing stage transitions, analyzing hiring trends, exporting data for reporting, or drilling down into individual candidate records, this report provides the insights needed to make informed recruitment decisions and optimize your hiring process. t: Candidate Pitching Agent
s: Learn how to use the Candidate Pitching Agent to create and send AI-powered candidate pitch emails to your clients.
h: How to use the Candidate Pitching Agent
1. Configure the Candidate Pitching Agent
2. Select a Preset or create Custom Instructions
3. Configure Branding Options
4. Preview, Save, Regenerate, and Reset
5. Pitch Candidates to Clients
6. Generate an AI-Powered Pitch Email

b: The Candidate Pitching Agent is designed to simplify and standardize how you pitch candidates to clients. It enables you to generate AI-powered, structured, and professionally formatted candidate pitch emails directly from the pitching workflow, while allowing control over instructions, layout, branding, and candidate information through Admin Settings. It helps to: • Reduce manual effort when pitching candidates • Ensure consistency in client communication • Improve the presentation of candidates • Create professional, branded candidate pitches in just a few clicks 📌 Note: The Candidate Pitching Agent is powered by the gpt-oss-120b (Cerebras) model and generates candidate pitches using AI. As with any AI-generated content, we recommend reviewing the generated pitch for accuracy, relevance, and tone before sending it to clients. ✨ How to use the Candidate Pitching Agent The feature is designed to be simple and flexible, allowing you to either select a predefined preset layout or build a completely custom configuration based on your preferred instructions, branding, and email style. ​1. Configure the Candidate Pitching Agent Open " Admin Settings " and navigate to " Fields Shared with Clients ". ​ Click on the Candidate Pitching Agent tab from the panel on the right. From here, you can configure how candidate pitch emails are generated. 2. Select a Preset or create Custom Instructions The Candidate Pitching Agent includes built-in presets that provide predefined email layouts, styling, and AI instructions to help you get started quickly. Available presets include: • Talent Grid (Default) – A compact, data-focused layout designed for quick candidate comparisons. • Navy White (Professional) – A clean and professional layout suitable for most recruitment workflows. • Light Gold (Editorial) – A premium, editorial-style design ideal for executive search and retained recruitment. ​ When you select a preset, its corresponding AI instruction is automatically added to the instruction box. You can use the preset as-is or customize the instructions to better match your preferred tone, layout, branding, and candidate presentation style. The instruction box controls how the AI generates your pitch emails, including: • Email structure • Tone of voice • Candidate presentation style • Branding preferences • Layout and formatting expectations ​ If you edit a preset's instructions, the preset is automatically deselected and the configuration becomes a custom setup. You can also select Custom to clear the instruction box entirely and create your own instructions from scratch. The most recently saved instructions are used for all future candidate pitch emails until they are updated again. 3. Configure Branding Options Once you have configured your preset and instructions, you can choose which branding elements should be included in your candidate pitch emails. These settings help ensure that generated emails align with your company's branding and provide a more professional experience for clients. You can configure the following branding options: • Include Your Company Logo Displays the logo configured under Admin Settings → Public Job Page Settings . If no logo has been configured there, the email will be generated without a company logo even if this option is enabled. ​ • Include Contact Company Logo Displays the logo associated with the company linked to the selected contact. If a contact is associated with multiple companies, the logo from the first linked company will be used. If no company logo is available, the email layout automatically adjusts to maintain a clean appearance. ​ • Include Email Signature Automatically adds the email signature associated with the email account used to send the pitch email. For users on the Business and Enterprise plans who have multiple email accounts connected, the signature corresponding to the selected sending account will be used. ​ These branding preferences are applied to the generated candidate pitch email and are included in all future pitches once the configuration is saved. ​4. Preview, Save, Regenerate, and Reset Once your configuration is ready, click Preview to generate a sample email and review how the pitch will appear based on the selected preset, instructions, and branding settings. If you're satisfied with the output, click Save Instructions to save your configuration. This saves the selected preset, the latest instruction prompt, and branding preferences, which then become the default settings used across future candidate pitches. If the generated layout or content does not fully meet your expectations, click Regenerate to create another version using the same instructions and configuration. You can also click Reset to restore the default preset and its original instructions. ​ ​5. Pitch Candidates to Clients Once you have configured the Candidate Pitching Agent, you can begin pitching candidates to your client contacts. You can start the pitching workflow from either side of the relationship: • From Candidates – Select one or more candidates from the Candidate List or Candidate Profile, then choose the contacts you want to pitch them to. From Contacts – Select one or more contacts from the Contact List or Contact Profile, then choose the candidates you want to pitch. 📌 You can pitch up to 20 candidates at a time . After selecting your candidates and contacts, click Select Fields & Email Contacts . From here, choose which candidate information should be included in the pitch email, including the Profile Picture field if you would like candidate photos to be visible to the recipient. Once you have reviewed and finalized the fields you want to share, proceed to the email generation step. 6. Generate an AI-Powered Pitch Email On the field selection screen, you'll find the Candidate Pitch Agent toggle. • When the toggle is ON (default), clicking Generate Email creates an AI-generated pitch email based on your configured instructions, selected candidate fields, branding preferences, and chosen layout. • When the toggle is OFF , Recruit CRM uses the standard candidate pitching workflow instead. ​ 📌 The toggle remembers your most recent preference. If you turn it off, it will remain off for future pitches until you enable it again. This preference is specific to each user. ​ More about the Profile Picture Field The Profile Picture field is available under Shared Candidate Fields and allows you to control whether candidate photos are shared with clients. Like other shared fields, it supports custom labels, visibility controls, drag-and-drop reordering, and can be selected when pitching candidates. When enabled, profile pictures are included in Candidate Pitch Emails, Candidate Submission Emails, Online Candidate Lists, and the Hiring Manager Portal. When disabled, they are hidden from all client-facing experiences. ​ 📌 Note: Profile Pictures and Full Names are controlled independently, and profile pictures are only shared when the Profile Picture field is explicitly selected. ​7. Review and Edit the Email The generated email remains fully editable before sending. ​ The draft automatically includes: • Selected candidate information • Structured candidate summaries • Branding elements • Layout styling based on your saved configuration Before sending, you can: • Edit the subject line • Modify recipients • Update the email content • Adjust formatting and layout • Make any final changes to candidate summaries If you prefer not to use the AI-generated version, click Switch to Default to return to the standard candidate pitch email template at any time before sending. You can also provide feedback on the generated email using the 👍 Thumbs Up or 👎 Thumbs Down options. Selecting Thumbs Down opens a short feedback form where you can share suggestions for improvement. ​ ​ 8. Preview Emails Before Sending Whether you are sending to a single contact or multiple contacts, Recruit CRM generates a separate personalized email for each recipient. Contacts are not added as CC or BCC recipients. When you first open the Compose Email screen, placeholder values are shown instead of the contact's actual details. Clicking Preview replaces those placeholders with the details of the first selected contact and highlights the resolved values so you can clearly identify previewed content. ​ 📌 During actual sending, each recipient receives their own personalized email with their corresponding contact details automatically populated. 💡 Best Practices while writing Instructions To achieve the best results: • Be clear and specific in your instructions. • Define your preferred tone, structure, and formatting expectations. • Use a preset as a starting point if you're unsure how to structure your instructions. • Keep instructions generic so they can be reused across multiple candidate pitches. • Always preview the generated email before saving your configuration. • Save only the version of the instructions that you want applied to fut

b: What this feature does and when to use it? Candidate Questions allow you to collect information from applicants that may not be available on their resumes. You can build a reusable library of questions, assign relevant questions to specific jobs, and review candidate responses. This feature is useful when you want to: Pre-screen candidates before interviews. Collect role-specific information during the application process. Make certain questions mandatory for applicants. Reuse a library of questions across multiple jobs. Include candidate questions in Profile Update Request Forms. How to create and add Candidate Questions Go to Admin Settings and open Job Application Form Settings. In the Job Application Form field settings tab, scroll down to the Candidate Questions section and click Add Questions. Create the questions you would like candidates to answer. If required, enable the Required option for questions that applicants must answer before submitting their application. Note: Questions added to your question library in the Admin settings do NOT appear in all job application forms by default. How to add related questions inside each job? Navigate to the Jobs page and open the job where you want to add candidate questions. Click the Edit (Pencil) icon. Scroll down to the Job Application Form section and ensure the Enable Job Application Form checkbox is selected. Select the questions you want to include from the dropdown for that job. Click Save Job. Note: Questions marked as Required in Admin Settings can still be made optional for individual jobs if needed. Add candidate questions to the Profile Update Request Form You can also display Candidate Questions in the Profile Update Request Form sent to candidates. Go to Admin Settings and open Profile Update Form . In the Profile Update Form Fields tab, search for Candidate Questions. Turn on the Visibility toggle to display Candidate Questions in the Profile Update Request Form, and mark the required questions as Required, if applicable. Save your changes. How to track the questions answered by a candidate? Candidate responses to the Candidate Questions can be viewed from three different locations: 1. View responses from the Candidate Pipeline Open the desired job and, under Candidate Pipeline, click View All. Switch to List View and click the Edit Columns (Pencil) icon. Enable the Candidate Questions column and position it wherever you'd like it to appear. Click View Q&A to view the candidate's responses. 2. View responses from the Candidate Profile: Open the candidate's profile. Navigate to the Questions tab. Here you'll find all questions answered by the candidate, along with the corresponding job. 3. View responses from Job Specific Details: Open the required job. Under Candidate Pipeline, locate the candidate and click Job Specific Details. Open the Candidate Questions tab. From here, you can view and edit the candidate's responses or use the search bar to quickly find specific questions. Troubleshooting Problem: Candidates cannot see the candidate questions when applying for a job. Likely Cause: The candidate's questions have not been added to the specific job. What to Check: Confirm that the required candidate questions have been selected for that job. Remember that questions created in the library are not automatically added to every job by default. Resolution: Add the required candidate questions to the job, and save your changes. FAQ 1. Can I use the same questions for multiple jobs? Yes. Once a question is created in the Candidate Questions library, it can be added to any job application form. 2. Can required questions be made optional? Yes. Even if a question is marked as Required in Admin Settings, you can make it optional when configuring an individual job. Conclusion: Candidate Questions help you collect job-specific information during both the application and profile update processes, making it easier to evaluate applicants and maintain accurate candidate records. t: Candidate Source Tracking in Recruit Craft
s: This article will help you understand how the candidate source tracking works and help identify the source of the candidates.
h: How to use the ?source= parameter
Key Features of Source Tracking
Source detection
Smart fallback using browser referrer
Clean, readable source names
Stored in the Candidate Profile
Context-aware tagging
No overwriting on future visits
b: The Candidate Source Tracking feature automatically captures where each applicant applied from, whether it’s from LinkedIn, job boards, or your website. This allows for smarter and more informed sourcing decisions based on data. The source is recorded automatically during the application or sign-up process. 💡 How to use the ?source= parameter To track where your candidates are coming from, you can manually add the ?source= tag at the end of your job application or Candidate Portal links. For example: In this case, “Promotion” will be recorded as the candidate’s source. You can customize the value to match any platform you're using, like Facebook , EmailCampaign , CareersPage , or even a recruiter’s name. Just make sure the value is clear and easy to identify. This method is especially useful when sharing job links across multiple channels, so you can track which ones bring in the most candidates. 🎯 Key Features of Source Tracking Source detection Tracks the candidate's source using the ?source= parameter in the job application and Candidate Portal sign-up links. Smart fallback using browser referrer If the ?source= parameter is missing, the system uses the browser’s referrer (the previous webpage the user was on) to identify the source. Clean, readable source names Referrer domains like linkedin.com or indeed.com are automatically mapped to user-friendly names like “LinkedIn” or “Indeed.” Stored in the Candidate Profile The source is saved in the "Source" field of each candidate’s profile, which is very useful for filtering and reporting. Context-aware tagging Depending on how the candidate enters, the source is tagged as either: From a job application: Apply Page – [SourceName] From the Candidate Portal: Candidate Portal – [SourceName] No overwriting on future visits Once the source is recorded, it won’t change—even if the candidate returns through a different link. ❓ FAQs What if a candidate uses a link without ?source= and there’s no browser referrer? The system will still tag the context as "Apply Page" or "Candidate Portal." Can a candidate have multiple sources? No. The source is captured only once during the first visit and remains unchanged. Why use both URL parameters and referrer data? URL parameters provide more accurate tracking, especially for campaigns. Referrer data acts as a reliable backup. What if the referrer is blocked or unavailable? The system will still log the context (Apply Page or Candidate Portal), even without the source name. Will the source be retained across multi-page forms? Yes. The system preserves the source throughout the entire session. Hope this helps! b: The Candidate Submission Agent is designed to simplify and standardize how you can send candidate submission emails to clients. It enables you to generate AI-powered, structured, and professionally formatted submission emails directly from the candidate submission flow, while allowing control over instructions, layout, and branding through Admin Settings. It helps to: Reduce manual effort in drafting submission emails Ensure consistency in client communication Improve the overall presentation of candidates Note: The Candidate Submission Agent runs on the gpt-oss-120b (Cerebras) model. ✨ How to use the Candidate Submission Agent The feature is designed to be simple and flexible, allowing you to either use a ready-made format or create your own. Open " Admin Settings " and navigate to " Fields Shared with Clients ". ​ Access the Candidate Submission Agent from the panel on the right. ​ Select from one of the available presets , which provide a predefined structure and styling for your submission email. These presets help you get started quickly with a ready-made format that you can use as-is or customise further. Alternatively, you can create your own format by adding custom instructions in the Instruction box. You can also select a preset and tweak its instructions to better match your requirements. The available presets include: • Navy & White (Professional) – Clean and corporate layout with a deep navy header, white candidate cards, and blue accent labels. Best suited for formal hiring briefs in industries like finance, legal, or technology. • Dark Gold (Editorial) – Premium and editorial style with a near-black header, warm beige background, and gold accents. Ideal for executive search or boutique recruitment. • Talent Grid (Spreadsheet-Style) – Compact and data-focused layout where all candidates are displayed in a single table format. Best for internal hiring teams or quick comparison use cases. ​ Click Preview to see how the email will look. ​ If satisfied, click Save Instructions . If the generated layout does not fully match your expectations, click Regenerate to create another version using the same instructions and overall structure. ​ Please Note Saving instructions is allowed only after previewing. The AI may not always follow instructions perfectly and can sometimes produce slightly inconsistent results. We recommend previewing the generated template and refining instructions if needed. The email layout may vary slightly depending on the recipient's inbox (e.g., Gmail or Outlook). Once saved, the system keeps the structure fixed and simply fills in candidate and job data each time you send an email. ​ To use the configured template, go to the job you are working on and click on Submit Candidates . Then select Email with Attachments and Candidate Grid . Make sure the Candidate Submission Agent toggle is turned ON to generate the AI-powered submission email. The Candidate Submission Agent toggle state will persist based on the user’s last action. This behaviour is user-specific and applies across all jobs. Example: If a user turns OFF the toggle while submitting candidates for a job, the toggle will remain OFF the next time they initiate candidate submission (via Email with Attachments and Candidate Grid method) for any job, until it is manually turned ON again. You can continue with your submission process, and if needed, edit the generated email (subject, recipients, and content) before sending. ​ The candidate details shown in the email are based on the " Fields Shared with Clients " settings: Any updates made at the global level (via Admin Settings) will apply to all existing and future jobs. If fields are updated for a specific job, then the candidate submission email for that job will follow the job-specific field configuration. This ensures consistency while still allowing flexibility. ​ 🧩 Presets available The agent provides built-in templates to help you get started quickly: • Navy White (Professional): A clean and professional layout • Dark Gold (Editorial): A more premium/editorial style ​ • Talent Grid (Spreadsheet-Style): A compact grid-style format for quick comparison Selecting a preset automatically fills in the instruction field, which you can further edit if needed. You can also reset your setup back to the default preset and instructions at any time (with confirmation). Clicking on the 'Reset' option restores the default preset along with the default instruction prompt. 💡 Best practices for writing instructions To ensure your submission emails look consistent and professional, it’s important to define each part of the layout clearly. Here’s what you should cover: • Define the overall theme and colours clearly Describe the look and feel of your email (for example, corporate, minimal, or premium). Specify exactly where each colour should be used, such as the header background colour, accent elements colours (labels, borders), page background colour, and card or content background colour. Avoid vague terms like “use blue” and instead use precise values (like HEX codes) to ensure consistent results. Click here for an example instruction "The header should have a dark navy background. Use a bright blue as the accent colour for labels and borders. The page background should be a very light blue-grey. Candidate cards should have a white background with a 4px blue left border." • Specify font styles and usage across sections Mention which fonts should be used for headings, candidate names, and body text. If you want a single font throughout, state that clearly. If you prefer a mix (for example, serif for headings and sans-serif for body), define it for each section to avoid mismatched or inconsistent text styling. Click here for an example instruction "Use Arial throughout - for headings, labels, and all body text. No serif fonts anywhere." Or "Use Georgia for the candidate name and headings. Use Arial for all labels, body text, and tags." • Structure the header layout in detail The header appears at the top of every email and contains the job role name, your company name, and optionally your logo and the client's logo. Clearly define what the header should include and how it should appear. This can include a small top label, the main job title, company name, and logo placement. Also describe styling such as font size, alignment, and positioning of each element. A well-defined header ensures every email looks structured and branded. Click here for an example Instruction "The header should have a small eyebrow label at the top that always reads: CANDIDATE SHORTLIST · CONFIDENTIAL. Below that, a large heading that says 'Top Talent for' followed by the job role name on the next line in the accent colour and italic. Below the heading, a smaller line showing 'Presented by [my company name]' in grey italic. If a logo URL is provided, show it as a circular image in the top right corner of the header." • Define how candidate information should be displayed Specify whether candidates should appear as individual cards or in a table format. Also describe how each field should be shown (for example, label-value pairs, inline text, or tags), how the candidate name should be highlighted, and how each candidate section should be separated. This helps avoid issues like misaligned fields or inconsistent layouts. Click here for an example Instruction Card style: "Each candidate should appear as a separate card with a white background and a 4px blue left border. The candidate name should be the largest and most prominent element in the card. Below the name, show other details as label-value pairs - the label on the left in small uppercase blue text, and the value on the right in normal black text. Labels and values must always be on the same line, never stacked. Separate each card with a thin horizontal line." Table style: "All candidates should appear as rows in a single data table. Each column corresponds to a candidate field. The candidate name column should use a slightly larger bold font. Alternate row backgrounds between white and very light grey." • Define the overall layout style Clearly specify whether the email should follow a card-based layout, table/grid format, or any other structure to ensure consistency across all submissions. • Provide complete instructions for logo handling Clearly explain how logos should appear, including their position, shape (for example, circular), and alignment. Most importantly, define all scenarios: when both logos are present, when only one is available, and when no logos are provided. This prevents broken layouts or empty placeholders in your emails. If both a client logo and my company logo are provided, show the client logo on top and my company logo below it with a small gap between them. If only one logo is provided, sh

t: Changing A User's Role
s: Now control what your teammates have access to.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Change a user's role
Default roles in Recruit CRM:
1. Admin
2. Team Member
3. Restricted Team Member
4. Account Owner
Troubleshooting
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Changing a user's role in Recruit CRM determines the level of access and actions available to them within the system. Roles control which records users can view and manage, including candidates, companies, contacts, jobs, and deals, as well as activities such as notes, call logs, tasks, and meetings. They also define access to features like data exports and account settings. Recruit CRM's default and custom roles help ensure that users have the appropriate permissions based on their responsibilities. Use this feature when you want to: Assign roles to new team members. Limit users to viewing and managing only their own records. Change a user's role Click on Admin Settings and navigate to Users under Account Management. Locate the team member whose role you want to update by searching for their name. Once located, click the Edit (pencil) icon to the extreme right. Click the Role dropdown and select the role you want to assign to the user. Review the changes and click Update to save them. Default roles in Recruit CRM: A user's role determines the records, activities, and administrative features they can access within Recruit CRM 1. Admin An “Admin” can add records (candidates, companies, contacts, jobs), delete records (candidates, companies, contacts, jobs), view the complete database, export data from the list pages to CSV (up to 1000 records), and also have complete access to the admin panel (except Plans, Billing and API & integrations) and can invite teammates too. Admins share many permissions with account owners but have certain limitations. Admins do not have access to the roles and permission section, plans and billings, premium job boards, and API integration tokens. 2. Team Member A "Team Member" can add records (candidates, companies, contacts, jobs), view the complete database, and add/edit activities like adding notes/call logs/tasks & meetings. They CANNOT delete records and activities, export data, and also won't have access to the admin panel. When it comes to Deals, they will only be able to view and edit deals they own. 3. Restricted Team Member A "Restricted Team Member" can add records (candidates, companies, contacts, jobs), and can only view the data that they are adding to the system and not the other user's data unless they have been made "owner" or "collaborator" on the record(s), including activities (notes, call logs, etc). They cannot delete any data and WON'T have access to the admin panel. 4. Account Owner Account Owners have complete access and control over the account. Other than all the access admin shares, only account owners can purchase calling credits, change account ownership, change account currency, and access full data export. Account owners also have access to the "Sent Email Conversation" KPI in team performance reports. These permissions will also impact the user's ability to see, create, edit and delete Notes, Call Logs, Tasks and Meetings inside each entity. ​ E.g. If a user has permission to edit only candidates they own, they won't be able to edit the notes inside a candidate that belongs to someone else, even if the note was added by the user themselves. ❌ If a record from a specific entity (candidates, companies, etc.) doesn't have an owner, the user will not be able to edit or delete the Notes, Call Logs, Tasks or Meetings. Note: If you don’t see the pencil icon, try scrolling to the right to locate it. Alternatively, you can adjust the page zoom to a lower percentage, which should make the pencil icon visible as well. Different roles and permissions can be assigned to users on the Business Plan and Enterprise Plan by creating a custom role. ​ 👉 Click here to learn more about custom roles. Troubleshooting Problem: The user still cannot access certain records after their role was changed. Likely cause: The newly assigned role may not have permission to access those records or activities. What to check: Review the permissions associated with the assigned role and verify record ownership. Resolution: Assign a role with the required permissions or update record ownership if necessary. Problem: I cannot see the pencil icon to edit a user. Likely cause: The action buttons may be hidden due to screen size or browser zoom settings. What to check: Check whether you can scroll horizontally in the Users list and verify your browser zoom level. Resolution: Scroll to the right to locate the pencil icon or reduce your browser zoom level until it becomes visible. Conclusion: Changing a user's role in Recruit CRM allows you to control the level of access and permissions available to each team member. By assigning the appropriate role, you can ensure users have the visibility and actions they need while maintaining data security across your account. b: What this feature does and when to use it? Hiring Stages help you track a candidate's progress throughout your recruitment process for each job they are assigned to. You can update hiring stages from both the Candidate Profile and the Job Details page, add remarks, create follow-up tasks, and maintain an accurate hiring history. This feature is useful when you want to: Track a candidate's progress through your hiring pipeline. Update a candidate's hiring stage for a specific job. Add remarks or create follow-up tasks while changing a hiring stage. Bulk update hiring stages for multiple candidates. Update a candidate's hiring stage You can update a candidate's hiring stage from either the Candidate Profile/Details Page or the Job Details page. 1. Update the hiring stage from the Candidate Profile Navigate to the Candidate entity and open the required candidate's profile. Open the Assigned Jobs tab, locate the relevant job, and click on the candidate's current Hiring Stage . Select the appropriate hiring stage from the dropdown list. The available stages are based on your Hiring Pipeline configuration, such as Shortlisted, Assigned, Interview, Rejected, Placed, and more. You can also add a remark or create a follow-up task before saving the stage update. Note: A red dot appears on the Remark icon whenever the candidate's current hiring stage includes a remark added by either you or the client. Click the Remark icon to view the remark. When updating an individual candidate's hiring stage to Placed , you can also update the candidate's Current Salary by enabling the Update Current Salary toggle, clicking the Pencil icon, entering the updated salary, and saving the hiring stage. 2. Update the hiring stage from the Job Details page Navigate to Jobs and open the required job. Under the Candidate Pipeline tab, choose the relevant candidate and click on the candidate's current Hiring Stage . Select the appropriate stage from the dropdown menu and hit submit to save the changes You can also update hiring stages for multiple candidates; click View All from the Candidate Pipeline. List View: Click an individual candidate's hiring stage to update it, or select multiple candidates and perform a Bulk Update of their hiring stage. Kanban View: Simply drag and drop candidates between hiring stages to update their status. You can also edit remarks or delete hiring stage history entries directly from Stage History . Open the candidate's Stage History and click the three-dot (⋮) menu beside the relevant entry. Select Edit or Delete . Please note: The Edit/Delete option is not available for stages or remarks added by the client, the initial Applied or Assigned stage in the candidate's current hiring history, or the latest Assigned stage created after a candidate has been unassigned and reassigned. Troubleshooting Problem: I don't see the option to update the candidate's current salary. Likely Cause: The option is only available when changing an individual candidate's hiring stage to Placed. What to Check: Confirm that you're updating a single candidate's hiring stage to Placed. Resolution: Change the hiring stage to Placed, and the Update Current Salary option will become available. FAQs Can I update hiring stages for multiple candidates at once? Yes. From List View, you can select multiple candidates and perform a bulk update of their hiring stage. 2. Can I customize the hiring stages? Yes. Hiring stages can be customized from the Hiring Pipeline in your Admin Settings. Conclusion: Keeping hiring stages up to date helps your team accurately track every candidate's progress throughout the recruitment process. Whether you're updating an individual candidate, performing bulk updates, managing candidates from the Kanban View, or maintaining hiring stage history. b: What this feature does and when to use it? Transferring account ownership in Recruit CRM allows the current Account Owner to assign ownership of the account to another user. Since the Account Owner has access to billing, account settings, user management, and other account-level controls, transferring ownership ensures that the right person has administrative control of the account. t: Changing the status of a job
s: This article will help you manage the status of your jobs in Recruit CRM
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to Customize the Job Status
How to Change the Status of Jobs in Recruit CRM
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Job Status feature in Recruit CRM helps you efficiently track and manage the lifecycle of jobs using predefined statuses such as Open, Closed, Hold, and Canceled, while also allowing custom statuses to match specific hiring workflows. Users can update job statuses individually or in bulk, filter jobs based on status in list or Kanban view. How to Customize the Job Status Go to Admin Settings and open the Job Status section. Review the predefined job statuses available by default, such as Open, Closed, Hold, and Cancelled. To create a custom job status, click Customize . Add the new status as required and save your changes. The newly created status will then be available across job records and status dropdowns. Open indicates the jobs that are currently active. Closed indicates the jobs that are finished . Hold indicates a job that's been paused for a period of time. Cancelled indicates a job that was called off/withdrawn. Please note: These statuses can't be deleted or edited as they are used to power events in the app. How to Change the Status of Jobs in Recruit CRM 1. From the Job Details Page Open the job you want to update from the Jobs List . Click the Job Status button beside the job name. Select the required status from the dropdown menu. Additionally, you can add a remark for the update. Finally, click Submit to save the changes. All the jobs where the status is NOT "Closed" are considered Active jobs , provided you have the Job Application Form Link enabled. Those jobs will be automatically posted on free job boards like ZipRecruiter, Neuvoo, CareerJet, JobRapido, etc. ​ To ensure the jobs aren't available on the jobs page, we have two criteria: The job should be "Closed" Job Application Form should be disabled You can choose one of them. ​ Here you can read more about how it works! 2. From the Jobs List Page (Bulk Update) Go to the Jobs List and select the jobs you want to update. And click Update Field at the top of the page. Search for and select Status . Select the new status you want to apply, add a remark for the update, and click Submit to save the changes. All the selected jobs will now be seamlessly updated to the new status you’ve chosen. While changing the status of a job, you can also choose to close this job on external job boards and disable its Job Application Form. For jobs marked as 'Closed' , both checkboxes are force-checked and cannot be modified. For jobs marked as 'On Hold ' or 'Canceled' , both checkboxes are checked by default but can be manually edited. For jobs marked as 'Open' or any other custom statuses , both checkboxes remain unchecked by default and are editable. You can use the Quick View button on the List View to see all jobs with the default status (open, on hold, closed, and cancelled). In the Kanban View , you can choose which job statuses are visible and easily drag and drop jobs between stages as their status changes. Click here to learn more about the Kanban View for Jobs! Conclusion: Keeping job statuses up to date helps ensure your job records accurately reflect their current stage and availability. t: Client Performance Report
s: The Client Performance Report in Recruit CRM helps you measure business operations by comparing key performance indicators (KPIs) across your clients.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Generate and Analyze the Client Performance Report
View Detailed Records:
Export the Report:
Troubleshooting
Problem: The hiring stage numbers in the report do not match the current stages of candidates.
Problem: The report does not show some expected companies.
FAQs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Client Performance Report provides a comprehensive view of how your clients are performing across key recruitment KPIs (Key Performance Indicators). It helps you compare multiple clients, monitor hiring activities, and analyze client-specific performance over a selected time period through interactive charts and detailed reports. Use this feature when: • You want to evaluate the performance of one or more clients over a specific time period. • You need to compare multiple clients side by side using consistent recruitment KPIs. • You want to monitor hiring activities, including hiring stages, notes, tasks, meetings, candidate pitches, and contact stages associated with your clients. • You want to export client performance data for reporting, presentations, or further analysis. The report allows you to generate insights for one or more clients using a wide range of KPIs. Results are displayed through an interactive bar chart and a detailed company-wise table , making it easy to compare performance across clients. You can drill down into individual records by clicking on the bar, apply additional filters, perform Boolean searches, customize the displayed columns, and export both summary and detailed reports for further analysis. Generate and Analyze the Client Performance Report 1. Open the Client Performance Report Navigate to the Reports section from the left-hand navigation menu and open the Client Performance Report . ​ 2. Select the companies Choose the companies you want to include in the report. You can: • Search for specific companies by name. • Use filters to narrow down the company list. • Select companies from a Company Hotlist using the Quick View option. ​ After making your selections, review the list to ensure you've included the correct companies. 3. Select the KPIs Open the KPI dropdown and choose the metrics you want to analyze. Available KPIs include: • Hiring Stages • Notes • Tasks • Meetings • Pitched Candidate Stages • Contact Stages ​ 4. Select the date range Choose the required date range for the report. You can select one of the predefined ranges or specify a Custom Date Range by choosing the desired start and end dates. 5. Generate the report After reviewing your company selection, KPIs, and date range, click Generate Report . Once the report is generated, you'll see an interactive bar chart displaying the selected KPIs for each company, along with a detailed summary table below the chart. ​ Please Note : If you are seeing numbers related to any Hiring Stage (Assigned/Placed etc.), This is historical data which means, the candidates were in that hiring stage during some point in the date range the report was generated for, Their current hiring stage may be different. ​ View Detailed Records: Each bar in the chart is clickable. Click any bar to view the detailed records. ​ Export the Report: You can export the report in multiple ways: • Click Export Report to CSV to download the summary report as a CSV file. • Click the Export icon in the top-right corner of the bar chart to download it as a PNG, JPG, or SVG image. • Click any bar in the chart to open the detailed report, then select Export Report to CSV to download. ​ Troubleshooting Problem: The hiring stage numbers in the report do not match the current stages of candidates. Likely cause: The report shows historical data within the selected date range, not only current stages. What to check: Confirm the date range used when generating the report. Resolution: Remember that if you see numbers for stages like Assigned or Placed, they represent candidates who were in that stage at some point during the date range. Their current hiring stage may now be different. Problem: The report does not show some expected companies. Likely cause: The companies were not selected or were filtered out during selection. What to check: Reopen the company selector, review search terms and filters, and check the list of selected companies. Resolution: Adjust search and filters, add the missing companies to the selection, and regenerate the report. FAQs Q1: What does the Client Performance Report show? It shows a visual bar graph and detailed tables of KPIs such as hiring stages, notes, tasks, meetings, pitched candidate stages, contact stages, billable revenue, and cash collected for selected companies over a chosen date range. Q2: Can I select multiple companies in one report? Yes. You can select multiple companies directly, use the company hotlist from quick view, search for companies, and filter the list before generating a single report. Q3: Are the hiring stage numbers current or historical? They are historical. If you see numbers for stages like Assigned or Placed, they represent candidates who were in those stages at some point during the date range. Their current stages may be different. Q4: Can I customize the columns in the detailed list? Yes. In the detailed list opened from a bar, you can use the Edit Columns option to choose which fields to display. Conclusion: The Client Performance Report gives you a clear, data-driven view of how each client is performing across key hiring and activity metrics, with flexible filters, drill-downs, and exports to support deeper analysis. If you need further help interpreting the data or configuring your pipelines, reach out to Recruit CRM support for guidance. t: Client Portal for Timesheets (Beta)
s: A simple, secure way for clients to review and manage contractor timesheets.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Who can access the Client Portal?
Enable Client Portal access for timesheets
Client access control and permissions
View and manage timesheets
Timesheet approvals
Real-time synchronization
Troubleshooting
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Client Portal for Timesheets gives clients secure access to contractor timesheets associated with their jobs. Depending on the permissions granted, clients can view, create, edit, delete, and approve timesheets, with every action syncing automatically to Recruit CRM. This feature improves collaboration between agencies and clients by providing real-time visibility into contractor timesheets while maintaining complete control over client permissions. This feature is useful when you want to: Share contractor timesheets with clients. Allow clients to create, edit, or delete timesheets. Enable designated client contacts to approve timesheets. Keep all timesheet updates synchronized with Recruit CRM. Maintain a complete audit trail of timesheet activity. Please note: This feature is currently available in Beta . If you'd like to enable it for your account, please contact your Account Manager . Who can access the Client Portal? The Client Portal is available through the Hiring Manager Portal (HMP). To learn how Hiring Managers are invited, sign up, and access the portal, refer to t his article. Enable Client Portal access for timesheets Before enabling timesheet access, ensure the client contact has been added to the relevant company and is associated with the appropriate Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job in Recruit CRM. Open the required job and click Submit to Client . Select the permissions you want to grant to the client, then click Online Candidate List to activate the portal link. Once enabled, your client will be able to view shared timesheets in real time through the Hiring Manager Portal. To access the shared job, the client can open the email containing the Online Candidate List link, then click View in Portal. They will be taken to the Timesheets tab by default. Please note: If the Online Link is disabled at any time, the client's access to timesheets is removed immediately. For the best experience, ensure the client already exists as a Contact in Recruit CRM for that specific job before enabling portal access. Client access control and permissions Client access is fully controlled by your agency and is available only for Contract and Contract-to-Permanent jobs. When enabling the Online Candidate List , you can choose whether clients are allowed to: Create timesheets Edit timesheets Delete timesheets Please note: All permissions are enabled by default when Portal Access is first activated. Any changes you make are saved and applied going forward. You can update these permissions at any time if your client's responsibilities change. View and manage timesheets After signing in to the Client Portal, clients can access the Timesheets tab to review and manage all shared contractor timesheets in one place. Clients can: View timesheets for shared jobs. Filter timesheets by This Week , Last Week , This Month , or Last Month . Create new timesheets (if permitted). Edit existing timesheets by clicking the Pencil icon. Submit completed timesheets. Approve timesheets (if assigned as the approver). Each timesheet clearly displays who created, submitted, and approved it, along with the corresponding timestamps, providing a complete audit trail. Timesheets for candidates who have been deleted from the Recruit CRM remain visible in the Client Portal and are clearly marked as Deleted . While clients cannot create new timesheets for deleted candidates, they can continue viewing existing timesheets and perform permitted actions where applicable. Timesheet approvals Agency users can assign specific client contacts as timesheet approvers while enabling Portal Access for a job. Only assigned approvers can approve timesheets. Other client contacts may still be able to view, create, edit, or delete timesheets based on the permissions granted to them, but they cannot approve submissions. All approval actions performed in the Client Portal are synchronized instantly with Recruit CRM. Real-time synchronization All actions performed in the Client Portal, including creating, editing, submitting, and approving timesheets, are synchronized with Recruit CRM in real time. Each activity is automatically logged, ensuring complete visibility for agencies, clients, and contractors. Troubleshooting Problem: I can't approve timesheets. Likely Cause: You're not assigned as the timesheet approver. What to Check: Confirm with your agency that you've been assigned as the approver for the job. Resolution: Only designated approvers can approve timesheets. Other users can only perform the actions permitted by their assigned permissions. FAQs 1. Can I control what clients can do with timesheets? Yes. You can independently allow clients to create, edit, delete, and approve timesheets through the Portal Access permissions. 2. What happens if I disable the Online Link? The client's access to shared timesheets is removed immediately, and the timesheets will no longer be visible in the Client Portal. 3. Can clients view timesheets for deleted candidates? Yes. Existing timesheets remain visible and are clearly marked as Deleted , although new timesheets cannot be created for deleted candidates Conclusion The Client Portal for Timesheets simplifies collaboration between agencies and clients by providing secure, real-time access to contractor timesheets. With configurable permissions, instant synchronization, and a complete audit trail, agencies can confidently manage timesheet workflows while giving clients the flexibility they need. The Job Cloning feature in Recruit CRM allows users to create a new job based on an existing one by copying key details such as job fields, job descriptions, and partnered job board posting settings. Important note when using our API endpoints While asking our API to GET/POST/DELETE the required data, one must not directly query the endpoint on the front end/webpage, as it exposes the API token. You would need to hide the Recruit CRM API token/Bearer token. This can be done by introducing a server in between or by making the API token abstract. Basically, the webpage on the front end would query a private server in between which would then query the Recruit CRM API. This is the safest way of doing this, as it would then prevent exposing the Recruit CRM API token/key publicly. A) General data flow to fetch jobs from Recruit CRM using its API: ​ ​ 1. In this case, the job_status value will be ‘1’ as we don’t use alphabets for job status but integers or IDs, and the same can be found here: Job Status List The cURL request would look something like this: curl --request GET \ --url 'https://api.recruitcrm.io/v1/jobs/search?job_status=1' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_API_TOKEN}' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' The response to this API request will fetch a list of all the “Open” jobs from the Recruit CRM account whose API token is given in the request. t: Commonly used API Endpoints for Careers Page (Part 2)
s: This article will provide you the commonly used API endpoints for careers page
b: Click here to check the Part 1 article 4. Display only some specific types of jobs from Recruit CRM to the Careers page (Your Website): Use the Search for Jobs endpoint - Segregate jobs on the basis of custom fields GET https://api.recruitcrm.io/v1/jobs/search This logic would make sense while segregating jobs based on custom fields in Recruit CRM. Let’s say the client has a dropdown-type custom jobs field titled “Job Category,” which has two values a.) Permanent b.) Temporary, and they want to display only the “Permanent” positions on their website. To make that happen, this endpoint needs to be used. The request body should contain the custom field’s ID, the filter type, and the filter value to get what exactly is required from which field. Custom fields work based on ID because they can be renamed, and the system won’t be able to distinguish or identify the same, unlike standard fields. Here’s how the request body would look: { "custom_fields": [ { "field_id": 1, "filter_type": "equals", "filter_value": "Permanent" } ] } Carrying our example forward, the field ID would be the unique ID of the custom job field titled “Job Category,” the filter type would be “equals,” and the filter value would be “Permanent.” The field IDs, supported filter types, and search values can be found here on API Doc: Custom Field IDs & Values for Jobs Supported Filter types for Custom fields The response structure, once again, would be similar to the ones shared in the above scenarios. It will fetch a list of all the jobs from Recruit CRM that matches the condition sent in the request body. 5 . Display Specific Types of Jobs on Two (or more) Websites or Different Pages on The Same Website (Your Website): Use the Search for Jobs endpoint - Segregate jobs on the basis of custom fields GET https://api.recruitcrm.io/v1/jobs/search The logic behind this scenario is similar to the 4th scenario. The only difference here is that the client’s developer would need to change the filter depending on their requirement. Continuing our example in scenario 4, if the client wants to display the “Permanent” roles on one website and the “Temporary” roles on another, then their developer would need to make the API call for the permanent roles in the required website and replicate the same process to call for the “Temporary” role in the other website. The idea here is to clearly define which custom field segregates the jobs and which types of jobs need to be displayed. Once that is clear, making the API call is just a way to reach the destination. The logic is as simple as that! 6 .
