t: Compliance Support in Recruit Craft
s: Ensure a consistent, transparent, and compliant job application experience for every candidate.
h: How it works
What candidates will experience
SMS consent handling
Key things to note
Why this matters
FAQs
b: Recruit Craft supports compliance-related elements within the job application form. This ensures that candidates see the correct policies and consent options based on your existing settings, without any additional configuration required. The experience stays aligned across platforms, helping you maintain accuracy, trust, and compliance throughout the application process. ⚙️ How it works Compliance elements in the job application form are controlled entirely through your existing settings in Recruit CRM. Based on what is enabled or disabled, the form dynamically updates to display only the relevant sections. The following elements are supported: • Candidate Terms • EEO Policy (Equal Employment Opportunity policy) • SMS Terms If any of these are disabled in your settings within Recruit CRM, they will not appear on the application form. This ensures that candidates only see what is applicable, keeping the form clean and relevant. All labels, checkbox text, and content are pulled directly from your configured job application form settings in Recruit CRM. This means the wording remains consistent across Recruit Craft and Recruit CRM. Click here to know more about handling EEO policy in Recruit CRM Click here to know more about how to manage the Candidate Terms in Recruit CRM Click here to know more about handling SMS terms in Recruit CRM 👀 What candidates will experience When candidates apply for a job, they will see compliance-related sections based on your setup. • Each policy (Candidate Terms, EEO, SMS Terms) appears as a checkbox with clearly defined text • Clicking on any of these opens a detailed view with full policy information • The content shown always matches what is configured in your system ​ This creates a transparent experience where candidates can review and understand the terms before submitting their application. 📩 SMS consent handling If SMS Terms are enabled and a candidate opts in: • Their consent is captured at the time of application submission • This allows recruiters to send SMS communications only to candidates who have explicitly agreed ​ This ensures that all SMS outreach remains compliant and respects candidate preferences. Please note: This is currently available only for users based in the US. ⚠️ Key things to note • Compliance elements are shown only if they are enabled in your settings • No additional setup is required in Recruit Craft • All content and labels are automatically synced from your existing configuration • This applies to accounts where the Candidate Portal is not enabled 💡 Why this matters This improves both compliance and candidate experience: • Ensures accurate and consistent policy display across platforms • Eliminates the need for manual updates or duplicate configurations • Builds trust by clearly communicating terms to candidates • Helps you stay compliant with communication consent (especially for SMS) ❓ FAQs Do I need to configure anything separately in Recruit Craft? No. All compliance elements are controlled through your existing job application form settings. What happens if a policy is disabled? It will not be shown on the job application form. Can candidates view full policy details? Yes. Clicking on any policy opens a detailed view with the complete content. How is SMS consent captured? Consent is recorded when candidates opt into SMS Terms during application submission. Compliance is seamlessly built into your job application flow, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and transparency without adding extra steps to your workflow. b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Connecting your email to Recruit CRM using Nylas.com lets you send and receive emails from within Recruit CRM while keeping your mailbox in sync with your actual email provider. The mailbox in Recruit CRM acts as a mirror of your real mailbox, including folders and emails. You can connect up to two email accounts (on supported plans such as Business and above), choose a default sending address, and switch between connected mailboxes as needed. Before you begin: Recruit CRM has partnered with Nylas.com to power our email services. It will take up to 2-3 hours for your initial folders to sync with Recruit CRM and it may take up to 24 hours for your older emails to sync completely. This is just a one-time activity when you connect your email to Recruit CRM using Nylas for the first time. Email settings should be configured to comply with updated email protection policies from providers like Google and Yahoo, including SPF, DKIM, DMARC, easy unsubscription, and maintaining a low spam rate. ​ Connecting custom IMAP email to Recruit CRM Here are the Step-by-step instructions on how to connect a custom IMAP email to Recruit CRM- 1. Go to https://app.recruitcrm.io/user/sync_email ​ 2. You'll get an option to connect your email accounts. You can connect up to two emails at a time. NOTE: 2 email connections are only available for users in the Business Plan and above. ​ One email must be set as the default for sending emails, but you can switch between emails as needed. ​ If only one email is connected, it will automatically be set as the default. 3. Enter your email that you wish to connect to Recruit CRM: 4. Now you'll have the following option to select the correct service provider: If you are connecting Office 365 family, Office 365 personal, or Office 365 free accounts please click on "See all providers" and choose "Custom IMAP settings" as shown below. 5. You can choose your correct provider from the list by clicking on "See all providers", or you have the option to choose custom IMAP settings: 6. To connect via "Custom IMAP settings" click on the option and it will redirect you to the page where you'll need to enter your server information: 7. Once your email is connected, you can access your mailbox from the menu bar on the left: ​ Your mailbox in Recruit CRM will mirror your Outlook mailbox, meaning all the existing folders and emails will be the same. ​ 8. You can also switch between mailboxes of the emails connected: ​ ​ You can choose to expand or collapse the Folders & Labels section in the Mailbox. The selected state is also persisted, so it remains the same when you return. Accessing your email port settings on Outlook If you are an Office 365 user unsure of your server settings, you can find this by signing in to Outlook on the web . Use your Microsoft 365 email address and password. 1. In the upper-right corner, click on the gear button and select Settings >>> View all Outlook settings . 2. Select Mail > Sync email . You can find the server settings as shown below: Once you have entered the correct details click on "Log in" and you'll have successfully connected your email! Configure your email settings to align with email protection policies For a seamless and secure email experience, please adhere to the enhanced security measures implemented by Google and Yahoo . Follow this quick walkthrough to make necessary adjustments in your email settings according to the updated policies: Adhering to Google & Yahoo's email protection policy These measures, including email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), easy unsubscription, and maintaining a low spam rate, are essential to align with the latest security protocols and ensure optimal email communication. ​ Thank you for your cooperation in maintaining a safe and efficient email exchange. Concerned about your email data security? The Recruit CRM's mailbox operates as a mirror of your real email provider. When you connect your email using our integration, Nylas stores this information on their servers. Be assured that Nylas fully complies with GDPR. You can review Nylas's GDPR policy below 👇 GDPR at Nylas How to retain the emails of deactivated users? Here are two ways through which you can retain the emails of the deactivated users: 1. Move/transfer the emails of the deactivated users to a folder within the mailbox of an active user: You can move/transfer the emails of the deactivated users to a folder within the mailbox of an active user on G Suite/Outlook etc. The Recruit CRM's mailbox operates as a mirror of your real email provider, so all the emails in the respective folder will be synced and will be visible in Recruit CRM as well. 2. Create a new email ID and connect it in Recruit CRM: You can create a new common email ID specifically to backup emails and as Recruit CRM allows users to connect 2 email accounts (available on the Business plan and above) any one of the users on your team can connect this common email to their Recruit CRM account as their 2nd email. Whenever someone leaves your team, you can transfer their emails to this common email account before deleting the email ID of the ex-employee. This will ensure emails are retained once someone leaves without transferring emails into any specific individual's email account. ​Hope this helps! t: Connecting Recruit CRM & other apps with Workflow Automation
s: Automate and streamline various recruitment tasks by creating automation workflows.
h: A. Connecting through the connection wizard
B. Connecting through the recipe editor
b: Connect your Recruit CRM account with Workflow Automation You can connect your Recruit CRM account in two ways: through the connection wizard or in the recipe editor. A. Connecting through the connection wizard The same process can be followed to connect 3rd party apps with Workflow Automation. Head over to Workflow Automation & Integration from your Admin Settings . Go to the Workflows module and click on Create >> Connection. Search Recruit CRM on the search bar and select the app. Enter the Connection Name, Location, and API Token to set up your Recruit CRM connection. Once connected you can use this connection to create your Recipes. Here's where you can find your API Key ​ B. Connecting through the recipe editor Head over to Workflow Automation & Integration from your Admin Settings . Click on Workflows >> Create >> Recipe. Give your recipe a name, and the location (folder) where you want it to be saved, and pick your starting point as “Trigger from an app” to start building the recipe. Search for Recruit CRM in the app directory and select it as the trigger app for your recipe. Choose the trigger and connect your account by entering the API token. Once connected, you’ll be able to use the same connection every time you create a recipe. Click here to find your Recruit CRM API Key Specify the trigger event that will initiate the workflow. For example, in Recruit CRM, you can choose to trigger the recipe when a new candidate is added, a job is updated, or any other supported trigger event. Once your trigger is set up, you can add various actions that should follow the trigger event. These actions can include updating candidate records, sending notifications, or creating tasks within Recruit CRM or other apps. ​ Connect third-party apps with Workflow Automation The below steps will help you connect your third-party applications such as Outlook, Gmail, Google Sheets, or any other apps. 1. Create a New Recipe or an Action for the existing recipe. ​ 2. Choose your third-party applications by searching them. 3. Authenticate the third-party app by signing into your account. ​ Before you complete your authentication process, please choose the “Requested permissions (Oauth scopes)” from the Advanced Setting section. ​ ​ It’s recommended to select all the scopes to have complete access to your account while setting up relevant triggers and actions. ​ ​ If you have trouble selecting all the scopes then try deselecting the nonessential ones, select the important scopes, and proceed. 4. Once you have connected your third-party app account, you’ll be able to set the relevant triggers and actions. This is all! Now you can have fun creating your own recipes :) Related Articles Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM Workflow Automation: Create Contacts in Recruit CRM from Dripify Workflow Automation: Create Candidates in Recruit CRM from Dripify How to connect your Recruit CRM app in Workflow Automation Integrating Xobin to Recruit CRM

b: Recruit Craft allows you to connect a custom subdomain to your career page so candidates can access your jobs using your own domain. This helps maintain your company’s branding and makes your career page feel like a natural extension of your main website. Once connected, your Recruit Craft career page will be accessible through your chosen subdomain (for example, careers.youragency.com ), while still being fully managed inside Recruit Craft. ⚙️ How to connect your custom domain? Follow these steps to connect your domain to Recruit Craft: ​ 1. Open Custom Domain Settings Open your Recruit Craft account and click the Custom Domain option from the left-hand navigation panel to begin the setup process. ​ 2. Enter your custom domain in Recruit Craft Provide the subdomain you want to use for your career page and re-enter it again to verify and avoid errors. ​ Example: careers.youragency.com ​ Once done, click on Connect. Recruit Craft then begins processing the request and prepares the configuration needed for the connection. Please note The custom domain entered should match your default Jobs Page URL. 3. Copy the generated CNAME records Recruit Craft will automatically generate two CNAME records required for the domain connection. You will receive an email notification once the CNAME records are ready. At this stage, the connection status will appear as In Progress , indicating that the domain configuration is still being set up. ​ 4. Add the CNAME records in your DNS provider Log in to your domain provider (for example, GoDaddy, Cloudflare, Namecheap, or others) and add the CNAME records provided by Recruit Craft. These records connect your chosen subdomain with your Recruit Craft career page. ​ 5. Wait for DNS verification Once the DNS records are added, Recruit Craft will automatically verify the configuration. During this time, the connection status will continue to show In Progress until the records are detected and validated. After verification is successful, the status will change to Completed , and your career page will start working through your custom domain. ​ DNS propagation may take a few minutes to several hours , depending on your domain provider. ❓ Frequently Asked Questions Do I need to move my website hosting? No. Your existing website hosting does not need to change. Only a subdomain needs to be connected to Recruit Craft. Can I use my main website domain? No. This feature works only with subdomains , such as careers.domain.com or jobs.domain.com. How long does the connection take? DNS propagation can take a few minutes to several hours , depending on your domain provider. What happens if the CNAME records are added incorrectly? If the records are incorrect, the connection status will remain In Progress until the correct DNS settings are added. s: This article will help you connect your Outlook/Office 365 email to Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Connect your Outlook/Office 365 email

Troubleshooting
Problem: My emails haven't finished syncing.
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM integrates with Outlook and Office 365 through Nylas.com , allowing you to access your native mailbox directly within Recruit CRM. Once connected, your mailbox mirrors your Outlook mailbox, enabling you to send, receive, and manage emails without leaving the platform. This feature is useful when you want to: Connect your Outlook or Office 365 mailbox to Recruit CRM. Send and receive emails directly from Recruit CRM. Connect up to two email accounts (Business plan and above). Switch between connected mailboxes. Sync your Outlook mailbox with Recruit CRM. Connect your Outlook/Office 365 email It will take up to 2-3 hours for your initial folders to sync with Recruit CRM and it may take up to 24 hours for your older emails to sync completely. This is just a one-time activity when you connect your email to Recruit CRM using Nylas for the first time. Navigate to Profile Settings > Email Settings . Please note: You can connect up to two email accounts on the Business Plan and above, and you can switch between connected mailboxes at any time. If only one email is connected, it will automatically be used as your default sending address. Click Connect , then, on the Nylas page, select Continue with Microsoft . Enter the Outlook or Office 365 email address you want to connect. Please note: If you're connecting an Office 365 email account, you'll be automatically redirected to the Microsoft sign-in page. Simply sign in to your account, review and grant the requested permissions, and you'll be good to go 👍 Sign in to your Microsoft account, grant the requested permissions, and click Continue . Once your account is verified, your mailbox will be connected to Recruit CRM. Open Mailbox from the left navigation menu to access your synced emails. Your Recruit CRM mailbox mirrors your Outlook mailbox, so your existing folders and emails will begin syncing automatically. Note: Currently we don’t have the ability to organize the folders in the same way they appear in Outlook. The arrangement is entirely dependent on the responses we receive from Nylas, our third-party email service provider. If you have multiple connected email accounts, you can switch between mailboxes from within the Mailbox using the Dropdown. Important Note Since Recruit CRM is a verified Microsoft app, most of the users will not need the Admin approval to connect their email. However, if your organization has strict security settings, you might still see a 'Need Admin Approval' message. If this happens, ask your Microsoft Admin to follow the steps below to grant access. Grant Admin access on Microsoft Azure Portal If your Admin Approval is still required, your Microsoft/Office 365 administrator will need to log in and approve the connection for users under the same domain/account. Once this is done, other users under the same domain can connect their email to Recruit CRM without any further issues. Connecting Microsoft Office 365 accounts using IMAP settings If you are using any one of the following types of Microsoft Office 365 accounts: Office 365 family Office 365 personal Office 365 free Connect your mailbox using the Custom IMAP Settings option by selecting View all Providers on the email connection page. Connecting IMAP email to RCRM You can choose to expand or collapse the Folders & Labels section in the Mailbox. The selected state is also persisted, so it remains the same when you return. Configure your email settings to align with email protection policies For a seamless and secure email experience, please adhere to the enhanced security measures implemented by Google and Yahoo . Follow this quick walkthrough to make necessary adjustments in your email settings according to the updated policies: Adhering to Google & Yahoo's email protection policy These measures, including email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), easy unsubscription, and maintaining a low spam rate, are essential to align with the latest security protocols and ensure optimal email communication. ​ Email data security Recruit CRM's mailbox acts as a mirror of your real email provider. When you connect your email using our integration, Nylas stores this information on their servers. Nylas is GDPR compliant , helping ensure your email data is handled securely and in accordance with industry standards. For more information, you can review Nylas' GDPR Policy here: GDPR at Nylas How to retain the emails of deactivated users? Here are two ways through which you can retain the emails of the deactivated users: 1. Move/transfer the emails of the deactivated users to a folder within the mailbox of an active user: You can move/transfer the emails of the deactivated users to a folder within the mailbox of an active user on G Suite/Outlook. The Recruit CRM's mailbox operates as a mirror of your real email provider, so all the emails in the respective folder will be synced and will be visible in Recruit CRM as well. 2. Create a new email ID and connect it in Recruit CRM: You can create a new common email ID specifically to backup emails and as Recruit CRM allows users to connect 2 email accounts (available on the Business plan and above) any one of the users on your team can connect this common email to their Recruit CRM account as their 2nd email. Whenever someone leaves your team, you can transfer their emails to this common email account before deleting the email ID of the ex-employee. This will ensure emails are retained once someone leaves without transferring emails into any specific individual's email account. Troubleshooting Problem: My emails haven't finished syncing. Likely Cause: The initial mailbox synchronization is still in progress. What to Check: Check how long ago you connected your mailbox. Resolution: Allow up to 2–3 hours for folders to sync and up to 24 hours for older emails to appear. FAQs Which email account is used to send emails? If only one email account is connected, it will automatically be set as the default. If multiple accounts are connected, you can choose which email account to send from. Conclusion Connecting your Outlook or Office 365 mailbox to Recruit CRM allows you to manage your email communication directly from the platform. s: Helps you understand the progress of the client relationship
h: Option 1: To change the contact stage from the contact list page
Option 2: From within the contact

b: Contact Stage is a contact (client) property that indicates where a contact (client) is in your marketing/sales funnel. There are 2 ways in which you can change the Stage of a contact. ​ Option 1: To change the contact stage from the contact list page Select a bunch of contacts whose Stage you want to change and click on the "Update Field" button. Select the "Stage" option from the drop-down. Choose an appropriate Sales/Contact Stage from the list. After selecting the desired stage, you will have the option to enter a reason for the change. Once you have provided your reason, simply click on 'Submit' to finalize the update. Here's a short video on how to do it! You can also update the contact stage directly from the main contact page by using the 'Stage' column of any contact. ​ Option 2: From within the contact Click on the Contact name. Click on the contact stage that is towards the right of the contact name. Clicking on the contact stage will open a drop-down list where you can select the desired stage and provide a reason for the change. Contact Stage History You can easily view the history of changes made to the contact stages, allowing you to visualize every stage the contact has gone through and the reasons for each change. To view the history of stages, click on the 'Remarks' icon next to the contact stage in the contact's profile. You'll see all the stages the contact has gone through, along with the remarks (reasons) for each change, the date each stage was updated, and the user who made the update. This will help you monitor your sales pipeline. ​ Related Articles Deals Pipeline Changing Hiring Stage (New UI) Customizing And Using Your Contact Stages (New UI) Contact Stage (Sales Pipeline) (New UI) Submit candidates to contacts (New UI)

Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Contact Stage indicates where a contact (client) is in your sales or marketing funnel. Updating the contact stage helps your team track client relationships, monitor progress through the sales funnel, and maintain a complete history of stage changes. This feature is useful when you want to: Track a contact's progress through your sales pipeline. Update the stage of one or multiple contacts. Record the reason for a stage change. View the complete history of stage updates for a contact. Update a contact's stage You can update a contact's stage either from the Contact List Page or directly from the Contact Details Page. From the Contact List Page: Navigate to Contacts and select one or more contacts, and click Update Field . Select Stage from the dropdown menu and choose the appropriate Contact Stage. Enter a reason for the stage change and click Submit to save your changes. You can also update an individual contact's stage directly from the Stage column on the Contact List page. From the Contact Profile/Details Page: Open the required contact's profile. Click the current Contact Stage displayed beside the contact's name. Select the required stage from the dropdown, enter a reason for the change, and save your update. Please note: A red dot appears when there's a remark added for the contact's current contact stage. Can I see who changed a contact's stage? Yes. The Stage History displays the user who updated the stage, the date of the change, and any remarks provided. 2. Is adding a reason when changing a stage mandatory? No, adding a reason isn't mandatory. However, it's considered a best practice as it provides additional context for the stage change and makes it easier for your team to understand the contact's progress when reviewing the stage history. Conclusion: Keeping your Contact Stages up to date helps your team accurately track client relationships throughout the sales pipeline. With bulk updates, individual stage management, and a complete stage history, Recruit CRM makes it easy to monitor every interaction. b: What is a CMS and when can you use it? A CMS (Content Management System) is a tool that helps you create and manage multiple pieces of similar content without building each one as a separate page. For example, if you want to publish 50 blog posts, you do not need to design 50 individual pages. With a CMS, you design the structure once, add your content, and the website automatically uses that structure for each entry. Recruit Craft's Content Library is built directly into the Website Builder, allowing you to create, manage, customize, and publish repeatable content without using a separate CMS such as WordPress. You can use the CMS to create content such as: Blog posts and insights Team member or consultant profiles Client testimonials and case studies Candidate resources and career advice Company news and press updates The same content can be displayed across different pages of your website through a configurable CMS display section. 📌 Please note: The CMS is available only for Full Website projects . Career-Page-only projects do not have the CMS option. How to access and use the CMS The Recruit Craft CMS is organized around four main components: Collections: Organize similar content into groups, such as Blog Posts or Team Members. Posts: Individual pieces of content within a collection. CMS display section: Displays posts from a collection on your website. Dynamic detail page: Automatically displays the full content of each post. For example, you can create a Blog Posts collection, add multiple posts to it, and place a CMS section on your homepage to display those posts. Each post can also have its own automatically generated detail page. ​ Access the CMS To open the CMS: Open your Full Website project in Recruit Craft. In the left sidebar, select Content Library . ​ Create and manage a collection A collection is a group of related content. For example: Blog Posts for articles and insights Team Members for recruiter profiles Testimonials for customer reviews Case Studies for customer success stories To create a collection: Open Content Library from the left-side panel once you are inside your project. Select the option to Create a collection. Enter a name for the collection. Save the collection. ​ Once the collection is created, you can start adding posts to it. Inside the Content Library, you can create and manage collections. Each collection displays its name, item count, and actions such as Rename and Delete. ​ Please note - Collection names must be unique within a project. A collection that contains posts cannot be deleted until its posts are removed. You can create up to 25 collections in a project. Create a CMS post A post is an individual content item within a collection. For example, if you have a Blog Posts collection, each article you create within that collection is treated as a separate post. Each post can have its own content, featured image, writer, publish date, tags, excerpt, and SEO settings. To create a post: 1. Open the relevant collection From the Content Library , open the collection where you want to add the content. For example, open your Blog Posts collection if you want to create a new blog article. 2. Add a new post Select the option to Create to add a post and open the post editor by entering the relevant Post Title. ​ 3. Add and format your post content You can create the content manually using the rich text editor or use AI to generate an initial draft. ​ Click here to learn more about how to write and format your post Recruit Craft provides a rich text editor that lets you create and format your content directly within the post editor. You can use the editor to add: Headings Paragraphs Bold and other text formatting Bulleted and numbered lists Links Inline images Source/HTML editing You can either write the post manually or use AI to generate a first draft . When generating a post with AI, you can provide details such as: Topic or brief Tone Word count Whether to include images Whether to add tags Based on the information you provide, AI generates a draft and title for your post. You can then review, edit, and format the generated content directly in the post editor before publishing. This gives you the flexibility to use AI for the initial draft while retaining full control over the final content. 4. Configure the post details Once you have added the main content, configure the information that will be used when the post is displayed on your website. ​ Click here to learn more about how to add post details Open the post Settings panel from the left side panel to configure details such as: Featured image: Add the image that represents your post on CMS cards and other areas where the post is displayed. Alt text: Add alternative text to describe the featured image. Publish date: Set the date associated with the post. Author Name: Specify the person who wrote the post. Excerpt: Add a short preview of the post that can be displayed on content cards. Tags: Add tags to categorize or describe the post. If you leave the Excerpt field blank, Recruit Craft automatically uses the beginning of the post body as the excerpt. If Writer or Tags are left blank, these fields will not be displayed on the content card. You can also control the visibility of the publish date, writer, and tags through the Website Builder settings. 5. Configure SEO settings Each CMS post has its own SEO configuration , allowing you to configure how that specific post is represented for search engines and shared content. You can access the SEO Settings by clicking on the 3 dots under the Action panel. ​ Click here to learn more about the SEO settings You can configure the following SEO fields: Route/URL: Set the URL route for the post. Page title: Define the title used for the page. Page description: Add a description for the post. Metadata: Configure additional metadata for the page. Thumbnail: Set the image used for the page's SEO/social representation. ​ Because these settings are available at the individual post level, you can configure SEO information separately for each piece of CMS content. 6. Save or publish the post Once you have completed the content, post details, and SEO settings, you can save the post as a Draft or Publish it. You can publish a post in either of the following ways: While creating or editing the post: Click the Publish button at the top of the post editor to publish it directly. From the collection: Locate the post in the collection and select Publish from its Actions panel. The post can have one of the following statuses: Draft: Keeps the post in the CMS without displaying it on the live website. Published: Makes the post eligible to appear on your live website when the relevant CMS section is mapped to the collection. 📌 Please note: A post title is required before you can save or publish the post. Manage posts in a collection Each collection has a dedicated post list where you can view and manage all the content within it. The list displays the post name, publish date, and status , with posts marked as either Draft or Published . You can also search by post name and filter posts by publish date or status to quickly find the content you need. ​ Actions available for individual posts From the Actions menu for a post, you can publish , move a published post back to Draft by unpublishing it , pin or unpin it, rename the title, manage the SEO Settings or delete it. Pinning a post keeps it at the top of both the collection's post list and the live CMS card order , regardless of its publish date. By default, pinned posts appear first, followed by the newest posts based on publish date. Deleting a post is permanent and requires confirmation. ​ Bulk actions When you need to manage multiple posts at once, select the relevant posts and use bulk actions to Publish , Unpublish and move them to Draft, or delete them. ​ Add CMS content to your website Once you have created posts, you can display them on your website using the Blog section . The Blog section is a draggable section that connects to a CMS collection and displays its posts as cards. To add a Blog section: 1. Open the page where you want to display the content. ​ 2. Add the Blog section to the page. 3. From the settings on the right, select the collection you want to display. 4. Configure the card layout and design . Click here to learn more about customizing Blog cards and layout The Blog section uses a shared card design for all posts in the selected collection. Cards can display the featured image, title, excerpt, writer, publish date, and tags . You can control the visibility of available metadata and customize the elements displayed on the card. Any styling changes made to one card are applied across all posts in the collection, while the content remains unique to each post. Use the Blog Layout settings to control how the cards are arranged and displayed. You can configure the number of cards displayed per row and the number of posts shown at a time. The

s: Recruit CRM allows contractors to generate invoices directly from their approved timesheets in the Contractor Portal.
h: What does this feature do and when to use it?
Before you begin
Generate Contractor Invoices
1. Generate an invoice from the Contractor Portal
Generate an invoice from the Agency Portal
For a single Timesheet:
For multiple Timesheets:
Manage Contractor Invoices
b: What does this feature do and when to use it? Contractor Invoices helps agencies and contractors manage the invoicing process directly from approved timesheets. This feature is useful when you want to: Generate invoices from approved contractor timesheets. Allow contractors to generate their own invoices. View, download, and delete generated invoices. Access invoices directly from their related timesheets. Before you begin Contractor Invoicing must be enabled from the Timesheet form . The timesheet must be approved before a contractor invoice can be generated. Please note: The invoice setting is based on its state at the time the timesheet is approved. Changes made to the setting after approval do not affect previously approved timesheets. Generate Contractor Invoices 1. Generate an invoice from the Contractor Portal Contractors can generate an invoice directly from an approved timesheet in the Contractor Portal . Open the desired approved timesheet . Click Generate in the top-right corner. The contractor invoice will be generated automatically. The generated invoice includes the relevant timesheet and payment information, such as: Billed From and Billed To details Timesheet period Work hours, overtime hours, and total hours for hourly timesheets Payable amount Approved payable reimbursements Total invoice amount Generate an invoice from the Agency Portal Agency users can generate contractor invoices from the Agency Portal for either a single timesheet or multiple timesheets in bulk. For a single Timesheet: Go to the specific Job and, from the candidate pipeline, click View Timesheets for the contractor. Open the timesheet for which you want to generate an invoice. On the timesheet details page, under Contractor Invoice , click Generate . For multiple Timesheets: Select the timesheets for which you want to generate invoices. Click the dropdown arrow beside Create Invoice and select Create for Contractor. You can generate up to 15 invoices at a time . Before generating invoices, Recruit CRM checks whether each timesheet is eligible. An invoice will not be generated if: The timesheet is not approved. Contractor Invoicing is not enabled for the contractor. A contractor invoice has already been generated. The invoice will be generated for the selected timesheet and automatically linked to it. The contractor receives an email and an in-app notification when an agency user generates an invoice on their behalf. Manage Contractor Invoices Contractors and agency users can manage generated invoices from the respective portal. You can: View invoices Download invoices Delete invoices Access an invoice directly from the related timesheet using the invoice link Notifications Recruit CRM sends notifications based on who generates the contractor invoice: Agency user generates an invoice: The contractor receives an email and an in-app notification. Contractor generates an invoice: The designated agency approver receives an email notification. Please note: Contractor invoices are not available on the Client Portal . FAQs 1. Can I enable Contractor Invoicing after a timesheet has already been approved? No. Enabling the setting after approval will not update previously approved timesheets. The setting is captured based on its status at the time of approval and will only apply to timesheets approved after it is enabled. 2. What happens if the contractor has already generated the invoice? The invoice will automatically be linked to the timesheet. Agency users can view and download the invoice from the relevant timesheet. 3. Can expenses be updated after a Contractor Invoice is generated? No. Once a Contractor Invoice has been generated, expense claims cannot be updated for that timesheet. Conclusion Contractor Invoices simplifies the invoicing process by allowing agencies and 1099 contractors to generate invoices directly from approved timesheets. With individual and bulk invoice generation, invoice management, automatic timesheet linking, and notifications, agencies can manage contractor invoicing more efficiently. t: Contractor Portal in Recruit CRM - Timesheets (Beta)
s: This article explains how the Contractor Portal works and how contractors can use it to manage their timesheets.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Who is considered a contractor?
How to enable Contractor Portal access?
How to manage timesheets in the Contractor Portal?
Set the time format
View assigned timesheets
Save open timesheets
Create new timesheets
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Contractor Portal provides contractors with a secure space to access jobs where timesheets are enabled, create and submit timesheets, track approvals, and manage their timesheet activity independently. All actions performed in the portal are synchronized with Recruit CRM in real time, giving agencies complete visibility into contractor timesheet activity. This feature is useful when you want to: Give contractors secure access to manage their own timesheets. Allow contractors to create, save, edit, and submit timesheets. Enable contractors to track timesheet approvals and rejections. Reduce manual follow-ups between agencies and contractors. Keep timesheet activity synchronized with Recruit CRM in real time. Please note: This feature is currently available in Beta and can be enabled upon request. Please contact your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. Who is considered a contractor? A candidate is considered a contractor when timesheets are enabled for at least one job assigned to them. Once timesheets are enabled, the candidate is automatically identified as a contractor in Recruit CRM. A contractor can have one of the following statuses: Contractor Assigned: The contractor is currently working on a job with an active job duration. Contractor Available: Timesheets are enabled for the contractor, but they are not currently working on an active job. How to enable Contractor Portal access? You can enable portal access directly from a contractor's candidate profile, allowing them to manage their timesheets independently. Open the candidate's profile and ensure timesheets are enabled for at least one assigned job. You can confirm this by checking for the Contractor: Available or Contractor: Assigned status at the top of the profile. Click the three-dot menu on the candidate's profile and select Enable Portal Access . Review the contractor's email address in the confirmation window, then click Enable and Send Invite . Once the invitation is sent, the Portal Invitation Sent tag will appear on the candidate's profile, and the contractor will receive an email containing a signup link. Please note: You can resend the portal invitation if required, but only up to three times within a 24-hour period . Once the contractor completes the signup process using the invitation link, the status automatically changes from Invitation Sent to Portal Enabled . The contractor can then log in and start managing their timesheets directly from the portal. Important notes for portal access: Portal access cannot be enabled if the candidate does not have an email address on their profile. Each email address can be associated with only one portal account, so if an email is already linked to an existing portal account, it cannot be used to enable portal access for another candidate. How to manage timesheets in the Contractor Portal? Once contractors have completed sign-up and logged in, they can manage their timesheet activities directly from the portal. Set the time format Contractors can choose whether timesheets are displayed in a 12-hour or 24-hour format. To update the time format, navigate to Settings → Profile , select the preferred option under Time Format , and click Save Profile . All timesheets will then be displayed using the selected format. View assigned timesheets Contractors can view only the jobs they are assigned to where timesheets have been enabled. All timesheets related to eligible jobs are available in one place, and contractors can filter them by time periods, such as This Week or This Month , to quickly find the required entries. Save open timesheets While a timesheet is in the Open status, contractors can enter their timesheet details and click Save without submitting it. The timesheet remains open and can be accessed later for further updates or submission. Create new timesheets Contractors can create timesheets for jobs where timesheets are enabled. Click + Add Timesheet , select the relevant job and time period, and create the timesheet. Add time entries and submit timesheets To add time, click the Pencil icon in the Actions column of the relevant timesheet. Depending on the Rate Type configured for the contractor, enter either the hours worked (plus any breaks) or the day's attendance (Full Day, Half Day, No Show), then submit the completed timesheet for approval. If a submitted timesheet is rejected, the contractor can view the rejection status, edit the timesheet to make the required changes, and resubmit it for review. Track timesheet status Contractors can track the status of each timesheet directly from the portal. Timesheets clearly indicate whether they are Submitted , Approved , or Rejected , along with updates made during the approval process. Real-time data sync and activity history All timesheets created, saved, updated, submitted, or resubmitted through the Contractor Portal are synchronized with Recruit CRM in real time. Each timesheet also displays who submitted and approved it and when each action occurred, providing contractors and agency users with a clear activity history. How to disable Contractor Portal access? Agency users can disable portal access at any time if a contractor no longer requires access or if access needs to be temporarily paused. Open the contractor's profile in Recruit CRM. Click the three-dot menu and select Disable Portal Access. A confirmation window will appear. Click Disable to confirm. Once portal access is disabled, the candidate's status tag changes to Portal Disabled . The contractor is immediately logged out of the portal, sees a message indicating that access has been disabled, and receives an email notification about the change. Portal access can be enabled again later if required. Once re-enabled, the contractor receives a new notification and can log in using their existing credentials. Candidate deletion and portal lifecycle If a candidate record is deleted from Recruit CRM, the associated Contractor Portal account is automatically deleted. If candidate records are merged and the secondary candidate has an associated Contractor Portal account, that portal account is also deleted as part of the merge process. This ensures Contractor Portal access remains aligned with active candidate records in Recruit CRM. Troubleshooting Problem: I can't enable Contractor Portal access for a candidate. Likely Cause: The candidate doesn't have an email address, timesheets haven't been enabled for an assigned job, or the email address is already linked to another portal account. What to Check: Confirm that timesheets are enabled for at least one assigned job, the candidate has a valid email address, and the email isn't already associated with another portal account. Resolution: Enable timesheets for an assigned job and add a unique email address to the candidate's profile before enabling portal access. FAQs 1. Can I resend a Contractor Portal invitation? Yes. You can resend the invitation up to three times within a 24-hour period. 2. A re the bill rate and bill amount f ields visible to contractors? No. Bill rate and bill amount fields are client-specific and are not visible to contractors in the portal. 3. How can an agency user change the email address of a contractor who already has portal access? An agency user can update the email address directly from the candidate record. Once the new email is saved, the change takes effect immediately. A notification is sent to both the old and the new email addresses, and the contractor can log in using the updated email. Note: If the email being updated already exists in the portal (whether added manually, through a profile update, etc.), the system will display an error, and the email change will not be allowed. 4. What happens if a contractor is unassigned from all jobs where timesheets are enabled? The candidate will no longer be considered a contractor. If portal access already exists, related options will still be available, and the contractor will no longer be able to view timesheets for jobs they have been unassigned from. 5. Is it possible to save a timesheet having status other than “Open”? No, it is currently not possible to save a timesheet having any other status except “Open” 6. What happens if a Contractor wants to edit a Timesheet with status- Submitted or Rejected? In such a case, the Save option is not available. They must resubmit timesheets after editing them. Conclusion The Contractor Portal gives contractors a secure and convenient way to manage their timesheets while keeping agencies informed through real-time synchronization with Recruit CRM. Contractors can create, save, submit, and track timesheets independently, while agency users retain control over portal access and contractor records. t: Converting CSV files to Excel
s: This article will show you the steps to convert the CSV files generated by Recruit CRM into Excel files.
h: Convert CSV to XLS files in Windows 👇
Option 1: CSV to Excel using the “From Text/ Data” Option
Option 2: CSV to Excel using the “Text to Column” Option
Option 3: CSV to Excel using Google Sheets option
Convert CSV to XLS files in Mac OS 👇
Here are the steps:
b: We understand that sometimes our clients require their Recruit CRM data in Excel format rather than CSV. In this article, we will guide you through the straightforward steps to seamlessly convert CSV files into Excel, ensuring a smooth transition for enhanced data management and analysis. Converting CSV and XLS files online 🧞‍♂️ Convert CSV to XLS Convert XLSX to XLS Converting CSV to XLS manually 🧑‍💻 Convert CSV to XLS files in Windows 👇 Option 1: CSV to Excel using the “From Text/ Data” Option 1. Open Microsoft Excel, and start a Blank workbook. 2. Once the new spreadsheet is open, select Data from the ribbon, and then click on the From Text/ CSV button on the upper-left-hand side of the window. An Import Data pop-up box will appear. From there, select the CSV file you want to import and click on Import: 3. A new tab will appear, asking you to define certain parameters within the imported data, like File Origin , Delimiter , and Data Type Detection . Under delimiter select the delimiter used in your CSV file; It is best to choose comma by default. Once everything’s set, click on Load: 4. Once you click on Load, excel will load your data from the CSV file into a formatted table: 5. After this you can save your file by clicking the File and then Save As and Excel will save your file as an xls or Excel file: Option 2: CSV to Excel using the “Text to Column” Option 1. Open Microsoft Excel, and start a Blank workbook. 2. Click on File , go to the "Open" tab of the left bar, and choose Browse from the Open side-pane to display all the files from your device. Choose the CSV file you want to convert and click on Open: Once Excel has opened your CSV file, you’ll notice that your data is separated into the appropriate rows. However, it’s not separated into the appropriate columns. Instead, the data is saved in the first column of each row. Luckily, you can automatically sort the data by using the Text to Column option. 3. Go to the Data tab in the ribbon. Select the rows of data that you want to convert, and click on the Convert to Text option located in the Data Tools field. This will open a Convert Text to Column Wizard that will guide you through the process. 4. Under the Original data type , choose Delimited , and click Next . In the next section, check the box next to the type of delimiter your CSV file uses (our example uses a comma). The Data Preview field will allow you to see the data being assigned to corresponding columns. Click Next , choose the spreadsheet destination, and click Finish . Your data is now separated into the corresponding columns: 5. Click on the File tab and select the Save option. When the Save dialog box appears, give your file a name, and choose Excel Workbook in the Save as type drop-down menu: Option 3: CSV to Excel using Google Sheets option 1. Log into Google Sheets using your Google credentials. If you don’t own a Google account, you might have to create one. After you’ve logged in, select the Blank option to create a new spreadsheet. Once the new spreadsheet is open, click on the File menu in the upper right corner of the page, and select Import : 2. This will open up an Import file dialog box. Click on the Upload tab, and either drag and drop your file or click on the Select a file from your device button to locate the file and upload it. Google Sheets will ask you about the import location and separator (delimiter type) it should use to derive data. You can leave the delimiter selection drop-down at Detect Automatically and click on Import data : 3. Google Sheets will automatically separate the data into its appropriate cells. Now you can save the file. 4. Once you’ve made the necessary changes, if any, go to File , and choose Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) from the Download drop-down menu: Convert CSV to XLS files in Mac OS 👇 Importing CSV files in Excel to convert them into XLS files in Mac is pretty similar to the options we have for Windows. Here are the steps: 1. Once you have downloaded the CSV into your device, you need to open a blank Excel spreadsheet. Select File > Import : 2. Choose CSV file and select Import : 3. Make the following selections: Select Get Data . Choose Delimited. Select Next . Delimiters: Comma (no other options should be checked). Select Next . In the Data Preview window, select all columns. Column data format: Text If you select all of the columns, you'll see a label above each column in the preview that says Text : 4. Click on Finish. 5. Excel will ask you where you want to put the data. choose Existing sheet and select OK . That's it 😄 You have successfully converted your CSV file into an Excel sheet! t: Create Company/Team Specific Public Job Pages
s: This article will guide you on how to create team-based & company-based job page URLs
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin
Team-Specific URLs
Company-Specific URLs:
Access Requirements
Generate a Team-Specific Public Job Page URL
Step 1: Open Public Job Page Settings
Step 2: Copy the Team URL:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? With this feature, you can create unique job page URLs for specific teams and companies , ensuring only relevant job postings appear on your external websites. This targeted approach simplifies job listing management, offering greater flexibility and precision without additional integration efforts. You can generate URLs that display: • Jobs associated with a specific team. • Jobs associated with a specific company. This allows you to create focused job pages for different audiences without additional development work. Use this feature when: • You want to display only one team's open roles on a specific website or careers page. • You manage multiple teams and need separate job pages for each team. • You want to create a dedicated public job page for a specific company. 📌 Before you begin Before generating team-specific or company-specific public job page URLs, ensure the following requirements are met: Team-Specific URLs • Available only on the Business and Enterprise plans, as Teams are supported on these plans only. • The relevant team must be added as a collaborator on the job. • You must know the Team ID. Company-Specific URLs: • Available on all Recruit CRM plans. • You must know the Company Slug. Access Requirements • You must have access to Admin Settings. • You must have access to Public Job Page Settings. 👥 Generate a Team-Specific Public Job Page URL Follow these steps to generate a team-specific public job page. Step 1: Open Public Job Page Settings Navigate to Admin Settings → Public Job Page Settings → Job Page Integration and scroll to the bottom of the page, where you will find the Team URL and Company URL formats. Step 2: Copy the Team URL: Locate the Team URL format provided by Recruit CRM. Copy the URL as shown in the screenshot and paste it into a new browser tab. Step 3: Find the Team ID: To find the Team ID: • Click the Click Here link available on the same page for quick access, or • Navigate to the ' Teams ' page and locate the Team ID for the required team Copy the Team ID. Step 4: Generate the Team-Specific URL Append the Team ID to the end of the Team URL. Once completed, the URL will display jobs associated with that specific team. Requirements for jobs to appear on a Team-Specific Job Page For a job to appear on a team-specific public job page: • The relevant team must be added as a collaborator on the job. • The job status must not be set to Closed. • The Enable Job Application Form option must be enabled. Only jobs meeting all of these requirements will appear on the team-specific job page. 🏢 Generate a Company-Specific Public Job Page URL Follow these steps to generate a company-specific public job page. Step 1: Open Public Job Page Settings Navigate to Admin Settings → Public Job Page Settings → Job Page Integration and scroll to the bottom of the page, where you will find the Team URL and Company URL formats. Step 2: Copy the Company URL Locate the Company URL format provided by Recruit CRM. Copy the URL as shown in the screenshot and paste it into a new browser tab. Step 3: Find the Company Slug To find the Company Slug: Open the company record. Look at the URL in your browser. Copy the alphanumeric value that appears after: https://app.recruitcrm.io/v1/company/ Example: https://app.recruitcrm.io/v1/company/abc123xyz In this example: abc123xyz = Company Slug Step 4: Generate the Company-Specific URL Append the Company Slug to the end of the Company URL. The completed URL will display jobs associated with that specific company. You can now: • Share the URL. • Embed it on external websites. • Create dedicated company-specific careers pages. Here is a short video on it: Requirements for jobs to appear on a Company-Specific Job Page For a job to appear on a company-specific public job page: • The job must be associated with the selected company. • The job status must not be set to Closed. • The Enable Job Application Form option must be enabled. Only jobs meeting all of these requirements will appear on the company-specific job page. 🛠️ Troubleshooting Problem: Team-Specific URL shows no jobs Likely cause: The team has not been added as a collaborator on the jobs, or the jobs do not meet the visibility requirements. ​ ​ What to check: • The correct team is added as a collaborator • The job status is not Closed • Enable Job Application Form is enabled ​ ​ Resolution: Add the team as a collaborator. Verify the job status. Enable the Job Application Form. Refresh the URL. Problem: Company-Specific URL shows no jobs Likely cause: The Company Slug is incorrect. ​ ​ What to check: • The Company Slug copied from the company URL • Any missing or extra characters ​ Resolution: Re-copy the Company Slug. Update the URL. Refresh the page. Problem: Some jobs are missing from the Company-Specific page Likely cause: The jobs are not linked to the correct company or do not meet visibility requirements. ​ What to check: • Company association on the job • Job status • Enable Job Application Form setting ​ Resolution: Update the company association. Enable the Job Application Form. Ensure the job is open. Refresh the URL. Problem: Cannot find the Team URL or Company URL Likely cause: Insufficient permissions or unsupported plan. ​ What to check: • Access to Admin Settings • Access to Public Job Page Settings • Current Recruit CRM plan ​ Resolution: Contact your Account Owner or Admin. Upgrade to Business or Enterprise if Team functionality is required. ❓ FAQs How do I generate a team-specific or company-specific job page URL? Go to Admin Settings → Public Job Page Settings → Job Page Integration and append the relevant team or company identifier to the default job page URL. What happens if a job is linked to multiple teams? The job will appear in the job page URLs for all associated teams. Will the job page update automatically when job assignments change? Yes, any changes in team or company assignments will be reflected in the respective job page URLs. What are the conditions for jobs to be displayed on the jobs page? 1. Job's status should NOT be " Closed ". 2. The "Enable Job Application Form" option should be checked. Conclusion: Team-specific and company-specific public job page URLs allow you to display focused, relevant job listings on external websites without requiring additional integrations. By using team and company filters, you can create tailored job experiences for candidates while keeping job management centralized within Recruit CRM. t: Creating a Chart (Question) in Advanced Analytics
s: This article will guide you on how to filter, group, and visualize data using the Advanced Analytics Query Builder.
h: Step-by-step instructions on how to create and visualize a basic question in Advanced Analytics
How to add your question to a dashboard?
Alternative way to add a question to a dashboard
How to change the visualization type in Advanced Analytics?
Refine results at each step
Visualization options
Add more steps
Troubleshooting
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Query Builder in Advanced Analytics is a graphical interface that allows you to explore your data without writing SQL. In Advanced Analytics, queries and their visualizations are called "questions." Use the Query Builder whenever you need a custom view that an existing dashboard doesn't already cover, for example, checking deal values by owner, tracking candidates through pipeline stages, or spotting trends in placements over a chosen date range. Because you build the question step by step, you can start with a simple table and keep refining it until it answers the exact question you have. You can build your question using the following components: Filters – Narrow down your data based on specific conditions. Summaries – Aggregate data, such as calculating totals or averages. Custom Columns – Create new columns, like adding a Total column that sums Subtotal + Tax. Joins – Combine data from multiple tables. Sorts – Arrange data in ascending or descending order for better analysis. With these building blocks, you can filter, group, and visualize your data effectively within the Advanced Analytics interface. You can combine the query builder blocks in different order, and have multiple blocks of the same type — for example, filter, summarize, then filter the summarized results, join them with a different table, and add another summary. The next step of your query will use the result from the previous one. Step-by-step instructions on how to create and visualize a basic question in Advanced Analytics For example, we’ll work with the Deals table in the database. 1. Select the data source Start a new query builder question using table Deals from the Database as the source: Click on the “+ New” button Select “Question” In the data picker, switch to “Tables” tab, select the Deals table. Once selected, Advanced Analytics will open the Query Builder, displaying Data, Filter, and Summary options. 2. Preview the data Click the Play button next to the Data section to preview the table. At every stage of your question, you can preview results as a table or create a visualization, and you can switch between the query builder, the query’s result as a chart, and the results as a table at any time. In our case, the Deals table looks like this: 3. Filter results Deals in the table seem to have different Deal Stages. Let’s filter the data to show just the Deals in “Won” Deal Stage . In the Filter block, click "Add filter." (If no Filter block exists, click the green Filter icon below the Data block.) Select the Deal Stage column. Set the filter type to "Is" and choose "Won." Click the Play button to preview the filtered results. 4. Summarize the filtered results To see if there are any patterns in these deals, let’s see how the Deal Values are distributed by Owner Names. 1.In the gray “Summarize” block, add a “Sum” metric of Deal Value grouped by the Owner Name column. Advanced Analytics might have already added a blank Summarize block for you, but if not, you can click on the gray “Σ” icon below the Filter block to add it. 2.Click the Play button to preview the summarized data. 5. Visualize To view the results as a chart, click on the “Visualize” button at the bottom of the query builder. That’s it! Advanced Analytics will automatically create a bar chart for you: 6. Sort your results To reorder the bars, we can sort the result of our query. Go back to the query builder by clicking on the “Show editor” button in the top right corner; Add a Sort block and sort by Sum of Deal Value. Click on the ↑ icon to change the sort order from descending to ascending. Visualize. 7. Save To save your question for future reference or sharing click on the “Save” button at the top right corner. Advanced Analytics will ask you which collection you want to save your question in. Collections in Advanced Analytics are like folders – you can use them to organize your work. This allows you to easily access, manage, and share your visualizations later. How to add your question to a dashboard? After saving your question, you can add it to a dashboard for easier access and reporting. Open the saved question. Click the Add to Dashboard option in the top-right corner. 3. Choose an existing dashboard or create a new dashboard. 4. Select the desired dashboard and click Save . 5. Open the dashboard to verify that the chart has been added successfully. Tip: Adding questions to dashboards allows you to combine multiple charts and metrics in a single view, making it easier to monitor key recruitment performance indicators. Alternative way to add a question to a dashboard Open any existing dashboard. Click on the edit button on the top right. 3. Then click on Add question (+) . 4. Select the chart (question) that is to be added to the dashboard. 5. Place it where you want and click on Save . How to change the visualization type in Advanced Analytics? Advanced Analytics automatically selects a suitable chart type based on your data. For example, a time series will default to a line chart, while categorical summaries typically appear as bar charts. Let’s change the bar chart to a pie chart: If you are in the query builder, enter the visualization view by clicking on the “Visualize” button; Open visualization options by clicking on the “Visualization” in the bottom left corner; Select a pie chart (or another preferred chart type). 💡 Tip : Advanced Analytics has a ton of chart options, but not all chart types work with every dataset. At the top of the visualization sidebar, Advanced Analytics highlights the best options based on your data. Charts in the “Other charts” section may not be compatible. Refine results at each step If you want to analyze seasonal trends in deal value while focusing only on existing business deals, follow these steps: Try the following: Filter: Add a filter for Deal Type = Existing Business. Summarize: Group the data by Close Date: Month. Sort: Add a secondary sort by Close Date (ascending). Visualize: The grouped data will automatically switch to a line chart with a date axis, showing a separate time series for each Owner. It’ll look something like this: This approach helps you refine and customize your analysis for deeper insights. Visualization options To view values on data points in the chart, follow these steps: Click the settings button next to the visualization. Navigate to the "Display" section. Enable the "Show values on data points" option. This will make the values visible on the chart. Similarly, you can add currency values to the data points by following these steps: Click the settings button next to the visualization. Click on the three dots (more options). Select "Currency" to apply the currency format. Add more steps You can continue refining your query by adding more filters, summaries, or even joining another table . For example, we see on our line chart that there are times where the Sum of deal value has huge spikes. Let’s count these spikes per plan. Go back to the query builder by clicking on “Show editor” button in the top right corner. Add another Filter block after the Summarize block and filter for Sum of deal value over 2,000,000. Add another Summarize block after the second Filter block, and Count the rows by Owner Name. Visualize. Switch views between the chart and raw table by clicking the table button at the bottom center. By layering filters and summaries , we created a complex query that counts, by Owner Name, the months where the total Deal Value exceeded 2,000,000 —all without writing SQL! Troubleshooting Problem: If you’re unable to select a particular chart type. Likely cause: The selected visualization is not compatible with the current dataset. Some chart types require specific data structures (for example, a pie chart requires one dimension and one metric). What to check: Verify that your chart includes the required dimensions and metrics. Check whether the data has been grouped or summarized appropriately. Resolution path: Use one of the recommended chart types, or modify the Summarize step so the query returns data compatible with the desired visualization. Problem: If you’re experiencing a “Something went wrong" error message. Likely cause: The query contains an invalid filter combination, depends on a modified or deleted saved question/model, or has timed out due to processing a large dataset. What to check: Review any recently added filters. Verify that the underlying data source or saved question is still available. Resolution path: Remove or simplify filters one at a time to identify the issue. If the problem persists, reduce the query complexity or contact your administrator to verify the underlying data source or model. Conclusion: The Query Builder lets you filter, summarize, sort, and visualize data without writing SQL, turning raw tables into charts you can save and share on dashboards. s: This article will guide you on creating and managing invoices in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Invoices feature in Recruit CRM lets you create, customize, and manage invoices directly within the platform. You can generate invoices from supported records such as candidates, contacts, companies, jobs, deals, and placements, use customizable invoice templates and fields, track invoice statuses from a centralized dashboard, work with multiple currencies using automatic exchange rate updates for reporting, and perform bulk actions such as exporting, downloading, archiving, deleting, and updating internal fields. Use this feature when: You need to generate invoices directly from candidate, contact, company, job, deal, or placement records. You want to monitor invoice statuses such as Paid , Due , and Overdue from a single dashboard. You work with multiple currencies and need consistent reporting in your account's base currency. You want to create customized invoice templates and add client-facing or internal custom fields. You need to bulk manage, export, archive, or report on invoice data from the Invoice List page. Locating t he Invoices Section The Invoice List page serves as the central dashboard for managing all invoices created in Recruit CRM. From here, invoices can be tracked, organized, and managed from a single location. From the left-hand sidebar, click Placements & Invoices . On the Placements & Invoices page, select the Invoices tab to view all invoices created. This section gives you a centralized view of all invoices, making it easier to monitor billing activity and manage invoice records efficiently. ​ Underst anding t he Invoice List Page The Invoice List Page acts as the central dashboard for managing invoices. From here, you can track invoice statuses, organize records, and perform actions such as editing, downloading, archiving, or exporting invoices. ​ Invoice Overview Metrics: At the top of the invoice list page, you will see a quick overview of key invoice statistics, including: Total Invoices Paid Invoices Due Invoices Overdue Invoices These metrics give you a quick snapshot of your billing performance. You can also click on any of these metrics to instantly filter the list and view invoices belonging to that category. ​ For example: Selecting Paid Invoices will show all invoices marked as paid. Selecting Overdue Invoices will display invoices whose due date has passed. Multi-Currency Support Recruit CRM supports invoices in multiple currencies to accommodate different billing requirements. Exchange rates are automatically fetched once per day , and invoice values are converted into the account's base currency for reporting. This ensures that reports display consistent values in the configured account currency. While creating or editing an invoice, open the invoice form. On the left side of the invoice form, select the required Currency from the currency dropdown. Save the invoice. On the Invoice List page, review the following information: Invoice currency Total amount Converted amount based on the account's base currency ​ Note: Daily exchange rate updates may cause small fluctuations in report totals. ​ Grouping Invoices To make invoice tracking easier, you can organize invoices using the 'Group By' feature. ​ Steps to group invoices: Click on the "Group By" button on the top right of the invoice list page. Select the entity you want to group invoices by (Jobs, Deals, Companies, or Contacts). The system will automatically organize invoices into groups based on the selected entity, allowing you to quickly review invoices associated with the specific records. ​ ​ Filtering & Searching Invoices The invoice list page also supports Filter search and Boolean search. ​ You can: Filter invoices by status, company, currency, or other attributes. Sort invoices based on fields such as creation date or invoice amount. Use the search bar to locate specific invoice records. Click here to learn how to run a search in Recruit CRM (New UI) ​Bulk Actions on Invoices You can select multiple invoices and perform actions such as: Download Invoices You can select the invoice you want to download as a PDF, then click on the 'Download PDF' button. Exporting Invoices You can select the invoice you want to export, then click on the 'Export' button. Archiving Invoices Select the invoice you want to archive. Then click on the 'Archive' button: ​ To view Archived Invoices, click on the Quick View button and click on 'Archived': ​ Deleting Invoices After selecting the invoice you want to delete, click on the 'Delete' button. ​ Creating an Invoice Option 1: From within the record 1. Choose the entity for which you want to create the invoice. ( Candidate, Contact, Company, Jobs & Deals). Here we have selected a company record as an example. ​ 2. You can create an invoice directly from a Company record by clicking on the three-dot menu (⋮) at the top right and selecting "Create Invoice". ​ Alternatively, you can also create it within the Invoices tab. The option to Create Invoice will appear if there are any other existing linked invoices. ​ 3. The invoice will automatically link to that company. ​ Option 2: From the Placements & Invoices tab 1. Go to Placements & Invoices → Invoices . Click " + New Invoice". ​ 2. Select a template (Recruit CRM provides default templates that you can edit or clone. You can also create a new template ). ​ 3. Choose the template and record from the options below (candidate, contact, company, jobs or deal you’d like to associate this Invoice with). ​ 4. Once the form opens, you’ll see a live preview on the right showing your template and real-time calculations. ​ 5. Filling Invoice Details : ​ Entering Invoice Details (Left-hand Side): ​ While creating the invoice, you can enter values like salary, placement fee, a start and due date. You’ll see the total amount update automatically based on your formulas and fields. ​ ​ ​ Customizing the Invoice Layout (Right-hand Side): ​ On the right-hand side of the invoice creation screen, you will see a live preview of the invoice template . This preview is fully customizable and allows you to edit the layout and formatting of the invoice directly from the editor. ​ At the top of the editor, you will find several formatting and editing tools that allow you to structure and customize the invoice document. ​ Using the tools, you can: Create a new file within the editor Use Undo and Redo options to revert or reapply changes Upload or insert images (for example, a company logo) directly from your computer Insert tables by specifying the number of rows and columns Add hyperlinks within the invoice content Insert a Table of Contents for structured documents Add headers and footers to organize the layout Insert page numbers to structure multi-page invoices Add page breaks to control how content flows across pages Configure Page Setup and layout settings to adjust how the invoice appears in the final document Use Find to quickly locate text within the document Paste content from your local clipboard Modify text formatting , including font type, font size, and other styling options​ The options allow you to format and structure the invoice document directly within the preview editor, similar to working in a standard document editor. ​ Once done, click on "Save" to keep it as a draft or "Save & Send" to email it to your client. ​ ​ Note: The invoice number is auto-generated but can be customized anytime from your billing settings. Option 3: Creating Invoices from the Hiring Pipeline You can also create an invoice automatically when updating candidate stages in the hiring pipeline. ​ Go to a specific Job and click View All to see all the candidates assigned to that job. ​ Select the candidate(s) whose hiring stage you want to update and create an invoice for. You can do this from either the List View or the Kanban View , and click Update Hiring Stage from the top. ​ Change the Hiring Stage as required. Below the Remark box , enable the Create Invoice option and click Submit. ​ Choose an invoice template and click Create Invoice. The system will automatically generate invoices and associate them with the relevant records. ​ You can also generate invoice directly by changing the candidate's hiring stage, simply update the Hiring Stage and make sure to check the Create Invoice option at the bottom. ​ Creating custom fields for Invoices You can add your own fields to capture extra billing details like “Project Code,” “Tax Category,” or “Payment Type.” 1. Go to Admin Settings → Invoice Fields and templates . ​ 2. Click "+ Add Custom Field" button. ​ 3. Choose the type of field (Text, Long Text, Date, Number, Dropdown, or Multi-select). Name the field and set visibility. Click "Save" . ​ These fields appear on your invoice creation form and can also be used inside templates.
