b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Resume Formatting feature allows you to create reusable Header, Footer, Cover Letter, and Watermark templates that can be applied to resumes and CVs before sharing them with clients. These templates help you maintain consistent branding by automatically adding elements such as company logos, colors, company information, cover letters, and watermarks without the need for manual editing each time. Use this feature when: • You want to standardize the appearance of resumes sent to clients. • You are tired of manually reformatting resumes before sharing them. • You want consistent branding across all formatted CVs and resumes. • You need different formatting templates for different clients, industries, or job types. • You want to include a cover letter as the first page of a formatted resume. • You want to add a watermark to protect or brand candidate resumes. Once created, these templates can be mixed and matched during the resume formatting process, allowing you to quickly generate professionally branded resumes while maintaining flexibility for different client requirements. Step-by-step instructions Go to “ Admin Settings ” and click on “ Resume Formatting Settings ” under CRM Process Customization. 2. You will now see the options: Header templates , Footer templates , Cover letter templates , and Watermark templates . You can now create customized templates for each of these. Create Header and Footer Templates Header templates appear at the top of a formatted resume or CV, while footer templates appear at the bottom. These templates can be used to add branding elements such as logos, recruiter information, colors, and candidate details, helping you create a consistent and professional presentation. Create a Header template : In the Header template section, click the New Header button. Enter a name in the Template Name field to help you identify the template later. ​ Choose where the header should appear: • Cover Page only • All Resume Pages • Both the Cover Page and All Resume Pages ​ Upload your company logo using the Upload Header Logo option. ​ Choose whether you want candidate details to be displayed in the header by configuring the Candidate Information option. ​ Under Recruiter Information , add the placeholders you would like to display, such as: • Recruiter Name • Recruiter Email • Recruiter Phone Number • Or any combination of the above ​ Customize the template further by selecting your preferred background color and title color . You can check the preview of how the header will appear from the Preview section at the bottom. Click Submit to save the template once you are done. Create a Footer Template In the Footer Templates section , follow a similar process to create a footer template. Configure the desired footer content, branding elements, placeholders, and styling options, then click Submit to save the template. ​ 📌 Tip: If you would like your teammates to use the same header or footer templates, enable the Share with Teammates toggle before saving. Cover Letter Templates Cover Letter templates allow you to include a customized cover letter along with a candidate's formatted resume or CV. You can create multiple cover letter templates for different clients, industries, or submission requirements and select the appropriate one when formatting resumes. To create a cover letter template: Navigate to the Cover Letter Templates section and click New Cover Letter . Enter a suitable name in the Template Name field to help you identify the template later. ​ In the editor, add the content of your cover letter by either: • Typing the content directly into the editor, or • Pasting your own HTML code into the Source section if you have a pre-designed layout. ​ Use Candidate Placeholders within the cover letter body to automatically populate candidate information from their profile. ​ Customize the cover letter as needed by adding: • Links • Images • Font styles and sizes • Text alignment • Other formatting elements available in the editor Once you're satisfied with the design and content, click Submit to save the template. 📌 Note: When a cover letter template is applied during resume formatting, it is automatically added as the first page of the formatted resume or CV. ​ Watermark Templates Watermark templates allow you to further brand your formatted resumes and CVs by displaying custom text and an optional logo across the document. ​ To create a watermark template: Navigate to the Watermark Templates section and click New Watermark . In the pop-up window, enter a suitable name in the Template Name field. ​ Choose where you would like the watermark to appear: • Cover Page only • All Resume Pages • Both the Cover Page and All Resume Pages ​ In the Watermark Text field, enter the text you want displayed, such as your company name or other branding text. 📌 Note: The Watermark Text field is mandatory and must be completed before the template can be saved. ​ If you would like to include your company logo as part of the watermark, upload it using the Upload Header Logo option. ​ Customize the appearance of the watermark by adjusting: • Font Size • Text Color • Opacity ​ Use the preview section at the bottom of the page to review how the watermark will appear on the formatted resume. Once you are satisfied with the design, click Submit to save the watermark template. Deleting a CV/Resume template To delete a CV/Resume formatting template, go to the CV/Resume Formatting Templates section and locate the template you want to remove. Under the Action column, click on the trash can icon next to the respective template and select Delete . Once deleted, the CV/Resume formatting template will no longer be available for resume formatting. Troubleshooting Problem: The header or footer does not appear on some pages Likely cause: The display option for the header or footer was set only to the cover page or only to resume pages. ​ What to check: Open the relevant header or footer template and review the selection for where it should appear (cover page, all resume pages, or both). ​ Resolution : Update the selection to include both the cover page and resume pages if required, then save the template and reformat the resume. ​ Problem: Candidate details are missing from the header. Likely cause : Candidate information was not enabled or correctly selected in the template. ​ What to check : In the header template, review the Candidate’s Information dropdown. ​ Resolution : Select the appropriate candidate information placeholder, save the template, and reapply it to the resume. Problem: Recruiter contact details do not show in the header Likely cause : Placeholders for recruiter name, email, or phone were not added. ​ What to check : In the Recruiter Information section of the header template, confirm that placeholders for recruiter name, recruiter email, and/or recruiter phone number are included. ​ Resolution : Add the necessary placeholders, save the template, and format the resume again. Problem: Watermark is not visible or is too faint Likely cause : Opacity or text color makes the watermark hard to see. ​ What to check : Open the watermark template and review the opacity , text color , and font size settings. ​ Resolution: Increase the opacity, adjust the color to a more visible shade, and modify font size as needed, then save and preview the watermark again. Problem: Cover letter does not appear as the first page Likely cause : The cover letter was not attached when formatting the resume. ​ What to check : Confirm that a cover letter template was selected when generating the formatted CV. ​ Resolution : Reformat the resume and ensure the appropriate cover letter template is added; it will then appear on the first page of the CV file. FAQs Can I create multiple templates for headers, footers, cover letters, and watermarks? Yes. You can create multiple templates of each type and use them as needed for different clients or roles. Where will the cover letter appear in the formatted CV? When added, the cover letter is placed on the first page of the CV file. Can I use HTML to design my cover letter? Yes. In the cover letter editor, you can paste HTML code into the Source section to control layout and styling. Can I automatically include candidate information in templates? Yes. You can use candidate placeholders in the cover letter body and select candidate information options in the header template to auto-populate data from candidate profiles. How do I share templates with my teammates? Use the Share with Teammates toggle in the template settings. When this toggle is turned on, templates are shared with teammates. Conclusion: By setting up header, footer, cover letter, and watermark templates in Resume Formatting Settings, you can standardize and brand every CV or resume you send with minimal effort. If you need further assistance using these templates in your day-to-day workflow, contact Recruit CRM

t: Creating Invoices for Timesheets (Beta)
s: This article will help you create and manage invoices for approved timesheets.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Default invoice templates
How to create an invoice for timesheets?
How are timesheet statuses updated?
Troubleshooting
Problem: I can't select a timesheet for invoice creation.
Problem: Timesheets remain Unbilled after creating an invoice.
FAQs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows you to create invoices directly from approved timesheets, making the contract billing process faster and more consistent. You can select multiple approved timesheets, generate an invoice, customize invoice details, and send it to your client directly from Recruit CRM. This feature is useful when you want to: Create invoices directly from approved timesheets. Combine multiple eligible timesheets into a single invoice. Review and customize invoices before sending them to clients. Automatically track timesheet billing and collection statuses. Manage contract staffing invoices without relying on separate billing tools or manual exports. Please note: This feature is currently available in Beta and can be enabled upon request. Please contact your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. Default invoice templates Recruit CRM provides two standard templates for creating invoices from timesheets: Contract Job Template: Displays the total hours and billed amount and is suitable for summary-based invoicing or billing cycles that don't require a daily breakdown. Contract Job with Weekdays Template: Displays hours for each day from Monday to Sunday and is best suited for weekly timesheets. You can customize the theme, header, and footer of both templates. However, the table content and fields are fixed and cannot be renamed or edited. You can also reset the templates to their default format whenever needed. How to create an invoice for timesheets? You can begin creating an invoice from either the C ontractor Details Page or the Timesheets section of a Deal. From the Contractor Details Page , navigate to Jobs , open a Contract or Contract to Permanent job, scroll to the Candidate Pipeline , and click View All Timesheets to view the timesheets associated with the contractor for that job Alternatively, navigate to Deals , open a Deal associated with a Contract or Contract to Permanent job, and open the Timesheets section to view the timesheets of contractors associated with the Deal. Select the approved timesheets you want to include in the invoice. Please note: Invoices can only be created from eligible, approved timesheets. Click Create an Invoice . A preview window will display the selected timesheets. Review the details and click Proceed to continue. The system automatically validates the selected timesheets before creating the invoice. The first approved timesheet selected is used as the reference for validating the company and currency. Please note- A timesheet cannot be included in the invoice if it belongs to a different company, isn't approved, has already been billed or collected, is attached to a draft invoice, or uses a different currency. Any ineligible timesheets are automatically excluded from invoice creation. Select the invoice template you want to use and, if required, add a description for internal reference. The description is visible only to recruiters and does not appear on the invoice sent to the client. You can choose between the following two templates: Contract Job: A clean, simple layout showing total hours and the billed amount. Contract Job with Weekdays: A detailed version showing daily hours and corresponding amounts. Click Create Invoice to generate the invoice. Review the complete invoice and make any required adjustments. You can edit client details, update the issue and due dates, remove timesheets, add additional line items, change the invoice template, or add Additional Notes that will appear on the final invoice. Click Show Preview to review how the invoice will appear to the client, and click Save after making any changes. Once the invoice is ready, use the dropdown beside Save to either save it as a draft or send it directly to the client via email. Once an invoice is saved, including it as a draft, it is automatically linked to the corresponding timesheets. How are timesheet statuses updated? Recruit CRM automatically updates timesheet statuses based on the actions performed on their linked invoice. When an invoice is created, the linked timesheets move to Billed . Once the invoice is marked as Paid , the timesheets move to Collected . Timesheets linked to a draft invoice remain Unbilled until the invoice is finalized. If the invoice is deleted, the invoice association is removed, and the linked timesheets return to Unbilled . You can also manually mark timesheets as Paid and add a payout number and payout details. If the timesheet status is changed back to unpaid, the payout number and payout date are automatically cleared. Troubleshooting Problem: I can't select a timesheet for invoice creation. Likely Cause: The timesheet isn't approved or isn't eligible for invoice creation. What to Check: Confirm that the timesheet is approved and hasn't already been billed, collected, or attached to a draft invoice. Resolution: Approve the timesheet and ensure it isn't already associated with another invoice before creating a new invoice. Problem: Timesheets remain Unbilled after creating an invoice. Likely Cause: The invoice has been saved as a draft. What to Check: Check whether the associated invoice is still in draft status. Resolution: Finalize the invoice. The linked timesheets will automatically move to the appropriate billing status. FAQs 1. Can I create an invoice using timesheets with different currencies? No. All timesheets included in an invoice must use the same currency as the first approved timesheet selected. 2. Can I customize the default invoice templates? Yes. You can customize the theme, header, and footer. However, the table content and fields are fixed and cannot be renamed or edited. 3. What happens when I save an invoice as a draft? The invoice is linked to the corresponding timesheets, but the timesheets remain in the Unbilled status until the invoice is finalized. Conclusion Creating invoices directly from approved timesheets simplifies contract billing by allowing you to select eligible timesheets, generate and customize invoices, send them to clients, and automatically track billing statuses in Recruit CRM. This helps maintain accurate billing records and keeps your contract staffing workflow organized. Related Articles How to Create and Manage Timesheets? b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Teams feature allows you to organize users into teams or divisions within Recruit CRM. You can assign users to one or multiple teams, configure team-based access through Custom Roles, and generate reports to track and compare the performance of individual teams. This feature is useful when you want to: Organize users into teams, divisions, or business units. Assign users to multiple teams. Restrict data access to specific teams using Custom Roles. Generate performance reports for individual teams. Compare the performance of multiple teams. Create and Manage Teams Note: The features described in this article are available only on the Business and Enterprise plans. Create a team: Navigate to Admin Settings > Users > Teams . Click on New Team in the top right corner. Enter a name for the team and select the users you want to add to the team. Note: A user can belong to multiple teams simultaneously. Click on the Submit button. Configure team-based access: Recruit CRM allows you to create Custom Roles with Team Only permissions, ensuring users can access only the records that belong to their team. For example, if you have two teams of Recruiters and you wish to give the users on each team access to only the candidate database of their respective teams, you can create a custom role with 'Team Only' view & edit permissions for the candidate module. Similarly, for each action and module, you can set 'Team Only' permission: Navigate to Admin Settings > Users > Roles & Permissions . Create a new Custom Role or edit an existing one. Configure the required module permissions and select Team Only wherever applicable. Save the role and assign it to the appropriate users. Related Article: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions in Recruit CRM. Generate team performance reports: Recruit CRM enables you to generate reports for individual teams and compare their performance over a selected period. Navigate to Reports and Open the Team Performance Report . Select Team Member, choose the required team(s), KPIs, and date range. Generate the report to review or compare team performance. You can also generate Deals by Teammates/Team and Deals Won/Lost reports for individual teams. Related Article: Deals by Teammates/Team & Deals Won/Lost Reports. Troubleshooting Problem: I cannot create a team. Likely Cause: Your subscription plan or user permissions may not support the Teams feature. What to Check: Verify that your organization is on the Business or Enterprise plan and that you have administrator permissions. Resolution: Upgrade your subscription if required or contact your Account Owner for the necessary permissions. Problem: A user cannot access records for their team. Likely Cause: The assigned Custom Role may not have the correct Team Only permissions, or the user may not belong to the appropriate team. What to Check: Confirm that the user has been added to the correct team and that the assigned Custom Role includes the required Team Only permissions. Resolution: Update the user's team membership or modify the Custom Role permissions as needed. FAQ's 1. Can a user belong to more than one team? Yes. Users can belong to multiple teams simultaneously. 2. Can I restrict users to viewing only their team's records? Yes. You can achieve this by assigning a Custom Role with Team Only permissions. 3. Can I compare the performance of multiple teams? Yes. The Team Performance Report allows you to compare multiple teams using selected KPIs and a specified date range. Conclusion: The Teams feature helps you organize users, manage team-based access, and analyze team performance within Recruit CRM. t: Custom Field Parsing Agent
s: Automatically populate candidate custom fields during resume parsing using AI.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Step-by-Step Instructions
2. Enable AI Parsing for Candidate Custom Field:
Enabling it while creating New Custom Candidate Fields:
Enabling AI Parsing for an Existing Candidate Custom Field:
Managing Parsing-Enabled Custom Fields
Enable Parsing for a Child Field
Troubleshooting
b: ✨ What this feature does and when to use it? The Candidate Custom Field Parsing Agent uses AI to analyze resumes and automatically fill candidate custom fields based on the Field Description configured for each field. This works across supported sources such as resume uploads, job board applications, Chrome Extension imports, and other external candidate sources. This feature is especially useful when you: • Want to automatically extract information from resumes and populate selected candidate custom fields during parsing. • Want to reduce manual updates after resume parsing. • Need more consistent candidate data across records. Important Notes The Field Description acts as an instruction for the AI and helps define what information should be extracted from the resume and populated into that field. More specific descriptions generally produce more accurate results. To maintain reliable performance, parsing can be enabled for up to 10 candidate custom fields per account. Fields with parsing enabled display a purple parsing icon in the custom field list for quick identification. ⚙️ Step-by-Step Instructions 1. Go to Admin Settings in Recruit CRM and navigate to the Candidate Fields under Data Customization. ​ ​2. Enable AI Parsing for Candidate Custom Field: Enabling it while creating New Custom Candidate Fields: 1. On the Candidate Data Customization page, click the + New Custom Field button to create a new candidate custom field. ​ 2. Enter the Field Name and choose the appropriate Field Type. Note: 1. Certain field types are not supported for parsing, such as: File type fields Entity type fields Date-time type fields For these field types, the ‘Enable Parsing Agent’ option will not be shown while creating or editing the field. 2. Additionally, Dropdown and Multi-Select fields support parsing only when they contain 100 values or fewer. If these fields contain more than 100 values, the parsing option will remain disabled, and you will not be able to enable parsing for that field. 3. In the Field Description area, write a clear description as the field description helps the AI understand what type of information should be extracted and what kind of value is expected in the field. Make sure that the description is between 30 and 500 characters . The Enable Parsing Agent checkbox remains inactive until a valid description is entered. ​ 💡 Example Field Description: For a certifications field: "Identify and list all professional certifications and industry-specific qualifications mentioned in the candidate's resume." For a notice period field: "Extract the candidate's stated notice period or availability to start, expressed in weeks or months." 4. Once a valid description is added, the Enable Parsing Agent checkbox becomes active. Select the checkbox and save the field to enable AI parsing for that custom field. After the field is saved with parsing enabled, the live parsing counter updates automatically to reflect the total number of parsing-enabled fields in the account. 5. Once the custom field is saved with parsing enabled, the AI will automatically attempt to extract and populate values for that field during resume parsing. Enabling AI Parsing for an Existing Candidate Custom Field: 1. On the Candidate Custom Fields page, locate the existing field you want to update. Open the field for editing by clicking on the pencil icon. 2. Add or update the Field Description to clearly explain what information should be extracted and what kind of value is expected. Ensure it meets the 30 to 500-character requirement. ​ Once a valid description is present, the Enable Parsing Agent checkbox becomes active. Select it to enable parsing, or clear it to disable parsing for this field. ​ 3. Review the live parsing counter to ensure the total does not exceed 10 enabled fields , and save your changes. 📌 Note: You cannot change the field type of an existing candidate custom field. Managing Parsing-Enabled Custom Fields Recruit CRM allows AI parsing to be enabled for up to 10 candidate custom fields per account. Follow these steps to manage the parsing limit: Go to Admin Settings → Data Customization → Candidate Custom Fields . Review the live parsing counter displayed on the page (for example: 07/10 ) to see how many fields currently have parsing enabled. If the maximum limit has been reached: Open any parsing-enabled custom field that is no longer required. Disable the Enable Parsing Agent option for that field. Save the changes to make that parsing slot available again. You can then enable parsing for another custom field as needed. 📌 Please note: Once the limit of 10 parsing-enabled fields is reached, the Enable Parsing Agent option becomes unavailable for additional fields until an existing parsing-enabled field is disabled. Enable Parsing for a Child Field If a candidate custom field is configured as a child field, the parent field must first be configured correctly before parsing can be enabled for the child field. Before enabling parsing for a child field, ensure that the parent field: Has a valid Field Description between 30 and 500 characters. Has parsing enabled for that field. If these conditions are not met, the following message will appear: “Add description and enable parsing for parent field to parse child field”. Complete the parent field configuration first, then return to the child field and enable parsing. 🛠️ Troubleshooting Problem: “Enable Parsing Agent” checkbox is disabled and cannot be selected Likely cause: No valid Field Description has been entered, or the description does not meet character limits. ​ What to check: Confirm that the Field Description field is filled and check that the description meets the minimum and maximum character limits: Minimum: 30 characters Maximum: 500 characters. ​ Resolution: Edit the Field Description to be within the allowed character range. Once valid, confirm that the Enable Parsing Agent checkbox becomes active and then select it. Problem: Cannot enable parsing for another custom field Likely cause: The account has already reached the maximum of ten candidate custom fields with parsing enabled. ​ What to check: Review the live parsing counter on the Candidate Custom Fields page. ​ Resolution: Identify fields that currently have parsing enabled but are less critical. Edit one or more of those fields and clear the Enable Parsing Agent checkbox to reduce the count. Then enable parsing on the new field you want to prioritize. Problem: AI parsing is enabled, but the custom field remains empty after resume parsing Likely cause: The resume does not contain information matching the field description. The Field Description is too vague or unclear for the AI to interpret. What to check: Review the Field Description and confirm it clearly states what information should be extracted and in what form. Check the resume to verify that the expected data actually appears. Resolution: Improve the Field Description to be more specific about the information and value format. Test with another resume that clearly includes the target information. Problem: Unable to change the field type of an existing candidate custom field Likely cause: Existing system behavior does not allow editing the field type of already created candidate custom fields. Resolution: Keep the existing field type as is. If a different field type is required, create a new candidate custom field with the desired field type and, if needed, enable the parse agent for that new field. ❓ FAQs Why is the “Enable Parsing Agent” option disabled? The “Enable Parsing Agent” option can remain disabled for multiple reasons: A valid Field Description has not been added. The Field Description contains fewer than 30 characters. The field type is File, Entity or Date-Time, which are not supported for parsing. The Dropdown or Multi-Select field contains more than 100 values. The account has already reached the maximum limit of 10 parsing-enabled custom fields. Why is the Field Description required? The Field Description helps the AI understand what type of information should be extracted from resumes and what kind of value is expected in the field. This additional context helps improve parsing accuracy and ensures the extracted information is mapped correctly. Can existing custom fields also be configured for parsing? Yes. Users can edit existing custom fields, add a valid field description, and enable parsing for those fields. How can users identify which fields have parsing enabled? Fields that have parsing enabled will display a purple parsing icon in the custom fields list. How many candidate custom fields can I enable for AI parsing? You can enable AI parsing for a maximum of 10 candidate custom fields per account. The live parsing counter on the Candidate Custom Fields page shows how many fields currently have parsing enabled, for example 04/10. When the limit is reached, you must disable parsing on an existing field before you can enable it on a new one.

t: Custom Roles - Access Control & Permissions In Recruit CRM
s: Create roles with custom access and permission options to control what each user can see and do within Recruit CRM.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
How to Create a Custom Role? 🎯
Configure module-level permissions
Configure report visibility
Configure bulk actions and admin permissions
Save the role
Clone an existing role:
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Custom roles in Recruit CRM let you define exactly what actions users in a role can take and what data they can see. You can configure permissions separately for each module, including whether users can view, create, edit, delete, change ownership, or manage files. These roles can be edited or updated at any time to adjust the level of access or control you want to provide. Eg. For a team manager, you can create a custom role to grant them access to generate specific reports to analyze the performance of their team. You can also create and manage Teams within Recruit CRM and create custom roles for each team based on their responsibilities or job functions. Click here to learn how to create Teams in Recruit CRM You can use this when: You want to restrict what different users can view, create, edit, or delete in Recruit CRM. You need team managers to access specific reports without giving them full admin rights. Before you begin This feature is available only on the Business and Enterprise plans. By default, only the Account Owner can create custom roles. You should have clarity on: Which modules each role needs access to (for example: Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs, Deals, Placements, Invoices, Email Templates). Whether users in a role should access all records, only team records, only their own records, or none for each module. Which users need access to specific admin settings or bulk actions (like export to CSV). How to Create a Custom Role? 🎯 To create a new custom role, go to Admin Settings > Users and switch to the Roles & Permissions tab from the tab options at the top. Click on the +New Role button in the top right corner to create a new custom role. ​ Type the name of the role in the role name field and then configure permissions as per your requirements. ​ Configure module-level permissions For each module (such as Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs, Deals, Placements, Invoices, Email Templates), select the appropriate permissions to allow users to: View records Create records Edit records Delete records Change ownership Manage files ​ For each module, choose one of the four access levels: Everything : The user can view, edit, and delete all records in that module across the database. Team only : The user can view, edit, and delete only those records that belong to their team or themselves. Owned only : The user can view, edit, and delete only the records they personally own. Nothing : The user cannot view, edit, or delete any records in that module. ​ These permissions will also impact the user's ability to see, create, edit and delete Notes, Call Logs, Tasks and Meetings inside each entity. ​ E.g. If a user has permission to edit only candidates they own, they won't be able to edit the notes inside a candidate that belongs to someone else, even if the note was added by the user themselves. ❌ If a record from a specific entity (candidates, companies, etc.) doesn't have an owner, the user will not be able to edit or delete the Notes, Call Logs, Tasks or Meetings. Configure report visibility In the Report Visibility section, turn the toggles on or off to control which reports the role can see. ​ For the Team Performance report, choose whether users in this role see: Everything Team only Owned only Nothing Configure bulk actions and admin permissions In the Permissions area, set controls for bulk actions such as export to CSV : Only users with the permission to export to CSV will be able to export data from your database. ​ Choose whether users in this role have access to Admin Settings : No access at all to the admin settings; or Access to specific modules in the admin panel, such as data customization for an administrator-type role, while restricting other modules. Save the role After assigning all required permissions, click the Save Role button at the bottom of the page to save your new custom role. Clone an existing role: On the Roles and Permissions page, locate the role you want to copy. ​ Click on the three dots next to that existing role to open the role options menu. ​ Use the clone option in this menu to duplicate the existing role and then adjust permissions as needed. ​ Troubleshooting Problem: A user on the custom role cannot edit notes, call logs, tasks, or meetings on certain records. Likely cause: Their module access is set to Owned only or Team only , and they do not own the record (or the record has no owner). ​ What to check: The user’s role settings for the relevant module (for example, Candidates or Companies). Whether the record has an owner and whether that owner matches the user or their team. ​ Resolution: Adjust the user’s role permissions to a broader access level if appropriate (for example, from Owned only to Team only or Everything ). Assign a correct owner to records that currently have no owner. ​ Problem: A user cannot see or access a particular module (for example, Deals or Invoices). Likely cause: The role for that user has the module set to Nothing or only limited permissions. ​ What to check: The role’s permissions for that specific module, including view rights. ​ Resolution: Update the role to grant at least view access for that module if the user needs it. Problem: A user is unable to export data to CSV. Likely cause: The user’s role does not include permission to export to CSV. ​ What to check: The bulk action and export-related settings in the role’s Permissions area. ​ Resolution: Enable the export to CSV permission for that role if exporting is required for their work. ​ Problem: A user cannot access admin settings. Likely cause: The role is configured with no access to admin settings. ​ What to check: The Permissions section for admin access within the role. ​ Resolution: Grant access to the specific admin modules that the user needs (for example, data customization), while keeping other modules restricted. ​ FAQs Q1: Who can create custom roles in Recruit CRM? By default, only the account owner can create custom roles. Q2: Can I edit a custom role after creating it? Yes. You can edit or update custom roles at any time to adjust the level of access or control you want to provide. Q3: Can I customize default roles? Only custom roles can be customized. Default roles cannot be modified in the same way. Conclusion: Custom roles, access control, and permissions in Recruit CRM give you precise control over what each user can see and do, helping you align access with responsibilities and protect your data. s: You can replace Recruit CRM’s default job URL with a custom link for a seamless, branded candidate experience across all jobs.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

What happens if I don’t configure a custom URL?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? With this Custom Job Application Form URL feature, you can define a custom domain and URL pattern for job application forms, perfect for seamless branding and candidate experience. The custom URL replaces the default Recruit CRM job application form URL across multiple touchpoints, ensuring consistency and professionalism. ​ This feature is particularly helpful for users using Recruit Craft, custom APIs for career pages/site, and for directing applicants via job boards and XML feeds. Note: Only the Account Owner, Admins, and users with custom permissions can set up the custom URL. Choosing the Right URL Based on Your Setup Depending on how your organization hosts job pages: For this feature to work accurately, you need to use our API-built or RecruitCraft-powered pages under your company domain as the base URL. If you have integrated Recruit CRM’s job listings using an iframe on your website, this feature will not apply directly. Note: ✅ Valid URLs: https://recruitcraft.io/site/product/ API-Based Career Pages Are Supported If your company has built a custom career site using the Recruit CRM API , you can use that URL here. These pages are considered part of your own domain and fully support job slugs. Example: https://careers.yourcompany.com/ ​ ❌ Do not use any Recruit CRM hosted links , for example: https://jobs.recruitcrm.io/job/software-engineer https://yourcompany.recruitcrm.io/job/... These URLs are generated by Recruit CRM’s own hosting service and cannot be reused as custom URLs. Users who don’t have their own API-based job listings site cannot use this feature. Where does the custom URL appear? Once set, the custom URL will replace Recruit CRM’s default link in: Job boards such as Broadbean, CV Library, and TotalJobs XML feeds API endpoints like Find Job by Slug, Search for Jobs, Get Job Application Form, Show All Jobs The "Copy Job Application Form URL" button in the job details page. Public job page application links Note: As of now, this functionality is not available for free job boards. How to set up a Custom Job Application URL? The example in this article demonstrates the setup using a sample site built with RecruitCraft. Know more about integrating RCRM with Recruit Craft Only Admins can configure this setting. 1. Go to Admin Settings . Under Job Settings click on Public Job Page Settings ​ 2. Open the Job Page Integration section scroll down to Custom Job Application URLs and toggle the setting ON ​ 3. In the Configure Custom Branded URL field, enter your company’s base career site link for example in this case: https://recruitcraft.io/site/product ​ Recruit CRM will automatically append each job’s slug to this path. (You don’t need to type {job_slug} manually.) ​ The system immediately shows an example job URL below using the latest updated job’s data, confirming how it will appear for candidates. ​ 4. You can turn on the "Append a job field to the end of the URL" option to add one more job field as a placeholder (only text or dropdown fields are supported). Note: You can append the job field only if you have the same appended field in your base job application form URL on your careers page. ​ ​ Notes: This is a global setting that applies to all jobs in your account. ​ {job_slug} will be added mandatorily in the job application link once you configure it and only one additional job field can be added. A slug is a unique identifier for an entity in Recruit CRM, found in the URL after the last “/” on its profile page. ​ Spaces in placeholder values will be converted to hyphens (for example Marketing Manager becomes Marketing-Manager). ​ When you turn the toggle off, the system will revert to using Recruit CRM’s default application links, but your previous domain and configuration will be saved in case you toggle it back on. ​ The system checks for correct URL format before saving. ​ Recruit CRM does not validate the authenticity or correctness of the custom URL entered by the user. 6. Once the toggle is enabled and a URL is configured, the system will automatically replace Recruit CRM’s default job application form URL with the custom URL across all applicable locations, regardless of whether the target URL leads to a valid destination or contains a valid job. ​ It is entirely the user's responsibility to ensure the configured URL is functional, secure, and aligned with their job application URL flow. ​ Error Message for Incorrect Custom Job Application URL If the URL entered in the custom job application field is incorrect, candidates will see a "404 error: This page could not be found" when they try to open the job application form. ​ Disabling the custom URL Turn the Custom Job Application Form URL toggle OFF to immediately go back to Recruit CRM’s default job application links. ​ FAQ's What happens if I don’t configure a custom URL? No, currently only one additional job field (text or dropdown) can be used with the required {job_slug}. Can I add more than one additional placeholder in the URL? No, currently only one additional job field (text or dropdown) can be used with the required {job_slug}. Does the feature work for jobs accessed via APIs or XML feeds? Yes, once configured, the custom URL will reflect across all supported APIs and feeds. Can I set different URLs for different jobs? No, this is a global setting and applies account-wide to all jobs. What happens if a placeholder field is blank or has spaces? If a field is blank, the URL will still be generated but that portion may be empty. If it contains spaces, they’ll be automatically converted to hyphens (e.g., “Marketing Manager” → “Marketing-Manager”). Does Recruit CRM verify the URL I configure? No. Recruit CRM does not validate or check the availability, correctness, or security of the custom URL you enter. The system assumes the URL is valid and will use it as-is. Make sure your destination page is live, functional, and supports your application process. Can I use this with a career site built using the Recruit CRM API? Yes! You can use any API-built or RecruitCraft-powered page under your company domain as the base URL. Conclusion: The Custom Job Application URL feature helps you provide a consistent and branded application experience by replacing Recruit CRM’s default job links with URLs based on your Recruit Craft-powered or API-based career site. Once configured, the custom URL is automatically used across supported channels, while Recruit CRM handles job slugs and optional job fields based on your settings. Recruit CRM also lets you customize Job Application Forms with fields of your choice! To set up your Job Application Form, follow the steps below: First, Click on Admin Settings Then Click the Job Application Form Settings button. Once you’re in, you'll see the first tab as "General Page Settings", where you can set the following things: Job Description or Job Application 📝 Choose what you wish to show first. Choose whether you wish to show the job description or the job application directly on your application form. Turn the toggle ON to show the Job Description on the job application form and OFF to remove the job description from the job application form. How to choose which logo appears on your Job Application Form? You can control which logo shows up on your job application form: your Account Logo , the Job’s Company Logo , or No Logo . 1. Choosing the Logo for an Existing Job Open the Job >>> Click the pencil icon to access the Job Application Form, and under Default Job Application Form Visibility, choose whether you want to show the Account Logo, Company Logo, or No Logo, and click 'Save'. ​ 2. Setting a Default Logo for All Newly Created Jobs Go to Admin Settings and click on Job Fields . Locate Default Job Application Form Visibility . ​ Choose the logo option you wish to apply by default, and turn on the toggle if you want users to select a logo while creating new jobs. You can mark it as the default for all jobs so it automatically applies whenever a new job is created. Click save. ​ Social Media Icons Hide or show the social media share icons on your job application form. Turn the toggle on or off depending on whether you want to show the social media icons on the Job Application form or not. Automated “Thank you for applying” emails You can send Automated Emails to candidates who apply for jobs using your online job application forms. 1. First off, you'll need to create an email template for the automated email you send out. Here's how you can create Email Templates for automated workflows. 2. Now choose the template. 3. You can also choose the sender from your users who have connected their emails to Recruit CRM. Setting-up candidate terms Set your Candidate Terms that candidates will need to agree to before submitting their application forms. GDPR needs to be turned on in Account Settings for this to appear. Job application form fields The next step is selecting the fields that you want on the Job Application Form Switch to the "Job Application Field Settings" tab from the top. You can reorder the sequence of the fields by dragging the fields up / down. You can set the field labels to words in your language and also add a placeholder text by clicking on the edit button next to the field label. You can also choose which fields you want to be mandatory on the application form and turn off the visibility for ones you don't wish to show. Adding Job associated files to the Application - these are job-specific files that you can ask the candidate to upload for each job. Once this is done, you'll have the following option to select the candidate questions for each job while creating/editing a job. 3. The questions and their answers can be found under the "Candidate Questions" tab on the candidate's profile. Note: Currently the job application forms are not disabled if the account is inactive (users are active but don’t log in to the system). We only disable the forms and delete the setting on account deactivation. In this case, users have to log in and disable the job application URLs to disable the application forms. t: Customize your content with the fonts available in Recruit CRM
s: Discover the different fonts you can use in Recruit CRM to enhance the appearance of your content!
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

2. Use the source code

How operating systems, devices or browsers affect the font:

Problem: My custom font looks different on another device.
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows you to customize the appearance of your content using different fonts. You can select WebSafe fonts directly from the in-app editor or use custom HTML source code for additional font options. Font customization is available when creating content such email templates , job descriptions , candidate summaries, or executive search reports. This feature is useful when you want to: Customize the appearance of your content. Choose fonts directly from the Recruit CRM editor. Apply custom fonts using HTML source code. How to change fonts in Recruit CRM You can customize fonts in Recruit CRM in two ways: 1. Use the in-app editor Open the content you want to create or edit in Recruit CRM. From the formatting toolbar above the text editor, click the Font dropdown. Select your preferred font from the available options. Please note: Only WebSafe fonts are available in this dropdown to ensure consistent viewing across all devices, operating systems, and browsers. 2. Use the source code Open the content you want to create or edit. Click the Source icon from the formatting toolbar. Enter or paste your custom HTML source code into the editor and apply your changes. Please note: While you can use any font in the source code, we recommend sticking to WebSafe fonts (such as Arial, Times New Roman, Verdana) to ensure consistent appearance across different devices, operating systems, and browsers. What happens when you use non-WebSafe fonts? How operating systems, devices or browsers affect the font: When content is delivered/accessed, the operating system, browser, or device checks if the specified font is available. If not, it substitutes it with a similar available font. Example: Using non-WebSafe fonts like Calibri, Ink-Free, Roboto, Proxima-Nova, or Ronnia may cause inconsistencies in how your content appears to users depending on their device, operating system, or browser. To ensure consistent styling and avoid potential visibility issues, we recommend using WebSafe fonts whenever possible. Troubleshooting Problem: My custom font looks different on another device. Likely Cause: The selected font isn't available or supported on the device, operating system, or browser being used. What to Check: Confirm whether you're using a non-WebSafe font through the source code. Resolution: Use a WebSafe font to ensure a more consistent appearance across devices, operating systems, and browsers. FAQs 1. Where can I customize fonts in Recruit CRM? You can customize fonts in supported content editors, including email templates, job descriptions, candidate summaries, and executive search reports. 2. Can I use fonts that aren't available in the Font dropdown? Yes. You can apply other fonts using custom HTML source code through the Source option in the formatting toolbar. 3. Will custom fonts always appear the same for every user? No. If a font isn't available on the recipient's device, operating system, or browser, it may be replaced with a similar available font. Conclusion Recruit CRM provides two ways to customize fonts: selecting WebSafe fonts directly from the in-app editor or applying additional fonts through custom HTML source code. For the most consistent appearance across devices, operating systems, and browsers, we recommend using WebSafe fonts whenever possible. t: Customize Your Hiring Pipeline And Create Multiple Hiring Pipelines
s: Create and customize your master hiring pipeline and also add multiple custom hiring pipelines.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin:
How to Customize the Master Hiring Pipeline 💫
How to Create a Custom Hiring Pipeline? 👷
How to Choose the Hiring Pipeline for Each Job? 💼

Troubleshooting
FAQs
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The multiple hiring pipeline feature in Recruit CRM lets you: Maintain a master hiring pipeline that contains all stages you might use across jobs. Create custom hiring pipelines that use selected stages from the master pipeline. This supports flexible, role-specific workflows while preserving consistent tracking, automation, and reporting. You can use this when: You hire for different types of roles and need separate hiring pipelines for each. You need to control which stages clients can see and use when reviewing submitted candidates. Before you begin: Plan availability: Pro plan users can have one master (default) hiring pipeline and create one custom hiring pipeline. Business plan users can create multiple custom hiring pipelines. Permissions: Only users in admin or account owner roles can customize the hiring pipeline. Users on the Business plan and above can also create custom roles with access to the hiring pipeline. System-locked stages: Recruit CRM includes default stages that are system-locked across both the master hiring pipeline and all custom hiring pipelines. These locked stages include: Assigned, Applied, Placed (final stage in the pipeline). Locked stages cannot be edited, renamed, reordered, or removed in any pipeline.They are locked because the platform relies on them for core system functions such as application tracking, workflow automation, and consistent reporting across all jobs. Maintaining these stages ensures data accuracy and prevents workflow inconsistencies. Dependency : All stages you want to use in any custom hiring pipeline must first be added to the master hiring pipeline. How to Customize the Master Hiring Pipeline 💫 Go to the Admin settings. ​ Under CRM Process, click Hiring Pipeline. ​ Click the Edit button at the top right to start adding or changing hiring stages. ​ Click the blue Add Stage button to add a new hiring stage. ​ Type the name of the new hiring stage in the field provided. To reorder a stage, click and drag the small equal-to icon next to the hiring stage to its new position in the pipeline. ​ You will also see a checkbox with the option "Let clients use" next to each hiring stage. If you have ticked the checkbox then, once you share your online " Submit Candidate " link, your clients will be able to move the candidates across the hiring stages you have ticked ​ To remove a hiring stage, click the X icon on the right of that stage. ​ After all additions, removals, and changes are complete, click Submit to save the updated master hiring pipeline. How to Create a Custom Hiring Pipeline? 👷 Make sure all the hiring stages you need are already added to the master hiring pipeline. ​ Click the green Create New Hiring Pipeline button. ​ Enter a name for the new custom hiring pipeline. ​ Use the green Visibility toggle next to each stage to turn visibility on for stages you want to include in this custom pipeline, and off for stages you want to exclude. ​ Reorder the visible hiring stages by dragging them into the desired sequence in the pipeline. Once all changes are made, click Submit to save the new custom hiring pipeline. ​ After saving, you can mark this custom pipeline as the default pipeline if desired. ​ How to Choose the Hiring Pipeline for Each Job? 💼 When adding a new job, the hiring pipeline marked as default will be selected automatically. ​ For existing jobs, click on the pencil icon to open the job in edit mode to change the hiring pipeline. ​ Within the job edit view, locate the hiring pipeline option. ​ When editing a job, note that the pipeline currently marked as default will still appear as the default choice and then Save to update the job. ​ Handling warnings when changing pipelines on existing jobs While selecting a new pipeline when editing a Job the system will give you a warning if some of the candidates in the job are in hiring stages that are not available in the new pipeline selected: You can then move the candidates to one of the stages available in the new pipeline selected and then make the changes. Troubleshooting Problem: Clients cannot move candidates between certain stages Likely cause: The Let Clients Use checkbox is not enabled for those stages. What to check: In the master hiring pipeline, review the Let Clients Use setting for each relevant stage. Resolution: Tick the Let Clients Use checkbox for the stages you want clients to manage, then save the pipeline. Problem: Cannot create more than one custom hiring pipeline Likely cause: Account is on the Pro plan, which allows only one custom pipeline in addition to the master pipeline. What to check: Confirm the current plan (Pro or Business). Resolution: On Pro, manage within the one allowed custom pipeline. To create multiple custom pipelines, upgrade to the Business plan. FAQs Who can customize the hiring pipeline in Recruit CRM? Only users in admin or account owner roles can customize the hiring pipeline. On the Business plan and above, custom roles with access to the hiring pipeline can also be created. What is the difference between the master hiring pipeline and custom hiring pipelines? The master hiring pipeline contains all possible hiring stages and is the source for stages used in custom hiring pipelines. Custom hiring pipelines are built by turning visibility on or off for selected stages from the master pipeline and reordering them as needed. Why are some stages like Assigned, Applied, and Placed locked? These stages are system-locked because the platform relies on them for core system functions such as application tracking, workflow automation, and consistent reporting across all jobs. They cannot be edited, renamed, reordered, or removed. Conclusion: By configuring your master hiring pipeline and setting up custom hiring pipelines, you can tailor Recruit CRM to match different hiring workflows while keeping core tracking and reporting consistent. b: What this feature does and when to use it? You can post all open jobs on your company website or Job Boards to get applicants directly into your database. Recruit CRM also lets you customize Job Application Forms with fields of your choice and you can control the information collected during the application process. It helps you create a consistent, branded application experience while ensuring applicants are captured directly in your Recruit CRM database. You can use this feature when you want to: Customize application form fields, labels, placeholders, field order, visibility, and mandatory requirements. Configure general application page settings, including job description visibility, social sharing options, and candidate terms. Configure language and proficiency fields, including default languages and proficiency levels. Control which logo appears on job application forms, including the account logo, job company logo, or no logo. Configure General Page Settings The Job Application Form Settings page is the central location for managing your job application experience in Recruit CRM. From here, you can configure how application forms look and behave, including page settings, form fields, automated emails, candidate questions, branding, and job-specific application forms. To access these settings, navigate to Admin Settings → Job Settings → Job Application Form Settings . The first tab you will see is General Page Settings , which controls the overall appearance and behavior of your job application forms. ​ 1. Job Description or Job Application: From this section, you can control what candidates see first when they open your Job. You can choose whether to: • Display the Job Description first, allowing candidates to review the role details before applying • Display the Job Application Form directly, allowing candidates to start their application immediately You can also control whether the job description appears at all on the application page. • Turn the toggle ON to display the job description on the job application form. • Turn the toggle OFF to hide the job description from the job application form completely. This allows you to tailor the application experience based on your hiring process and the amount of information you want candidates to review before applying. 2. Social Media Share Icons: This setting allows you to control whether candidates can see social media sharing options on your job application form. When enabled, social media share icons will be displayed on the application page, allowing visitors to easily share the job opening across supported social platforms and help increase the visibility of your job postings. To configure this setting: • Turn the toggle ON to display social media share icons on the job application form. • Turn the toggle OFF to hide the social media share icons from the job application form. 3. Automated "Thank You for Applying" Emails: Recruit CRM allows you to automatically send a confirmation email to candidates when they submit an application through the job application form. This helps acknowledge their application instantly and provides a better candidate experience. To configure automated application emails: First, create an email template that will be used as the automated "Thank You for Applying" email. Here's how you can create Email Templates for automated workflows. In the General Page Settings section, select the email template you want to use. If you do not have a suitable template yet, you can create one and then select it here. Choose the email account that should send these automated emails. You can select from users who have connected their email accounts to Recruit CRM. Once configured, candidates who apply through your job application forms will automatically receive the selected email from the chosen sender account. This can be used to: • Confirm that the application was successfully received. • Share next steps in your hiring process. • Provide additional information about the role or company. • Deliver a more professional and responsive candidate experience. 4. Candidate Terms and Policies: This section allows you to configure the terms and policies that candidates must review and agree to before submitting their job application. You can customize: • Candidate Terms – Terms and conditions related to candidate consent, data collection, data processing, and GDPR compliance. • Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Policy – The policy text displayed to candidates regarding equal opportunity and non-discriminatory hiring practices. The content entered here is shown directly on the job application form, allowing candidates to review the information before completing their application. 📌 Please Note: • For the Candidate Terms section to be visible on the job application form, the GDPR Compliance toggle must be enabled in Account Settings . • For the Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Policy to appear on the job application form, the EEO toggle must be enabled in Account Settings . If either setting is disabled, the corresponding section will not be displayed to candidates on the application form. To configure these settings: Enter your GDPR-related terms, general Candidate terms, and consent language in the Candidate Terms box. Add or update your Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Policy text as required. Save your changes. ​ 5.Customize Button, Link Labels, and Additional Form Settings: The Customize Button & Link Labels section allows you to customize the text displayed throughout the job application form, helping you tailor the candidate experience to match your preferred terminology, language, or branding. You can customize: • Button labels • Link text • Field labels • Other application form text displayed to candidates To update any label or text: Locate the item you want to customize. Click the Edit button next to it. Enter the text you want to display. Save your changes. ​ You can also control the visibility of additional sections on the application form from here. ​ Simply turn the corresponding toggle ON or OFF to show or hide: • Note for Candidate – Displays additional instructions or information to candidates on the application form. • SMS Terms and Conditions – Displays SMS consent terms when applicable. ​ These settings allow you to further customize the application experience while ensuring candidates see the information that is most relevant to your hiring process. Configure Job Application Form Fields Settings The Job Application Form Field Settings tab allows you to control which fields appear on your application forms and how candidates interact with them. To access these settings, navigate to Admin Settings → Job Settings → Job Application Form Settings and then switch to the Job Application Form Field Settings. ​ 1. Manage Field Visibility and Order: Open the Job Application Form Field Settings tab to view all available application fields. ​ You can choose which fields should be displayed on the application form and hide any fields that are not required. To change the order in which fields appear, simply drag and drop them into the desired sequence. You can also mark fields as mandatory to ensure candidates provide the required information before submitting their application. ​ 2.Customize Labels and Text: To customize a field, click the Edit button next to the field name. From here, you can: • Rename field labels to match your preferred terminology or language. • Add placeholder text to guide candidates while filling out the form. These customizations help align the application experience with your organization's branding and communication style. ​ 3. Add Job-Associated Files to the Application Form: Job-associated files allow you to collect additional documents from candidates that are specific to a particular job opening. These files are configured at the job level and can be used to request information that may not be relevant for every role, such as certifications, portfolios, work samples, licenses, or other supporting documents. When a candidate applies for the job, they will be prompted to upload the required files as part of their application. This is especially useful when different jobs require different supporting documents, allowing you to tailor the application process to the requirements of each position. b: What this feature does and when to use it? Contact Stages help you track where each contact is in your sales pipeline. You can customize these stages to match your business process, set a default stage for new contacts, and use them to organize and filter contacts more efficiently. This feature is useful when you want to: Create custom contact stages for your sales process. Set a default contact stage for new contacts. Update a contact's stage as they progress through your pipeline. Filter contacts based on their current stage. Customize and use Contact Stages Please note: Only Account Owners, Admins, and users with permission to the Contact Stages section in Admin Settings can create or customize Contact Stages. To customize your Contact Stages: Navigate to Admin Settings , under CRM Process Customization, click Contact Stages . Click the Pencil icon to edit your contact stages. To create a new stage, scroll down and click Add Stage . Enter the stage name. If you'd like it to be the default stage for newly created contacts, select the Default checkbox. You can also drag and reorder existing stages to match your preferred workflow. Click Save to apply your changes. To delete a contact stage , click the – (minus) icon next to the stage you want to remove. ​ 📌 Please note: Once a contact stage is deleted, any contacts currently assigned to that stage will have their Contact Stage set to Empty . What to Check: Verify that you're logged in as an Account Owner, Admin, or on a custom role with permission to access Contact Stages section in Admin Settings. Resolution: Only Account Owner and Admin users can create, edit, reorder, or delete Contact Stages. Contact your Account Owner or Admin if you need assistance. By creating meaningful stages, setting a default stage, and filtering contacts based on their progress, you can easily monitor and manage your client relationships. t: Customizing Fields on the Details Page
s: This article explains how to customize fields on a record’s profile page in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
Step-by-step instructions to replace a field
Step-by-step instructions to Add/Remove or Reorder fields
Troubleshooting
FAQs
1. Does customizing the candidate profile fields affect other users?
2. Can I use these steps for companies, contacts, and jobs as well?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Customizing fields on the profile page lets you reorder, replace, and add the fields shown in the Information Overview section for all record types, including candidates, companies, contacts, and jobs. This helps you display the most relevant information and customize the view based on your needs and workflows. Use this feature when you want to make record pages easier to scan and more relevant for your team to: • Highlight key details like company, job title, or location for faster decision-making. • Standardize layouts across your team for consistency. • Show role-specific data such as skills or certifications. • Remove unnecessary fields to reduce clutter. Before you begin: • Ensure you have access to the relevant record type (candidates, companies, contacts, or jobs) • The steps below use the candidate profile as an example, but apply to all record types • Decide which fields you want to display, reorder, or hide before making changes. Step-by-step instructions to replace a field 1. From the candidate list page, open the specific candidate. 2. To replace any existing field on the profile: Hover your mouse over the area next to the field name in the Information Overview section. When the pencil icon appears next to the field name, click it. 3. In the configuration box, click the Replace field option at the bottom of the box. • From the list, select the new field you want to use in place of the current one. • After selecting the desired field, click Replace . The selected field will immediately replace the existing one in the profile view Step-by-step instructions to Add/Remove or Reorder fields 1. On the candidate profile page, click Customize Information Overview in the Information Overview section. You can access it by clicking the icon in the top right corner of the section. 2. Within the Customize Information Overview panel: To increase the number of fields visible , adjust the number of visible fields using the control provided. To add a new field , select any additional field you want to display from the available list. To reorder fields , drag and drop the fields into your desired order. To remove a field , simply deselect it by unchecking its checkbox. After arranging the position of all fields and selecting any new fields that need to be added, click Save to apply your changes. Once saved, you will see a confirmation message indicating that your view was updated successfully. The Information Overview layout updates to reflect your selected fields and order. Troubleshooting 1. Problem You cannot see a specific field when trying to replace, reorder, or add it. ​ ​ Likely cause The field’s visibility is turned off in Admin Settings for that record type. ​ ​ What to check • In Admin Settings , open the relevant record type (candidates, companies, contacts, or jobs). • Confirm that the field exists and that its visibility toggle is turned on. ​ Resolution path • Turn the field visibility on (or toggle it off and on again). • Click Save in Admin Settings. • Return to the profile page and open Customize Information Overview again to check if the field now appears. 2. Problem You changed the number of visible fields, but the layout doesn’t look updated. Likely cause Changes were not saved after adjusting the number of visible fields or reordering. What to check • Confirm that you clicked Save in the Customize Information Overview panel. • Check for the confirmation message that the view was updated successfully. ​ Resolution path • Reopen Customize Information Overview , verify your selections and order, and click Save again. • Refresh the profile page to confirm the updated layout. 3. Problem After replacing a field, the information shown looks incorrect or incomplete. Likely cause The new field type differs from the old one, or the data was not updated after the replacement. What to check • Review the new field’s content on the profile page. • Confirm whether the new field expects different data (for example, text vs. date). ​ Resolution path • Edit the field on the profile page. • Add, correct, or confirm the information. • Click Save to ensure the new field stores the correct data. FAQs 1. Does customizing the candidate profile fields affect other users? No, customizing the fields and their order on the details page cannot affect how other users see that record type. However, the account can set a default view for all users. 2. Can I use these steps for companies, contacts, and jobs as well? Yes. The same steps for replacing, reordering, and adding fields apply to all record types, including candidates, companies, contacts, and jobs. 3. What happens to existing data when I replace a field? When you replace a field, the new field type is applied. You should review, edit, or add information in the new field and click Save to confirm the data. 4. Can I undo changes to the field order or visibility? You can reopen Customize Information Overview at any time to change the visible fields and their order again. You can click on the Reset to Default button at the bottom to undo all your changes. Conclusion: Customizing profile fields helps you focus on the most relevant information and create a cleaner, more efficient workflow. h: What this feature does & when to use it?
How to customize Kanban Cards for clients

The fields displayed on an existing job have changed
FAQs

2. What happens to Kanban Cards that were previously customized for individual jobs?
3. Do the Kanban View and List View follow the same field-setting behavior?
b: What this feature does & when to use it? The Fields Shared with Clients settings allow you to control which candidate information is visible to clients when candidates are shared through the Online Candidate List. The Kanban Card and List View field settings now follow consistent behavior. Any fields selected or deselected under Admin Settings → Fields Shared with Clients apply to all existing and new jobs . This feature is useful when you want to: Control which candidate information is visible to clients. Customize the additional fields displayed on Kanban cards. Maintain consistent field visibility across the Kanban View and List View. Apply the same field settings across all existing and new jobs. How to customize Kanban Cards for clients Go to Admin Settings → Fields Shared with Clients and click Customize Kanban Card . Select the fields you want to display on the candidate cards. Rearrange the selected fields by dragging and dropping them into your preferred order. You can add up to five additional fields to each Kanban card. These are displayed in addition to the name, social media profile, phone number, email, resume, and remarks fields that are already available by default in the header or footer. Note: Any field selected or deselected under Admin Settings → Fields Shared with Clients applies to all existing and new jobs . If a Kanban Card was previously customized for a specific job, it will no longer be treated as an exception. The settings configured in Admin Settings will apply instead. Troubleshooting The fields displayed on an existing job have changed Likely Cause: Kanban Card field settings now follow the same behavior as the List View settings. Previously customized jobs are no longer treated as exceptions. What to Check: Go to Admin Settings → Fields Shared with Clients and review the fields currently selected for the Kanban Card. Resolution: Update the fields under Admin Settings → Fields Shared with Clients as required. The configured settings will apply to all existing and new jobs. FAQs 1. Can I customize Kanban Card fields separately for individual jobs? No. Kanban Card field settings are managed through Admin Settings → Fields Shared with Clients and apply across all existing and new jobs. 2. What happens to Kanban Cards that were previously customized for individual jobs? They are no longer treated as exceptions. The settings configured under Admin Settings will apply to them. 3. Do the Kanban View and List View follow the same field-setting behavior? Yes. Fields shared with clients follow consistent behavior across both views.
