t: Daily Timesheets
s: Learn how to configure and use Per Day rate timesheets for Daily Timesheets in Recruit CRM
h: What this feature does and when to use it
Before you begin
Selecting a Rate Type
Enabling Per Day timesheets for a candidate
Entering time on a Per Day timesheet
Filtering and viewing Per Day timesheets
Bulk adding time for Per Day timesheets
Creating invoices for Per Day timesheets
b: What this feature does and when to use it The Per Day Rate Type lets you pay and bill contractors based on the number of days worked instead of hours worked and create Daily Timesheets. You can select Per Hour or Per Day for Contract and Contract-to-Perm jobs. The selected Rate Type determines how Pay Rate, Bill Rate, timesheet entries, invoicing, and reporting are calculated. ​ Use Per Day when: You pay or bill contractors based on a daily rate. You want to track attendance as Full Day, Half Day, or No Show instead of hours. You want timesheets, invoices, exports, and reports to reflect days worked. Before you begin Per Hour is selected by default. Select Per Day when you want to manage the contractor based on days worked. The Rate Type and Work Schedule are captured when a timesheet is created. Changes made afterward apply only to newly created timesheets. Existing timesheets continue to use the settings they were created with. Per Day timesheets do not require a Rule Template . Instead, you configure the contractor's Work Schedule directly in the Enable Timesheet form. Selecting a Rate Type Go to Jobs and open a Contract or Contract-to-Perm job, or create a new one. In the Job form, select the Rate Type : Per Hour : Contractors are paid and billed based on hours worked. Per Day : Contractors are paid and billed based on days worked. ​ Enabling Per Day timesheets for a candidate Once you select Per Day as the Rate Type for the job, you can enable a Per Day timesheet for individual candidates in the Candidate Pipeline. When enabling the timesheet, define the contractor's Work Schedule, Pay Rate, and Bill Rate so the timesheet can calculate daily pay and billing correctly. Open the job and scroll to the Candidate Pipeline . ​ Click Enable Timesheet on the candidate's card. In the Enable Timesheet window, select Per Day as the Rate Type. ​ Under Work Schedule , select the days the contractor is expected to work. Any day you do not select is treated as a day off. Enter the contractor's Pay Rate and Bill Rate . ​ Click Enable to activate the timesheet. Please note: Per Day timesheets do not use a Rule Template . You only need to select the Work Schedule that applies to the contractor. ​ Entering time on a Per Day timesheet After the timesheet is enabled, you can record the contractor's attendance for each scheduled working day. Instead of entering the number of hours worked, select the attendance status that applies to each day. Open the contractor's timesheet. For each working day, select the appropriate attendance type: Full Day: Counts as 1 day and applies the full daily Pay Rate and Bill Rate. Half Day: Counts as 0.5 day and applies 0.5x the daily Pay Rate and Bill Rate. No Show: Counts as 0 days and applies 0x the daily Pay Rate and Bill Rate. ​ For example, if the daily rate is $100 , a Full Day is $100 , a Half Day is $50 , and a No Show is $0 . ​ ​ Total Work Days are calculated automatically based on the attendance entries. For example, 4 Full Days + 1 Half Day = 4.5 Total Work Days . ​ Click Submit once all entries are complete. ​ Filtering and viewing Per Day timesheets Rate Type and Total Work Days are available as columns on the Timesheets page . You can also filter timesheets by Rate Type and select: Per Hour Per Day ​ Bulk adding time for Per Day timesheets If you need to update multiple Per Day timesheets at once, you can use the bulk time entry options from supported Timesheet views. The selected timesheets must use the same Rate Type for the bulk action to work. Select the timesheets you want to update in bulk. ​ Make sure the selected timesheets use the same Rate Type . The Rate Type of the first selected timesheet is used as the reference. ​ If the selected timesheets use different Rate Types, you'll see "Timesheet setting is different." Enter Full Day, Half Day, or No Show for the relevant dates. Use Copy to All or Copy to Period to apply entries across the selected timesheets. ​ Here is how you can bulk update timesheets on the Timesheets Page- Here is how you can bulk update timesheets from the Job- Total Work Days is displayed for the selected Per Day timesheets. Creating invoices for Per Day timesheets Approved Per Day timesheets can be used to create invoices based on the total number of billable days. When creating the invoice, make sure the selected timesheets use the same work schedule type so the appropriate invoice template can be applied. Select the approved Per Day timesheets you want to invoice. The selected timesheets must use the same work schedule type. Then click the Create Invoice button at the top. You can see that the invoice template has been by defualt selected as the Per Day invoice template. The template includes Description, Number of Days, and Amount . Here, enter the description details and click on Create Invoice. ​ Number of Days represents the total billable units: Full Day = 1 Half Day = 0.5 No Show = 0 For example, 4 Full Days + 1 Half Day = 4.5 days on the invoice. Review and save the invoice as you would for other timesheet invoices. Viewing Per Day data in Billing and Revenue Report Go to Reports and open the Billing & Revenue Report . In the KPIs dropdown, select Total Billable & Payable Days . The KPI is calculated from approved Per Day timesheets, including half days. For example, 43 Full Days + 0.5 Day = 43.5 days . You can generate the report for Overall, Company, Job, and Contractor report types. ​ Exporting Per Day timesheets Rate Type and Total Days are available as export fields for Per Day timesheets. Day-wise exports show whether each day was logged as a Full Day or Half Day . Hour-based fields remain empty for Per Day timesheets, while Per Day-specific fields remain empty for Per Hour timesheets. Per Day timesheets in the Contractor and Client Portals Per Day timesheets are also supported in the Contractor Portal and Client Portal . Timesheets created through these portals follow the Rate Type configured for the contractor . Contractors configured with Per Day can submit Full Day, Half Day, or No Show entries through the portal. FAQs What is the Per Day Rate Type? Per Day allows you to pay and bill contractors based on the number of days worked instead of hours worked. How is a Full Day calculated? A Full Day counts as 1 day and applies the full daily Pay Rate and Bill Rate. How is a Half Day calculated? A Half Day counts as 0.5 day and applies half of the daily Pay Rate and Bill Rate. How are total days calculated? Full Days count as 1 and Half Days count as 0.5 . For example, 5 Full Days + 2 Half Days = 6 Total Days . Can I change the Rate Type after timesheets have already been created? Yes. However, the change applies only to newly created timesheets . Existing timesheets continue to use the Rate Type that was configured when they were created. Do Per Day timesheets require a Rule Template? No. Per Day timesheets do not require a Rule Template . You only need to select Per Day as the Rate Type and configure the required Work Schedule in the Enable Timesheet form. Conclusion The Per Day Rate Type lets you manage contractor pay and billing based on days worked rather than hours. With Full Day, Half Day, and No Show entries, the selected rate type carries through timesheets, bulk actions, invoicing, exports, reporting, and the Contractor and Client Portals. t: Data Enrichment: Find Email & Phone Number of Candidates/Contacts
s: This article will help you understand more about the Data Enrichment feature.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
How to enrich the email or phone number?
How to purchase the credits or the Data Enrichment subscription?
Enabling/Disabling Data Enrichment
How to check Data Enrichment History?
FAQs
What are the parameters required for fetching the email/phone number?
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The Data Enrichment feature helps users find missing email addresses and phone numbers for candidates or contacts using their LinkedIn profiles and other available information. Recruit CRM performs enrichment using a waterfall model i.e, when contact data is requested, Recruit CRM automatically requests data from RocketReach and FullEnrich. The waterfall model increases the chance of finding valid contact details without requiring additional steps from the user. For candidates, personal emails are fetched. For contacts, work emails are fetched. If more than one personal or work email is available, the secondary email is saved as a note. You can use this when: You need to find missing email addresses or phone numbers for candidates/contacts. Before you begin Data Enrichment is an Enterprise plan feature which can also be added at an additional cost to the Pro or Business plan subscriptions. Free Plan: Users on the Free plan will have 25 free Data Enrichment credits to try out this feature. The free credits are assigned on a per-user basis and cannot be shared across the account. The free credits do not have an expiration period and will remain available in the account until they are fully utilized. Pro Plan and Business Plan : Pro and Business Plan users can try the Data Enrichment feature using the free Recruit CRM Credits . Enterprise Plan : Users will receive the Data Enrichment credits included with their Recruit CRM subscription. These credits can be used for AI Sourcing as well. AI Sourcing beyond free monthly searches consumes 1 enrichment credit per search/per page. A valid LinkedIn profile URL is required for enrichment to work, and at least one of the fields (email or phone) must be empty. If the LinkedIn URL is not available or is invalid, the system will attempt to find data using a combination of the Candidate/ Contact's Full Name, Job Title, and Current Organization, provided all three fields have valid data. 📧☏ How to enrich the email or phone number? 1. Manual Enrich (Users not having an active data enrichment subscription): Open a candidate or contact profile that is missing an email address, a phone number, or both. ​ Confirm that there is a valid LinkedIn URL on the record, or that full name, job title, and current organization fields are filled in if LinkedIn is not available. ​ Locate the manual Find Email/ Find Phone button and click it to attempt to enrich the email address. If you don’t have an active data enrichment subscription, you will see manual 'Find Email' and 'Find Phone' buttons to enrich data. In such a case, data may or may not be found when the user hits these buttons. If data is not found, no credits are consumed. 2. Auto Detection (Users having an active data enrichment subscription) Open a candidate or contact profile that does not have email, phone, or both fields filled. Wait while the system automatically checks for available email or phone data. If data is available, look for “email available” or “phone available” indicators on the profile. Click to fetch the available email or phone and populate it into the record. If data is available, it shows 'Email Available' or 'Phone Available' and you can fetch the email or phone instantly with a click. Note : For candidates, personal emails are fetched, and for contacts, work emails are fetched. If there is more than one personal or work email available for a candidate or contact, the secondary email will be saved as a note. You can provide feedback on the fetched data using feedback buttons, and you can always enter or edit email/phone number manually as well: 💲How to purchase the credits or the Data Enrichment subscription? Click on Admin Settings >>> Data Enrichment ​ Click on the Buy Subscription button. ​ Review the available options for the number of credits you can purchase. ​ Select the number of credits you would like to purchase from the shown options. ​ Confirm your choice from the available options displayed. ​ Click on the Buy Subscription button to finalize the purchase. ​ You can even check the credits that are consumed and are available for your account on the Data Enrichment page Credit System: The credits on the paid Data Enrichment subscription plan are shared across the account. Here is the credit consumption system for data enrichment: 1 Work Email (Contact) = 1 Credit 1 Personal Email (Candidate) = 3 Credits 1 Phone (Contact or Candidate) = 4 Credits Credits will be consumed if the email/phone is successfully fetched, even if it is incorrect/outdated. Credits are consumed only once for a successful data fetch, regardless of whether the data came from RocketReach or FullEnrich. This ensures efficient credit usage while providing access to two powerful data sources. Account Owners get notified via email when: 80% of the credits are used 100% of the credits are exhausted For the monthly data enrichment subscription, the credits must be consumed within that month (30 days from the date of purchase), and any leftover credits won't be rolled over to the next month. ​ Similarly, for the annual data enrichment subscription, the credits must be consumed within that annual billing period (1 year from the date of purchase), and any leftover credits won't be rolled over to the next billing cycle. The credits on the paid Data Enrichment subscription are shared across all users within the same account, ensuring that all team members can utilise the same pool of credits. This facilitates better collaboration as credits are accessible and usable by all team members when needed. ✅ Enabling/Disabling Data Enrichment Click on Admin Settings >>> Data Enrichment Navigate to the Data Enrichment section. Use the available toggles to enable or disable Data Enrichment separately for candidates or contacts. Ensure that users who should perform enrichment have edit access on the relevant records and have the data enrichment permission enabled (for custom roles). ​ Only users with Edit access on a record and Data enrichment permission can enrich data. A new data enrichment permission has been added for Custom roles in User Settings : For default roles, enrichment permission is based on ‘Edit’ access for the record. 📋 How to check Data Enrichment History? A detailed audit log is available to see credit consumption and data unlocked in Admin Settings >>> Data Enrichment 🤔 FAQs What are the parameters required for fetching the email/phone number? A valid LinkedIn URL and at least one empty field (email or phone). If the LinkedIn URL is not available or is invalid, the system will attempt to find data using a combination of the Candidate/ Contact's Full Name, Job Title, and Current Organization, provided all three fields have valid data. Here are some troubleshooting tips if data enrichment is not working as expected: 1. Make sure the LinkedIn URL is entered correctly. 2. Confirm that at least one required field (email or phone) is empty. I don’t have an active data enrichment subscription. Can I use this feature? Yes! You’ll see manual enrich buttons ('Find Email' and 'Find Phone') and get 25 free credits to try it out. Can it provide more than one email address? Yes. If multiple emails are found, the primary one is added to the profile, and any additional emails are saved as a note under the record. In this case too, only one credit will be consumed. Additional credits aren’t consumed if multiple emails are found. Can I still enter email/phone manually? Absolutely! You can type or paste it yourself anytime. What if the data I enriched is wrong? Use the feedback option next to the field to report any incorrect results. However, there’s no refund of credits even if the enriched data is incorrect. Who can use this feature in my team? Anyone with edit access or permissions on the record and data enrichment access. Is this GDPR compliant? Yes, the feature is fully GDPR compliant. It only sources data from publicly available web profiles. Click for more details . Can credits be refunded? No, credits are non-refundable. How does credit usage work in annual plans? All credits are granted upfront and can be used at any point during the active subscription period. There is no monthly cap or rollout. Can we alter the bonus credit offering in the future? We can adjust the bonus credit offerings at our discretion, whether by increasing or decreasing them, as stated in our updated Terms of Service Conclusion: Data Enrichment in Recruit CRM allows you to quickly find and manage missing contact details for candidates and contacts while controlling usage through plans, permissions, and shared credits. You can provide feedback on the fetched data using feedback buttons, and you can always enter or edit email/phone number manually as well: 💲How to purchase the Recruit CRM credits? Click on Admin Settings >>> Data Enrichment ​ Click on the Buy Credits button. ​ Select the number of credits you would like to purchase from the shown options. ​ Click on the Buy Subscription button to finalize the purchase. You can even check the credits that are consumed and are available for your account on the Data Enrichment page Credit System: The credits on the paid Recruit CRM Credits subscription plan are shared across the account. Here is the credit consumption system for data enrichment: 1 Work Email (Contact) = 1 Credit 1 Personal Email (Candidate) = 3 Credits 1 Phone (Contact or Candidate) = 4 Credits Credits will be consumed if the email/phone is successfully fetched, even if it is incorrect/outdated. Credits are consumed only once for a successful data fetch, regardless of whether the data came from RocketReach or FullEnrich. This ensures efficient credit usage while providing access to two powerful data sources. Account Owners get notified via email when: 80% of the credits are used 100% of the credits are exhausted For the monthly Recruit CRM Credits subscription, the credits must be consumed within that month (30 days from the date of purchase), and any leftover credits won't be rolled over to the next month. ​ Similarly, for the annual Recruit CRM Credits subscription, the credits must be consumed within that annual billing period (1 year from the date of purchase), and any leftover credits won't be rolled over to the next billing cycle. The credits on the paid Recruit CRM Credits subscription are shared across all users within the same account, ensuring that all team members can utilise the same pool of credits. This facilitates better collaboration as credits are accessible and usable by all team members when needed. ✅ Enabling/Disabling Data Enrichment Click on Admin Settings >>> Data Enrichment Navigate to the Data Enrichment section. Use the available toggles to enable or disable Data Enrichment separately for candidates or contacts. Ensure that users who should perform enrichment have edit access on the relevant records and have the data enrichment permission enabled (for custom roles). ​ Only users with Edit access on a record and Data enrichment permission can enrich data. A new data enrichment permission has been added for Custom roles in User Settings : For default roles, enrichment permission is based on ‘Edit’ access for the record. 📋 How to check Data Enrichment History? A detailed audit log is available to see credit consumption and data unlocked in Admin Settings >>> Data Enrichment 🤔 FAQs What are the parameters required for fetching the email/phone number? A valid LinkedIn URL and at least one empty field (email or phone). If the LinkedIn URL is not available or is invalid, the system will attempt to find data using a combination of the Candidate/ Contact's Full Name, Job Title, and Current Organization, provided all three fields have valid data. Here are some troubleshooting tips if data enrichment is not working as expected: 1. Make sure the LinkedIn URL is entered correctly. 2. Confirm that at least one required field (email or phone) is empty. I don’t have an active data enrichment subscription. Can I use this feature? Yes! You’ll see manual enrich buttons ('Find Email' and 'Find Phone') and get 25 free credits to try it out. Can it provide more than one email address? Yes. If multiple emails are found, the primary one is added to the profile, and any additional emails are saved as a note under the record. In this case too, only one credit will be consumed. Additional credits aren’t consumed if multiple emails are found. Can I still enter email/phone manually? Absolutely! You can type or paste it yourself anytime. What if the data I enriched is wrong? Use the feedback option next to the field to report any incorrect results. However, there’s no refund of credits even if the enriched data is incorrect. Who can use this feature in my team? Anyone with edit access or permissions on the record and data enrichment access. Is this GDPR compliant? Yes, the feature is fully GDPR compliant. It only sources data from publicly available web profiles. Click for more details . Can data enrichment credits be refunded? No, data enrichment credits are non-refundable once utilized. How does credit usage work in annual plans? All credits are granted upfront and can be used at any point during the active subscription period. There is no monthly cap or rollout. Can we alter the bonus credit offering in the future? We can adjust the bonus credit offerings at our discretion, whether by increasing or decreasing them, as stated in our updated Terms of Service Conclusion: Data Enrichment in Recruit CRM allows you to quickly find and manage missing contact details for candidates and contacts while controlling usage through plans, permissions, and s

t: Deactivating an existing user & inviting a new user to your current plan
s: Brief explanation about how to deactivate a teammate, invite a new user and transfer the ownership of records to the new user
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

2. Invite a new teammate

Troubleshooting
Problem: I cannot invite a new user after deactivating an existing one.
Problem: The new teammate cannot see records owned by the previous user.
FAQs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows you to deactivate an existing user, invite a new teammate to use the same paid seat, and transfer record ownership when team members leave or change roles. Deactivating a user removes their access to the system but does not remove the paid license associated with your subscription. This ensures a smooth transition while preserving your existing plan and account configuration. Use this feature when you want to: Replace a departing teammate with a new user. Manage user transitions without losing data. Please note : Deactivating a user does not imply removing the paid seat/license from your subscription charges.​ Instead, the license becomes available and can be reassigned to another teammate. Please note that your subscription charges are based on the number of paid licenses in your account, not the number of active users. As a result, you will continue to be billed for any unused licenses that remain in your subscription. If you no longer need a vacant license, you can reduce the number of paid licenses in your subscription separately. Step-by-step instructions Navigate to Admin Settings > Users . Locate the user you want to deactivate and click the Edit (pencil) on the far right of the user's row. In the user pop-up, click Deactivate (bottom left) to remove their access to Recruit CRM. If you do not want to reduce the license, untick the 'Deactivate user and reduce license' checkbox and click the 'Yes Deactivate' option. If the 'Deactivate user and reduce license' checkbox is not ticked, once you have successfully deactivated the old user, you can invite a new user on the same seat, without making changes to your current plan. 2. Invite a new teammate Navigate to Admin Settings > Users . ​ Click the Invite Teammates button in the top-right corner of the page. Enter the new teammate's email address and select the appropriate role. Click Send Invitation to invite the user to your Recruit CRM account. The user will receive an email invitation to join Recruit CRM. 3. Transfer ownership of records If you wish to transfer the ownership of records of the user that has left to the new user or an existing user, follow the steps below once the new user has joined your team: Go to " Admin Settings " and click on Users Search for the deactivated user whose records you want to transfer, or filter the list to display deactivated users. Once located, click the Edit (pencil) icon. Click Transfer to begin the ownership transfer process. Select the user who should become the new owner of the records from the Transfer ownership To drop-down and click on Submit. Confirm the transfer and wait for the success message to appear. Troubleshooting Problem: I cannot invite a new user after deactivating an existing one. Likely cause: The user may not have been fully deactivated, or no vacant seat is currently available. What to check: Verify that the original user shows as deactivated and confirm the number of available licenses in your account. Resolution: Complete the deactivation process or free up an additional license before sending the invitation. Problem: The new teammate cannot see records owned by the previous user. Likely cause: Record ownership has not yet been transferred. What to check: Verify who owns the affected records. Resolution: Transfer record ownership from the deactivated user to the appropriate teammate. FAQs 1. Does deactivating a user remove the paid license? Not always. The license will only be reduced if the "Deactivate user and reduce license" checkbox remains selected during deactivation. To keep the license for reuse, uncheck the box before confirming. 2. Can I invite a new user without upgrading my plan? Yes. You can invite a new user without upgrading your plan, provided you have an available license that can be assigned to them. 3. Can I transfer records from a deactivated user? Yes. Record ownership can be transferred to another active user after the original user has been deactivated. Conclusion: Recruit CRM makes it easy to manage team transitions by allowing you to deactivate users, invite replacements, and transfer record ownership while continuing to use your existing subscription. t: Deactivating Teammates & Reducing Paid Seats
s: Brief explanation about how to deactivate a teammate and reduce the number of paid licenses to cancel the user cost from your subscription.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Deactivating a user
Reducing your paid licenses/users
Managing deactivated users
2. Ability to Add Deactivated Users to Teams
3. Display of the 'Deactivated' label
4. Deal Split Persistence
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? This feature allows you to deactivate users in Recruit CRM and, if required, reduce your paid license count so you are no longer charged for unused seats. Deactivating a user removes their access to the Recruit CRM database while preserving historical records, reporting data, team associations, and deal attribution. When deactivating a user, you can either: • Keep the license active, allowing you to invite a replacement user or reactivate the same user later. • Reduce the license count, which updates your subscription and stops future charges for that unused seat. Use this feature when: • A team member leaves your organisation and no longer requires access to Recruit CRM. • You want to deactivate a user and reduce your paid licenses to avoid being charged for an unused seat. Please note: Deactivating users does not imply reducing the number of purchased licenses. To avoid getting charged for deactivated users, you have to reduce the unused purchased licenses/seat s. Also Recruit CRM, just like any other SaaS product works on a prepaid subscription model. And, as per our company’s terms, all Recruit CRM subscriptions are non-refundable. ​ You can Refer to point 9.5 of Recruit CRM terms for the same. Deactivating a user 1. Go to the user management section from your admin settings . 2. Click on the pencil icon to the right of the user you want to deactivate and click on "Deactivate". ​ 3. Now, the system will give you a pop-up with the following option: ​ If you check the option to "Deactivate user and reduce license", your subscription will be automatically updated, and the license will be reduced. If you don't tick the option, you'll be deactivating the user so they no longer have access to your database, but your subscription won't be updated, and their paid licence will be maintained. And you will still be charged for the unused purchased license till the time you reduce the license after deactivating the user. ​ If you decide to keep the license, you can then invite a new user to the license or reactivate a deactivated user . Note: If you have any unused purchased licenses, a message will display the number of such licenses available in your account, at the top of the User Management page . From here, you'll have two options to choose from: ' Inviting new user (s)' to use the available seats' or alternatively; ' Reducing license count ' to match the number of active users. Now, let's see how you can reduce your paid licenses so you do not get charged for the license that your team is no longer using. Reducing your paid licenses/users 1. Head over to the Admin Settings and click on the Plans & Billings under the Account Management section. 2. Now, go to "View Current Plan" and click on "Edit Current Plan" 3. Then, decrease the "Total Users" count by the number you want to reduce. For example: If you have 10 licenses and wish to reduce 2, then decrease the "Total Users" count by 2. Thus, the "Total Users" count should be 8 . Here, you'll also be able to see the number of unused licenses you have so that you can reduce the correct number of seats for all the unused licenses and not get charged for them on your next renewal. 4. Then, click on Review Order and verify your new "Total Users". 5. Now, before you "Update Plan & Pay" click on 'I agree to Recruit CRM's Terms Of Service'. You won't be charged anything for this since you’re reducing a user. Click here to reduce your paid licenses now! That's it! Now, you won't be charged for the deactivated user and unused licenses on your next renewal :) Managing deactivated users 1. Persistence of Deactivated Users in Teams Deactivated users remain in their respective teams even after deactivation. They are marked with a "Deactivated" label next to their names in the team edit section. 2. Ability to Add Deactivated Users to Teams Deactivated users can still be searched and added to teams as needed. Click here to learn how to create teams in Recruit CRM An 'Audit Log' entry will also be created whenever a deactivated user is added to a team. This includes details such as the team name and any changes made, providing a clear trail of actions for accountability and tracking purposes. 3. Display of the 'Deactivated' label The "Deactivated" label is prominently displayed in various parts of the application to maintain clarity and transparency, including: Reports (Tables) : All generated reports reflect the deactivated status of users. Dashboard Reports : Dashboards show the status of deactivated users in relevant sections. Collaborator Widget: The status of users is visible in the collaborator widget for easy identification. List View and Detail View Pages: Both in list and detail views, deactivated users are marked accordingly. Deactivated users are listed at the bottom of any list to differentiate them from active users. 4. Deal Split Persistence Deactivated users also remain part of any deal splits they were involved in. This ensures that historical data and records are preserved accurately. You can add deactivated users to new deal splits if necessary, maintaining flexibility and comprehensive record-keeping. FAQ Why can’t I invite a new user even though I have a license available? If you see an open license but cannot invite a new teammate, it’s usually because when you deactivated the user, the license count was also reduced. Here’s how to reactivate the license: ​ 1. Go to Admin Settings --> Plans & Billing : ​ 2. Click Edit Current Plan on the first page. ​ 3. Increase the license count by 1 . ​ 4. Scroll to the end of the page and click Review Order . Note: Make sure the blue box shows 0 for both values . This means you won’t be charged again for this license. Click Upgrade Plan . ​ You can now invite your new user . Does deactivating a user automatically reduce my paid licenses? No. Deactivating a user does not automatically reduce your purchased licenses. You must either select the option to “deactivate user and reduce license” during deactivation or manually reduce your total users count in the Plans & Billing section. Will I be refunded if I reduce my licenses mid-term? No. Recruit CRM subscriptions work on a prepaid model and are non-refundable as per the company’s terms (see point 9.5) . Reducing licenses prevents future charges for those seats at renewal; it does not generate a refund for the current term. Can I reactivate a deactivated user later? Yes. If you keep the license, you can reactivate a deactivated user or invite a new user to that license. The deactivated user’s data and history remain in the system. How do I know how many unused purchased licenses I have? If you have any unused purchased licenses, a message at the top of the User Management page will display the number of such licenses available in your account. Can deactivated users still be part of teams or deal splits? Yes. Deactivated users remain in their teams, can be searched and added to teams, and maintain their share in any deal splits. They are clearly labelled as deactivated to preserve transparency and accurate historical records. Conclusion: Deactivating teammates and reducing paid seats in Recruit CRM lets you control both access and cost while preserving complete historical records. Use deactivation together with license management to keep your subscription aligned with your active team and maintain clear, auditable data across your account. Related Articles Canceling your subscription and permanently deactivating the Recruit CRM account Managing Your Recruit CRM Subscription Adding more licenses to your Recruit CRM account Deactivating an existing user & inviting a new user to your current plan How to reactivate a deactivated user in Recruit CRM

t: Deal Split
s: This article will guide you in splitting deal amounts with teammates and teams.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Adding team members and/or teams to a split
Setting up the deal split
Understanding deal splits in reporting
Tracking deal splits on the dashboard
Troubleshooting
Problem: Only the deal owner appears in the Deal split tab with 100% split.
FAQs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? With the deal split feature, you can collaborate with your teammates, assign split percentages, distribute the commission, and generate comprehensive reports for better insights. You can use this feature when: You need to split a deal amount or commission between multiple teammates. You want to include teams (not just individuals) in a deal split. You need accurate reporting and dashboard insights based on deal splits. Learn more about: ​ ​ Deal splits in reporting. Tracking deals splits on the dashboard. Adding team members and/or teams to a split 1. Open the relevant deal in Recruit CRM. 2. Click the Deal split tab on the deal details page. 2. If there are no collaborators yet, this section will show the deal owner with a 100% deal split percentage. 3. Now, click on the ' Edit Deal Split' button. In the search field, search for the teammates and/or teams you want to add to the split. 4. Select the teammates and/or teams to include them in the deal split. Once added, they automatically become collaborators on the deal. ​ The user will also receive an email informing they have been added as a collaborator in the deal. ​ Setting up the deal split 1. By default, the deal is set on ' Equal Split '. This means that each collaborator will be assigned an equal split percentage. 2. To customize the split percentages, select ' Custom Split ' from the drop-down menu. Now, you will be able to make changes and assign split percent values for each teammate or team. 3. Once the percentages are assigned, you can track the Commission for each teammate throughout the deal's progress through stages under the ' Weighted Deal ' column. Understanding deal splits in reporting With the ' Deal by Teammate/Team Report ,' you can gain a comprehensive overview of all deals in all stages in two distinct tables- one for teammates and another for teams. Additionally, the bar graphs provide a clear visual distinction between the teammates and the teams. The "Unallocated" row ensures transparency in deal splits. Any split percentage that hasn't been distributed to specific team members or teams is shown in this row. It ensures that the total split value always sums up to 100%. The "Total" column represents the overall deal value, calculated as: Sum of all stage values - Sum of lost stage value = Total Tracking deal splits on the dashboard On the dashboard , the Total Deals Statistics report displays all deal stages and provides us with the status of each deal. In addition to viewing the overall statistics, you can also generate reports specific to individual teammates or teams where you can see metrics of split amount and weighted split amount , allowing for more targeted analysis. Here is a quick video to get you started: Troubleshooting Problem: Only the deal owner appears in the Deal split tab with 100% split. Likely cause: No collaborators have been added yet. What to check: Open the Deal split tab and look for the Edit deal split button. Resolution: Click Edit deal split, search for the required teammates and/or teams, and add them to the split. FAQs Where do I manage deal splits for a specific deal? You manage deal splits from the Deal split tab on the deal details page. What happens if there are no collaborators on a deal split? If there are no collaborators, the Deal split tab shows the deal owner with a 100% deal split percentage. What is the default behavior when I add multiple collaborators? By default, the deal is set to equal split, so each collaborator is assigned an equal split percentage. Do collaborators get notified when they are added to a deal split? Yes. When you add teammates or teams to a split, they automatically become collaborators on the deal and receive an email informing them they have been added. Conclusion: Using the deal split feature in Recruit CRM helps you share deal amounts fairly, keep collaborators informed, and track commission accurately as deals progress. t: Deals by Revenue Report
s: This article explains how to generate, read, and export the Deals by Revenue report so you can analyze performance by team or teammate.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Generate and Analyze the Deals by Revenue Report
Review the Report
View Detailed Deal Records
Export the Report
Schedule the Report
Troubleshooting
Problem: The Deals by Revenue report is empty or shows fewer deals than expected.
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Deals by Revenue report provides a comprehensive view of your deals and the revenue they generate across different deal stages and time periods. It helps you monitor revenue performance, compare results across teammates or teams, identify revenue trends over time, and gain deeper insights into your deal pipeline through interactive charts and detailed reports. Use this feature when : • You want to track the total revenue generated across selected deal stages. • You need to compare deal revenue performance between teammates or teams. • You want to analyze revenue trends by week, month, or year . • You need to export revenue reports or charts for further analysis or presentations. • You want to schedule revenue reports to be automatically generated and shared with selected teammates. The report summarizes deal revenue by team member or team , displays revenue trends over your selected time period, and provides both visual charts and detailed deal records. You can drill down into the underlying deals, apply additional filters, customize the displayed columns, export report data in multiple formats, or schedule reports for automatic delivery to keep your team informed. Generate and Analyze the Deals by Revenue Report 1. Open the Deals by Revenue Report Navigate to the Reports section from the left-hand navigation menu. Open the Deals Report , then select Deals by Revenue . ​ 2. Select the deal stages Choose the deal stages you want to include in the report. ​ 3. Select the date range Choose the time period for the report. You can select one of the predefined ranges, such as Today, Yesterday, This Week, Last Week, This Month, or Last Quarter , or specify a Custom Date Range by selecting the required start and end dates. ​ 4. Generate the report After selecting the deal stages and date range, click Generate Report to create the report. 5. Adjust the report view After the report is generated, you can further customize how the data is displayed. Use the Show By option to group the report by: • Week • Month • Year You can also choose whether the report should be based on the deal's: • Added On date – The date the deal was created in Recruit CRM. • Close Date – The date the deal was marked as closed. ​ Review the Report The generated report provides a breakdown of deal revenue for the selected stages, grouped by team members and teams , along with the total deal amount for each time period. ​ The data is organized based on the selected Show By interval (Week, Month, or Year), making it easier to analyze revenue trends over time. The report includes: • A bar chart displaying historical deal data, showing every stage that deals moved through during the selected time period. • A comprehensive table showing stage-wise performance for each team and teammate included in the report. View Detailed Deal Records Each bar in the chart is clickable, click any bar to view the detailed list of deals associated with that stage and time period. ​ Within the detailed report, you can: • Review the underlying deal records. • Sort the data by clicking any column header. • Customize the displayed information using Edit Columns . • Apply additional filters to narrow down the results. • Perform a Boolean Search to quickly locate specific deals. • Export the filtered deal list as a CSV file. Export the Report You can export the report in multiple ways: • Click Export Report to CSV above the table to download the summary table as a CSV file. • Click the Export icon in the top-right corner of the bar chart to download the chart as an image in PNG, JPG, or SVG format. • Click any bar in the chart to open the detailed candidate list for that KPI, then click Export Report to CSV to download the detailed report as a CSV file. ​ Schedule the Report You can schedule the Deals by Revenue report to be generated automatically and delivered to selected teammates at your preferred intervals. To learn how to configure scheduled reports, click here Please note that the bar graph will display historical data, showing all the stages the deals have been in that particular time frame. Troubleshooting Problem: The Deals by Revenue report is empty or shows fewer deals than expected. Likely cause: Deal stages or timeframes are too narrowly selected, or date filters (added on vs. closed date) do not match your expectations. ​ What to check: Confirm that the correct deal stages are selected before generating the report. Verify the timeframe covers the dates when the deals were added or closed. Check whether the filter is set to added on date or closed date and whether this aligns with what you want to measure. Resolution: Adjust the selected stages, timeframe, and date reference, then click Generate Report again. Problem: You cannot see all the columns or stages you need in the detailed list view. Likely cause: The default column layout does not include all desired fields or stages. ​ What to check: Open the column editing option in the detailed list view. Check which columns are currently selected and their order. Resolution: Edit the columns to add the needed deal stages and reorder them so key information appears where you expect. FAQs Q1: What is the difference between the Deals by Revenue and Deals by Teammates reports? The Deals by Revenue report focuses on deal amounts and accumulated revenue across stages and timeframes, while the Deals by Teammates report focuses on performance grouped primarily by teammate. In the Deals by Revenue report, you still see breakdowns by teams or teammates, but the core metric is revenue. Q2: Can I change how the Deals by Revenue report groups data over time? Yes. You can use the “Show by” options to group and display data by week, month, or year. The report will then store and present data according to the interval you select. Q3: What is the difference between filtering by added on date and closed date? Filtering by added on date uses the date the deal was added to the system, helping you analyze new pipeline creation. Filtering by closed date uses the date the deal was closed in the application, helping you analyze revenue conversion in a specific period. Q4: Can I drill down into the deals behind a specific bar in the chart? Yes. All bars in the Deals by Revenue report are clickable and open a detailed list view of the deals represented in that bar. From there, you can search, filter, adjust columns, and export the data. Q5: In which formats can I export the Deals by Revenue report? You can export the bar chart as PNG, JPG, or SVG image files. The detailed list of deals can be exported as a CSV file for further analysis. Conclusion The Deals by Revenue report gives you a clear, flexible view of your deal amounts and revenue across stages and timeframes, with options to drill down, export, and schedule insights for your team. Use the filters, visualizations, and exports described here to keep your pipeline performance transparent and your revenue tracking accurate. t: Deals by Teammates/Team
s: The Deals by Teammates/Teams report in Recruit CRM helps you track the number and value of deals across different deal stages for each team and team member.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Generate and Analyze the Deals by Teammates/Teams Report
View Deals by Numbers and Value
Drill Down into Deal Details
Review Deal Value and Weighted Deal Value:
Export the Report:
Troubleshooting
Problem: The Teams option is not available in the report
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Deals by Teammates/Teams report provides a comprehensive view of your deal pipeline, helping you monitor revenue opportunities and track how deals are progressing across different deal stages. It enables you to compare the performance of individual teammates and teams by analyzing deal counts, deal values, weighted deal values, and stage distribution over a selected time period. Use this feature when: • You want to see how many deals each teammate or team is managing across different deal stages. • You need to monitor the value and progress of revenue opportunities in your deal pipeline. • You want to compare deal performance between individual teammates and teams. • You need to export deal data or charts for reporting, presentations, or further analysis. Generate and Analyze the Deals by Teammates/Teams Report 1. Open the Deals by Teammates and Teams Report Navigate to the Reports section from the left-hand navigation menu. Open the Deals Report , then select Deals by Teammates/Teams . 2. Select team members or teams Choose the team members you want to include in the report from the user dropdown. If you want to view the combined performance of all selected users, select Total Deal Statistics . Alternatively, select individual team members to generate recruiter-specific reports. If you're on the Business Plan or above , you can also select one or more Teams along with the team members to generate team-level reports. 3. Select the deal stages (KPIs) Open the Deal Stages (KPI) dropdown and select the deal stages or metrics you want to include in the report. ​ 4. Select the date range Choose the required date range for the report. You can select one of the predefined ranges or specify a Custom Date Range by choosing the desired start and end dates. You can also choose whether the report should be based on the deal's: • Added On date – The date the deal was created in Recruit CRM. • Close Date – The date the deal was marked as closed. 5. Generate or save the report Click Generate Report to run the report. If you plan to reuse the same report configuration in the future, click Save and Generate Report to save the report settings while generating the report immediately. Once the report is generated, you'll see interactive charts displaying the selected deal statistics. View Deals by Numbers and Value The report provides two different ways to analyze your deal pipeline: • Numbers – Displays a bar chart showing the number of deals in each deal stage for the selected team members or teams during the chosen date range. • Value – Displays the percentage distribution of the total deal value across the different deal stages. ​ Drill Down into Deal Details Each bar in the chart is clickable. Click any bar to open a detailed list of the deals associated with that stage for the selected time period. Within the detailed report, you can: • Review the underlying deal records. • Sort the data by clicking any column header. • Customize the displayed information using Edit Columns . • Apply additional filters to narrow down the results. • Perform a Boolean Search to quickly locate specific deals. • Export the filtered deal list as a CSV file. Review Deal Value and Weighted Deal Value: Below the bar chart, you'll find two donut charts that provide additional insights into your deal pipeline. 1. Deals by Value: This chart shows the percentage distribution of the total deal value across each deal stage. For example, if there are six deals in the In Progress stage, the total value of those six deals is added together, divided by the total value of deals across all stages, and then converted into a percentage. 2. Deals by Weighted Value: This chart displays the percentage distribution based on each deal's weighted value rather than its actual value. It calculates the total weighted value of deals in each stage, divides it by the weighted value of deals across all stages, and converts the result into percentages. ​ Understanding the Charts 📌 Bar Chart The bar chart displays historical data , showing every deal stage a deal passed through during the selected date range. As a result, a deal may appear in multiple stages if it moved through them within that period. 📌 Donut Charts The Deals by Value and Deals by Weighted Value donut charts display live data , meaning each deal is counted only in its current stage at the time the report is generated. Export the Report: You can export the report in multiple ways: • Click Export Report to CSV to download the detailed report data as a CSV file. • Click the Export icon in the top-right corner of any chart to download it as a PNG, JPG, or SVG image. • Click any bar in the chart to open the detailed candidate list for that stage, then select Export Report to CSV to download the detailed candidate report as a CSV file. Troubleshooting Problem: The Teams option is not available in the report Likely cause : The account is not on the Business Plan or higher. What to check : Confirm the current subscription plan. Resolution: Upgrade to the Business Plan or above to access team-level reporting. Problem: The numbers in the bar graph do not match the donut charts Likely cause : The bar graph shows historical data, while the donut charts show live data. What to check : Confirm whether you are expecting historical stage movement or current stage distribution. Resolution : Use the bar graph when analyzing all stages deals passed through in the selected timeframe, and use the donut charts when you need current-stage snapshots. Problem: Deals are missing from the report for the expected period Likely c ause : The wrong date filter (added on vs close date) or date range is selected. What to check : Verify whether the filter is set to “added on date” or “close date,” and confirm the chosen date range. Resolution : Adjust the date type and range to match how you want to filter deals (by creation or by closure). Problem: Cannot see specific fields in the detailed deal view Likely cause: The required columns are not enabled in the detailed view. What to check: In the detailed deals view, open the column settings from the top right corner. Resolution: Edit the columns and select the specific deal details you want to display, then re-run or refresh the view. FAQs What does the Deals by Teammates and Teams report show? It shows the number and value of deals in different deal stages for selected team members and, on Business Plan and above, for teams, along with historical bar graphs, live donut charts, and a detailed table. Who can use the Teams part of the report? Only users on the Business Plan and above can use the Teams report functionality. What is the difference between deals by value and deals by weighted value? Deals by value show the percentage share of total deal value per stage. Deals by weighted value add the weighted deal value of deals in a stage, divide it by the total weighted deal value across all stages, and then convert that into a percentage. How are percentages calculated in the value chart? For example, if there are six deals in the “In Progress” stage, the system adds the deal value of those six deals, divides that sum by the total deal value of deals across all stages, and converts the result into a percentage. Can I export charts and tables from this report? Yes. You can export bar and donut charts as PNG, JPG, or SVG from the top-right corner of each chart, and you can export detailed tables and deal lists as CSV using the Export to CSV button. Conclusion The Deals by Teammates and Teams report in Recruit CRM gives you clear visibility into deal volume, value, and stage distribution across your users and teams, with flexible filters and export options for deeper analysis. t: Deals in Recruit CRM
s: This article will explain everything you need to know about the Deals in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to change the Deal's currency?
How to add a Deal?
From the Deals section
While adding a job
Within the Candidate/Contact/Job/Company's details page
Through the "+" icon:
What are Deal Stages?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? A Deal in Recruit CRM represents any opportunity your team is actively pursuing to generate revenue. This could include consulting projects, pitching candidates to clients, or facilitating candidate placements. The Deals section helps you track these opportunities from start to finish by organizing them into customizable stages, monitoring progress, forecasting revenue, and collaborating with teammates. Use this feature when: You want to track and manage revenue opportunities such as consulting projects, candidate pitches, and placements. You need to organize opportunities into customizable deal stages to monitor progress and forecast revenue. You want to link deals with candidates, contacts, companies, and jobs for a complete view of each opportunity. You need to collaborate with teammates using deal splits and generate reports based on deal performance, revenue, and team contributions. You want to archive, restore, or clone deals as your sales pipeline evolves. How to change the Deal's currency? The deal's currency is the same as the account's currency. Only the Account owner has the option to change the Account currency; follow along to know how this can be done - ​ 1. Go to Admin Settings . 2. Open the Account option to change the account currency, which will also change the deal currency. How to add a Deal? There are several ways by which you can add a deal in Recruit CRM: From the Deals section Navigate to the Deals section and click the Add Deal button. Enter the required deal details. If needed, select a Deal Type and fill in any custom deal fields relevant to your workflow. Click Submit to create the deal. Note: The Deal Type field is an optional field, and it can also be hidden from the add form/edit form if not needed for your workflow. Additionally, if you have specific requirements, you can include custom 'Deal' fields to store additional details as needed. Click here to learn how to add custom fields for deals! While adding a job Start creating a new job in Recruit CRM. Scroll to the bottom of the job form and enable the Create New Deal checkbox. Complete the remaining job details and submit the form. A new deal will be created and linked to the job automatically. Within the Candidate/Contact/Job/Company's details page Open the details page of a candidate, contact, job, or company. Navigate to the Related Deals tab to view all associated deals. Click the option to Add Deal to create and link a new deal directly from the record. Through the "+" icon: Click the Global Add (+) icon at the top of Recruit CRM and select Deal . Enter the required deal details and click Submit to create the deal. What are Deal Stages? Deal stages represent various phases of a deal's progression. Each stage is assigned a specific percentage value, which determines the proportion of revenue earned as the deal advances. You can customize the deal stages and create a deal pipeline as per your requirements. Learn how to create and customize your deal pipeline View and manage deal stages Open the Deals section and choose how you want to view your pipeline: List View for a tabular list of deals. Kanban View to organize and visualize deals by their stages. If you're using the Kanban View , simply drag and drop a deal card into the desired stage to update its progress. Whenever you change a deal stage, a pop-up window appears prompting you to: Select or confirm the new deal stage (if applicable). Enter a remark or reason for the stage change. Once you've entered the required information, confirm the update to save the new stage. Change a deal stage from the deal profile You can also update a deal stage directly from an individual deal profile. Open the deal you want to update. Click the current Deal Stage on the deal profile. In the pop-up window, select the new stage from the dropdown menu. Enter a remark or reason for the change. Click Submit to update the deal stage. View deal stage history Recruit CRM keeps a history of every deal stage update for future reference. To view it: Open the relevant deal profile. Click the Remarks icon next to the Deal Stage . The history panel displays: Each deal stage change. The remarks added during the update. The date and time of the change. The user who made the update. This allows you to track the complete progression of a deal throughout its lifecycle. ​ Filter deals using record-specific fields Open the Deals section and use the available filters to narrow down your results based on information associated with the deal. You can filter deals using fields from: Deals Companies Contacts Jobs Candidates Activities Apply one or more filters to quickly find, organize, and manage deals based on your business requirements. Note: Placed candidates under a job associated with a deal will be automatically linked to that deal, only when the job type is Contract or Contract-to-Perm. For all other job types, candidates will not be auto-linked. What are the Deal Pipeline metrics? There are 4 metrics you need to take into consideration while keeping track of your Deals in Recruit CRM: Total Weighted Pipeline Represents the proportion of revenue earned according to the deals' current stages in the Deal Pipeline. Total Pipeline Represents the sum of the total deals' values, regardless of their stage. Deals Won Measures the total revenue earned on deals in the "won" stage. Deals Lost Measures the total revenue lost on deals in the "lost" stage. How to archive a Deal? There are two ways to archive a deal. From the Deals list page Open the Deals page. Select one or more deals you want to archive. Click Archive from the top toolbar. From the deal details page Open the deal you want to archive. Click the More Options (⋮) menu. Select Archive Deal . Once a deal is archived: It is marked with an Archived tag at the top of the deal profile. It no longer appears in the active Deals list. Its Deal Amount and Weighted Deal Amount are removed from the Total Pipeline and Total Weighted Pipeline metrics on the Deals page. How to unarchive a Deal? You can restore an archived deal from either the Deals list or the deal profile. From the Deals list Open the Deals page. In Quick View , select Archived to display archived deals. Select the deal(s) you want to restore. Click Unarchive from the top toolbar. ​ From the deal details page Open the archived deal. Click the More Options (⋮) menu. Select Unarchive Deal to restore the deal. How to clone a deal? To create a copy of an existing deal: Open the deal you want to clone. Click the More Options (⋮) menu. Select Clone Deal . A duplicate deal is created with the same details as the original, allowing you to reuse existing deal information without creating a new deal from scratch. What is the Deal Split feature? With the deal split feature, you can collaborate with your teammates, assign split percentages, distribute the commission, and generate comprehensive reports for better insights. Click here to learn more about the Deals Split feature! What are the different reports on Deals? You have the option to generate two distinct types of reports based on Deals: 1. Deals by Teammates/Teams This report will give you an overview of the number of deals in different deal stages and their deal value for various teams and team members. See a full breakdown of the Deals by Teammates report 2. Deals by Revenue This report allows you to generate a comprehensive report to track all your deals and the accumulated revenue. See a full breakdown of the Deals by Revenue report Troubleshooting Problem: Deal currency is not what you expect Likely cause: The account currency is set to a different value than you want for deals. What to check: Confirm the current account currency in the Admin Settings under the Account option. Resolution: Ask the account owner to update the account currency; the deal currency will automatically follow the account currency. Problem: A placed candidate is not automatically linked to a deal Likely cause: The associated job is not of type contract or contract to permanent . What to check: Review the job type for the job associated with the deal. Resolution: Automatic linking of placed candidates to deals only occurs when the job type is contract or contract to permanent. For other job types, manually link candidates if required. Problem: An archived deal no longer appears in the deals list Likely cause: The deal has been archived and is hidden from the default deals list. What to check: In the Deals list page, open the Quick View and select Archived to see archived deals. Resolution: If needed, un-archive the deal from the archived view or from the deal details page to make it visible again and restore its impact on pipeline metrics. Problem: Pipeline metrics seem lower than expected Likely cause: Some deals may have been archived, or their stages may have changed to lost. What to check: Review: Archived deals in the Quick View → Archived filter.

t: Deals Pipeline
s: This article will help you create a Deals Pipeline and keep track of all monetary transactions in your company.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

2. Choosing Default Deal Fields and Adding Custom Deal Fields

b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Deal Pipeline on Recruit CRM lets you keep a tab on all revenue opportunities and "deals" your team is working on. You can create deal stages, customize deal fields, and track any Job, Company, or Contact associated with a deal. The system also maintains deals pipeline metrics that are automatically updated as you create new deals, delete or archive old ones, and move deals through different stages. You can use this feature when: You want to track all revenue opportunities your team is working on. You need a structured deals pipeline with clear stages. You want to customize deal fields to capture specific information about each deal. You want to monitor your revenue pipeline on a total and weighted basis. Understanding the Deals Pipeline's Metrics There are 4 metrics you need to take into consideration while keeping track of your Deals in Recruit CRM:​ Total Weighted Pipeline Represents how much you have earned or will earn according to the deals' current stages in the Deal Pipeline. Total Pipeline Represents the sum of the total deals' values, regardless of their stage. Deals Won Measures the total amount earned on deals in the "won" stage. Deals Lost Measures the total amount lost on deals in the "lost" stage. These metrics are automatically updated as you create new deals, delete/archive old ones, and move the deals through the different stages. Creating Stages in the Deals Pipeline The stages in the Deals Pipeline are responsible for the amount calculated in the Total Weighted Pipeline . Recruit CRM has two default stages in the Deals Pipeline that cannot be removed: ​ Won ​ Lost You can customize your Deals Pipeline in the Admin Settings. ​ 1. Creating Custom Deal Fields Like every other record type on Recruit CRM, you can customize the data you want to see on deals as well from the "Deals Field" section within admin settings. 2. Choosing Default Deal Fields and Adding Custom Deal Fields You can set Default fields & make them visible and/or mandatory based on your workflow. For any additional information, you want your team to enter on deals, you can use up to 16 custom fields to collect extra information. 3. Managing Deal stages Use the 'Deals Pipeline" option to view & customize the stages you'd like to move your deals through within your Workflow. 4. Customize/change your Stages ​ Finalize the stages you'd like to see on your Kanban Board for Deals along with the probability of winning deals at every stage Your Deals Pipeline is now ready to use in both List & Kanban Views! ​ You can now track your revenue pipeline on both a total & weighted basis :) 5. Change the deal stages You have the flexibility to view your deal pipeline in both List and Kanban views. In the Kanban view, you can change the deal stage by simply dragging and dropping the deal to the desired stage. When you change the stage, a pop-up window will appear, allowing you to enter a remark or reason for the stage change. You can also change the deal stage by directly accessing the deal profile. ​ Click on the stage, and the same pop-up window will appear, prompting you to choose a new desired deal stage from the drop-down menu and enter a reason for the change. ​ Afterwards, click on submit, and the deal stage will be updated accordingly. ​ You can view the complete history of changes made to the deal stages, including remarks left, dates of updates, and the user who performed the stage change. Simply click on the remarks icon next to the deal stage to access this information. ​ Troubleshooting Problem: Team cannot find specific deal stages on the Kanban board Likely cause: The desired stages have not been configured or finalized for display. What to check: In the deals pipeline settings, review the list of stages and confirm which are included on the Kanban board and their probabilities of winning. Resolution: Customize or change the stages so that all required stages appear on the Kanban board with appropriate probabilities. FAQs What are the default stages in the deals pipeline? The deals pipeline in Recruit CRM has two default stages, won and lost, which cannot be removed. Can I customize the stages in my deals pipeline? Yes. You can use the deals pipeline option in admin settings to view and customize the deal stages you would like to move your deals through within your workflow and to set the probability of winning deals at every stage. How can I see who changed a deal stage and when? Click on the remarks icon next to the deal stage to view the complete history of changes, including remarks, dates of updates, and the user who performed the stage change. Conclusion: By setting up your deal stages, configuring deal fields, and using both list and Kanban views, you can manage your deals pipeline in Recruit CRM and track your revenue opportunities on a total and weighted basis. t: Default Fields in Recruit CRM
s: This article will tell you about all the default fields available for candidate, company, contact, job, and deal records in Recruit CRM.
h: Candidate Default Fields
Company Default Fields
Contact Default Fields
Job Default Fields
Deals Default Fields
FAQs ❓
b: Recruit CRM offers specific default fields for every entity (candidate, company, contact, job, deals) so that users do not have to start setting up their accounts from scratch. Note: Default fields CANNOT be edited or deleted inside Recruit CRM. Instead, you can hide the visibility of the default field and create a custom field and use it to store the data. Table of Contents: Candidate Default Fields Company Default Fields Contact Default Fields Job Default Fields Deals Default Fields You can easily identify a candidate field as default or custom by going to the candidate fields in your admin settings. While default candidate fields do not have any tags: A custom candidate field will have a "Custom Field" tag: Further, you can see under the company / contact / deal / job fields in your admin settings that all the default fields are available on the left side of the page while the default fields that you create on the right side appear under the "Additional Information (Custom Fields)" section: Now, let's take a look at all the default fields available for all the entities: Candidate Default Fields First Name (Text) - This field is required by default and you can not add a candidate without a first name. Email (Email Address) , Phone (Phone Number) , LinkedIn Profile (Text) - These are the unique identifiers to detect duplicate records for candidates. Full Address (Text) - Radius Search in Advanced Search is implemented using this field. The same is also applicable to Contact, Company, and Job Fields. Gender (Dropdown) - This field is only visible when the EEO toggle is turned OFF from the account management settings in admin settings. Birth Date (Date) - This field is used to calculate the value for the " Age " field which is also visible only when the EEO toggle is turned OFF from the account management settings. Locality (Text) - This field is auto-populated using the " City " and " Country/Region " fields on LinkedIn using the Chrome Extension. The same is also applicable to Contacts. Summary (Long Text) - Data added to this field is used to populate the candidate summary field in the Executive Search Report . You can also add templates for candidate summary . Resume (File) - The Advanced Search query searches for the keywords only on the file added to the default "resume" field. Work History, Education History, Employment Information (Field Sections) - All the fields in these sections are auto-populated when parsing a resume. Source (Text) - This field tracks the source of the candidate when added from different platforms, for example, LinkedIn, Talent Pool Page, Job Boards, etc. Click here to understand how to track the source of job applicants. Skills (Text) - This field tracks the skills of the record and is auto-populated when the Candidate is added from LinkedIn using the Chrome Extension. Company Default Fields Company Name (Text) - This field is required by default and you can not add a company without a name. About Company (Long Text) , City (Text) - These fields are auto-populated when adding a company from LinkedIn using the Chrome Extension. Industry (Dropdown) - You can select the relevant industry type for a company from this dropdown. Website (Text) , Linkedin Profile URL (Text) - These are the unique identifiers to detect duplicate records for companies. Contact Default Fields First Name (Text) , Last Name (Text) , Phone (Phone Number) - Basic information of your clients. Title (Text) - This field is auto-populated when adding a company using the Chrome Extension from the "Headline" field in LinkedIn. Email Address (Email Address) , Linkedin Profile URL (Text) - These are the unique identifiers to detect duplicate records for contacts. Stage (Dropdown) - A contact can go through various stages while they are in your database, for example - going from a lead to a follow-up client. These stages can be customized from the Contact Stages section in admin settings following these steps . Job Default Fields Job Title (Text) , Number Of Openings (Dropdown) , Company (Dropdown) - These fields are required by default. Contact (Dropdown), Secondary Contacts (Dropdown) - Once the company field is selected, you can select from the dropdown a contact associated with the respective company. Job Description (File/Rich Text) - It is advised to add the job description as text. Most of the external job boards do not accept jobs where the job description is added in a file format. Currency (Dropdown) - While you can choose the currency for every job, the default currency can be changed from your profile settings . Select Owner (Dropdown) - Refers to the user who is the owner of a job. Collaborator (Dropdown) - You can add other users from your team to collaborate on your jobs . Enable Job Application Form (Checkbox) - Enabling/disabling this checkbox impacts the visibility of your jobs on external job sites. Job Application Form Questions (Checkbox) - Enabling/disabling this checkbox impacts the visibility of additional questions on your Job Application URL. Account owners and admins have access to create these questions. Note For Candidates (Checkbox) - Enabling/disabling this checkbox impacts the visibility of the notes you add to your Job Applications. Pay Rate (Number) , Bill Rate (Number) - These appear only for Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job types and can be marked as required in Admin Settings, but not hidden. Deals Default Fields Name (Text), Deal Type (Dropdown) Owner (Dropdown) - The visibility of these fields can not be changed and they are required by default to track reports and conduct searches. Value (Number) - Required field indicating the estimated amount the deal is worth. Close Date (Date) - This is a required field that indicates the date by which a deal is estimated to be closed. A deal will only show up in a report when its close date lies in the period you're running the report for. For instance, a deal created in January with a close date of February will not show up in the reports for the month of January. Stage (Dropdown) - Indicates the current stage of a deal to calculate its weighted value. Deal stages can be customized from the Deal Pipeline in admin settings following these steps . FAQs ❓ How the system identifies duplicates for Candidates, Contacts and companies records? Candidates → Email Address, Phone Number, LinkedIn Profile URL Contacts → Email Address, LinkedIn Profile URL Companies → Company name, Website URL, LinkedIn Profile URL Hope this helps!
