t: Define target companies for a job
s: Define target companies in Recruit CRM to streamline candidate selection by focusing on preferred applicants from a certain company.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Define target companies for a job
Add target companies and assign candidates
Troubleshooting
Problem: I can't see the Target Companies field while creating a job.
Problem: Expected candidates aren't appearing under Candidates From Target Companies.
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? With this feature, you can select target companies for any of your jobs. This allows you to get recommendations for candidates currently related to those companies when sourcing and assigning candidates from your account to a specific job. This aims to streamline the candidate selection process by focusing on applicants from preferred target companies, thus enhancing the quality and relevance of the applicants. This feature is useful when you want to: View recommendations based on a candidate's current organization. Bulk assign candidates from target companies. Define target companies for a job Before you can use Target Companies while assigning candidates, you'll need to enable the Target Companies field. Navigate to Admin Settings > Data Customization > Job Fields . Under the Job Details section, locate the Target Companies field and enable its visibility, and click Save to apply the changes. Once enabled, the Target Companies field will be available while creating and editing jobs, and the Candidates From Target Companies tab will appear when assigning candidates to a job. If you no longer wish to use this feature, simply disable the Target Companies field visibility in the admin settings, and both sections will be hidden. Add target companies and assign candidates Create a new job or edit an existing one. In the Target Companies field, add one or more companies from your Recruit CRM database. Save the job. Please note: The Company field and Target Companies field serve different purposes. The "Company" field specifies the employer for the job being created (in other words, your client). On the other hand, the "Target Companies" field specifically means adding companies where candidates currently employed may be relevant to the position you are creating. When assigning candidates to the job, open the Candidates From Target Companies tab. Recruit CRM will display candidates whose Current Organization matches the target companies you've selected. You can select multiple candidates and assign them to the job in bulk. You can also edit or remove the selected target companies at any time by clicking Edit . You'll only be able to see candidates from the targeted company if they have that specific company as their current organization in Recruit CRM. ​ ​ Please refer to this article to learn how to link a candidate to their current organization. Troubleshooting Problem: I can't see the Target Companies field while creating a job. Likely Cause: The field visibility is disabled. What to Check: Verify that the Target Companies field is enabled under Admin Settings > Data Customization > Job Fields. Resolution: Enable the field visibility and save your changes. Problem: Expected candidates aren't appearing under Candidates From Target Companies. Likely Cause: The candidate's Current Organization doesn't match any of the selected target companies. What to Check: Verify the candidate's Current Organization field and ensure it matches one of the configured target companies. Resolution: Update the candidate's current organization if necessary and refresh the assignment page. Conclusion: The Target Companies feature helps recruiters focus on candidates from preferred organizations by automatically recommending relevant profiles during candidate assignment. By configuring target companies for each job, you can streamline sourcing, improve candidate relevance, and speed up your recruitment workflow. t: Deleting emails from Recruit CRM
s: In this article, we'll walk you through the process of deleting emails from Recruit CRM.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin:
How to delete emails from Recruit CRM?
Troubleshooting
FAQs
Conclusion:
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Recruit CRM has partnered with Nylas.com to power our email services. Recruit CRM displays the same emails that exist in your email provider’s mailbox, across all folders (Inbox, Sent, Trash/Bin, Junk, etc.). When an email is permanently deleted from your native mailbox, it is also removed from Recruit CRM and will no longer appear there. Before you begin: Your email account must be connected to Recruit CRM. You must have access to your native mailbox (for example, Gmail, Outlook, or another email provider). You need permission in your email provider to delete and permanently remove emails from all folders, including Trash, Bin, or Junk. 📧 How to delete emails from Recruit CRM? Open your native mailbox (for example, Gmail or Outlook) where the email account connected to Recruit CRM is hosted. ​ Locate the email you want to remove from Recruit CRM in your Inbox, Sent, or any other folder. ​ Delete the email from that folder using your email provider’s standard delete option. ​ Go to your email provider’s Trash, Bin, or Junk folder (the folder name depends on your email service). ​ Find the same email in Trash/Bin/Junk and delete it again so it is permanently removed from your mailbox. ​ Wait for the sync between your mailbox and Recruit CRM to complete; once the email is permanently deleted from your native mailbox, it will no longer be visible in Recruit CRM. ​ As Recruit CRM mirrors your entire mailbox, the " All Emails " tab comprises the emails present in all the different folders in your native mailbox, including the bin. Thus, to ensure the emails do not show up in Recruit CRM, you have to delete them permanently. ​ Troubleshooting Problem: An email still appears in Recruit CRM after I deleted it from my inbox. Likely cause: The email is still present in your Trash, Bin, or Junk folder in your native mailbox. What to check: Open your email provider and check the Trash, Bin, and Junk folders for the same email. Resolution: Permanently delete the email from these folders. Wait for the mailbox to sync with Recruit CRM and refresh the All Emails view. FAQs Can I delete emails directly from Recruit CRM? No. Because Recruit CRM mirrors your mailbox, you must delete emails directly from your native mailbox (such as Gmail or Outlook). Once deleted there (including from Trash/Bin/Junk), they will disappear from Recruit CRM. Conclusion: To delete emails from Recruit CRM, always remove them permanently from your native mailbox, including any Trash/Bin/Junk folders, so they no longer appear in the mirrored All Emails view. Click on the blue ' View/Rename Candidates Hotlists' button present at the bottom of the Hotlist section. 3. You will see the list of hotlists of that particular entity and the option to edit and delete the hotlists you want. To delete a specific hotlist, just click on the Trash icon. You can also filter the hotlists based on the 'Created On', 'Created By', or 'Updated On' fields: Troubleshooting Problem: If you’re unable to delete the hotlist. What to check: Check if you are the Account Owner or the person who created the hotlist, or if your custom role includes permissions to edit/delete hotlists owned by others. Problem: The hotlist is still visible after deletion. Likely cause: The page has not refreshed, or the view is cached. What to check: Confirm that you clicked the trash icon and that no error was shown. Resolution path: If the hotlist is still visible after deletion, try refreshing the page and check if that helps. Conclusion: Deleting a hotlist helps you keep your Recruit CRM database clean and focused while keeping all underlying records safe. b: What this feature does and when to use it? This article explains how to delete records in Recruit CRM, both individually and in bulk, along with the permissions required and how to manage bulk action options on list pages. The delete functionality allows Account Owners and Admins to permanently remove records that are no longer needed. You can delete a single record from its profile/details page or remove multiple records at once using bulk actions from the list page. You can also customize which bulk actions are available and how they appear, helping you manage records more efficiently. Please Note Deletion is permanent. Records that are deleted cannot be recovered. There is no undo option, so review your selection carefully before confirming. Only Account Owners and Admins can delete records by default. Users on the Team Member and Restricted Team Member role do not have permission to delete records. Deletion applies to Candidate, Contact, Company, Job, and Deal records. Step-by-Step Instructions Delete an Individual Record: 1. Navigate to the profile of the Candidate, Contact, Company, Job or Deal you want to delete. 2. Click the ellipses icon (...) located at the top of the profile page. ​ 3. Select Delete from the dropdown menu that appears. 4. A confirmation pop-up will appear. Enter the number of records you are deleting and click Delete to confirm. Delete Records in Bulk: 1. Navigate to the list page for the record type you want to delete. You can go to the Candidates, Contacts, Companies, Jobs, or Deals list page. ​ 2. Select the records you want to delete by checking the checkbox on the left side of each row. To select all records on the page, use the checkbox beside the column header. You can use the ' Select 3000 records ' button to select 3000 records at a time. Learn to select more than 1000 records at a time. 3. Click the ellipses icon (...) and then click Delete . 4. A confirmation pop-up will appear. Enter the number of records to be deleted and click Delete to confirm. The method for deleting records is the same for all the entities(candidates, contacts, jobs, companies and deals). 📌 Note: The confirmation step requires you to enter the exact number of records being deleted. This is intentional and helps prevent accidental bulk deletions. Troubleshooting Problem: The Delete option is not visible on a record Likely cause: Your user role does not have permission to delete records. What to check: Confirm whether you are logged in as an Account Owner or Admin, or your custom role has the permissions to delete the record. Resolution path: Contact your Account Owner to request the necessary permissions or to perform the deletion on your behalf. ​ Problem: The number I enter in the confirmation box is not accepted Likely cause: The number you typed does not match the actual count of selected records. ​ What to check: Recount the selected records in the list or confirm you are deleting only one record from a profile page. ​ Resolution path: Enter the exact number of records shown as selected (for example, “1” for a single record, “4” for four selected records). Problem: Associated notes, tasks, meetings, or call logs disappeared from other entities after deleting a record. Likely cause: These items were originally added to the deleted primary record. What to check: Whether the missing activities were created on the record that was deleted. Resolution: Be aware that when a note, task, meeting, or call log added to a specific record is deleted, it is removed from all associated entities. This cannot be reversed. Problem: I deleted the wrong record and want to restore it. Likely cause: The deletion was confirmed in error. What to check: Verify whether the record is still visible anywhere in the system. Resolution: Records once deleted cannot be recovered. You will need to recreate the record manually. FAQs Who can delete records in Recruit CRM? By default, only Account Owners and Admins can delete records. Users on the Team Member and Restricted Team Member role do not have permission to delete records. Can a deleted record be recovered? No. Deletion is permanent and irreversible. Once a record is deleted, it cannot be restored through the application. Always confirm your selection carefully before proceeding. Which record types can be deleted? You can delete Candidate, Contact, Company, Job, and Deal records, both individually and in bulk. What does the confirmation step in the delete pop-up require? Both the individual and bulk delete flows require you to type the number of records being deleted before the deletion is processed. This step is a safeguard to prevent accidental removal of records. Conclusion Deleting records in Recruit CRM is a straightforward process, but it is permanent. t: EEO Compliance
s: This article explains how EEO (Equal Employment Opportunity) compliance works in Recruit CRM and how to activate or deactivate it from your account settings.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How EEO Compliance Works in Recruit CRM
How to Change the EEO Compliance Settings
Troubleshooting

Does Recruit CRM support EEO compliance?
What happens when I activate EEO compliance?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The EEO Compliance setting in Recruit CRM helps you meet Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) requirements by controlling the visibility of sensitive candidate information. When EEO Compliance is enabled, the Gender and Age fields are hidden throughout the system when adding, viewing, or managing candidate records. When disabled, these fields remain available as normal. This feature is intended for Account Onwers and users responsible for managing compliance, privacy, and account-level settings. Use this feature when: • You want Recruit CRM to support your organization's EEO compliance requirements. • You need to hide candidate gender and age information from recruiters and hiring teams. • You are reviewing or updating privacy, compliance, or legal settings for your account. How EEO Compliance Works in Recruit CRM When EEO Compliance is enabled: • The Gender and Age fields are hidden throughout the system. • Users cannot enter gender or age information while creating or editing a candidate. • Users cannot view gender or age information on existing candidate records. When EEO Compliance is disabled: • The Gender and Age fields become available again. • Users can view, add, and edit this information as part of candidate records. This helps organizations align their recruiting processes with Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) requirements by limiting access to sensitive candidate information. How to Change the EEO Compliance Settings Follow the steps below to enable or disable EEO Compliance in Recruit CRM: Navigate to Admin Settings from the left navigation menu and click Account to open your account settings. On the Account page, scroll down to the Legal Settings section and locate the EEO Compliance toggle. Turn the toggle ON to activate EEO Compliance or turn the toggle OFF to deactivate EEO Compliance. Your changes will take effect across the account and will determine whether gender and age information is visible within candidate records. Troubleshooting Problem: Gender and age fields are not visible when adding a candidate. Likely cause: EEO compliance is activated. What to check: Go to Admin Settings → Account → Legal Settings and check the EEO compliance toggle. Resolution: If your policy allows it and you need to see these fields, turn the EEO compliance toggle off. FAQs Does Recruit CRM support EEO compliance? Yes. Recruit CRM allows you to activate or deactivate EEO compliance, including at the time of account creation. What happens when I activate EEO compliance? When you activate EEO compliance, fields like gender and age become invisible. You cannot add gender or age when creating a candidate, and you cannot see these fields when viewing candidate details. Can I change my EEO compliance setting after creating my account? Yes. You can change it anytime by going to admin settings → Account → Legal Settings and adjusting the EEO compliance toggle. Where exactly is the EEO compliance toggle located? The EEO compliance toggle is in the Legal Settings section on the Account page, which you can access from the admin settings on the left side. Does EEO compliance affect existing candidate details? When EEO compliance is activated, gender and age become invisible when viewing candidate details, regardless of whether they were previously added. Conclusion: The EEO Compliance setting provides a simple way to align Recruit CRM with your organization's privacy and Equal Employment Opportunity requirements. By enabling or disabling the setting from Account Settings, you can control whether gender and age information is visible throughout the platform. t: Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM
s: You can schedule emails to be sent for a particular date and time from Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does & when to use it?
How to schedule your emails?
How to track your scheduled emails❓
Troubleshooting
Problem: I can’t select the time I want; the system won’t let me schedule.
Problem: My scheduled email did not send at the planned time.
Here's a tutorial on how to schedule emails in Recruit CRM
FAQs
b: What this feature does & when to use it? Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM lets you compose an email now and schedule it to be sent automatically at a specific future date and time. Recruit CRM will deliver the email exactly as scheduled, even if you are offline. This feature allows you to plan and automate your communication, ensuring your emails are delivered exactly when you want them to be. This feature is ideal when you want to: Send emails to candidates or clients at a specific time. Schedule follow-up emails in advance. 🕒 How to schedule your emails? 1. Open the email composer from either the candidate/contact list view or the detailed profile view in Recruit CRM. The list view: The Detailed profile view: You cannot bulk-select candidates/contacts and schedule emails. To send a scheduled email to multiple recipients, manually enter each email address in the To field. Please note that you can add up to 10 recipients per email at a time, and this feature is available on all plans. 2. Write your email as usual, then click the clock icon next to the Send button. This option is labelled Send Later and opens the scheduling window. 3. Select the date and time you want the email to be sent based on your time zone and hit the schedule button. When scheduling an email, you can select from which connected email you wish to send the email: ​ NOTE: 2 email connection is only available for users in the Business Plan. Save your settings to schedule the email. Recruit CRM will automatically send the email at the selected time, even if you are offline. It's worth noting that you need to select a date and time at least 15 minutes ahead of the current time. For example, if the current time is 1:43 PM, selecting 1:45 PM will not allow you to schedule the email. Make sure to set the time for 1:58 PM or later to ensure your email is properly scheduled. How to track your scheduled emails❓ All the emails you have scheduled will appear in your mailbox under the " Scheduled Emails " tab. Please note that you'll be able to view only your own scheduled emails, not those of your team members. If a scheduled email fails to send, you can easily reschedule it from the "Scheduled Emails" section in your mailbox, ensuring your important messages still reach their intended recipients. Here are some important limits to keep in mind when scheduling emails: 1. Per Slot Limit: Each user can schedule up to 20 emails within any 5-minute slot. Note that if there are 3 recipients in an email, it will be counted as 3 separate emails, since our bulk email functionality sends individual emails to each recipient. 2. Daily Limit: Users can schedule up to 100 emails per day, based on the GMT zone over 24 hours. 3. Recipient Limit: You can add a maximum of 10 recipients per email. Troubleshooting Problem: I can’t select the time I want; the system won’t let me schedule. Likely cause: The selected time is too close to the current time. What to check: Confirm the time you’re choosing is at least 15 minutes ahead of the current time. Resolution path: Adjust the scheduled time to be 15 minutes or more in the future (for example, from 1:45 PM to 1:58 PM or later) and try scheduling again. Problem: My scheduled email did not send at the planned time. Likely cause: The send may have failed due to email provider issues or temporary connectivity problems. What to check: Go to your mailbox and open the Scheduled Emails tab to see the status of the email. Resolution path: If the email shows as failed, open it from the Scheduled Emails section and reschedule it for a new time. 🎥 Here's a tutorial on how to schedule emails in Recruit CRM 🤔FAQs Can I schedule emails to multiple candidates at once using bulk select? No. You cannot bulk-select candidates or contacts to schedule a single email to all of them. You must manually enter each recipient’s email address in the To field, and you can add up to 10 recipients per scheduled email. What happens if I add multiple recipients to one scheduled email? Each recipient is counted as a separate email , because Recruit CRM’s bulk email functionality sends individual emails to each recipient. For example, one email with 3 recipients counts as 3 emails towards your per-slot and daily limits. Conclusion: Email Scheduling in Recruit CRM allows you to send candidate and client emails automatically at the time you choose. It helps you stay organized and maintain timely communication with less manual effort. By following the steps in this guide, you can easily schedule and manage your emails with confidence. t: Email Sequencing Analytics
s: In this article, we'll take a look at the key statistics used to evaluate the performance of an email sequence and how they are calculated.
h: Use this feature when:
How to Check Sequence Analytics
Option 1: From Admin Settings
Option 2: From Your Mailbox
Understanding Sequence Analytics Metrics
1. Total Enrollment:
2. Opened rate:
3. Reply Rate:
b: How do you measure the effectiveness of an email sequence ? ​ Email Sequencing Analytics in Recruit CRM provides performance metrics that help you understand how prospects are engaging with your email sequences. These analytics track key interactions such as total enrollment rate, open rate, reply rate, and unsubscribe rate, giving you a clear view of how individual sequence steps and entire sequences are performing. Each metric is calculated using a defined formula, allowing you to consistently evaluate results, compare performance across different sequences, and identify opportunities for improvement. Use this feature when: • You are reviewing the performance of an existing email sequence. • You are comparing different sequences or sequence steps to determine which performs better. How to Check Sequence Analytics You can view sequence analytics from either the Sequences section in Admin Settings or directly from your Mailbox . Option 1: From Admin Settings Navigate to Admin Settings → CRM Process Customization → Sequences . Open the sequence whose analytics you want to review. The sequence analytics will be displayed, allowing you to view performance metrics and engagement statistics. Option 2: From Your Mailbox Open your Mailbox from the left navigation panel. Scroll down and select My Sequence Enrollments . Open the sequence whose analytics you want to review. The sequence analytics will be displayed, allowing you to view performance metrics and engagement statistics. 📊 Understanding Sequence Analytics Metrics 1. Total Enrollment: This refers to the total number of prospects who have been enrolled in the email sequence/step. ​ This number also indicates all the prospects who have been added to the sequence/step, even if they were manually or automatically removed at a later stage. Total Enrollment = Active Enrollments + Unenrolled Prospects 2. Opened rate: The percentage of emails that were opened within a sequence/step by the prospects in the sequence. Opened Rate = (Total Mails Opened * 100) / Total Mails Sent 3. Reply Rate: The percentage of emails that received a reply from the prospect in the sequence/step. Reply Rate = (Total Mails Replied * 100) / Total Mails Sent 4. Unsubscribe Rate: This is the percentage of prospects who unsubscribed from the email sequence. Unsubscribe Rate = (Total Prospects Unsubscribed*100)/ Total Prospects Enrolled Conclusion: Email sequencing analytics in Recruit CRM help you measure how many prospects you reach, how they engage with your emails, and where you may need to adjust your sequences. Use total enrollment, open rate, reply rate, and unsubscribe rate together to understand performance and guide improvements to your email outreach. t: Email Sequencing in Recruit CRM
s: Leverage the sequencing feature to keep your email sequence running until the recipient responds, while efficiently managing internal tasks.
h: Steps to create a sequence
Enrolling contacts into a sequence while Pitching the Candidates to the Contacts
FAQs On Sequencing
b: This is a Business Plan feature and for the Pro/Free plan, users will have access to create only 1 sequence. Only the account owners, admins, and users on custom roles with access to sequences can create a sequence. You can send a series of precisely timed email templates to candidates and contacts over a specified period. Using sequencing, you can create a combination of tasks and emails steps, one by one, for your contacts or candidates . The sequence will continue until the recipient responds to any of the emails sent. Steps to create a sequence 1. Go to Admin Settings > CRM Process Customization > Sequences . 2. Click on "Create Sequence". 3. Select either "Candidates" or "Contacts" as the recipient of the sequence. 4. The next step is to name your sequence and select the task or email step that needs to be executed. You can choose to either select an existing email template or create a new one dedicated to the sequence. 5. Then, specify the number of days and the time when the sequence step should be executed. It is important to know exactly when an email will be sent in relation to the starting date of the sequence. To calculate this, you can use the following formula: Send Date = Start Date + Specified No. Of Days (Send Email In) Here, "Start Date" represents the date when the email sequence was initiated. "Specified Date" or "Send Email In" is the number of days you have indicated for the email to be sent after the start of the sequence. The resulting "Send date" is the calculated date on which the email will be sent. For example - If you start the email sequence on January 1st and specify that the email should be sent in 2 days, the Send Date would be calculated as follows: Send date= January 1st + 2 days =January 3rd. You can also set the " Send Email In " date as 0, establishing the beginning of your sequence in Day 0 . This way, the first email will be sent on the same day you enroll prospects into a sequence. In addition, we provide the option to execute email or task steps exclusively on business days. All you need to do is turn on this toggle : 6. When creating an email step, you'll have the option to include an unsubscribe/ opt-out link within each email. 7. You can easily rearrange the sequence steps by using the drag-and-drop functionality. 8. Set a specific number of days for each step to execute, with a range of 1 to 250 calendar days or business days. Refer to this article to know more about how you can enrol and unenroll records from a sequence: Managing Your Sequence Note: If a candidate/contact is marked as Off limits and if they are enrolled in an active sequence, they will NOT be opted out of the sequence. If you’ve created a signature on this page: Email Signature Settings , it will also appear in your sequence emails. Enrolling contacts into a sequence while Pitching the Candidates to the Contacts Here is how you can do it: 1. You need to click on the 'Enroll Selected Contacts to Sequence' option while pitching the candidates to the contacts After successful completion of sending the email/marking the candidates as pitched, you will be automatically redirected to the page where you can enroll them into the sequence. Hope this helps! FAQs On Sequencing What are the time slots/execution times of the sequences? Emails in a sequence are fired in 30-minute slots (e.g. 9:00 AM, 9:30 AM, etc.). Also, the email's timestamp is based on the timezone set in the user profile who initiated the enrolment . ​ Here's how a user can check their timezone: How many prospects can be enrolled in a sequence at a time? The limit on the number of prospects that can be enrolled in a sequence depends on the number of users in the account. Each user can enrol up to 500 prospects in a sequence at a time. Is there any limit on the number of candidates/contacts that a user can enroll in a sequence? A user can enrol up to 500 candidates/contacts in either 1 or across multiple sequences at any given point in time. Once a user reaches the maximum active + paused enrollments i.e. 500, they will not be able to enrol any further records until the active sequence(s) are completed or they manually unenroll some records. How many steps can you have in a particular sequence? Add steps to the sequence as required, up to a maximum of 40 steps , which includes a maximum of 10 email steps, 10 task steps , 10 LinkedIn steps and 10 SMS steps . You can easily rearrange the sequence steps by using the drag-and-drop functionality. What happens when a user edits a running sequence? If someone edits the sequence that is already running, then the changes will apply to only future enrollments. How many sequences can be created on an account? In total, you can add up to 1000 sequences to a business plan account. However, on the pro plan, you can test the feature with 1 sequence. When does a prospect get unenrolled from the sequence? 1. Whenever someone replies to the email sequence , the sequence gets paused for that specific prospect and it gets unenrolled from the sequence. 2. If the candidate/contact chooses to opt out of the email they will get automatically unenrolled. 3. If you manually unenroll them from the sequence. Can we add a candidate/contact to multiple sequences? No, each candidate/contact can only be a part of a single sequence at a time. Is there a time gap between each email sent in a sequence? Yes, consecutive emails will experience a delay ranging from 3 to 5 seconds. This measure has been implemented to prevent email throttling. How to add an image and resize it on the signature? You can click on the 'Insert image' option under the 'Email Signature' section and add the image: You can even re-size it by clicking it and dragging it at the bottom right of the image: How do I stop a sequence? Here's how you can stop a sequence: 1. Go to Admin Settings → Sequences . Find the sequence you want to stop and click on the three dots on the top-right of its card. Select "Unenroll All enrollments" Hope this helped! b: What This Feature Does & When to Use It? Recruit CRM lets you send and track emails to candidates and contacts directly from the platform. You can send individual or bulk emails, use email templates and AI-generated drafts, attach files, and it automatically links each email to the relevant candidate, contact, company, and job records available in the database. All conversations are stored under the Related Emails tab, so you can view the complete communication history in one place. This feature lets you: Send emails to candidates and contacts and manage them directly from Recruit CRM. 🔗 Connecting your email to Recruit CRM First off, make sure your email is connected. Refer to these articles to set up the connection: Connect your Gmail Connect your custom email Connect your Outlook/Office365 📧 Composing emails 1. Inside your mailbox Click on the email icon to be directed to your mailbox in Recruit CRM and select the green button to compose an email. You can add attachments, save drafts, and schedule emails to be sent out later: Attach files to emails from Recruit CRM's "Saved Files" section: Click here to learn how to save files in the Files section To add files from the "Saved Files" section, you can click on the arrow button beside the 'Upload From Device' option and then click on the 'Select From Saved Files' option. You will be able to see up to 15 recently used files. You can search for the specific record(s) by using the search bar and then select the record(s). After that click on the 'Search' button. You'll be able to see all the files related to that specific record. You can also preview the files by clicking on the file name. You can select the desired files by clicking on the 'Add Files' option. You can search files from multiple profiles to add to your email. Once you select all the files, click on 'Done'. Now your selected files will be added to the email :) ​ Notes 1. You can give the recipients the option to be excluded from future email communications by enabling the opt-out/unsubscribe link. 2. When composing an email, you can select from which connected email you wish to send the email. However, the ability to connect two emails is only available for users in the Business Plan. ​ 2. Inside the candidate/contact profile Open the candidate or contact profile from the Candidates or Contacts list, then click on the email address to instantly open the Compose Email window. If you would like to store additional email addresses, you can create a custom field with the field type set to Email . Any email addresses saved in this field will be clickable, and clicking on them will automatically open the Compose Email window. ​ Here's how you can create a custom field You can also bulk-email multiple candidates at once. 3. Anywhere in the app You can start emailing no matter what Recruit CRM page you're on by clicking on the "Compose Email" button at the top right of your screen. ​ Setting up email templates Click here to learn how to create email templates Easily access all your emails! You can locate your emails in two simple ways: Mailbox In Recruit CRM, your mailbox mirrors your native email inbox. This means you can view all your emails in one place, including emails sent and received both inside Recruit CRM.​ Related Emails Tab Within each candidate, contact, and company profile, the Related Emails tab shows all emails exchanged between you, your team and the email address associated to that record. ​ Please Note 1. Clicking "View All" lets you see the last 100 emails exchanged with the candidate/contact. 2. If multiple email addresses are linked to a profile using email-type custom fields , emails for all those addresses will appear in the related emails tab. 3. For companies, the Related Emails section includes conversations linked to their associated contacts. Tracking opened emails You can also track the status of emails that were opened. Here's a guide: Click here to learn how to track sent emails ➕ Add Associations in email You can associate emails to Candidates, Contacts, Companies, and Jobs so that they can be viewed under the 'Related emails' tab directly in the respective entity types, ensuring seamless tracking and context for my communication. 🤖 Use AI to compose emails You can use Recruit CRM’s AI Assist to quickly draft new emails and generate replies to candidates and clients, helping you write professional messages more efficiently. Open the pop-up to compose an email. In it, you'll see an option called "AI Assist". Once you click on it, you'll have different possibilities for using AI to compose an email. 👈 Let's go through all of them! You can select from one of our ready-made suggestions to immediately draft an email: ​ You can type in a prompt to indicate the topics you wish the AI to write about: ​ You can also use voice commands to speak your prompt by clicking on the microphone icon. You can select from one of our nine supported languages. You can select the tone of the email, which can be formal, casual, friendly, or neutral.​ Users can include placeholders in the emails, however, we recommend replacing the AI-generated placeholders with the placeholder from the dropdown to avoid potential errors. Please refer to the video for more context. After inserting your prompt, you can save it by clicking the "Save" icon. You will be asked to name your prompt and you can decide whether you want to share it with your teammates or not. Don't forget to hit "Save"! The prompts will be stored in the "Saved Prompts" section, which will help you save time writing manual prompts for specific needs. By clicking on "Saved Prompts", you'll also be able to pin and unpin the prompts you have saved. 💡 AI Assist FAQs What languages does this feature support? The AI-Assisted Email Template Creation feature currently supports the following languages: English Deutsch Français Dutch Español Português Japanese Finnish Is there any limit to the number of prompts I can save? The limit of prompts that can be saved is 50. How many prompts can be pinned? You can pin up to 10 prompts. Is there any limit on this feature? The AI-Assist feature has a monthly token limit. Users on the free plan will get 50k/user/month, while users on a paid subscription get 2 million/user/month. What happens if I reach the token limit? If users reach the token limit, the AI-assist features will stop generating new content until the next monthly cycle begins. If that happens, you will get this error: Oops! It seems you have exhausted your 2 million token limit for this month. It will be restored on {date} Why do placeholders need to be updated by the user? Recruit CRM placeholders have a specific format, like {candidate_name}, {candidate_city}, etc. However, AI may generate different results in terms of placeholders, such as [candidate_fullname], or , etc. ​ Therefore, users are advised to update the placeholders using the placeholder dropdown to avoid issues. If placeholders are incorrectly added, they will not work. Related Articles Bulk emailing candidates/contacts Parsing resumes and creating candidate/contact records from your mailbox in Recruit CRM. b: What this feature does & when to use it? Recruit CRM gives you the option to include an unsubscribe link within your email that allows candidates/contacts to opt out of further emails from you, helping you build the right contact list and protect your email marketing strategy. You can add an unsubscribe link to your emails, manually opt records out, and later opt them back in if needed. You can use this when: You send bulk or individual marketing or outreach emails from Recruit CRM, and you need to comply with email marketing regulations and respect unsubscribe requests. You want to improve email engagement by maintaining a clean, consent-based contact list. Before you begin: Please note: Email opt-out behavior is based on the email address, not just the individual record. Opting out/unsubscribing means that all the records linked to that specific email ID will no longer receive your email communication. Bulk opt-out is not supported; you can only opt out records individually. Account Owners can customize or translate the opt-out button text under Admin Settings → Email Opt Out Settings. ​ How to include the unsubscribe link in the emails sent to candidates and contacts You can include an unsubscribe link in both individual and bulk (mass) emails sent via Recruit CRM. 1. Open the candidate or contact details page and click their email address to open the email composer. 2. Enter the email body and subject line. 3. In the top-right corner of the email composer, locate the Include opt-out/unsubscribe link checkbox and check this box to add an unsubscribe link to the email. When this checkbox is selected, an unsubscribe/opt-out link is automatically added to the email. The candidate/contact can simply click and unsubscribe from your emails: Recognize Unsubscribed/Opted-Out Profiles Once a candidate or contact clicks the unsubscribe link and opts out, their Recruit CRM profile is updated with a specific label indicating they have opted out or unsubscribed. All candidates or contacts marked as opted out or unsubscribed are automatically skipped when sending bulk or mass emails. You do not need to manually exclude them while selecting records for bulk emails. Manually Opt a Candidate or Contact Out of Emails Apart from the self-service unsubscribe link, you can manually remove a candidate or contact from your email list. 1. Open the candidate or contact’s profile. 2. Click the Opt Out of Email icon or option. 3. In the confirmation pop-up, click the Yes, Opt Them Out (green) button. The profile will now be marked as opted out, and they will no longer receive emails from you. Re-Enable Email for an Unsubscribed or Opted-Out Record If you need to start sending emails again to a candidate or contact who previously unsubscribed or was opted out: 1. Open the candidate or contact’s profile. 2. Locate the Opted out of all emails tag/button and click on 'Remove opt out from all emails' 3. When the confirmation pop-up appears, click Yes, Opt Them In . After this, the unsubscribe/opt-out status is removed, and you can send emails to this candidate or contact them again. Show and Use the Opt-Out Column on the Contact List To easily see which candidates/contacts have opted out: 1. Go to the Candidates/Contact List page and click on the pencil icon at the top right corner. 3. Ensure the Opt-Out column is turned on (visible). 4. Reorder the columns if needed so that Opt-Out is clearly visible. 5.You will now see a Yes/No value in the Opt-Out column on the List Page: Yes = candidate/contact has opted out of email communication No = candidate/contact has not opted out Filter Contacts/Candidates by Email Opt-Out Status You can filter candidate/contacts based on whether they have opted out of emails: On the Candidate/Contact List page, open the Advanced Search or filtering options. Add a filter condition on the Opt-Out field: Opt-Out = Yes to view only candidates/contacts who have opted out Opt-Out = No to view only candidates/contacts who have not opted out Apply the filter to see the resulting list. Note: At this time, bulk opt-out is not supported ; opting out must be done on an individual basis. FAQs Can I bulk opt out multiple contacts at once? No. Bulk opt-out is not supported currently. You can only opt out candidates or contacts individually, or let them opt out themselves via the unsubscribe link in your emails. Conclusion: Use the unsubscribe link, manual opt-out, and opt-in controls together with list filtering to keep your communication targeted and respectful of recipient preferences. ​ Also, you might want to check out our Blog & Article: Best Recruiting Email Templates: A Complete List for Use by Recruiters in 2022 Bulk Emailing Candidates & Contacts Hope this helps :) Related Articles Emailing Candidates & Contacts Bulk emailing candidates/contacts Emailing Candidates & Contacts (New UI) Bulk emailing candidates/contacts (New UI) Enable the 'unsubscribe/opt-out from email' link for emails sent to candidates/contacts (New UI)

You want to improve email engagement by maintaining a clean, consent-based contact list. Before you begin: Please note: Email opt-out behavior is based on the email address, not just the individual record. Opting out/unsubscribing means that all the records linked to that specific email ID will no longer receive your email communication. Bulk opt-out is not supported; you can only opt out records individually. Account Owners can customize or translate the opt-out button text under Admin Settings → Email Opt Out Settings. ​ How to include the unsubscribe link in the emails sent to candidates and contacts? You can include an unsubscribe link in both individual and bulk (mass) emails sent via Recruit CRM. 1. Open the candidate or contact details page and click their email address to open the email composer. 2. Enter the email body and subject line. 3. In the top-right corner of the email composer, locate the Include opt-out/unsubscribe link checkbox and check this box to add an unsubscribe link to the email. ​ When this checkbox is selected, an unsubscribe/opt-out link is automatically added to the email. The candidate/contact can simply click and unsubscribe from your emails: Recognize Unsubscribed/Opted-Out Profiles Once a candidate or contact clicks the unsubscribe link and opts out, their Recruit CRM profile is updated with a specific label indicating they have opted out or unsubscribed. All candidates or contacts marked as opted out or unsubscribed are automatically skipped when sending bulk or mass emails. You do not need to manually exclude them while selecting records for bulk emails. Manually Opt a Candidate or Contact Out of Emails Apart from the self-service unsubscribe link, you can manually remove a candidate or contact from your email list. 1. Open the candidate or contact’s profile. 2. Click the Opt Out of Email icon or option. 4. In the confirmation pop-up, click the Yes, Opt Them Out (green) button. The profile will now be marked as opted out, and they will no longer receive emails from you. Re-Enable Email for an Unsubscribed or Opted-Out Record If you need to start sending emails again to a candidate or contact who previously unsubscribed or was opted out: 1. Open the candidate or contact’s profile. 2. Locate the Opted out of all emails tag/button. 3. Click this tag/button, then click Opt In to Emails . ​ 4. When the confirmation pop-up appears, click Yes, Opt Them In . After this, the unsubscribe/opt-out status is removed, and you can send emails to this candidate or contact them again. Show and Use the Opt-Out Column on the Contact List To easily see which contacts have opted out: 1. Go to the Contact List page. 2. Click Show/Hide Columns . ​ 3. Ensure the Opt-Out column is turned on (visible). 4. Reorder the columns if needed so that Opt-Out is clearly visible. 5. Click Apply to save your column settings. You will now see a Yes/No value in the Opt-Out column: Yes = candidate/contact has opted out of email communication No = candidate/contact has not opted out Filter Contacts/Candidates by Email Opt-Out Status You can filter candidate/contacts based on whether they have opted out of emails: On the Candidate/Contact List page, open the Advanced Search or filtering options. Add a filter condition on the Opt-Out field: Opt-Out = Yes to view only candidates/contacts who have opted out Opt-Out = No to view only candidates/contacts who have not opted out Apply the filter to see the resulting list. Note: At this time, bulk opt-out is not supported ; opting out must be done on an individual basis. FAQs Can I bulk opt out multiple contacts at once? No. Bulk opt-out is not supported currently. You can only opt out candidates or contacts individually, or let them opt out themselves via the unsubscribe link in your emails. Conclusion: Use the unsubscribe link, manual opt-out, and opt-in controls together with list filtering to keep your communication targeted and respectful of recipient preferences. t: Enterprise Plan
s: This article will provide you information about the Enterprise plan.
h: Key Features
What does 'Unlimited' mean on the Enterprise plan for AI Sourcing?
How to upgrade to the Enterprise plan?

Can I still purchase additional credits separately?

b: Recruit CRM’s Enterprise Plan is designed for recruitment agencies that want complete access to every feature—without the hassle of purchasing at an additional cost. This all-inclusive subscription bundles all current and future integrations, enhanced quotas into a single plan, streamlining billing, procurement, and feature access. Whether you're looking to boost automation, scale outreach, or unlock advanced analytics, the Enterprise plan gives you everything, without the extra complexity. 🎯 Key Features All-Inclusive Subscription: You can get access to all current features, including LinkedIn Messages Integration , RecruitCraft , Job posting and distribution , Advanced Analytics , and more — no separate purchases required. Note: If you would like to start using Advanced Analytics, please feel free to reach out to your Account Manager, who will be happy to assist you. Enterprise plan feature quotas (per user/month): Workflow Automation: 1,000 tasks Data Enrichment: 500 credits Calling Credits: Region-specific credits are allotted per user. Job Advertising: 10 jobs RecruitCraft Jobs: Unlimited (if connected) 30,000 records per entity per user (candidates, contacts, companies) Unlimited Advanced Analytics & LinkedIn Messaging Unlimited AI Sourcing credits* What does 'Unlimited' mean on the Enterprise plan for AI Sourcing? The Enterprise plan includes unlimited candidate searches, meaning there is no fixed monthly quota. You can run searches freely based on your hiring needs. To ensure consistent platform performance for all users, we apply a soft Fair Usage limit of 2,500 searches per user per month. This limit is designed to prevent misuse (such as automated scripts or bulk extraction) and does not impact normal recruiting activities. Note: Even though credits are provided per user, they are pooled at the account level meaning all users will be able to use all credits form the combined pool. Seamless Upgrade Experience: You can upgrade to Enterprise plan from Pro plan or Business plan with prorated billing and optional migration of existing add-ons. Flexible Credit Management: The Enterprise plan credits refresh monthly. You can also purchase additional credits if you have a higher usage (except Workflow Automation). Additional Calling Credits will not refresh monthly. Scalable with Your Team: You can add users anytime and quotas auto-scale. You can deactivate users and quotas adjust at the next renewal cycle. How to upgrade to the Enterprise plan? 1. Click on Admin Settings > Plans & Billing > Plans 2. Select 'Enterprise Plan' and review your order & proceed to checkout to make the payment. Hope this helps!😊 🤔FAQs Can I still purchase additional credits separately? Yes, if you are on the Enterprise Plan all features are bundled. However, if you need additional credits (except Workflow Automations), you can still purchase top-ups separately. It is not directly possible to purchase additional tasks for Workflow Automation on the Enterprise plan. This is a limitation from workato but if you need additional tasks you can reach out to us through the chat bot at the bottom right corner of your screen and we can add additional credit to an account from the backend. What happens to my current additional feature subscriptions when I upgrade? You’ll be prompted to either cancel or retain them. If retained, they will sync to your new Enterprise billing cycle. Do Enterprise Plan credits roll over? No. Credits refresh monthly and expire if unused. How do quotas work in multi-user teams? Quotas are assigned per user but pooled at the account level. If you add/remove users, your overall quota adjusts accordingly. Conclusion: The Enterprise plan gives your team access to Recruit CRM’s full feature set, enhanced quotas, and flexible credit management in one subscription. t: Entity Type Custom Fields
s: This article will help you to create entity type custom fields.
h: How to create an Entity Type Custom Field
Why are these fields only multi-select and not single-select?
Why are some fields not clickable?
Can I search records I don’t have access to?
Why can’t I use placeholders with these fields?
What happens if an imported value doesn't match any record?
Why aren’t these fields supported on the Talent Pool or Job Application settings?
b: Custom Entity-Type Fields empower recruiters to tailor their CRM and ATS to fit their unique workflows by linking key records like Candidates, Jobs, Contacts, Companies, Deals, Users, and Teams. These fields streamline data management, boost visibility across connected entities, and enhance automation and reporting capabilities across platforms. This feature brings the flexibility of creating multi-select searchable fields that connect entities, ensuring data integrity, consistency, and a major productivity boost — especially when used with automation tools like API, Zapier, and Webhooks. ​ 🧩 How to create an Entity Type Custom Field You can create and manage custom fields linking to Candidates, Contacts, Companies, Jobs, Deals, Users, and Teams. Please note that this is supported on Candidates, Jobs, Contacts, Companies, and Deals. 1. Go to Admin Settings and refer to the section 'Data Customization'. Select Candidate, Company, Contact, Deal or Job Fields: 2. Now, click on 'New Custom Field', name your field, and then on 'Field Type', choose between Candidates, Contacts, Companies, Jobs, Deals, Users, and Teams. 3. There you go! You have created your field and now can see it on the record type selected. You can also add those fields to the Profile View: And to the List View: Hope this helps! 😃 FAQs Why are these fields only multi-select and not single-select? Multi-select ensures users can associate multiple related records (e.g., multiple candidates to a job) for richer data linking and flexibility. Why are some fields not clickable? For User and Team fields, profile viewing is restricted for privacy and security. Clicking is disabled to avoid exposing sensitive team/user info. Can I search records I don’t have access to? No, if you don't have access to view a record, you won't be able to search it. Why can’t I use placeholders with these fields? Placeholder support is intentionally excluded since entity fields are structured references rather than free-text entries. What happens if an imported value doesn't match any record? The field is skipped to maintain data accuracy. You must ensure correct slugs, email IDs, or team names are used. Why aren’t these fields supported on the Talent Pool or Job Application settings? These fields are meant to track internal data and are ideally not to be exposed. b: What this feature does & when to use it? Custom Entity-Type Fields empower recruiters to tailor their CRM and ATS to fit their unique workflows by linking key records like Candidates, Jobs, Contacts, Companies, Deals, Users, and Teams. These fields streamline data management, boost visibility across connected entities, and enhance automation and reporting capabilities across platforms. This feature brings the flexibility of creating multi-select searchable fields that connect entities, ensuring data integrity, consistency, and a major productivity boost — especially when used with automation tools like API, Zapier, and Webhooks. Step-by-step instructions You can create and manage custom fields linking to Candidates, Contacts, Companies, Jobs, Deals, Users, and Teams. Please note that this is supported on Candidates, Jobs, Contacts, Companies, and Deals. Go to your Admin Settings . Navigate to the Data Customisation section, where custom fields are managed. In Data Customization, select the record type where you want to add the entity type custom field. (Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Deals, or Jobs.) Within the chosen record type, click New Custom Field . Enter a Field Name that explains the relationship (for example, “Key Account Contacts”, “Associated Recruiters”, or “Related Jobs”). From the Field Type options, choose one of the supported entities: Candidate, Contact, Companies, Job, Deals, Users, or Team. Once saved, the field becomes available on all records of that record type. You can also add those fields to the Profile View: And to the List View: Troubleshooting Problem: The entity type custom field is not visible on records Likely Cause: The entity type custom field was created for a different record type than the one you are currently viewing in Recruit CRM. What to Check: Go to Settings > Custom Fields and confirm which record type (Candidates, Contacts, Jobs, etc.) the field was created under. Resolution Path: Open a record of the matching type, or create the same field under the correct record type if you need it elsewhere. Problem: Users can see the field, but cannot edit it Likely cause: Role or permission restrictions are preventing edits. What to check: Review user roles and permissions related to editing records and custom fields. Resolution path: Adjust user roles to grant edit access where appropriate. Ask an Admin to verify that no additional restrictions are configured on that record type. FAQs 1. Why are these fields only multi-select and not single-select? Multi-select ensures users can associate multiple related records (e.g., multiple candidates to a job) for richer data linking and flexibility. 2. Why are some fields not clickable? For User and Team fields, profile viewing is restricted for privacy and security. Clicking is disabled to avoid exposing sensitive team/user info. 3. Can I search records I don’t have access to? No, if you don't have access to view a record, you won't be able to search it. 4. Why can’t I use placeholders with these fields? Placeholder support is intentionally excluded since entity fields are structured references rather than free-text entries. 5. What happens if an imported value doesn't match any record? The field is skipped to maintain data accuracy. You must ensure correct slugs, email IDs, or team names are used. 6. Why aren’t these fields supported on the Talent Pool or Job Application settings? These fields are meant to track internal data and are ideally not to be exposed. Conclusion: Entity type custom fields in the new UI let you connect candidates, jobs, contacts, companies, deals, users, and teams in a structured, searchable way. By setting them up thoughtfully and adding them to your key views, you can streamline workflows, improve data integrity, and unlock more powerful reporting and automation. t: Explore dashboards in Advanced Analytics
s: This article will guide you on how to see, and explore the data behind dashboards and questions in Advanced Analytics.
h: Step-by-step instructions on how to explore dashboards in Metabase
Tabular View of Results
How to change the visualization type
Drill down on records
Summary
Troubleshooting
Problem: The dashboard or chart displays outdated data.
Problem: The numbers on the dashboard do not match the same chart when opened separately.
b: Step-by-step instructions on how to explore dashboards in Metabase You can find the Shared collection in the left navigation sidebar. If you need a refresher, check out the article on how to find data in Advanced Analytics . We’ll work with the Default dashboard pinned in the Shared collection. Tabular View of Results In Advanced Analytics, you can explore the numbers behind every dashboard and chart by viewing them in table format. 1.Go to the default dashboard in the Shared collection You should see multiple tabs and cards with charts. For example, the “Candidates added per month” card shows the new candidate count for each month. The data shows an interesting seasonal pattern for candidates, so let’s explore it further! 2.Open the question “Candidates added per month” by clicking on the chart title in the dashboard. From the question view, you can add summaries and filters, but first, let’s look at the raw results behind the question. 3.See the results as a table by clicking on the table icon under the chart. Each row represents a month, and there are two columns: one for created on: month and other for count of candidates, corresponding to the series displayed on the chart. You can switch back to visualization by clicking on the chart icon next to the table icon. How to change the visualization type You can modify a chart’s visualization without affecting other users unless you overwrite the question. For example, you can switch between showing time series as a bar chart or a line chart, or maybe you just really hate pie charts (not us – we love all our charts equally). And our pies are technically donuts. Let’s make “ Candidates added per month ” into a bar chart. 1.Open the question “Candidates added per month” from the Shared Collection. 2.Open the visualization sidebar by clicking on the “Visualization” icon in the bottom left of the chart. You’ll see that this is currently a line chart. 3.Switch to a bar chart by clicking on “Bar”. Now the series – total candidates added per month will be represented by bars. Drill down on records Many charts in Advanced Analytics allow you to drill down into data by simply clicking on a data point. 1.Open the default dashboard and switch to the “Deals & Companies “ tab . The “Total Deals by Deal Stage ” chart shows the number of deals for each deal stage. The Won stage has the largest number of deals. We can dive deeper into these numbers and look at the deals that contribute to this. 2. Look at all deals in Won stage on the “Total Deals by Deal Stage” chart: Click on the Won region. Select “See these Deals” from the menu. This will open a table displaying all deals in the won stage. You can now look for patterns, such as which owners have the most deals at this stage. Let’s look for all Won stage deals for a specific filter. 3. How can I filter deals by a specific owner? Once you’ve drilled down to a table view, you can further refine the data: Find all records for deals with “Vivek Singhs” as Owner Name: Find the Owner Name column and click on column name. Choose option Filter by this column 3.Select name of the person you want to filter out by and click add filter 4.The table will now show only deals in won stage for this owner. The active filters will be displayed above the table. 5.You can continue drilling further, for example, by clicking on a Collaborator name to filter deals for that owner and collaborator. 6 . Return to the original “Total Deals by Deal Stage” question by clicking on “Started from Total Deals by Deal Stage ” at the top left of your screen. The drill through options that you get depend on the type of chart you’re using and your data: for example, on time series charts you can select a time period to zoom in on it. Summary You can explore the data behind the dashboards and questions on your own. For example, you can See the results as a table. Change the visualization type. Drill down on metrics to see individual records. Troubleshooting Problem: The dashboard or chart displays outdated data. Likely cause : The results are being served from your browser cache. What to check: Refresh the page after clearing your browser cache. Open the underlying question to verify whether it now displays the latest data. Resolution path: Clear your browser cache and reload the page. This resolves the issue in almost all cases. Problem: The numbers on the dashboard do not match the same chart when opened separately. Likely cause : Dashboard filters are being applied in addition to the chart's own filters, resulting in different values. What to check: Check whether any dashboard filters are currently applied. Open the underlying question and compare its configured filters with the dashboard filters. Verify whether both the dashboard and the standalone question are using the same filter values. Resolution path: Clear any active dashboard filters and compare the chart again. If the values still differ, review the filters configured within the underlying question and ensure they align with the dashboard filters. Conclusion: Dashboards aren't just static charts, you can view the underlying data as a table, switch visualization types, and drill down into individual records to investigate the patterns behind the numbers. These exploration tools help you move from a high-level chart to specific, actionable insights without leaving Advanced Analytics. If you need help at any stage, feel free to reach out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance. Hope this helps! This feature allows you to export data from Recruit CRM into CSV or Excel files directly from list pages or reports, preserving your selected fields and filters for easy use outside the platform. Use this feature when you want to: Analyse data in Excel or Google Sheets. Create backups of your records. Step-by-step instructions 1. Export records from the list page: You can use the same export process for candidates, contacts, jobs, companies, and deals. Navigate to the list page of your desired entity. For example, go to the Candidates entity page. Select the number of records that you want to export. Click on the Export button from the top header bar under the More tab. In the export pop-up, choose the fields that you want to have in the exported sheet. Hit the Export button to download the file (CSV or Excel, as available). The GIF illustrates how to export the selected records to CSV/Excel. When exporting Jobs, the "Updated By" column shows the user's full name (e.g., Ryan Cooper), just like other user-reference columns in the export. 2. Export all candidates from the list page (beyond 3,000 records): This will allow you to export all the candidate records in a section when exporting more than 3,000 candidates while still respecting any filters you have applied. Navigate to the Candidate list page. You can bulk select the candidates or only those from a filtered search. Click on the Export All button from the top header bar under the More tab. Choose the fields you want to have in the exported sheet and hit the Export button to download the file. The GIF below shows exactly how it works. 3. Export data from Reports: Navigate to the Reports section. Select a report you wish to generate. Select the parameters, i.e., timeframe, teammates, etc, and generate the report. Once the report is generated, click on the Export Report to CSV button to download the tabular data of the report. Additionally, each bar on the chart is also clickable and will direct you to the detailed list of data. You can also export this data by clicking the Export to CSV button located on the header bar. Troubleshooting Problem: You can’t see the Export or Export All options. Likely cause: You do not have the required permission to export. What to check: Confirm whether you are the Account Owner or an Admin. Resolution path: Ask the Account Owner/Admin to either export the data for you or update your role/permissions. Problem: You can’t find the “Export All” option for candidates. Likely cause: You have fewer than 3,000 candidates selected. What to check: Check the total number of selected candidates on the candidate list page. Resolution path: If under 3,000, use the standard export from the list page. “Export All” appears only when more than 3,000 candidates are selected. Problem: Report export works, but the chart-level detail export does not show the expected records. Likely cause : You clicked a specific bar that only represents a subset of the data. What to check: Confirm which bar on the chart you have clicked and what filters are applied to that view. Resolution path: Adjust filters or select a different bar if you want a different subset of data, then export again. FAQs 1. Who can export data to CSV or Excel from Recruit CRM? Only the Account Owner, Admins, and users on custom roles can export data from list pages and reports. 2. Which entities can I export from the list page? You can export records from Candidates, Contacts, Jobs, Companies, and Deals. The method of exporting data for all entities is the same. 3. Is export available on the free plan? Yes. The export option from the list page is available on all plans, including the free plan. 4. Does export respect filters and selections? Yes. Both standard exports and “Export All” for candidates respect any filters you have applied and the fields you select. Conclusion: Exporting data to CSV or Excel from Recruit CRM helps you analyse, share, and back up your records across candidates, contacts, jobs, companies, deals, and reports. b: What this feature does & when to use it? This feature allows you to export data from Recruit CRM into CSV or Excel files directly from list pages or reports, preserving your selected fields and filters for easy use outside the platform. Use this feature when you want to: Analyse data in Excel or Google Sheets. Create backups of your records. Please Note: Only the Account Owner, Admins, and users on the Custom Roles with access to export can export data. Users on the Team Member role and Restricted Team Member roles cannot use export. How to export records from the list pages? You can use the same export process for candidates, contacts, jobs, companies, and deals. Navigate to the list page of your desired entity. For example, go to the Candidates entity page. Select the number of records that you want to export. Click on the Export button from the top header bar under the More tab. In the export pop-up, choose the fields that you want to have in the exported sheet. Hit the Export button to download the file (CSV or Excel, as available). When exporting Jobs, the "Updated By" column shows the user's full name (e.g., Ryan Cooper), just like other user-reference columns in the export. How to export data from Reports? Navigate to the Reports section. Select a report you wish to generate. Select the parameters, i.e., timeframe, teammates, etc, and generate the report. ​ Once the report is generated, click on the Export Report to CSV button to download the tabular data of the report. Note: Click the Export As PNG/JPG/SVG options next to the bar graph to export an image of the chart itself. Additionally, each bar on the chart is also clickable and will direct you to the detailed list of data. You can also export this data by clicking the Export to CSV button located on the header bar. Click here to learn about reports in Recruit CRM 📈 Troubleshooting Problem: The Export option is not visible on the list page. Likely cause: The user does not have the required permissions. ​ What to check: Confirm whether you are logged in as the account owner or an admin or a user with the custom role and necessary permission. ​ Resolution: Log in with an account that has account owner or admin rights, or ask the Account Owner to perform the export. Problem: The exported file is missing some fields you expected. Likely cause: The fields were not selected in the export pop-up. ​ What to check: Review which fields you selected before exporting. ​ Resolution: Repeat the export process and, in the export pop-up, select all the fields you need before clicking Export. Problem: The detailed data for a chart bar is not exporting. Likely cause: The detailed list view was not opened before exporting. ​ What to check: Confirm that you clicked on the specific bar in the chart and are viewing the detailed list of records. ​ Resolution: Click the desired bar on the chart to open the detailed list, then use the Export to CSV button at the top of that list. FAQs Q1: Who can export data from Recruit CRM? Only the account owner and admins can export data and users with the custom role with the necessary permissions. Q2: Which record types can I export from list pages? You can export candidate, contact, job, company, and deal records from their respective list pages. Q3: Can I choose which fields are included in the export file? Yes. When the export pop-up box appears, you can select the relevant and necessary fields you wish to export before clicking the Export button. Conclusion: Exporting data to CSV or Excel from Recruit CRM helps you analyse, share, and back up your records across candidates, contacts, jobs, companies, deals, and reports. What if I choose day-wise columns?

b: Export timesheets in just a few clicks so you can send data to clients or integrate it with payroll systems. It brings flexibility, speed, and better organization to your workflow. 1. Only users with export permissions can export timesheets. 2. If a user cannot view a candidate, they cannot export that candidate’s timesheets. Note : Currently, this feature is in beta version and can be enabled upon request. Please feel free to reach out to your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. 📋 How to Export Timesheets Go to the Jobs page and open a job with the type set to Contract or Contract to Permanent . ​ Scroll to the Candidate Pipeline section and click View All Timesheets . 3. There are two ways to export timesheets: individually or in bulk. ​ Export an Individual Timesheet You can directly export the desired timesheet in XLSX (default format) by clicking on the Export button in the Action column. ​ If you want to export it in CSV, follow along - ​ i. Click on the desired timesheet period. ii. Choose the preferred export format (XLSX or CSV). iii. Click Export . ​ ​ Export Multiple Timesheets i. Select the timesheets you want to export, or use the top box to select all. ​ ii. Click the Export button on the top header bar. ​ iii. Choose the fields you want to include that will be exported in the timesheet. ​ iv. ​If you want to export each day as a separate column, check the box at the top. This generates a day-wise breakdown with separate sheets for each timesheet period, with the option to include daily work and overtime hours. ​ v. Select the desired format (XLSX or CSV) and click Export. If CSV is selected with day-wise export enabled, the output is delivered as a ZIP file containing a separate CSV for each timesheet period.​ ​ Please note You can follow the same steps to export timesheets from the Deals section. 🚀 Key Features Comprehensive Export Export timesheets in any status: Open, Submitted, Approved, or Rejected. ​ Bulk Export Export multiple timesheets in one action from the Contractor Details or Deals Details page. ​ Single Timesheet Export Export an individual timesheet directly from its detail view. ​ Multiple Formats Export in XLSX (default) or CSV. ​ Customizable Fields Select fields such as candidate name, job name, company name, deal name, and other timesheet-related details. ​ Day-wise Breakdown Export each day as a separate column for detailed totals, including work hours and overtime. Separate sheets are created for each timesheet period when day-wise breakdown is enabled. ​ Organized Data Timesheet dates are exported in MM/DD/YYYY format. Hours appear in decimal form (e.g., 8h 30m shows as 8.5). If you would like to learn more about this feature, you can book a quick call with our team through this link . ❓ FAQs What if I choose day-wise columns? In XLSX, each timesheet period appears as a separate sheet within one file. In CSV, each period is exported as an individual file, and all files are bundled in a single ZIP. If day-wise export is not selected, all data appears in one sheet with the chosen fields. How are work hours exported for shifts? Shift-based timesheets show hours exactly as recorded. For example, a shift from 09:00 to 17:00 appears the same in the export. t: FAQ Handbook
s: All the most frequently asked questions about Recruit CRM
h: 1. Does Recruit CRM provide a free trial, and how long can I use the free trial?
https://recruitcrm.io ​
2. Can I log into Recruit CRM from multiple devices?
iPad: https://apps.apple.com/uz/app/recruit-crm/id1532855707#?platform=ipad
Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.recruitcrm
