t: How Free Job Board Posting Works in Recruit CRM
s: How to post job on job boards?
b: Posting jobs to free job boards is super simple in Recruit CRM! We do all the heavy lifting for you and it's 100% Automatic. Recruit CRM posts jobs on the following free job boards: Zip Recruiter CareerJet Google for Jobs Talent.com (earlier known as Neuvoo) Job Rapido Adzuna Post Job Free My Jobhelper Jooble Twine Note: If you want to post jobs on Adzuna, Post Job Free, My Jobhelper, Jooble or Twine then you need to select these job boards in the "XML feeds" field while adding or editing a job. On Jooble, applicants will see a "Direct apply" feature rather than being redirected to the Apply page, but please note that we will not get data on custom fields and mandatory fields that you might have added on your application page. How to get a job posted on the free job boards Before you create a new job in Recruit CRM, please make sure you have ticked the job posting box inside Job Fields in Admin settings . This will help post your open jobs on your website and other job boards. ❌ Please note that if you untick the checkbox none of your jobs will be posted. The first step is to make sure all the necessary criteria are met for the jobs to be visible on the XML Feed and posted on the free job boards. These are: The job application form should be enabled; The Updated On date should be within the last 30 days; All the fields where you see the message "Required To Post On Partner Job Boards" (City, State, Country, Maximum Salary, Job Description, Currency, Salary Type) need to have a value; The required fields might change in the future according to the demands of job boards. You may enter either the full name or just the initials in the required fields (necessary for posting on partner job boards), as both options are acceptable. 'Note for candidates' should be filled in (only if the Job Description is uploaded as a file); The "Post On Job Boards" option should be selected inside Admin Settings >> Job Custom Fields ; The job status should not be 'closed', 'on hold' or 'cancelled'; Select "Free Job Board" under the XML Feeds section ⬇️⬇️⬇️ You have the ability to selectively push job postings to specific XML feeds. While adding/editing a job, you'll get an option to select the XML feeds from both the default and custom XML feeds that you have built, provided the 'Post on Job Board' option is enabled from the Job Fields settings . While creating a new job or editing an existing one, make sure you select "Free Job Boards" in the XML Feeds section to get your jobs posted on the correct XML Feed. ​ By selecting the appropriate XML feeds, you can ensure that your jobs reach the intended audience through the most relevant job boards. You also have the option to preselect the XML feeds in the Build Job Feed XML page. This means the XML Feed will automatically be selected for all new jobs created. ​ If you don't want a job to be automatically posted on the Free Job Boards XML Feed you can simply disable the preselection on the Build Job Feed XML or uncheck the XML Feed while creating/editing the job: The jobs will be indexed to the external boards only if the requirements given above are met. Once you add details to these fields, the job goes through the review process. If everything is fine, Recruit CRM will publish your jobs with partner job boards instantly. Please note that since this is a free integration, the decision to post the job or not is up to the job board. Each job board has its own criteria and your job might not fit into their requirements. And that's it! You'll start receiving applications for those jobs in Recruit CRM! How do I know if my job was posted? 1. You can check the list of jobs eligible to be pushed to the free job boards' feed by going to Admin Settings >>>>>> Build Job Feed XML . Here you can click on "View Listed Jobs" to get a list of all the jobs in your account that currently meet the required criteria: If one of your jobs is not on the list, one of the necessary criteria is not being met. ​ Common Issues in Job Visibility: Job Removed from Free Job Boards: • Unchecking the "Default Job Application Form Visibility/post on job boards" option or leaving a required field blank will remove the job from the XML feed. This will effectively take the job off the free job boards. Make sure these settings are carefully reviewed and configured. Job Not Visible Despite Meeting All Steps: • Ensure that the correct XML feed includes the intended job boards. Double-check your selections and include "Free Job Boards" in the XML feed configuration. You can also run an Advanced Search inside the Jobs List Page to see all the jobs that have been posted on Indeed (including old jobs that are no longer being pushed to the XML feed). ​ 2. You can search the job boards' websites to check if the job was posted. When your job is posted on the partner job boards, it will look something like this: The view will vary depending on the job board. The attached image is an actual job posting for one of our clients Once the candidate clicks on the " Apply on Website " button, they will be redirected to your website where the job is posted. There they can read the job description and apply for that job. 3. Another way to verify if the job was posted or not is to look for applicant candidates in your database. You can do this by enabling the Source field in Candidate Fields : ​ With the Source field, you'll be able to track the origin of how the candidate was added to the system. If the candidate applies externally, the name of the job board will be mentioned in the field: ​ You can even run an Advanced Search on the Source field: ​ Learn how to track the source of job applications How will you get applications for the jobs? When a candidate fills out the application form, you'll be notified in Recruit CRM. You can see all the website applicants on the candidate list page . How to post jobs on other portals? If you want to post jobs on other portals, you need to follow the steps below: 1. Go to the Jobs page and open the job you want to post. 2. Copy the Job Application URL inside the job and share it on social media or in the advert inside the job board you already partner with. ​ Click here to learn more about sharing jobs on social media You can also create your own custom XML Feed to integrate with other job boards directly. Click here to learn more That's about it! You know what to do if you need help ;) Related Articles Integrating Indeed With Recruit CRM Build your own XML feed for job boards Organic Posting Network (OPN) How Free Job Board Posting Works in Recruit CRM (New UI) Integrating Indeed With Recruit CRM (New UI)

t: How Free Job Board Posting Works in Recruit CRM (New UI)
s: This article explains how free job posting works in Recruit CRM, including supported partner job boards, XML feed configuration, and how to make jobs eligible for posting.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Supported Free Job Boards:
Before You Begin:
Step-by-step instructions
1. Enable global settings for Job Application form visibility
2. Enable the Job Application Form for the job.
3. Keep the “Updated On” date within the last 30 days.
4. Fill in all fields marked “Required to post on partner job boards”
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Free job posting automatically sends eligible jobs to partner job boards through XML feeds, helping you advertise roles across multiple platforms without manually posting on each one. Applications received through these job boards are automatically captured in Recruit CRM as candidate records. This feature is especially useful when you want to: • Advertise jobs on multiple free job boards automatically. • Receive applications directly into Recruit CRM. Supported Free Job Boards: Recruit CRM posts eligible jobs to the following ten free partner job boards: Zip Recruiter CareerJet Google for Jobs Talent.com (earlier known as Neuvoo) Job Rapido Adzuna Post Job Free My Jobhelper Jooble Twine 📌 Important notes on specific boards: Adzuna, Post Job Free, My Job Helper, Jooble, and Twine: You must explicitly select them in the XML feeds field when adding or editing each job. Jooble Direct Apply: On Jooble, applicants see a Direct Apply option rather than being redirected to your application page. Recruit CRM will not receive data for any custom fields or mandatory fields you have added to your application form when candidates apply through this method. Before You Begin: Admin access required for global settings: Only users with access to Admin Settings can configure Job Fields, Job Custom Fields, and Build Job Feed XML. Recruiters and team members handle job-level settings only. This is a free integration: Recruit CRM includes your job in the XML feed when it meets all criteria, but each partner job board makes its own decision about whether to publish the job. Meeting all requirements in Recruit CRM does not guarantee the job will appear on every board. Step-by-step instructions The first step is to make sure all the necessary criteria are met for the jobs to be visible on the XML Feed and posted on the free job boards. 1. Enable global settings for Job Application form visibility Before jobs can be posted to free job boards, the required account-level settings must be enabled. Go to Admin Settings in Recruit CRM and open Job Fields under the Data Customisation section. Ensure the Default Job Application Form Visibility checkbox is enabled.Once the Default Job Application Form Visibility is enabled, make sure to select the Post on Job Boards option. If this setting is disabled, jobs will not be posted on your website or partner job boards. ​ 2. Enable the Job Application Form for the job. In the Add/Edit Job form, scroll to the Job Application Form section and make sure the checkbox for Enable Job Application Form is selected. 3. Keep the “Updated On” date within the last 30 days. The job must have been updated within the last 30 days. Jobs that have not been updated during this period are excluded from the XML feed. ​ ​ 4. Fill in all fields marked “Required to post on partner job boards” Open the job form and fill in all fields labeled Required to post on partner job boards . This currently includes fields such as City, State, Country, Maximum Salary, Job Description, Currency and Salary Type. ​ Please note: • Both full names and initials are accepted in required fields. • Required fields may change over time based on partner job board requirements. 5. Fill the “Note for candidate” field when using a file-based job description If the Job Description is uploaded as a file instead of entered as text, the Note for Candidate field must also be completed for the job to qualify for posting. 6. The job status should not be 'closed', 'on hold' or 'cancelled'. A job must have the status set to Open in order to be eligible for posting on job boards in Recruit CRM. Jobs with statuses like Closed, On Hold, or Cancelled cannot be posted. ​ 7. Select “Free Job Boards” in the XML Feeds section. Recruit CRM allows you to selectively push jobs to specific XML feeds, helping you control which job boards receive each posting. While creating or editing a job, locate the XML Feeds field and select Free Job Boards from the available feed list. Save the job after making your selection. If you want the job to appear on specific partner job boards such as Adzuna, Post Job Free, My Job Helper, Jooble, Twine, make sure those boards are also selected in the XML feed options for that job. You can choose from both: • Default XML feeds provided by Recruit CRM • Custom XML feeds created by your team Please note that XML feed selection will only work if the Post on Job Board option is enabled under the Job Fields settings, as mentioned in Step 1. You can also preselect XML feeds from the Build Job Feed XML page. When preselected, those XML feeds will automatically be selected for all newly created jobs. ​ If you do not want a job to be posted to the Free Job Boards XML feed automatically, you can: • Disable the XML feed preselection from the Build Job Feed XML page, or • Manually uncheck the XML feed while creating or editing the job. ​ ​ Please note: • Jobs will only be indexed and pushed to external job boards if all the eligibility requirements mentioned above are met. • Once all required details are added, the job goes through a review process. If everything is fine, Recruit CRM pushes the job to partner job boards automatically. • Since this is a free integration, the final decision to publish the job remains with the respective job board. Each partner board follows its own review criteria, and some jobs may not qualify based on their internal requirements. Verify Whether a Job Was Posted Use the following three methods to confirm that a job is live on partner job boards. ​ Method 1: Check the Build Job Feed XML Listing Go to Admin Settings → Build Job Feed XML . Click View Listed Jobs for the Free Job Boards feed or for the other Job Boards that you have selected. Review the list. All jobs that currently meet all eligibility criteria will appear here. If a job is missing from the list, at least one eligibility criterion is not being met." ​ 💡 Tip: You can also run an Advanced Search on the Jobs List page to view all jobs where XML feeds have been selected. ​ Method 2: Search the Partner Job Board Website Directly Go to the relevant partner job board website, for example, ZipRecruiter or Talent.com. Search for the job by title, location, or other identifying details to check if the job was posted. Once the candidate clicks on the " Apply on Website " button, they will be redirected to your website where the job is posted. There they can read the job description and apply for that job. Method 3: Track Applications via the Source Field Enable the Source field in Candidate Fields if it is not already visible on candidate records. When a candidate applies externally from a job board, the Source field on their candidate record will display the name of the job board they applied from. You can run an Advanced Search on the Source field from the Candidate List page to filter and see all candidates who came from specific job boards. Get applications for jobs posted on free job boards When a candidate fills out the application form (either via your website or through an Apply on Website button on a job board), Recruit CRM will: • Add the application as a candidate record. • Notify you inside Recruit CRM. ​ 1. t: How Google for Jobs Works With Your Recruit Craft Career Page
s: Learn how Recruit Craft submits job listings to Google for Jobs and which Recruit CRM job details are used for Google for Jobs listings.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
What is Google for Jobs?
How it works
Fields sent to Google for Jobs
FAQs
Will my job definitely appear in Google for Jobs if every required field is filled in?
What happens if an optional field is missing?
Why does my company name sometimes look different on Google compared to my career page?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? When you publish a job on your Recruit Craft career page, Recruit Craft automatically submits the job details to Google for Jobs , Google's job search experience. This gives candidates another way to discover your open positions when searching on Google. There is no separate setup required. Recruit Craft automatically creates the information Google needs using the details already available in Recruit CRM. Use this article to understand: How Google for Jobs works with Recruit Craft Which Recruit CRM fields are sent to Google When specific job details are included What to check if Google reports missing information What is Google for Jobs? Google for Jobs is a feature within Google Search that collects job listings from different websites and displays them in a dedicated job search experience. Candidates can use filters such as location and job type to find relevant opportunities. To make a job available for this experience, Google reads structured information from the job's webpage. Recruit Craft automatically creates this information for jobs published on your career page using the JobPosting format defined by Schema.org . You do not need to configure or manage this structured data yourself. Recruit Craft handles the formatting and uses the information stored in your Recruit CRM job record. How it works When you publish a job, Recruit Craft takes the relevant information from the job record in Recruit CRM and maps it to the fields expected by Google. Some fields are always included because they are required for a valid job listing. Other fields are included only when the required information is available, or a specific setting has been enabled in Recruit CRM. 📌 Please note: Having complete and valid job information does not guarantee that the job will appear in Google for Jobs. Google decides which jobs are indexed and displayed based on its own indexing and ranking process. Recruit Craft follows Google's recommended structured data practices, so keeping your job information complete gives your listing the best possible chance of being picked up accurately. Fields sent to Google for Jobs The table below shows the information Recruit Craft can send to Google, where the information comes from in Recruit CRM, and when it is included. What Google receives Comes from in Recruit CRM When it is included Job title Job Title Always Job description Job Description Always Date the job was posted Last Updated Date Always Date the listing is valid through Last Updated Date + 30 days Always Job address including street, locality, state or province, postal code, and country Street Address, Locality, State/Province, Postal Code, Country Only when available on the job Whether the job is remote Job Location Type Only when Job Location Type is set to Remote Country candidates must be located in for remote jobs Country Only when the job is Remote and a Country is set Employment type such as full time or part time Job Type Only when the Job Type can be matched to a type recognized by Google Salary currency, minimum, and maximum Salary Currency, Minimum Annual Salary, Maximum Annual Salary Only when the salary range is visible on the job card in Recruit Craft and the relevant value is available Your company's identifying name on Recruit Craft Recruit Craft Company Name Always Unique reference for the job listing Job Slug Always Whether candidates can apply directly from Google Set automatically Always Job category Job Category Only when available on the job card in Recruit Craft Company name shown to candidates Company Name Always. When company information is configured and visible on the job, Google uses the job's Company Name. Otherwise, it uses the Recruit Craft Company Name. Company logo shown to candidates Company Logo When company information is configured and visible on the job, and a Company Logo is available. Link to the company's website Company Website When company information is configured and visible on the job, and a Company Website is available. Please note - Company information is available to Google when either of these fields is configured and visible on the job: Company Image → Company Logo Company Information Text → Company Name When either field is configured and visible, Google uses the Company Name from that job. If the job also has a Company Logo or Company Website, those details are included as well. If neither field is configured and visible, Google uses the Recruit Craft Company Name instead. The Company Logo and Company Website are not included in this case. ​ FAQs Will my job definitely appear in Google for Jobs if every required field is filled in? No. Google decides which jobs are indexed and displayed through its own indexing and ranking process. Recruit Craft cannot guarantee that a particular job will appear. Keeping the job information complete and valid gives it the best possible chance of being picked up by Google. What happens if an optional field is missing? The job can still be submitted to Google for Jobs. If an optional field does not have the required information, that field is simply left out of the listing. Why does my company name sometimes look different on Google compared to my career page? This depends on the company field mapping on the job. If a Company Image or Company Text field is mapped, Google uses the company information associated with that job. If neither is mapped, Google uses your Recruit Craft Company Name . Can I choose which jobs are sent to Google for Jobs? Jobs published on your Recruit Craft career page are submitted automatically. The information included in the Google listing depends on how complete the job details are in Recruit CRM. Conclusion Recruit Craft automatically prepares your published jobs for Google for Jobs using the information stored in Recruit CRM. Keeping your job records complete, especially details such as location, salary, employment type, and company information, helps ensure that your listings are prepared with the information Google expects and gives them the best possible chance of appearing accurately in Google for Jobs. t: How Radius-Search and Travel Time Search Works in Recruit CRM? (New UI)
s: This article will guide you on how Radius-Search and Travel Time Search work in Recruit CRM.
h: How is location data used in radius search?
How to enable radius search on your account?
Important Note
How to use the Radius Search?
Travel Time Search
b: Recruit CRM's Radius Search lets you look for candidates/contacts within the radius range you choose. The Radius Search feature in Recruit CRM is powered by Google Maps which works well if you have a candidate/contact's address available inside the "Full Address" field of candidate/contact. How is location data used in radius search? Radius search works using a process called Geocoding . Geocoding converts location information into geographic coordinates. Recruit CRM uses these coordinates to calculate distance and return records that fall within the selected radius. ✅ How to enable radius search on your account? Only account owners, admins, and users with custom permissions will have the ability to enable the radius search options for each entity. You can choose which data you'd like to apply a radius search to by toggling the switch for each type of record in Recruit CRM (such as candidates, contacts, companies, and jobs). Follow these steps to enable a radius search for your records. 1. Navigate to your Account section in the Admin Settings . 2. Scroll down until you find the "Radius Search" settings, then switch on the toggle for each entity where you want to perform radius searches. 📌 Important Note Adding a full address through a CSV import does not automatically enable radius search. Radius search works only when the toggle is turned on for the relevant record type, as this allows the system to process the address through geocoding and convert it into coordinates that can be used for searches. 🔍 How to use the Radius Search? Do you need to find iOS Developers in New York who stay within a radius of 10 km of Central Park on your candidate database? Let me show you how you can find your candidate in just seconds! 1. Before you do the search, do make sure you have made the "Full Address" field visible on your list view, by clicking on the small pencil icon next to Advanced Search: Now make sure that you have ticked the "Full Address" field from here: 2. Then go to candidates and click on the 'Add Filters' button: 3. Type the location you want & you can see suggestions as you type, select your preferred location. If it's Central Park, click & select that address from the drop-down: You can also choose to add other filters along with the Radius search. 4. Click on Apply filters and your results will be displayed instantly on the same screen. Also, you can Save this combination of filters if you happen to use this often, by clicking on "Apply Filters & Save Search". P.S. If you are importing a bunch of records in bulk and want to be able to run a radius search on them, please give us an intimation and we will help you with the process. 🚘Travel Time Search You can filter jobs based on travel time instead of just distance! The Travel Time Search filter helps identify jobs that fall within a realistic commuting range from a candidate’s location—based on how long it would take to reach the job by driving, walking, cycling, or public transport. This improves job-candidate matching accuracy, reduces manual screening, and ensures recruiters focus only on viable opportunities. The Travel Time Search Filter is available on the Candidate's New List Page Version and Job’s list page - Advanced Search >>> Full Address. You can enter the candidate’s address or pin code as the starting point, specify commute time (5 to 60 minutes), select travel mode : Driving Public Transport Cycling Walking and filters jobs based on reachability from the candidate’s location using real commute data. Happy Recruiting! Related Articles How to Use Radius Search in Recruit CRM? How to Run a Search in Recruit CRM (New UI) How Radius-Search Works in Recruit CRM? s: This article will give you an overview of how Recruit CRM's data migration process works
h: Step-by-step instructions on how the Data Migration is carried out

b: Recruit CRM's Data Migration service helps transfer your existing database from another ATS or CRM into your Recruit CRM account. The migration process includes extracting your exported data, analyzing and filtering records, mapping fields to Recruit CRM, cleaning and transforming the data where required, testing the import in a test environment, and finally uploading the verified data into your live account. Throughout the process, Recruit CRM's dedicated data migration team works to ensure an accurate, efficient, and hassle-free migration while helping you start with a clean and well-structured database. Use this when: You are moving from another ATS or CRM into Recruit CRM. You want Recruit CRM's data migration team to migrate your existing database. You want to understand the migration process, timelines, and responsibilities. You want to reduce migration costs by cleaning or filtering your records before migration. ​ Step-by-step instructions on how the Data Migration is carried out Step 1: Request and share your data export: Request a complete data export from your previous ATS/CRM provider. Once you receive the exported data, share it with Recruit CRM's Data Migration team through your Customer Success Manager. After receiving the files, the Data Migration team will extract the data and upload it into their internal systems for further processing. Step 2: Count analysis and initial filtering: Once the exported data has been imported into the team's local database, an initial analysis of the data is performed. During this stage, the team verifies the total record count for: Candidates Companies Contacts Jobs The team can also apply filters to remove outdated or unnecessary records based on criteria such as: Last updated date Location Other filters agreed upon during the migration planning process This helps create a cleaner, more functional database by excluding records that are no longer required. ​ Example: If 5,000 candidates have not been contacted since 2021 and you only want recently updated candidate profiles, those older records can be excluded from the migration. Once the analysis is complete, the team shares the record counts with you for verification. Once the counts are confirmed to be accurate, we proceed to raise an invoice for the data migration service. If any discrepancies or special conditions are identified, the team performs another round of analysis to resolve them before moving forward. Note: Filtering the data is a good way of reducing the data migration cost since it's calculated on the total number of records in the database. Step 3: Data analysis and field mapping: The next crucial step is to analyze and extract the required data from the source and map it with the equivalent columns in Recruit CRM in a spreadsheet. This process is important to determine what columns will be imported into the system and avoid unnecessary data being mapped into Recruit CRM's database. Note: actual field mapping varies by source system and is confirmed with you during Step 3. The completed field mapping document is then shared with you for review and confirmation. Once you approve the mapping, the Data Migration team begins the data cleaning process. From this point onward, your involvement in the data migration process is complete. The Data Migration team takes care of the remaining steps until the migration is successfully completed. Step 4: Data cleaning and transformation: In data cleaning, we will transform the data according to data analysis and Recruit CRM's database structure. Step 5: Test the data in a test environment: Before importing your data into your Recruit CRM account, the cleaned CSV files are first uploaded into a test environment. This allows the team to verify that: The field mapping is correct. The data structure matches Recruit CRM's requirements. The data imports successfully without any technical issues. Any issues identified during testing are resolved before the final migration begins. Step 6: Upload the verified data to your Recruit CRM account: Once the test import is successful, the same verified data is uploaded into your live Recruit CRM account. After the upload is complete, the data migration process is finished. Your Customer Success Manager or the Data Migration team will notify you once the migration has been successfully completed. Congratulations! Your data migration to Recruit CRM is now complete. ​ Import your data yourself (optional) If you prefer not to use Recruit CRM's paid Data Migration service, you can import your data yourself by: Uploading spreadsheets directly into Recruit CRM. Importing candidate information using the Resume Parser. These self-service options allow you to migrate your database independently whenever needed. Browse the Help Center for more resources 📚 Register for a live training session 💻 FAQs Q1: What is included in Recruit CRM’s data migration process? The process includes extracting your exported data, analyzing and counting records, filtering outdated data, mapping fields to Recruit CRM, cleaning and transforming the data, testing uploads in a test environment, and finally uploading the tested data into your live account. Q2: How is the data migration cost calculated? The data migration cost is calculated based on the number of records in your database. Filtering out unnecessary or outdated records reduces the total cost. Q3: What do I need to provide to start the migration? You need to request and obtain a full data export from your previous ATS or CRM and share it with the data migration team through your customer success manager. Q4: Can I avoid using the paid data migration service? Yes. Instead of the paid migration, you can import your database yourself by directly uploading spreadsheets or using the resume parser in Recruit CRM. Conclusion: With Recruit CRM’s data migration process, you can move your existing data seamlessly while ensuring everything is properly mapped, organized, and ready to use. Our team will guide you through the process and help ensure a smooth transition to Recruit CRM. If you have any questions or need assistance with your migration, feel free to reach out to our Support team. ​ Related Articles Import Mapping Template in Recruit CRM Bulk Importing Jobs into Recruit CRM How Radius-Search and Travel Time Search Works in Recruit CRM? t: How the Candidate Portal Works
s: This article provides an overview of how the Candidate Portal works and highlights key areas that can be configured for the hiring process.
h: Candidate Job Search and Sign-Up process
Onboarding Form
Candidate Dashboard
Candidate Statistics
Application History
Open Jobs
Application Process
Saved Jobs
b: The Candidate Portal is a powerful feature of Recruit Craft that enhances the candidate experience by streamlining job applications and profile management. It ensures a seamless and efficient process while keeping everything fully integrated with Recruit CRM , allowing candidates to manage their profiles, track applications, and engage with recruiters effortlessly. Note : The Candidate Portal feature is part of Recruit Craft. RecruitCraft is an Enterprise plan feature that can also be added at an additional cost to Pro or Business plan subscriptions. If you are interested in knowing more about how to access the feature and the price details, you can reach out to us through the chatbot or via email at support@recruitcrm.io Candidate Job Search and Sign-Up process The Candidate Portal integrates with the Career Pages , allowing candidates to view all open jobs. However, they must sign up or log in to apply for positions. Here's the process: Browsing Jobs : Candidates can explore job listings without signing up. Sign Up : Candidates complete a quick signup form. They confirm their email address via an OTP sent to their email address. Upon confirmation, they’re directed to the Onboarding Form . Onboarding Form After signing up, candidates are presented with an Onboarding Form , on which they provide essential details to complete their profiles. The Onboarding Form fields are directly linked to the Profile Update Form in Recruit CRM. You can configure this form in the Admin Settings to collect the information required for your hiring process. Candidate Dashboard Once the Onboarding Form is submitted, candidates are redirected to their Dashboard , which serves as their portal home. Here's what candidates can see: Candidate Statistics A quick overview of their total applications and the stages of each application (e.g., Applied, Assigned, Shortlisted, Placed, etc.). Application History A summary of all the jobs they’ve applied to and the progress of each application. Open Jobs A real-time view of all open positions they can apply to and can bookmark jobs for the future. Application Process By clicking the Apply Now button, candidates can quickly begin the job application process. The application form is designed to be simple and easy to complete, allowing candidates to review their details, fill in any missing information, and submit their application from a single page. ​ ​ ​ When the application form opens, relevant information from the candidate’s profile such as name, contact details, and resume data , is automatically pre-filled where available. This helps reduce the amount of manual input required and allows candidates to focus only on completing any missing details required by the job’s application form. All fields remain editable, so candidates can review and update their information directly before submitting the application. If any required fields are incomplete, they are clearly highlighted to guide the candidate toward the sections that need attention. The Save & Apply button becomes active only after all required information is completed, ensuring that applications are submitted with accurate and complete details. Once the application is submitted successfully, candidates will see a confirmation pop-up on the bottom right corner of the screen, indicating that their application has been received. Saved Jobs Candidates can bookmark jobs they are interested in for future reference. These saved jobs appear on a dedicated Saved Jobs Page . Profile Management Candidates can update their details anytime from the Profile Section of the portal. The profile updates automatically sync with Recruit CRM, keeping candidate information accurate and up-to-date. The Profile section is also linked to the Profile Update form, just like the Onboarding form. It's also possible to change your password from the Profile Section . Application History A detailed Application History Page provides candidates with a record of all jobs they’ve applied to, along with current statuses. Configuration in Recruit CRM You can control how the Candidate Portal works through Recruit CRM. Key configurations include: Onboarding and Profile Update Forms : Customize fields in Admin Settings to gather needed. Job Listings : Ensure jobs are updated in Recruit CRM for visibility on the portal. Application Stages : Regularly update hiring stages to provide candidates with real-time status updates. ​ Disabling Candidate Portal If you no longer want to keep the Candidate Portal active, you can disable it at any time by following these steps. Go to the project you are currently working on. From the dropdown at the top left of the screen, select Candidate Portal . ​ Now navigate to the Pages, and on the left side of the page, you will see a toggle to turn the Candidate Portal on or off. Switch the toggle off to disable the Candidate Portal. ​ A confirmation box will then appear, informing you that candidates will no longer be able to access the portal through this website. It will also clarify that their login credentials, including email and password, will be retained for access to other projects within your account. Select the Disable Portal button in the confirmation box to complete the process. ​ Once disabled, the Candidate Portal will no longer be accessible to candidates. ​ ​ That's it. Cheers! Let us know in case you need any help! :) Related Articles Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s) Signing up on the Hiring Manager Portal How to check the candidate pipeline in your Hiring Manager Portal Recruit Craft: No-Code Career Page & Candidate Portal Builder Compliance Support in Recruit Craft

t: How to access the XML feed
s: This article will guide you on how you can access the XML feed.
h: Step-by-step instructions
Troubleshooting

FAQs
1. Are jobs posted to the job board immediately after they are updated in the XML feed?
2. How often does Indeed check the XML feed for new or updated jobs?

Conclusion:
b: An XML feed is a structured data format used to distribute job listings across different platforms, including job boards. It provides a standardized and machine-readable way to share job-related information. The XML feed follows a specific format organizing details like job titles, descriptions, locations, requirements, and application instructions. Job boards consume the feed to display job listings consistently on their platforms. With the automatic transfer of applicant information, this functionality saves time and reduces errors. You can access the XML feed when: You want to verify which jobs are being sent via XML. Step-by-step instructions Navigate to the Admin settings > Build Job Feed XML . Copy the XML feed URL and paste it into the new tab. You'll see a page with a list of all the jobs eligible to be posted on the job board, provided they fulfil the necessary criteria. Right-click anywhere on the page and select "View Page Source". Now, you'll be able to see the XML feed. Troubleshooting Problem: A job is not visible in the XML feed. Likely cause: The job does not meet the necessary criteria for eligibility. What to check: Confirm if the necessary criteria are met for the jobs to be visible on the XML feed you have created. Click here to learn more about the criteria . Resolution path: Update the job so it fulfils the necessary criteria, wait for the feed to refresh, then check the XML feed again. FAQs 1. Are jobs posted to the job board immediately after they are updated in the XML feed? No. The XML feed is updated automatically, but the timing of when the jobs are actually posted depends on the specific job board. 2. How often does Indeed check the XML feed for new or updated jobs? Indeed uses automated crawlers to check the XML feed approximately every 6 hours (about four times a day). If you add or update a job, Indeed will usually pick up the changes during the next crawl. However, the final decision on whether and when the job is published is entirely up to Indeed. 3. Does every job appear in the Indeed XML feed? No. Only jobs that fulfil the necessary criteria are eligible and will appear in the feed. Conclusion: By following these steps, you can easily access and review your XML feed, verify which jobs are eligible for posting, and share the feed URL with the job board when required. If you have any questions please feel free to reach out to our chatbot located in the bottom-right corner of the page. b: What this feature does and when to use it? Call logs in Recruit CRM help you record and manage phone conversations directly against candidate, contact, or company records. They create a searchable and organized history of call activity, making it easier to track conversations, review outcomes, and collaborate with your team. Each call log can include: • Notes summarizing the conversation • Call start time and duration • Collaborators who participated in the call • An associated record • A contact number • A customizable call type to match your workflow This feature is especially useful when you want to: • Record important candidate or contact conversations • Build a searchable call history on records • Categorize calls and track outcomes over time • Add and manage call logs while working on mobile devices Before you begin: Please note: Make sure you can access the relevant candidate, contact, or company record where you want to add a call log. Be aware that the call outcome field is a default, non-editable field in Recruit CRM. On mobile, ensure you have the Recruit CRM app installed and can access the floater button on the bottom right of the screen. How to Add a Call Log 📞 Method 1: Add a call log from a candidate or contact profile Open the relevant record, such as a candidate or contact profile. ​ Select the specific record you want to work with. Click the call log icon on the profile to start adding a new call log. ​ Fill in the call log details in the form that appears. ​ In the Related to field, confirm or add the company if needed. This can be done when adding call logs from a candidate, contact, or company profile. ​ If needed, specify or update the contact number. The contact number field is optional when adding call logs. On the contact number field, either select a number from existing standard or custom fields or manually enter a new number. ​ Once all details are added, click the green Submit button to save the call log. ​ Use the call notes section to capture key highlights of the conversation so that you and your team can get value from the call history. Method 2: Add a call log using the Global Add plus button: Click the Global Add plus button on the top right of the screen. ​ In the menu that appears, click the Call Log option. ​ A call log form will open on the right side of the screen. ​ Fill in all required and relevant details, including the Related to field, which you must complete manually in this method. ​ Click Submit to save the call log. ​ Note: When you add a call log from a record profile, the Related to field is auto-filled. When you add a call log via the Global Add plus button, you must fill the Related to field yourself. Customizing call type You can add customized call types to tag a call with a specific type so you and your team can easily identify or categorize calls. Use the option to customize call types if you want more granular tracking (for example, different call purposes or stages). Click here to learn how to customize the call type How to Access the Call Logs? 🎯 Open the details view of a candidate or any record. ​ Navigate to the Notes and Calls tab to access the call logs associated with that record. ​ To broaden your view of the activity section, click the expand icon at the top right of the activity area. ​ Use the search box within the expanded activity section to find specific call logs quickly. Apply filters to refine your view and manage your call logs efficiently. ​ On each call log, check the bottom right of the activity card to see the date and time of the call. This is the date you selected when adding the call log. To see when the call log was actually added to the system, hover over the clock icon on the bottom left of the activity card. How to Add Call Logs on the Mobile App? 📲 Open the profile of the specific entity (such as a candidate, contact, or company) in the mobile app. ​ Tap the floater button located at the bottom right corner of the page. ​ Select the option to add a call log. ​ Fill in the call log details, including related record information and call notes. ​ Save the call log to record the call in the system. ​ How to delete call logs? Please note: System generated call logs associated with phone calling credits cannot be deleted by any user. This restriction helps maintain accurate Phone Calling credit usage and prevents discrepancies in credit reporting. Manually created call logs can still be deleted by users such as Account Owners, Admins, and users on custom roles with the appropriate permissions to delete call logs. To delete manually added call logs, click on the 3 dots icon on the call log and select the 'Delete' option. Click on 'Yes' in the delete call log pop-up. FAQs Is the call outcome field editable? No. The call outcome field is not editable. It is a default field designed to track the results of calls made within Recruit CRM, such as whether the call was successful or unsuccessful. Conclusion By following these steps, you can accurately add, review, and manage call logs in Recruit CRM, ensuring every call attempt and conversation is captured for your team. t: How to add collaborators on notes, call logs, tasks, and meetings
s: Add your team members as activity collaborators to keep a track of the performance.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Adding Collaborators
Collaborator Notifications: Keeping Everyone in the Loop
Reporting on Collaborators: Analyzing Impact and Insights
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The collaborator feature lets you add teammates or teams (for Business plan and Enterprise users) to a note, task, call log, or meeting. When you add collaborators to a note, task, call log, or meeting, those collaborators are associated with the activity for better tracking and shared context. Please note: For Business Plan and above users who are part of a team, the collaborator field is auto-populated with the team name so that team members are included by default. Adding Collaborators 1. You will find the "Collaborator" field while adding a note, task, call log, or meeting wherein you can add your teammates or teams to collaborate. ​ 2. You can choose to remove all the team/teammates from the collaborators' field by clicking on the "X" icon on the team/teammate card. 3. You can also add collaborators to the activities while performing the actions from the Chrome extension. Collaborator Notifications: Keeping Everyone in the Loop The selected team members will receive an email notification letting them know they’ve been added as collaborators. They might need to mark this email as "Not Spam" the first time so that all future emails show up right in the inbox. If a "Team" is added in the collaborator section in any activities, the team members of that said team will not get email notifications . Only the teammates who are added as collaborators directly will get an email notification. Reporting on Collaborators: Analyzing Impact and Insights Along with the user performing the action, you can track your collaborators' (only the teams) performance in the reports section, under the team performance report . The activities (notes, call logs, tasks, and meetings added) are generated based on " Created By" (user performing the action), and " Teams" that have been explicitly added in any activity as collaborators. Thus, if a " team" is added as a collaborator on an activity, the same will reflect on the team's statistics in reports. However, it is important to note, that if a "teammate" is directly added as a collaborator, the same will not be reflected in their statistics on the Team Performance Report. Conclusion: Adding collaborators to notes, call logs, tasks, and meetings in Recruit CRM helps keep your team aligned and informed on shared activities. Review the collaborator field each time you create an activity—whether in the main app or via the Chrome extension—to ensure the right teammates and teams are included. t: How to Add Files, Create Folders, and Use Saved Files in Recruit CRM
s: This article explains how to upload files to candidate, job, company, and contact records in Recruit CRM, how to organize those files into folders.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
How to Upload Files to a Record? 🗃️
How to Create Folders in the Files Tab? 📁
How to Attach a file from the Files section to a file-type field? 🎯
How to Attach files to emails from the Saved Files section? 📧
Troubleshooting
FAQs
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The Files section in Recruit CRM lets you store and organize documents related to any record in your database, such as candidates, jobs, companies, and contacts. You can upload files, create folders to keep them organized, and reuse saved files when filling file-type fields or composing emails. You can use this when: You want to store job descriptions, recommendations, or client briefs against specific records. You need to organize files into folders within a record’s Files section. You want to attach existing files from a record’s Files section to file-type fields. Before you begin Please note: Files must be related to an existing record (candidate, contact, company, or job) and uploaded via that record’s details page. Individual file sizes cannot be more than 8 MB. On the business plan, you can create custom roles with restricted access to the Files section. You need access to the relevant record’s details page and Activity section to view and manage files. How to Upload Files to a Record? 🗃️ Open the details page of the record (candidate, job, company, or contact) where you want to store files. ​ In the Activity section, click on the Files tab. ​ Click on the Upload option. ​ Choose the file from your local system that you want to upload, or drag and drop the file into the Files section. ​ Wait for the upload to complete; the file will then appear in the Files section for that record. How to Create Folders in the Files Tab? 📁 In the record’s Files section, click on the Create New Folder button. ​ In the pop-up menu, enter a name for your folder. ​ Click OK to create the folder. ​ Upload or move files into the appropriate folders to keep your documents organized. How to Attach a file from the Files section to a file-type field? 🎯 You can attach files already stored in a record’s Files section directly to file-type fields, without re-uploading from your local system. This works for candidates, contacts, companies, and jobs. Go to the record and locate the file-type field you want to fill. ​ Click on the pencil (edit) icon next to that file field. ​ Click on the arrow icon beside the file upload option. ​ Select the Select from Saved Files option. ​ The files in the record’s Files section will appear in a dropdown list. You can also click on a file name to open a preview before confirming your selection. ​ Select the file you want to attach from the list. Click on the tick mark icon to upload and save it to the file field. ​ Note: You can upload files from the record’s Files section in the edit form and directly to the file fields on the record. Only files uploaded to the specific record you are editing will be visible in the dropdown list, which keeps the process clean and secure. You can still choose Upload File to upload a new file directly from your local system if needed. How to Attach files to emails from the Saved Files section? 📧 You can attach files to emails directly from the Saved Files section, without uploading from your device again. In the email compose window, locate the attachment area. ​ Click on the arrow button beside the Upload from Device option. ​ Click on Select from Saved Files . ​ A list of up to 15 recently used files will be displayed. ​ To find a file linked to a specific record, use the search bar to search for the record, then click on the Search button. ​ Click on a file name to preview it, if needed. ​ Click on Add Files to select the desired files. If required, repeat the search to select files from multiple profiles; you can add files from more than one record to the same email. ​ Once all desired files are selected, click on Done . ​ The selected files will be added as attachments to your email. ​ Troubleshooting Problem: You cannot upload a file to a record. Likely cause: The file size exceeds the allowed limit. What to check: Confirm the file size on your device. Resolution: Reduce the file size to 8 MB or less, then upload it again. Problem: You cannot find a file when attaching from Saved Files in an email. Likely cause: The file is not among the fifteen recently used files or you have not searched by the correct record. What to check: Use the search bar to look up the specific record and click Search to load all files for that record. Resolution: Once the record’s files are visible, select the required file and click Add Files , then Done . Problem: A user cannot see or access the Files section. Likely cause: Their role may have restricted access to the Files section (on the business plan). What to check: Ask an administrator or account owner to review the user’s custom role and permissions. Resolution: Update the role to grant the necessary access to the Files section if appropriate. FAQs Can I attach files from multiple records to a single email? Yes. You can search files from multiple profiles and add them to your email before clicking Done . Conclusion Using the Files section, folders, and Saved Files options in Recruit CRM helps you keep all candidate, client, and job documents organized and easy to reuse across records and emails. t: How to Add Notes and Customize Note Types in Recruit CRM
s: This article will guide you on how to add/write notes to Candidates, Companies, Jobs and Contacts.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
How to Add a Note to a Record? 📝
Mention teammates in a note
Pin, edit, or delete notes:
Associate a note with multiple records
Automatic job association from the candidate pipeline:
How to Customize Note Types? ✨
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The notes feature in Recruit CRM lets you write, pin, edit, delete, and categorize notes on candidate, company, job, and contact records. Notes can be tagged with a note type, associated with multiple records, and used to notify teammates via @mentions. You can use this feature when: You want to record important updates or interactions on a candidate, job, company, or contact record. You need to categorize notes using custom note types for better tracking and reporting. You want to @mention teammates so they receive an email notification linked to a specific record. Before you begin Only users with access to the admin panel on the Business plan, or users with the Admin role on the Pro plan, can customize note types and set default note types. Notes added via the candidate pipeline will automatically associate with the corresponding jobs when using single or bulk note additions. How to Add a Note to a Record? 📝 Open the page for the relevant entity (Candidates, Companies, Jobs, or Contacts). ​ Open the details view of a specific record. On the right-hand side of the details view, click the first icon to add a note. ​ Type your note content into the note field, then click the Add Note button to save it to that profile. You can also click on the Select Note Type dropdown to choose a specific custom note type for your note. ​ Mention teammates in a note In the note field, type the @ symbol and select your teammate to mention them; this sends an email notification with a link to that record. Pin, edit, or delete notes: To pin an important note to the top of the notes section, click the three dots on that note and select Pin Note . To edit or delete a note, click the options (three dots) on the note and choose the relevant action. Associate a note with multiple records While adding a note, click Create Associations to link the note to more than one record at a time. Automatic job association from the candidate pipeline: When you add notes via the candidate pipeline, they will automatically be associated with the corresponding jobs. This applies to both single and bulk note additions and works across all candidate pipelines by hiring stage, job, company, recruiter assigned, or owner. How to Customize Note Types? ✨ Go to Admin Settings . ​ In the CRM Process Customization section, click Note Type Customization . ​ Click the Customize button. ​ Click Add New Status and enter a name for your note type. ​ Ensure your note type name is within the allowed limit of up to 50 characters. ​ To make this the default note type, check the box next to it. ​ You can also customize the default Note types by editing the corresponding Note type name to the one most relevant to you. Click Save Status to save your new note type. ​ Remember that the number of available call types, meeting types, and note types is 30 in total. How to Access Your Notes? 🎯 To access notes, open the details view of any record. ​ Go to the Notes and Calls tab on that record. ​ To broaden your view of the entire activity section, click the expand icon. From the expanded activity view, use the search options to find notes you have added, and apply filters to refine and manage your notes efficiently. Troubleshooting Problem: A note you expect to see is not appearing in the list. Likely cause: Filters or search criteria may be hiding it. What to check: In the Notes and Calls tab, review applied filters and search terms, and use the expand icon to view the full activity section. Resolution: Clear or adjust filters and search again; widen the view using the expand icon to ensure the note is not hidden. FAQs Q1: Do notes added via the candidate pipeline automatically link to jobs? Yes. Notes added via the candidate pipeline are automatically associated with the corresponding jobs, for both single and bulk note additions, across all candidate pipelines. Q2: Can I link a single note to multiple records? Yes. While adding a note or meeting, you can click Create Associations to associate the note with more than one record at a time. Q3: How do I find specific notes later? Go to the record’s details view, open the Notes and Calls tab, use the expand icon to see the full activity section, then use search and filters to locate specific notes. Conclusion Using notes and custom note types in Recruit CRM helps you capture detailed activity, collaborate with your team, and keep records organized and easy to search. b: What this feature does and when to use this feature? This feature allows you to personalise all Recruit CRM external pages with your company’s branding, ensuring that every page shared with candidates or clients reflects your brand identity. You can use this feature: To display your company name and logo on all external pages and forms shared with candidates. To ensure that public job pages and talent pool pages reflect your company's branding. To present online candidate lists to clients with your agency or company branding. Step-by-step instructions 1. Profile Update Request Form You can easily add your company logo, name, and page title to the Profile Update Request Form you share with your candidates. Navigate to Admin Settings > Account Management > Account . Click the pencil icon next to your account name. Enter your company name and click Save. Now, to add your Company Logo, go back to the Admin Settings > Job Settings > Public Job Page Settings. In the Appearance section, scroll down to upload your company Logo. Your company name and logo will now appear on the Profile Update Request form shared with candidates. 2. Public Jobs Page Now, let's quickly customise the Public Jobs Page by adding a logo, page banner (background image), title, and subtitle! Go to Admin Settings > Job Settings > Public Job Page Settings . In the Appearance section, enter a Title and Subtitle for your public job page. Scroll down to upload your company Logo and a Background Image (banner). Your public job page will now reflect your company branding. 3. Talent Pool Page Personalising your Talent Pool Page is especially important in order to create a brand image for your candidates. Go to Admin Settings > Job Settings > Talent Pool Page Setting . In the Appearance section, upload your company Logo and Page Banner. Enter a Title, Subtitle, and Description to customise your talent pool page. Click Save to apply your changes. Your talent pool page will now display your custom branding and messaging. 4. Online Candidate List Submitted to Clients Adding your company name and logo to the online candidate list submitted to clients is easy, and here's a detailed step-by-step guide on how you can do this! 5. Client and Contractor Portals Business and Enterprise accounts can now display their agency branding across both the Client Portal and Contractor Portal. The portals automatically use the logo and account name configured in Account Settings . Any changes made to your logo or account name in Account Settings will automatically be reflected across both portals. Agency branding is also supported on the mobile app. The existing “Powered by Recruit CRM” branding remains unchanged. For Free and Pro plans, the existing Recruit CRM branding will continue to be displayed. ​ This ensures that clients and contractors see your agency's branding when accessing the portals, while keeping your account information consistent across Recruit CRM. Additionally, you can remove Recruit CRM branding from all external pages so that only your company branding is displayed. Learn how to remove Recruit CRM branding from all external pages FAQs 1. What changes after I set my company name and logo in Admin Settings? Your company name and logo will appear on external pages such as the profile update request form, public job page, talent pool page, and online candidate list submitted to clients. 2. Can I remove Recruit CRM branding from all external pages? Yes, you can remove Recruit CRM branding from all external pages, depending on your plan and permissions. Conclusion: By configuring your company name, logo, titles, and banners in Admin Settings, you can ensure all Recruit CRM external pages present a consistent, professional brand experience to both candidates and clients. t: How to add your LinkedIn contract to your job advertising subscription
s: Learn how to integrate your LinkedIn contract with your job advertising subscription to share your job postings directly on LinkedIn
h: Adding the LinkedIn contract in Recruit CRM
Posting jobs through your LinkedIn contract
Understanding LinkedIn's Invited Candidates Feature
b: If you already have an existing LinkedIn job board contract , you can easily add them to Recruit CRM and post jobs through it. Recruit CRM has partnered with VONQ to streamline your job posting process. Click here for more details on how to connect with other job boards Please follow the steps below to connect your LinkedIn contract with your Jjob advertising subscription. ➕ Adding the LinkedIn contract in Recruit CRM 1. Navigate to the Admin Settings --> Job Advertising : 2. Under the 'Added Contracts' section, click on the 'Add Contracts/Job Board' button: 3. Type 'LinkedIn' in the contract provider's search bar and select the 'LinkedIn' option. If you have a free LinkedIn account or LinkedIn Recruiter Lite, you will need to choose the "LinkedIn Limited Listings" option. Then you just need to fill in your LinkedIn contract information. ​ Please add the 'Company ID' of your LinkedIn account to proceed with the connection. Here is an article that will guide you on how to find the correct company ID for your LinkedIn account. ​ ​ 4. You will then see instructions on how to authenticate your LinkedIn account for posting jobs. Click on the green "Initialize Authentication" button: 5. You will be redirected to a new tab where you'll be prompted to log into your LinkedIn account. Please log in with the credentials of the account where you wish to post your jobs. 6. Once logged in to LinkedIn, you need to select the contract that you intend to connect to Recruit CRM. Please note that if you have multiple accounts tied to your login, they will be presented here. 7. After selecting the correct account, you must edit the Job Poster information. The job poster is the name of the user under which the jobs will be posted. If you have an enterprise LinkedIn account, you can choose any user for which the jobs will be posted. Please note that the system may already display the name correctly. However, it is essential to complete this step to ensure the connection is set up correctly. Click the "Edit" button located to the right of the "Job Poster" section, under the displayed name. 8. After clicking the 'Edit' button, you will need to retype your name and then press 'Save'. This will initialize the connection between your LinkedIn posting account and the Recruit CRM job advertising system/Contract Posting Credits. You'll be redirected back to the Recruit CRM contract instructions, where you'll need to add the remaining information after authenticating your LinkedIn account. 9. Please add the 'Company ID' of your LinkedIn account to proceed with the connection. Here is an article that will guide you on how to find the correct company ID for your LinkedIn account. 10. Once you add the company ID, you need to select/create a contract group: Groups function as folders where you can organize your contracts. It's important to note that in each group you can't have more than one contract of the same type . Eg. Let's say you want to add two LinkedIn accounts. In that case, you'll need to create a separate group for each account. 11. In the 'Optional Details' section, you can include additional information and click on the green "Add To My Contracts" button to add the contract: It's worth noting that: The optional details are just for reference purposes and won't impact your ability to post jobs on job boards in any way. The details of the fields can vary based on the requirements of the different job boards. 12. You can now click on "Add to My Contracts" to conclude the connection :) 💼 Posting jobs through your LinkedIn contract First, make sure you have purchased the credits for posting jobs. Click here to learn how to buy credits! You'll have access to two free job posting credits per month to test the job posting through your added contracts. Here's how you can post jobs through your contracted job boards: 1. Go to Admin Settings >>>> Job Settings >>>> Job Advertising . ​ 2. Click on "Advertise Job" to start a new ad. ​ 3. A pop-up will appear prompting you to fill in the basic information for the job campaign. These fields are: Job Name Search for an existing job in your database Campaign Name Give your job advertising a name for future tracking Job Function Role and responsibilities of the job Location Where the opportunity is situated Industries The job's general industry All the fields except "Job Name" and "Campaign Name" do not impact the ability to post the job on the job boards. They are used just for filtering and recommending job boards. 4. Click on "Continue" and select your preferred contract to add to the campaign. In this case, you would need to select your "LinkedIn" contract. 5. Once you've selected your preferred contract (LinkedIn), click on "Continue to Review Details" to proceed: 6. Fill in and review the necessary details of your campaign and hit the "Confirm & Post Job" button: Jobs that have the status: "on hold", "closed" or "canceled" cannot be advertised. 7. You can keep track of all your existing ads by going to the "All Campaigns" tab and sort based on active campaigns or drafts. You also have the ability to sort them based on the 'Created On', 'Start Date', 'End Date', 'Total Cost', 'Visitors', and 'Applicants', and apply different filters. You can effortlessly advertise your jobs from the job details page as well by simply clicking on the 'Advertise Job' button and the rest of the process remains unchanged: Furthermore, you can also track the job campaigns on the same page under the 'Job Campaigns' tab: And that's it! You now have that contract connected to your Recruit CRM account and you can start sharing your jobs via LinkedIn! 😊 ​ Understanding LinkedIn's Invited Candidates Feature The Invited Candidates feature gives you a way to reach people who are a strong match for your open role, rather than waiting for applicants to find the posting on their own. It is available when a job is promoted through select Job Distributor or Applicant Tracking System partners. This feature is only available when the LinkedIn offering is purchased through the marketplace, and is supported only on the Medium and Large promotion offerings. Once the feature is enabled, LinkedIn begins identifying a curated group of potential applicants and automatically sends them an invitation to consider the role. Eligible candidates receive a notification on LinkedIn encouraging them to review and apply. The selection of candidates is driven by an AI matching system that looks at attributes such as skills, experience, location and behavioral hiring signals. This allows the system to surface people who closely reflect what the job requires. LinkedIn sends invitations in batches of up to 25 per day for a period of up to 14 days, which means as many as 350 individuals can be invited over the full cycle. Keeping the role active for the entire period ensures that all potential invitations can be delivered. This feature is not supported for contract or temporary job postings and will only work for full time or permanent roles. Access to this feature is tied to the job promotion process and is available when purchased alongside job distribution through approved partners. The amount paid for the promotion is added directly to the LinkedIn job promotion budget for that posting. Some partners also offer an optional daily email digest linked to the job poster’s LinkedIn account. When available, these emails provide a simple overview of the individuals who were invited to apply that day. This option may vary by partner and region. Overall, Invited Candidates is designed to expand the reach of a job posting by connecting it with people who are already strong fits. It supports both visibility and applicant quality by making sure well-matched individuals are aware of the opportunity, even if they were not actively searching for it. ​ Hope this helps! t: How to Archive/Unarchive Jobs?
s: This article will show you multiple ways of archiving and unarchiving jobs.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to Archive Jobs in Recruit CRM?
How to view archived jobs from the job list page
How to Unarchive Jobs in Recruit CRM
FAQs
1. Does archiving a job delete it from Recruit CRM?
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Job Archiving feature in Recruit CRM helps you manage jobs more efficiently by moving jobs from the active “All Jobs” list into an archived state while keeping the records accessible in a dedicated “Archived Jobs” view. You can also choose to delete any associated sponsored job campaign during the archiving process. The unarchive feature allows archived jobs to be restored to the active job list whenever needed. This functionality is especially useful when you want to: Clean up your active job list by archiving closed, filled, paused, or inactive roles. Temporarily archive jobs that are on hold and unarchive them later when hiring resumes. Review and restore archived jobs anytime from the dedicated “Archived Jobs” view onto the 'All Jobs' section. How to Archive Jobs in Recruit CRM? You can archive jobs in Recruit CRM either from the Jobs list page or directly from the Job Details page. From the Jobs List Page Go to the Jobs list page and select the job or jobs you want to archive. Click the Archive button. (New UI)- (Old UI)- A confirmation pop-up will appear. If any selected job has an associated sponsored job campaign or postings on LogicMelon and Broadbean will be closed by selecting the box 'Close job on External Job Board.' You can also choose to Disable the Job Application form by selecting the box 'Disable Job Application Form.' (New UI)- (Old UI)- Click the Archive job to complete the action. The selected jobs will then be archived and removed from the active “All Jobs” list. 2. From the Job Details Page Open the job and click the three ellipses (three-dot menu) on the Job Details page. From the drop-down menu, select Archive Job . (New UI)- (Old UI)- A confirmation pop-up will appear. You can also choose to 'Close Job on External Job Board' and 'Disable Job Application Form' by selecting the boxes. Click Archive Job to complete the action. (New UI)- Please note: 1. Once archived, these jobs will not appear on your jobs list. 2. Archived jobs will still be visible in the 'Assigned jobs' section under candidate profiles. How to view archived jobs from the job list page Go to your Jobs list page. In the top-left area of the page, locate the quick view section. Click on Archived jobs in the quick view section. (New UI)- You will see a comprehensive list of all your archived jobs. How to Unarchive Jobs in Recruit CRM You can unarchive jobs in Recruit CRM either from the Jobs list page or directly from the Job Details page. From the Jobs List Page Go to the Jobs list page. In the quick view section at the top-left, click Archived Jobs to view all archived jobs. Select the job or jobs you want to restore. Click the Unarchive option. The selected jobs will be unarchived and moved back to the active “All Jobs” list. (New UI)- (Old UI)- 2. From the Job Details Page Open the archived job from the Quickview section. Click the three ellipses (three-dot menu) on the page. From the dropdown menu, select Unarchive Job . The job will be restored and will once again appear in the “All Jobs” list and other active job views. (New UI)- (Old UI)- FAQs 1. Does archiving a job delete it from Recruit CRM? No, archiving a job does not delete it. The job is simply moved from the active jobs list to the Archived Jobs view, where it can still be accessed and unarchived later if needed. Conclusion: Archiving and unarchiving jobs in Recruit CRM helps keep your active job list organized while preserving important job history and associated data. s: This article will teach you how to shortlist candidates by assigning them to specific positions.
h: What this feature does & when to use it?

2. Assign a candidate from the candidate profile
