b: What this feature does & when to use it? Assigning candidates to jobs lets you assign people to specific open roles directly from the candidate list page, candidate profile page, job profile page, or while creating a new candidate. You can use this when: You want to assign one or more candidates to open jobs. You need to email primary job contacts at the same time as assigning candidates. You’re viewing a job profile and need to assign existing or new candidates. You’re parsing resumes or using the Chrome extension and want to assign candidates immediately. Before you begin: Please note: Ensure job records have primary contacts with valid email addresses if you plan to email them. Have your candidate resumes and attachments ready if you plan to share files. 1. Assign a candidate from the candidate list page: From the candidate list page, select the candidate(s) you want to assign by clicking the checkbox beside each candidate’s name. At the top of the list, you will see new action options appear, including the option to assign the selected candidates to a job. Use the assignment options to either create a new job or select one of the existing jobs in your database. During this process, you can also choose to immediately update the hiring stage of the candidate for the selected job. If the candidate is already assigned to that specific job, the system will alert you with a pop‑up so you do not create duplicate assignments. Emailing the contacts of the selected jobs While assigning candidates to jobs from the candidate list, you can choose to directly email the primary contacts of the selected jobs. This allows you to assign candidates and share their details with job contacts in a single workflow. In the job assignment window, click the Email Contacts button at the bottom. Then complete the assignment by clicking Assign or Assign and Update Stage , as required. If you have selected candidates who are already assigned to the job, the system will skip reassigning them, but they will still be included in the email that is sent to job contacts. A pop‑up will appear where you can select which candidate fields and files to share (for example, resume, summary, or other attachments). Once you have made your selections, click Generate Email . If any of the selected job contacts are missing an email address, a validation box will appear listing those records. You can review the highlighted records in the validation box and then click Continue to proceed with the valid contacts only. After continuing, you will be redirected to the Compose Email screen. Here, the email will be pre‑filled with: Recipients (only primary contacts linked to the selected jobs) A subject line The default Pitch candidate template The candidate details and files you selected Review the email content and simply click Send to share the candidates with the selected job contacts. Note Only the first 20 candidates (based on the last updated date) will be included in the email. Only primary contacts linked to the selected jobs will receive the email. 2. Assign a candidate from the candidate profile To assign a candidate from the candidate profile/details page, scroll down to the candidate’s job section and click the Assigned Jobs tab. There, you will be able to see all the jobs the candidate is currently assigned to and assign them to a new job by clicking on Assign to Jobs . Jobs that the candidate is already assigned to will be pre-selected and will not be selectable again, and you will have the option to view unassigned jobs for easier selection. 3. Assign candidates from within a job profile From inside a job profile, use the Assign Candidates option to add existing candidates to that job. If a candidate does not yet exist in your database, you can parse their resume and assign them to the job as part of the same flow. 4. Using the Chrome Extension The assignment can also be performed via the Chrome extension. After saving a new candidate, click on the 'Assign to Job' option on the Chrome Extension, and you will have the option to assign the candidate to the job: If a candidate exists in your database, click on the 'Assign to Job' option as shown below, and you will have the option to assign the candidate to the required job: Click here to learn more about Chrome Extension 5. Using the Resume Parser You can also assign the candidate to a job using our Resume Parser Feature. Click on the 'Assign to Job' option as shown below: Click here to learn more about the Resume Parser FAQs How many candidates can be included in the email to the job contacts? Only the first twenty candidates, sorted by last updated date, will be included in the email sent to job contacts, even if you assign more than twenty in the same action. Which contacts receive the email when I use Email Contacts? Only primary contacts linked to the selected jobs will receive the email. Other contacts on the job who are not marked as primary will not be included. Conclusion: Assigning candidates to jobs helps you keep pipelines accurate, share profiles with job contacts, and streamline your recruiting workflow from multiple entry points. t: How to bring your job board contracts to Recruit CRM
s: Bring in your existing contracts and post jobs through them.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
Adding contracts in Recruit CRM
Posting jobs through your contracted job boards
Troubleshooting
Problem: You cannot post jobs from your account
FAQs
Can I use job advertising on the free plan?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? If you already have contracts with external job boards, Recruit CRM allows you to add and manage them directly within the platform. Once connected, you can post jobs through those contracts and track advertising campaigns from a single location. Use this feature when: • You already have job board contracts and want to manage them inside Recruit CRM. • You want to post jobs directly to your contracted job boards from within Recruit CRM. • You need a centralized place to organize and manage multiple job board contracts. • You want to track and monitor job advertising campaigns from both the Job Advertising section and individual job records. Before you begin: Job advertising is available for all accounts with a paid Recruit CRM subscription. If you’re on the free plan (in the beta phase), you won’t be able to post jobs, but you can still search and connect your contracts. Once you upgrade to a paid plan, you’ll experience a 3-day verification period . ➕ Adding contracts in Recruit CRM 1. Navigate to the Admin Settings --> Job Advertising under the Job Settings section. 2. Under the 'All Job Boards' section you can view a list of all contracts available with Recruit CRM's Job board posting feature. You can search and connect any contract directly from this page. Or you can add the contract from the 'Added Job Boards' tab as well: 3. Type the name of the contract/job board you wish to add: 4. Once you choose your preferred contract, you need to select/create a contract group: Note: Groups function as folders that help you organize your job board contracts in Recruit CRM. This is an inbuilt feature provided by our job advertising partner, VONQ . ​ Each group can contain only one contract per job board type .This means you cannot add multiple contracts from the same job board into a single group. ​ For example, if you want to add two separate Indeed accounts, you’ll need to create two different groups , with one Indeed contract in each group. This ensures the correct contract is used when posting jobs. 5. In the 'Optional Details' section, you can include additional information and click on the green "Add To My Contracts" button to add the contract: It's worth noting that: The optional details are just for reference purposes and won't impact your ability to post jobs on job boards in any way. The detail fields can vary based on the requirements of the different job boards. Click here for more details on how to connect with specific job boards 💼 Posting jobs through your contracted job boards First, make sure you have purchased the credits for posting jobs. Click here to learn how you can buy credits! Pro Plan and Business Plan : Users can try the Job Advertising via Added Contracts feature using the free Recruit CRM Credits . Enterprise Plan : Users will receive the Job Advertising credits included with their Recruit CRM subscription. You can add your contract with a free job board and post through it, however, you need to buy a Job Posting Subscription if you are posting to any free job boards via added contracts. Some examples of free job boards are Joblift, Adzuna, Careerjet, telent.com , jobrapido . Please note: When you try to advertise a job via Added Contracts using Recruit CRM Credits, 25 credits are utilized when posting a job on one or more of the contracts (job boards added by the user) for a job campaign. Here's how you can post jobs through your contracted job boards: 1. Go to Admin Settings >>>> Job Settings >>>> Job Advertising . ​ 2. Click on "Advertise Job" to start a new ad. ​ 3. A pop-up will appear prompting you to fill in the basic information for the job campaign. These fields are: Job Name Search for an existing job in your database Campaign Name Give your job advertising a name for future tracking Job Function Role and responsibilities of the job Location Where the opportunity is situated Industries The job's general industry All the fields except "Job Name" and "Campaign Name" do not impact the ability to post the job on the job boards. They are used just for filtering and recommending job boards. 4. Click on "Continue" and select your preferred contract to add to the campaign. 5. Once you've selected your preferred contract, click on the "Continue to Review Details" button on the right to proceed: 6. Fill in and review the necessary details of your campaign and hit the "Confirm & Post Job" button: Jobs that have the status: "on hold", "closed" or "canceled" cannot be advertised. 7. You can keep track of all your existing ads by going to the "All Campaigns" tab and sort based on active campaigns or drafts. You also have the ability to sort them based on the 'Created On', 'Start Date', 'End Date', 'Total Cost', 'Visitors', and 'Applicants', and apply different filters. You can effortlessly advertise your jobs from the job details page as well by simply clicking on the 'Advertise Job' button and the rest of the process remains unchanged: Furthermore, you can also track the job campaigns on the same page under the 'Job Campaigns' tab: Note : If your LinkedIn job postings are not being visible on LinkedIn but are being shown as Online in Recruit CRM, this is because your company is being classified as a Recruitment and Staffing agency on LinkedIn, and LinkedIn is now enforcing its policy requiring such companies to sponsor their job postings. To continue posting, you must use a LinkedIn Recruiter account or post through the LinkedIn Marketplace. However, you will still be able to post on behalf of your clients, provided those clients are not classified as staffing agencies. Troubleshooting Problem: You cannot post jobs from your account Likely cause : You are on the free plan. What to check : Confirm your current Recruit CRM plan and whether you have completed the three-day verification period after upgrading. Resolution : Upgrade to a paid Recruit CRM subscription and wait for the three-day verification period to complete before posting. FAQs Can I use job advertising on the free plan? If you are on the free plan, you cannot post jobs, but you can still search and connect your contracts. Job advertising is fully available on paid plans after the three-day verification period. Conclusion: Using Recruit CRM job advertising, you can centralize your existing job board contracts, post jobs efficiently, and track campaign performance from one place. Change the Default Calling App on Android:

Conclusion:
b: Setting the default calling app helps users who want to call candidates/contacts from within Recruit CRM using the native caller option to automatically call in a preferred calling application. The default calling app allows you to choose which application handles calls by default, such as Skype, Zoom, Microsoft Teams. Once configured in your device settings, clicking on the Open Native Caller beside the phone number to automatically start the call. This is especially useful when you: • Want phone numbers in Recruit CRM to open in a specific calling app automatically. • Frequently use tools like Skype, Zoom, or Teams for calling. Before you begin: You must have your preferred calling app (e.g., Skype, Zoom, Teams, or another dialer) installed on your device. You need access to your device’s system settings (Windows or Android). Changes are device-specific, so you’ll need to repeat the setup on each computer or phone you use. Make sure your browser is allowed to open external applications when prompted. Step-by-step instructions Change the default calling app on Windows: 1. On your Windows computer, open the Start menu and type “Default apps” into the search bar. 2. From the search results, click Default apps by link type at the bottom. 3. In the Choose default apps by link type window, scroll down until you find the TEL link type. 4. Click on TEL , then select your preferred calling app from the list of installed apps. Compatible options include Skype, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and any other app installed on your computer that supports phone links. ​ Your selection takes effect immediately. The next time you click Open Native Caller in Recruit CRM it will open directly in the app you selected. Change the Default Calling App on Android: 1.Open the Settings app on your Android device. 2.Tap Apps and notifications (this may also appear as Apps depending on your device and Android version), then tap Default apps . 3. Under Default apps , locate and tap Phone app . 4. From the list of available apps, select the calling app you want to use by default for all phone calls on this device. FAQs Can I use different calling apps on different devices? Yes. Defaults are device-specific. You can use one app as default on your Windows computer and another on your Android phone. Will changing the default calling app affect existing data in Recruit CRM? No. Changing the default calling app does not change or delete any candidate, client, or activity data. Can I switch back to the previous calling app later? Yes. You can repeat the same steps on Windows or Android and select a different app (including the original dialer) at any time. Conclusion: Setting your default calling app on Windows and Android ensures that every time you click Open Native Caller beside the phone number it opens seamlessly in your preferred calling tool. b: Your card on file is charged at the commencement of your billing cycle, which can be monthly or yearly depending on your plan. Changing your card on file updates the debit or credit card Recruit CRM uses to charge your subscription at the start of each billing cycle. Once you save the new card in your billing settings, all future recurring subscription charges will be attempted using the updated payment method that is set as default. You may want to update your card if: Your current debit or credit card has expired or is about to expire. Your organization has changed its primary business card. You want future subscription charges to be billed to a different debit or credit card. How to change your card on file on Recruit CRM? 1. Go to Admin Settings & click on Plans & Billing . 2. Troubleshooting Problem: You cannot access the Plans and Billings section Likely cause: Your user role does not have access to Admin Settings . What to check: Confirm with an account administrator whether your account is allowed to view billing settings. Resolution: Ask an administrator or the account owner to either update the card for you or grant you access to Admin Settings . FAQs When will my new card be charged after I update it? After you update and save the new card, future charges at the start of each billing cycle will use that card. Can I change my card at any time? Yes. You can replace your card at any point by going to Admin Settings , opening Plans and Billing , and updating the payment method . Does changing my card affect my current plan or billing cycle? No. Updating the card only changes the payment method. Your selected plan and billing cycle (monthly or yearly) remain the same. Conclusion: You're all set! If you encounter any issues while updating your card, please contact our support team for assistance. t: How to choose which jobs are visible on your website? (New UI)
s: Control which jobs appear on your website and accept applications using a single setting.
h: What This Feature Does and When to Use It?
Before You Begin:
Step-by-Step Instructions
Troubleshooting
FAQs
Conclusion:
b: What This Feature Does and When to Use It? Recruit CRM lets you control exactly which jobs appear on your website and external jobs page. Each job has a single setting called Enable Job Application Form that acts as the on and off switch for public visibility. When this checkbox is checked, the job is visible on your website and candidates can submit applications through the job application form. This gives you precise control over your careers page without needing to delete or close a role internally. Use this feature when: You want to publish a job on your website and allow candidates to apply online. You need to hide a specific job from your website while keeping it active in your internal pipeline. You want to temporarily pause new applications for a role that already has enough candidates. You are cleaning up your careers page to show only current, relevant openings. You want to keep confidential or internal-only roles out of the public view. ​ ⚠️ Important: Jobs with a Closed status will never appear on your website, regardless of whether the Enable Job Application Form checkbox is checked. To make a job visible again, the job status must first be changed back to an active or open status. Before You Begin: Confirm that you have access to the Jobs section in your Recruit CRM account. Confirm that your user role includes permission to edit jobs. If you cannot see the Edit Job option on a job record, contact your Account Owner to request access. Changes to job visibility may take a short time to appear on your website, depending on your browser cache or website integration settings. ​ Step-by-Step Instructions Navigate to the Jobs section in Recruit CRM and open the specific job you want to show or hide on your website. ​ Click the pencil icon or the Edit Job button at the top of the job profile to open the Edit Job form. If you cannot see the Edit button directly, click the three dots icon and select Edit Job . Scroll down the Edit Job form until you find the Enable Job Application Form checkbox. ​ Set the checkbox according to what you want: Check the box to make the job visible on your website and external jobs page. Candidates will be able to see the job and submit an application through the form. Uncheck the box to hide the job from your website and external jobs page. Candidates will not be able to find or apply for the job through public channels. ​ 5. Click Save to apply the change. The update will take effect shortly, depending on your website cache or integration settings. To learn more about the Public Jobs Page, please check out the articles below: Setting up your Jobs Page How to Integrate Jobs Page to my Website ​ Troubleshooting Problem: The job is not appearing on my website. Likely cause: The Enable Job Application Form checkbox is unchecked, or the job status is Closed . ​ ​ What to check: Open the job, go to Edit Job , and verify the Enable Job Application Form checkbox and the job status. ​ ​ Resolution path: If you want the job visible, set the job status to an open/active status and check ​ Enable Job Application Form . Save the job and refresh your website or external job page. ​ FAQs Does disabling the application form delete existing candidates or applications? No. Unchecking Enable Job Application Form only hides the job from your website and external job pages and stops new applications. Existing candidate records and previous applications remain in Recruit CRM. Conclusion: Managing job visibility on your website in Recruit CRM is controlled primarily through the Enable Job Application Form checkbox and the job status. By following the steps above, you can decide exactly which jobs appear publicly and when candidates can apply, while keeping full internal control over all roles. t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to Cloudflare
s: Learn how to connect your custom Recruit Craft career page domain to Cloudflare using CNAME records.
h: What this article covers
Before you begin
Generate your DNS records in Recruit Craft
For a full domain
For a subdomain
Add the CNAME records in Cloudflare
Wait for DNS propagation
Troubleshooting
b: What this article covers This article explains how to connect a domain managed through Cloudflare to your Recruit Craft career page. You can connect either your full domain, such as yourcompany.com , or a subdomain, such as careers.yourcompany.com . You will first generate the required CNAME records in Recruit Craft, add them to Cloudflare, and then wait for the domain to be verified. Before you begin Make sure you have: Access to the Cloudflare account that manages your domain. Your domain set up with Cloudflare's Full DNS setup , meaning its nameservers point to Cloudflare. The domain or subdomain you want to use for your career page. ​ Generate your DNS records in Recruit Craft Before adding anything to Cloudflare, generate the DNS records required for your custom domain in Recruit Craft. For a full domain In Recruit Craft, go to Custom Domain from the panel on the left. Under Default Project URL , set a unique name for your project and click Save . For a full domain setup, this name must match the domain you want to connect. Under Custom Domain , enter your domain in both fields to confirm it, then click Connect . For a subdomain In Recruit Craft, go to Custom Domain from the panel on the left. Under Custom Domain , enter your preferred career page subdomain in both fields to confirm it, then click Connect . Make sure the subdomain matches the name of your Default Project URL . Recruit Craft will then generate two CNAME records . A CNAME (Canonical Name) record is a type of DNS record that directs a domain or subdomain to another address. Copy the Name and Value for both records. You will need to add each record separately in Cloudflare. Record 1: Used to verify your SSL certificate and secure your career page connection. Record 2: Used to point your domain or subdomain to your Recruit Craft career page. Please note: Keep both CNAME records handy before moving to Cloudflare. You will need to add both records. ​ Add the CNAME records in Cloudflare Once you have the two CNAME records from Recruit Craft, add them to your domain's DNS settings in Cloudflare. For a full domain Log in to Cloudflare and select your domain. Go to DNS > Records from the panel on your left. ​ Click Add record and select CNAME as the record Type . ​ In the Name field, enter the Name provided by Recruit Craft exactly as shown, including the domain. ​ In the Target field, enter the Value provided by Recruit Craft. ​ Set Proxy status to DNS only . Click Save . ​ Repeat steps 3 to 7 for the second CNAME record. For the second record, enter your root domain as the Name , for example, yourcompany.com . Please note: Cloudflare supports CNAME records on root domains using a feature called CNAME flattening . This feature is enabled automatically on all Cloudflare plans, including the Free plan. You do not need to enable it manually. ​ For a subdomain Log in to Cloudflare and select your domain. ​ Go to DNS > Records . ​ Click Add record and select CNAME as the record Type . ​ In the Name field, enter the Name provided by Recruit Craft exactly as shown, including the domain. ​ In the Target field, enter the Value provided by Recruit Craft. ​ Set Proxy status to DNS only . Click Save . ​ Repeat steps 3 to 7 for the second CNAME record. For this record, use your subdomain as the Name , for example, careers.yourcompany.com . Please note: Set both CNAME records to DNS only . Do not enable Cloudflare's proxy for these records. Important when entering the Name Cloudflare does not automatically add your domain to the Name field. Enter the Name exactly as it appears in Recruit Craft for both CNAME records. For example, if Recruit Craft provides a Name that includes your complete domain, copy the complete value into Cloudflare. Wait for DNS propagation After saving the CNAME records, the DNS changes need some time to become available. Since Cloudflare is the authoritative DNS provider when your domain uses its Full DNS setup, the changes typically take effect within five minutes or less . If your custom domain does not work immediately, wait a few minutes and check again. Once the DNS records have propagated, return to Recruit Craft to continue or verify your custom domain setup. Recruit Craft may take up to 5 hours to verify the records after they become available. Troubleshooting Problem: Recruit Craft is asking you to add CAA records before you can continue with custom domain setup. Why this is required: Recruit Craft uses AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue the SSL certificate for your custom domain. The CAA record authorizes Amazon to issue a certificate for your domain. If Recruit Craft displays CAA records during the custom domain setup, you must add those records to your DNS provider and verify them before you can proceed to the CNAME records. ​ ​ Resolution: If Recruit Craft provides a CAA record, add the record to Cloudflare exactly as shown in the Recruit Craft custom domain setup. For example, Recruit Craft will provide: Type: CAA Name: sharmaayush.site Value: 0 issue " amazon.com " To add the record in Cloudflare: 1. Log in to Cloudflare and select your domain. 2. Go to DNS > Records . 3. Select Add record and choose CAA as the record type. 4. In Name , enter the name provided by Recruit Craft. 5. Cloudflare separates the CAA value into multiple fields. If Recruit Craft provides: ​ 0 issue " amazon.com " enter the values as: ​ Flags: 0 ​ Tag: Issue ​ CA domain name: amazon.com 6. Leave TTL set to Auto . 7. Select Save . 8. Return to Recruit Craft and select Verify . ​ Please note: Do not enter 0 issue " amazon.com " as a single value in Cloudflare. Cloudflare requires the CAA value to be entered separately as Flags , Tag , and CA domain name . Once the CAA record has been successfully verified, Recruit Craft will allow you to continue with the CNAME record setup. If Recruit Craft provides a CAA record, use the values provided there rather than creating a different CAA record. If you already have CAA records for other certificate authorities, do not remove them unless you understand the impact of doing so. ​ FAQs Can I use a CNAME record for my root domain? Yes. Cloudflare supports CNAME records for root domains through CNAME flattening , which is enabled automatically on all Cloudflare plans. Should I use Proxy or DNS only for these records? Use DNS only for both CNAME records. Cloudflare proxying is not required for this setup. What if Cloudflare says the name is already in use? This usually means another DNS record already exists with the same name. Check your existing DNS records and edit or remove the conflicting record before adding the CNAME provided by Recruit Craft. How long does it take for my custom domain to work? DNS changes on Cloudflare typically take effect within a few minutes. After the records are live, Recruit Craft may take up to 5 hours to verify the connection. Conclusion Adding the two CNAME records provided by Recruit Craft to your Cloudflare DNS settings connects your custom domain or subdomain to your Recruit Craft career page. Once the DNS changes have propagated, return to Recruit Craft to complete or verify the connection. t: How to Connect Your Recruit Craft Career Page to GoDaddy
s: Learn how to connect a custom Recruit Craft career page domain to GoDaddy using CNAME DNS records.
h: What this article covers
Before you begin
Generate your DNS records in Recruit Craft
Add the CNAME record in GoDaddy
Wait for DNS propagation
Troubleshooting
Problem: Recruit Craft is asking you to add CAA records before you can continue with custom domain setup.
FAQs
b: What this article covers This article walks through connecting a subdomain hosted on GoDaddy (for example, careers.yourcompany.com) to your Recruit Craft career page, from generating the DNS records in Recruit Craft, to adding them in GoDaddy, to verifying the connection. Before you begin Make sure you have: Access to Custom Domain settings in Recruit Craft. Sign-in access to the GoDaddy account that manages your domain. The subdomain you want to use for your career page (for example, careers.yourcompany.com ). Generate your DNS records in Recruit Craft Before making any changes in GoDaddy, you first need to generate the DNS records required by Recruit Craft. These records tell your domain provider where your Recruit Craft career page is hosted. In Recruit Craft, go to Custom Domain from the panel on the left. ​ Under Custom Domain , enter your preferred career page subdomain in both fields to confirm it, then click Connect . Make sure the subdomain matches the name of your Default Project URL in Recruit Craft. ​ Recruit Craft will generate two CNAME records . A CNAME (Canonical Name) record is a type of DNS record that directs a domain or subdomain to another address. ​ Copy the Name and Value for both records. You will need to add both records to GoDaddy. Record 1: Used to verify your SSL certificate , which helps secure your career page connection. Record 2: Used to point your subdomain to your Recruit Craft career page. ​ 📌 Please note: Keep both CNAME records handy before moving to GoDaddy. You will need to add each record separately. ​ Add the CNAME record in GoDaddy Once you have the two CNAME records from Recruit Craft, add them to your domain's DNS settings in GoDaddy. Sign in to your GoDaddy Domain Portfolio . ​ Select the domain you want to configure to open its Domain Settings page, then select DNS to view the existing DNS records. Select Add New Record , then select CNAME as the record Type . In the Name field, enter the Name provided by Recruit Craft. For example, if Recruit Craft provides careers as the Name, enter: careers When entering the Name, GoDaddy applies the following restrictions: Periods (.) are allowed but not as the first or last character Consecutive periods (…) are not allowed Cannot begin or end with a hyphen (-) Cannot be the @ symbol Not already in use by another record 63 characters in a row not separated by a period (.) Example: 63characters.63characters.coolexample.com 255 characters maximum 5. In the Value field, enter the Value provided by Recruit Craft. ​ 6. Set the TTL (Time to Live) to 1/2 hour . TTL determines how long DNS information is cached before it is refreshed. ​ 7. Select Save to add the CNAME record. GoDaddy will display a confirmation box with the record details. Review the information and select the option to Change , then click Save to confirm the changes. 📌 Please note: If Domain Protection is enabled for your GoDaddy domain, GoDaddy may ask you to verify your identity using 2-step verification or a one-time passcode before the DNS record can be saved. ​ Wait for DNS propagation After saving the CNAME record, it may take some time for the DNS change to become available. ​ 📌 Please note: Most DNS changes take effect within an hour, but they can take up to 48 hours to fully propagate. If your custom domain does not work immediately, wait for the DNS change to propagate and check again. ​ Once the record has propagated, return to Recruit Craft and continue or verify your custom domain setup. Troubleshooting Problem: Recruit Craft is asking you to add CAA records before you can continue with custom domain setup. Why this is required: Recruit Craft uses AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue the SSL certificate for your custom domain. The CAA record authorizes Amazon to issue a certificate for your domain. If Recruit Craft displays CAA records during the custom domain setup, you must add those records to your DNS provider and verify them before you can proceed to the CNAME records. ​ ​ Resolution: If Recruit Craft provides a CAA record, add the record to GoDaddy exactly as shown in the Recruit Craft custom domain setup. ​ For example, Recruit Craft will provide: Type: CAA Name: sharmaayush.site Value: 0 issue " amazon.com " To add the record in GoDaddy: 1. Sign in to your GoDaddy Domain Portfolio . 2. Select the domain you want to configure, then go to Domain Settings > DNS . 3. Select Add New Record and choose CAA as the record type. 4. In Name , enter the name provided by Recruit Craft. Use the exact value shown in Recruit Craft. 5. If GoDaddy provides a CAA RDATA field, enter the complete value provided by Recruit Craft, for example: ​ 0 issue " amazon.com " GoDaddy may automatically separate this into the corresponding CAA fields. If the fields are shown separately, enter: ​ Flag: 0 ​ Tag: issue ​ Domain: amazon.com 6. Leave TTL at its default value. 7. Select Save . 8. Return to Recruit Craft and select Verify . Once the CAA record has been successfully verified, Recruit Craft will allow you to continue with the CNAME record setup. ​ Please note: If Recruit Craft provides a CAA record, use the values provided there rather than creating a different CAA record. If you already have CAA records for other certificate authorities, do not remove them unless you understand the impact of doing so. FAQs Can I use a CNAME record for my root domain? No. GoDaddy's CNAME record type does not support a root domain such as yourcompany.com ; the Name field cannot be set to @ . This setup is therefore for subdomains , such as careers.yourcompany.com . ​ 📌 Please note: The available guidance for GoDaddy covers subdomain setup. Full-domain setup using GoDaddy has not been confirmed here. ​ What if GoDaddy says the name is already in use? This usually means another DNS record already exists for the same name. Check your existing DNS records and edit or remove the conflicting record before adding the CNAME provided by Recruit Craft. ​ How long does it take for my custom domain to work? Most DNS changes take effect within an hour, but allow up to 48 hours for the change to fully propagate. Conclusion Adding the CNAME record provided by Recruit Craft to your GoDaddy DNS settings connects your custom subdomain to your Recruit Craft career page. Once the DNS change has propagated, return to Recruit Craft to complete or verify the connection. t: How to Create a Website Using Recruit Craft
s: This article explains how to create and customize a website from scratch using Recruit Craft.
h: What this feature does and when to use it
Step-by-step instructions
1. Create a new website project
2. Edit your website pages
3. Add elements to a page
4. Add sections to a page
5. Customize the default pages
6. Add additional pages
b: What this feature does and when to use it Recruit Craft allows you to create and customize a website from scratch without any coding. You can start a new project using either a blank canvas or a pre-built template , then personalize it by editing pages, updating text and styling, adding sections and elements, and creating additional pages beyond the default homepage, job listing, and job description pages. Use this feature when: You want to build a new website using Recruit Craft. You want to launch a website quickly by customizing an existing template. You need full control over your website's content, layout, styling, and navigation. You want to create additional pages to expand your website beyond the default pages Step-by-step instructions 1. Create a new website project Log in to Recruit Craft and navigate to the Projects page. Click + Project in the top right corner, select Build Full Website , then choose one of the following: Blank Project to build your website from scratch. Template to start with a pre-designed website that you can customize. ​ If you're using a template, click View to preview it, then select Edit Template to begin customizing it. 2. Edit your website pages Use the page navigation within the editor to switch between the Homepage , Job Listing , Job Description , About Us , or any other page you want to customize. ​ Every part of a page is editable. Simply click the element you want to modify, such as text, an image, a button, or another component. Once selected, the relevant configuration options will appear in the panel on the right. From the right-hand panel, you can customize the selected element based on its type. For example, when editing a text element, you can modify options such as: Font and font weight Text size and alignment Colors and styling Letter and line spacing Width and height Links and button redirects Other elements, such as images, buttons, sections, or forms, display their own configuration options, allowing you to customize their appearance and behavior. Review the page after making your changes to ensure the content, layout, and styling appear as expected. 3. Add elements to a page To add new content to a page, open Elements from the left-hand panel and select the component you want to insert. Recruit Recruit Craft offers a variety of elements, including: Text (H1 to H6 headings and paragraph text) Buttons Images Forms Videos Lines and dividers Social icons Custom HTML for embedding custom code or iframes After adding an element, click it to customize its appearance and behavior using the right-hand panel. Depending on the element type, you can configure options such as: Size, style, and alignment Colors and backgrounds Width, height, padding, and spacing Button styles Links and redirect URLs Image styling Layout settings Other advanced properties specific to the selected element Form layouts and field configuration Video playback settings Other advanced properties specific to the selected element ​ Note: The available customization options vary depending on the selected element. For example, forms allow you to configure fields, layouts, and submission behavior, while videos provide playback and display settings. 4. Add sections to a page To quickly build your page layout, open Sections from the left-hand panel and drag the section you want onto your page. Recruit Craft includes several pre-built sections, including layouts with ready-to-use form components, such as: Flexbox Grid Spacer Header Footer Hero Testimonials FAQs About Us Banner Block Quote Custom HTML Form These ready-to-use sections include predefined layouts, making it easy to build pages without creating every section from scratch. Once a section has been added, you can: Reorder it anywhere on the page Edit the section's layout and design Modify individual elements within the section Change text, colors, spacing, backgrounds, images, and links Add your own elements to Grid or Flexbox sections If you prefer to create a completely custom layout, start with a Grid or Flexbox section and build it by adding elements manually. ​ 5. Customize the default pages Repeat the same editing process for the Job Listing and Job Description pages by updating their content, layout, elements, and sections. Review each page to ensure the design and navigation remain consistent across your website, and save your changes regularly. 6. Add additional pages To create pages beyond the default ones, open Pages from the left-hand panel and click Add New Page . Enter a name for the page, then customize its content, layout, and design using the same editing tools available throughout the website editor. ​ FAQs Can I add a contact form to my website? Yes. You can add a Form element from the Elements panel or use a pre-built section that includes a form. Forms support multiple layouts and allow you to collect visitor information directly from your website. What fields can I add to a form? Forms support Text , Email , and Phone fields. Every form must include at least one field and a Submit button. First Name and Email are required for a successful submission. Can form submissions create records in Recruit CRM? Yes. You can choose to automatically create a Contact record in Recruit CRM for each form submission. The submitted First Name , Email , and Phone are mapped to the corresponding Contact fields, and the submitted message is saved as a note. If a Contact with the same email address already exists, the submission is added to the existing Contact instead of creating a duplicate. Will I receive notifications when someone submits a form? Yes. Recruit Craft sends an email notification to the email address associated with your Recruit Craft account whenever a website visitor submits a form. Can I add videos to my website? Yes. The Video element lets you upload videos directly from your device or embed videos using YouTube , Vimeo , or Loom links. Uploaded videos are stored for reuse, similar to uploaded images. Which video formats are supported? You can: Upload MP4 and WebM videos. Embed videos from YouTube , Vimeo , and Loom . Unsupported links display an error prompting you to upload a video or use a supported provider. Can I customize how videos play? Yes. You can configure: Autoplay Loop Mute Show or hide controls Poster (thumbnail) image Size, spacing, positioning, and styling When Autoplay is enabled, Mute is automatically enabled because most browsers require autoplay videos to be muted. Why are some playback settings unavailable for Loom videos? Due to limitations of the Loom player, the Loop and Show Controls settings are not available for embedded Loom videos. Related Articles Recruit Craft vs iFrame Building a Custom Careers Page with the Recruit Craft Website Editor Recruit Craft Website Builder SEO Settings in Recruit Craft Content Management System (CMS) in Recruit Craft

t: How to create and access templates for notes, call logs, and tasks
s: This article explains how to create, customize, and access activity templates for notes, call logs, and tasks in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Create a new activity template
Accessing the templates while adding notes, call logs, and tasks
Role access to set up activity templates
Granting access to activity templates on custom roles
Troubleshooting
Problem: Cannot create more activity templates.
Problem: Cannot see an expected template when adding a note, call log, or task.
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Activity templates let you predefine the content and structure for notes, call logs, and tasks in Recruit CRM. Each template is linked to a specific activity type and a target entity, such as a candidate, contact, company, job, or deal. When you add a new note, call log, or task, you can quickly insert a template instead of typing everything from scratch. This helps keep your activity logging faster, more consistent, and easier for the whole team to follow. You can use this feature when: When you frequently add similar notes, call logs, or tasks and want to save time. When your team needs standardized activity formats for consistent data capture. You can create up to 30 templates on the free trial and 100 templates in total on the Pro and Business plans. Create a new activity template 1. Go to Admin Settings , then select Activity Templates . 2.In the Activity Templates area, locate and click the Create New Template button. 3. Add all required details for the template, choosing the desired activity type (such as note, call log, or task). 4. Select the targeted entity , such as candidates, contacts, companies, jobs, or deals, and complete the remaining template fields as needed. ​ 5. Once all details are filled in, click the Save button to create the template.​ You can use the search bar to look for specific templates and also filter them based on team member, activity, or entity. 6. To delete an activity template, click the trash icon on the right side of the template you created. ​ 7. To edit an activity template, click the pencil icon on the right side of the template to make any necessary changes and click on Save to save these changes. Accessing the templates while adding notes, call logs, and tasks 1. Once you have created an activity template, you can access it while adding a note, call log, or task by clicking Insert Template . 2. For call logs , you can add a call template from the calling widget while you are on a live call . 3. Alternatively, you can insert a call template from the widget after the call ends, before saving the call log. Please note: Inserting a template replaces the existing content, similar to how it works when adding a manual call log. 4. You'll also have the option to add a new template while adding the note/call log/task. You can not use the activity templates on the mobile app and the Chrome extension. Role access to set up activity templates 1. By default, only the Account Owners and admins have access to set up activity templates from the admin settings. ​ 2. On the Business plan and above, however, you can grant access to set up activity templates to users on custom roles as well. Granting access to activity templates on custom roles 1. Go to Admin Settings >> Users >> Roles & Permissions . 2. Click on "New Role" or the pencil icon to edit an existing custom role. 3. Scroll down and turn the toggle ON for "Activity Templates" under Data Customization. Troubleshooting Problem: Cannot create more activity templates. Likely cause: You have reached the plan limit for templates. What to check: Confirm whether you are on the free trial or a Pro, Business, or Enterprise plan and how many templates already exist. Resolution: On the free trial, reduce the number of templates if you are at the 30-template limit. On Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans, check if you have reached the 100-template limit and delete unused templates if necessary. Problem: Cannot see an expected template when adding a note, call log, or task. Likely cause: The template may be set for a different activity type or entity. What to check: In Admin Settings > Activity Templates , verify the activity type and targeted entity for the template. Resolution: Edit the template and adjust the activity type or entity if needed, then try inserting it again from the relevant activity screen. FAQs Which activity types and entities can use templates? You can create templates for notes , call logs , and tasks , and link them to entities such as candidates , contacts , companies , jobs , or deals . Can I edit existing templates after creating them? Yes. In the Activity Templates section, you can click the pencil icon next to a template to edit its details and save your changes. Conclusion: Using activity templates for notes, call logs, and tasks in Recruit CRM helps you log activities faster and more consistently across your team. t: How to Create and Manage Timesheets? (Beta)
s: This article will help you create and manage timesheets.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Enable and access timesheets for a candidate
How Timesheet Periods Work in Recruit CRM
Example 1: Job Starts on the Week Start Day
Example 2: Job Starts Mid-Week
How to Add and Manage Timesheets
How to Add a Timesheet?
How to Submit a Timesheet?
b: Note: Currently, this feature is in beta and can be enabled upon request. Please feel free to reach out to your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. What this feature does and when to use it? The Timesheets feature in Recruit CRM helps you track and manage work hours for candidates working in contract or temporary roles. It enables you to record hours worked, submit timesheets for approval, and automatically calculate payable and billable amounts based on the pay rates, bill rates, and rule templates configured for the job. This provides a structured workflow for agencies, clients, approvers, and candidates while keeping all timesheet-related activities in one place. Once timesheets are enabled for a job, you can create and manage timesheets, monitor their progress through the approval workflow, and calculate payments based on approved hours. Use this feature when: • You need to track candidate work hours for contract or temporary placements. • You want to automatically calculate payable and billable amounts using predefined rates and rule templates. • You require a structured approval workflow for timesheets (Open → Submitted → Approved/Rejected). • You want candidates, approvers, and agency users to collaborate on timesheets through their respective portals. • You need flexible time logging with support for unpaid breaks , multiple work segments, shifts, and configurable timesheet periods. Timesheets are automatically created based on the job duration, the configured timesheet frequency (such as weekly), and the selected week start day. Throughout the process, Recruit CRM keeps candidates, approvers, and agency users informed with email and in-app notifications, ensuring everyone stays updated on the status of each timesheet. Enable and access timesheets for a candidate After enabling timesheets, you can add new timesheets, track them, and manage approvals for the specific job they’re working on. How to enable timesheets? Once you enable Timesheets for a candidate, you’ll see a green button under the Candidate Pipeline of the Job where the candidate is assigned. When you click this button, you’ll be able to view the timesheet details for that candidate in one place. This makes it easy to track and manage the timesheet-related details for each candidate. How Timesheet Periods Work in Recruit CRM When you enable timesheets for a candidate, the system automatically splits the job duration into timesheet periods based on the Timesheet Frequency and the Start of the Week you’ve configured (e.g., Weekly starting on Monday). Example 1: Job Starts on the Week Start Day Job Duration: Jan 6, 2025 – Jan 19, 2025 Timesheet Frequency: Weekly Start of the Week: Monday In this case, the timesheet periods will be: Jan 6 – Jan 12 (Week 1) Jan 13 – Jan 19 (Week 2) Example 2: Job Starts Mid-Week Job Duration: Jan 8, 2025 – Jan 19, 2025 Timesheet Frequency: Weekly Start of the Week: Monday In this case, the system will create: Jan 8 – Jan 12 (Partial week, starting from job start date) Jan 13 – Jan 19 (Full week, aligned with week start) Note: Only 12 timesheet periods will be visible at a time. New periods will appear automatically as you continue adding timesheets. How to Add and Manage Timesheets Each timesheet goes through the following statuses: Open : The timesheet is created but no hours have been added yet. Submitted : The candidate has filled in their working hours and submitted the timesheet for approval. Approved :The approver has verified and approved the timesheet. Rejected : The timesheet was not approved and needs correction. How to Add a Timesheet? Click "Add Timesheet", then select the date ranges you want to add. Then click "Add". This will create timesheet rows for the selected dates, and their status will be set to Open. How to Submit a Timesheet? Timesheets are created based on the hour logging method defined in the Rule Template selected when enabling timesheets for the candidate. Click here to know more about how to enable timesheets You can enter working hours for each day. You can also add multiple start and end time entries within a single day, allowing hours to be logged across separate time segments. This is supported in both single and bulk time entry workflows, and the system automatically calculates the total hours for all entries combined. For Work Hours methods: You can enter break time directly by typing the break duration in hours or minutes (for example, 1 hour or 30 mins ). ​ You can also add multiple breaks within each time entry. Any break added is automatically deducted from the logged working hours , and the existing calculation and validation logic is applied automatically. ​ For the Shifts method: Breaks must be added as separate time slots within your shift. ​ For example, if your working hours are from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM and you took a break from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM , add a break slot: Break: 1:00 PM – 2:00 PM ​ The system automatically treats this as a break and deducts the break duration from the total working hours . You can add multiple break slots if needed. ​ 📌 Note: Any break added to a timesheet is always deducted from the logged working hours and is not included in pay or bill calculations. Note: You can copy the work hours and break hours for all days. After submission, the system automatically calculates billable and payable amounts based on the rule template and the set bill/pay rate. ​ When the Round time entries option is enabled, the time entry is automatically updated according to the selected rounding interval and rounding method as soon as the time is entered. For Per Day timesheets: If the contractor's Rate Type is set to Per Day, you'll log attendance instead of hours. For each working day defined in the Work Schedule, select one of: Full Day — applies 1x the daily Pay and Bill Rate Half Day — applies 0.5x the daily Pay and Bill Rate No Show — applies 0x the daily Pay and Bill Rate The total number of days for the timesheet is calculated from these entries. For example, 4 Full Days and 1 Half Day totals 4.5 days. You can also add Remarks for each row if there’s anything specific you want to note. Remarks can be marked as mandatory while enabling timesheets for a contractor. If enabled, remarks will be required for every time entry across the agency, contractor, and client portals, and this setting will apply to both existing and newly created timesheets. Once you’ve entered all the details, click Submit . The timesheet status will change to Submitted , and it will be sent to the assigned Approver for review. If you are the timesheet Approver, you can submit and approve simultaneously. Please Note A timesheet with zero logged hours can be submitted . Entries with no logged time will display “ No hours logged .” Zero-hour timesheets will also show an indicator next to their status. Hover over the indicator to see the tooltip “ No hours logged in this timesheet. ” ​ Zero-hour timesheets will not appear on the Approvers’ Review Timesheets page and will not trigger automatic submission notifications to approvers. They will continue to be available in All Timesheets, Contractor Portal, Agency Portal, Client Portal, Contractor Details, and Deals, and in Reports when approved. Agency and client users can still manually approve zero-hour timesheets when required. If a Custom Reminder is manually sent, approvers will receive the reminder and can review the timesheet. ​ If a timesheet that previously had logged hours is resubmitted with zero hours, it will be removed from the approvers’ review queue. Click here to know more about how to bulk add time to the timesheets How to Approve or Reject a Timesheet? If you are the Approver , click on the timesheet period to open it and review the hours. If the details are correct, click Approve . If corrections are needed, you can either Edit the hours and then approve. You can also Reject it with a remark, if it needs further correction. Once a timesheet is Approved , it cannot be edited. Timesheets in Open , Submitted , or Rejected status can still be edited and submitted. For approved/rejected timesheets, the system automatically calculates billable and payable amounts based on the rule template and the set bill/pay rate. You can click the Remarks button next to the timesheet status to view the history of changes. How to delete a Timesheet? To delete a single timesheet, you can click on the trash icon to the right of it: To delete them in bulk , select multiple timesheets and click the Delete button above. Once a timesheet is marked as Approved, it cannot be deleted. Which roles and permissions are required to access timesheets? Timesheet permissions are determined by the permissions of both the candidate and the job. Account Owners, Admins and users on the custom roles with the following permissions have access to timesheets: Candidate: • Can create Candidate : - No → Cannot create timesheets - Yes → Can create timesheets. • Can Delete

t: How to Create, Edit, and Manage Custom Fields in Recruit CRM
s: This article will help add custom fields to store your internal information for candidates, contacts, companies & jobs.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin:
Step-by-step instructions
Supported Custom Field Types in Recruit CRM
Choosing the Right Custom Field Type
How to Rearrange Custom Fields and Sections
How to Replace Existing Fields with Custom Fields
Troubleshooting
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Custom fields in Recruit CRM allow you to capture and organize additional information for records such as Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs & Deals. Using custom fields, you can tailor Recruit CRM to match your recruitment workflows and standardize data collection across the organization. Before you begin: On the Pro plan, you can create up to 15 custom fields per entity (candidates, companies, contacts, jobs, deals). On the Business plan, up to 100 custom fields per entity can be created. You need access to Admin Settings to create and manage custom fields. Deleting a custom field permanently deletes all data stored in that field. Custom fields are configured per entity. Step-by-step instructions 1. Navigate to Admin Settings in your Recruit CRM account. 2. Under Data Customization , select the entity (Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs, or Deals) for which you want to add custom fields. 3. On the right side of the screen, click the + New Custom Field button. ​ 4. Create the new field by selecting the appropriate field type, entering the correct value or label, and then clicking Save Field . 5. After saving, you can find the newly created field under Additional Information (Custom Fields) in the list on the left. Note: Once a custom field of a specific type is created, its type cannot be changed later. If you need a different type, create a new custom field and delete the old one. Deleting a custom field will permanently remove all data stored in that field. Supported Custom Field Types in Recruit CRM Field Type Purpose Best Used For Example Text (You can add up to 2000 characters in this field) This field type is used to input the data of the "text" type. Short custom information. Current project being worked on Long Text (You can add up to 5000 characters in this field.) This field type is used to add a paragraph. Adding detailed notes. Client-facing summaries or internal private notes about a candidate Dropdown This field type selects an option from a pre-defined set of values. Standardized options Candidate Status Phone Number This field type is used to capture the phone number. You can click on the number to take further action. Store phone numbers Secondary Contact Number Multi-select This field type selects multiple options from a pre-defined set of values. Multiple selections Skills Email This field type is used to capture an email address. You can just click on the value inside this field and it will open a pop-up to compose an email. Capture an email address Work & Personal Email Date Field This field type is used to input the date. Manage date and time details Offer-letter sign date & time File This field type is used to attach and upload files. Upload files (PDF/DOC/JPEG etc.) Certificates, etc,. Number Field This field type is only used to input the data of the "number" type. It will not allow any character or special characters in this field. Numeric values Number of awards or achievements Social Profile (You can read more about this in this article .) This field type allows you to enter the URL for a social media app, creating an icon on the record for easy access. Clicking on the icon redirects you to the records' social media profile URL. URL for a social media app Twitter Checkbox This field type is used to capture the data of type "Yes" or "No". Yes/No values Remote Ready Date-Time This field type is used to track and manage date and time details effectively and it supports MM-DD-YYYY, HH:MM format with a calendar and time picker (12-hour format). For eg, Jan 20, 2025, 12:30 PM Manage date and time details Offer-letter sign date & time Choosing the Right Custom Field Type Use dropdowns when values should remain standardized. Use multi-select fields when users may select multiple options. Use text fields only when flexible input is required. Use date fields for tracking milestones/date related data. Use number fields to store numeric values. How to Rearrange Custom Fields and Sections 1. To customize the arrangement of fields and sections that appear when you manually add or edit candidates, contacts, companies, deals, or jobs, go to the respective field settings in Admin Settings . 2. Use drag-and-drop to reorder fields or entire sections to match your preferred layout. Now your fields will appear in the updated order when you add or edit profiles. ​ How to Replace Existing Fields with Custom Fields 1. On the profile layout, choose any field that you no longer want in that section. Hover over the existing field, click the pencil (edit) icon , and select Replace Field . Then select the custom field you created to replace the old one. 2. Once placed, the custom field will appear on all records for that entity, allowing users to enter and edit data directly in that field. Troubleshooting Problem: I created a custom field, but I cannot see it on the profile page. Likely cause: The custom field is created but not added to the entity’s profile layout. ​ What to check: Confirm the field appears under Additional Information → Custom Fields for the correct entity and ensure the visibility toggle is enabled. Check the profile layout to see if the field has been added by replacing an existing field. Resolution path: Go to the entity’s profile page. Hover over a field you do not need, click the pencil icon, and use Replace Field to select your custom field. Problem: I need to change a custom field type (for example, from text to dropdown). Confirm whether you are on the Pro plan (15 custom fields per entity) or Business plan (100 custom fields per entity). Resolution path: Remove unused custom fields to free up capacity, or Consider upgrading to a plan with a higher limit if needed. Common Mistakes to Avoid Creating duplicate fields. Naming fields inconsistently. Using free-text instead of dropdowns. Deleting fields without reviewing existing data. FAQs Does deleting a custom field affect existing data? Yes. Deleting a custom field permanently removes the field and all data stored in that field across all records. This action cannot be undone. Can I use different custom fields for different entities? Yes. Custom fields are configured separately for candidates, companies, contacts, jobs, and deals. You can have different fields and layouts for each entity. Conclusion: Custom fields help teams tailor Recruit CRM to their specific workflows while improving data consistency. By organizing fields strategically and following best practices, teams can maintain cleaner records. t: How to Create, Edit, and Manage Email Templates in Recruit CRM
s: Send customized email templates to your candidates or contacts
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
Email Template Types
How to Create a New Email Template 📝
How to Filter Templates in Your Mailbox 👀
Use placeholders for personalization
How to Edit an Existing Email Template ✏️
How to Delete an Email Template 🗑️
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Email templates in Recruit CRM let you save reusable email messages that you can send to candidates or contacts. You can use this when: You frequently send the same emails to candidates or contacts and want to avoid retyping them. You want automated emails to go out when specific events occur in your hiring workflow. You need consistent messaging across your team for outreach, updates, or application responses. You want to personalize bulk or repeated emails with candidate or contact details using placeholders. Before you begin Email templates are available on all Recruit CRM plans: Free, Pro, Business, and Enterprise. On the Business plan, you can set up to two email signatures if you have connected two email accounts to Recruit CRM. Having your signature ready before using templates is recommended. Email Template Types There are 3 types of Email Templates in Recruit CRM: Automated workflow Templates These are triggered automatically when a specific event occurs, such as when a candidate’s hiring stage changes or when a candidate applies through your website. Candidate Templates These are templates you create specifically for candidates. They appear in the template dropdown when sending emails to candidates and only include candidate-related placeholders. Contact Templates These are templates you create specifically for contacts. They appear in the template dropdown when sending emails to contacts and only include contact-related placeholders. The Job ID placeholder is available in Automated Candidate Workflow email templates and when sending emails to candidates within a specific job’s candidate pipeline . The placeholder automatically populates with the corresponding Job ID. Recruit CRM also lets you add custom placeholders inside templates to personalize messages while still using a standard structure. How to Create a New Email Template 📝 Go to the Mailbox in Recruit CRM. ​ Open the Email Templates section. ​ Click the green Create Email Template button. ​ Choose the Template Type as required. Enter the Template Name so you can easily identify it later. ​ Enter the Email Subject for the template. ​ (Optional) Turn on the Share with Everyone toggle if you want all users in your account to see and use this template. ​ In the email body editor, write your message content. ​ Insert placeholders where you want Recruit CRM to automatically insert values like candidate first name, candidate last name, contact name, company name, or job name. ​ (Optional) Copy any placeholder and paste it into the Email Subject line if you want the subject to be personalized as well. ​ Save the template. IMPORTANT NOTE If users in your account have a custom role OR a default role with Email Template permissions set to "View Everything" they will be able to see all existing templates , regardless of whether the creator chose to share it with everyone or not. ​ Even if a user doesn't enable the "Share with everyone" option, those with the "View Everything" permission in their role will still have access. If you don't wish to see other teammate's email templates, you can filter the templates in your mailbox based on your own templates or those created by other users, depending on your email template permissions. How to Filter Templates in Your Mailbox 👀 Go to the Email Templates section in your mailbox. ​ Use the filter option to control which templates you see. ​ Choose to view: Only your own templates, or Templates created by other users (depending on your email template permissions). Use placeholders for personalization While editing or creating a template, locate the placeholder options provided by Recruit CRM. ​ Place the cursor in the body where you want the dynamic value to appear and insert the placeholder. How to Edit an Existing Email Template ✏️ Go to the Mailbox and open the Email Templates section. ​ Find the template you want to modify. ​ Click the pencil icon next to that template to open it for editing. ​ Make your changes to the template name, subject, body, or placeholders. ​ Click the green Save button to save your changes. How to Delete an Email Template 🗑️ Go to the Email Templates section in your mailbox. ​ Locate the template you want to delete. ​ Click the dustbin/trash can icon located next to the pencil icon on the same line as the template. ​ Note: Before using your email templates, make sure your email signature is ready! ​ On the Business Plan, you can set up two email signatures if you have connected two email accounts with Recruit CRM. ​ You can read more about how to set up email signature in Recruit CRM from here: Setting Up and Customizing Your Email Signature Troubleshooting Problem: Placeholders are not populating correctly in sent emails. Likely cause: The wrong type of template (candidate vs. contact) was used, or placeholders do not match the record type. What to check: Confirm that candidate templates are used for candidate emails and contact templates are used for contact emails. Verify that the placeholders inserted are valid for that template type. Resolution: Edit the template to use the correct placeholders or create a new template of the correct type and resend. FAQs Q1. What is the difference between candidate templates and contact templates? Candidate templates are used when emailing candidates and support candidate-specific placeholders. Contact templates are used when emailing contacts and support contact-specific placeholders. Conclusion: Using email templates in Recruit CRM helps you send consistent, personalized messages to candidates and contacts while saving time and reducing manual effort. t: How to Enable Timesheets for Contract Staffing Jobs in Recruit CRM (Beta)
s: This article will walk you through the steps to enable timesheets for contract and contract-to-permanent jobs, both individually and in bulk
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to enable timesheets for an individual candidate
How to enable timesheets for multiple candidates
How to verify that timesheets are enabled
Troubleshooting
Problem: The Enable Timesheet option isn't available.
FAQs
What is the difference between Margin and Markup?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM's Timesheets feature helps you track, manage, and approve contractors' working hours. Once enabled, contractors can submit timesheets for approval, making payroll and client billing more accurate and efficient. This feature is useful when you want to: Track working hours for contract staff. Configure pay rates, bill rates, and approval workflows. Automate pay and bill calculations using rule templates. Process payroll and client billing more accurately. Please note: This feature is currently in Beta and can be enabled upon request. Please get in touch with your Account Manager to enable it for your account. Timesheets can only be enabled for Contract and Contract-to-Permanent jobs. Candidates in the Applied stage cannot have timesheets enabled. How to enable timesheets for an individual candidate 1. Go to Jobs and open a job with the Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job type. 2. Scroll to the Candidate Pipeline and click Enable Timesheet on the candidate's card. 3. In the Enable Timesheet window, enter the required details to configure timesheet tracking for the candidate. Field Description Job Start Date The start date of the job contract. Job End Date The end date of the job contract. Rate Type Choose whether the contractor is paid and billed Per Hour or Per Day . Per Hour is selected by default. Timesheet Frequency Choose how often timesheets should be submitted: Weekly – The contractor submits a timesheet once every week. Bi-Weekly – The contractor submits a timesheet once every two weeks. Monthly – The contractor submits a timesheet once every month. Start Of The Week/ Start of The Month You can choose any day from Monday to Sunday if the timesheet frequency is set to weekly or bi-weekly, / select any date of the month if the frequency is set to monthly. Timesheet Approver Person responsible for reviewing and approving submitted timesheets. Pay Rate The rate paid to the candidate, per hour or per day depending on the selected Rate Type Bill Rate The rate you’ll bill your client per hour of the candidate’s work. When Margin or Markup is selected, the Bill Rate is calculated automatically based on the selected value. Calculate Charge By Choose how the Bill Rate should be calculated: Fixed Rate, Margin, or Markup . Margin The desired profit margin used to automatically calculate the Bill Rate. Markup The desired markup on the Pay Rate used to automatically calculate the Bill Rate. Work Schedule Select the contractor's working days. Any day not selected is treated as a day off. Used when creating and managing day-based timesheets. Only applicable when Rate Type is set to Per Day. Per Day timesheets don't use a Pay and Bill Rule Template. Only the Work Schedule shown above applies. If Rate Type is set to Per Hour, continue configuring a Rule Template as described below. ​ How Bill Rate is calculated Fixed Rate: Enter the Pay Rate and Bill Rate directly. Margin: Enter the desired profit margin, and Recruit CRM automatically calculates the Bill Rate. The value can be between 0% and 99% and cannot be a negative value. Markup: Enter the desired markup on the Pay Rate, and Recruit CRM automatically calculates the Bill Rate. The value can be between 0% and 10,000% and cannot be a negative value. For example: Pay Rate Calculation Bill Rate $10 50% Markup $15 $10 50% Margin $20 Please note: The Margin and Markup fields are used based on the option selected under Calculate Charge By . When Fixed Rate is selected, the Pay Rate and Bill Rate can be entered directly. ​ Configure Additional Settings (Optional) Make Remark Mandatory on Timesheet – Enable this option to require a remark for every time entry logged in a timesheet. Enable Expense Claim – Enable this option to allow contractors to submit expense claims through the Contractor Portal for reimbursement. Learn How to Manage Contractor Reimbursements Please note: If pay and bill rates are already configured for the job, they'll be pre-filled. The previously selected approver, frequency, and start day/date will also be pre-populated and can be updated if needed. Existing jobs will continue to use Fixed Rate , so existing rate configurations will not be changed. Margin, Markup, and Calculate Charge By are also available in relevant job and timesheet workflows, including the Job Add/Edit form, Job Details, Job List, Timesheet views, exports, filters, APIs, Workato, and Zapier integrations . Rate Type is also available in relevant Job views, filters, exports, imports, and APIs. Changing the Rate Type after timesheets have been created only affects newly created timesheets going forward, existing timesheets keep using the Rate Type they were created with. 3. If you are enabling the timesheet for Per Day Rate Type, then you can next select the working days under the Working Schedule section. If you are enabling the timesheet for Per Hour Rate Type, click Insert Pay and Bill Template , then select an existing template from the dropdown. You can also click Create New Template directly from the Rule Template dropdown to create a new template without navigating to Admin Settings . This option is available based on your role and permissions. Create Pay and Bill rule template 4. Once selected, review the automatically populated rules. You can modify the template or add custom rules, such as overtime or shift rules, without affecting the original template. 5. Click Enable to activate timesheets for the candidate. 6. Once enabled, the Timesheet icon next to the candidate turns green , indicating that timesheets are active. How to enable timesheets for multiple candidates 1. Open the required Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job. Scroll to the Candidate Pipeline and click View All Candidates . 2. Select the candidates you want to enable timesheets for. 3. Click Enable Timesheet from the bulk actions menu. 4. Complete the required details, insert a Pay and Bill Template , make any necessary changes, and click Enable . Timesheets can also be enabled through Deals: Learn how to enable and manage timesheets through deals How to verify that timesheets are enabled Once timesheets are enabled, the Timesheet icon next to the candidate's name turns green, indicating they are active. You can view this icon on the Candidate List page for the job. If it's not visible, enable the Timesheet field from your view settings. If any selected candidates are not eligible for timesheet activation, you will see an error message before proceeding. Candidate is in applied stage – Timesheets can only be enabled for candidates who are not in the applied stage. Timesheet is already enabled – This indicates that a timesheet is already active for the selected candidate. Troubleshooting Problem: The Enable Timesheet option isn't available. Likely Cause: The job isn't configured as a Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job, or the candidate is in the Applied stage. What to Check: Verify the job type and the candidate's current pipeline stage. Resolution: Update the job type if required and move the candidate beyond the Applied stage before enabling timesheets. FAQs What is the difference between Margin and Markup? Markup is the percentage added to the Pay Rate to calculate the Bill Rate. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% markup results in a $15 Bill Rate . Margin represents the percentage of the Bill Rate that is profit. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% margin requires a $20 Bill Rate . Conclusion The Timesheets feature makes it easy to manage contractor time tracking by enabling timesheets individually or in bulk, configuring approval workflows, and automating pay and billing calculations through reusable rule templates. s: This article will help you download all your Recruit CRM subscription invoices

Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Plans and Billing area in Recruit CRM lets you: Access all subscription invoices/receipts in one place. Download subscription invoices for record-keeping or accounting. View the current or active payment method on file. Change the card details used for subscription billing at any time. Update billing information so it appears on future invoices. Before you begin: Only Account Owners have access to the Plans & Billing section. You can check who the Account Owner is in Admin Settings > Account . On the Business plan and above , access can be granted to Plans & Billing to users on custom roles . Recruit CRM does not store your card information in its own database; card details are stored with the billing partner, Stripe . Download all your Recruit CRM subscription invoices/receipts 1. Open Admin Settings from your Recruit CRM account. 2. Go to Plans & Billing within Admin Settings. 3. Click on Invoice History on the left-hand side to view all your subscription invoices and receipts. 4. From the Invoice History page, download the required subscription invoices/receipts as needed.
