To change the card on file, use the option 'Add Payment Method' on the Payment Methods page to add a new card at any time in the future. On the top of the payment method's page, you will be able to see the Active/current card and also add a new card. Need VAT/Tax ID on your Recruit CRM subscription invoices? 1. If you need a VAT or tax ID on your invoices, go to the Billing Information section and update your billing information there and this information will appear on all your future invoices. Troubleshooting Problem: You cannot see the Plans and Billing section. Likely cause: You are not the Account Owner and do not have the required permissions. What to check: Confirm who the Account Owner is under Admin Settings > Account . Check if your role is a custom role with billing access (on the business plan and above). ​ Resolution: Ask the account owner to access billing for you, or Ask the account owner to grant billing access to your custom role (if you are on the business plan or above). Problem: Your VAT or tax ID does not appear on past invoices. Likely cause: The billing information was updated after those invoices were generated. What to check: Confirm that your VAT or tax ID is correctly entered in the billing information section. Resolution: Use the updated billing information for future invoices; past invoices will not automatically change. Conclusion: You can manage all your Recruit CRM subscription invoices, payment methods, and billing details from the Plans and Billing section, as long as you have the right access. If you still have questions, please contact Recruit CRM support for further assistance. t: How to find if an app is supported on Workflow Automation
s: The following article helps you identify the supported apps that could be integrated with Workflow Automation
h: Method 1 - Searching for the app while creating a recipe
Method 2 - Searching the app in the community library
b: Only users with access to the admin panel on the Business plan or account owners and admins on the Pro plan can perform this action. Method 1 - Searching for the app while creating a recipe 1. Go to Admin Settings >> Workflow Automation & Integration under CRM Process Customization. 2. Go to the Workflow module. 3. On the extreme right, click on “Create” and then click on “Recipe” to create a new recipe. 4. It will now prompt you to add a name to your “Recipe” and select the folder to which you want to save this recipe (you can also create a new folder if you desire). After that, make sure "Pick A Starting Point" is set to "Trigger From An App" which is also the default option, and then click on the “Start Building” button. 5. On the right side of the new window, search for the app you want to integrate with Recruit CRM, if your app appears, the integration is possible, if you do not find your chosen app, proceed to method 2 . Method 2 - Searching the app in the community library 1. Under “ Workflow Automation & Integration ” click on the “ Community Library ” module and go to the "Custom Connectors" tab. 2. Search for the app you wish to integrate with and if you find it, click on the app. 3. Now click on the “Install” button. 4. Finally click on “Release connector”. t: How to Generate a Google Meet Link While Scheduling Meetings in Recruit CRM
s: This article explains how to generate a Google Meet link while setting up meetings in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

Where does the Google Meet link appear in the meeting details?

b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Google Meet integration lets you generate a Google Meet link directly while creating a meeting in Recruit CRM. When you add a Google Meet link from within the meeting form, the system places the link in the “Where” section or in the meeting description with a default message. The system can also generate a confirmation email with the meeting details, Google Meet link, and description for the candidate or contact. You can use this feature when: When you schedule interviews or meetings inside Recruit CRM and need an automatically generated Google Meet link. When you are scheduling meetings from the Chrome extension and want to add a Google Meet link. Integrating Google Meet with Recruit CRM 1. Once you have integrated your calendar with Recruit CRM, you can click on the Profile icon and select the Meeting Integration tab. 2. Click the Connect button next to Google Meet Integration. 3. Select the Google account you want to connect and allow the necessary access when prompted. Generating Google Meet links while creating meetings 1. Open the candidate or contact record you want to schedule a meeting with. 2. Click Add Meeting from either: The Activities section on the right, or The Assigned Jobs widget next to the respective candidate details. 3. In the meeting form, under the Where section, click the Add G Meet Link button. 4. You will see the generated link under the “Where” section. 5. Click the Add button to save and schedule the meeting. 6. Once you click on the “Add” meeting button, the system will generate the confirmation email with the meeting details, the link, and the description that you choose to send out to the candidate/contact or not. Generate a Google Meet link from the Chrome extension 1. On the Recruit CRM Chrome extension, after saving the candidate/contact you can add a meeting as well: The candidate/contact will then receive the confirmation email and they can join the meeting right from their mail. Please note: The description box and the link are adjusted to the system language set by you in the profile settings . Troubleshooting Problem: The Google Meet link option does not appear in the meeting form. Likely cause: Google Meet is not connected. What to check: Confirm that your calendar is integrated and that the Google Meet integration in calendar settings shows as connected. Resolution: Go to your profile’s calendar settings, scroll to the Google Meet integration, click Connect , choose your account, and allow access. FAQs Where does the Google Meet link appear in the meeting details? The Google Meet link appears in the Where section. Does the candidate or contact receive the Google Meet link by email? Yes, if you choose to send the confirmation email when adding the meeting, the email will include the meeting details, the Google Meet link, and your description. Conclusion: By connecting your Google Meet account to Recruit CRM, you can generate Google Meet links directly while scheduling meetings, ensuring candidates and contacts receive clear, join-ready invitations. b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The executive search report feature lets you generate a detailed, customizable executive search progress report for a specific job in Recruit CRM. You can: Create a PDF or Word (.docx) report with candidates you select from the job pipeline. Customize sections such as the Executive Search Title (cover page), Candidate List, Candidate Profile, custom pages, and Team. Insert placeholders for job, candidate, company, contact, user, and job statistics data. Control formatting, section order, and visibility of individual sections. Decide whether empty placeholders show fallback text or appear as blank spaces. The revamped version provides enhanced formatting options, improved placeholder management, and better section organization, so reports are more flexible and client-ready. Before you begin This feature is available only for users on the Business plan and above. You must have access to the detailed view of the job whose candidates you want to include in the report. You need permission to use the “Submit to Client” action for that job. To configure candidate summary templates and placeholder behavior, you need access to Admin Settings. Step-by-step instructions Go to the detailed view of the job for which you want to generate the executive search report. ​ In the job’s detailed view, click the Submit to Client button. ​ In the pop-up that appears with three options, select Executive Search Report . ​ Select candidates for the report: In the Executive Search Report flow, choose the candidates you want to include in the report. Note: You can only select up to 100 candidates at once while generating an executive search report. ​ After selecting candidates, click Next to proceed to the report editor. ​ Use the Executive Search Report Editor After selecting the candidates, you'll see the Executive Search Report editor section, where you can rename the report and access all the formatting options for the report: ​ Configure the Executive Search Title (cover page): The first tab that you see under the 'Sections' is the 'Executive Search Title', which will be the cover page for the report. ​ Create a new template or select an existing template for the Executive Search Title from the dropdown, and insert placeholders as required. ​ Use the job statistics report integration placeholder to insert job statistics data as either a table or a chart on the title page. Charts are embedded as images, and tables are inserted directly. ​ Define the date range for the job statistics data you want to display in this section. Keep in mind that only 10 KPIs can be displayed in a job statistics report table. ​ Configure the Candidate List tab: Switch to the Candidate List tab to choose which candidate fields to show to your client in the list view. ​ Select the candidate placeholders (fields) you want to include in the Candidate List table. You can select up to 10 candidate placeholders in the Candidate List table. ​ Finalize the structure of the Candidate List table before applying formatting, because any formatting applied will be removed if you later add or remove placeholders. ​ Configure the Candidate Profile tab: 1. Go to the Candidate Profile tab and select a candidate to customize that candidate’s profile section individually. ​ 2. For each candidate, choose which fields to include in the profile, such as candidate fields (including candidate summary and custom fields), contact placeholders, company placeholders, job placeholders, and user placeholders. ​ 3. The candidate summary content in the report is taken from the Candidate Summary field on the candidate’s profile. ​ Users with access to Admin Settings can create templates for candidate summaries from the Candidate Field settings . Important Notes You can add additional candidates under the Candidate Profile section. You can reorder the candidates and sort candidates on the basis of First Name, Last Name,Hiring Stages, Assigned On Date, Updated On Date or Visibility and the sorting and reordering done in the Candidate Profile section applies to the Candidate List table as well. Candidates can be removed from the Candidate Profile section, but they will remain in the Candidate List table and move to the bottom of the list. Formatting applied to the Candidate List table will be removed if users add or remove any placeholders. To avoid this, apply formatting only after finalizing the table structure in the Candidate List section. Custom Pages: You can add custom pages to executive search reports for additional content and add jobs, contacts, companies, users placeholders, and job statistics report. Custom pages can be reordered like other sections. ​Configure the Team tab: Open the Team tab (the last tab in the editor) to manage team-related information in the report. ​ Add details of the job owner and collaborators associated with that job in the Team section. ​ Turn on the visibility toggle to make these users visible in the report, and use placeholders to include additional information about them. ​ Hide sections, preview, save, and share: Hide any of the main sections—Executive Search Title, Candidate List, Candidate Profile, and Team—by clicking the X icon next to the section name if you do not want it to appear in the final report. ​ Click the Preview (eye icon) button to see how the report will look before sharing it with the client. ​ Save your report using the Save button. You can return and continue editing it later using the Edit button. ​ When ready, share the report via email directly from Recruit CRM or download (down arrow icon button) it as a PDF or Word file and share it externally. ​ 5. If you generate the same report more than once, ensure that each version has a different report title to avoid confusion. Note: The default email template for Executive Search Reports has been updated. The current Executive Search Report email templates on your account remain unchanged. However, if you click on the "Reset" button for the ESR email template, the updated default template will be applied. Removal of Placeholders using Placeholder Settings You can now choose whether empty placeholders should display fallback text like “Field Name - Not Available” or appear as clean, blank spaces. This helps ensure Executive Search Reports look polished and client-ready, even when some fields are missing data. This applies to both: Executive Search Report templates defined in Admin Settings Dynamic placeholders added while building individual reports Click on Placeholder Settings under Admin Settings : When the toggle is turned ON, the empty placeholders render as blank When turned OFF (default) it show fallback as “{Field Label} - Not Available” Note: In work and education history, when both Start Date and End Date are missing, a dash ( – ) will still appear between them and this cannot be removed, even with the placeholder removal setting turned on. Known Limitations Template Design Limitations: The Executive Search Report is generated using a document editor , making it difficult to replicate templates created in PowerPoint or other external tools exactly. It is recommended to create the report using the available features to ensure smooth functionality and avoid formatting discrepancies. Old Template Migration & Formatting Variations: All the old templates and drafts created on the old version of the Executive Search Report will remain accessible until December 31st, 2025. Old templates are not directly migrated but remain available under Executive Search Report settings in Admin Settings until December 31st, 2025. Users can download old templates in HTML format using the Download button: Then import them into the new editor using the Open button. Formatting may vary after import, so users might need to adjust the layout or styles to match the original template. Here is a video for reference: Migrate Old Executive Search Report Template to New Editor Candidate List table- formatting limitations: Any formatting (e.g., font styles, borders, colors) applied to the Candidate List table within the template will not be retained when the report is generated. Additionally, if users add or remove placeholders after applying formatting in this case too the formatting would be lost. ​ Recommendation : Apply formatting only after the report is generated and the Candidate List table structure is finalized. 🤔 FAQs Can I reorder sections in my report? Yes, all sections can be reordered using a drag-and-drop feature. Is there a limit on the number of candidates in a report? Yes, the maximum number of candidates per report is 100. Can I generate a job statistics report for a specific date range? Yes, you can specify a date range when adding job statistics to the report. What happens if I close the editor without saving? A confirmation prompt will appear to prevent accidental loss of changes. What happens if I remove a candidate from the Candidate Profile section? The ca

t: How to grant admin access on the Microsoft Azure portal
s: This article will help you to connect your admin email within Recruit CRM.
h: Before you begin:
Grant Admin Consent Directly to the Application
Step 1: Sign In to the Azure Portal
Step 2: Navigate to Enterprise Applications
Step 3: Find and Open Recruit CRM
Step 4: Open Users and Groups

Step 6: Grant Admin Consent
b: If users in your organization see a "Need admin approval" error when connecting their email to Recruit CRM, an Azure admin needs to grant the required permissions in the Microsoft Azure Portal. This article walks you through the complete process — from signing in to confirming that access has been successfully granted. Before you begin: Please note: You need to have Admin permissions in your Microsoft Account to grant Admin Consent to an enterprise application in the Azure Portal. Important: The Recruit CRM application (labeled Recruit CRM-v3) will only appear in the Enterprise Applications list if a user has already attempted to connect their email in Recruit CRM. Make sure a user triggers that connection request before you proceed. Grant Admin Consent Directly to the Application This is the primary method for granting Recruit CRM the permissions it needs. Follow these steps as an Azure admin. Step 1: Sign In to the Azure Portal Go to portal.azure.com and sign in using your administrator account credentials. Click Sign in now . Step 2: Navigate to Enterprise Applications From the Azure home screen, search for "Enterprise applications" in the top search bar, or locate it in the left-hand navigation menu. Click on Enterprise applications . You will land on the Enterprise applications | All applications page, listing every application connected to your organization's tenant. Step 3: Find and Open Recruit CRM In the applications list, locate Recruit CRM-v3 . Click on the application name to open it. Step 4: Open Users and Groups Inside the Recruit CRM-v3 application page, click on Users and groups in the left-hand menu under the Manage section. This shows which users and groups currently have access to the application. 📝 Note: If you cannot find Recruit CRM in the list, make sure a user in your organization has first attempted to connect their email within Recruit CRM. This action registers the application in your Azure tenant. If you need to add more users or groups to the application, use the + Add user/group button at the top of this page. Step 5: Navigate to Permissions In the left-hand menu, scroll down to the Security section and click on Permissions . This page lists all permissions that have been granted to Recruit CRM for your organization. Step 6: Grant Admin Consent On the Permissions page, click the "Grant admin consent for [your organization]" button. A confirmation dialog will appear — review the requested permissions and click Accept to grant consent on behalf of all users in your organization. ✅ Tip: Granting admin consent means all users in your organization can use Recruit CRM with the required Microsoft permissions (such as accessing email and calendar data) without needing to individually consent. This is a delegated permission granted at the tenant level. After granting consent, check both the Admin consent and User consent tabs to verify that permissions are correctly listed. Step 7: Review User Consent Settings Click on Admin consent requests . Under My Pending Tab, click on "RecruitCRM-v3" and then click Review permissions and consent. ✅ Tip: After granting admin consent, navigate back to the Recruit CRM-v3 Permissions page and confirm that permissions appear under the Admin consent tab. Users in your organization can now connect their email in Recruit CRM without the "Need admin approval" error. Conclusion: Once admin consent has been successfully granted, your team members will be able to connect their email accounts to Recruit CRM without any interruptions. t: How to Handle Duplicate Candidates in Recruit CRM
s: Learn how to compare, edit, and choose which fields update when Recruit CRM finds a duplicate candidate.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Step by step instructions when a duplicate is detected
How it works
FAQs
What happens when a duplicate candidate is detected?
Can I edit values b efore updating the candidate?
Which field types suppor t inline editing?
What happens if I leave a required field empty?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? When you add a candidate through the Add Candidate form and Recruit CRM finds that the candidate already exists in your database, Recruit CRM automatically fills any empty fields with the incoming information and then shows a comparison page for fields where existing information can be updated. You can review the incoming details and choose exactly what gets updated. Use this feature when you want to: Review what is different between an existing candidate and a new submission before anything changes Update only specific fields, or only fields that are currently empty Correct or refine incoming details before they are saved, without leaving the Add Candidate flow ​ Step by step instructions when a duplicate is detected When you submit the Add Candidate form and Recruit CRM finds a matching existing candidate, it automatically updates any empty fields with the incoming information before opening the comparison page. The comparison page shows fields where the existing and incoming values differ, allowing you to review and control which existing information should be updated. Both default and custom candidate fields are included. ​ You can then review and control the update before applying it: Compare the existing and incoming values for each field. All eligible fields are selected by default. ​ Deselect any fields you do not want to update. Edit incoming values directly in the page if they need to be corrected by using the pencil icon next to the field. You can get the pencil icon by hovering over the field that you wish to edit. Apply the update. ​ 📌 Please note: Empty fields are automatically populated with available incoming information before the comparison page is shown. The comparison page is therefore focused on fields where existing information can be reviewed and potentially overwritten. How it works Required fields: Required fields are marked in the comparison page. If you try to apply an update while a required field is left empty, the update is blocked, the field is highlighted, and a validation message appears. You can keep editing freely while the page is open; validation only runs when you apply the update. ​ Closing without applying: If you have made changes in the comparison page and try to close it, Recruit CRM asks you to confirm before discarding your edits, so partly reviewed changes are not lost by accident. ​ When there is nothing to update: If Recruit CRM detects a duplicate but finds no new or different values to bring in, it skips the comparison page entirely. You are taken straight to the existing candidate's profile, with a notification letting you know no update was needed. ​ FAQs What happens when a duplicate candidate is detected? Recruit CRM automatically fills any empty fields with available incoming information and then opens a comparison page where you can review and control changes to existing candidate information. Can I edit values b efore updating the candidate? Yes. Incoming values can be edited directly within the comparison page before you apply the update. Which field types suppor t inline editing? Text, number, email, phone, URL, date, dropdown, multi select, skills, files, work history, and education history fields can all be edited. What happens if I leave a required field empty? The update is blocked until every required field has a valid value. What if there are no differences between the duplicate and the existing candidate? The comparison modal is skipped, and you are redirected to the existing candidate with a notification that no new data was available to update. Can I cancel after making edits? Yes. If you have made changes and try to close the comparison modal, you will be asked to confirm before your edits are discarded. Conclusion Recruit CRM automatically fills empty candidate fields with available incoming information and gives you control over changes to existing information through the comparison page. You can review, edit, select, or deselect incoming values before applying the update, while the comparison step is skipped when there is nothing new to update. b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The Current Organization field lets you associate a candidate with a company in your database as their current employer. This is how you can manage the relationship between candidates and their current organizations and easily update a candidate's profile after being placed in a company. You can use this when: You want to associate candidates with companies stored in your Recruit CRM database. You need to update existing candidates with their current organization. Before you begin: Please Note: The Current Organization field will not be filled automatically for old candidates already in your database. You will need to manually update the field for those records. There are multiple ways to update the Current Organization field, including from the candidate form, candidate profile, bulk actions, placement workflow, and the Chrome extension. Only the account owner can manage whether current organizations sourced from LinkedIn are added as companies via Account Settings . The Current Organization field can be added or made visible in layouts if you do not see it by default. Step-by-step instructions Method 1 - Through the add/edit form You'll find the Current Organization field under Employment Information while adding/editing a candidate. You can search for an existing company or add a new one directly from the search: If you do not see the Current Organization field, you may need to make it visible first. Click here to learn how you can make a field visible Method 2 - Add Current Organization from Candidate Profile View 1. Open the candidate’s profile. 2. Hover over an existing field you want to replace, then click the pencil icon to edit the layout. Next, click Replace Field . 3. From the list of available fields, select Current Organization to add it to the candidate’s profile layout. 4. Once added, you can set or update the candidate’s current organization directly in their profile. For a candidate's Current Organization field, you can save it as plain text, even if a matching company record already exists - instead of it always linking to a company, by clicking on the 'Add as Text' button after entering the current organization: When you search for a company name, you'll see an 'Add as Text' option alongside 'Add as Company' if no company match is found for the entered text. You can click on the 'Add as Company' to create a new company record: Method 3 - Update Current Organization in Bulk 1. From the candidate list page, select all candidates whose current organization you want to update. 2. Click the Update Field option from the options at the top. 3. In the field selection dropdown, choose Current Organization . 4. Then select the appropriate company from the dropdown list. Pro tip: Use Advanced Search to filter candidates where Current Organization is set to “Not Available,” then bulk update this field if you know their current employer. Method 4 - Update Current Organization When Placing a Candidate When you move a candidate to the Placed hiring stage, you will see an option to update their Current Organization based on the company linked to the job. Confirm this update so the candidate is automatically associated with the hiring company as their current employer. Method 5 - Use the Chrome Extension to Maintain Current Organization When sourcing candidates via the Chrome extension , the candidate’s current organization will automatically be added as a new company in Recruit CRM if it does not already exist. Note: A candidate’s current organization will now always be updated with the latest data when sourcing via the Chrome Extension, even if the Override Data toggle is turned off. This ensures users never miss the most up-to-date employer information. If you don't want the candidate's current organization to be added to your database while sourcing candidates through LinkedIn, you can disable the feature in the Account Settings: Only the account owner will be able to manage the settings. When a new candidate is added to the database, if the current organization is available and the same organization is present in the database, the candidate will be automatically associated with the current organization based on the company’s. ​ If we are unable to match the candidate to a company it will simply be stored as plain text. View All Candidates Employed at a Company 1. Inside a candidate’s profile, click the Current Organization field value to open that company’s profile page. 2. On the company profile, scroll down and click the Candidates Employed tab. 3. Here, you will see a list of all candidates currently working for that company. From this tab, you can perform bulk actions such as assigning them to a job, updating fields, composing an email, adding a note, and more. You can also hide specific fields and run an Advanced Search within this list to refine the view. When saving a company via the Chrome extension, you will have the option to also save the associated contact as a candidate. If selected, that person will be added as a candidate in the system and automatically appear under the Candidates Employed tab for that company. Troubleshooting Problem : The Current Organization field is not visible when adding or editing a candidate. Likely cause: The field is hidden in your layout. What to check: Look for the help button in the Employment Information section and confirm field visibility settings. Resolution path: Make the Current Organization field visible in the layout, then return to the candidate form and fill it in. FAQs Can I stop new companies being created from LinkedIn sourcing? Yes. If you don't want the candidate's current organization to be added to your database while sourcing candidates through LinkedIn, you can disable the feature in the account settings. Only the account owner will be able to manage the settings. Conclusion: Using the Current Organization field is the most reliable way to keep candidate–company relationships accurate in Recruit CRM. By combining individual updates, bulk actions, placement workflows, and the Chrome extension, you can maintain a clean, searchable database and quickly see which candidates work for which organizations. t: How to Manage Contractor Reimbursements in Recruit CRM (Beta)
s: Recruit CRM allows contractors to raise reimbursement requests directly through timesheets, while agencies and clients can review and manage them from their respective portals.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Enabling reimbursements in timesheets
Managing reimbursements through the Contractor Portal
Managing Reimbursements from the Agency Portal
Reopening Reimbursements
Managing Reimbursements from the Client Portal
Exporting Reimbursements
Reimbursement Attachments for Reimbursements
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM’s Reimbursements feature enables contractors to submit and manage expense claims directly within timesheets while giving agencies and clients full visibility into the approval process. Once enabled, contractors can raise reimbursement requests for expenses such as travel, accommodation, meals, and fuel. Agencies can review, approve, and manage these reimbursements, while also choosing which expense claims are shared with client approvers. This helps streamline expense tracking, simplify approvals, improve invoice accuracy, and provide greater control over client visibility. Note- This feature is currently in beta release and will be gradually rolled out to all users over the next few weeks. Enabling reimbursements in timesheets This is an individual feature that can be enabled on a Contractor basis, while enabling Timesheets for a Contractor, in a Contract/contract-to-permanent type job. While enabling Timesheets from any place on the app, you can turn ON the Toggle of “Enable Expense claim.” When Enable Expense Claim is turned on, a Share expenses with client checkbox appears below it. This setting is enabled by default and determines whether newly created expense claims are automatically shared with client approvers. You can change this setting at any time, and it will only affect expense claims created after the change. Once enabled: An Expense Claim tab appears in newly generated timesheets. Contractors can submit reimbursement requests. Agencies can review and manage all reimbursement requests. Expense claims are shared with client approvers based on the Share expenses with client setting, which can be overridden for individual claims. Managing reimbursements through the Contractor Portal Contractors can raise reimbursement requests directly from the Expense Claim tab within their timesheet. They can: Add multiple reimbursement requests in a single timesheet Upload receipts or supporting documents Track reimbursement status View remarks and reimbursement history Edit and resubmit rejected reimbursements NOTE: Reimbursements can only be edited while they are still under review or rejected. Managing Reimbursements from the Agency Portal Agency users can review and manage reimbursement requests from Recruit CRM. Each reimbursement includes a Share with Client toggle that allows agency users to control whether an individual expense claim is visible on the Client Portal. The toggle can be updated at any time, regardless of whether the reimbursement is Pending , Approved , or Rejected , and whether or not an invoice has already been created. Reimbursements move through the following statuses: Pending, Approved & Rejected Only designated timesheet approvers can approve or reject reimbursements. Other users can still view reimbursement details. Once approved, reimbursements are automatically marked as Payable and Billable. Approvers can choose not to mark them as Payable or Billable. The Share with Client setting does not affect the Payable or Billable status of a reimbursement. Reopening Reimbursements Timesheet Approvers at Recruit CRM can reopen approved reimbursements. Once reopened: The reimbursement status changes back to Pending Payable and Billable options are automatically disabled The reimbursement goes back through the approval process Remarks and status history remain visible for tracking purposes. Please note that reimbursements cannot be reopened, updated or deleted once a client invoice is linked to the timesheet. Managing Reimbursements from the Client Portal Clients can review reimbursement details only for expense claims that have been shared with them by the agency. Only approvers can approve or reject reimbursement requests, but they cannot edit or delete them. If an expense claim is not shared, it will not appear on the Client Portal, even if the timesheet itself has been shared. Note: If an expense claim was previously shared and later hidden by turning off the Share with Client toggle, clients will no longer be able to view that reimbursement, even if they had already received an in-app notification for it. Exporting Reimbursements Approved reimbursements can be exported along with timesheets in Excel or CSV format. During export, approved reimbursements appear in a separate sub-sheet, with each reimbursement listed as an individual row for easier tracking and reporting. Reimbursement Attachments for Reimbursements When you click Save & Send to Client while sending an invoice, any reimbursement attachments associated with that invoice are automatically included in the email. You can remove attachments before sending the email if required. Removing an attachment from the email does not delete it from the reimbursement or the timesheet. When exporting reimbursements, any available attachments are sent to your email as a downloadable ZIP file. The reimbursement data itself continues to download separately as a CSV or Excel file. Please Note: Reimbursement attachments included in invoice emails follow the existing 25 MB attachment size limit. Reimbursement attachments are downloaded separately as a ZIP file and are not bundled with the CSV or Excel export. FAQs 1. Why isn't an expense claim visible on the Client Portal? The expense claim may not be shared with the client. Check the Share with Client toggle for that reimbursement. If it is turned off, the claim will remain visible only to agency users. 2. Why can’t a reimbursement be edited or deleted? Reimbursements cannot be updated once they are approved or linked to an invoice. 3. Why are Payable and Billable options disabled? These settings only become available after the reimbursement is approved. 4. Can rejected reimbursements be submitted again? Yes. Rejected reimbursements can be edited and resubmitted for approval. 5. Is currency conversion supported automatically in invoices? No. Currently, if the pay currency and bill currency are different, reimbursement amounts are not automatically converted as of yet. The reimbursement amount will be added directly using the bill currency without any currency conversion. 6. If I change the Share expenses with client setting, will it affect existing expense claims? No. The setting only applies to expense claims created after the change, including new claims added to existing timesheets. Existing claims keep their current sharing status. 7. Can I override the sharing setting for an individual expense claim? Yes. Each reimbursement has its own Share with Client toggle, allowing agency users to show or hide individual expense claims regardless of the default setting. 8. Can I change the sharing setting after a reimbursement has been approved or rejected? Yes. The Share with Client toggle can be updated at any time, regardless of the reimbursement status or whether an invoice already exists. Conclusion: Recruit CRM’s Reimbursements feature simplifies contractor expense management by allowing reimbursement claims to be submitted and tracked directly within timesheets. t: How to Navigate Candidates Within a Hiring Stage Using Sequence View (New UI)
s: This article shows you how you can get into a workflow of viewing candidates within a job in a sequence to get work done faster.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to View and Navigate Candidates Within a Hiring Stage
What You Can Do in the Sequence View?
Troubleshooting
Problem: The Next button does not appear or does not move to another candidate.
FAQs
Where is the Next button located?
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? This feature allows you to view and navigate through all candidates within a specific hiring stage of a job. From the candidate pipeline, you can open a candidate's profile and move through the remaining candidates in the same stage using the Next button, making it easier to review and manage candidates without repeatedly returning to the pipeline. While reviewing candidates, you can also see the total number of candidates associated with the job, view all candidates in the selected hiring stage, and perform actions directly from each candidate's profile details page. Use this feature when: • You want to review all candidates in a specific hiring stage for a job • You need to quickly move between candidates in the same stage using the Next button • You want to evaluate candidate profiles directly from the job pipeline • You need to perform actions such as adding activities, updating records, or managing candidate profiles while reviewing candidates in a stage How to View and Navigate Candidates Within a Hiring Stage Follow the steps below to review all candidates within a specific hiring stage of a job: Navigate to the Jobs list page and open the job you want to review. Scroll down to the Candidate Pipeline , located at the bottom of the job page. Click on the hiring stage whose candidates you want to view. From the list of candidates in that stage, click on any candidate. The candidate's profile will open in Sequence View , which appears at the top of the page and allows you to navigate through all candidates within that hiring stage. Use the Next button to move through candidates one by one without returning to the pipeline. Note: The Next button only navigates through candidates within the currently selected hiring stage. It does not move between different hiring stages. What You Can Do in the Sequence View? • Move between candidates in the selected hiring stage using the Next button • View the total number of candidates available in that stage • Access candidate details, activities, notes, and other profile information • Continue reviewing candidates without returning to the Candidate Pipeline This view provides a faster way to review candidates stage by stage while staying within the context of the same job and hiring pipeline. ​ To learn more about how hiring stages work, please check this article: ​ Changing Hiring Stages Troubleshooting Problem: The Next button does not appear or does not move to another candidate. Likely cause: There may be only one candidate in that hiring stage, or you are already on the last candidate in the sequence. What to check: Confirm how many candidates are listed in the hiring stage and review the total candidate count for the job. Resolution: If multiple candidates exist, continue using the Next button to move through them; if only one candidate is present, there will be no further candidate to move to. FAQs Where is the Next button located? Use the Next button at the top right corner in the sequence view to move through all the different candidates that are in that particular hiring stage of that particular job. Conclusion: By using the candidate pipeline and sequence view inside a job, you can quickly review candidates in a specific hiring stage and manage their profiles efficiently from one place. t: How to reactivate a deactivated user in Recruit CRM
s: This article will help you understand how you can reactivate a deactivated user.
h: What this feature does and when to use this feature?
Step-by-step instructions
Troubleshooting
Problem: You can’t reactivate a user because the Reactivate User action fails.
Problem: The user did not receive the reactivation email.
FAQs
1. What happens to a user’s data when I reactivate them?
2. Do I need an extra/unused license to reactivate a user?
b: What this feature does and when to use this feature? Reactivating a deactivated user in Recruit CRM restores their access to the system and, if applicable, reassigns their previously owned records back to them. (While deactivating a user, you have the option to transfer the data under their ownership to another user . But, in case you've not already transferred the data, by reactivating the user, all the data previously added under their ownership will be mapped back to them.) It also uses one unused license from your purchased licenses. You can use this feature when: You need to restore access for a user who was previously deactivated. Step-by-step instructions 1. Go to Admin Settings > Users > User Management , locate the deactivated user you want to reactivate, and click the pencil (Edit) icon next to their name. 2. In the user details window, click Reactivate , confirm the user's email address, and then click Reactivate User to send the invitation. Note- If there are no available purchased licenses on your subscription, you will be prompted to purchase an additional license before you can continue. 3. Once the invitation is sent, a Resend Reactivation Email button will appear in the user profile, allowing you to resend the invite until the user accepts it and rejoins your team. That's it! If you have purchased licenses that are not currently assigned to any users, a message at the top of the User Management page will display the number of available licenses in your account. From this message, you can choose to: Invite New Users to assign the available licenses. Clicking this option opens the Invite Teammate window. Reduce License Count to match the number of active users. Clicking this option takes you to the Payment and Billing page. Note: Only the Account Owner and other users on roles that have access to these sections will be able to complete the tasks. Additionally, the User Management page allows you to filter users by status, making it easy to view only Active or Deactivated users as needed. You can also use the search bar to quickly find a specific user instead of manually browsing through the entire list. Troubleshooting Problem: You can’t reactivate a user because the Reactivate User action fails. Likely cause: There are not enough purchased licenses available on your subscription plan. What to check: The number of purchased licenses you have. Resolution path: If there is no available unused license, purchase an additional license from the plans and billing section. Problem: The user did not receive the reactivation email. Likely cause: Email address entered is incorrect, or the email went to spam/junk. What to check: The email ID you added in the Reactivate User window. The user’s spam/junk folder and email filters. Resolution path: Correct the email if needed, then click the Send Reactivation Email button from the user’s edit window until the user successfully joins the team. FAQs 1. What happens to a user’s data when I reactivate them? If you did not transfer their data at deactivation, all the data previously added under their ownership will be mapped back to them when you reactivate the user. 2. Do I need an extra/unused license to reactivate a user? Yes. Reactivating a user consumes one license. If there are not enough purchased licenses available on your subscription plan, you will need to buy a new license before you can complete the reactivation. Conclusion Reactivating a deactivated user in Recruit CRM is simple. With built-in license visibility, user filters, and search functionality, Recruit CRM makes it easy to restore user access and manage your subscription seats efficiently. b: What this feature does & when to use it? Recruit CRM’s Advanced Search feature helps recruiters quickly find candidates and contacts using Boolean search, filters, and activity-based search options. You can search through candidate profiles, resumes, candidate attachments, notes, call logs, meetings, and tasks, then save your search criteria for future use to locate the exact records you need faster and more accurately. Use this feature to: Quickly locate specific records. Reuse frequently used filter setups. Step-by-step instructions 1. Boolean Search Click on the Boolean Search section to start building your keyword query. You can use Boolean Search to find specific keywords across candidate profiles, the resume uploaded in the default Resume field, and supported candidate attachments. In the Boolean search, you can combine AND, OR, and NOT operators to narrow down your search results. Use the Contains search option to find records that include a specific keyword, even if the exact phrase does not match. For example, searching for ‘sales’ may return results such as ‘sales manager,’ ‘international sales,’ or ‘business sales. Select the sources you want to search, including: Candidates (candidate fields and the resume uploaded in the default Resume field) Files (candidate attachments in PDF, DOC, and DOCX formats, excluding the default resume) Notes Call Logs Tasks Meetings ​ The Candidates and Files options work independently, allowing you to search either source individually or both together. When searching attachments, Recruit CRM searches the 10 most recent supported files for each candidate. 2. Save Search Click Save Search to store your search criteria for future use. Once saved, the search will appear under the Quick View section in the Saved Searches tab. To clear your current Boolean search, click the Reset button. 3. Add filters Click Add Filters to apply filters to default and custom fields. You can combine multiple filters to narrow down your results and improve search accuracy. To further narrow down candidates based on location, you can also use Radius Search in Recruit CRM. Learn how to run a radius search inside the system 4. Search on Activity Fields Recruit CRM also lets you search across notes, call logs, tasks, meetings, and candidate attachments, making it easier to find previous interactions or information stored outside the default resume. FAQs Q: Can I search within candidate attachments other than the default resume? Yes. Select the Files option in Boolean Search to search supported candidate attachments in PDF , DOC , and DOCX formats. This searches up to the 10 most recent supported attachments for each candidate. The default resume is searched through the Candidates option. Q: What's the difference between the Candidates and Files options? Candidates searches candidate fields and the resume uploaded in the default Resume field. Files searches other supported candidate attachments. You can select either option individually or both together depending on where you want Boolean Search to look. Q: Can I combine Boolean search and filters in the same search? Yes. You can use both together to refine your results. Q: Can I search within notes and tasks? Yes. You can search within notes, call logs, tasks, and meetings. Conclusion Using Recruit CRM's Advanced Search feature helps you quickly locate candidates and contacts by searching across candidate profiles, resumes, supported attachments, activities, and filters, making it easier to find the right records and save frequently used searches for future use. ​ Related Articles Resume parsing on Recruit CRM How to run a search in Recruit CRM Boolean Search and Filters in Recruit CRM Filter types for Advanced Search (New UI) Resume parsing on Recruit CRM (New UI)

Method 1: From the Jobs list page
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The Recruit CRM Public Jobs Page allows candidates to view open positions and apply directly to the jobs visible on the Recruit CRM Public Jobs Page. You can customize the page to match your brand, embed jobs or application forms on your website, share it via a direct link, manage social media sharing settings, control which jobs are publicly visible, and create dedicated job page URLs for specific teams or companies. Use this feature to showcase open roles, streamline applications, and manage how jobs are displayed externally. Before you begin: Please note: Ensure you can access Admin Settings in Recruit CRM, as the Public Job Page Settings are configured there. The open API used for advanced customizations is available on the Business plan and above. Only jobs that are not closed and have Enable Job Application Form checked will appear on the public jobs page. The image or logo you set in the Social Media Sharing tab applies to all social media posts that use your jobs page link. Have your branding assets ready, such as your logo, background image, and preferred color codes. If you plan to embed the jobs page or forms, ensure you or your web team can edit your website’s HTML. Step-by-step instructions 1. Go to Admin Settings in Recruit CRM. 2. In Admin Settings, select Public Job Page Settings . 3. In Public Job Page Settings, review the three tabs available: Appearance Settings Tab: In the Appearance Settings tab, locate the field for Job Page Title and enter the title you want displayed at the top of your jobs page. Enter a Job Page Subtitle to add a short descriptive line under the title. In Link to More Jobs , add a URL if you want to redirect users to a main jobs page or another relevant page. If you do not want this section to display, leave the field blank. Set the Placeholder Text for Search Box to define the text that appears inside the search box before users type anything. Upload a Background Image to visually brand the page. Upload your Logo so your brand appears clearly on the jobs page. Accepted file formats are: .jpg, .png, .jpeg Adjust Text and Background Colors so the jobs page aligns with your company website theme. Fine-tune the list color and apply button color to ensure they are on-brand and accessible. If you need deeper or more complex customization beyond these settings, use the Recruit CRM open API , available on the Business plan and above , to build custom integrations and experiences. Here's our API Documentation for your reference: https://docs.recruitcrm.io Job Page Integration Tab: Review the Website link option: Use this if you do not have a website or want a simple, shareable link. Copy the jobs page link and paste it on any platform where you want candidates to access your jobs. When candidates apply via this link, their applications go directly into your Recruit CRM database. You can set the job pages link name to the name of your choice to control how the link text appears. Review the Website integration option: Use the provided iframe code to embed the full jobs page into your website. Copy the iframe code from the Job Page Integration tab. Paste this iframe code into your website’s HTML where you want the jobs page to appear. To embed a specific job application form instead of the full jobs page: Copy the iframe code provided in the Job Page Integration tab. In that code, find the portion that starts with src="...". Replace the link inside the quotes after src="..." with the URL of the specific job application form. Paste the modified iframe code into your website’s HTML at the location where you want that job’s form to appear. Social Media Sharing Tab: Customize the text that will be used when your jobs page is shared on social media platforms. Upload an image or logo that will be displayed for all social media posts that share your jobs page. Remember that the image or logo set here applies to all your social media posts that use this jobs page link. Access the jobs page link You can access your jobs page link in two main ways. Method 1: From the Jobs list page Go to the Jobs list page in Recruit CRM. On the Jobs list page, locate the link to the job page at the top right of the page. Method 2: From Public Job Page Settings Open Public Job Page Settings from Admin Settings. Within the Public Job Page Settings tab, locate and copy the jobs page link provided there. Ensure jobs appear on the public jobs page To control which jobs display on the public jobs page, check the following conditions: Job status must not be closed. t: How to set up Email Triggers in Recruit CRM
s: This article explains how to set up email triggers (email automation) in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

How to set up an Email Trigger?
Troubleshooting

b: What this feature does and when to use it? Email triggers in Recruit CRM automatically send emails or update stages when specific events occur in your pipelines. You can: Send emails automatically when a candidate’s hiring stage is changed. Send emails automatically when a contact’s sales stage is changed. Automatically update a candidate’s hiring stage when a “Submit Candidate – Online Link ” email is sent. Automatically update a candidate’s hiring stage when a “Submit Candidate – Candidate Grid ” email is sent. Before you begin: Make sure you can access the Admin settings in Recruit CRM. Ensure your email account is connected in Email settings . Prepare or review the email templates you want to use for each trigger, so you can select the correct one during setup. ⚙️ How to set up an Email Trigger? 1. Go to Admin Settings in your Recruit CRM account & click on Email Triggers under CRM process customization. ​2. Click on Add Email Trigger. ​3. Enter a clear, descriptive name for your email trigger so you can easily recognize its purpose later (for example, Candidate moved to Interview — to be confirmed ). 4. Select the execution event that should activate the trigger. ​ ​The email trigger offers four types of execution events that will determine when the email is sent and whether stages are updated. ​ The available execution events are: 📩 Email Triggers for Stage Changes When the hiring stage is changed: This trigger works when a candidate’s hiring stage changes in the hiring pipeline. You can configure it to automatically send an email whenever a candidate is moved into a selected stage. When the contact stage is changed: This trigger works when a contact’s stage changes in the sales pipeline. You can configure it to automatically send an email whenever a contact is moved into a selected stage. ⚠️ Note: The email will be sent directly to the candidate or contact once the email trigger is activated and the stage is set. It will not be sent internally. 🔄 Stage Changes Triggered by Sending Emails When "Submit Candidate" email is sent (Online Link) This trigger updates a candidate’s hiring stage automatically when a Submit Candidate – Online Link email is sent. When "Submit Candidate" email is sent (Candidate Grid) This trigger updates a candidate’s hiring stage automatically when a Submit Candidate – Candidate Grid email is sent. ✅ Please Note: The hiring stage will only be updated if the email is sent successfully. Click here to learn more about how to submit candidates to contacts ​4. Select the Execution Event Value, your hiring stages will appear here, you can add more stages to this pipeline from here . ​5. Select the email template you want to use or you can create email templates from here . This article about email templates will help you create one. 6. Select the sender from the list (from whom the email trigger should be sent). Please note that if the sender has more than one email ID connected, the email trigger will be sent from the 'Default Email Address' as set in the 'Email Settings' . ​7. Just make sure everything is correct and hit Save. And that's how you set email triggers in Recruit CRM. After saving: When you change the hiring stage of a candidate to the stage defined in the trigger, the system will prompt you to the email trigger. For “Submit Candidate” triggers, the candidate’s hiring stage will be updated only when the corresponding email is successfully sent. Troubleshooting Problem: Email is being sent from the wrong email address Likely cause: The default email address in Email settings is different from the address you expect. What to check: In Email settings , confirm which email ID is set as the default . In the trigger configuration, check the sender selected. Resolution: Update the default email address in Email settings if required. Adjust the sender selection in the email trigger, then save and test. FAQs Where do I find email triggers in Recruit CRM? Email triggers are available under Admin settings in the CRM process customization section as Email triggers . Who receives the emails sent by email triggers? Emails configured in email triggers are sent directly to the candidate or contact associated with the event. They are not sent internally to team members. Conclusion: Email triggers in Recruit CRM help you automate key communication steps and keep your pipelines up to date with less manual work. If you still have questions, just click on the chat icon on your bottom right and hit us with a message. t: How to Set Up Parent and Child Company Relationships in Recruit CRM
s: This article will show you how you can create links between companies to define Parent/Child/Subsidiary relationships between them
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
Method 1: Link parent and child companies from the company profile:
Method 2: Link parent and child companies during import:
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The parent–child company relationship feature in Recruit CRM lets you link companies together as parent and subsidiary (child) records. You can: Set one company as the primary parent company. Link other companies as secondary or subsidiary (child) companies. Create these links one by one from the company profile. Create these links in bulk while importing companies using a CSV or XLS file. Identify whether the company you are viewing has a parent company. View all contacts grouped together for related parent and subsidiary companies. See subsidiary or child companies listed on the parent company profile page. This helps you manage complex client organizations where multiple entities belong to the same group. Before you begin Make sure you have access to the company’s details view so you can open the company profile and use the three dots menu. Prepare your CSV or XLS file carefully if you plan to link parent and child companies during import. The file should contain a column that clearly lists the parent company for each subsidiary. Ensure that the parent company names in your sheet match the company names you intend to use as parents in Recruit CRM, so the mapping to the “parent company name” field works correctly. Method 1: Link parent and child companies from the company profile: On the company details view, click the three-dot icon (more options menu). ​ From the menu that appears, choose the option to link the company to its parent or child company. ​ After you have completed the linking on those companies, you will see whether the company is related to a parent company when you view its profile. ​ Method 2: Link parent and child companies during import: Prepare your CSV or XLS file with all the companies you want to import, including a column that contains the parent company for each subsidiary company. ​ Start the company import process in Recruit CRM and upload your CSV or XLS file. ​ During the import mapping step, map each column in your sheet to its respective field in Recruit CRM. ​ Specifically, map the column in your sheet that contains the parent company to the “parent company name” field in Recruit CRM. ​ Complete the import so that Recruit CRM can create the companies and link them as parent and child based on the mapped parent company name column. ​ Once you have assigned a parent or subsidiary company through this import process, you can view all contacts grouped together in the “Group Contacts” section on the company profile. ​ On the parent company profile page, you will be able to see the subsidiary or child companies listed, confirming the parent–child relationships you set up. ​ Conclusion: The parent–child company relationship feature in Recruit CRM helps you organize and manage complex company structures by connecting parent organizations with their subsidiaries. Whether added individually or through bulk imports, these links make it easier to track related companies, view grouped contacts, and maintain a clear overview of business relationships within an organization. t: How to Share Candidates and Other Records With Teammates/Users in Recruit CRM
s: This article will help you share candidates & other records with your teammates including users with restricted access
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
Share a record using @mention
Give a restricted user access by adding them as a collaborator:
What restricted users see and what happens on access errors:
Conclusion:
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Recruit CRM lets you share any record with any user by mentioning them in the note section of that record. When you mention a teammate using the at symbol (@) in a note, Recruit CRM sends that user an email that includes the note details and a direct link to the record. Check out this article on how the mention feature works. For restricted users, access to that record still follows restricted‑access rules. The Restricted Access role is generally used by companies to grant access to RPO Clients & Freelance/Part-Time Teammates. While Inviting your teammates to Recruit CRM, you set their Roles (Recruiter or Admin) and Access (Full Access or Restricted Access). They will only be able to open the shared record if they already have permission to view it, typically by being a collaborator on the related job or by having added the data themselves. Before you begin Make sure the teammate you want to share records with has a Recruit CRM user account with the correct role and access level (full access or restricted access). Understand that restricted users can only see data they added themselves, or candidates assigned to jobs where they are added as collaborators on the job. If you want a restricted user to work on a specific job or its candidates, you must add them as a collaborator on that job first. Share a record using @mention Open the record you want to share (for example, a candidate or another type of record). ​ Go to the note section of that record. ​ Type a new note and use the at symbol (@) followed by your teammate’s name to mention them in the note. ​ Save the note. Recruit CRM will send the mentioned user an email with the note details and a link to the record. Give a restricted user access by adding them as a collaborator: Open the job you want the restricted user to access. ​ Click the option to edit the job. ​ In the job view, select the Edit Job action. ​ In the Edit Job form, locate the collaborator section. ​ Start typing the restricted user’s name in the collaborator section and select them from the list. ​ Save the job. Once added as a collaborator, the restricted user will have access to that job and the candidates assigned to it. What restricted users see and what happens on access errors: A user with restricted access will get an error message when they try to access the data that is not available for them. ​ Here you can see the list of Jobs inside the login of a user with " Restricted Access ", They have access to jobs & Candidates inside while they are not "Owners" because they have been added as collaborators on those jobs. Conclusion: Using @mentions together with collaborator settings lets you share candidates and other records efficiently while keeping restricted users limited to only the jobs and data they should see. t: How to track the latest communications with candidates and contacts
s: This article will guide you on tracking the last communications with your candidates and contacts!
h: Step-by-step instructions
What does each column represent?
Run a search using communication columns
Troubleshooting
FAQs
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does & when to use it? This feature helps you track and analyze interactions with candidates and contacts by showing details like last call log added, last email sent on, last SMS sent on, last meeting added, last note added on and last LinkedIn message sent on. It gives clear visibility into recent communication, making it easier to manage relationships and stay updated on outreach. Use this feature when you want to: Check the last interaction with a record. Quickly review interaction history in a list view. Step-by-step instructions Recruit CRM allows you to customize and arrange the fields (for Candidates/Companies/Contacts/Jobs) in the list view in any way you want! To view the last communication data, all you have to do is, make the columns Last Email Sent On, Last Communication, Last Call Log Added, Last Note Added On, Last SMS Sent On , 'Last Meeting Added' and 'Last LinkedIn Message Sent On' visible on the list page. Here is a video for your reference. Once these columns are visible on the list page, you can easily see the latest interactions for each record. Click here to learn more about how to enable field visibility and rearrangement on the lists What does each column represent? Last Call Log Added: Displays the timestamp of the last call log added for a candidate or contact. Last Communication: Reflects the most recent communication method (call, SMS, or email) based on the latest timestamp. Last SMS Sent On: Shows the date and time of the most recent SMS sent. Last Email Sent On: Captures the date of the last email sent only from Recruit CRM. Last Meeting Added (only for candidates, contacts, and companies) : Captures the time stamp when the meeting was added. Last LinkedIn Message Sent On : Tracks the LinkedIn Messages sent using the LinkedIn Integration feature. ​ Last Note Added On: Tracks the timestamp of the most recently added note for the specific entity. If no note exists, the field will display Not Available . Please note: The Last Note Added On field is not considered a last communication tracking field, as it only records internal note activity added within the record’s profile. Click here to learn more about texting Candidates/contacts in Recruit CRM Run a search using communication columns Below, you'll find an example of how to perform an Advanced Search on this. Select the relevant communication column (e.g., Last Communication, Last Email Sent On, Last SMS Sent On, etc.). You can customise your search by selecting the columns and choosing different filter types, such as is, is not, is visible, between, before, after, etc, depending on your specific needs and dates. Specify the date or date range to narrow down your results. This empowers you to filter candidates and contacts based on their most recent interactions, making the recruitment process more efficient and targeted. Click here to learn more about how to run search in Recruit CRM Troubleshooting Problem: The communication columns are not appearing in the list view. Likely cause: Columns have not been added to the visible list view layout. What to check: Open the list view customization and confirm whether the columns are selected. Resolution path: Add Last Call Log Added, Last Communication, Last SMS Sent On, Last Email Sent On, Last Meeting Added, and Last LinkedIn Message Sent On to your list view and save the layout. FAQs 1. What happens to the Last Note Added On field if I delete the latest note? If the latest note is deleted, the field recalculates to the next latest note, and if no notes remain, the value becomes Not Available. 2. Is there another way to track this information instead of using columns? Yes! When you enter a candidate or contact's profile and click on the 'Last Updated' icon, you can see the most recent interaction method, its timestamp, and the person who performed the action; all displayed just by clicking the 'Last Updated' icon on the candidate/contact details page. 3. To which plans does this apply? 4. Is it possible to view the communication tracking columns in the candidate/contact list views within the Reports? Yes, when generating a report for the following KPIs in these specific reports: If you hover over the bars showing the results from the report, you can click on them to open a new window. From there, you can click on 'Edit Columns,' select the columns you want to display, and drag them to your preferred position: Conclusion: By making the last communication columns visible, understanding what each represents, and using them in advanced search, you can track recent interactions and manage follow-ups more efficiently. If you need any assistance setting this up or interpreting the data, please contact our support team using the chat icon in the bottom-right corner of your screen. t: How to Unassign a Candidate from a Job
s: This article will guide you on unassigning candidates from jobs without deleting their profiles.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Step-by-step instructions to Unassign Candidates
Method 1: Unassign a single candidate from a job
Method 2: Unassign multiple candidates from a job
Method 3: Unassign a candidate from the Candidate profile
Method 4: Unassign Candidate from Jobs in the Old UI
Troubleshooting
Problem: The candidate still appears in the job’s Candidates pipeline after trying to unassign.
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Assigned a candidate to the wrong job? Recruit CRM lets you quickly unassign candidates from a job to keep your hiring pipeline accurate and organized. Unassigning a candidate removes the association between that candidate and the selected job, preventing further progress tracking for a role they should no longer be part of. Use this feature when: A candidate was assigned to the wrong job by mistake. You want to clean up a job's candidate pipeline. You need to remove multiple candidates from the same job at once. You can: Unassign a single candidate directly from a job's candidate pipeline. Unassign multiple candidates from the same job in bulk. Unassign a candidate from a job through the candidate's profile. Step-by-step instructions to Unassign Candidates Choose the method that fits your situation: unassign one candidate from a job's pipeline, unassign several at once, unassign from a candidate's own profile, or use the steps below if you're on the older interface. Method 1: Unassign a single candidate from a job Open the Job from which the candidate needs to be unassigned. ​ Scroll down to the Candidate Pipeline section. ​ Locate the candidate to be removed from the job. ​ Click on the 3 dots right next to the candidate's name and click on the Unassign Candidate option. When the confirmation dialog appears, review the message and click Unassign to complete the action. The candidate will be removed from the selected job while remaining available in Recruit CRM for assignment to other jobs. Method 2: Unassign multiple candidates from a job Open the required Job . ​ Scroll down to the Candidate Pipeline section and click View All Candidates to open the complete list of all the assigned candidates to the job. Select the candidates to unassign by clicking the checkbox next to each candidate. ​ Click the Unassign Candidate from Job button at the top. ​ Review the confirmation message and click Unassign . The selected candidates will be unassigned from the job simultaneously. Method 3: Unassign a candidate from the Candidate profile Open the required Candidate profile. ​ Scroll down to the Assigned Jobs tab. ​ Locate the job from which the candidate needs to be unassigned. ​ Click the More options (⋮) next to the job. Select Unassign Candidate . ​ Review the confirmation message and click Unassign . The candidate will immediately be removed from that job while remaining associated with any other assigned jobs. Method 4: Unassign Candidate from Jobs in the Old UI 1. Open the job profile and scroll down to the "Candidate Pipeline" section. 2. Hover your cursor over the candidate you wish to unassign. 3. Click on the " X " icon that appears in the top-right corner and hit the " Unassign " button. Note: This method applies to accounts still using the older Recruit CRM interface. Troubleshooting Problem: The candidate still appears in the job’s Candidates pipeline after trying to unassign. Likely cause: The unassign action or confirmation step was not completed. ​ What to check: •Confirm you clicked Unassign (for single unassign) or Confirm (for bulk unassign) in the pop-up. •Refresh the job profile page and check the Candidates pipeline again. ​ Resolution: Repeat the unassign steps and ensure you complete the confirmation in the pop-up, then refresh the page. Problem: Not seeing the Unassign candidate option in the three-dot menu. Likely cause: You may not be in the correct location or looking at the correct menu. ​ What to check: Confirm you are clicking the three dots next to the candidate’s name in the Candidates pipeline, or next to the job’s name in the candidate’s Assigned jobs tab. ​ Resolution: Navigate back to the job profile or candidate profile and follow the steps exactly, making sure you open the correct three-dot menu. FAQs Q1: Does unassigning a candidate from a job delete the candidate? Unassigning a candidate from a job only removes their association with that specific job. It does not delete the candidate’s profile. Q2: Can I unassign multiple candidates from the same job at once? Yes. Use the View all candidates button in the job’s Candidates pipeline, multi-select the candidates, and click Unassign candidate from job . Q3: Can I unassign a candidate from a job using only the candidate's profile? Yes, this is useful if you only know the candidate, not the job. Open the candidate's profile, go to the Assigned Jobs tab, click the three dots next to the job, and choose Unassign Candidate. Q4: Will I see a confirmation before candidates are unassigned? Yes. A confirmation pop-up box appears when unassigning both single and multiple candidates. You must confirm the action for the unassignment to complete. Conclusion: Unassigning candidates from jobs in Recruit CRM is quick and flexible, whether you do it from the job’s Candidates pipeline or directly from the candidate’s profile. t: How to use Direct Apply for Indeed
s: This article will guide you through using Direct Apply when posting jobs to Indeed.
h: Using Direct Apply when posting Jobs to Indeed
How to add your Indeed contract to your job advertising subscription
b: When you post jobs to Indeed through Recruit CRM, you can decide whether candidates apply directly through Direct Apply , or they get redirected to another page to complete the application. Using Direct Apply when posting Jobs to Indeed 1. Go to the job you want to post, and click on Advertise Job .: 2. You can edit the pre-filled name of your campaign, or simply click Continue to keep it as is: 3. On the Added Contracts page, you’ll see all your connected job board accounts. How to add your Indeed contract to your job advertising subscription This is a one-time setup to configure your Indeed contract. ​ To enable posting to Indeed by using your own account and budget with Indeed, please follow these steps: Fill in the linked form . Do not create the contract yourself. VONQ will validate the company information with Indeed. After validation is complete, you will receive your sourceName over email. You can now create the contract and input the obtained sourceName After you create the contract, your connection will be activated, and you can start posting jobs. Please note: In order for your jobs to be visible to potential candidates, once sent from your ATS, must be sponsored from your Indeed company admin portal. You can manage sponsorship directly on your Indeed account, either manually or by setting up rules in your Indeed dashboard. This contract setup is not meant for organic/free advertising on Indeed. 4. Click Add to Campaign under your Indeed contract. 5. You’ll be asked to select or create a " Groups" . These are inbuilt (via VONQ ) and act as folders for job board contracts, allowing only one contract per job board type per group. ​ You’ll see existing options like a Default group and a Test group , or you can create a new group and rename it as needed. Once added, you can save the changes , as well as rename or remove the group . ​ ​ 5. Once you’ve filled in all the details for your posting, scroll down to Application Type . Here, choose Indeed Apply . Finally hit the "Confirm & Post Job" button. Please note If a job is posted to Indeed through Recruit CRM without the “Direct Apply” option selected, candidates will not complete the application directly on Indeed. Instead, they will be redirected to the job application form page, where they can submit their application through your Recruit CRM career page or application form. Any questions you want candidates to answer when applying via Direct Apply must be added to the Job Application Form : When candidates apply, their answers to these questions will be available under the Candidate Questions tab in their profile: That's it, I hope this helps! Feel free to reach out if you have any questions.
