t: How to use Easy Apply for LinkedIn
s: This article will guide you through using Easy Apply when posting jobs to LinkedIn.
h: Using Easy Apply when posting Jobs to LinkedIn
Click here to know how you can connect your LinkedIn Premium Contract
FAQs
If you purchase job slots, will you be able to use Easy Apply?
Will the Easy Apply work for all LinkedIn accounts?
b: When posting jobs to LinkedIn through Recruit CRM, you can choose whether candidates apply directly via Easy Apply or get redirected to another page to complete the application. Using Easy Apply when posting Jobs to LinkedIn 1. Open the job you’d like to post and click on Advertise Job. 2. You edit the pre-filled campaign name if needed, or simply click Continue to move ahead: 3. On the Added Contracts page, you’ll see all your connected job board accounts. Click here to know how you can connect your LinkedIn Premium Contract Note: A Premium Recruiter account is required in order to connect to LinkedIn via the ATS. A Recruiter Lite account will not succeed. You can read more about the differences between the two types of accounts on LinkedIn's page here . Connecting your LinkedIn contract requires a multi-step process that includes logging in to the LinkedIn account that is authorized to use the contract’s job slot inventory. The steps below must be followed exactly in order to properly connect your LinkedIn contract. 1. You must have a LinkedIn Recruiter Account. Go to LinkedIn and log out of that account. 2. Begin typing in the search field for MyContracts within the ATS platform to find the job board you wish to set up. In this case, search for “LinkedIn” (not Limited Listings) and select it from the drop down. Once you select the desired job board, the page will automatically render the instructions and fields that are specific to that job board. 3. To begin the setup/initialization process for LinkedIn, click the GREEN “Initialize Authentication” button. Clicking this button will take you to a LinkedIn login page. 4. Click Sign In and enter your login credentials to log in to LinkedIn. ​ 5. Once logged in to LinkedIn, you must select the contract that you intend to connect to MyContracts. If you have multiple accounts tied to your login, they will be presented here. Be sure that you choose the correct account. 6. After selecting the correct account, you must edit the Job Poster information. Click the Edit button to the right of “Job Poster” and under the name. It may already show the name correctly - you MUST complete this step. 7. After clicking the Edit button, you will need to retype your name and then press Save. This will initialize the connection between your LinkedIn posting account and the MyContracts delivery system. 8. Now return to the MyContracts setup screen. Your LinkedIn Company ID will now appear in the COMPANY ID field. Verify that the Company ID is correct. 8. There are various optional fields that you can now use for managing your contract in MyContracts. Contract Alias allows you to give your contract a name. Contract Expiry allows you to set the date that your contract will expire. Purchase Price allows you to display the cost of the posting. This is informative for users, this does not result in a fee being charged. How Many Credits allows you to set the amount of posting inventory you have with a job board. MyContracts will track and display inventory in real time. This is not reconciled with job boards - if you post a job directly to a job board and not through MyContracts, the credit tracker will not track that. Link to Walkthrough Video Click Add to Campaign under your LinkedIn contract: 4. Fill in the posting details, then scroll down to the Application Type section. Here, choose On Site Apply (Apply Connect). Finally hit the "Confirm & Post Job" button. Any questions you want candidates to answer when applying via Easy Apply must be added to the Job Application Form : When candidates apply, their answers to these questions will be available under the Candidate Questions tab in their profile: FAQs If you purchase job slots, will you be able to use Easy Apply? VONQ provides two types of LinkedIn contracts: LinkedIn Listing and LinkedIn Limited Listing. If you don’t have a LinkedIn Recruiter account, you won’t be able to use job slots, even if purchased separately. Will the Easy Apply work for all LinkedIn accounts? LinkedIn Easy Apply is only available with LinkedIn Recruiter accounts. It won’t work on other types of LinkedIn accounts. That's it, I hope this helps! Feel free to reach out if you have any questions. t: How to use IF & IF/Else conditions in a Recipe on Workflow Automation
s: In this article, we'll delve into the fundamentals of IF and IF/Else conditions in Workflow Automation
h: 1. Conditional statement
2. Actions if a condition is true
3. Actions if a condition is false
1. Contains
2. Starts with
3. Ends with
4. Does not contain
5. Does not start with
b: What are IF and IF/ELSE conditions? IF and IF/ELSE conditions serve as vital components within workflow automation, offering the ability to apply conditional logic and precisely control the flow of a recipe to align with your specific workflow needs. This type of action consists of: 1. Conditional statement Conditional statements in workflow automation serve to evaluate whether a specific condition is true or false. These statements are constructed using data outputs from the preceding steps in the recipe. For instance, consider the following example where the condition checks whether a candidate added has an Email ID. 2. Actions if a condition is true A block of actions that will be executed whenever the condition evaluates to true. 3. Actions if a condition is false A block of actions that will be executed whenever the condition evaluates to false. This is only applicable for IF/ELSE conditions. What are Conditions? Each condition consists of 3 parts: Data Condition Value Conventionally, the data block on the left-hand side represents variable data from your application. For example, Email. We'll walk you through the 14 distinct conditions available for selection. Using trigger conditions as examples, we'll provide detailed insights into how each condition operates within the context of workflow automation. Moreover, we'll demonstrate how you can leverage the power of logical operators such as AND/OR to combine multiple conditions. Please note: Each condition will be valid for different data types. If a condition is attempted to be used for invalid data types, it might prevent the recipe from starting successfully. What are the different Condition types available? 1. Contains This condition evaluates whether the data contains a specific value. This condition can work with any characters, numbers, words, letters, and symbols present in the data. It's important to note that it is case-sensitive, so if case sensitivity isn't a concern, it's advisable to standardize the case (lowercase or capitalize) before comparison. Valid types: This condition is only valid for array and string data types. Examples: 2. Starts with This condition checks if the trigger data string begins with the value. It's important to note that it is case-sensitive, so if case sensitivity isn't a concern, it's advisable to standardize the case (lowercase or capitalize) before comparison. Valid types: This condition is only valid for string data types. Examples: 3. Ends with This condition checks if the trigger data ends with the value. It works with any characters, numbers, words, letters, and symbols. It's important to note that it is case-sensitive, so if case sensitivity isn't a concern, it's advisable to standardize the case (lowercase or capitalize) before comparison. Also, if the field you specify in your condition is left blank in the application you’re using, then no event will be picked up. Valid types: This condition is only valid for string data types. Examples: 4. Does not contain This condition is the opposite of the “ contains" condition. It checks if the trigger data DOES NOT contain the value. It's important to note that it is case-sensitive, so if case sensitivity isn't a concern, it's advisable to standardize the case (lowercase or capitalize) before comparison. Valid types: This condition is only valid for array and string data types. If the field you specify is left blank in the application you are using, the “Doesn’t contain” condition will not count it, and no event will be picked up. This can be circumvented by using the “Is true” or “Is not true” conditions with a string formula, as shown in the Is true section below, or by pairing it with the “Is present” condition. Examples: 5. Does not start with This condition is the opposite of the “Starts with” condition. It checks if the trigger data string DOES NOT begin with the value. It's important to note that it is case-sensitive, so if case sensitivity isn't a concern, it's advisable to standardize the case (lowercase or capitalize) before comparison. Valid types: This condition is only valid for string data types. If the field you specify is left blank in the application you are using, the Don’t Start with condition will not count it, and no event will be picked up. As with the Doesn’t contain trigger condition, this can be circumvented by using a string formula with the Is True formula as shown in the Is True section below, or by pairing it with the Is present condition. Example: 6. Does not end with This condition is the opposite of the Ends with the condition. It checks if the trigger data DOES NOT end with the value. It works with any characters, numbers, words, letters, and symbols. It's important to note that it is case-sensitive, so if case sensitivity isn't a concern, it's advisable to standardize the case (lowercase or capitalize) before comparison. Valid types: This condition is only valid for string data types. If the field you specify is left blank in the application you are using, the Doesn’t end with condition will not count it, and no event will be picked up. Similar to the Doesn’t contain trigger condition, this can be circumvented by using a string formula with the Is True formula as shown in the Is True section below, or by pairing it with the Is Present condition. Examples: 7. Equals This condition checks if the trigger data equals the value. It works with any characters, numbers, words, letters, and symbols. It's important to note that it is case-sensitive, so if case sensitivity isn't a concern, it's advisable to standardize the case (lowercase or capitalize) before comparison. Valid types: This condition is valid for all data types, for example, integers, and floats, dates, and arrays. Example: 8. Does not equal This condition is the opposite of the “ Equal condition” . It checks if the trigger data DOES NOT equal the value. It works with any characters, numbers, words, letters, and symbols. It's important to note that it is case-sensitive, so if case sensitivity isn't a concern, it's advisable to standardize the case (lowercase or capitalize) before comparison. Valid types: This condition is valid for all data types, for example, integers, and floats, dates, and arrays. Examples: 9. Greater than This condition checks if the trigger data is greater than the value. If the value is set to a number, and the trigger data field has a null value, the recipe will raise a trigger error, as computationally, a number cannot be compared with a null value. To resolve this issue, add an is present condition along with the greater than condition. Valid types: This condition is valid for string, integer, and number data types. Examples: 10. Less than This condition checks if the trigger data is less than the value. If the value is set to a number, and the trigger data field has a null value, the recipe will raise a trigger error, as computationally, a number cannot be compared with a null value. To resolve this issue, add an is present condition along with the less than condition. Valid types: This condition is valid for string, integer, and number data types. Example : 11. Is true It can also be used to check that the formula provided in the trigger data input field evaluates to true. For example, you can convert string type datapills via string formulas into conditions that evaluate to a boolean. This condition is only valid for boolean data types. We can use this condition to check against a boolean datapill or check against a formula that evaluates to true or false . Valid types: This condition is only valid for boolean data types. We can use this condition to check against a boolean datapill or check against a formula that evaluates to true or false. Example: 12. Is not true This condition is the opposite of the “is true condition” . It checks that the trigger data “IS NOT” true. It can also be used to check that the formula provided in the trigger data input field evaluates to false. For example, you can convert string type datapills via string formulas into conditions that evaluate to a boolean. Examples: 13. Is present This condition will check the trigger data. If there is data present, the trigger event will be picked up by the recipe. If the input is null or an empty string, the trigger event will not be picked up by the recipe. Valid types: This condition is valid for all data types, for example, integers, and floats, dates, and arrays. Example : 14. Is not present This condition will check the trigger data. If there is data present, the trigger event WILL NOT be picked up by the recipe. If the input is null or an empty string, the trigger event WILL be picked up by the recipe. Valid types: This condition is valid for all data types, for example, integers, and floats, dates, and arrays. Example: If you have questions about these conditions, feel free to reach out to us at support@recruitcrm.io . 😄 Related Articles Basic elements of Workflow Automation in Recruit CRM How

s: Search for candidates within a specific area/location using the Radius Search
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin:
Step-by-step instructions
Step 1 - Enable radius search for your records:
Step 2 - Prepare your list view for radius search:
Step 3 - Run a radius search from Advanced/Filter Search:
Troubleshooting
Conclusion:
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Radius search in Recruit CRM lets you find records (candidates, contacts, companies, or jobs) that are located within a specific distance from a chosen address or location. Use radius search in Recruit CRM when you want to: Find candidates or contacts who live within a certain distance of a client’s office or job location. Identify local talent around a specific landmark, city centre, or address. Filter jobs or companies by physical location proximity. Combine location-based filters with skill, role, or other criteria for targeted sourcing. Before you begin: Please note: This feature is available on all plans. Once radius search is enabled, users who can access those entities (candidates, contacts, companies, jobs) can use radius search on them. The Radius Search feature in Recruit CRM is powered by Google Maps which works well if you have a candidate/contact's address available inside the "Full Address" field of the candidate/contact. The Radius Search relies on accurate geocoding based on the "Full Address" field, which maps records to precise geographical locations. Step-by-step instructions Step 1 - Enable radius search for your records: Only Account Owners, Admins, and users with custom permissions can perform these steps. Go to Admin Settings in your Recruit CRM account. Click on the Account section. Scroll down until you find the Radius Search Settings area. For each entity type where you want to use radius search (such as Candidates, Contacts, Companies, Jobs), switch the toggle to On. Important behaviour: Radius search only works for record types where the radius search toggle is turned on in Admin Settings. Adding a full address through a CSV import does not automatically make those records available for radius search unless the relevant toggle is enabled, allowing the system to geocode the addresses. If you plan to import a large number of records and then run radius searches on them, you should inform us so we can help with the process and ensure geocoding is handled correctly. Step 2 - Prepare your list view for radius search: Navigate to the entity you want to search, for example, Candidates. In the list view, locate the small pencil icon next to the Resume Parser button. Click the pencil icon to edit the visible columns in your list view. In the column selection panel, find and tick the “Full Address” field. Save or apply your column changes so that the Full Address field is visible on the list view. ​ Step 3 - Run a radius search from Advanced/Filter Search: Go to the relevant module, for example, the Candidates page. Click on Advanced Search or Filter Search. In the search/filter panel, locate the Full Address field. In the Radius Search option, start typing the location you want to search around. As you type, review the suggestions that appear under the Full Address field. Select the correct address from the dropdown suggestions. Once the location is selected, choose the radius (for example, 10 km) around that location. Click Apply Filters. Optionally, add other filters along with the radius search, such as: Job title or keywords (e.g., “iOS Developer”). Skills. Status or tags. After setting your radius and additional filters in the Advanced/Filter Search panel, click Apply Filters and Save Search . Give the saved search a clear, descriptive name. Save it so you can quickly re-run the same radius-based search in the future without re-entering the filters. Troubleshooting Problem: Radius search returns fewer records than expected Likely cause: Some records do not have a valid or complete Full Address, or geocoding has not occurred for those records. What to check: Confirm the Full Address field is visible in the list view and check if addresses are present. Verify that addresses are complete enough for Google Maps (e.g., street, city, state/region, postal code, country where applicable). Check if radius search is enabled for that entity type in Admin Settings > Account > Radius Search Settings. Problem: Radius search results do not match the expected area Likely cause: The starting location selected from the suggestions is not the correct one, or the addresses on the records are inaccurate. What to check: Confirm that you chose the correct location from the suggestions in the Full Address field (for example, if multiple cities share the same name). Review sample records in the results to verify that their Full Address values are accurate and correspond to the intended region. Resolution path: Re-run the search and carefully choose the correct address from the dropdown suggestions. Correct inaccurate addresses in the Full Address field on records. Run the radius search again to confirm that the results match the intended geographic area. Conclusion: Radius search in Recruit CRM gives you a powerful, Google Maps–powered way to find candidates, contacts, companies, and jobs based on real-world proximity, as long as your Full Address data is complete and the feature is enabled correctly. t: How to Use Related Emails in Recruit CRM
s: Learn how to view, filter, refresh, and manage emails associated with your Recruit CRM records.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Viewing related emails
Refreshing emails on demand
Managing deleted emails
Emails from deactivated users
Managing stored email data
FAQs
Does Related Emails work with all email providers?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Related Emails lets you view emails associated with a candidate, contact, job, deal, or company directly from the relevant record. You can browse recent and older emails, filter emails, and manually resync your email data. ​ Use Related Emails when you want to: View the latest emails associated with a record Browse or filter your email history Retrieve older emails Manage stored email data as an Account Owner Please note: This feature is released for some of the beta accounts and will be rolled out to all users in the coming weeks. Viewing related emails The Related Emails tab displays the most recent emails associated with the record. To browse the complete email history, click View All . The View All page uses infinite scroll, allowing you to continue browsing older emails as you scroll. ​ You can also use filters to quickly find specific emails based on: From To CC BCC Status such as read or unread Associations Date Range Refreshing emails on demand Each record's Related Emails tab includes a manual Resync option. You can use this to retrieve the latest emails associated with the record whenever needed. Please note At the moment, Related Emails displays emails from the past one year only. After resyncing a record, you must wait 1 hour before you can resync the same record again. Managing deleted emails Deleting or archiving an email in Gmail or Outlook does not remove it from Related Emails. Once an email has been synced to Recruit CRM, it remains available in Related Emails unless you explicitly delete it there or delete the associated parent record, such as a candidate or contact. You can delete either an entire email thread or an individual message directly from Related Emails by clicking on the 3 dots and selecting the Delete option. ​ Delete a thread: Removes the entire email conversation from Related Emails. Delete a message: Removes only the selected message. The rest of the conversation remains available. When a message is deleted from a thread that contains other messages, the conversation displays a "message has been deleted from this conversation" notice in place of the deleted message. When you delete an email from Related Emails, its content is permanently removed, and Recruit CRM does not retain the email itself. A small identifier, such as a unique email ID, is retained so the system can recognize which emails you previously deleted. If you disconnect and later reconnect the same mailbox, you'll be asked whether you want to sync those previously deleted emails back into Related Emails. They will not reappear automatically unless you choose to sync them again. Mailbox vs. Related Emails: The Mailbox reflects the current contents of your connected email account. Deleting or archiving an email in Gmail or Outlook affects your mailbox, but does not remove the email from Related Emails. Emails from deactivated users Emails from a user's mailbox remain available in Related Emails even after the user is deactivated. These emails are clearly labelled to indicate that they belong to a deactivated user . This allows you to continue accessing the email history associated with the record while making it clear that the mailbox owner is no longer active. ​ Managing stored email data Account Owners can manage stored email data for the entire account from Account Management in Admin Settings . This setting is available only to the Account Owner. ​ From here, the Account Owner can: View all users whose mailboxes are currently connected. View users whose mailboxes were previously connected but still have stored email data. Check the last sync time for each user. Search for a specific user. Filter users by status: All Connected Disconnected Deactivated Delete stored email data belonging to disconnected mailboxes or deactivated users. ​ Please note Stored email data cannot be deleted while a mailbox is actively connected. The delete option becomes available only after the mailbox has been disconnected or the user has been deactivated. FAQs Does Related Emails work with all email providers? Yes. Related Emails supports all email providers connected to Recruit CRM . Which entity records support Related Emails? Related Emails is available for candidates, contacts, jobs, deals and companies . What happens to emails when a user is deactivated? The user's stored emails remain visible in Related Emails and are labelled as belonging to a deactivated user . The Account Owner can delete the stored email data if it is no longer required. How far back can I view emails? At the moment, Related Emails displays emails from the past one year only. How often can I resync a record? You can manually resync a record whenever needed, but after a resync, you must wait 1 hour before resyncing that same record again. Does deleting an email from Gmail or Outlook remove it from Related Emails? No. Deleting or archiving an email in Gmail or Outlook does not remove it from Related Emails. You can delete emails directly from Related Emails when you want to remove them from the CRM. Can I delete an email from Related Emails? Yes. You can delete an entire email thread or an individual message directly from Related Emails. When is an email removed from Related Emails? An email is removed when you explicitly delete it from Related Emails or when its associated parent record, such as a candidate or contact, is deleted. Can a previously deleted email be synced again? Yes. If the same mailbox is connected again, Recruit CRM asks whether you want to sync previously deleted emails back into Related Emails. Conclusion Related Emails gives you a centralized and searchable view of the email history associated with your Recruit CRM records. You can browse recent or older conversations, use filters to find specific emails, and resync records to retrieve the latest available emails. Account Owners can also manage stored email data across the account, including data from disconnected and deactivated mailboxes. t: How to use the Global Search Bar in Recruit CRM
s: The Global Search Bar in Recruit CRM helps you quickly find records across your entire database without navigating between different entities.
h: Where to find the Global Search Bar
What can you search for with the Global Search?
How Global Search works
How does the View More Records option work in the Global Search
FAQs
Q. Which fields does Global Search search?
Q. Can I apply additional filters after clicking View More Records in the Global Search results?
Q. Why is the Saved Search option unavailable after clicking View More Records?
b: The Global Search Bar is accessible from every page in the platform, making it the fastest way to locate candidates, contacts, jobs, companies, or deals when you already know a key detail. Where to find the Global Search Bar The Global Search Bar is located at the top of your screen and is available across all the entities. What can you search for with the Global Search? Using the Global Search, you can search for any of the following entities: Candidates Companies Contacts Jobs Deals This grouped view makes it easy to identify the correct record type and navigate directly to it. You can use the Global Search Bar to look up records using key identifiers such as: Name / ID (Candidate, Contact, Company, etc.) Job title / Job ID Email address LinkedIn URL Simply type any of the above details into the search bar, and Recruit CRM will fetch all matching records across entities. How Global Search works Global Search looks for records using a specific set of fields for each entity to return the most relevant matches. The searchable fields include: Entity Searchable Fields Candidates Candidate ID, Name, Phone Number, Email Address, LinkedIn Profile Companies Company ID, Company Name, Website, LinkedIn Profile Contacts Contact ID, Name, Phone Number, Email Address, LinkedIn Profile Jobs Job ID, Job Title, Company Name Deals Deal ID, Deal Name, Company Name Global Search also interprets your search input. For example: Alphanumeric searches (such as names, email addresses, job titles, or LinkedIn URLs) are matched against relevant text-based fields. Numeric searches (such as phone numbers or record IDs) are matched against supported numeric fields. This helps return more relevant results based on the type of information you're searching for. How does the View More Records option work in the Global Search If your search returns more results than can be displayed in the preview of the Global Search results, click View More Records to open the complete search result list for that entity. The expanded results use the same search logic as the initial Global Search, helping ensure the records shown remain relevant and consistent. When you open the full results: The selected Global Search filter is automatically applied to the list page. You can apply additional filters or perform a Boolean Search to further narrow down the results. The Global Search filter remains applied as you navigate between list pages until you remove it using the × icon. While the Global Search filter is active, Saved Search is unavailable. You will have to remove the Global Search filter to enable the Saved Search again in this view. ​ FAQs Q. Which fields does Global Search search? Global Search searches a predefined set of fields for each entity, such as names, IDs, email addresses, phone numbers, LinkedIn profiles, company names, and job titles. Q. Can I apply additional filters after clicking View More Records in the Global Search results? Yes. After opening the full Global Search results, you can apply additional filters or use Boolean Search to further refine the results. Q. Why is the Saved Search option unavailable after clicking View More Records? When you open the expanded search results, a Global Search filter is automatically applied. While the Global Search filter is active, Saved Search is unavailable. You will have to remove the Global Search filter to enable the Saved Search again in this view. I hope this helps! t: How to View Placeholder Values While Sending Emails
s: This article explains how to preview Recruit CRM emails with real placeholder values before sending.
h: What this feature and when to use it?
Before you begin:
Previewing emails inside a candidate or contact profile
Previewing placeholders when sending bulk emails
Troubleshooting
Problem: Placeholders appear blank in preview
FAQs
Is the placeholder preview available in all editors in Recruit CRM?
b: What this feature and when to use it? The email placeholder preview feature helps you preview emails with real placeholder values filled in before you send them. In preview mode, placeholders are highlighted in yellow and show actual values from the selected record so you can check formatting, spot missing data, and confirm the final content for both individual and bulk emails. This works seamlessly for both plain text and HTML emails, so what you see in the preview is exactly what your recipients will receive. You can use this feature when: You are sending personalized one-to-one emails/bulk emails to candidates or contacts and want to confirm how placeholders (like first name) will appear. Before you begin: Note This feature will be available for new rich text editor (powered by Syncfusion ), which is currently in the testing phase and will be available to all users soon. Previewing emails inside a candidate or contact profile 1. Open a candidate or contact profile and click on the Email . ​ 2. Draft your email and add placeholders where needed (e.g., {{First Name}} ​ Click the Preview button in the email editor toolbar to open your email in preview mode. ​ 3. Placeholders will appear in yellow with actual values from the profile, any missing values in the record will show up as blank, and once you’re satisfied with how everything looks, simply close the preview and click Send . ​ Previewing placeholders when sending bulk emails 1. Navigate to the candidate list page or contact list page, depending on who you want to email. 2. Choose the candidate or contact records you want to include in the bulk email. 3. Click the Email button to open the bulk email editor. 4. Compose your email and insert placeholders as you normally would. 5. Click Preview in the editor toolbar to open the email preview. 6. The preview shows how the email will appear for the first recipient in your selected list, with placeholders filled with that recipient’s actual data. 7. Confirm that all placeholders are displaying correctly. Once you are satisfied with the preview, close it and click Send in the bulk email editor to send the email to all selected recipients. Troubleshooting Problem: Placeholders appear blank in preview Likely cause: The corresponding fields are empty in the candidate or contact records. What to check: Open the candidate or contact profile and verify that the fields used in your placeholders (for example, first name) contain data. Resolution: Update the missing data in the record or remove/replace the placeholder in your email content before sending. 🤔FAQs Is the placeholder preview available in all editors in Recruit CRM? The preview feature is available in the new Rich Text Editor powered by Syncfusion, which is currently in testing and will be rolled out to all users. It may not appear in older editors. Conclusion: By previewing placeholder values before sending an email, you can verify that personalization fields are pulling the correct information and avoid sending emails with missing or incorrect data. t: How to view the candidate hiring pipelines for jobs in Recruit CRM?
s: In this article, we'll show you all the places in the system where you can find the candidates assigned to jobs.

Step-by-step instructions

Customize the assigned candidates list

b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The candidate pipeline feature shows all candidates assigned to a specific job in one place. Let's you see candidates by hiring stage, including an Applied stage for applicants. It allows sorting by hiring stage, visibility, candidate name, and last updated date.Provides a View All option for the full assigned candidates list, where you can: Run searches on assigned candidates. Perform bulk actions on multiple candidates. Switch to a Kanban view of the pipeline. Use this feature when you want to: Review all candidates assigned to a specific job and their current stages. See which candidates have applied for a job using the Applied stage. View and manage assigned candidates for all jobs under a company. Check candidate pipelines related to the companies associated with a specific contact. Perform bulk actions, searches, and Kanban view analysis on a job’s assigned candidates. Before you begin Please note: Only users with permission to view a job can see that job’s candidate pipeline. Only users with access to a company profile can use View Candidate Pipeline and View Assigned Candidates for that company. Only users with access to a contact profile can view the jobs related to that contact’s companies and their pipelines. Step-by-step instructions 1. View the candidate pipeline inside a job: Open the Job you want to review in Recruit CRM. On the job profile page, scroll down until you see the candidate pipeline section. Review the list of candidates assigned to the job in this pipeline. To focus on applicants, use the Applied stage to view all candidates who have applied for that position. Use the available sorting options to sort the pipeline by: Hiring stage Visibility Candidate name Updated on (last updated date) To work with the complete assigned candidates list, select the View All button in the candidate pipeline section. In the View All list, you can: Perform bulk actions on multiple candidates assigned to the job. Run searches to filter or locate specific candidates within the job pipeline. Switch to the Kanban view to see candidates organized by hiring stages. From within the pipeline, you can also: Assign candidates to the job . Submit candidates to clients , using the available submission options in the job’s candidate pipeline area. Customize the assigned candidates list While viewing the assigned candidates list (for example, after selecting View All from the job’s candidate pipeline), click on the 'Pencil ico' at the top right corner of the page. Use the field selection interface to pick the fields you want to display as columns on the page. Use the search bar within the field selection to quickly find specific fields by name. Add or remove fields (columns) from the assigned candidates list as needed, including fields like stage date. Rearrange the order of the columns by dragging them up or down in the configuration panel. Save or apply your changes so that the assigned candidates list reflects your chosen columns and column order. ​ 2. View candidate pipelines inside a company Open the Company profile you want to review. On the company profile page, locate the section that lists all jobs associated with the company . Use the available job status filters to filter the list of jobs based on their job statuses. For any listed job, select the View Candidate Pipeline option to see the candidate pipeline for that specific job. To see all candidates assigned to all jobs for this company in one place, select View Assigned Candidates on the company profile. 3. View candidate pipelines inside a contact Open the Contact profile you want to review. On the contact profile page, locate the section showing jobs related to the companies that the contact is associated with . For each job listed, you will see the respective candidate pipeline linked to that job. From this contact profile view, you can perform the same actions available inside the company profile. Use these pipelines to understand which candidates are in process for the jobs connected to the contact’s associated companies. Troubleshooting Problem: The Applied stage shows no candidates, but you know candidates applied Likely cause: Candidates may not be in the Applied stage or have been moved to other stages. What to check: Open the job’s candidate pipeline and review all stages, not just Applied. Resolution: Look through other stages to locate those candidates. FAQs How do I see only candidates who applied to a job? Open the job’s candidate pipeline and use the Applied stage to view all candidates who have applied for that position. Conclusion: By using job, company, and contact profiles, you can quickly view and manage candidate pipelines for all your jobs in Recruit CRM, customize the assigned candidates list, and take action on candidates at scale. t: How to Whitelist an IP address on Recruit CRM?
s: This article explains how to set up IP whitelisting in Recruit CRM so you can control which IP addresses are allowed to access your account.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
Note
Step-by-step instructions
Troubleshooting
Problem: User cannot log in and sees an IP restriction error
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? IP whitelisting in Recruit CRM lets you specify a list of trusted IP addresses that are allowed to access your Recruit CRM account to help protect your organization’s data from unauthorized access. When IP whitelisting is enabled: Recruit CRM checks the IP address of each login attempt. If the IP address is in your trusted list, the user can log in (subject to their normal credentials). If the IP address is not in the trusted list, the user will see an IP restriction error and will not be able to log in. You can use this feature when you want to: Allow logins only from your office network or company VPN. Prevent unauthorized access from unknown or public networks. Strengthen compliance with internal security policies that require IP-based access control. Before you begin: Note This feature is available only on the Business Plan and Enterprise plan. Only the Account Owner and users on the Custom roles with permissions to access 'Account' settings in the Admin Settings have access to this feature. The IP address restriction is applicable for all users except the Account Owner. But if you do not wish to have the IP restriction for certain users on your team, you can create a custom role and disable the IP Restriction for just the users on this role. You can create the custom roles from Admin Settings > Users > Roles & Permissions . Here is a quick article on creating custom roles: Creating Teams & User Roles in Recruit CRM . Step-by-step instructions To whitelist an IP address: 1. Go to Admin Settings and open Account under Account Management. 2. On the Account Management page, scroll down until you see the IP Whitelisting section and you'll see the box where you can add the trusted IP addresses. The system will automatically show your current IP address there, so you can easily add it to your trusted list. 3. You can enter the trusted IP addresses in the box and once complete, click outside the text box to save the IP restriction settings. After you have set this up, users will be restricted from logging in from IP addresses that have not been whitelisted. If a user tries to log in, from an IP address that is not marked as trusted, they will get the following error: Troubleshooting Problem: User cannot log in and sees an IP restriction error Likely cause : The user is trying to access Recruit CRM from an IP address that is not whitelisted. What to check : Confirm the user’s current IP address (ask them to share their IP). Compare the user’s IP address with the list of trusted IP addresses in Admin Settings > Account > IP Whitelisting. Check whether the user is assigned to a custom role with IP restriction disabled. Resolution : Add the user’s IP address to the trusted IP list, or Ask the user to connect via a whitelisted network (for example, office or VPN), or Assign the user to a custom role where IP restriction is disabled, if appropriate. Conclusion: IP whitelisting in Recruit CRM helps control which IP addresses are allowed to access your account to improve data security and manage login access for your teams. Hope this helps! t: Import Mapping Template in Recruit CRM
s: This article explains how to use import mapping templates in Recruit CRM to map CSV or XLS columns to Recruit CRM fields.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
Save a new mapping template
Delete or edit mapping templates
Key points to note for mapping!
FAQs
Conclusion:
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Import mapping templates let you save the way you map your CSV or XLS columns to Recruit CRM fields during an import. Once saved, you can apply the same template to future imports so the fields are mapped automatically. This removes the need to repeat the manual mapping process for files with the same structure. You can use this when: You frequently import CSV or XLS files with the same column structure. You want to avoid manually mapping each column to a Recruit CRM field on every import. You need consistent, repeatable field mapping across multiple imports. You want to reduce mapping mistakes during candidate data imports. Before you begin Ensure you have a CSV or XLS file ready to upload. Confirm that your file has clear column names that can be used for mapping. Be aware that if you choose the option to include the first header row of the CSV or XLS file in a way that removes column names for mapping, you will not be able to save a template. Only the creator of a mapping template can edit or delete that template. 🎯 Save a new mapping template Upload your CSV or XLS file and proceed to the field mapping stage of the import. ​ Map each column in your file to the correct Recruit CRM field. ​ After completing the mapping process, click the Save Mapping button to store your current field mappings as a template. ​ Confirm the save action as prompted so that the mapping fields are stored as a template. You can also choose to share it with your teammates by enabling the Share with all teammates toggle. ​ This lets you select the same mapping each time you upload a similar file, eliminating the need to manually map fields every time. ✏️ Delete or edit mapping templates Hover your cursor over the template you want to manage. ​ When you hover, you will see options to edit or delete the template. ​ Click the pencil icon to edit the existing mapping template. ​ Click the trash icon to delete the template if you no longer need it. ​ Only the creator of a template can delete or edit that template. ​ 🔑 Key points to note for mapping! If there are columns in your data sheet that you do not wish to import, you can skip them by selecting Don’t import this column from the dropdown for that column. Once a field is mapped, it will no longer be available in the dropdown for mapping again. Make sure the field type in Recruit CRM matches the type of value in the column you are mapping. For example, if you are trying to map the column “Work Experience”, you need to find a field that accepts numeric values viz the Number field. If you’ve mapped it to a field that is a text field, then the values for the column Work Experience will not be imported to Recruit CRM. If a column in your spreadsheet does not match any existing field in Recruit CRM, you will need to create a custom field before importing so that the data can be stored correctly. FAQs Do I need to create a mapping template every time I import a file? No. You only need to create a template once for each file structure. After that, you can select the saved template on future imports with the same column layout. What happens if I change the column names in my CSV or XLS file? If column names change, the template may no longer correctly identify which columns to map, and some fields may not map as expected. Keep your column names consistent when reusing templates. Conclusion: Using import mapping templates in Recruit CRM lets you save time and maintain consistent, accurate data imports by reusing your field mappings across similar CSV or XLS files. If you have any questions or need further help with mapping templates, please reach out to the support team via chat. b: What this feature does and when to use it? The CV Library integration lets Recruit CRM automatically post jobs you add in Recruit CRM to your CV Library account. b: . The first step is to make sure your account is verified with Recruit CRM from the account management settings. Here, fill in all the account information and click on "Verify Account". In case, the auto-verification fails, you have the option to send a manual request to our team. Once the account is verified, you will receive an in-app notification and email notification that your account is enabled for job postings on Indeed. In case you update any account information, you will have to verify the account again. 2. Making sure your jobs meet Indeed's publishing criteria Please note that users on Recruit CRM's free plan can not integrate with Indeed. Criteria to push the jobs to the XML feed 1. The job application form should be enabled; 2. The Updated On date should be within the last 30 days; 3. All the fields where you see the message "Required To Post On Partner Job Boards" (City, State, Country, Maximum Salary, Job Description, Currency, Salary Type) need to have a value; Adding city, state, country, and postal code fields is mandatory only if the job type is hybrid or onsite. If it's remote it's not mandatory. 4. 'Note for candidates' should be filled in (only if the Job Description is uploaded as a file); 5. The "Post On Job Boards" option should be selected inside Admin Settings >> Job Custom Fields ; 6. The job status should not be 'closed', 'on hold' or 'canceled'; 7. Jobs posted on Indeed should be EEO complaint. Discrimination on the basis of age, sex, marital status, religion, nationality, sexual orientation, or disability is not tolerated. Discrimination based on language is not permitted either. If point 7 is not complied with, it could result in a ban of your with Indeed. 8. The job description should be well-formed with at least 300 characters. Emojis are not allowed in the description and the title. 9. You need to sponsor your jobs on Indeed. Free posting is not allowed as per the Indeed guidelines. Points to note Recruit CRM can take action against accounts if any spam or fraudulent job is posted to Indeed. Only the job types full-time and part-time are mapped to the Indeed field. Experience is considered as minimum experience. For instance, if you add 5 years on Recruit CRM, on Indeed it will reflect as 5+ years. Salary description on Indeed is based on how salary fields are added: If Max salary = Min Salary, the salary field will have a single value (e.g., "Pay: $15 per hour"). If Max salary > Min salary, the salary field will have a range between two amounts (e.g., "Pay: $10-15 per hour"). If only Min salary is present, the salary field will have “from” (e.g., "Pay: From $10 per hour"). if only Max salary is present, the salary field will have “up to” (e.g., "Pay: up to $10 per hour"). If you don't want to share salary information this field can be left blank and salary will not appear on the XML feed. 3. Select "Indeed" under the XML Feeds section You have the ability to selectively push job postings to specific XML feeds. While adding/editing a job, you'll get an option to select the XML feeds from both the default and custom XML feeds that you have built, provided the 'Post on Job Board' option is enabled from the Job Fields settings . While creating a new job or editing an existing one, make sure you select "Indeed" in the XML Feeds section to get your jobs posted on the correct XML Feed. ​ By selecting the appropriate XML feeds, you can ensure that your jobs reach the intended audience through the most relevant job boards. You also have the option to preselect the XML feeds in the Build Job Feed XML page. This means the XML Feed will automatically be selected for all the new jobs created. ​ If you don't want a job to be automatically posted on the Indeed XML Feed you can simply disable the preselection on the Build Job Feed XML or uncheck the XML Feed while creating/editing the job: The jobs will be indexed to Indeed and other external boards only if the requirements given above are met. After fulfilling the necessary criteria, the jobs will be visible on the Indeed XML Feed. How to integrate with Indeed The next step is to copy and integrate the XML Feed URL with Indeed. 1. To access the XML feed, go to Admin Settings >>>> Build Job Feed XML . ​ 2. Click on the XML Feed URL for Indeed. ​ 3. You'll be redirected to a new page with the XML Feed page source. Copy the URL and submit it to your Indeed account manager. First, an Indeed account must be created for the integration to work. If you have a paid Indeed account, you'll have a dedicated account manager and can share the XML feed with them directly. How to verify which jobs are being pushed to the Indeed XML Feed You can check the list of jobs being pushed to Indeed's XML Feed by going to Admin Settings >>>>>> Build Job Feed XML . Here you can click on "View Listed Jobs" to get a list of all the jobs in your account that currently meet the required criteria: You can also run an Advanced Search inside the Jobs List Page to see all the jobs that have been posted on Indeed (including old jobs that are no longer being pushed to the XML feed). ​ If one of your jobs is not on the list, one of the necessary criteria is not being met. Applicants will be auto-directed to your Recruit CRM Job Application forms and they will be directly added to your Recruit CRM database. How will you get applications for the jobs? When a candidate fills out the application form, you'll be notified in Recruit CRM. You can see all the website applicants on the candidate list page . You can also specifically look for Indeed applicant candidates in your database by enabling the Source field in Candidate Fields : ​ With the Source field, you'll be able to track the origin of how the candidate was added to the system. If the candidate applies externally, the name of the job board will be mentioned in the field: ​ You can even run an Advanced Search on the Source field: Feel free to reach out if you have any questions! t: Integrating Kynzo and Recruit CRM
s: Bring saved target customer contacts into Kynzo so LinkedIn™ engagement becomes part of a repeatable business development workflow.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How the Integration Works
Who Is This Integration For?
How to Set Up the Integration
Step 1: Install the Kynzo Chrome Extension
Step 2: Open Kynzo and Sign In
Step 3: Connect Your Recruit CRM Account
Step 4: Allow Initial Sync
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Recruit CRM and Kynzo integration helps you turn the client and prospect contacts already stored in Recruit CRM into a structured LinkedIn business development workflow. Instead of manually searching LinkedIn for contacts, monitoring activity across multiple accounts, and trying to remember who to engage with, Kynzo automatically syncs your target customer contacts from Recruit CRM and brings their LinkedIn activity into a centralized feed. This helps you stay visible to the right people, engage at the right time, and build stronger professional relationships through meaningful interactions. Use this integration when: • You use Recruit CRM to manage client and prospect relationships. • You use LinkedIn as part of your business development strategy. • You want an easier way to stay engaged with target accounts and hiring managers. • You want to reduce the manual effort involved in monitoring LinkedIn activity. • You want a consistent and repeatable approach to relationship building across your team. 🔄 How the Integration Works Recruit CRM remains the source of truth for your client and prospect data, while Kynzo uses that information to power LinkedIn engagement workflows through a daily one-way sync. Once your contacts are synced, Kynzo helps you: ​ 1. Stay Updated on Relevant LinkedIn Activity: Kynzo automatically surfaces posts from your saved contacts in a single feed, making it easier to: • Monitor activity from clients, prospects, and hiring managers. • Discover engagement opportunities as they happen. • Avoid manually searching LinkedIn for updates. • Engage while conversations are still relevant and active. ​ 2. Create Personalized Engagement Faster: Kynzo helps you draft relevant LinkedIn comments using AI assistance. Each suggested comment is based on the content of the original post and can be edited to match your preferred tone and communication style. All comments are reviewed and approved by you before being published, ensuring that engagement remains authentic and fully under your control. 3. Identify Engagement Opportunities: Kynzo tracks engagement signals such as profile visits, post likes, and comment interactions. These insights can help you identify when a contact is becoming more familiar with your brand and when it may be a good time to start or continue a conversation. Who Is This Integration For? This integration is ideal for teams that use Recruit CRM to manage client and prospect relationships and want to extend those relationships into LinkedIn. It is particularly useful for organizations looking to increase visibility with target accounts, strengthen business development efforts, and create a more consistent approach to LinkedIn engagement across their team. 🛠️ How to Set Up the Integration Setting up the integration only takes a few minutes. Here is a step-by-step instruction to help you set it up - Step 1: Install the Kynzo Chrome Extension Install the Kynzo Chrome Extension from the Chrome Web Store. Kynzo operates directly within LinkedIn through this extension. ​ Step 2: Open Kynzo and Sign In Once the extension has been installed, open LinkedIn and click on the Kynzo Extension from your browser toolbar. This will open the Kynzo window, where you can either: Log in if you already have a Kynzo account, or Sign up for a 14-day free trial on Kynzo if you're a new user . 📌 No credit card details are required to start the free trial on Kynzo. ​ Step 3: Connect Your Recruit CRM Account To connect Recruit CRM with Kynzo, navigate to the Integrations tab from the left-hand panel within Kynzo. Locate Recruit CRM in the list of available integrations and click Connect . You will then be prompted to enter your Recruit CRM API Key . Copy your API key from Recruit CRM and paste it into the provided field, then click Connect to complete the setup. ​ Step 4: Allow Initial Sync After connecting, Kynzo will begin syncing your target customer contacts from Recruit CRM. Step 5: Start Engaging Once the initial sync is complete, your customer feed will begin populating with LinkedIn activity from your synced contacts. 📌 Tip: Start by testing the workflow with one or two target accounts before introducing it across your entire team. ​ For more information about setting up and using the Recruit CRM + Kynzo integration, click here. ❓ FAQs Do I need to rebuild my contact lists inside Kynzo? No. Kynzo automatically imports your target customer contacts from Recruit CRM, so there is no need to recreate lists manually. Can Kynzo automatically post comments? No. Kynzo never auto-posts comments, sends automated direct messages, or publishes content on your behalf. All AI-generated comments must be reviewed and approved by the recruiter before they are posted. Does the integration require technical setup? No. Most recruiters can complete setup in under ten minutes using the Chrome extension and guided setup process. What happens when new contacts are added to Recruit CRM? New contacts are automatically included during the next daily sync and will appear in your Kynzo feed without any manual action. What information does Kynzo sync from Recruit CRM? Kynzo performs a daily, one-way sync from Recruit CRM to Kynzo . The integration syncs: • Target customer contacts • Associated LinkedIn profile URLs This allows Kynzo to surface relevant LinkedIn activity for those contacts. The integration does not sync: • Candidate records • Candidate LinkedIn profiles • Any candidate-related data 📌 Important: Only client and prospect contacts are imported into Kynzo. Recruit CRM remains the source of truth, and no data is synced back from Kynzo into Recruit CRM. Conclusion: The Recruit CRM and Kynzo integration helps recruitment teams transform existing CRM contacts into an active LinkedIn engagement workflow. By automatically syncing target customer contacts, surfacing relevant LinkedIn activity, and supporting personalized engagement, Kynzo enables recruiters to build stronger prospect relationships while reducing manual effort. b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM makes it easy to connect your Squarespace website to your Recruit CRM account, allowing you to display your live job listings directly on your website. Candidates who apply through the embedded job are automatically added to your Recruit CRM database, eliminating the need to manually manage applications or update job postings in multiple places. Use this feature when: • You manage your website on Squarespace and want to display live job openings from Recruit CRM. • You want candidates applying through your website to be added directly to your Recruit CRM database. • You want Recruit CRM to remain your single source of truth for managing jobs while using Squarespace as your public-facing careers site. • You prefer a simple, copy-and-paste integration using Recruit CRM's website integration code snippet. Embed Your Recruit CRM Job Board into Squarespace If you're managing your website using Squarespace, the steps below will help you do that- 1. Log in to your Squarespace account and open the website where you want to display your Recruit CRM jobs. 2. From the left-hand panel, click Pages , then click the + icon to create a new page. ​ 3. Select Blank Page , enter a name for the page (for example, Jobs Page ), and open it in the page editor. ​ 4. Click Add Section , then select Add Blank to insert a blank section on the page. 5. Inside the blank section, click Add Block , scroll through the available options, and select Markdown . And then click Edit to open the Markdown block. 6. In Recruit CRM, navigate to Admin Settings → Public Job Page Settings → Job Integration . ​ 7. Under Website Integration , click Copy to copy the integration code snippet. 8. Return to your Squarespace page and paste the copied code into the Markdown block. Resize or reposition the Markdown block as needed to match your preferred page layout. 9. Click Save to publish your changes. Once saved, your Recruit CRM public job board will appear on your Squarespace page, and candidates who apply through it will be added directly to your Recruit CRM database P.S. You can choose if you want to add a banner either from Squarespace OR from Recruit CRM. Troubleshooting Problem: The job board appears misaligned or too small/large on the page. Likely cause: The Markdown block or section size has not been adjusted. ​ What to check: Verify the position and size of the Markdown block within the blank section. ​ Resolution: Drag and arrange the box on your page and resize it within Squarespace until it fits your design. FAQs Q1. Which block should I use in Squarespace to add the Recruit CRM job board? Use a Markdown block inside a blank section on your Squarespace page, then paste the Recruit CRM Website Integration code into that block. Q2. Do applications from the Squarespace Jobs Page go into Recruit CRM automatically? Yes. When candidates apply from your website through the embedded Recruit CRM job board, they are added directly to your Recruit CRM database. Q3. Can I resize or move the embedded job board on my page? Yes. After adding the Markdown block and pasting the code, you can drag and arrange the box and adjust its size within Squarespace. Conclusion: By following these steps, you can integrate your Recruit CRM career page into a Squarespace Jobs Page so that candidates apply directly into your Recruit CRM database, while your website continues to serve as the main destination for job seekers. b: The Broadbean integration is available only to our business plan users. You'll need an active Broadbean account for this. RecruitCRM has integrated with Broadbean , a leading job distribution and candidate-sourcing platform, to make job posting easier for you! With a few simple steps, you can integrate your Broadbean account with Recruit CRM and seamlessly post job listings to multiple job boards. This integration also allows you to manage candidate applications directly from RecruitCRM. URL for Broadbean: Broadbean will ask you to share an endpoint URL. You can share this URL through email: https://jobboard.recruitcrm.io/v1/broadbean/candidates How to integrate Recruit CRM with Broadbean 1. Go to Admin Settings > External Job Boards Please note that only the account owner, Admins, or users with a custom role can access the External Job Boards page. For the first access, the Account Owner will first need to permit users to connect their individual Broadbean accounts or add their ADC username to accounts connected by the Account Owner. 2. Click on "Connect" and enter your Account Alias (the name of your account). You will also need to type your Client ID, Secret, and ADC username, which are registered with your Broadbean account. You can connect multiple accounts using the Broadbean Integration. 3. After this, select the Broadbean Account Type: Email Apply and Direct Apply are account configurations that are done by Broadbean based on the client's preferences. Email Apply: if the user has a Broadbean account with an email apply configuration, the candidate that applies to the posted jobs will first be added to Broadbean, and then they will be sent to Recruit CRM. Users can also configure their candidate retrieval settings inside Recruit CRM. Direct Apply: if the user has a Broadbean account with a direct apply configuration, the candidate that applies to the posted jobs will directly be added to their Recruit CRM's database through the Recruit CRM external job application page. 4. Select the desired Candidate Retrieval Settings: Retrieve All Candidates & move them to applied stage : all the candidates will be retrieved from Broadbean and added to Recruit CRM's database in the "Applied" hiring stage. Flag-based retrieval : Broadbean offers 3 flags inside their system (Green//Suitable; Yellow/Maybe Suitable; Red/Unsuitable) and you can decide whether to add the candidate to the database (yellow), move them to the Applied stage (green) or not retrieve this candidate at all (red). 5. After choosing your preferred settings, just hit "Add Account". The system will prompt you with an "Account Added Successfully" message. You can add another account if necessary. By clicking on the amount of accounts connected, you'll see a list of your accounts, on which you can make editions or delete them: Posting Jobs from Recruit CRM on Broadbean To post your job on Broadbean, you have to go through the following steps: 1. Go to the job that you want to post on Broadbean (if you have yet to create a job, you can refer to this article for creating jobs inside Recruit CRM ) Conditions for a job to be posted on Broadbean Some fields must be populated for your job to be posted on Broadbean. The required fields are: Title Location Job Type Job Description Industry Sector 2. Click on the three dots and select the "Post Job External Job Board" option. 3. Select the desired account and click on "Post". 4. Choose the desired Job Boards and review the details. After that, you can preview and send your advert. 5. Click on "View Responses" to check your applicants. 6. You can also check your Job Posting Status, edit and repost it, and delete your active posts. FAQs on Broadbean Integration Can multiple Broadbean accounts be connected to RecruitCRM? Multiple users can connect multiple accounts if allowed by the Account Owner. What does ADC Username stand for? ADC Username stands for Ad Courier Username. What is Veritone? Broadbean was recently acquired by Veritone resulting in a rebranding. Since it's a recent change, we kept the name Broadbean to avoid confusion. The interface allows you to post jobs to multiple boards, directly to your company website, and across all your social media networks at the same time. Before you begin: You must be on the Recruit CRM Business plan or Enterprise plan to use the LogicMelon integration. You need an active LogicMelon account. You must have your LogicMelon username, password, and API key available. Only the Account Owner, Admin and users on the custom role with access to the ' External Job Boards' section in Recruit CRM can access and connect the LogicMelon account. How to integrate Recruit CRM with LogicMelon 1. Go to Admin Settings > External Job Boards . 2. Find LogicMelon in the list and click Connect next to it. 3. Enter the username and password associated with your LogicMelon account, then enter your LogicMelon API key and click Save. 4. After saving, your Recruit CRM account is successfully integrated with your LogicMelon account. Posting Jobs from Recruit CRM on LogicMelon: To post your job on LogicMelon, you have to go through the following steps: 1. Go to the Job in Recruit CRM that you want to post on LogicMelon. If you do not yet have a job created, create a new job first, then open that job. 2. Inside the job, click on the Post on External Job Board button. 3. On the next screen, click the green Post button next to LogicMelon. This opens LogicMelon in an iframe within Recruit CRM, where you must select your LogicMelon account name and fill out all required fields for the posting. 4. When all required fields are completed, click the Finish button in the LogicMelon iframe. Your job post will be successfully sent from Recruit CRM to LogicMelon. How to close jobs on LogicMelon job boards while updating the job status and archiving a job You can close a job on the Logicmelon Job Board while updating its status or archiving it. 1. When changing the status of a job in Recruit CRM, look for the Close the Job on Job Board checkbox. 2. This checkbox is checked by default, and this will close the job campaigns and postings on LogicMelon and Broadbean once the checkbox is selected. 3. Click Submit to save the changes. Conditions for a job to be posted on job boards While creating the job or while editing it, please populate all the required fields. If all the required fields are not populated, the job won't be posted to any job board. The required fields are: Job Description Country Note for Candidates (only when the Job Description is uploaded as a file) City Salary Type Maximum Salary State Currency Other than these, also make sure that the following conditions are satisfied so the job will be added to the feed: Job status should be "Open" The Updated On date should be within 30 days The "Post On Job Boards" option should also be selected inside Admin Settings >> Job Fields If the job satisfies all the above requirements, it gets added to the feed and published on the job board. Checking the status of your LogicMelon job post You can also keep a tab on the status of the job post from Recruit CRM itself. 1. Go to the Job that you posted in Logic Melon through Recruit CRM, click on the three dots, and select "Post Job" 2. Here, you will find if the job has been posted to LogicMelon and you can check the status of the job by clicking on the arrow next to the " Job posting status". Troubleshooting Problem: The job is not appearing on any job board after posting. Likely cause: One or more required job fields are missing. ​ What to check: Confirm that Job Description, City, State, Country, Salary Type, Currency, Note for Candidates (if the job description is uploaded as a file), and Maximum Salary are all populated. Check that the job status is Open and the Updated On date is within 30 days. Verify that the Post on Job Boards option is enabled in Admin Settings → Job Fields. Resolution: Fill in all required fields, ensure the job meets the status and date conditions, confirm the Post on Job Boards option is selected, then attempt to post again. Problem: You cannot see the LogicMelon connection option in Admin Settings. Likely cause: You may not have the required role or plan. ​ What to check: Confirm you are an Admin or Account Owner or on a custom role with access to External Job Boards section in Recruit CRM. Confirm your account is on the business plan or above. ​ Resolution: Ask the Account Owner to set up the integration or adjust your role and plan as needed. FAQs Which Recruit CRM plan supports the LogicMelon integration? The LogicMelon integration is available only for business plan users and above. Do I need a LogicMelon account to use this integration? Yes, you must have an active LogicMelon account, along with your LogicMelon username, password, and API key. Conclusion: Once the integration is set up, you can seamlessly publish jobs from Recruit CRM to LogicMelon. If you need further help with any step, please feel free to reach out to the support team via our chatbot. t: Integrating your Recruit CRM "Jobs Page" with Wix
s: This article will show you how you can integrate your Recruit CRM Job Board With Your Wix Powered Website
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin:
Step-by-step instructions
Get the Recruit CRM Website Integration link:
Embed the Recruit CRM job board in Wix
Adjust layout and appearance in Wix
Troubleshooting
Conclusion:
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The Recruit CRM Website Integration feature provides an HTML embed option with a source link for your public job page. When you add this link into a Wix “Embed a Widget” block as a website address, your Recruit CRM jobs appears within your Wix jobs page. This lets candidates view and apply for jobs directly on your site, while Recruit CRM continues to handle the job listings and applications in the background. Before you begin: You need access to your Wix account and permission to edit the website. You need access to your Recruit CRM account and Admin Settings. You should already have a jobs page created in Wix, or be ready to create one. You will use the Website Integration option from Recruit CRM and embed it as a widget in Wix. Step-by-step instructions Log in to your Wix account. ​ On the top, beside your website name, click the Site Actions dropdown and select Edit Site to open the website builder. ​ In the website builder, click the Pages tab (the first tab on the left-hand side). ​ Select the jobs page you have already created. ​ If you do not yet have a jobs page, create a new page that will be used to display your jobs. Get the Recruit CRM Website Integration link: Open a new browser window or tab and log in to your Recruit CRM account. ​ Go to Admin Settings . ​ Scroll down and click Public Job Page Settings . ​ Click the Job Page Integration tab. ​ Under Option 2 - Website Integration , locate the HTML code that is provided. From this HTML code, select only the source link (the URL), and not the entire HTML code. ​ Please ensure you do not select the inverted quotes but only the source link. (Click on the above image and zoom in to see what has been selected in blue as that is the only text you need to copy) Embed the Recruit CRM job board in Wix Go back to your Wix website editor page. ​ In the left-hand panel, click the + Add icon (the third icon on the left). ​ Select Embed , then click Embed a Widget . ​ Click into the Enter Code text box. ​ Switch to the Website Address radio button so that Wix expects a URL instead of raw code. ​ Paste the source link you copied from Recruit CRM into the text box as the website address. ​ Close the text box to return to the page layout. Adjust layout and appearance in Wix Click on the HTML page element you just added on your Wix page. ​ Click the Stretch button that appears above the element. ​ Turn on the toggle switch labeled Stretch to Full Width . ​ Drag the page box to the top of your jobs page and adjust its size and position until the appearance matches your design preferences. ​ Click the Preview button in Wix to see how the jobs page will look before publishing. ​ If needed, go back from Preview, make further layout or appearance adjustments, and then publish your site once you are satisfied. Troubleshooting Problem: The job does not appear on the Wix page. Likely cause: The full HTML code was pasted instead of only the source link, or the wrong option was selected in Wix. What to check: Confirm you selected only the source link from the HTML code in Recruit CRM. Check that you selected the Website Address radio button (not a raw code option) in the Wix “Enter Code” area. Resolution: Copy just the URL from the Website Integration option again, ensure the inverted quotes are not included, and paste it into the Website Address field in Wix. Problem: Changes in Recruit CRM are not visible on the Wix preview. Likely cause: The Wix preview may be cached or not refreshed. What to check: Refresh the Wix preview after saving changes in Recruit CRM. Ensure the correct jobs page is being previewed in Wix. Resolution: Save updates in Recruit CRM, refresh the Wix editor or preview, and re-check the embedded page. Conclusion: Integrating your Recruit CRM job board with your Wix website allows you to showcase your latest job openings on a dedicated careers page while keeping all applications centralized in Recruit CRM. Once the Website Integration link is embedded, your job listings stay synchronized with Recruit CRM, giving candidates a seamless application experience directly from your website. Before publishing, preview the page in Wix to confirm the jobs displays correctly and adjust the layout as needed for the best user experience.
