t: Invite your Clients to the Hiring Manager Portal
s: This article will help you invite clients to the Hiring Manager Portal (HMP), manage their portal access, and understand the different invitation methods available.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Invite clients to the Hiring Manager Portal
1. Invite a client from the Contact Details page
2. Invite multiple clients from the Company Details page
Who appears in the dropdown?
3. Invite clients from the Hiring Manager Portal
Share Jobs with Your Hiring Manager
Disable a client's portal access
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Hiring Manager Portal (HMP) allows your clients to securely access the jobs, candidate pipelines, and timesheets you've shared with them. You can invite clients directly from Recruit CRM or from within the Hiring Manager Portal itself. This feature is useful when you want to: Invite a single client to the Hiring Manager Portal. Invite multiple contacts from the same company at once. Send invitations directly from the Hiring Manager Portal. Manage and revoke client portal access. Share recruitment updates securely with your clients. Please note: There are no email domain restrictions when inviting clients. Invitations can be sent to any valid email address, including personal email providers such as Gmail or Rediffmail. Invite clients to the Hiring Manager Portal Recruit CRM offers three different ways to invite clients to the Hiring Manager Portal. 1. Invite a client from the Contact Details page Use this method when you want to invite a single contact. Open the required Contact record. Click the three-dot menu and select Enable Portal . Confirm the action when prompted. An invitation email will be sent to the contact. Email validation: Before sending the invitation, Recruit CRM validates the contact's email address. If no email address is available, you'll be prompted to add one before continuing. If the email address is already associated with an existing Hiring Manager Portal account (either within your Recruit CRM account or another agency's account), the invitation cannot be sent. Once the invitation is sent, an Invite Sent tag appears on the contact. After the client completes the signup process, the tag automatically changes to Client Portal Enabled . You can hover over the tag to see who sent the invitation and when. Please Note: When enabling portal access for the first time, if the contact is associated with multiple companies, you'll be prompted to choose the company for which you'd like to enable portal access. The client will then be linked to that company's Hiring Manager Portal. 2. Invite multiple clients from the Company Details page Use this method when you want to invite several contacts from the same company. Open the required Company record. Click the three-dot me nu and select Enable Portal . A dropdown will appear listing the contacts in that company who can still be invited. Select the contacts you want to invite. Who appears in the dropdown? Only contacts who have not yet been invited or have not yet activated their portal account are available for selection. Contacts who already have an invitation pending, an active portal account, or belong to a subsidiary or group company won't appear in the list. If every eligible contact already has portal access, the Enable Portal option will be disabled, along with a tooltip explaining why. Review any validation messages and make the required corrections before sending the invitations. Each selected contact will receive a separate email at their respective email address. 3. Invite clients from the Hiring Manager Portal Sign in to the Hiring Manager Portal and click the Hiring Managers icon from the left navigation menu. Click Invite Hiring Manager and enter the client's email address, and click Send Invite . Pro Tip: Use Add Another Email to invite multiple users at the same time. The client will receive an invitation email containing a signup link. After clicking the link, the client can complete the signup process using the same email address that received the invitation. Share Jobs with Your Hiring Manager Share jobs with your Hiring Managers through the HMP so they can review candidates and collaborate with your team. Learn How to Share Jobs with Your Hiring Manager Disable a client's portal access Navigate to the contact's details page. Click on the three-dot menu or on the "client Portal Enabled" tag and select the option to disable the portal. A warning modal will appear. Once confirmed, an email is sent to the client, the portal tag is updated across all records associated with that email, and the contact can no longer log in. Please note: If you enable portal access again later, a new invitation email will automatically be sent to the client. Troubleshooting Problem: The Enable Portal option is disabled for a company. Likely Cause: All eligible contacts within the company already have invitations pending or active portal accounts. What to Check: Review the contacts associated with the company. Resolution: No further invitations are required unless you add a new eligible contact. FAQs 1. How many times can I send an invite to the same contact? You can send the invite up to 3 times a day from the Contact Details page. If you change the contact's email, the limit resets and the 'Invite Sent' tag is removed. 2. Another agency has the same contact. What happens? Whichever agency successfully sends the invite first, owns the portal relationship for that email. If you try to invite a contact whose email already has a portal account on another agency, you will see a message that a portal account already exists, and the invite will not be sent. 3. Two of my contact records have the same email. Will both update? Yes. When the client signs up, all contact records with that email address are linked to the same portal account and will show the 'Client Portal Enabled' tag. 4. I changed a contact's email after the invite was sent but before they signed up. What happens? The client can still sign up using the original invite link, but because the email on the record no longer matches, the 'Client Portal Enabled' tag will not appear on the updated record, and timesheets for that contact will no longer be visible. 5. Will the client see who invited them? The sender's name and timestamp are visible to your team on hover. Conclusion The Hiring Manager Portal makes it easy to collaborate with your clients by giving them secure access to jobs, candidate pipelines, and timesheets you've chosen to share. Whether you're inviting a single contact, multiple contacts, or managing portal access, Recruit CRM provides flexible options to simplify client collaboration. Click Invite Teammates in the top-right corner. Enter the user's email address and select the appropriate role. If required, select an existing team to add the user to. Adding a user to a team during the invitation process is optional. Click Send Invitation . The invited user will receive an email containing a link to join your Recruit CRM account. Bulk invite multiple teammates If you need to invite multiple users at once, you can use the bulk invite option. Upload a CSV or XLS file containing the users' email addresses. Map the email column from the uploaded file. Complete the import to send invitations to all users in the file. This option helps streamline onboarding when adding multiple teammates to your account. Different User Roles in Recruit CRM A user's role determines the records, activities, and administrative features they can access within Recruit CRM 1. Admin Admins have broad access across the account. They can create and delete candidates, companies, contacts, and jobs, view the complete database, export up to 1,000 records from list pages to CSV, invite teammates, and access most areas of the Admin Panel. However, Admins do not have access to Roles & Permissions , Plans & Billing , Premium Job Boards , or API Integration Tokens . 2. Team Member Team Members can create records such as candidates, companies, contacts, and jobs. They can also add and edit activities, including notes, call logs, tasks, and meetings. They cannot delete records or activities, export data, or access the Admin Panel. For Deals, Team Members can only view and edit deals that they own. 3. Restricted Team Member Restricted Team Members can create records but can only view records they own or records where they have been assigned as an owner or collaborator. They can access activities related to those records but cannot view other users' data by default. Restricted Team Members cannot delete data or access the Admin Panel. 4. Account Owner Account Owners have the highest level of access in Recruit CRM. In addition to all Admin permissions, they can manage account ownership, change the account currency, purchase calling credits, access full data exports, and manage billing-related settings. Account Owners also have access to the Sent Email Conversation KPI within Team Performance Reports. Troubleshooting Problem: I cannot invite a new user. Likely cause: You may not have permission to invite users. What to check: Verify whether you are an Account Owner, Admin, or have a custom role with user management permissions. Resolution: Contact your Account Owner to grant the necessary permissions. Problem: I receive the error "This email ID is already in use". Likely cause: The user has already signed up for a Recruit CRM trial account using the same email address. What to check: Confirm whether the user has an existing Recruit CRM account. Resolution: Ask the user to deactivate their trial account before sending the invitation again. Click here To learn How to deactivate Account . FAQs 1. Who can invite users to a Recruit CRM account? Only Account Owners, Admins, and users with the appropriate permissions can invite new users. 2. Is adding a user to a team mandatory during the invitation process? No. Adding a user to a team is optional and can be done later if needed. click here to learn How to create Teams inside RCRM? 3. Can I invite multiple users at once? Yes. Recruit CRM allows you to bulk invite users by uploading a CSV or XLS file containing their email addresses. Conclusion: Recruit CRM makes it easy to onboard new teammates by allowing you to send individual or bulk invitations, assign roles, and add users to existing teams. Before inviting a user, ensure you have the necessary permissions and verify that the email address is not already associated with another Recruit CRM account. s: Learn about different job metrics of your job ad.

b: What this feature does and when to use it? Job Campaign Analytics in Recruit CRM helps you track and measure the performance of job advertisements across different job boards. It provides insights into campaign reach, visitor engagement, applicant activity, conversion rates, and advertising costs, helping agencies identify the best-performing recruitment channels and optimize hiring strategies. This feature is especially useful when you want to: Monitor active job advertising campaigns Compare performance across multiple job boards Track applicant and visitor traffic Measure campaign effectiveness using conversion data Make data-driven recruitment advertising decisions Click here to learn how to advertise your jobs through Recruit CRM's Job Marketplace ​ Click here to learn how to bring your job board contracts to Recruit CRM ​ Click here to learn how to add your LinkedIn contract to your job advertising subscription Tracking the job campaigns ↗️ Once your job has been advertised through Recruit CRM’s Job Advertising feature, you can track campaign performance from two different locations. Track analytics from the Job Details page Open the relevant job record. Navigate to the Job Campaigns tab. Locate the campaign you want to analyze. Click on the Analytics button. Track analytics from Admin Settings Navigate to Admin Settings > Job Advertising > Go to the All Campaigns tab. Select the required campaign. Click on Analytics . You can sort your ads based on 'Active Campaigns' or 'Drafts'. You also have the ability to sort them based on the 'Created On', 'Start Date', 'End Date', 'Total Cost', 'Visitors', and 'Applicants', and apply different filters. Understanding the Analytics dashboard 📊 Click on the Analytics button to open the analytics dashboard, where you can view detailed insights and metrics related to your job advertisements. Total Cost Displays the total expense incurred for posting the job. Active Channels Shows the number of job boards where the campaign is currently active compared to the total number of boards where the job has been posted. Days Active Displays the total number of days the job post will remain active. Visitors Shows the number of individuals who have viewed your job post. Applicants Displays the number of applicants who applied to the job. Conversion Ratio This ratio is calculated using the formula: (Number of Applicants / Number of Visitors) x 100. It indicates the percentage of visitors who applied for the job. In addition to campaign metrics, Recruit CRM also provides graphical reports to help recruiters better understand campaign performance over time. You can have a graphical analysis of visitor and applicant traffic, segmented by the different channels where your job is posted and over various time ranges. Additionally, the dashboard provides an overview of the top sources of your applicants, giving you valuable insights into where your candidates are coming from. Additionally, you can export the analytics data in CSV format directly from the Analytics dashboard. This allows you to download detailed tabular reports containing metrics such as visitors, applicants, and conversion ratios across different job boards and time ranges. It's important to note that the Visitor count data is auto-updated every 24 hours at 00:30 GMT. To pull the latest numbers at any time during the day, you need to click the ' Refresh Data ' button and this will update the numbers to reflect the most current data. FAQs Can I track campaigns across multiple job boards? Yes. Recruit CRM allows you to monitor job advertising performance across all supported job boards where your jobs are published. Why are analytics numbers not updated instantly? Visitor data is automatically refreshed every 24 hours. However, you can manually update the data anytime using the Refresh Data button. Conclusion: Job Campaign Analytics in Recruit CRM helps you make more informed recruitment advertising decisions. By regularly reviewing these insights, agencies can optimize recruitment marketing strategies, improve advertising ROI, and focus on the job boards that generate the strongest hiring results. t: Job Change Alert Report
s: This article will guide you on how to use the Job Change Alert Report.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
How does a job change get detected?
Accessing/Reviewing/Updating the Job Change Alert
What Happens on Update?
For Candidates:
For Contacts:
Setting up automated updates
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM automatically checks your existing candidates' and contacts' records publicly available data and lets you know when it detects a job change. This could mean the candidate/contact has moved to a completely new company or simply gotten a new title while staying at the same company, either way, you'll see it reflected as an alert under the 'Job Change Alert' Report. When Recruit CRM detects a change, a badge appears on the record's details page, showing the previous organization/title alongside the newly detected organization/title. Every pending alert also shows up under Reports → Job Change Alert Report , so you can review them individually from a profile or handle several at once from the Reports section. Job Change Alerts are useful whenever you want to: Know when a candidate or contact has moved to a new company. Catch a title change at the same company, which can signal a promotion or shift in seniority worth noting on their record. Keep current organization and title fields accurate across your database without manually checking each profile. Please note: This feature is currently in beta and will be live for all users in the coming weeks. Before you begin: Please Note: Job Change Alert report is available only on the paid plans (Pro, Business and Enterprise). Users with view access to a specific candidate or contact records will be able to view only those records in this report. You need Edit access to a record to update or dismiss its alert. If you don't have edit access and try to click Update, you'll see a "No access" screen instead. On the Free plan, detection doesn't run at all, and you'll still see the Job Change Alert Report, but it will remain empty. If you later upgrade to a paid plan, detection for your account begins from the next monthly detection cycle. One Manual job update/Automated job update (candidate or contact) will consume 1 Recruit CRM Credit. How does a job change get detected? For any record to be checked, it needs a valid LinkedIn profile URL added under the default LinkedIn Profile URL field, and the system uses it to match the record against the data source. Along with the valid LinkedIn profile URL: For candidates: The record needs at least one Work history entry with "Currently working in this role" toggled on, along with a start date for that role, company, and title filled in for that entry. For contacts: The record needs a current title and company name on the record. If a contact is linked to more than one company, the system checks against all the companies. Once the required data in the fields is available, the system matches records via LinkedIn URL against the publicly available data. An alert is generated only when the publicly available data's latest job start date is more recent than the record’s work history in Recruit CRM and either the company or title has changed. This detection check runs once every month, so alerts are refreshed on a monthly cycle rather than in real time. Accessing/Reviewing/Updating the Job Change Alert There are 2 ways of accessing the Job Change Alert that is detected: From the Reports section. From the Candidate/Contact's Details Page. You can review the alert, update or dismiss the alert. From the Reports section: 1. Go to Reports → Job Change Alert Report to see every candidate and contact with a pending alert in one place. From here, you can: Filter the list by record type, so you can look at candidate updates or contact updates separately. Search by the record's name or company to find a specific person quickly. You can check the 'Start Date' column, which reflects the start date of the record's newly detected job. You can apply Filters on the 'New Organization' and 'Start Date' columns. Name column shows the name of the candidate or contact record the alert belongs to. Current Organization and Title shows the current organization and title currently saved on that candidate or contact's record inside your database. New Organization and Title shows the new organization and title we've detected for them. You can scroll towards the right of the page and click on the 'Update' button to update the candidate's/contact's record individually: Or you can bulk select the records and click on the 'Update Profiles' option to update the records in bulk: Since bulk updates can take a moment to process, they run in the background, and you'll get a notification once they're complete. From the Candidate/Contact's Details Page: 1. When a job change is detected, an alert badge appears on the record's details page showing: Previous organization and title New organization and title An Update button to apply the change and each accepted update consumes 1 Recruit CRM Credit. The badge stays until you click on the ' Update Profile' or ' Dismiss' , or a newer job change is detected. Dismissing removes the alert from both the profile and the report and the same alert won't reappear in future cycles, but a new one will appear if the candidate/contact moves jobs again. What Happens on Update? For Candidates: The system updates the Current Organization and Current Title/Position . Creates a new work history entry with the detected job details. If the previous work history entry had "Currently working in this role" toggled on, its End Date is set using the publicly available data (left blank if unavailable). If the candidate has reached the maximum number of work history entries, the oldest is removed to make room. If the new employer doesn't exist as a company record, it is stored as plain text and no company record is auto-created. Note: When a work history entry is created via a Job Change Alert update, mandatory work history field validation is bypassed . If mandatory fields configured in your account are not available from the publicly available data, those fields will remain empty in the new entry. For Contacts: The system updates the Company and Title fields. For contacts linked to more than one company: the system check the publicly available data for an end date on each company. If a company has an end date, it's removed from the contact's record. Companies without an end date stay as they are, and the newly detected company is added on top. If the new company doesn't exist in your account, it is auto-created as a company record (name, website, logo filled from the publicly available data). Mandatory field validation for company creation is bypassed in this scenario. Setting up automated updates If you'd rather not review these manually every time, you can turn on automatic updates. Users with access to the Recruit CRM Credits page will be able to perform this action: 1. Go to Admin Settings → Recruit CRM Credits. Click on the 'Enable Credits For' option. 2. Turn on 'Auto Update Candidate Records' and 'Auto Update Contact Records' under the Job Change Alert section and click on Save. This can be switched on separately for candidates and for contacts, depending on which record type you want automated. Please note: Each successful update, whether you apply it manually or it happens automatically, uses 1 Recruit CRM Credit. When enabled: Once you turn this on, any updates that were already pending for your account are applied immediately. From then on, new updates are applied automatically every month as part of the regular detection cycle, as long as you have enough credits to cover them. The system checks for updates every 30 days and applies them automatically. A badge on the work history entry indicates an automated update; hovering shows "Updated by Recruit CRM." If credits run out mid-cycle, automated updates pause and the Account owner and all Admins receive an in-app and email notification: "Automated job change updates paused due to low credits." Updates resume once credits are available. You can enable/disable the toggles for Manual Update for Candidate/Contact records using the 'Manual Update Candidate Records' and 'Manual Update Contact Records' under the Job Change Alert section and click on Save. Additional Notes Duplicates: The system won't generate duplicate alerts for the same record (unless there is a newly detected job/company). A dismissed alert won't reappear unless the person moves to a different role or company later. Merged records: When two records are merged, the job change check re-runs for the merged record and alerts are surfaced accordingly. Deleted records: Deleting a candidate or contact removes their entries from the Job Change Alert Report. Manual work history match: If you manually add a work history entry matching an active Job Change Alert, the badge and the corresponding report entry are automatically removed. Conclusion: Job Change Alerts help you keep candidate and contact records up to date without manually checking each profile. You can review and apply updates one at a time from a record's badge, handle several together from the Job Change Alert Report, or turn on automated update

t: Job Description Parsing on Recruit CRM
s: Learn how to use Recruit CRM's AI-powered Job Description Parser to automatically extract and populate job details from your job descriptions.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin:
How to Parse a Job Description
What Information is Parsed?
FAQs
Conclusion:
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Recruit CRM's AI-powered Job Description Parser automatically extracts important information from a job description and populates the supported job fields, helping you create jobs faster while reducing manual data entry. Use the Job Description Parser when you: Want to quickly create a new job from an existing job description. Want to save time by automatically filling supported job fields instead of entering them manually. Need to parse job descriptions that are in different formats, including structured or multilingual job descriptions. Want more accurate skill extraction from the entire job description for improved search and matching capabilities. Before you begin: All supported job fields continue to be parsed automatically. If you manually clear a parsed field after parsing, Recruit CRM will not automatically populate that field again when the job description is reprocessed. 🚀 How to Parse a Job Description Go to the Jobs entity. ​ Click on the + Add Job button. ​ Upload the Job Description File in the 'Upload File' option under the Job Description section. ​ Recruit CRM will automatically extract the supported job details and populate the relevant fields. 📋 What Information is Parsed? Recruit CRM automatically extracts supported information from the job description and fills in the corresponding job fields such as: Job Title Job Description Skills Salary Experience City Country Full Address Note: The exact information extracted depends on the content available in the job description. Recruit CRM's AI-powered parser can accurately process a wide variety of job description formats, including: Plain text job descriptions. Structured job descriptions with sections such as Responsibilities, Requirements, and Qualifications. Multi-column layouts. Table-based job descriptions (where supported) Recruit CRM extracts skills from the entire job description , rather than only from a dedicated Skills section. This allows the parser to identify relevant skills even when they appear within responsibilities, qualifications, or other sections of the job description, resulting in more accurate and standardized skill extraction. The Job Description Parser supports all system-supported languages. Recruit CRM automatically parses supported job information while maintaining the same parsing experience across different languages. Once your job has been parsed, you can use AI Job-to-Candidate Matching to automatically find candidates whose profiles best match the job requirements. AI Matching analyzes the job details and candidate profiles to identify the most relevant matches, helping you shortlist candidates faster. Click here to learn more about AI Job Candidate Matching in Recruit CRM FAQs Why wasn't a field repopulated after I re-parsed the job description? If you manually clear a field that was previously populated by the Job Description Parser (for example, Job City ), Recruit CRM will not automatically fill that field again when you re-parse the same job description. This behavior is intentional to ensure that your manual changes are not overwritten. Conclusion: The AI-powered Job Description Parser helps you create jobs faster by automatically extracting supported information from a variety of job description formats. t: Job Statistics Report
s: The Job Statistics Report in Recruit CRM helps you measure job status and overall job performance across key hiring KPIs.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Generate and Analyze the Job Statistics Report
Export the Report:
View Candidate Details:
Review the Report Tables:
Troubleshooting
Problem: Numbers in the hiring stages do not match the current pipeline
FAQs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Job Statistics Report provides a comprehensive view of how your jobs are performing. You can quickly run a report on all your Jobs with all the available KPIs to have a deeper understanding of whether everything is going as per the plan. This report enables you to compare various jobs and identify those performing exceptionally well. Additionally, you can search for specific jobs and download an Excel file containing the applicants' names and their current stages in the hiring process for the selected job. The Report includes all notes associated with a job not just those added directly to it. This means any notes originally added to other records (Candidate, company, contactor deal) but linked to the job are also counted, providing a complete view of all job-related activities. ​ Use this feature when: • You want to measure the performance of one or more jobs using key hiring KPIs. Generate and Analyze the Job Statistics Report 1. Open the Job Statistics Report Navigate to the Reports section from the left-hand navigation menu and open the Job Statistics Report . 2. Select the jobs you want to analyze Choose the jobs you want to include in the report. You can generate the report for all jobs or select specific ones. Use the available filters to quickly find jobs based on their status, including: • Open • Closed • On Hold • Cancelled • Archived • Hot Lists ​ To include every job in the report, select the checkbox at the top of the job list. 3. Select the KPIs Choose the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) you want to analyze. Available KPIs include: • Hiring Stages • Notes • Note Types • Meetings • Meeting Types • Tasks • Task Types ​ ​ 4. Select the date range Choose the time period for the report. You can select one of the predefined ranges, such as Today, Yesterday, This Week, Last Week, This Month, or Last Quarter , or specify a Custom Date Range by selecting the required start and end dates. 5. Filter by team members or teams If required, select specific team members or teams to view report data only for their activities. ​ 6. Generate or save the report After selecting the jobs, KPIs, date range, and team members, click Generate Report . If you plan to use the same report again, click Save and Generate Report . This saves the report for future use while generating the report immediately. ​ Once the report is generated, you'll see: • A bar chart visualizing the selected KPIs. • Detailed summary tables displaying the report data, including the Fill Rate for each job if the Placed Hiring stage is selected as one of the KPIs. The Fill Rate is calculated as: (Placed Candidates ÷ Number of Openings) × 100 Please Note: If you are seeing numbers related to any Hiring Stage (Assigned/Placed etc.), This is historical data which means, the candidates were in that hiring stage during some point in the date range the report was generated for, Their current hiring stage may be different. ​ Export the Report: You can export the report in multiple ways: • Click Export Report to CSV above the table to download the summary table as a CSV file. • Click the Export icon in the top-right corner of the bar chart to download the chart as an image in PNG, JPG, or SVG format. • Click any bar in the chart to open the detailed candidate list for that KPI, then click Export Report to CSV to download the detailed report as a CSV file. View Candidate Details: Each bar in the chart is clickable. Click any bar to view the candidates associated with that KPI for the selected jobs and date range. Within the detailed report, you can: • Review the candidate records. • Sort the data by clicking any column header. • Customize the displayed information using Edit Columns . • Apply additional filters to narrow down the results. • Perform a Boolean Search to quickly locate specific records. • Export the filtered candidate list to a CSV file after selecting the required fields. Review the Report Tables: Scroll below the chart to view the report tables, which provide a comparative breakdown of the selected jobs across the KPIs you chose. If you've selected both individual users and teams , two separate tables will be displayed: • The first table shows data for the selected individual users. Expand a job using the dropdown arrow to view a member-wise breakdown for that job. • The second table displays aggregated data for the selected teams. Similarly, you can expand a job to view the team-level breakdown. ​ 📌 Note: The report includes all notes associated with a job , including notes originally created on linked Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Contractors, or Deals , giving you a complete view of all job-related activities. Troubleshooting Problem: Numbers in the hiring stages do not match the current pipeline Likely cause : The Job Statistics Report uses historical data within the selected date range, not current hiring stages. What to check: Confirm the date range selected. Review whether candidates have moved to different stages after the date range. Resolution: Understand that if you see numbers for hiring stages like assigned or placed, they indicate candidates who were in that stage at some point during the selected date range. If you need current pipeline only, cross-check with live job pipelines outside this report or the Dashboard Statistics. FAQs What kind of data does the Job Statistics Report include for each job? The Job Statistics Report can include hiring stages, notes and note types, meetings and meeting types, tasks and task types, fill rate if the default placed hiring stage is selected, and other KPIs you select. It also counts notes originally added to candidates, companies, contractors, or deals when those notes are linked to the job. How is fill rate calculated in this report? Fill rate is calculated as placed candidates divided by the number of openings, multiplied by 100. Can I export the report and charts? Yes. You can export the report data to CSV and export the bar graph as PNG, JPG, or SVG. Conclusion The Job Statistics Report in Recruit CRM gives you a complete, historical view of how your jobs are performing across stages, activities, and teams, with flexible filters and export options to support deeper analysis and reporting. t: Job-Associated fields and files
s: This article will help you upload and share candidate fields/files associated with jobs.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to add custom job-associated fields?
How to make job-associated fields visible on the job application form?
Accessing job-specific details submitted by candidates 📄
Job-Associated files
How to share job-associated fields with clients? ✅
Troubleshooting
Problem: New job-associated field does not appear on the job application form
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Job-associated fields let you tailor the application process to the specific requirements of each job opening. Recruit CRM streamlines the process of managing candidate information by allowing you to customize fields based on the different job roles the candidate is being considered for. Job-associated files let you add, store, and share files that are specific to each job a candidate is associated with. This allows you to manage different resumes, cover letters, portfolios, or other documents for the same candidate across multiple roles. Together, these features streamline how you collect, store, and share candidate information that varies by job. You can use this feature when: You need to ask job-specific questions on the job application form. You want to store different resumes, cover letters, or portfolios for each job a candidate applies to. You can easily add and share job-specific fields for candidates, and ensure you gather the most relevant information for each position. How to add custom job-associated fields? 1. Navigate to your Admin Settings -> Job Application Form Fields Settings 2. Scroll down to the “Job Associated Files” section and click on 'Add Field': 3. Enter the field name and select its type from the following options: 'Text', 'Long Text', 'Dropdown', 'Multiselect', 'Number', or 'Checkbox'. 4. Click on the green 'Save Field' button to add the field. Recruit CRM lets you add 5 custom job-associated fields apart from the 5 default 'File' type job-associated fields in the system. How to make job-associated fields visible on the job application form? 1. Once you add the fields, turn the visibility 'ON' of the desired fields to make them visible on your job application form. Additionally, you can mark fields as 'Required' to make them mandatory for applicants to fill out. 2. Click the green 'Save' button to save your changes: 3. Upon saving the changes, the desired fields will become visible on the job application forms as well, ensuring that applicants can easily access and fill them out as required. Any changes you make in the Job application form settings will apply to all the job application forms. However, you can also customize these fields uniquely for each job application form. Click here to learn how to do it! Accessing job-specific details submitted by candidates 📄 On the job details page, within the "Candidate Pipeline" tab, click on the "Job Specific Details" button in the candidate details section to access job-related information for each candidate. You'll be able to access the job-associated fields that you've added, enabling you to upload files, add values to those fields, and view previous values added by yourself or submitted by candidates via the job application form. Furthermore, you'll also be able to review the candidate questions that the candidate has submitted for that specific job. Job-Associated files You might need different information from a candidate such as a different Cover Letter or Resume based on the different job roles they're being considered for. Recruit CRM makes it easy to add, store, and share job-specific files for Candidates. If one of your candidates wants to apply to 2 different jobs, say a Marketing role and a Sales role, with 2 job-specific Resumes. The candidates can now submit different CVs/ Portfolios/ Cover letters/ Other files for different jobs from the job application form. 1. If you are on the Candidate’s profile, you can find the “View Files” option under the Assigned Jobs tab. (as shown in the image below): 2. On the Job profile, you’ll find the “Job Specific Details” option under Candidate Pipeline: Once you click on the “Job Specific Details” button under each Job assignment, you’ll have the option to add/ store 5 standard files such as Formatted Resume, Cover Letter, Portfolio and an additional 2 other files for each job. These can also be Resumes formatted and Cover Letters created within Recruit CRM. This article will give you more information: Resume/ CV Formatting There are two ways in which you can add a candidate file associated with the job: 1. You can click on the “Upload file” option and upload a brand new file into the system OR 2. You can use the “Select file” option to choose an existing file from within the files section of the Candidate. How to share job-associated fields with clients? ✅ While submitting candidates to clients, you can share the fields/files associated with the particular job. To do that, click on the "Fields Shared with Clients" button and select the fields/files that you want to share. Click here to learn more about the Submit Candidates to Contact feature! On the Assigned Candidates list within a job, you have the flexibility to display job-associated fields in the List view, run Advanced searches based on these fields, and seamlessly export them along with the candidate data. Troubleshooting Problem: New job-associated field does not appear on the job application form Likely cause : The field’s visibility is turned off or changes were not saved. What to check : In Job Application Form Field Settings , confirm the field is listed under Job Associated Fields . Verify the Visibility toggle is turned on for that field. Confirm you clicked the green Save button after making changes. Resolution : Turn visibility on for the field, click Save , and refresh or reopen the job application form to verify the field now appears. Problem: Cannot add more job associated fields Likely cause : You have reached the limit of custom job associated fields. What to check : Count how many custom job associated fields are already created. Resolution : Since Recruit CRM allows five custom job associated fields (in addition to five default file-type job associated fields), remove or repurpose existing custom fields if you need to create new ones. FAQs Can a candidate upload different resumes for different jobs? Yes. Using job-associated files, a candidate can submit different resumes, cover letters, portfolios, or other files for each job they apply to. Can I choose which job-specific fields and files to share with clients? Yes. b: Streamline your job posting process and publish job ads in an easy and targeted way in Recruit CRM. You can share your jobs on different job boards in two ways: Posting jobs by integrating your existing job board contracts in Recruit CRM. Posting directly to job boards without having to create an account with them (job marketplace). Please note that you DO NOT require a job advertising subscription or purchase job posting credits to post jobs directly through the job marketplace . To purchase a job campaign on the job marketplace, you pay the cost of the campaign directly to VONQ, seamlessly. However, to post jobs using your existing job board contracts , you need to purchase credits as add-ons to your Recruit CRM subscription. You can buy credits on a monthly or annual basis, irrespective of your subscription plan , directly from the job advertising module. How to buy job posting credits To test or use job postings on contractual job boards, you receive two free monthly credits with your paid Recruit CRM subscription. You can also buy additional credits as needed. 1. Go to the Job Advertising section in the Admin Settings . 2. Click Buy Contract Posting Credits under the Added Contracts tab. 3. Choose the number of credits you require based on how many jobs you want to advertise per month or year, then click Continue to Checkout . 4. Now, add your card details for the payment. Once you review the bill summary >> Understand and agree to the terms of service >> Click on 'Pay'. That's it :) ​ Once payment is successful, you can use these credits to post jobs on your contracted job boards directly through Recruit CRM. Here's how: ​ Bring your job board contracts to Recruit CRM & post jobs easily! ➕ Upgrading your job posting subscription Here's how you can increase the number of credits on the subscription or upgrade from the monthly to the yearly payment plan: ​ ⬆️ Upgrading to a higher-tier credit subscription 1. Go to the Job Advertising section >> Click on "Edit Current Plan": 2. Choose the new, higher number of credits you want. Click Continue to Checkout to confirm the payment. If you're on the annual subscription, on updating to a higher-tier plan, you will only be charged a prorated amount for the remaining period of your annual billing cycle. The job posting credits will also be prorated for the first month. 📅 Upgrading from the monthly to the annual subscription Upon upgrading to the annual subscription, the remaining credits will only be carried forward for the first month. 1. Go to the Job Advertising section and click Edit Current Plan . 2. Switch the payment option toggle to "Annual". 3. You can also upgrade the number of job credits. Then, click on "Continue to Checkout," and you'll be prompted to pay the required amount. ⊖ Downgrading your job posting subscription You have the option to downgrade the number of credits in your Vonq subscription if you're not posting as many jobs as you have credits for. ⬇️ Downgrading to a lower-tier credit subscription You can downgrade your plan, for example , from credits for 50 jobs per month to credits for 10 jobs per month. From the next renewal date, you will be shifted to a lower bucket of jobs. 1. Go to the Job Advertising section >> Click on "Edit Current Plan": 2. Choose the new bucket that matches the number of credits you require. 3. Click Continue to Checkout . You will not be charged during the change and purchase process. The charge will only be applied on the next renewal date for the lower-tier job credits. In case of the annual subscription, you can downgrade your subscription, however, your new subscription plan for the credits will start at the next renewal date. 📅 Yearly to Monthly You will not be able to downgrade from the yearly to the monthly subscription from within the app. Please contact us using the chatbot or email us at support@recruitcrm.io so we can assist you with it. ❌ Cancelling your job posting subscription If you wish to cancel your subscription, you can do so from your 'Job Advertising ' section. 1. Click on the 'Cancel Plan?' button located underneath the 'Edit Current Plan' button on the right panel. 2. Confirm the cancellation by clicking on the 'Cancel Contract Posting Plan' button: By doing this, you won't be charged for the next renewal, and you can continue to utilize the remaining job credits that you've already paid till the end of the subscription expiry. Conclusion: Managing your job advertising subscription in Recruit CRM, whether buying credits, upgrading, downgrading, or canceling is handled from the Job Advertising section and gives you flexible control over your job advertising costs. If you have any questions or need help with a specific change, contact Recruit CRM via the in-app chatbot or email support@recruitcrm.io . b: Our LinkedIn messages integration, powered by Unipile , helps you manage your LinkedIn conversations seamlessly within Recruit CRM. It provides a complete view of all interactions with candidates and contacts, enabling you to communicate with them directly through LinkedIn without leaving Recruit CRM. Notes LinkedIn Messages Integration is an Enterprise plan feature which can also be added at an additional cost to the Pro or Business plan subscriptions. The LinkedIn Messages Integration is powered by Uniplie and it is GDPR compliant . The LinkedIn Messages Integration supports the following plans, i.e, LinkedIn Recruiter, Recruiter Lite, Sales Navigator core, business, and career plan. 🎥 Here is a tutorial on how to send and receive LinkedIn messages: 🔗 Connecting your LinkedIn account to Recruit CRM 1. Click on the 'Profile' icon and select the ' LinkedIn Integration ' tab. 2. Click on 'Connect'. 3. Enter your LinkedIn account credentials and verify the details. If you haven’t connected your LinkedIn account through the profile settings, you’ll see a button to connect it under the LinkedIn Messages tab inside any candidate or contact profile. How to use the Cookie login method to avoid multiple LinkedIn login sessions being detected in the app? Click here to know more about the multiple LinkedIn login sessions You can follow the following steps to overcome the LinkedIn multiple sessions login error detected in the app: 1. Under the LinkedIn Integration tab, click on 'Connect' 2. Click on the 'Cookies' tab. 3. Now you need to enter your li_at/li_a value under the Cookies section. To know these values you need to open your 'Linked Account' on the new tab and right click anywhere on the screen and select 'Inspect'. Then click on the 'Application Tab ' and expand the 'Cookies' section. Now, click on the LinkedIn URL ( www.linkedin.com ). You can use the search bar and find the li_a/li_at value and make sure to copy the 'value'. If your account has a Recruiter or Sales Navigator subscription, you need to copy the li_a value too. Now you need to paste the value under the Cookie section while you are connecting your account and click on 'Login'. Here is a tutorial on how to log in via the Cookie Method: 🤝 Send and Manage LinkedIn Connection Requests You can send and manage LinkedIn connection requests directly from Recruit CRM without leaving the platform, helping you keep your sourcing and outreach workflow in one place. Send a connection request: Open the candidate or contact profile and navigate to the LinkedIn Messaging tab. You might need to scroll a bit towards the right in the Widgets section at the bottom of the page. If you are not already connected with the person on LinkedIn, click Send Request . You'll now be prompted to add a personalized note to your connection request. While this is completely optional, including a brief, relevant message can improve the chances of your connection request being accepted. ​ ​ Please note: LinkedIn allows a maximum of 200 characters for connection request notes. Once you're ready, click Send Connection Request to send your connection request. ​ Once the request is sent, its status will be displayed within the LinkedIn tab. ​ Withdraw a pending connection request: If needed, you can withdraw a pending connection request directly from Recruit CRM. Please note that LinkedIn applies the same restrictions as its native platform. If you withdraw a connection request, you won't be able to resend another request to the same person until the three-week waiting period has passed. ​ ​ Refresh the connection status: After sending a request, you can manually refresh the connection status by clicking the Refresh button. This lets you check whether the recipient has accepted your connection request without waiting for the status to update automatically. ​ Receive connection notifications: When your connection request is accepted, you'll receive an in-app notification in Recruit CRM. ​ 📌 Please note: There may be a slight delay before the notification appears. If you'd like to check immediately, simply use the Refresh button to retrieve the latest connection status. ​ Once your connection request is accepted, you can start messaging the candidate or contact directly from the LinkedIn tab in Recruit CRM. ​ 💬 Start LinkedIn Conversations Once you're connected with a candidate or contact on LinkedIn, you can start and manage your LinkedIn conversations directly from Recruit CRM. If you have a supported LinkedIn Premium plan, you can also send InMails where applicable ​ Follow these steps to start the conversation: 1. Navigate to the candidate/contact’s profile >> Click on the LinkedIn tab to start a conversation. Note: If you have less than 50 API requests, the messages will be fetched directly (if available). If your API requests are between 51–70, you’ll need to click the "Start Conversation" button to send/view messages. If you’ve made more than 70 API requests, the "Start Conversation" button will appear along with a warning message: “You’re reaching the daily limit set by LinkedIn for retrieving conversations. Exceeding this limit could risk blocking your LinkedIn account.” 2. Click on the Message button to open the messaging interface. 3. Type your message or insert Message template and optionally insert placeholders for personalization >> Click Send to deliver the message. 4. When a new message is received, a Load New Message button will appear within a minute or two. Click this button to view real-time updates. 5. Then click on the 'Application Tab ' and expand the 'Cookies' section. Now, click on the LinkedIn URL ( www.linkedin.com ). Note: If you have less than 50 API requests, the messages will be fetched directly (if available). If your API requests are between 51–70, you’ll need to click the "Start Conversation" button to send/view messages. If you’ve made more than 70 API requests, the "Start Conversation" button will appear along with a warning message: “You’re reaching the daily limit set by LinkedIn for retrieving conversations. Exceeding this limit could risk blocking your LinkedIn account.” 2. Type your message or insert Message template and optionally insert placeholders for personalization >> Click Send to deliver the message. 3. t: LinkedIn Sequencing in Recruit CRM
s: This article will guide you on how to create LinkedIn sequences to interact and enhance your engagement with candidates and contacts.
h: Please note:
How to set up a sequence
Criteria for enrolling prospects into LinkedIn Sequences
Enrolling prospects into a sequence
Key points to note
1. Prospect Replies to LinkedIn Sequence
2. LinkedIn Disconnected
3. LinkedIn Add-On Expiry
b: You can send a series of scheduled LinkedIn messages to candidates and contacts using LinkedIn Sequences. This helps your team stay in touch with prospects automatically, leading to better response rates and a smoother recruitment process. Please note: To use LinkedIn steps in sequences, you'll first need to purchase the LinkedIn Messages Integration from your Plans & Billing section. LinkedIn Messages Integration is an Enterprise plan feature which can also be added at an additional cost to Pro or Business plan subscriptions. ​ Once the feature is active, LinkedIn Integration will be enabled on your account. ​ Make sure your LinkedIn account is connected here to start using LinkedIn Sequences. Click here to learn more about the LinkedIn Messages Integration How to set up a sequence 1. Go to Admin Settings > CRM Process Customization > Sequences . 2. Click on "Create Sequence". 3. Select either "Candidates" or "Contacts" as the recipient of the sequence. 4. The next step is to name your sequence and select the LinkedIn step that needs to be executed. You can choose to either select an existing Message template or create a new one dedicated to the sequence. You can create a LinkedIn-only sequence or mix task steps with email steps and SMS steps as well, as long as you respect the limit of 40 steps in total (10 each). 5. Then, specify the number of days and the time when the sequence step should be executed. It is important to know exactly when the LinkedIn message will be sent in relation to the starting date of the sequence. To calculate this, you can use the following formula: Send Date = Start Date + Specified No. Of Days (Send SMS In) Here, "Start Date" represents the date when the sequence was initiated. "Specified Date" or "Send SMS In" is the number of days you have indicated for the message to be sent after the start of the sequence. The resulting "Send date" is the calculated date on which the message will be sent. For example : If you start the sequence on January 1st and specify that the SMS should be sent in 2 days, the Send Date would be calculated as follows: Send date= January 1st + 2 days =January 3rd. You can also set the " Send Message In " days count as 0, establishing the beginning of your sequence in Day 0 . This way, the first message will be sent on the same day you enroll prospects into a sequence. 6. Add steps to the sequence as required, up to a maximum of 40 steps , which includes a maximum of 10 LinkedIn steps, 10 email steps, 10 SMS steps and 10 task steps . You can easily rearrange the sequence steps by using the drag-and-drop functionality. 7. Set a specific number of days for each step to execute, with a range of 1 to 250 calendar days or business days. Tasks can be created on the same day as the sequence initiation by setting the day as "0". ​ When implementing a task on the 0th day, it's crucial to align the step timing with the previous steps or set it for a later time than the preceding step to ensure a seamless workflow. Criteria for enrolling prospects into LinkedIn Sequences 1. You must be connected on LinkedIn If you're not already connected with the prospect on LinkedIn, you'll need to send them a connection request manually first. 2. LinkedIn URL is required Make sure each prospect’s profile in Recruit CRM has their LinkedIn profile link added. 3. Different LinkedIn URLs for prospect and sender The LinkedIn URL added for the prospect must not be the same as the one connected for your user account. This is to ensure the system correctly identifies the sender and receiver. 4. LinkedIn Conversation Must Be Initiated Manually First You should initiate the conversation on LinkedIn by clicking the LinkedIn tab on the prospect’s details page. This will fetch the prospect’s profile and connection status. Once this is done, you can proceed to enroll them. This step helps prevent your LinkedIn account from being temporarily blocked due to API rate limits. Enrolling prospects into a sequence 1. Start by bulk selecting the prospects you want to enroll and click on Enroll. 2. Then select the sequence you want to enroll them in, these could include Email , Tasks , SMS or LinkedIn steps . 3. Once they have made their selection, the system will automatically check if each selected prospect meets the necessary requirements for that sequence (like having an email ID, LinkedIn URL, etc.). Only the prospects who pass all the checks will be enrolled into the sequence. If your sequence includes LinkedIn and SMS, the system checks for A2P 10DLC (US), KYC (UK), and SMS consent before sending. Key points to note 1. Prospect Replies to LinkedIn Sequence If a prospect replies to your LinkedIn message, they won’t be automatically unenrolled from the LinkedIn Sequence due to technical limitations. You’ll need to manually unenroll them from the sequence. 2. LinkedIn Disconnected If your LinkedIn account gets disconnected from Recruit CRM, any active LinkedIn Sequences will be paused automatically . 3. LinkedIn Add-On Expiry If your LinkedIn Add-On expires and you try to enroll prospects in a sequence, the system will ask you to renew the LinkedIn Integration first. 4. Updating LinkedIn URL in Another Tab If you have Recruit CRM open in two tabs, and you change the LinkedIn URL from the candidate details page in one tab, you’ll need to: Close the validation popup in the other tab Refresh the page Try enrolling again This ensures the system picks up the updated LinkedIn URL. 5. Limitations in LinkedIn Sequence Analytics In LinkedIn sequencing, metrics like 'Open rate,' 'Reply rate,' and 'Unsubscribe rate' cannot be tracked. That's it, I hope this helps. t: Linking Candidates & Contacts That Are The Same Person
s: Sometimes a candidate can become a client or vice versa
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
To link two Records:
Identifying Candidates Who Are Also Contacts
Identifying Contacts Who Are Also Candidates
FAQs
Can I have more than one candidate linked to the same contact (or vice versa)?
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? In recruitment, it’s quite common to come across situations where a candidate you’re working with later becomes a client, or a client you’ve been in touch with decides to look for new opportunities as a candidate. This feature in Recruit CRM lets you connect a candidate record and a contact record that represent the same person. ​ To make handling such scenarios simple, Recruit CRM gives you three easy options: Link an existing candidate and contact – If both records belong to the same person, you can link them together. Create a candidate from a contact – Turn an existing client or contact into a new candidate profile. Create a contact from a candidate – Convert an existing candidate into a new client or contact record. Once you’ve linked the records, you can then access and view the associated “Linked Record” from both candidate and contact profiles. To link two Records: 1. Go to a Candidate or Contact Record. Click on the "Link To Contact/Candidate" button in the header section. ​ For Candidate record: ​ For Contact record: If the Candidate or Contact record you wish to link is already in the system you can search for it or you can just hit the blue "Add Contact" or "Add Candidate" button to create a new record and automatically link it. Once you hit the green "Link Contact" or "Link Candidate" button in the pop-up, the 2 records will be linked. After linking, the candidate and contact profiles are connected you can navigate between the linked records directly. ​ Note: If you wish to unlink them, just click on the button "Contact Linked" or "Candidate Linked" button and then click on the 'Unlink' option: Now, if you wish to delete them as a contact but still leave them as a candidate and vice versa, you can simply delete them as a normal record. Although both are linked, contacts and candidates are different entities, so if you delete one, it won't delete the other. 🔍 Identifying Candidates Who Are Also Contacts From the Candidates List Page , click on the name of the candidate to open their profile. On the candidate’s profile page, look for the red “Contact-Linked” label at the top. Hover over the “Contact-Linked” label a dropdown will appear showing the linked Contact details of the same person. You can click the contact name in the dropdown to open their Contact profile directly. 🔍 Identifying Contacts Who Are Also Candidates Individually from the Contact's Profile: ​ From the Contacts List Page , click on the name of the Contact to open their profile. On the contact's profile page, look for the green “Candidate-Linked” label at the top. Hover over the “Candidate-Linked” label, and a dropdown will appear showing the linked Candidate details of the same person. You can click the candidate name in the dropdown to open their profile directly. ​ In bulk from the Contact list page: ​ Go to the Contact List Page and click the " Add Filter" button located near the top of the page. In the filter search bar, type “Candidate-linked” , then click on the Candidate-linked filter option from the results. This will open the Yes/No selection for you to choose from. Select “Yes” to see only contacts who are also saved as candidates, or select “No” to view contacts not linked to any candidate profile. Then, click Apply to set the filter. ​ 🤔FAQs Can I have more than one candidate linked to the same contact (or vice versa)? The standard use case is a one-to-one link between a candidate and a contact who are the same person. Conclusion: Here is how you can manage people who are both candidates and contacts in Recruit CRM. If you have more queries, just reach out to us using the chatbot in the bottom right corner! ​ Related Articles Social Profile Links - Candidates/Companies/Contacts Pitch Candidate(s) to Contact(s) Enable the 'unsubscribe/opt-out from email' link for emails sent to candidates/contacts Linking Candidates & Contacts That Are The Same Person (New UI) Social Profile Links - Candidates/Companies/Contacts(New UI)

t: Managing Candidate Work & Education History in Recruit CRM
s: This article will help you understand how to edit and customize candidate Work and Education History.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Candidate Work and Education History can be edited in multiple ways:
Customizing the Candidate Work and Education History section
How are Work and Education History entries handled within Recruit CRM?
FAQs
Do visibility and required settings apply to all users?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? This feature allows you to add, view, edit, and manage a candidate’s Work experience and Educational details directly within the candidate's profile. Candidate Work and Education History can be edited in multiple ways: 1. Open the relevant candidate profile in Recruit CRM and click on the Edit Candidate button (pencil icon). 2. Scroll down to the Work History or Education History section you want to update. Click on the pencil icon within that section, make the required changes, and then click Save to apply them. Note: In the Description box, you can also format text using Bold, Italics, Underline, Bullet points, Numbered lists, and even add Hyperlinks. Once you're done, hit the "Submit" button. You can also edit Candidate Work and Education History from the "Details" tab under candidate profiles by clicking on the "pencil" icon. Customizing the Candidate Work and Education History section You just need to follow these simple steps: 1. Go to Admin Settings and click on Candidate Fields under data customization. 2. Click on the "pencil" icon against the work or education history section to change the section name. You can also show/hide the education or work history sections using the toggle beside the section name. 3. You can turn the visibility toggle on/off to show/hide a field on the "Add Candidate" and "Edit Candidate" forms. You can also make a field "Required" by hitting the checkbox against it. By making a field mandatory, you and your team will not be able to add/edit a candidate without filling in some data in these "required" fields. Note: The "Educational Qualification" under the Education History section and the "Title" under the Work History section are default fields and can not be edited. P.S. You can see multiple cascading-type sections divided into different categories in the admin settings. How are Work and Education History entries handled within Recruit CRM? When a candidate's resume is updated, the system identifies any manually added or edited work and education history entries. We understand the importance of the effort put into customizing the profiles, so we retain these specific entries. Simultaneously, we automatically replace the remaining entries with the most recent data from the uploaded resumes. This ensures that you have access to the most up-to-date work and education history. In cases where you use our Chrome extension to source and parse resumes, the override data option plays a crucial role. When the override data option is turned on, the system will replace all the work and education history entries with the data extracted from the resume, regardless of whether they were manually added or edited. However, when the override data option is turned off, no changes will be made to work and education histories. This gives you more control over the data allowing you to retain manually added or edited information. If a candidate manually enters their work and education history using the talent pool, or job application form, or when a candidate updates their resume from the profile update form, we preserve their entries in the original form. ​ However, when the work and education history details are sourced from a resume then the information provided by the external forms is replaceable. 🤔FAQs Do visibility and required settings apply to all users? Yes. Changes made in Candidate Fields apply account-wide to all users working with candidate profiles. If a candidate manually enters their work and education history using the talent pool, or job application form, or when a candidate updates their resume from the profile update form, we preserve their entries in the original form. ​ However, when the work and education history details are sourced from a resume then the information provided by the external forms is replaceable. 🤔FAQs Do visibility and required settings apply to all users? Yes. Changes made in Candidate Fields apply account-wide to all users working with candidate profiles. t: Managing Off-Limits Records (Candidates, Companies, and Contacts)
s: This article explains how to tag candidates/contacts/companies as "off limits" to prevent communicating with them by mistake.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to mark records as off-limits❓
Setting up custom off-limits status ⭕️
How to find your off-limits records 🕵️
How to remove the off-limits?
FAQs
Can I have multiple off-limits statuses for different reasons?
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? This feature lets you mark candidates/contacts/companies as Off-limits so they are separated from active records and protected from accidental contact or changes. You can assign a specific status, timeframe, and reason for each off-limits record and configure custom off-limits statuses. How to mark records as off-limits❓ 1. Navigate inside the profile of any record (candidates, contacts, or companies), click on the three-dot button, and then click on "Mark as Off-limits": 2. Once you're inside the off-limits pop-up window: Choose the Status to assign to the record. Set the Timeframe for how long the record should remain off-limits. Specify the Reason for marking the record as off-limits. When setting companies as off-limits, you also have the option to mark the associated contacts or candidates off-limits. 3. Another way to mark records as off-limits is by selecting multiple records in bulk. To do this, go to the list page of the records, select them in bulk , and then click on the "Off-Limits" button. Follow the same process to mark them as off-limits: Whenever a record is set as to off-limits, they will appear with a tag next to their profile picture: 4. You can also set up candidates as off-limits while placing them in any job. In the "Update Hiring Stage" window, you'll find an option to mark them as off-limits once their hiring stage is changed to "Placed": If you're sourcing candidates or clients through the Chrome Extension, you'll be able to see a message letting you know a record was marked as "off limits" in the system: ​ Setting up custom off-limits status ⭕️ Here's how you can create customized off-limits statuses, which can serve as tags or reasons for marking candidates as "off-limits": ​ 1. Navigate to your Admin settings and click on "Off-Limit Status" . 2. Click on the "Customize" button: 3. To add new off-limits statuses, simply click on "Add new status". You can choose a specific color for the tag by selecting "Select color", and if you want to make it the default, just click on the "Default" checkbox: 4. Now hit the "Save Status" button to confirm the statuses you've added. How to find your off-limits records 🕵️ To find all of your off-limits records, navigate to your Quickview and click on "Off-Limit Candidates/Contacts/Companies": Records that have been marked as off-limits will also display a tag on their profile, and you will also have the ability to: View the off-limits history of the record. Update the off-limits setup for that record. Remove off-limits from that record. Use cases for off-limits tags For example at the moment, it’s only possible to archive jobs, not candidates. In this case, you can use our Off limits feature, where you can add this candidate to an Off limit tag. How to remove the off-limits? Open the profile of the record that is currently under Off-limits. Click on the Off Limits status displayed at the top left corner of the screen. Click the Remove button. 🤔FAQs Can I have multiple off-limits statuses for different reasons? Yes. You can create multiple custom statuses such as “Do Not Contact,” “Hired by Client,” or “Legal Block,” each with its own color. Conclusion: Using the Off-Limits feature in Recruit CRM helps you keep your database clean, compliant, and safe from accidental outreach by separating restricted records from active ones. Hope this helps! t: Managing Your Email Sequence
s: This article will guide you on how you can enroll and unenroll candidates/contacts from a sequence.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
Enrolling Candidate/Contacts in a sequence
Unenrolling Candidates/Contacts from the sequence
Tracking the number of active enrollments
Troubleshooting
Problem: A candidate/contact does not appear in the enrollment list
FAQs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Sequence Enrollment feature allows you to enroll one or multiple candidates or contacts into a predefined multi-step email sequence and customize the timing, sender email address, content, and starting step during enrollment. It supports bulk enrollment and un-enrollment, automatically pauses and removes records from a sequence when a recipient replies, and lets you track active enrollments and remaining capacity. This feature is useful when you want to: Run structured multi-step email outreach campaigns. Enroll multiple candidates or contacts into a sequence in bulk. Automatically stop follow-ups when a recipient replies. Monitor active enrollments and remaining sequence capacity. Before you begin: This is a Business Plan feature and above, and in the Pro/Free plan, users will have access to create only 1 sequence. Only the account owners, admins, and users on custom roles with access to sequencing can create a sequence. Enrolling Candidate/Contacts in a sequence Navigate to the Candidates or Contacts list page and select the record(s) you want to enroll in a sequence. Click Enroll In Sequence from the header bar at the top of the list. In the pop-up window, select the sequence you want to use. You can search for a sequence by name or use filters to quickly find the right one. Once selected, the system will display the records eligible for enrollment and automatically exclude: Records that have opted out of emails Records already enrolled in a sequence Records without an email address Please note- If a record is missing an email address, you can add or update it directly from this screen by clicking the edit (pencil) icon . Any changes made here will also be saved to the record. Click Continue and review the sequence steps. To customize a specific step for this enrollment, click the pencil icon beside the step. Configure the sequence as needed: Adjust the number of days between steps Set the preferred execution timing for each step Select the connected email address that should send the sequence (if multiple email accounts are connected) Learn How to Connect Two Email Accounts If you want to execute the first stage of the sequence today, then click on the " Send Today " button and the rest of the steps will be rolled out accordingly. Optionally, customize the content of each step by editing the email subject, body, and attachments. Note- The customization is limited to steps that haven't been executed yet. To begin the sequence from a later step, use the Start Sequence From dropdown and select the desired step. Any preceding steps will be skipped. While enrolling records in the sequence, you'll be able to see a preview of the placeholders used in each step. The placeholders will be highlighted in yellow in the preview, but not in the email sent in the sequence. If you're enrolling multiple records in the sequence, the placeholders will reflect the information of the first person enrolled. 9. Once you're satisfied with the configuration, confirm your settings and hit the "Enrol in sequence" button 10. You can also enroll candidates or contacts directly from the Sequences section. Simply open the desired sequence and click the Enroll button to add records to it. You can also enroll records in a sequence from the jobs page . This will enroll all the primary contacts for that job in the selected sequence. Unenrolling Candidates/Contacts from the sequence You can bulk unenroll candidates or contacts from a sequence by opening the desired sequence and navigating to the Enrollments tab. From there, select the records you want to remove and unenroll them in bulk. Alternatively, you can unenroll an individual candidate or contact directly from their detailed profile page if you only need to remove a specific record from the sequence. The user who has initiated the enrollment process should have his/her email settings connected with Recruit CRM. This is mandatory since the emails will be sent out using the enrolled user’s email settings. Tracking the number of active enrollments You can see how many records you currently have enrolled in a sequence inside your Recruit CRM mailbox in the "My Sequence Enrollments" tab. This section provides a clear overview of the number of candidates and contacts currently enrolled in active sequences, as well as how many you can still enroll. Troubleshooting Problem: A candidate/contact does not appear in the enrollment list Likely cause: The record has opted out of emails, is already enrolled in a sequence, or does not have an email address. What to check: Verify that the record has a valid email address, has not opted out of email communication, and is not already enrolled in another sequence. Resolution: Add a valid email address if one is missing, update email preferences if consent has been obtained, or un-enroll the record from the existing sequence before enrolling them in a new one. FAQs What happens if I edit a sequence that already has active enrollments? Changes made to a sequence will only apply to future enrollments. Candidates or contacts who are already enrolled will continue following the version of the sequence they were enrolled in. What happens when a candidate or contact replies to a sequence email? When a recipient replies to an email in the sequence, the sequence is automatically paused and the candidate or contact is unenrolled to prevent further automated follow-ups. Conclusion: Using sequence enrollment in Recruit CRM, you can automate structured outreach, customize messages at enrollment time, and stay in control of who is enrolled and when. If you need more help with a specific sequence or enrollment scenario, please reach out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance.
