t: Managing Your Recruit CRM Subscription
s: This article will help you better understand Recruit CRM's pricing plans & billing process.
h: What are the different plans we offer?
What are the different ways you can pay?
1. Monthly
2. Annual
Is it possible to switch between the plans?
What are the record limits for each plan?
What are the cancellation policies?
FAQs
b: Recruit CRM offers flexible subscription plans that let you choose the features, billing cycle, and account capacity that best suit your recruitment team's needs. You can select from Pro , Business , and Enterprise plans, choose monthly or annual billing , manage record limits for candidates, contacts, companies, and jobs, and purchase additional record capacity i.e, data add-ons, without adding user seats. What are the different plans we offer? Recruit CRM offers three plans designed for teams of different sizes: Pro Plan Click here to explore the features included in our Pro plan! Business Plan Click here to explore the features included in our Business plan! Enterprise Plan Click here to explore the features included in the Enterprise plan! You can check the pricing for each plan from here: Recruit CRM Pricing What are the different ways you can pay? 1. Monthly With monthly billing, you're charged for your provisioned seats at the beginning of your billing cycle every month. 2. Annual The Annual billing option charges you a discounted per-month rate upfront for the whole year. Please note: Although you have the flexibility to reassign deactivated seats to new users, it's important to understand that we do not offer refunds or credits for unused time on these seats. The currency and the amount you pay will differ depending on the country in which your company is based. Is it possible to switch between the plans? You can change/review your current plan anytime by going to the Plans in Admin Settings. Click here to learn how to switch or upgrade your plan! For any switch you make, the immediate charges will be calculated on a pro-rated basis for the remaining days in your billing cycle. The full cost of the new plan will only be charged when your account renews in the next billing cycle. What are the record limits for each plan? Free Trial Pro Plan Business Plan Enterprise Plan Candidates 50 10,000 per user 20,000 per user 30,000 per user Companies 50 10,000 per user 20,000 per user 30,000 per user Contacts 50 10,000 per user 20,000 per user 30,000 per user Jobs 4 Unlimited Unlimited Unlimited The candidate, company, and contact limits shown above are calculated per user and then the per-user limit is multiplied by the number of users to determine the account's overall record capacity. For example: • Pro Plan : If your account has 3 users , your total record limit will be 30,000 Candidates, 30,000 Companies, and 30,000 Contacts (10,000 × 3 users). • Business Plan : If your account has 5 users , your total record limit will be 100,000 Candidates, 100,000 Companies, and 100,000 Contacts (20,000 × 5 users). • Enterprise Plan : If your account has 10 users , your total record limit will be 300,000 Candidates, 300,000 Companies, and 300,000 Contacts (30,000 × 10 users). Record limits are calculated at the account level , not at the individual user level . All users share the same combined pool of Candidate, Company, and Contact records. The per-user limit does not cap how many records a single user can create inside the system. Any user with the required permissions can create more records, provided the account has not reached its total record limit. If you need to increase the data limit on your account, we have your back with our 'Additional Records Limit'! An 'Additional Records Limit' is a monthly add-on to your subscription. It allows you to increase the storage limits for your account by adding 10,000 more candidates, contacts, and company records each, without you having to pay for a complete additional user. The Add-Ons will also sync with the account renewal dates. For example: If 3 add-ons of $25 each are subscribed to on the 20th of the month and the renewal date is the 1st, only one-third of the amount (prorated) i.e., $25, will be charged immediately. On the 1st of next month, the entire amount of $75 will be charged along with the user subscription fee. A similar prorated calculation will be done for the annual purchase of Add-ons. Click here to learn how to purchase an add-on! What are the cancellation policies? Please note that any changes to the account or any payment-related issues should be done/communicated to us before the renewal date to avoid getting charged on your renewal. Upon cancellation of your account, you will not incur any charges from the next billing date onward. However, it's important to note that as per our Terms and Conditions , no refunds will be issued for any unused portion of your subscription. FAQs Q1. What plans does Recruit CRM offer? Recruit CRM currently offers three plans: Pro, Business, and Enterprise. Q2. How does monthly billing work? With monthly billing, you are charged for your provisioned seats at the beginning of your billing cycle every month. Q3. Can I get a refund if I deactivate a user or cancel early? No. While you can reassign deactivated seats to new users, Recruit CRM does not offer refunds or credits for unused time on those seats or for any unused portion of your subscription after cancellation. Conclusion: Managing your Recruit CRM subscription effectively means understanding your plan options, billing cycle, record limits, and cancellation terms so you can align the system with your recruitment needs and budget. If you have specific questions about your account, billing, or limits, reach out to Recruit CRM support for tailored assistance. t: Mark Email Conversations as Public/Private
s: This article will help you learn how to hide specific email conversations with candidates or contacts from your team members in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
How to Mark Emails Private or Public
1. From the Mailbox
2. From a Candidate or Contact Profile
FAQs
Who can mark an email conversation as private or public?
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Public/Private Email feature allows you to control the visibility of individual emails in Recruit CRM. When an email is marked as Private: It will be hidden from the Related Emails tab in the Candidate or Contact record. It will not be visible to your team members. You can still access it from your Private Emails folder in your Mailbox. Marking an email as Public makes it visible to your team wherever related emails are displayed in the system. This feature is particularly useful when you need to: Keep sensitive candidate or client email conversations private. Hide specific emails without disabling email sharing for all emails. Control which email conversations are visible to your team. Before you begin: By default, this feature is available to Admins and the Account Owner. Business Plan users can also create a custom role and grant permission to users in that role to Make an email conversation private in the related email tab. ​ Only the sender (email owner) can mark their emails as private or public. 📥 How to Mark Emails Private or Public 1. From the Mailbox Navigate to Mailbox in Recruit CRM. Select the email(s) you would like to make private by checking the box next to each email. You can also use the checkbox at the top to select all visible emails. Click Make Email Private . Once Emails marked as private: The selected emails will be hidden from other team members. They will no longer appear in the Related Emails tab of linked candidate or contact records. They will remain visible to you in your mailbox, including the Private Email tab and the All Email section. Additionally, if you'd like to make private emails visible to your team again, simply select the desired emails in your mailbox and click Make Email Public . The emails will then reappear in the Related Emails tab of the associated candidate and contact records. 2. From a Candidate or Contact Profile Open the relevant Candidate or Contact profile. Navigate to the Related Emails tab and open the email conversation you want to manage. Click the lock icon in the top-right corner of the email and select Make This Conversation Private . Please note: After the conversation is marked as private, the conversation will remain accessible only to you and the email recipients, including anyone added in CC or BCC . To make the conversation visible to your team again, click the lock icon and select Make This Conversation Public . FAQs Who can mark an email conversation as private or public? Only the email sender (email owner) can change the visibility of their email conversations by marking them as private or public. Conclusion: Using the public/private email controls in Recruit CRM, you can keep sensitive or internal conversations hidden while still collaborating effectively with your team. If you need more help with email visibility, you can reach out to support using the blue chat box at the bottom-right of your Recruit CRM screen. t: Mark email IDs and Domains as Confidential (New UI)
s: This article explains how to mark email IDs and domains as confidential in Recruit CRM so that email communication with specific candidates, contacts, or entire domains is hidden from the rest of your team.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
How to block an email ID or domain
How to unblock an email ID or domain
Troubleshooting
Problem: Emails with a candidate or contact are missing from the Related Emails tab.
Problem: You cannot unblock a specific email ID.
FAQs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? This feature gives you the ability to hide all email communication with specific Candidates/ Contacts or a specific domain of your choice from the rest of your team by making their email IDs confidential. You can add individual candidate or contact email addresses, or entire domains, to a blocked list. Once blocked, all sent and received emails associated with those email addresses or domains are hidden from: The Related Emails tab on candidate, contact, and company records. The Sent Email Conversation KPI in Team Performance Reports. These emails remain visible only within your personal mailbox in Recruit CRM, helping you control who can access sensitive or confidential communications. This feature is especially useful when: • You need to keep communication with certain candidates or contacts private from other team members. • You want to hide all emails associated with a specific client or company domain. Before you begin: Please Note Only the account owner, admins, and users with custom permissions can block email IDs and domains. Making an email ID or domain confidential is account-specific. All email exchanges with that email ID or domain and any user on your account will be hidden from the rest of the users. Blocked emails will still be visible in your personal mailbox within Recruit CRM. How to block an email ID or domain Click on your profile icon in Recruit CRM and navigate to Email Settings → Blocked Emails/Domains . Click Add to Blocked List . In the popup window, enter the email address or domain you want to block, then select the appropriate email ID, candidate, contact, or domain from the suggestions. Review the selected email address or domain and click Save . • A message will appear in the Related Emails tab indicating that the email address or domain has been blocked. • A Blocked tag will appear alongside the email communication in your mailbox and in Team Performance Reports, indicating that the emails are confidential. How to unblock an email ID or domain Account owner control: If the account owner blocks an email ID, other users will not be able to unblock it. Only the account owner can unblock an email ID that they have blocked. Click on your profile in Recruit CRM and navigate to Email Settings → Blocked Emails/Domains . ​ Locate the email address or domain you want to unblock. You can use the search bar to quickly find a specific blocked email address or domain. Click Unblock next to the relevant email address or domain and confirm your selection. Once unblocked, the email address or domain is removed from the blocked list, and email communication associated with it will no longer be treated as confidential. All the related emails will again be visible according to your account's normal email visibility settings. Troubleshooting Problem: Emails with a candidate or contact are missing from the Related Emails tab. Likely cause: Their email ID or domain has been blocked (marked as confidential). What to check: Open Email Settings and go to the Blocked Emails and Domains tab. Search for the candidate’s email ID or their domain. Resolution: If you have permission and the email is blocked, click Unblock next to the email ID or domain to restore visibility. Problem: You cannot unblock a specific email ID. Likely cause: The email ID was blocked by the account owner. What to check: Confirm that the email ID appears in the blocked list and that the Unblock option is not available for your role. Resolution: Contact the account owner and request that they unblock the email ID, as only the account owner can unblock email IDs they have blocked. FAQs What happens when I block an email ID or domain in Recruit CRM? When you block an email ID or domain, all sent and received email communication with that email ID or domain is hidden from the Related Emails tab and the Sent Email Conversation KPI in Team Performance Reports, and remains visible only in your personal mailbox. Who can block email IDs and domains? Only the account owner, admins, and users with custom permissions can block email IDs and domains in Recruit CRM. Is blocking an email ID or domain account wide? Yes. Making an email ID or domain confidential is account-specific. All email exchanges with that email ID or domain and any user on your account will be hidden from the rest of the users. How can I tell if an email is blocked? You will see a specific message in the Related Emails tab for that profile, and a blocked tag will appear for their email communication inside your mailbox and in the Team Performance Report. Conclusion: Using the confidential email (blocked emails and domains) feature in Recruit CRM lets you control who can see sensitive email communication with specific candidates, contacts, or domains while keeping your own records complete. t: Meeting Scheduler
s: This article will guide you on how you can generate meeting scheduling links to share with candidates and contacts.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to create a schedule page (meeting scheduler link)
Further Customizations
How to share the Meeting Schedule Page?
Troubleshooting
Problem: I cannot create a scheduling page
Problem: Booked meetings are not visible in my calendar
Problem: Images are not displaying on the scheduling page
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Meeting Scheduler helps streamline the process of scheduling meetings with candidates and contacts by allowing them to book a meeting directly based on your availability. Instead of coordinating schedules through multiple emails or messages, you can share a personalized booking link that lets recipients select a suitable time from your available slots directly from a personalized booking page. The feature automatically syncs booked meetings with your connected calendar and allows you to customize availability, event settings, booking forms, confirmation behavior, email notifications, and scheduling page branding. Use this feature when: • You want candidates or contacts to book meetings directly based on your availability from a personalized booking page. . • You need a reusable scheduling link that can be shared in emails, messages, or workflows. Click here to know how syncing your calendar to Recruit CRM works Note: This feature is available on all plans (Free plan, Pro, Business, and Enterprise) 🗓️ How to create a schedule page (meeting scheduler link) 1. Click on the Profile icon and select the 'Meeting Scheduler' option. 2. Click on the 'Create New' button. If you haven't connected your email or calendar in Recruit CRM then you will be prompted to connect your email and calendar in order to create a schedule page. Note : We recommend connecting the same/default email ID to your 'Calendar Settings' to ensure the visibility of scheduled meetings in Recruit CRM. Meetings booked through the scheduler's link will be added to the connected email ID's calendar. 3. You will now be prompted to choose the event type. Select the type of scheduling page you would like to create: • One-on-One Bookings – Ideal for interviews, screening calls, consultations, or any meeting involving one organizer and one participant. • Group or Class Bookings – Best suited for events where one organizer hosts multiple participants, such as webinars, training sessions, or group discussions. Once selected, Recruit CRM will configure the scheduling page based on the chosen meeting type. ​ 4. Add the details regarding the meeting. Event Name : You can add the title of the event/meeting type. Event Duration : Select the duration of the meeting from the available options. Event Meeting or Location : In the event location, you can see options such as: None Custom Location Google Meet or Teams, based on the email that you have connected. Notes: To add Zoom as the event location, you can add the Zoom link by selecting the 'Custom Location' option, similarly, for other apps as well. If you have an Outlook free account, then in the meeting location, when you select Teams and send the scheduled link, candidates/contacts can book the call, but it will not contain the automated meeting link of Microsoft Teams. This will work for Outlook Premium accounts only. 5. You can select the calendar where you want to add event bookings and click on 'Create'. 6. Under the 'Event Info' tab you can add the event description under the Event Description section. Further Customizations After creating the event, you can further customize your scheduling page by configuring availability, booking rules, form fields, notifications, confirmation settings, and page branding. 1. Customizations under the 'Availability' Tab. Under the 'Availability' Tab, you will be able to: Select the calendar where you want to add event bookings. Select the calendars to use for checking your availability. Set when you're regularly available for event bookings. 2. Customizations under the 'Participants' Tab. Under this tab, you can: Add people in your team or organization to join the event as participants Set participant open hours. If not set, the default open hours will be used to calculate availability for this participant. 3. Customizations under the 'Booking Options' Tab. Under the 'Booking Options' tab, you can: Customize what to be shown when a booking is confirmed. You can either display the default confirmation page or redirect users to your own confirmation page. Set empty buffer time before and after an event, Event limits and Time slot intervals, and other Additional settings (Allow Guests to invite additional guests, hide reschedule and cancellation buttons on the booking page). 4. Customizations under the 'Booking Form' Tab. Under this tab, you will be able to add custom fields to the booking form. 5. Customizations under the 'Communications' Tab Under this tab, you will be able to: Set up automatic confirmation emails. Customize the Booking confirmation email and set reminders before emails. 6. Customizations under the 'Page Styles' Tab. Under this tab, you can set the Scheduling Page name and Page styling. Note: Images used in the Meeting Scheduler must be publicly accessible, served over HTTPS, and not restricted by authentication, IP blocking, or anti-bot rules. Hosting images on S3, a CDN, or the company website is the recommended approach. And to save all your customizations, you need to click on the 'Save Changes' option and click on the 'Back' button. To preview your customized Schedule Page, you can click on the 'eye icon' at the bottom of the page. ➡️ How to share the Meeting Schedule Page? Click on the three dots icon on the Meeting Scheduler page and select the 'Copy Link' option. You can paste this link in your email/while sending an SMS as well to share it with candidates and contacts. You will even have options to edit, preview, and delete the schedule page. Once the candidate/contact clicks on the shared link, they will be able to select the time slots to schedule the meeting, add their details, and schedule the meeting. The meeting confirmation emails will be sent to you and the candidate/contact. Once the meeting is scheduled, the candidate/contact will have the option to 'cancel' and 'reschedule' the meeting as well. Troubleshooting Problem: I cannot create a scheduling page Likely cause : Calendar or email is not connected. ​ What to check: Confirm your calendar is connected in the Meeting Scheduler area. Check whether you have connected your email in Recruit CRM. Resolution: Connect your calendar when prompted in the Meeting Scheduler. If you are prompted to connect email, complete the email connection process, then try creating the scheduling page again. Problem: Booked meetings are not visible in my calendar Likely cause : The wrong email ID or calendar is connected, or the target calendar is not selected in the event settings. What to check: Verify which email ID is connected to Recruit CRM. Confirm which calendar is selected under the event’s calendar options and under the Availability tab. Resolution: Connect and use the same default email ID in your calendar settings and in Recruit CRM. Ensure the correct calendar is selected for adding event bookings. Problem: Images are not displaying on the scheduling page Likely cause: Images are not publicly accessible or not served correctly. What to check: Confirm that images are served over HTTPS. Ensure images are not behind authentication, IP blocking, or anti-bot rules. R esolution: Host images on S3, a CDN, or your company website. Make sure the image URLs are publicly accessible over HTTPS before adding them to the Page Styles tab. Problem: Candidates or contacts cannot reschedule or cancel meetings Likely cause : Reschedule and cancellation buttons are hidden in Booking Options. What to check: Open the Booking Options tab for the event and review whether reschedule and cancellation buttons are enabled or hidden. R esolution: Enable the reschedule and cancellation buttons if you want candidates and contacts to manage their own bookings from the booking page. 🤔 FAQ's What happens if I have two email connections? If you have multiple emails connected, meetings will be scheduled on the calendar associated with your default email . What happens if my email connection is lost? If your email connection is lost, a warning message will notify you, and new meetings will not sync until you reconnect your email. Where can I see scheduled meetings within Recruit CRM? Meetings are accessible on the Meetings List Page , Calendar View , and in the connected calendar . How do I add or upload my logo to the Meeting Scheduler? You can open the scheduler editor by clicking on Edit beside the Scheduling page: Click on the Communications tab. Here you can enter your Company Logo URL: This logo appears in the booking confirmation email. Please note that the URL must be publicly accessible. The image will be scaled down to a max size of 200px x 100px. Conclusion: Using the Meeting Scheduler in Recruit CRM, you can create customizable scheduling pages, share a single link with candidates and contacts, and have all confirmed meetings automatically added to your connected calendar. t: Meeting Type Customization
s: This article explains how to customize meeting types in Recruit CRM so you can better categorize and manage your meetings.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

b: What this feature does and when to use it? Meeting type customization lets you create and manage custom meeting types in Recruit CRM. You can add new meeting types, name them, and set one as the default. This helps you tag and categorize meetings in a way that matches your recruitment process, making it easier for you and your team to identify and manage different types of communication. You can use this feature when: When you want to create custom meeting types that match your internal workflow. When your team needs clearer tagging and categorization of meetings. Before you begin: Only users with access to the admin settings on the Business plan and above can customize meeting types. On the Pro plan, only Account Owners and users with the admin role can perform meeting type customization. On the Business plan and above, you can also grant access to meeting type customization to team members with custom roles. Customize meeting types 1. Go to Admin Settings > click on Meeting Type Customization under CRM Process Customization. 2. Click on the Customize button. 3. Click on Add New Status . 4. Enter a name (up to fifty characters) for your meeting type. To make this the default meeting type, check the box next to it. Click the Save Status button to save your new meeting type. 5. You can also customize the default meeting types by editing the corresponding meeting type name to suit your needs. ​ ​ Please notice that you can also add the Meeting Type while adding a meeting through Recruit CRM's Chrome Extension . Please Note - The number of available meeting types is a total of 100, including 2 meeting types available in the system by default, i.e, Client Meeting and Internal Meeting. Meeting Type Customization access for Custom roles: Additionally, on the Business plan and above, you can grant access to the "Meeting Type Customization" option to your team members on custom roles as well. Here's how you can do this: ​ 1. Go to your User Management settings in the admin settings . 2. Click on the Roles and Permissions tab. Find the role you want to update and click the three-dot icon next to that role click on Edit. 3.Scroll down and turn on the toggle for Meeting type customization . 4.Click the Save Role button to apply the permission changes. Troubleshooting Problem: You cannot see the Meeting Type Customization option in Admin Settings. Likely cause: Your user role or plan does not have permission to customize meeting types. What to check: Confirm that your account is on the Business plan or Pro plan. On the Pro plan, confirm that you are an Account Owner or have the Admin role. On the Business plan and above, confirm that your custom role has the meeting type customization toggle turned on. Resolution: Ask an Account Owner to either perform the customization or update your role permissions as described in the steps above. Problem: You cannot add more meeting types. Likely cause: You have reached the maximum limit of thirty meeting types (including the two default system meeting types). What to check: Count your existing meeting types to confirm if you have reached the total of thirty. Resolution: Remove or repurpose existing meeting types if you need to add new ones. FAQs How many meeting types can I create in Recruit CRM? You can have a total of thirty meeting types, including the two meeting types available in the system by default. What happens if I reach the meeting type limit? If you reach the total of thirty meeting types, you will not be able to add more until you remove or adjust existing meeting types. Conclusion: Customizing meeting types in Recruit CRM helps you better categorize and manage your meetings, giving your team clearer visibility into different types of communication. t: Merging duplicate records
s: This article will help you merge Candidates, Contacts, and Companies in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Merging Duplicate Records
How Recruit CRM Detects Duplicate Records
Troubleshooting
Problem : A duplicate record was created even though details match.
FAQs
1. What happens to the secondary record after merging?
2. What happens to a candidate’s hiring stage when two candidates are merged?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Merge feature in Recruit CRM allows you to combine duplicate candidate, contact, company, or job records into a single primary record, helping maintain a clean and accurate database. When records are merged, the primary record is retained while the duplicate record is removed, reducing confusion in reporting, communication, and day-to-day operations. This feature is particularly useful when: Duplicate records are created through CSV/Excel imports or manual data entry. The same candidate, contact, or company exists with different email addresses, phone numbers, or other contact details. You need to consolidate duplicate records to maintain a clean and accurate database. Common Causes of Duplicate Records Duplicate records can be created in the following scenarios: The same candidate, contact, or company is added multiple times using different email addresses, phone numbers, or other unique identifiers. A CSV or Excel file containing duplicate entries is imported into Recruit CRM more than once. The same company is added under slightly different names, such as Apple Inc. and Apple Incorporation . The Allow Duplicates setting is enabled in Account Management Settings , allowing duplicate records to be created. Merging Duplicate Records The process for merging candidates, contacts, and companies is the same. Navigate to the candidate, contact, or company record that you want to keep as the primary record . Click the three-dot menu located in the top-right corner of the record and select Merge . If you are unable to see the merge candidate option, then you have to first make it visible by customizing the options. ​ Click here to explore how you can customise the Candidate Actions for Quick Access view In the merge window, search for and select the duplicate record that you would like to merge into the primary record. Please Note- When a merge is completed, the secondary record is permanently deleted from the system and cannot be restored. Please verify that you have selected the correct primary and duplicate records before proceeding. Once you have selected the duplicate record, click Merge to begin the merge process. Recruit CRM will display a confirmation message indicating that the merge request has been initiated. After the merge is processed, you will receive a notification confirming that the records have been successfully combined. (Old UI) - During the merge process, only empty fields in the primary record are updated with data from the secondary record. Any existing information in the primary record remains unchanged and will not be overwritten. It's also possible to merge jobs in Recruit CRM! Click here to learn How to Merge Jobs How Recruit CRM Detects Duplicate Records Recruit CRM automatically checks for duplicate records when new candidates, contacts, or companies are added to your database. How duplicates are handled depends on the Allow Duplicates setting in your Account Management Settings . The following fields are used to identify duplicates: Record Type Fields Checked Candidates Email Address, Phone Number, LinkedIn Profile URL Contacts Email Address, LinkedIn Profile URL Companies Company Name, Website URL, LinkedIn Profile URL When Allow Duplicates is OFF: Recruit CRM checks new records against existing records in your database. If a match is found, the existing record is updated instead of creating a duplicate. When Allow Duplicates is ON: Recruit CRM allows duplicate records to be created, even when matching information already exists in the database. Troubleshooting Problem : A duplicate record was created even though details match. Likely cause: The “Allow Duplicate” setting is turned On. What to check: Open Account Management and confirm the toggle for "Allow duplicates" is set to off. Resolution: If you want to prevent automatic duplicate creation, set “Allow Duplicate” to Off. Then manually merge any existing duplicates. FAQs 1. What happens to the secondary record after merging? The secondary record is permanently deleted from Recruit CRM once the merge is complete. Its data is combined into the primary record. 2. What happens to a candidate’s hiring stage when two candidates are merged? When duplicate candidate records are merged, assignment histories from both records are preserved to maintain a complete view of the candidate’s journey. If both records contain assignments for the same job, all unique stage histories are retained under the Candidate History tab. When the same stage exists in both records, the system keeps the entry with the older Stage Updated On date. Any stage containing client feedback or internal remarks is always retained, even if the hiring stage appears duplicated. The candidate’s current hiring stage for a job is determined based on the stage with the most recent assignment date. These retained histories are also reflected in Candidate Lifecycle Reports , ensuring accurate reporting and full visibility after a merge. Conclusion Merging duplicate records helps keep your Recruit CRM database clean, organized, and accurate. By understanding how duplicate detection works and using the Merge feature when needed, you can prevent duplicate entries, maintain complete record histories, and ensure reliable reporting across your account. t: Merging Jobs
s: This article will help you merge Jobs in Recruit CRM.
h: Merging duplicate jobs
b: If you think two or more jobs in the database are duplicated, Recruit CRM allows you to merge these records. Merging duplicate jobs 1. Go to a primary job with which you want to merge the other job. 2. Click on the three dots on the right and select "Merge Job". 3. You can then search and select the job you want to merge the primary job with. Please keep in mind that the selected job will be deleted after merging into the primary job. Only the empty fields in the primary job will be updated with new data from the selected job No existing data on the primary job will get overridden while merging. You won't be allowed to do the merging process if the secondary job has: A draft/live job campaign (requires deletion before merging). An active external job posting (must be taken offline first). If the job has approved Timesheets. Also, if the secondary job has any Executive Search Reports , you will be notified. Candidates are retained in the merged job. If a candidate is in both jobs and has any common stages for both jobs, then their oldest assignment entry (for that stage) will be preserved. 4. Once you click on the merge button, the system will give you an intimation that the process has been initiated. The Online Candidate Link for the secondary job will be disabled post-merge. 5. You will receive a notification once the merge is complete. Hope this helps! t: Nested Custom Fields
s: This article will guide you on how you can create nested custom fields
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to create Nested Custom Fields
Troubleshooting
Problem: Child options are not appearing when a parent value is selected
Problem: Parent field type cannot be selected in dependency setup
FAQs
Why do we need nested custom fields?
Can I create dependencies for default fields?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Nested Custom Fields feature allows you to create parent-child relationships between custom fields, ensuring that only relevant field options are displayed based on selections. This helps organize complex data more effectively, improves data accuracy, reduces input errors, and provides a more guided data entry experience for your team. Use this feature when: • You want to improve data organization across Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs, or Deals. • You want to reduce data entry errors by displaying only relevant choices. • You are managing complex data sets that require multiple levels of field dependencies. ​ Important Notes Nested Fields are available for all entities (Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs, and Deals) in the Admin Settings under the respective Custom Fields section. One Child field can have only one direct Parent field. Multi-level dependencies are supported up to 5 levels deep, i.e., each parent field can have up to 5 child fields (siblings). ​ Unlinking a Parent-Child Relationship is possible only if the child field has no dependencies. ​ Deleting Parent Fields is restricted until all child fields are unlinked. 🔗 How to create Nested Custom Fields 1. Navigate to the Admin Settings . 2. Under 'Data Customization ', choose the entity to which you want to add nested custom fields. 3. As usual, create the custom fields that you would like to link/connect by clicking on the '+ New Custom Field'. Note : Parent Fields support only Checkbox (Yes/No), Dropdown, and Multiselect custom field types, whereas Child Fields support all custom field types. 4. Now, to establish the parent-child relationship between the custom fields created, you need to click on the 'Add' option next to the 'Field Dependency' section. 5. Select the 'Parent field' and the 'Child field' from the dropdown list. 6. Now you can 'Map the Dependency' according to your requirements i.e., you can select the 'Child field' options that need to be shown when a specific option is selected under the 'Parent field' and click on 'Save'. 7. To view the linked fields, you can click on the 'View' option next to the 'Field Dependency' section. 8. You can unlink/edit/add more fields by selecting the respective option under the 'Dependency Actions' column. 9. All the created nested custom fields will be visible under the Additional Information (Custom Fields) section: Troubleshooting Problem: Child options are not appearing when a parent value is selected Likely cause: The dependency mapping between the parent and child options is incomplete or incorrect. What to check: Open the dependency configuration and verify that each relevant parent option has the correct child options mapped. Resolution: Update the mappings so that the desired child options are associated with the appropriate parent options, then save and retest. Problem: Parent field type cannot be selected in dependency setup Likely cause: The field type is not supported as a parent. What to check: Confirm the field type of the intended parent field in the custom field settings. Resolution: Use only supported parent field types (checkbox, yes/no, drop-down, or multi-select). If needed, recreate the parent field using one of these types. 🤔 FAQs Why do we need nested custom fields? Flat custom fields make data entry disorganized. Nested fields allow logical structuring , reducing errors and improving efficiency. Can I create dependencies for default fields? No, only custom fields can be used for nested relationships. Can a child field have multiple parent fields? No, a child field can have only one parent , but a parent can have multiple child fields . What happens if I delete a parent field? You cannot delete a parent field until all its child fields are unlinked. What happens if I edit dropdown options in a parent field? If an option is already used in a dependency, editing/removal is restricted to prevent breaking the nested structure. Is there a limit to how many nested levels I can create? Yes, 5 levels deep per nested relationship and 5 child fields per parent . Conclusion: Nested custom fields in Recruit CRM help you control which options and fields appear based on previous selections, making data entry cleaner, more accurate, and easier to manage. b: The new Candidates Details or Profile page in Recruit CRM brings a cleaner layout, smarter organization, and greater customization across every section. From managing candidate details to tracking activity and assignments, the updated UI helps streamline everyday recruiting tasks. ✨ Here is the list of all the key features: 🧩 Candidate actions The new UI allows you to perform a wide range of candidate-related actions directly from the top corner of the candidate profile. You can perform several actions for a candidate directly from the details page, including: Requesting an updated profile Adding the candidate to a hotlist Enrolling the candidate in a sequence Pitching the candidate Editing the candidate record Merging candidate records Generating a formatted resume Opting the candidate out of emails Marking the candidate as off limits Creating an invoice Deleting the candidate This layout makes it easier to scan and quickly find the action you need. You can also customize and rearrange these actions based on how frequently you use them, making your workflow more efficient. You can click on the three dots menu to view more actions. Click here to explore how you can customise the Candidate Actions for Quick Access view Click on the three dots on the candidate’s details page and select Customize Options at the bottom of the list. ​ Drag and drop your top five most frequently used actions to the top of the list and click Save to apply the changes. ​ Once saved, these selected actions will be directly accessible at the top of the candidate’s details page, making them quicker and easier to use. Account Owners can set the default action visible for the team from the Others View section. They can also choose to lock this view by selecting the option that prevents other users from editing or changing it. ​ ​ Please note: Users may still be able to modify field order and visibility even when the view is locked at the account level, if the permission “Allow users to override locked view layouts” is enabled in their role. By default, this permission is enabled for the Admin role and disabled for Team Member and Restricted Team Member roles. b: 🎉The new version of our Candidate List page is designed to streamline your recruitment process with enhanced features and an intuitive design. It offers a sleek, more user-friendly design that allows you to effortlessly navigate and manage candidate profiles, ensuring seamless candidate management and an overall smoother recruitment experience. 🚀 To switch to the new version, click on the 'Profile icon' and select the 'Switch to New Version' option. You can switch back to the previous design at any time by using the same option. Here is the list of all the key features: 🔢 Display of Count in the Quick View You can view the total count of records in the Candidate View section. The Quick View also shows the total count of Hotlists and Saved Searches, along with the count of records present in those hotlists. You can edit, pin, and delete hotlists by clicking on the three dots next to each Hotlist. Similarly, you can edit, pin, clone and delete the Saved Searches as well. You can minimize and maximize the Candidate View, Candidate Hotlists and Saved Searches sections by using the arrow icon next to each section. ∞ Infinite Scroll option With the infinite scroll feature, you can view the candidates continuously as you scroll, without switching between pages. When a user lands on the candidate list page, the first 100 records are loaded initially. If the user bulk-selects the records, all the 100 records are selected. You can scroll manually to select more records and the records will be automatically selected up to 3000. You can click on the 'Scroll to Top' button to scroll to the top of the list. Bulk Selection on the List page When selecting candidates in bulk, Recruit CRM offers multiple ways to choose records: Header checkbox: Selects the first 50 loaded records. As you continue scrolling, 50 additional records are automatically selected at a time. Custom Record Selection: Click the arrow next to the header checkbox , enter any number between 1 and 3,000 , and click Select to choose the exact number of records based on the current list order. Please note: Custom Record Selection replaces any existing manual or bulk selection. Once a custom selection has been applied, automatic scroll-based selection is disabled until the selection is cleared. Only numeric values between 1 and 3,000 are accepted. If a value greater than 3,000 is entered, Recruit CRM displays an error message. When 3,000 records are already selected, the Select All option is disabled. ✅ Candidate Bulk Actions Display of important bulk actions upfront The 5 most commonly used bulk actions are listed upfront by default, and the other options are listed under the 'More' tab. The options to be shown upfront by default can be customized as well. Customization of Bulk Actions to be shown upfront: 1. Click on the 'Customize Bulk Action' option under the 'More' tab. 2. Move the Options above the dashed line to show them outside the 'More' Dropdown and click on the 'Save' button. How to set up a default bulk action arrangement for the entire account If you are the Account Owner you can set up a default bulk action arrangement on the Candidate List Page for all users in the account. While customizing the bulk actions, you'll have the option to switch to "Others View". All changes you make in this view will apply to all the users in your account. If you wish to enforce the bulk action arrangement and prevent the users from having a different setup, you can simply tick the checkbox 'Do not allow users of your account to edit their view' This will ensure that the account owner's bulk actions arrangement remains the same for all users in the account. Users with an Admin role or custom permissions will still be able to rearrange the actions even if the toggle is on. ​ If you're creating/editing a custom role, you just need to make sure to enable the "Allow User to Choose their Own Field Order and Visibility" ​ Export All Candidates 📥 This will allow you to export all the candidate records in a section, beyond the 3,000-record limit, while still respecting any filters you've applied. How to export all candidates at once? ↔ Candidate Column Level Actions You can click on the arrow button to perform column level actions: Pin Column You have the option to pin a column in order to freeze its position at the left/right of the screen, allowing other columns to remain scrollable for improved readability. Add column to Right/Left You can add columns to the right/left of the selected column by clicking the respective 'Add Column to Right/Left' options >>> Select the column >>> Click on 'Apply'. Note : Only the hidden columns will be displayed in the list while adding a column to the left or right. Sort the values in the columns in ascending/descending order You can sort the values in the column in ascending or descending order by clicking on the 'Sort Ascending/ Sort Descending' options. Multi Sorting You can apply multi-column sorting by clicking the arrow and selecting "Sort Ascending" or "Sort Descending" for different columns. Alternatively, you can hold the Shift key and click on multiple columns to enable multi-column sorting. Hide Column You can hide a specific column by clicking on the 'Hide Column' option. 👀 Show/ Hide Columns To show/ hide columns, click on the 'Show/Hide Columns' option next to the 'Resume Parser' button. You can even view the count of the 'Visible Columns' and 'Hidden Columns' as well. Note: If you pin a column, you will be able to unpin it from the Show/Hide Columns section as well. ​ How to set up a default column arrangement for the entire account If you are the Account Owner, you can set up a default column arrangement on the Candidate List Page for all users in the account. While customizing the visibility of columns, you'll have the option to switch to "Others View". All changes you make in this view will apply to all the users in your account. If you wish to enforce the column arrangement and prevent the users from having a different setup, you can simply tick the checkbox 'Do not allow users to edit their view' This will ensure that the account owner's column arrangement remains the same for all users in the account. Users with an Admin role or custom permissions will still be able to rearrange the column even if the toggle is on. ​ If you're creating/editing a custom role, you just need to make sure to enable the "Allow User to Choose their Own Field Order and Visibility" ​ The 'Updated By' column is available on the Candidate list page similar to other entity list pages. In the Hide/Show Columns page, searching for a field scrolls to and highlights the matching field(s), with a counter (e.g., 1/2) to jump between matches. You can still drag and drop to reorder columns while a search is active. View and Edit Candidate Summary from the List Page To view or edit a candidate’s summary from the list page, click on the summary icon under the Summary column for a specific candidate. After the summary opens, click on Edit at the bottom right of the screen. You will be redirected to the candidate’s Summary page, where you can update the details and save the changes by clicking on Submit. ​ ​ 📝 Candidate Level Actions You can click on the three dots next to each candidate under the 'Name' Column to perform the following actions: -Edit Candidate -Add note -Add Call Log -Add Task - Add Meeting -Mark as Off-Limits -Merge Candidate -Opt out of Email -Delete Candidate Increase/Decrease the Width of each column You can hover over the margin next to the column name and drag it to increase/decrease the column width. You can even increase the width of the Quick View section as well. If a candidate has multiple skills, you can adjust the width of the Skills column to control how many skills are displayed directly in the column. Widen or reduce the Skills column as needed to display the skills based on your preferred view. At the maximum column width, hover over the additional skills indicator to view the remaining skills. ​ Switch to Classic View in New Advanced Search The “Switch to Classic View” feature allows users to quickly apply filters using the familiar grid modal, making searches faster and more intuitive for everyday workflows. Once switched to Classic View, users continue to see the grid modal by default when clicking Add Filters . Confirmation message appears when switching back to dropdown/compact view, warning that applied filters will be reset. Filters are treated as independent AND conditions. ⚠️ Important Note: The classic grid view does not support duplicate filters, group filters, or cross-entity filters. The dropdown-based advanced search interface remains fully functional and unchanged. You can switch back anytime using the Switch to Compact View button to the New Advanced Search. Hope this helps! 😊 Related Articles New Version Of The Company List Page New Version of Candidate Details Page New Version Of The Contact List Page New Version of The Jobs

t: Notes Restriction in Recruit CRM
s: This article will help you set restrictions on adding, viewing, editing & deleting notes based on the role assigned to users
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Configure Notes Restrictions
1. Notes permissions on the Pro Plan
2. Notes permissions on the Business Plan
Troubleshooting
Problem: A user cannot delete a note.
FAQ's
1. Can Team Members delete notes on the Pro Plan?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows users to add notes to records such as candidates, companies, contacts, jobs, and deals. The actions users can perform on notes such as adding, viewing, editing, or deleting, depend on their assigned role or custom role permissions. This feature is useful when you want to: Control who can add, view, edit, or delete notes. Manage note permissions based on user roles. Configure note access using Custom Roles. Prevent unauthorized deletion of notes. Configure Notes Restrictions Note: Note permissions work differently depending on whether your organization is on the Pro Plan or the Business Plan . 1. Notes permissions on the Pro Plan On the Pro Plan, the " Role " of the user would determine whether they can view, edit or delete the notes. The basic logic that applies to restrictions around notes is that when you are able to view a record, you can add notes to it. But you cannot delete a note unless you are the Admin or the Account Owner. Following are the 4 default roles and the restrictions that they have around notes: Account Owner: An account owner has access to the entire database. So they can add, view, edit, and delete any note associated with any record. Admin: The admin can also add, view edit, and delete any note associated with any record. Team Member: A team member can only add, edit, and view all the notes but cannot delete any notes from the database. Restricted Team Member: A restricted team member can only add and edit notes on the records that they have added to the system or made collaborators on. They won't be able to delete any notes P.S. It's set up like this to avoid data loss that happens due to the deletion of notes. 2. Notes permissions on the Business Plan On the Business Plan, the determining factor to add, view, edit, or delete the notes depends upon the permission of the role the user is assigned. Apart from the four default user roles, on the Business Plan, you can create new roles with custom access to the database. Set up Custom Roles The permissions configured for each entity determine what actions users can perform on notes associated with that entity. For example, if a user has permission to: View: Everything Edit: Everything Delete: Owned Only They can view and edit all notes under the candidates, but cannot delete notes that are added on candidates that are not owned by them. The same permissions apply to notes associated with the following entities: Candidates, Companies, Contacts, Jobs, Deals. In cases, where the note is added to a candidate who is owned by the user and associated with records that are not owned by them, they can still delete the notes from all the records as they have the delete permission for the candidate record, which was the primary record where the note was added. Troubleshooting Problem: A user cannot delete a note. Likely Cause: The user's role or Custom Role does not include permission to delete notes. What to Check: Verify the user's assigned role. If you're on the Business Plan, review the Delete permission configured for the relevant entity in the user's Custom Role. Resolution: Update the user's role or modify the Custom Role permissions if the user should be allowed to delete notes. FAQ's 1. Can Team Members delete notes on the Pro Plan? No. Only Account Owners and Admins can delete notes on the Pro Plan. 2. Can I customize note permissions on the Business Plan? Yes. Note permissions are determined by the Custom Role permissions configured for each entity. 3. Why can a user delete a note associated with multiple records? The permission is determined by the ownership of the primary record where the note was originally created. Conclusion: Recruit CRM provides flexible note permissions based on user roles and Custom Roles, allowing administrators to control who can add, view, edit, and delete notes while protecting important information from accidental deletion. t: Obtaining consent for texting prospects
s: Learn how to obtain consent before texting prospects to ensure compliance.
h: Enabling consent through external pages
b: You can obtain consent from your candidates/contacts for texting and allow them to opt out whenever they request it. Gain consent through outbound SMS You can send SMS to candidates/contacts without requiring them to opt-in and can directly ask for opt-in through messages. You can also check in the details page if they have not given consent, next to meetings: In this scenario, it is necessary for you to include additional information on how to opt out of receiving SMS messages. The initial message that you send to take consent needs to include the following OPT IN and OPT OUT keywords: OPT-IN keywords: 'START' or 'YES' or 'SUBSCRIBE', or 'JOIN'. OPT-OUT keywords: 'STOP' or 'STOPALL' or 'UNSUBSCRIBE' or 'CANCEL' or 'END' or 'QUIT'. Once the text receiver replies with STOP or similar opt-out messages, Twilio blocks them from their end: You can also see a message on the details page indicating whether they’ve opted out of messages or emails: Opt-in through email You can also request opt-in through email from prospects by sending bulk emails. Obtain consent through external pages Recruit CRM also lets you obtain texting consent from prospects from different sections including the job application form, talent pool page, and profile update request form. There is an optional checkbox where candidates can subscribe to receive SMS updates about specific job opportunities. If the candidates have already given their consent, it simply updates on the candidate details page. This is how the consent checkbox appears at the bottom of external pages: 🧐 Enabling consent through external pages ​1. Go to Admin Settings > Job Application Form Settings / Talent Pool Page Settings / Profile Update Form Settings 2. Scroll down to locate: " Customize Button & Link Labels" , and look for the label "I'd like to receive SMS notifications about jobs at the provided phone number," which you can edit and choose to activate or hide. On the Job Application Form Settings , you can also edit the SMS Terms that your applicants can read before offering their consent. Hope this helps! b: What this feature does and when to use it? This feature ensures that you obtain and manage a prospect’s consent before sending them SMS from within Recruit CRM. It helps you stay compliant with messaging regulations. You can obtain consent from your candidates/contacts for texting and allow them to opt out whenever they request it. Use this feature whenever you want to send SMS/text messages to prospects. Gain consent through outbound SMS You can send SMS to candidates/contacts without requiring them to opt-in and can directly ask for opt-in through messages. You can also check on the details page if they have not given consent, under the 'SMS' tab: It is necessary for you to include additional information on how to opt out of receiving SMS messages. The initial message that you send to take consent needs to include the following OPT IN and OPT OUT keywords: OPT-IN keywords: 'START' or 'YES' or 'SUBSCRIBE', or 'JOIN'. OPT-OUT keywords: 'STOP' or 'STOPALL' or 'UNSUBSCRIBE' or 'CANCEL' or 'END' or 'QUIT'. Once the text receiver replies with STOP or similar opt-out messages, Twilio blocks them from their end: You can also see a message on the details page indicating whether they’ve opted out of messages or emails: Obtain consent through external pages Recruit CRM also lets you obtain texting consent from prospects from different sections, including the Job application form, Talent pool page, and Profile update request form. There is an optional checkbox where candidates can subscribe to receive SMS updates about specific job opportunities. If the candidates have already given their consent, it simply updates on the candidate details page. This is how the consent checkbox appears at the bottom of external pages: Record existing SMS consent manually If SMS consent has already been obtained outside Recruit CRM, you can record the existing consent directly in Recruit CRM instead of requesting consent again. To record existing consent: Open the SMS consent popup for the relevant candidate or contact by clicking on their contact number and selecting the Send Text Message button. Click Record SMS Consent Manually . Review the warning popup confirming that valid consent must have already been obtained from the prospect. ​ Confirm the consent to proceed with sending SMS. Please Note Recruit CRM does not verify consent recorded manually. You are responsible for ensuring that the consent is valid, properly documented, and compliant with applicable TCPA and carrier requirements . The Record SMS Consent Manually option is not available for records that are already opted in or have explicitly opted out. This option is available only when the account's texting region is the US . 🧐 Enabling consent through external pages ​1. Go to Admin Settings > Job Application Form Settings / Talent Pool Page Settings / Profile Update Form Settings 2. Scroll down to locate: " Customize Button & Link Labels" , and look for the label "I'd like to receive SMS notifications about jobs at the provided phone number," which you can edit and choose to activate or hide. On the Job Application Form Settings , you can also edit the SMS Terms that your applicants can read before offering their consent. 🤔FAQs How do I know if a candidate has opted out of SMS? Open the candidate/contact record and you will be able to see a message if they have opted out of SMS. What happens if a candidate replies STOP to my message? When a candidate replies with STOP or similar keywords (STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END, QUIT), Twilio automatically blocks further SMS messages to that number from their end. The candidate’s record in Recruit CRM will show that they have opted out. Conclusion: Obtaining and tracking SMS consent in Recruit CRM helps you communicate with candidates and contacts in a compliant, transparent way. t: Organic Posting Network (OPN)
s: This article will guide you on how to post jobs through Vonq's Organic Posting Network.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Organic Posting Network (OPN) , powered by VONQ , allows you to publish jobs from Recruit CRM to a network of 20+ free job boards through a single XML feed integration. Instead of manually posting jobs to multiple platforms, eligible jobs can be automatically distributed across participating job boards, helping you increase job visibility, reach a broader audience, and attract more candidates with minimal effort. Applications received through these job boards are captured directly in Recruit CRM, making it easier to track and manage applicants from a centralised location. Candidates who apply through the Organic Posting Network are identified within Recruit CRM, with the Source field displaying Organic Posting along with the associated job information. Use this feature when: • You want to publish jobs to multiple free job boards at the same time. • You want to increase the visibility of your open roles without paying for individual job board postings. Before you begin: Note: 1 Job posting credit or 25 Recruit CRM Credits will be consumed if you post the job through the organic posting network. You can buy Job Posting credits on a monthly or annual basis, irrespective of your subscription plan , directly from the job advertising module. Click here to know more about how to purchase credits Here is the list of all the job boards offered under OPN (going further, more job boards will be added): AboutJobs.com JobisJob Skillsire Adzuna.com Jobleads UWV.nl Alleskralle Jobrapido.com Vacatureplaats.nl Careerjet.com Jobtome Talent.com Jobatus.es Jooble OfferUp.com Jobcase.com Jora Jobisvertise JobGet Lensa LinkedIn Limited Listing Jobijoba.com Locanto Postjobfree JobInventory.com StudySmarter.de Twine.net Please note that the job might not get posted on all the job boards mentioned in the list. ​ VONQ does not guarantee the jobs to be posted on all job boards. The jobs will go on selective job boards only based on the parameters defined by the job boards. Example location, industry, specification, etc and filtering the jobs is Vonq’s discretion. ✅ How to get a job posted on the OPN job boards? The first step is to make sure all the necessary criteria are met for the jobs to be visible on the XML Feed and posted on the OPN job boards. Before you create a new job in Recruit CRM, please make sure you have ticked the job posting box inside Job Fields in Admin settings . This will help post your open jobs on your website and other job boards. The "Post On Job Boards" option should be selected inside Admin Settings >> Job Custom Fields ; ❌ Please note that if you untick the checkbox, none of your jobs will be posted. The necessary criteria to be met are: The job application form should be enabled. The Updated On date should be within the last 30 days; All the fields where you see the message "Required To Post On Partner Job Boards" (City, State, Country, Maximum Salary, Job Description, Currency, Salary Type) and "Required to post on Organic Job Boards" (Postal code, Job Function, Job Industry) need to have a value. You may enter either the full name or just the initials in the required fields (necessary for posting on job boards), as both options are acceptable. As LinkedIn Limited Listings is available as one of the OPN job boards, in order to post jobs on the company's LinkedIn page, the default 'LinkedIn Company ID' field needs to be filled with the LinkedIn company ID. Here is an article on how to find the LinkedIn Company ID. 'Note for candidates' should be filled in (only if the Job Description is uploaded as a file); ​ The job status should not be 'closed', 'on hold' or 'cancelled'; ​ ​ Account Logo needed to be uploaded. ​ Select "Organic Job Boards" under the XML Feeds section ⬇️⬇️⬇️ While creating a new job or editing an existing one, make sure you select "Organic Job Boards" in the XML Feeds section to get your jobs posted on the correct XML Feed. By selecting the appropriate XML feed, you can ensure that your jobs reach the intended audience through the most relevant job boards. You also have the option to preselect the XML feeds in the Build Job Feed XML page. This means the XML Feed will automatically be selected for all new jobs created. ​ If you don't want a job to be automatically posted on the Free Job Boards XML Feed you can simply disable the preselection on the Build Job Feed XML or uncheck the XML Feed while creating/editing the job: The jobs will be indexed to the external boards only if the requirements given above are met. Once you add details to these fields, the job goes through the review process. If everything is fine, Vonq will publish your jobs on Organic job boards instantly. Note: If the "organic job boards" option is selected from the XML fields section, you will be prompted to fill the required fields before you can save the job. This is to ensure your jobs are published through the feed. Please make sure all the required fields are filled in this step is essential for the job to go live. And that's it! You'll start receiving applications for those jobs in Recruit CRM! ❓How do I know if my job was posted? 1. You can check the list of jobs eligible to be pushed to the free job boards' feed by going to Admin Settings >>> Build Job Feed XML . Here you can click on "View Listed Jobs" to get a list of all the jobs in your account that currently meet the required criteria: If one of your jobs is not on the list, one of the necessary criteria is not being met. 2. You can search the job boards' websites to check if the job was posted. When your job is posted on the partner job boards, it will look something like this: The view will vary depending on the job board. 3. Another way to verify if the job was posted or not is to look for applicant candidates in your database. You can do this by enabling the Source field in Candidate Fields : ​ With the Source field, you'll be able to track the origin of how the candidate was added to the system. If the candidate applies, it will be mentioned in the field as 'Organic Posting Network' along with the Job ID. ​ You can even run an Advanced Search on the Source field as well. Troubleshooting Problem: A job is not appearing on any organic job board Likely cause : One or more required criteria for OPN posting have not been met. What to check: Verify that all OPN posting requirements outlined above have been met. Confirm the job is assigned to the Organic Job Boards XML Feed. Re-save the job after making any corrections. Resolution: Correct any missing or invalid field values, set the appropriate job status, re-save the job, and allow time for VONQ to process and publish it. Problem: The job is not visible on a specific job board in the OPN list Likely cause: VONQ’s filtering rules did not match the job to that particular board. What to check: Confirm that the job is otherwise eligible and visible on at least some other boards. Review whether the job’s location, industry, or specification might not align with that board’s parameters. Resolution: Adjust job parameters where appropriate (for example, industry or location), then save the job and monitor posting again. Keep in mind that VONQ does not guarantee posting to every job board in the list. FAQs Does posting to OPN consume job posting credits? Yes. One job posting credit or 25 Recruit CRM Credits is consumed each time you post a job through the Organic Posting Network. Job Posting Credits can be purchased on a monthly or annual basis directly from the Job Advertising module, regardless of your subscription plan. Will my job appear on every job board in the OPN list? No. VONQ does not guarantee posting on all job boards. Jobs are published on selective boards based on parameters defined by each job board, such as location, industry, and specification, and filtering is at VONQ’s discretion. How can I verify if a job posted via OPN is generating candidates? Enable the Source field on the Candidate List page and review candidate records. Candidates who applied via Organic Posting will show “Organic Posting” along with the job ID in the Source field, and you can run an advanced search on this field. Conclusion: Using the Organic Posting Network (OPN) in Recruit CRM, you can efficiently publish jobs to multiple free job boards and track resulting candidates directly in your database. t: Parsing Failed
s: This article will help you understand why resume parsing can fail sometimes?
b: Recruit CRM uses a proprietary Resume Parser to help recruiters add candidates into the system faster. You can check these articles How does the resume parser work and Resume parsing on Recruit CRM to learn more about how it actually works! Recruit CRM only supports .DOC/.DOCX/.PDF file types for Resume Parsing, and will return an error message if the file type is anything other than the 3 mentioned above. ​ There could be multiple reasons why parsing fails, Below are some of the common reasons: 1. Document type Not Supported: Recruit CRM's Resume Parser does not support any file type other than PDF, Doc & Docx. If a Resume/CV is scanned and stored in any other format, it will Not Be Parsed. ​ 2. If a Resume/CV file (.DOC/.DOCX/.PDF) contains images inside The parser might not parse data from the .DOC/.PDF file if the document has an image embedded in it. ​ 3. Image file converted to PDF While, OCR files are also supported by our resume parser, in some cases, parsing might fail for OCR files (image file converted to PDF). ​ 4. Internet connection If your internet connection drops or your upload speed is slow while parsing, it can also break the parsing process and lead to a failed parse. You can try parsing after some time when your internet connection is stable. You can check download & upload speeds at https://www.speedtest.net/ ​ ​ Hope this helped :) Related Articles Resume parsing on Recruit CRM How does the AI Resume Parser work? t: Parsing resumes and creating candidate/contact records from your mailbox in Recruit CRM.
s:
This article explains how to parse resumes or CVs directly from your Recruit CRM mailbox and create candidate records from attachments.
It also covers how to add an email sender (mailer) as a candidate or contact from within the mailbox view.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

Add a mailer as a candidate or contact from your mailbox:

b: What this feature does and when to use it? This feature lets you parse resume or CV attachments from an email in your Recruit CRM mailbox into candidate records. You can use this feature when: You receive resumes or CVs as email attachments and want to create candidate profiles quickly. You need to parse multiple CVs from a single email into candidate records. You want to add an email sender as a candidate/contact. Parse resumes or CVs into candidates from your mailbox: Go into your Recruit CRM mailbox and open the email that has the CV or resume attached. In the opened email, locate the green button that reads “Parse attachments into candidates.” 3. Click on the “Parse attachments into candidates” button to open the parsing pop-up. 4. In the pop-up, select the CV or CVs that you wish to parse. Click on the “Parse Resume” button to start parsing the selected CVs. You will get the option to: Compose an email to the candidate. Add notes to the candidate record. Assign an owner. Update fields. Assign the candidate to a job. Add the candidate to a hotlist. Add a mailer as a candidate or contact from your mailbox: Go to your mailbox and open the email whose mailer you want to add as a candidate or contact. Hover your cursor over the plus button in the email view. In the options that appear, choose whether to add the mailer as a candidate or as a contact. Click on “Add as a candidate” or “Add as a contact.” 5. In the form that opens, fill out all the necessary fields for the candidate or contact profile. 6.Click Submit to save the new candidate or contact record. Troubleshooting Problem: The “Parse attachments into candidates” button does not appear in the email view. Likely cause: The email may not contain a CV or resume attachment, or the mailbox view is not the Recruit CRM mailbox. ​ What to check: Confirm you are in the Recruit CRM mailbox and that the email includes at least one CV or resume attachment. ​ Resolution: Open the correct email in the Recruit CRM mailbox that has CV or resume attachments and check again for the green “Parse attachments into candidates” button. FAQs Can I parse multiple CVs from one email at the same time? Yes. You can select multiple CVs or attachments in the parsing pop-up and parse them at once. Do I need to download the CV before parsing it? No. You can parse the attached CV or resume directly from the email in your Recruit CRM mailbox. Conclusion: Using the mailbox parsing and mailer-creation options in Recruit CRM, you can quickly convert incoming emails and attachments into structured candidate and contact records with minimal manual work.
