t: Passcode for public pages (New UI)
s: This article explains how to secure public pages in Recruit CRM using passcodes, including online candidate lists shared with clients and candidate profile update request forms.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to set a passcode for Profile Update Request Forms?
Set a Passcode for Online Candidate List Pages (Account Level)
Create a Unique Passcode for an Individual Job (Job-Level)
Which public pages can be protected with a passcode?
Online Candidate Lists submitted to the client
Profile Update Request Forms
Troubleshooting
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Passcode for Public Pages feature allows you to protect external Recruit CRM pages with a passcode, ensuring that only authorized users can access them. Supported pages include online candidate list links shared with clients and candidate profile update request forms. You can configure a single account-level passcode for each type of public page, or create unique job-level passcodes that override the account-level passcode for specific online candidate lists. This feature is intended for account owners, admins, and users with the appropriate permissions who need greater control over access to externally shared Recruit CRM pages. Use this feature when: • You share online candidate lists with clients and want to restrict access to authorized viewers only • You send profile update request forms to candidates and want to protect those links with a passcode • You want a single passcode to secure public pages across your account • You need unique passcodes for specific jobs while maintaining a default account-level passcode for all other public pages ​ Important Notes Account Owners and Admins can now enable or disable passcodes independently for the Profile Update Request Form and Candidate Submission Links. Passcodes can include numbers, letters, and special characters, with a length requirement of 4 to 12 characters. Users with edit permissions can set unique passcodes for individual jobs in the Candidate Pipeline tab. How to set a passcode for Profile Update Request Forms? Follow these steps to protect your profile update request forms with a passcode: Go to Admin Settings . Under Account Management , click Account . Scroll down to the Set Passcode for Public Pages section and select Request Update / Profile Update Request Forms . Enable the password toggle and enter the passcode you want candidates to enter before accessing the form. Click Save Passcode to apply your changes. Once enabled, anyone opening a profile update request form will be prompted to enter the passcode before they can access and submit the form. Set a Passcode for Online Candidate List Pages (Account Level) Follow these steps to protect Online Candidate Lists shared with clients using an account-level passcode: Go to Admin Settings . Under Account Management , click Account . Scroll down to the Set Passcode for Public Pages section and select Online Candidate List Pages . Enable the Passcode toggle and enter the passcode you want clients to enter before accessing shared Online Candidate Lists. Click Save Passcode to apply your changes. Once enabled, anyone opening an Online Candidate List shared from your account will be prompted to enter the passcode before they can view the candidate information. Note: If the account-level passcode is updated later, it will apply to all jobs except those that have custom, job-specific passcodes. Create a Unique Passcode for an Individual Job (Job-Level) If you want a specific job to have its own passcode, you can create a job-level passcode that overrides the account-level passcode for that job's Online Candidate List. Follow these steps: Open the job for which you want to create a unique passcode. Navigate to the Candidate Pipeline section. Scroll down and locate the Passcode for Online Candidate List option. Click the Edit (✏️) icon next to the passcode field. Enter the passcode you want to use for that specific job. Click Save to apply the changes. Once saved, anyone accessing the Online Candidate List for that job will be prompted to enter the job-specific passcode. This passcode will override the account-level passcode configured for Online Candidate List pages. Which public pages can be protected with a passcode? When passcode protection is enabled, users will be required to enter the correct passcode before accessing the supported public pages. Currently, passcodes can be applied to the following Recruit CRM pages: Online Candidate Lists submitted to the client Online Candidate Lists are shared with clients when candidates are submitted for a job. To share an Online Candidate List: Go to the Jobs list page and open the relevant job. Click Submit Candidates . Click on the ' Submit Candidates ' button to submit a list of candidates to the contact associated with that job. When a client receives an email, they will receive a list of candidates that can be accessed only by entering the passcode you shared. Once the candidate list is shared, the recipient will receive a link to the Online Candidate List. If passcode protection is enabled, they must enter the correct passcode before viewing the candidate information. ​ Click here to know more on how to Submit Candidates to Clients Profile Update Request Forms Profile Update Request Forms are used to request updated information from candidates. To send a profile update request: Go to the Candidates list page. Select one or more candidates whose profiles need updating. Click Request Updated Profile . The candidate will receive an email containing a link to their profile update form. If passcode protection is enabled, they must enter the correct passcode before accessing and updating their profile information. ​ ​ Click here to know more about Requesting Candidate's Updated profile Troubleshooting Problem: Client cannot access the online candidate list (passcode rejected) Likely cause : The passcode shared with the client does not match the active passcode. ​ ​ What to check : •Confirm whether a job-level passcode is set for that job. •Verify the passcode in the “Set passcode for public pages” section (account level) and in the job’s Candidate Pipeline section. ​ ​ Resolution: •Share the correct, current passcode with the client. •If needed, reset the passcode (either at account level or job level), save it, and resend the link with the updated passcode. Problem: Candidate cannot open the profile update request form Likely cause : The candidate is entering an incorrect passcode or the account-level passcode has recently changed. ​ ​ What to check: •Confirm the current passcode set under “Set passcode for public pages” for profile update request forms. •Ensure the candidate has the updated passcode. ​ ​ Resolution: •Provide the candidate with the correct passcode. •If you change the passcode, resend the profile update email with instructions to use the new passcode. FAQs Who can enable or disable passcodes at the account level? Only account owners and admins can enable or disable passcodes for profile update request forms and online candidate list pages in the admin settings. Conclusion: Securing public pages in Recruit CRM with passcodes helps you control who can access candidate lists and profile update forms while keeping your data safe. If you need further assistance configuring passcodes or reviewing your setup, please contact your account owner, admin, or Recruit CRM support. t: Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields for Jobs
s: This article will guide you on how to use the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields for Jobs.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
What do these fields mean?
How to use the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields
Where can you access the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields?
Jobs List Page:
Job Details Page:
Job Add/Edit Form
Enable Timesheet Form
b: What this feature does and when to use it? When you create or edit a job with the Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job type, Recruit CRM automatically displays the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields. These fields help you track contractor pay and client billing rates for contract staffing. You can choose to calculate the Bill Rate using a Fixed Rate, Margin, or Markup . This feature is useful when you want to: Record contractor pay rates. Manage client billing rates. Require pay and bill rates for contract jobs. Filter, import, and export jobs using these fields. What do these fields mean? Before using these fields, it's helpful to understand what each one represents. Pay Rate: The amount paid to the contractor. Bill Rate: The amount billed to your client. Margin: The percentage of the Bill Rate that represents profit. Markup: The percentage added to the Pay Rate to calculate the Bill Rate. Calculate Charge By: Determines whether the Bill Rate is calculated using a Fixed Rate, Margin, or Markup. ​ Margin vs. Markup Markup is the percentage added to the Pay Rate to calculate the Bill Rate. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% markup results in a $15 Bill Rate. The value can be between 0% and 99% and cannot be a negative value. Margin represents the percentage of the Bill Rate that is profit. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% margin requires a $20 Bill Rate. The value can be between 0% and 10,000% and cannot be a negative value. Pay Rate Calculation Bill Rate $10 50% Markup $15 $10 50% Margin $20 Please note: These fields are conditional and only appear when the Job Type is set to Contract or Contract-to-Permanent. How to use the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields Create a new job or edit an existing one, then set the Job Type to Contract or Contract-to-Permanent. The Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields will automatically appear on the job form. ​ Select how the Bill Rate should be calculated: Fixed Rate: Enter the Pay Rate and Bill Rate directly. Margin: Enter the desired profit margin, and the system automatically calculates the Bill Rate. Markup: Enter the desired markup on the Pay Rate, and the system automatically calculates the Bill Rate. Admins can control the visibility of Pay Rate, Bill Rate, Margin, Markup, and Calculate Charge By navigating to Admin Settings → Data Customization → Job Fields . From here you can mark them as Required to ensure they are completed whenever applicable. Note: Existing jobs will continue to use Fixed Rate , so existing rate configurations are not changed. If Pay Rate and Bill Rate already exist, the corresponding Margin and Markup values can be calculated automatically. Where can you access the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields? Once available, the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields can be accessed throughout Recruit CRM. Jobs List Page: View the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields directly from the Jobs List Page . Job Details Page: View or update the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields from the Job Details page. Job Add/Edit Form Select the rate calculation method and enter the relevant rate information when creating or editing a contract or contract-to-permanent job. ​ Enable Timesheet Form Use the relevant rate calculation options when enabling timesheets. ​ Timesheet Views View the relevant rate information from applicable timesheet views. Hide/Show Columns option. Importing: Import Pay Rate and Bill Rate values while importing contract jobs. Export: Export Pay Rate and Bill Rate values along with other job information. Search Filters: Filter jobs using the Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields. How will this function while merging Jobs? Merging is not allowed if: The primary job is non-contract and the secondary job is contract/contract-to-perm , and timesheets are enabled for any candidates. Merging is allowed if: Both jobs are contract or contract-to-perm. The primary job is contract . The primary job is non-contract and the secondary job is contract , but no candidates have timesheets enabled. Note: These fields cannot be bulk updated. This is to prevent inconsistencies across mixed job types. Troubleshooting The Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields are not visible. Likely Cause: The job is not configured as a Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job. What to Check: Verify the Job Type selected for the job. Resolution: Update the Job Type to Contract or Contract-to-Permanent . The Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields will appear automatically. FAQs What is the difference between Margin and Markup? Markup is the percentage added to the Pay Rate to calculate the Bill Rate. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% markup results in a $15 Bill Rate. Margin represents the percentage of the Bill Rate that is profit. For example, a $10 Pay Rate with a 50% margin requires a $20 Bill Rate. Will this change my existing jobs? No. Existing jobs will continue to use Fixed Rate . If Pay Rate and Bill Rate already exist, the corresponding Margin and Markup values can be calculated automatically. Can I still enter Pay Rate and Bill Rate directly? Yes. Select Fixed Rate to continue entering both rates directly. Can I hide these fields? Yes. Admins can control the visibility of Pay Rate, Bill Rate, Margin, Markup, and Calculate Charge By through Admin Settings. Can I bulk update these fields? No. Bulk updates are not supported. Conclusion: The Pay Rate and Bill Rate fields help you manage contractor compensation and client billing for contract-based jobs. With Fixed Rate, Margin, and Markup options, Recruit CRM provides flexibility in calculating Bill Rates while keeping relevant rate information accessible across job and timesheet workflows. s: This article shows you how to pitch candidates to contacts/hiring managers without assigning them to a Job
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM lets you pitch or market candidates discreetly to multiple hiring managers/contacts without needing to assign them to a job role. You can use this feature when: You want to market a strong candidate profile to multiple clients without linking them to a specific job. You need to track which candidates were shared with which contacts for reporting or follow-up. You want to send candidate CVs and summaries as structured emails directly from Recruit CRM. The candidate won't receive an email when you send their application to a contact. This way, you can record if you shared Candidate CVs with your clients, even if the candidate isn't assigned to any specific job. Before you begin: Make sure your email is connected inside Recruit CRM, so you can send emails directly from Recruit CRM. Step-by-step instructions on Pitching a single candidate 1. Go to the relevant candidate’s profile. 2. Click the three-dot (ellipsis) button and select ' Pitch Candidate To Contact' . Alternatively, scroll to the middle of the candidate profile and click the Contacts Pitched widget to begin the pitch process. 3. Now you will be redirected to a page to select the contacts you want to pitch this candidate with and click on the Select fields and email contacts option (or you can mark the candidate as pitched if you have already pitched outside of Recruit CRM): 4. Select the candidate fields (including file/document fields) you wish to share with the contact, and then click on the " Generate Email" button: ​ In the File Columns section, you'll be able to select the option "Summary". The Candidate Summary will be converted into a .pdf file and attached to the pitch email. The file name generated will follow numeric order, to prevent sharing the name of the pitched record. 5. You can now see an email is generated with the fields you selected, ready to be sent to the contacts you selected individually (Recruit CRM sends an individual email to each contact listed in the To field so that recipients are not aware the email is being sent to multiple contacts): ​ Pitching multiple candidates from the list view This can also be done with multiple candidates from the list view by just selecting candidates & clicking on the "Pitch Candidate(s)" button that appears. Note: You can pitch a maximum of 20 candidates at a time. Viewing candidates pitched Once you have pitched the candidate(s), you will be able to track this pitch on both the candidates' & contacts' profiles. On the candidate's profile, you will find the "Contact(s) pitched" widget which has a timestamp with the name of the user who made the pitch to keep you organized. Similarly, from contact profiles: On the contact's profile, you will find the "Candidate(s) pitched" widget. Click here to know more about Pitch Candidate Pipeline Track and Update Pitches from Contact Profiles Once you receive a status update from the contact about a candidate, click on the pitch stage value and select a new stage (for example, Pitched ) from the options you have customized in your system. You can add a Remark or Feedback for future reference. Don't forget to hit Submit :) How to view a list of all the candidates I have pitched in Recruit CRM? Recruit CRM enables you to view all the candidates pitched by any team members by generating a report. This report provides a clear list based on their specific activities as a user. Access the Reports Section > Team Performance Report . Choose the team members in the report filters, and the time period. Select the KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) as stages from your Pitch Candidate pipeline , such as "Candidate Pitched - Pitched". Click on the option to generate the report . Once the report is displayed, you will see a bar graph summarizing your pitching activity. ​ Click on the bar graph. This will lead you to a detailed list of all candidates the selected team members have pitched. Click here to learn more on generating a Team Performance Report 🤔FAQs Can I pitch candidates without assigning them to a job? Yes. Recruit CRM lets you pitch a candidate or market candidates discreetly to multiple hiring managers or contacts without needing to assign them to a job role. Can I record a pitch that was sent outside of Recruit CRM? Yes. When selecting contacts during the pitching process you can choose to Mark the candidate as pitched if you have already pitched outside of Recruit CRM. This records the pitch without sending a new email. Conclusion: By following the steps above, you can pitch single or multiple candidates. Please feel free to reach out if you have any further questions via the chatbot. You can add a Remark or Feedback for future reference. Don't forget to hit Submit :) How to view a list of all the candidates I have pitched in Recruit CRM? Recruit CRM enables you to view all the candidates pitched by any team members by generating a report. This report provides a clear list based on their specific activities as a user. Access the Reports Section > Team Performance Report . Choose the team members in the report filters, and the time period. Select the KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) as stages from your Pitch Candidate pipeline , such as "Candidate Pitched - Pitched". Click on the option to generate the report . Once the report is displayed, you will see a bar graph summarizing your pitching activity. ​ Click on the bar graph. This will lead you to a detailed list of all candidates the selected team members have pitched. Click here to learn more on generating a Team Performance Report 🤔FAQs Can I pitch candidates without assigning them to a job? Yes. Recruit CRM lets you pitch a candidate or market candidates discreetly to multiple hiring managers or contacts without needing to assign them to a job role. Can I record a pitch that was sent outside of Recruit CRM? Yes. When selecting contacts during the pitching process you can choose to Mark the candidate as pitched if you have already pitched outside of Recruit CRM. This records the pitch without sending a new email. Conclusion: By following the steps above, you can pitch single or multiple candidates. Please feel free to reach out if you have any further questions via the chatbot. Hope this helps! t: Pricing and Billing in Recruit Craft
s: This article walks you through Recruit Craft’s pricing plans, billing process, and what to expect when managing payments.
h: How Billing and Pricing work in Recruit Craft
Upgrading from the Free Trial Account
Upgrading an existing subscription
Downgrading an account
b: 💸 How Billing and Pricing work in Recruit Craft Recruit Craft’s pricing is designed to be simple and flexible, so you only pay for what you need. Plans are based on the maximum number of jobs you can post on your website through Recruit Craft. The plans will be automatically updated to match your current increased job posting needs. This ensures you’ll always be on a plan that supports the number of jobs you want to display, providing a smooth experience without interruptions. ✅ Upgrading from the Free Trial Account When you first sign up for Recruit Craft, you’re automatically placed on a free trial account . With the free plan, you can connect your Recruit CRM account using your API key and preview your jobs in real time. The preview gives you a clear view of exactly how your jobs will appear once published, helping you set everything up just the way you want before going live. When you’re ready to post jobs publicly, upgrading is quick and effortless. Now, follow along to upgrade your plan from the Free plan. 1. Look to the top right corner of your screen and click Upgrade Now . You can also click your profile icon , go to Settings , and select Plans and Billing from the left-hand panel. 2. You’ll now see a list of plans tailored to your needs. The options will automatically adjust based on the number of open jobs in your Recruit CRM account. For example, if you have 20 open jobs, only plans that support 20 or more jobs will be shown. You can also switch between Annual and Monthly billing at the top of the page, depending on your preference. 3. Choose the plan that works best for your hiring needs and click Get Started . 4. A summary page will display all the choices you’ve made. If needed, you can still adjust the plan from the dropdown menu before moving forward. 5. Once you’ve confirmed everything looks correct, click Proceed to Purchase. 6. The system will ask you to check your details one final time. When you’re ready, click Confirm and Pay . The payment will be processed through the card on file that’s registered in your Recruit CRM account. 7. The charge will be processed through your Recruit CRM Stripe account. ⚠️ Important: If your Recruit CRM account is currently on the FREE plan , you’ll need to upgrade your Recruit CRM account first before completing the Recruit Craft upgrade. 🔼Upgrading an existing subscription Recruit Craft uses a dynamic billing system that adjusts plans based on how many jobs you have published. This ensures that your plan always aligns with your usage, without interrupting your hiring process. Additionally, you’ll receive email notifications whenever your job limit is crossed, keeping you informed and alert so you can take timely action. Automatic Upgrade If your job count exceeds the limit of your current plan for two consecutive days , Recruit Craft will automatically upgrade you to the next available tier . Proration of Fees – You won’t be billed the full amount for the new plan immediately. Instead, Recruit Craft calculates a prorated fee based on the number of days left in your billing cycle. This charge begins from the day your job count exceeds your plan’s limit. Invoice Update – The prorated charge is added to your card on file, and you’ll see this adjustment reflected in your next invoice. Example of Automatic Upgrade Imagine you are on the 6 to 15 Jobs plan and have 15 jobs published. If you publish a 16th job and maintain 16 jobs for two days in a row, the system will automatically upgrade you to the 16 to 50 Jobs plan. You will only be charged the prorated amount for the remaining days of your billing cycle at the new plan rate. Manual Upgrade Option If you prefer, you can manually upgrade your account at any time by following the same steps outlined for upgrading from a free trial. Just head to your profile, go to Settings , select Plans and Billing , and choose the new plan that suits your needs. 🔽 Downgrading an account If your hiring needs change and you’re managing fewer jobs, Recruit Craft gives you the flexibility to downgrade your plan to something more suitable. Follow these steps to make the switch: 1. Click on your profile icon in the top right corner of your screen and go to Settings . 2. Once inside the Profile Settings, navigate to the left-hand panel, and select Plans and Billing . 3. You’ll now be able to see your current plan along with other plans you can move to. If the plan you want is available, simply click Get Started on that option. Please note You can only downgrade if your open jobs are less than the limit of the plan you’re moving to. If your published or open jobs are more than that limit, the option to downgrade will be greyed out. The job count must also be below the starting limit of your current plan at the time of the request, if it’s equal to or higher, the downgrade won’t go through. For example: If you’re on the 16 to 50 Jobs plan and your job count drops to 13, you can request a downgrade to the 6 to 15 Jobs plan. Once validated, the downgrade will take effect at the start of the next billing cycle . 4. After selecting your new plan, review the details and note the effective date. Click Proceed to Purchase to continue. 5. Review everything carefully and click Confirm Downgrade. You’ve now successfully downgraded your account! The new plan will take effect from the start of your next billing cycle, whether you’re on a monthly or annual subscription. Once a downgrade has been initiated, if your job count increases beyond the limit of the selected downgraded plan, the downgrade will automatically be cancelled. Recruit Craft’s pricing and billing system is designed to keep things simple and flexible, so you can focus on hiring while we handle the details. Whether you’re upgrading, downgrading, or just exploring your options, the process is straightforward and transparent. If you ever have questions or need a little extra guidance, don’t hesitate to reach out to our chat support team. We’re always here to help you every step of the way! t: Pro Plan
s: Explore Pro Plan features including higher record limits, AI resume parsing, sourcing tools, etc.
h: What this plan does and when to use it?

2. Chrome Sourcing Extension
3. AI Resume Parsing
4. GPT Integration

b: What this plan does and when to use it? The Recruit CRM Pro Plan provides the essential recruitment tools needed to streamline hiring workflows. It includes features such as the Chrome Sourcing Extension, AI Resume Parser, AI Sourcing, GPT Integration, unlimited email templates, a fully integrated mailbox, deal pipelines, a complete reporting suite, unlimited open jobs, and job board posting, giving recruiting and sales teams everything they need to source talent, manage pipelines, communicate efficiently, and grow their business. Recruit CRM's Pro plan includes: 1. Record and Entity limit The Pro plan allows you to add up to 10,000 records for candidates, contacts, and companies each. 2. Chrome Sourcing Extension Our Chrome extension streamlines your workflow, enabling you to source candidates, contacts, and companies effortlessly from multiple recruitment platforms and lead databases with just one click! Currently compatible with LinkedIn, LinkedIn Recruiter, Recruiter Lite, Sales Navigator, Outlook, Gmail, ZoomInfo, Xing, Xing Talent Manager, Indeed, and Naukri Recruitment Management System, our extension is designed to enhance productivity and save you valuable time. 3. AI Resume Parsing Discover the power of the Resume Parser in Recruit CRM—an essential tool designed to automate the extraction of crucial information from candidate resumes. With our robust Resume Parser, you can effortlessly populate your database by directly uploading CVs stored on your computer into Recruit CRM. Note: You can parse up to 100 files at a time. 4. GPT Integration The GPT integration with Recruit CRM helps you streamline the process of creating email templates , job descriptions , candidate summaries , notes, and call logs . 5. Two Factor Authentication (2FA)/Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Two-factor authentication (2FA) or multi-factor authentication (MFA) adds a layer of protection and enhances the security of your Recruit CRM account beyond your standard login credentials. 6. Candidate - Candidate AI Matching (up to 2 matches) Using advanced AI, the system identifies and ranks candidates, based on biometric scoring, with profiles closely aligned to your ideal candidates, streamlining your search for the perfect fit. 7. Unlimited email templates Unlock the potential of our robust email template builder, empowering you to create personalized emails and effortlessly communicate with all your candidates and contacts. 8. Deal pipelines Experience full control over your revenue opportunities with Recruit CRM's Deal Pipeline feature. Seamlessly track every "deal" your team is pursuing, customize deal stages, and tailor fields to your specific needs. Plus, effortlessly monitor associated Jobs, Companies, or Contacts, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks. 9. Fully integrated mailbox Enhance your emailing experience by seamlessly integrating your mailbox with Recruit CRM. You can also create personalized email signatures, create and customize email templates, and efficiently send emails to your candidates and contacts—all using the Recruit CRM platform. 10. Complete reporting suite From tracking key metrics to analyzing performance, streamline your operations with ease using our powerful Reporting Suite. 11. Unlimited bulk emails Sending emails individually can be a time-consuming task! Save time, and boost productivity with our convenient bulk email feature! 12. Up to 15 custom fields Unlock the ability to add up to 15 custom fields to each of your records—candidates, companies, contacts, and jobs. Experience the power of personalized customization with Recruit CRM. 13. Job Board Posting We natively partner with top free job boards, including ZipRecruiter, Talent.com (formerly Neuvoo), CareerJet, Job Rapido, Google for Jobs, Adzuna, Post Job Free and MyJobHelper. You can enhance your recruitment efforts and maximize the number of quality applications received. 14. Save/Share Files Associated with a Candidates Job Application Easily view, store, and share job-specific candidate files within jobs to ensure tailored submissions to clients. 15. Texting Communicate seamlessly with your candidates/contacts using Twilio-powered texting within the USA, UK, Israel, Hong Kong, Canada & Sweden. 16. Phone Calling and Recording Easily call candidates or contacts using Twilio. Set up your calling number, buy credits, and start making calls with the option to record and store call details. 17. Advanced Analytics through Metabase You can create custom reports, visualize key metrics through dashboards, and share insights seamlessly across your teams and with external stakeholders. Advanced Analytics feature can be added at an additional cost to Pro plan subscriptions. 18. Workflow Automation You automate repetitive tasks between two or more apps - no code necessary. ​﻿The Workflow Automations feature can be added at an additional cost to Pro plan subscriptions. 19. Job posting and Advertising Streamline your job posting process and publish job ads in an easy and targeted way. You can share your jobs on different job boards in two ways: Posting jobs by integrating your existing job board contracts in Recruit CRM. Posting directly to job boards without having to create an account with them (job marketplace). 20. AI Job-Candidate Matching You can find the most suitable candidates for your job listings which helps you to streamline the recruitment process by automating candidate recommendations and improving overall efficiency. 21. LinkedIn Messages Integration: The LinkedIn Messages Integration provides a complete view of all interactions with candidates and contacts, enabling you to communicate with them directly through LinkedIn without leaving Recruit CRM. LinkedIn Messages Integration feature can be added at an additional cost to Pro plan subscriptions. 22. Create and access templates for notes, call logs, and tasks: You can create and customize upto 100 activity templates for notes, call logs and tasks. 23. Data Enrichment : The Data Enrichment feature helps users find missing email addresses and phone numbers for candidates or contacts using their LinkedIn profiles. Data Enrichment can be added at an additional cost to Pro plan subscriptions. Step-by-step instructions to upgrade to the Pro Plan Open Admin Settings in Recruit CRM and go to Plans and Billing . From the navigation panel on the left, select Plans . Select the Business Plan to review its features and pricing. ​ ​ Click here to upgrade to Pro plan ⭐️ Click here to know about our Business plan ⭐️ ⭐️ Troubleshooting Problem: Resume parser stops when uploading files Likely cause: You may be trying to parse more than one hundred files at a time. What to check: Confirm the number of resumes you are uploading in a single batch. Resolution: Reduce the upload batch to one hundred files or fewer and try again. FAQs Which record and custom field limits apply to the Pro Plan? The Pro Plan allows you to add up to 10,000 records each for candidates, contacts, and companies. It also unlocks the ability to add up to 15 custom fields to each of your records: candidates, companies, contacts, and jobs. How many resumes can I parse at once with AI resume parsing? You can parse up to one hundred files at a time when uploading resumes (CVs) from your computer into Recruit CRM. Are advanced analytics, Workflow Automation, LinkedIn message integration, and Data enrichment included in the Pro Plan by default? No. Advanced analytics through Metabase, Workflow Automation, LinkedIn message integration, and Data enrichment can be added at an additional cost to the Pro Plan subscription. Which platforms does the Chrome sourcing extension support? The Chrome sourcing extension is currently compatible with LinkedIn, LinkedIn Recruiter, Recruiter Lite, Sales Navigator, Outlook, Gmail, ZoomInfo, Xing, Xing Talent Manager, Indeed, and Naukri Recruitment Management System. What's the main difference between the Pro Plan and the Business Plan? The Business Plan doubles most Pro Plan limits (20,000 records vs. 10,000, 100 custom fields vs. 15) and adds features like Custom Roles, Teams, Executive Search Reports, Audit Logs, and Sequences that aren't included in the Pro Plan. Conclusion: The Recruit CRM Pro Plan brings together essential recruitment tools, including AI-powered sourcing and resume parsing, Chrome sourcing, GPT integration, integrated email communication, deal pipelines, reporting, unlimited open jobs, and job board posting. Together, these features help streamline sourcing, candidate management, communication, and reporting, enabling recruiting and sales teams to work more efficiently from a single platform. t: Product Roadmap
s: This article will show you where & how you can checkout features requested by other user.
h: How to access the Product Roadmap
How to submit a feature request
How to browse and vote for feature requests
Understanding feature request statuses
Share feedback from Recruit Craft
Troubleshooting
The feature I voted for hasn't been released yet.
FAQs
b: The Product Roadmap allows you to share feature ideas, vote on requests submitted by other users, and stay informed about features that are under review or currently in development. It gives you visibility into Recruit CRM's product planning while allowing you to contribute to future improvements. This feature is useful when you want to: Submit new feature requests for Recruit CRM. Vote for feature requests submitted by other users. Track the progress of upcoming product enhancements. Please note: Feature requests are reviewed and prioritized based on customer feedback, product strategy, and development priorities. As a result, implementation timelines may vary. Once a request receives a reasonable number of votes, our development team takes a look and adds it to our roadmap How to access the Product Roadmap Log in to your Recruit CRM account. Click your Profile icon in the top-right corner and select Give us Feedback under the Help and feedback dropdown. This will redirect you to the Product Roadmap. How to submit a feature request Click + Add a New Idea from the Feedback Portal. Enter a title for your idea. Select a category, add a description explaining your request, attach files if needed, and click Add Idea to submit it. How to browse and vote for feature requests The All Ideas page displays feature requests submitted by Recruit CRM users. You can: Search for feature requests using the Search bar. Click Vote to support an existing feature request. View ideas you've submitted, voted for, or subscribed to from the left navigation panel. Filter ideas by Category , Status , or change the Sort By option to organize the list. Understanding feature request statuses Use the Filter by Status option to view ideas based on where they are in the product development process. Status Description New When you put in the feature request Under Review The development team is checking the possibilities. In Development Development has started, and the feature is actively being worked on. Beta Released The feature is available for internal testing or selected beta customers before full release. Closed The feature request has been closed and is no longer being considered for development. Shipped The feature has been released and is generally available. This status is hidden by default but can be viewed by selecting it from the Status filter. Share feedback from Recruit Craft You can also access the Feedback Portal directly from Recruit Craft . Click your Profile icon and select Give Us Feedback. This opens the same Feedback Portal, allowing you to submit feature requests, vote on existing ideas, and track product updates without leaving Recruit Craft. Important Note : The feature requests on the roadmap are based on the development sprint we follow, so the timeline for the deployment and availability of the feature may vary based on priority. Troubleshooting The feature I voted for hasn't been released yet. Likely Cause: Feature requests are prioritized based on several factors, including customer demand and development priorities. What to Check: Review the feature's current status on the Progress Board. Resolution: Continue following the request on the Product Roadmap for future updates. Release timelines may change depending on product priorities. FAQs 1. Does every feature request get added to the roadmap? No. Every request is reviewed by the product team, but implementation depends on factors such as feasibility, customer demand, and product priorities. 2. What does "Beta Released" mean? It means the feature is being tested internally or is available to selected beta customers before its general release. Conclusion: The Product Roadmap gives you a direct way to shape the future of Recruit CRM. Whether you're submitting new ideas, voting on existing requests, or tracking feature progress, the roadmap keeps you informed about product improvements and helps the team prioritize enhancements that matter most to customers. t: Provision to Purchase Phone Numbers and Incoming Call Support
s: This article will assist you in purchasing a phone number within Recruit CRM and explain how incoming calls function.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
How to Purchase a Phone Number
Purchasing Phone Number details
Phone Purchase Cost deduction
Editing your phone number
Making a call
Incoming calls
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The purchase phone number feature in Recruit CRM (powered by Twilio) lets you buy US or UK (Local and Mobile) numbers to make outbound calls and receive inbound calls directly in the web app. You can use this feature when: You want to make outbound calls directly from Recruit CRM using a dedicated phone number. You need to receive incoming calls in Recruit CRM on the web app. You are setting up phone calling for a team and need to assign numbers to users. You want to track and edit call logs for incoming and outgoing calls within Recruit CRM. Before you begin: For the US region, mobile-type numbers are not supported. For a UK number, you are required to complete a KYC form. The number will only be available after the KYC form is submitted and approved. Learn more about KYC here . The Purchase Phone Number and Incoming Calls feature is available only on paid plans. Incoming calls are supported on the web app only. ☎️ How to Purchase a Phone Number 1. Go to Phone Calling & SMS Settings and click on 'Purchase Phone Number': 2. Choose a Number and then click Purchase . You can also 'Search by Number' and 'Search by Locality' to find the ideal number. Note: You can search for phone numbers that either start or end with specific digits by using the wildcard search pattern. Starts with : Type the starting digits followed by asterisks ( * ) to match any remaining numbers. Example: 212******* → finds numbers starting with 212 . Ends with : Type asterisks ( * ) followed by the ending digits. Example: *******212 → finds numbers ending with 212 . 3. After clicking Purchase , review the pop-up confirmation, where you will see the price of the recurring fee for that number. 4. Click Confirm to complete the purchase. 5. You can manage the numbers on the Phone Calling & SMS Settings , under the 'Purchased Phone Number' tab. Purchasing Phone Number details If your credits are low, a warning banner will appear prompting you to recharge credits. The phone number types are limited to local and mobile ; toll-free numbers are not allowed. For the US region, 'Mobile' is not supported. The purchased number is only available for paid plans and requires a minimum of $2 in credits. While free credits are provided after upgrading, additional credits may still be needed to meet this minimum. The 'Purchase' tab will remain visible, and users on a free plan will see an upgrade screen to upgrade. Phone Purchase Cost deduction All the cost deductions related to Phone number purchases will be reflected in the Recurring Payments Tab under Phone Calling and SMS Settings . You will be charged an exact 25% margin on the purchase of the phone numbers. Recurring charges for phone numbers will be deducted per month based on the payment cycle when the number is purchased with a 25% margin or $2 whichever is greater. For example: If the phone number costs $1.15 , the charge after a 25% margin would be $1.44 , but since this is less than $2 , the recruiter will be charged $2 . If the phone number costs $135 , the charge after a 25% margin would be $168.75 , which is greater than $2 , so the recruiter will be charged $168.75 . ☎️ Editing your phone number 1. Click on the pencil icon to edit your purchased phone number. 2. In 'Phone Number Details,' you can title your phone number, select the assigned user. Please notice that only Account Owners and Users with Custom roles and permissions for phone calling and SMS can assign phone numbers to users. The assigned number can also be configured from the Profile Settings . 3. For the 'Incoming Call Setup', you'll get the option to enable incoming calls, set the working hours (when you wish to receive incoming calls), and define a message for when a call is unanswered. About Working Hours Since the missed call will also be chargeable, to reduce costs, you can toggle Incoming calls ON or OFF when assigning a phone number. If enabled, you can set working hours, ensuring there are no missed calls outside those hours, which could incur charges. You can set the day, start time, and end time and can add multiple working hours based on their choice. In the day dropdown, you can select specific days (e.g., Monday, Tuesday) and also define a range of days. Standard day ranges are offered, including Monday to Friday, Monday to Saturday, and Sunday to Thursday. When you initially set the working hours, the default configuration is established as "Day: Mon - Fri." You will need to select the time range independently – no default setting will be given here. The date time format will be the 12-hour format. You can add up to 10 working hours. ☎️ Making a call While calling a record, there will be the option to choose from which number you're going to call – the default one from the system, or the number assigned to you. ☎️ Incoming calls 1. The incoming calls will be logged in the tab 'Account Credits & Usage'. 2. You can edit the call log by clicking on the pencil icon. There, you can edit the 'Related To' section, as the system does not link the call to a record automatically. You can also edit the Call Type, add Collaborators, create Associations, and add Call Notes. Please note that for Outgoing, Incoming, and Missed Calls, the "Related to" field will be optional. Call logs that don't have a 'Related to' value (Incoming/outgoing) will be added in Reports also under the 'Total Call Logs' KPI/ Incoming/outgoing. Related Field Optional Impact on Automation For automation (Public API / Workato / Zapier) we know that there are actions and triggers, so in the case of: Note: When the system adds a missed call log, the webhook/Zapier trigger is triggered. Actions (Call log) : It won't impact any existing Zaps, since all running Zaps 'Related to' call log action have both the fields mapped. After this enhancement, users will have the option to skip these fields (that will be the user's choice). Triggers (Call Log): There can be a case where the zap might fail only because the action (that might be related to any entity inside RCRM or any other action of any other app) has a "Related to" and "Related to type" as mandatory field. So, in this case, adding filters and paths in the automation workflow can handle the scenario. Find a Call Log that doesn't have 'Related to': From the web app, this can be done in two ways: one from the mailbox and the other from Admin Settings and Report listing. From Public API, we have the endpoint ' Find call log by ID'. Incoming Call configuration details The Incoming Call will be redirected to the Web App on the tab level. You have the option to toggle the setting for receiving Incoming calls ON or OFF while assigning a phone number. When toggled ON, it's possible to specify the working hours during which you wish to receive incoming calls. To handle the Incoming calls, you can set the message in when a call is not answered section while assigning the phone number, which will be played when the call is not picked up. That process is an async process and it's needed to fill in the 'Related to' field with the prospect's name and save the incoming call log. ☎️ Incoming Call calculations For Incoming Calls, the formula is: (Local Call Pricing + Browser/App Call Pricing + Recording Pricing (if applicable)) x 1.25 This includes storing the call as long as you use Recruit CRM. ☎️ Incoming and Missed calls use cases 1. If you decline the incoming call, it will be treated as an Incoming call and the log will be added

b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Purchase Phone Number and Incoming Calls feature is available only on paid plans. Incoming calls are supported on the web app only. ☎️ How to Purchase a Phone Number 1. Go to Phone Calling & SMS Settings and click on 'Purchase Phone Number': 2. Choose a Number and then click Purchase . You can also 'Search by Number' and 'Search by Locality' to find the ideal number. Note: You can search for phone numbers that either start or end with specific digits by using the wildcard search pattern. Starts with : Type the starting digits followed by asterisks ( * ) to match any remaining numbers. Example: 212******* → finds numbers starting with 212 . Ends with : Type asterisks ( * ) followed by the ending digits. Example: *******212 → finds numbers ending with 212 . 3. After clicking Purchase , review the pop-up confirmation, where you will see the price of the recurring fee for that number. 4. Click Confirm to complete the purchase. 5. You can manage the numbers on the Phone Calling & SMS Settings , under the 'Purchased Phone Number' tab. Purchasing Phone Number details If your credits are low, a warning banner will appear prompting you to recharge credits. The phone number types are limited to local and mobile ; toll-free numbers are not allowed. For the US region, 'Mobile' is not supported. The purchased number is only available for paid plans and requires a minimum of $2 in credits. While free credits are provided after upgrading, additional credits may still be needed to meet this minimum. The 'Purchase' tab will remain visible, and users on a free plan will see an upgrade screen to upgrade. Phone Purchase Cost deduction All the cost deductions related to Phone number purchases will be reflected in the Recurring Payments Tab under Phone Calling and SMS Settings . You will be charged an exact 25% margin on the purchase of the phone numbers. Recurring charges for phone numbers will be deducted per month based on the payment cycle when the number is purchased with a 25% margin or $2 whichever is greater. For example: If the phone number costs $1.15 , the charge after a 25% margin would be $1.44 , but since this is less than $2 , the recruiter will be charged $2 . The assigned number can also be configured from the Profile Settings . 3. For the 'Incoming Call Setup', you'll get the option to enable incoming calls, set the working hours (when you wish to receive incoming calls), and define a message for when a call is unanswered. t: Re-parsing Resume in Recruit CRM
s: Learn how to use the Re-parse Resume feature to update existing candidate profiles with newly parsed resume information.
h: How to Re-parse a Resume
Reviewing Parsed Information Before Updating
Updating Candidate Information
Managing Duplicate Candidates During Bulk Resume Parsing
Troubleshooting
FAQs
b: You can now use the Re-parse Resume option directly from the Candidate Details page to update candidate information using the newly parsed resume. 🚀 How to Re-parse a Resume The Re-parse Resume option is available in two places: From the default Resume field on the candidate profile ​ From the three-dot action menu ​ You can either upload a new resume from their system or select an existing resume from the candidate’s Files section. Once selected, the resume is parsed again, and the newly extracted information is compared with the candidate’s current profile details before any updates are applied. 🔍 Reviewing Parsed Information Before Updating Before applying updates, a comparison screen shows the Field Name , New Value , and Current Value side-by-side, allowing you to review and choose which fields should be updated. Updating Candidate Information You can choose how the candidate information should be updated by selecting either the ' Update Empty Field Values' option or the ' Override Selected Field Values' option: When the ' Update Empty Field Values' option is selected, the system will only fill fields that are currently empty in the candidate profile, while keeping the existing information unchanged. When the ' Override Selected Field Values' option is selected, the system will replace the existing candidate information with the newly parsed values for the fields you select. This gives you more control over which existing details should be updated from the latest resume. Note: Bulk resume re-parsing and bulk candidate updates are currently not supported. The comparison view currently supports only the default candidate fields available in the resume parser. 🔁 Managing Duplicate Candidates During Bulk Resume Parsing When parsing resumes in bulk, if duplicate candidates are detected, they are clearly marked with a “Duplicate” tag so you can easily identify them before proceeding. Each duplicate candidate also includes an “Update Values” option, allowing you to review the existing candidate profile alongside the newly parsed resume information before applying any changes. If multiple duplicate candidates are found, you can navigate through them one by one using the duplicate counter. You can choose to skip a duplicate or update selected field values and move to the next duplicate. For the final duplicate candidate, the option changes to Override Selected Field Values . Please Note: In the comparison screen, fields where changes are detected are automatically selected by default. You can review these selections and choose which fields should or should not be updated before saving the changes. Empty fields, Work History, and Education History are not shown as separate highlighted changes during duplicate review, as they are updated automatically before the comparison screen opens. 🛠 Troubleshooting Why are some fields already updated before I review the changes? In the Global Resume Parser flow, empty fields, Work History, and Education History may be updated automatically before the review step. These changes are saved before reviewing the remaining fields. I cannot see the Re-parse Resume option Make sure you are viewing the candidate’s profile page. The option is available from the default Resume field or the three-dot action menu . FAQs What happens to fields that already have information? Existing field values are only updated if you select them during the review process or choose the override option. What happens if the parsed resume contains information that is already available in the candidate profile? Fields with identical values remain unselected, as there is no new information to update. Are custom fields included in the comparison view? No. The comparison view currently supports only the default candidate fields available through the resume parser. t: Re-pitch candidates to contacts
s: This article will help you keep track of all your candidate pitches.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to re-pitch candidates to contacts
How to track your pitches
FAQs
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Learn to manage and track your candidate pitches, streamlining your process of pitching candidates multiple times to the same contact. You can use this feature when: You want to resend/re-share previously pitched candidates to the same client or contact. You need to track when and to whom candidates have been pitched. You want to mark candidates as pitched for internal tracking without emailing. How to re-pitch candidates to contacts 1. On the Candidates List page, select the candidates you would like to pitch and click on the "Pitch Candidates" button. This starts the pitching workflow from your candidate list page so you can quickly send or log pitches for one or more candidates. ​ 2. Select the contacts you would like to pitch your candidates to and click on "Mark Candidates As Pitched" (for internal tracking) or "Select Fields & Email Contacts" (to send the selected candidates to your client). Learn more about all the ways you can pitch candidates to contacts 3. If the candidates you selected have already been pitched in the past to the same contact, a message will appear asking you to confirm that you want to re-pitch those candidates. This confirmation helps prevent unintentional duplicate pitches. 4. Click 'Yes' to continue. ​ How to track your pitches You can track the pitches on both candidates' and contacts' profiles. On the candidate's profile, under the "Contact(s) Pitched" tab, you'll be able to see all contacts the candidates have been pitched to and the user who made the pitch as well. ​ The system will show you the most recent pitch made. You'll see all the past pitches once you click on the icon next to the Pitched stage. ​ The same goes for the contact’s profile: While generating a Team Performance Report , the number of times a candidate has been pitched to the same contact will be considered in the report, so that you can keep track of how many times you’ve re-pitched the candidate to the same contact. 🤔FAQs Can I re-pitch the same candidate to the same contact multiple times? Yes. When you select a candidate and contact combination that was pitched before, Recruit CRM will show a confirmation message. Click Yes to proceed with the re-pitch. Conclusion: Re-pitching candidates to contacts in Recruit CRM helps you manage repeat submissions and follow-ups while keeping a complete, accurate pitch history. t: Receive job requisitions on Recruit CRM from your hiring managers
s: Easily receive job requisition in Recruit CRM your hiring managers!
h: 1. Approve a job ✅
2. Decline a job ❌
3. Delete a job 🚮
b: One key aspect that significantly impacts the efficiency of the recruitment process is the seamless transmission of job requisitions from hiring managers to recruiters. With our Hiring Manager Portal , you can receive job requisitions from your hiring managers directly in Recruit CRM, ensuring accuracy and timely action on every hiring need. Managing job requisitions received in Recruit CRM As you navigate to your jobs list page, you'll find a tab labeled " Job Requisitions ". ​ Within this tab, you'll see a list of all job requisitions submitted by your hiring managers through the Hiring Manager Portal. Here's how the hiring managers can share job requisitions The user to whom a job requisition has been made by the hiring manager will receive an email notification of it. Actions that can be performed on the job requisitions received from your clients 🖇️ 1. Approve a job ✅ If you're satisfied that all essential information is present and you're ready to proceed to work on a job, simply click on the 'Tick' icon to approve it. Once approved, you'll be presented with the option to either add the job as a completely new entry in your database or to map it with an existing job already in your system. While mapping, if you want to override the details of your existing job with the newly approved job, check the 'Do you want to override the current job with shared job details?' option located at the bottom. Once you approve and add that job in Recruit CRM, you can start working on that job. 2. Decline a job ❌ Declining a job shares similarities with deleting it, but there are instances where it's essential to provide a reason, such as when crucial information is missing or further clarification is needed. In such cases, you can click on the 'x' icon to decline the job and have the option to include remarks along with the decline, facilitating clear communication with the hiring manager. 3. Delete a job 🚮 If you've decided that you do not want to work on a specific job, then click on the 'Trash' icon to remove the job from your Jobs Requisitions list. We hope this helps! t: Receiving feedback from clients through the Online Candidate link
s: Share candidates assigned with clients and receive feedback online.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Submit candidates and receive client feedback
To share candidates using the Online Candidate Link:
Leaving feedback on an online candidate Link
Troubleshooting
Problem: My client cannot view candidate details.
Problem: I'm not receiving notifications when clients leave feedback.
Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Online Candidate List Link allows you to submit candidates to clients or hiring managers through a secure online page. Clients can review candidate profiles, update hiring stages, and leave feedback, which is automatically synced back to Recruit CRM. This feature is useful when you want to: Share shortlisted candidates with clients. Collect client feedback in one place. Allow clients to update permitted hiring stages. Receive notifications whenever clients leave feedback or update a hiring stage. Submit candidates and receive client feedback To share candidates using the Online Candidate Link: Open the required Job and enable visibility for the candidates you want the client to review. You can also use Set Visibility for All Candidates to update visibility for all candidates at once. Candidate visibility can also be managed directly from each hiring stage by clicking the stage name. Click Submit Candidates , select Online Candidate List, and send the link to the assigned contact(s). The online link displays only the candidate fields you've chosen to share. You can configure the default shared fields in the Field shared with client. You can also customize the fields displayed on the Kanban cards for each job. Leaving feedback on an online candidate Link Once the client opens the link, they can choose between List View and Kanban View to review candidates. Clients can then update the hiring stage and leave remarks or feedback for each candidate. Please note: The client will only be able to change the Hiring Stages you have given them access to by selecting the "Let Client Use" option on the Master Hiring Pipeline : Whenever a client updates a hiring stage or submits feedback, the Job Owner and the Collaborators receive a notification in Recruit CRM. You can also review the client's feedback at any time by clicking the Remarks icon in the Candidate Pipeline for the job. Troubleshooting Problem: My client cannot view candidate details. Likely Cause: Candidate visibility hasn't been enabled, or the required fields aren't shared. What to Check: Verify that candidate visibility is turned on and confirm that the necessary candidate fields are included in the shared view. Resolution: Enable candidate visibility and update the shared fields before resending the online candidate link. Problem: I'm not receiving notifications when clients leave feedback. Likely Cause: No feedback has been submitted, or you're not the job owner or added as a collaborator. What to Check: Confirm that the client submitted feedback and verify the job ownership. Resolution: The job owner and collaborators receive notifications automatically whenever a client updates a hiring stage or leaves feedback. Conclusion: The Online Candidate Link makes it easy to collaborate with clients by allowing them to review candidates, leave feedback, and update permitted hiring stages in real time. This helps streamline communication, keeps everyone aligned throughout the hiring process, and ensures feedback is captured directly within Recruit CRM. t: Recent policy changes from Google,Yahoo & Microsoft
s: This article will help you keep up with Google & Yahoo's new email protection policy.
h: 1. Email authentication
1.1 SPF (Sender Policy Framework)
What is SPF?
How to set up SPF:
1.2 DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail)
What is DKIM?
How to set up DKIM:
1.3 DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance)
b: Google , Yahoo , and Microsoft announced an upcoming change to their policies to enhance security, privacy, and overall user experience. These changes aim to create a safer online environment for users and reduce the risks associated with email communication. As a result, it is crucial for you to ensure that your email practices align with these updated policies to avoid any disruptions in communication. To maintain a seamless and secure exchange of emails, we kindly request your cooperation in adhering to the following guidelines: 1. Email authentication Ensure that your email server supports industry-standard authentication protocols such as SPF (Sender Policy Framework), DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail), and DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance). This helps in verifying the authenticity of the sender and prevents email spoofing. 1.1 SPF (Sender Policy Framework) What is SPF? SPF is an email authentication protocol that allows the domain owner to specify which mail servers are authorized to send emails on behalf of their domain. How to set up SPF: To implement SPF for your domain: Access your domain's DNS settings. Add a TXT record containing your SPF information. For example: Example: v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all Customize the "include" values based on the email service providers you use. 1.2 DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) What is DKIM? DKIM adds a digital signature to outgoing emails, allowing the recipient to verify that the email was genuinely sent by the domain owner and has not been altered during transit. How to set up DKIM: To implement DKIM for your domain: Generate a DKIM key pair, usually provided by your email service provider. Add the public key as a TXT record in your domain's DNS. Example: selector._domainkey.yourdomain.com IN TXT "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIGfMA0GCSqGSIb3DQEBAQUAA4GNADCBiQKBgQC2Gv1u0Awuzx2pLkoHw84BYz0RL1D8lPKQxdJmy8QF3gIytkTcSkVLrLeQsWMx5bV8TVTIh6aBREwhHwV7PLUzB4JY0ULdnG0sW/W3UrcLCYQWqBA2vq8+jOuj6DUMcBoFwP5rtbCm0LiPy1f+yaq2KFEnq5XkFDnETUpTTekQIDAQAB" Adjust the "selector" and "p" values accordingly. 1.3 DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) What is DMARC? DMARC builds on SPF and DKIM to provide a policy framework for domain owners to specify how email receivers should handle messages that fail authentication. How to set up DMARC: To implement DMARC for your domain: Create a TXT record in your DNS with the DMARC policy. For example: _dmarc.yourdomain.com IN TXT "v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc@example.com; ruf=mailto:dmarc@example.com; fo=1" Customize the "p" value based on your desired policy (none, quarantine, or reject). Best Practices: To maintain strong email deliverability: 1. Regularly monitor DMARC reports and adjust policies accordingly. 2. Test your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configurations using online tools. DMARC Lookup SPF Lookup Domain Scanner 3. Keep your DNS records up to date as your email infrastructure evolves. If you encounter any challenges during the implementation process or have questions, please reach out to your Email Administrator/ Email Service Provider. 2. Enable Easy Unsubscription Email recipients must be able to unsubscribe from unwanted emails without any hassle. It should just take one click. 3. Ensure you are sending a wanted email Based on email sender guidelines from Google , you should maintain a spam rate of 0.1% or less to verify recipients of your email successfully receive your emails. If your spam rate is consistently 0.3% or more, you may experience email performance issues, including delays, spam filtering, or bounces. Troubleshooting Problem: Emails are being marked as spam Likely Cause: SPF, DKIM, or DMARC records are missing or incorrectly configured, or your spam complaint rate is too high. What to Check: Verify that your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records are valid and active. Review your spam complaint rate and email engagement metrics. Resolution: Correct any authentication issues, send emails only to recipients who expect them, and regularly clean your mailing lists to maintain a healthy sender reputation. FAQs Do I need all three authentication methods? Yes. Google, Yahoo, and Microsoft strongly recommend implementing SPF, DKIM, and DMARC together for the best protection and deliverability. How often should I review my authentication settings? Review your settings whenever you change email providers, update infrastructure, or experience deliverability issues. Conclusion: Google, Yahoo, and Microsoft have strengthened their email sender requirements to improve security and reduce unwanted email. To maintain reliable email delivery, ensure your domain is authenticated with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, provide a one-click unsubscribe option, and follow email-sending best practices. t: Recruit Craft vs iFrame
s: Wondering whether to use Recruit Craft or the iFrame integration for your jobs page? Let’s break it down in simple terms.
h: 1. Flexible customization options 🎨
2. Flexible layout options 🧩
3. Optimized for visibility 🔍
4. Built-in analytics support 📊
5. Enhanced candidate engagement 💼
6. Brand consistency 🌐
7. Smooth mobile experience 📱
8. Faster loading and consistent performance ⚡
b: Both the Recruit Craft and the iFrame integration allow you to display open jobs on your website efficiently, but they serve different needs and use cases. The iFrame provides a set-up that’s great for simplicity and speed, while Recruit Craft offers a quick, ready-to-use setup for additional flexibility, design control, and advanced tools for teams looking for deeper customization and insights. ​ Here’s a detailed look at how both solutions work and where Recruit Craft offers extended capabilities. 1. Flexible customization options 🎨 The iFrame integration helps you simply embed your job listings into your website while maintaining your brand’s basic look and feel through color and font adjustments. Recruit Craft, on the other hand, quickly expands on this by letting you customize not just the appearance but also how your job data and filters function. It adds a layer of flexibility, giving you full creative control over both design and functionality. You can adjust how listings are displayed and how candidates interact with them, giving you more creative freedom when needed. 2. Flexible layout options 🧩 The iFrame offers a consistent, ready-to-use layout that keeps implementation simple and efficient. In contrast, Recruit Craft expands on this by offering multiple professional templates, letting you pick a layout that best fits your website style. Each template can be edited in real time, with no developer assistance required. ​ 3. Optimized for visibility 🔍 Both integrations help showcase your job openings, but Recruit Craft adds SEO-friendly formatting and is compatible with Google for Jobs . This makes it easier for search engines to recognize and display your job posts in search results, helping you reach a wider audience and improves how your listings appear in search results, helping attract more organic candidates and reducing dependency on paid ads. 4. Built-in analytics support 📊 The iFrame provides a straightforward way to present job listings, while Recruit Craft offers deeper analytics options. It allows you to integrate with tools such as Google Tag Manager to monitor visitor engagement, clicks, and conversions which helps you analyze the performance and optimize results. ​ Click here to know how to add a GTM tracking pixel to your Recruit Craft page 5. Enhanced candidate engagement 💼 While the iFrame keeps the application process simple and direct, Recruit Craft includes a candidate portal where candidates can log in, track their application status, and manage their details. This optional feature is helpful for organizations that want to offer a more interactive experience to applicants, which leads to better engagement and higher completion rates. ​ Click here to know more about how the Candidate Portal works 6. Brand consistency 🌐 Both iFrame and Recruit Craft allow branding customization, but Recruit Craft provides a more detailed approach. You can align elements such as typography, layout, and colors more closely with your website, ensuring your careers page blends seamlessly with your brand identity and ensures that your careers page feels like a natural extension of your main website. 7. Smooth mobile experience 📱 The iFrame ensures your jobs page is quick to set up and displays consistently across devices. Recruit Craft adds further flexibility by letting you fine-tune how your careers page appears on mobile, ensuring full responsiveness and optimal readability. ​ 8. Faster loading and consistent performance ⚡ The iFrame integration offers a simple and reliable way to display your job listings directly on your website. Recruit Craft takes this a step further by providing a modern, performance-optimized setup that ensures quick loading and a seamless experience across all devices. Both options help you deliver a smooth candidate experience, with Recruit Craft focusing on enhanced responsiveness and visual consistency. Both the Recruit Craft and the iFrame help you share job openings with ease. If you’re looking for a direct setup, the iFrame is a good choice as it’s simple and efficient for getting started fast. However, if you want a more customizable, data-driven, and brand-focused solution, Recruit Craft is the way to go. It gives you greater flexibility to design your careers page, enhance candidate engagement, and create an experience that truly reflects your brand. s: Build and customize your recruitment website directly within Recruit Craft using a simple drag-and-drop editor.
h: What this feature does and when to use it
