t: Resume parsing on Recruit CRM
s: Our powerful Resume Parser lets you quickly build your database by directly uploading CVs already on your computer into Recruit CRM
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
How to parse resumes in Recruit CRM
Troubleshooting
Problem: Resumes are uploaded, but no candidate profiles are created.
Problem: Not all resumes in a large batch appear to be parsed.
FAQs
Q1: How many resumes can I parse at one time?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Adding candidates one at a time is painful. The Resume Parser in Recruit CRM automatically creates candidate profiles from uploaded resumes, making the process both efficient and accurate. The Resume Parser is designed with a user-friendly interface, making it seamless to add and manage candidate profiles. You can use this feature when: You need to upload and parse multiple resumes at once. You want to quickly create accurate candidate profiles from resumes. Before you begin: Please note: You can parse up to 100 files at a time. If you upload the resume in the Files section, then it will not be parsed. How to parse resumes in Recruit CRM Open Recruit CRM and go to the Candidate List page. ​ On the Candidate List page, locate the + Resume Parser button beside the AI Sourcing button, and click it. In the Resume Parser box, either drag and drop resumes into the upload box or select files from your computer. ​ Upload up to 100 resume files in a single batch, then wait for the system notification confirming all resumes have been parsed. Processing time may vary as larger batches can take a few minutes. Once parsing is complete, review the newly created candidate profiles from the Resume Parser page. ​ Use the available bulk actions to manage the newly added candidates. You can add notes, compose emails, add candidates to a Hotlist, and perform other available actions. ​ Edit individual candidate profiles if you need to review, complete, or update any of the parsed information. ​ You can also bulk assign the parsed candidates to a job directly from the Resume Parser page. Please note: If you are updating a single candidate and want their resume to be parsed, upload the resume in the default Resume field on the candidate profile. Do not upload the resume in the general Files section , as resumes uploaded there will not be parsed. You might also want to check out How Resume Parsing Works in Recruit CRM. Troubleshooting Problem: Resumes are uploaded, but no candidate profiles are created. Likely cause: The resumes belong to candidates who already exist in your Recruit CRM database. Recruit CRM identifies existing candidate records by matching information such as their email address, phone number, or LinkedIn URL and updates the existing profile instead of creating a duplicate candidate record. What to check: Search your candidate database for the candidate and check whether their existing profile has been updated with the information from the uploaded resume. Resolution: No further action is required if the existing candidate profile has been updated successfully if you do not want to create duplicate candidates. Problem: Not all resumes in a large batch appear to be parsed. Likely cause: The upload exceeds the limit of 100 files per batch, or parsing is still in progress. ​ What to check: Count how many files you attempted to upload and check whether you received the notification that parsing is complete. ​ Resolution: Ensure each upload batch includes no more than 100 files. If you uploaded a large number of files, wait a few minutes and watch for the completion notification before checking the candidate list again. FAQs Q1: How many resumes can I parse at one time? You can parse up to 100 files at a time in a single upload. Q2: How do I access the Resume Parser in Recruit CRM? Navigate to the Candidate List page and click the Resume Parser button beside the AI Sourcing button. Q3: Will files uploaded in the file section be parsed? t: Resume parsing on Recruit CRM (New UI)
s: Our powerful Resume Parser lets you quickly build your database by directly uploading CV's already in your computer into Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin
Step-by-step instructions
Re-parse Resumes & Choose Which Fields to Update
Troubleshooting
FAQs
How many resumes can I parse at once with the Resume Parser?
Can I parse a single resume while creating or editing a candidate?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Adding candidates one at a time is painful. The Resume Parser in Recruit CRM automatically creates candidate profiles from uploaded resumes, making the process both efficient and accurate. The Resume Parser is designed with a user-friendly interface, making it seamless to add and manage candidate profiles. You can use this feature when: You need to upload and parse multiple resumes at once. You want to quickly create accurate candidate profiles from resumes. Before you begin Please note: You can parse up to 100 files at a time. If you upload the resume in the Files section, then it will not be parsed. Step-by-step instructions Go to the Candidates section in Recruit CRM. Click on the Add Candidate button, then select the Resume Parser option from the dropdown to open the Resume Parsing window. ​ In the Resume Parser window, either drag and drop resumes into the upload box or click to select files from your computer. You will receive a notification once all resumes have been parsed. This may take a few minutes if you uploaded a large number of files. When duplicate candidates are detected during Global Resume Parsing, they are clearly marked with a “Duplicate” tag so you can easily identify them before proceeding. Each duplicate candidate also includes an “Update Values” option, allowing you to review the existing candidate profile alongside the newly parsed resume information before applying any changes. Please Note: In the comparison screen, fields where changes are detected are automatically selected by default. You can review these selections and choose which fields should or should not be updated before saving the changes. Empty fields, Work History, and Education History are not shown as separate highlighted changes during duplicate review, as they are updated automatically before the comparison screen opens. If multiple duplicate candidates are found, you can navigate through them one by one using the duplicate counter. You can choose to skip a duplicate or update selected field values and move to the next duplicate. For the final duplicate candidate, the option changes to Override Selected Field Values . Perform Bulk Actions on Parsed Candidates: Once parsing is complete, review the list of newly added candidates. From this page, you can perform bulk actions such as: Compose an email, add a note, assign to owner, update the field assign to a job, and add the candidates to a hot list and more. You can also edit the candidate profile and assign them to a job directly from the page. Use the Default Resume Field to Trigger Parsing : When creating or editing a candidate profile, you can upload a resume directly into the Default Resume field to trigger parsing for that specific candidate. You can also upload the resume in the default resume field to parse the resume. Re-parse Resumes & Choose Which Fields to Update You can replace a candidate's resume from the Candidate Details page using the default Resume field. When uploading a new resume, you can choose between: 1. Replace Resume: Replaces only the resume file without parsing it or updating the candidate's existing profile information. 2. Replace and Re-parse Resume: Replaces the existing resume, parses the newly uploaded file, and displays a comparison screen with the Field Name , New Value , and Current Value side-by-side, allowing you to compare the extracted information with the candidate's existing profile and choose which fields to update. Note: Recruit CRM remembers your last selected option and automatically pre-selects it the next time you replace a resume for any candidate. Users can choose to re-parse a candidate's resume from either of the following locations: From the default Resume field on the candidate profile From the three-dot action menu Once selected, the resume is parsed again, and the newly extracted information is compared with the candidate’s current profile details before any updates are applied. You can choose how the candidate information should be updated by selecting either the ' Update Empty Field Values' option or the ' Override Selected Field Values' option: When the ' Update Empty Field Values' option is selected, the system will only fill fields that are currently empty in the candidate profile, while keeping the existing information unchanged. When the ' Override Selected Field Values' option is selected, the system will replace the existing candidate information with the newly parsed values for the fields you select. This gives you more control over which existing details should be updated from the latest resume. Note: If a re-parsed resume contains no new information to update, the comparison screen displays a Save option along with the message: "No changes detected. Click Save to update the resume." so you can complete the process without updating any fields. Clicking Save replaces only the resume file; no candidate fields are updated. Bulk resume re-parsing and bulk candidate updates are currently not supported. The comparison view currently supports only the default candidate fields available in the resume parser. Troubleshooting Problem: Resumes are not being parsed after upload. Likely cause: The resumes were uploaded to the Files section instead of the Resume Parser or Default Resume field. What to check: Confirm whether the files were added through the Resume Parser button in the Add Candidate button in Candidates, or through the Default Resume field. Resolution path: To upload and parse resumes into Recruit CRM, click on the Resume Parser button inside the Add Candidate button in Candidates. You can also upload the resume in the default resume field to parse the resume. If you upload the resume in the Files section, then it will not be parsed. Problem: Parsing is taking longer than expected. Likely cause: A large number of files were uploaded at once. What to check: Check how many resumes you uploaded in a single batch. Resolution path: This might take a few minutes if you have uploaded a large number of files. Wait for the notification once your resume has been parsed. You will receive a notification once your resume has been parsed. FAQs How many resumes can I parse at once with the Resume Parser? You can upload and parse up to 100 files at a time, making it ideal for high-volume recruitment needs. Can I parse a single resume while creating or editing a candidate? You can also upload the resume in the default Resume field to parse the resume. When creating or editing a candidate profile, you can upload a resume directly into the Default Resume field to trigger parsing for that specific candidate. Conclusion: The resume parser in Recruit CRM lets you build your candidate database in seconds by automatically creating candidate profiles from uploaded resumes. By using the Resume Parser button in Candidates or the Default Resume field, you can parse up to a hundred files at a time and then perform powerful bulk actions, so you can move from raw resumes to ready-to-use candidate profiles with just a few clicks. Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Resume/CV Formatting feature allows you to customize resumes with your organization's branding before sharing them with clients. You can add headers, footers, cover letters, and watermarks while also redacting sensitive candidate information. This feature is useful when you want to: Brand resumes with your company details. Hide sensitive candidate information before sharing resumes. Create client-ready resumes in just a few clicks. Please note: Resume/CV Formatting, including Text Redaction and the ability to add custom Headers, Footers, Cover Letters, and Watermarks, is available on the Business plan and above . When converting DOC files to PDF, minor formatting differences may occur. How to format a Resume/CV? You can generate a formatted resume from either the Candidate Details page or by opening the candidate's existing resume. Open the Generate Formatted Resume window using either of the following methods: From the Candidate Details page, click the three-dot menu and select Generate Formatted Resume. Open the candidate's existing Resume and click Generate Formatted Resume . Under Templates, add or select the Header, Footer, Cover Letter, and Watermark you want to apply to the formatted resume. Use the Text Redaction feature to remove sensitive information, such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, or addresses. You can either: Enter keywords in the Text Redaction field and click Apply Redaction to remove matching text. Use the highlighter tool to manually select specific sections of the resume. Simply click and drag over the text or area you want to hide and click Apply Redaction . After making the required changes, click Save . You can optionally rename the file before saving. The formatted resume is automatically saved in the candidate's Files section. If you've created file-type custom fields, select the required field under Select Custom Field To Save File before saving. Please note: Only file-type custom fields created under Candidate Fields are available in the Select Custom Field To Save File dropdown. If required, create a new file-type custom field before saving the formatted resume. FAQs 1. Can I add my company's branding to resumes? Yes. You can add custom headers, footers, cover letters, and watermarks to create branded, client-ready resumes. 2. Where is the formatted resume saved? By default, it is saved in the candidate's Files section. You can also save it to a file- type custom field. Conclusion: The Resume/CV Formatting feature helps you quickly create professional, branded resumes by adding custom templates, redacting sensitive information, and saving formatted copies directly within Recruit CRM. For the best experience, we recommend setting up your Header, Footer, Cover Letter, and Watermark templates before formatting resumes. Conclusion:
b: What this features does and when to use it? Through this feature, you can generate branded, client-ready resumes directly from candidate profiles. You can apply branding elements such as headers, footers, cover letters, and watermarks to create consistent resume submissions across clients and roles. You can also redact sensitive information such as names, phone numbers, email addresses, physical addresses, and LinkedIn profiles before sharing candidate profiles externally. Once saved, the formatted resume is stored on the candidate record either in a selected file-type custom field or in the Files section. This helps you maintain a consistent, professional format across all submissions. Please note - The Resume/CV Formatting feature, including Text Redaction and the ability to add custom headers, footers, and watermarks is available on the Business Plan and above. You can use this feature when: You want to add your logo, agency details, or standardised branding to every CV sent to clients. You need to hide sensitive candidate information (like contact details or LinkedIn) before sharing resumes. Your client requires resumes in a specific, uniform layout or format. You want to store multiple versions of a candidate’s resume (raw vs. formatted) in structured fields. ​ Before you begin • If you want to save formatted resumes into specific fields, you will need file-type custom fields created under Candidate Fields . • When converting DOC files to PDF, minor formatting limitations may occur. While the system handles most conversions accurately, complete accuracy cannot be guaranteed in all cases. Step-by-step instructions 1. Use any of the following methods to access the Generate Formatted Resume tab - From within the Candidate Profile page To format a resume, go to the candidate profile and click on the three dots at the top of the profile. ​ Once you click this,in the menu that appears, select Generate Formatted Resume . ​ From within the Resume You can also open the candidate’s resume in Recruit CRM and scroll to the bottom of the page. From there, click on Generate Formatted Resume to proceed. 2 . Configure Header, Footer, Cover Letter, and Watermark Once you open the Generate Formatted Resume tab, use the Templates section to apply headers, footers, cover letters, and watermarks. These templates allow you to standardise resume branding across clients, teams, or submission workflows. You can select an existing template or create a new one based on your requirements. 3. Use Text Redaction to Remove Sensitive Information Text redaction allows you to hide sensitive candidate information from a resume before sharing it with clients. This can include details such as name, email, phone number, address, LinkedIn profile, or any other information you do not want to disclose. Text Redaction only affects the formatted resume that is generated. The original resume file and candidate profile remain unchanged. This is commonly used when sharing resumes with clients while withholding personal contact information during early recruitment stages. You can apply redaction in two ways: Keyword-based redaction Search for a specific keyword, and the system will automatically identify and select all instances of that term in the resume. For example, entering “LinkedIn” will highlight all occurrences of the word, allowing you to remove them in one go. ​ Manual redaction using highlighter Use the highlighter tool to manually select specific sections of the resume. Simply click and drag over the text or area you want to hide. ​ Once you’ve selected all the required sections, click Apply Redaction to remove or hide the highlighted content from the formatted resume. 4. Save the Formatted Resume and Choose Storage Location Saving creates a new formatted version of the resume. The original resume remains unchanged on the candidate record. You can choose where the formatted version is stored so it can be accessed later without regenerating it. Once you’ve made all the changes to the Resume/CV, click Save . A popup will appear where you can rename the file and choose where to store the formatted resume. Enter a file name and select a file-type custom field as the storage location. If you don’t have one set up, you can create a new file-type custom field directly from this popup. ​ If no custom field is selected, the resume will automatically be saved in the Files section of the candidate profile. ​ ​ Note: Only file-type custom fields created under Candidate Fields will appear in the dropdown. Troubleshooting 1. Problem: I cannot see the option Generate Formatted Resume on the candidate profile. Likely cause: Plan or permission limitations. What to check: Confirm that your account is on the Business plan or above and that your user role has permission to view and edit candidate files. Resolution path: Ask your account admin to confirm your plan and adjust your role permissions if needed. 2. Problem: My file-type custom field does not appear in the save dropdown. Likely cause: The custom field is not configured under Candidate Fields or is not of file type. What to check: Go to your field settings and verify that the field is a file-type custom field under Candidate Fields . Resolution path: If needed, create a new file-type custom field under Candidate Fields, then return to the save popup and check again. FAQs 1. What changes after I use CV formatting on a resume? The system creates a new formatted version of the candidate’s resume with your chosen header, footer, cover letter, watermark, and any applied redactions. The original resume file remains unchanged. 2. Which plans and roles can use the CV formatting feature? The resume/CV formatting feature, including text redaction and the ability to add custom headers, footers, and watermarks, is available on the Business plan and above. Users must have permission to access and edit candidate files. 3. Can I have different header and footer templates for different clients? Yes. Under the Template section, you can choose from existing header and footer templates or create new ones. This allows you to maintain multiple branded templates for different clients or use cases. 4. Does text redaction permanently remove data from the candidate profile? No. Text redaction only affects the formatted resume you generate. The original candidate data and original resume file remain intact in the candidate profile. 5. Where is the formatted CV stored after I click Save? If you select a file-type custom field in the popup, the formatted CV is saved in that field. If you do not select or create a custom field, the formatted CV will automatically be saved within the candidate’s Files section. 6. Does CV formatting modify the candidate's original resume? No. CV Formatting always creates a separate formatted version of the resume. The original resume file remains unchanged and available on the candidate record. 7. Can I apply multiple branding elements to the same resume? Yes. A formatted resume can include a header, footer, cover letter, watermark, and text redactions at the same time. These elements are combined into a single formatted version when the resume is generated. Conclusion: CV Formatting helps you create consistent, client-ready resume submissions without editing documents manually. By combining branding templates and text redaction, you can maintain professional presentation standards while controlling what candidate information is shared. t: Revoking your subscription cancelation & reactivating your canceled subscription
s: This article will help you understand how to revoke your canceled subscription and reactivate a canceled subscription.
h: Revoke the subscription cancelation before the subscription expiry
Restarting the subscription after the subscription expiry
b: Recruit CRM makes it very simple to get back and restart your Recruit CRM subscription or revoke the cancelation if you decide to cancel your subscription. Revoke the subscription cancelation before the subscription expiry In case you decide to schedule a cancelation for your subscription, you can easily revert the cancelation by following these steps: 1. Go to your admin settings and click on Account . 2. Scroll down, and click on "Revoke Cancelation". For instance, if your subscription expires on October 30 of the current year, and you cancel your subscription on October 20 of the same year, you will have complete access to your data till October 30 and you can choose to revoke the cancelation anytime during this period. Once you revoke the cancelation, the subscription will renew on the next renewal date and your account will be charged per usual. Restarting the subscription after the subscription expiry In case your subscription has already expired, you can restart the subscription anytime before deactivating the account : Your data will still be saved on our servers after the subscription expiry, but you will not be able to access it without restarting the subscription. However, once you deactivate the account, all your data will be permanently deleted from our servers. b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Schedule Report feature lets you automate the delivery of your saved reports to yourself and your teammates via email. Instead of manually generating and sharing reports, you can schedule them to be sent automatically at your preferred frequency, ensuring everyone receives the latest insights without any additional effort. Use this feature when: • You want reports to be emailed to you or your teammates automatically. • You need reports delivered on a regular schedule, such as daily , weekly , or monthly . • You want to share report insights with individual teammates or entire teams without manually exporting and sending them. • You need to manage multiple scheduled deliveries for the same saved report. When creating a schedule, you can choose the report frequency, start and end dates, recipients, and the export format ( CSV or XLS ). Once configured, Recruit CRM automatically generates and emails the report according to your schedule, helping you stay informed while saving time on repetitive reporting tasks. Schedule a Report 1. Generate the report Navigate to the Reports section and open the report you want to schedule. Configure the report using the required filters and click Generate Report . ​ Learn how to generate reports in Recruit CRM 2. Open the scheduling window After the report is generated, click Schedule Report . ​ 3. Configure the schedule Set up how and when you want the report to be delivered. Configure the following: • Frequency – Choose how often the report should be sent ( Daily , Weekly , or Monthly ). • Schedule Name – Enter a name to help you identify the scheduled report later. • Start Date & Time – Select when the schedule should begin. • End Condition – Choose one of the following options: End on a specific date. End after a specified number of occurrences. Continue indefinitely without an end date. 4. Choose the recipients Select the users who should receive the scheduled report via their registered email addresses. You can send the report to: • Individual teammates. • Entire teams. ​ 5. Configure the email Enter the details for the email that will accompany the report. Configure the following: • Email Subject • Email Body • File Format – Choose whether the report should be attached as a CSV or XLS file. ​ 6. Save the schedule After reviewing your settings, click Save Schedule to create the scheduled report. Track Scheduled Reports You can view and manage all scheduled reports from the Saved and Scheduled Reports tab. ​ From this page, you can: • View all your saved and scheduled reports. • Click the green Schedule label to view the schedule details and delivery history once reports have started sending. • Turn an existing schedule On or Off using the schedule toggle. • Create an additional schedule by clicking Add New Schedule . Add Another Schedule to a Saved Report A saved report can have multiple schedules, allowing you to send the same report at different times or to different recipients. To add another schedule: 1. Open the Saved and Scheduled Reports tab. 2. Locate the saved report and click the Calendar icon in the Actions column. 3. Click the ellipsis (⋯) menu and select Edit Schedule . 4. Click Add New Schedule . 5. Configure the schedule by selecting the frequency, start and end conditions, recipients, email details, and preferred file format. 6. Click Save Schedule to add the new schedule. 📌 Please note: A user can generate and save multiple reports but can only add two schedules to each of the saved reports. ​ Troubleshooting Problem: Recipients are not receiving scheduled reports by email Likely cause : The intended users were not added as recipients. What to check: Review the schedule configuration and confirm the correct users and/or teams are selected as recipients. Confirm that the users have active, registered email addresses in Recruit CRM. Resolution : Update the schedule to include the correct users or teams and ensure their email details are accurate. Problem: Scheduled report stops sending earlier than expected Likely cause: The schedule was configured with an end date or a limited number of repetitions. What to check: Open the schedule settings and review the ending options (specific date, repetitions, or run indefinitely). Resolution: Adjust the ending option to extend the schedule or set it to run indefinitely if you want ongoing delivery. Problem: The report arrives, but the format is not what the recipient expects Likely cause: The wrong file type (CSV or XLS) was selected when creating the schedule. What to check: Review the schedule configuration and verify which file format is selected. Resolution : Edit the schedule and change the report file type to the preferred format (CSV or XLS), then save the updated schedule. FAQs Q1: Can I schedule any report from the Reports section? You can schedule the delivery of reports that you can generate and save from the Reports section, using the Schedule Report button available after the report is generated. Q2: How many schedules can I add to a single saved report? A user can generate and save multiple reports, but can only add two schedules to each of the saved reports. Q3: What file formats are available for scheduled reports? You can choose between CSV and XLS as the file type for scheduled reports. Q4: Who receives the scheduled reports? Scheduled reports are sent by email to the users and teams you select as recipients in the schedule configuration, using their registered email addresses in Recruit CRM. Q5: Where can I see and manage all my scheduled reports? You can keep track of all your scheduled reports under the Saved and Scheduled Reports tab, where you can monitor schedules, view history, add new schedules, and turn existing schedules on or off. Conclusion: Automating report delivery with the Schedule Report feature in Recruit CRM helps you and your teammates stay informed without manual effort. Configure your schedules, recipients, and formats once, and the system will keep your reports flowing reliably to the right inboxes. t: Scheduling Reports for Your Dashboard in Advanced Analytics
s: This article will guide you on how you can schedule reports for your Dashboard in Advanced Analytics.
h: How can I send dashboard updates via email?
Step-by-step instructions on how to create a subscription to a dashboard
What email subscription options are available?
How to customize filters for different subscriptions?
Attach results as files
How to add multiple subscriptions to a dashboard?
How to delete a subscription?

b: What this feature does and when to use it? Dashboard Subscriptions let you deliver a dashboard's results automatically, on a schedule, without anyone having to log in and check it manually. Use this when you have stakeholders recruiters, account managers, clients, or teammates without a Recruit CRM license — who need regular visibility into a dashboard, such as a weekly placements summary or a daily pipeline snapshot, but don't need to interact with the dashboard itself. How can I send dashboard updates via email? You can use Dashboard Subscriptions to automatically send dashboard results to people via email, even if they don’t have a license on Recruit CRM. Once set up, updates will be sent at your chosen frequency, and any changes to the dashboard will be reflected in future deliveries. Note: Subscriptions are private to the person who created them, a subscription you set up won't be visible to your teammates, and you won't see subscriptions they've created either. The same is true for Alerts: only the person who created an alert can see it. All scheduled subscriptions are sent according to the UTC timezone . When selecting the delivery time, please make sure to account for the difference between UTC and your local timezone. Step-by-step instructions on how to create a subscription to a dashboard Open the dashboard you want to share. Click on the three dots (...) . Select Subscriptions . 4.In the sidebar that appears, choose Email it. When you click on Email it option in the sidebar, and advanced analytics will give us some options: 5.Set the delivery options, including recipients and frequency. What email subscription options are available? Add subscribers: Add email addresses to register subscribers. Determine frequency and timing: Choose how often to send updates: Hourly Daily Weekly Monthly And what time of day to send the dashboard? Send email now – Instantly send the dashboard update. Skip emails with no results – Prevents sending empty reports. Apply filters – Customize subscription filter values. How to customize filters for different subscriptions? You can apply different filter values to each subscription so that different users receive tailored reports. Here is how to set filter values for a subscription: Open the dashboard subscription panel . Locate the Set filter values for when this gets sent section. 3.Enter the filter values needed for this subscription. You can set values for each filter on the dashboard. If you have any dashboard filters with default values, you can override those defaults for a given subscription, or leave them as-is. This method allows you to maintain one dashboard while delivering personalized reports to different users. Attach results as files Attach results include dashboard data as a downloadable file. File format You can choose between the following file formats: .csv .xlsx .json Optionally, you can send raw, unformatted data by disabling visualization settings. Questions to attach: Here you can specify which questions Advanced analytics should attach results for. The attached files will include up to 2000 rows by default. To change this row limit on your Advanced Analytics Cloud instance, you can contact us and request a different row limit. Save your subscription. How to add multiple subscriptions to a dashboard? To add multiple subscriptions: Open the dashboard subscription panel. Click on the ➕ (plus) icon to add a new subscription. How to delete a subscription? Open the dashboard subscription panel . Select the subscription you want to remove. Click Delete this subscription at the bottom of the sidebar. 4.Confirm the deletion in the pop-up modal. Troubleshooting Problem: The scheduled email shows different numbers than the live dashboard. Likely cause: A scheduled subscription runs with a fixed set of filter values (either the dashboard's defaults, or whatever values were set when the subscription was created), it doesn't automatically use whatever filters you personally last had selected when viewing the dashboard live. What to check: Open the subscription's settings and check which filter values it's configured to send with. Resolution path: Edit the subscription and set the specific filter values you want it to always use, or leave it on the dashboard's defaults if that's the intended behavior. This is a configuration choice, not a bug. Conclusion: Dashboard Subscriptions let you automatically deliver dashboard results by email at a set frequency, with options to customize filters, attach files, and manage multiple recipients from a single dashboard. This makes it easy to keep informed. If you need help at any stage, feel free to reach out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance. Hope this helps! t: Search in Mailbox
s: This article will help you to make searches inside your mailbox in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to Search in Mailbox
Troubleshooting
Problem: No emails are returned after searching.
FAQ's
Can I search only by the email subject?

b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Search in Mailbox feature allows you to find emails by searching using keywords across different email parameters such as To, From, CC, BCC, Email Subject, Email Body. You can also refine your search using specific search parameters, folders, and date ranges to quickly locate the conversations you need. This feature is useful when you want to: Search for emails containing a specific keyword. Find emails sent to or received from a particular contact/candidate. Search using the email subject or body. Narrow down emails by folder, such as Inbox, Sent, or Trash. View emails from a specific date range. How to Search in Mailbox 1. Navigate to Mailbox , click the search bar, and enter the keyword you want to search for. 2. By default, Recruit CRM searches across all of the following parameters, however, you can also select the desired ones for a more refined result: To From CC BCC Email Subject Email Body Note: Some search parameters may not be available (greyed out) due to limitations imposed by your email provider. These options will appear disabled with a tooltip explaining the limitation. 3. Finally, click Apply Search to display the matching emails. 4. To further refine your search, use the filter panel at the top of the Mailbox. 5. Select the Folder you want to search, such as Inbox , Sent , or Trash . Select a Date Range to display emails from a specific time period. 6. Click Apply to use both filters together. Troubleshooting Problem: No emails are returned after searching. Likely Cause: The keyword entered may be incorrect, or the selected filters are too restrictive. What to Check: Verify that the keyword is spelled correctly. Check the selected search parameters. Confirm the selected folder and date range. Resolution: Modify the keyword or adjust the selected filters, then click Apply Search again. FAQ's Can I search only by the email subject? Yes. Select Email Subject as the search parameter before clicking Apply Search . Why are some search parameters unavailable? Some email providers do not support searching across all email fields. Unsupported parameters will automatically appear disabled. Can I search emails in the Sent or Trash folder? Yes. Select the required folder from the filter panel before applying your search. Conclusion: The Search in Mailbox feature makes it easy to find emails by combining keyword searches with advanced search parameters, folder selection, and date range filters. Using these options together helps you locate conversations quickly and manage your mailbox more efficiently. t: Secure your account using Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)/Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
s: This article will guide you on how to set up 2FA/MFA for your Recruit CRM account.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to set up Two-Factor Authentication?
How to enforce 2 Factor Authentication for all users
How to disable Two-Factor Authentication
Troubleshooting
Problem: I cannot log in because I do not have access to my authenticator app.
Problem: I am not sure what the 2FA status values mean in the user list.
FAQs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Two-Factor Authentication (2FA), or Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), adds an additional layer of security to your Recruit CRM account by requiring a verification code from an authenticator app in addition to your username and password when signing in. When 2FA is enabled, your Recruit CRM account is linked to an authenticator app using a QR code or setup key. The authenticator app generates a time-based, one-time six-digit verification code that must be entered during login. When 2FA is enforced at the account level, all users are required to configure and use 2FA unless they have been specifically excluded. Users receive an email notification prompting them to complete the setup and can configure it during their next login. Use this feature when: • You want to add an extra layer of protection to your Recruit CRM account • Your organization has security or compliance requirements that mandate 2FA or MFA. • You need to enforce 2FA for all users, or all users except selected individuals. How to set up Two-Factor Authentication? 1. To set up 2FA/MFA for your account, click on your Profile icon in the top-right corner of Recruit CRM and select Profile . ​ 2. Next, navigate to the Security tab. Once you are in the Security tab, turn on the Authentication App toggle to begin the 2FA/MFA setup process. ​3. The system will immediately open a pop-up with a QR Code to set up the authentication process. You can either: Download an authenticator app like Authy, Google Authenticator, 1Password, or Microsoft Authenticator from your mobile app store and scan the QR code. Manually enter the given code into the authenticator app. 4. Once you connect your Recruit CRM account to the security or authentication app, you'll get a one-time verification code whenever you need it. 5. Insert the 6-digit code and select the "Enable Two Factor Authenticator" option. ​ 6. You will then need to sign out of your account and log in again to set up Two-Factor Authentication. Enter both your password and a security code from your authenticator app to sign in to your account. ​ How to enforce 2 Factor Authentication for all users Users with permission to Account settings can enforce 2FA for all users and enhance security across the organization. 1. Go to Account on the Admin Settings to enforce the Two-Factor Authentication. You will get the option to make it required for all account users or to exclude specific users . ​ ​If you choose to exclude specific users, you'll see a list of all current teammates in your account, and you can select the ones you wish to exclude. ​ 2. After enforcing the Two-Factor Authentication, users will get an email to configure it and will have the option to set it up during their next login in Recruit CRM. ​ 🚫 How to disable Two-Factor Authentication If 2FA is not mandatory in your account, you can disable it from the Security tab in your Profile Settings by entering your Recruit CRM password. ​ In case a user is locked out of their account and 2FA is enforced, anyone with access to User Management settings can disable the 2FA option and allow the teammate to log into Recruit CRM. ​ You can quickly identify the Two-Factor Authentication status by checking the column. There are three possible statuses: Disabled 2FA is not enabled by the user Enabled 2FA was enabled by the user Enforced 2FA is mandatory for that specific user Enabling MFA will disable SSO if that is enabled on the account. Troubleshooting Problem: I cannot log in because I do not have access to my authenticator app. Likely cause: 2FA is enabled (or enforced), and you no longer have your device or app configured. What to check: Check whether 2FA is enforced on your account and whether someone in your organization has user management access. Resolution: Contact a user with user management settings access so they can disable 2FA for your user account. Once you regain access, you can set up 2FA again. Problem: I am not sure what the 2FA status values mean in the user list. Likely cause: The meaning of Disabled, Enabled, and Enforced is unclear. What to check: Look at the 2FA status column for each user. Resolution: Use these definitions: Disabled = 2FA is not enabled Enabled = user turned on 2FA Enforced = 2FA is mandatory for that user. FAQs Who can enforce two-factor authentication for all users? Users with permission to account settings can enforce 2FA for all users. Can I exclude specific users from enforced 2FA? Yes. In the Account settings , after enabling the enforce option, you can choose to exclude specific users and select those you do not want to enforce 2FA for. How can I see whether a user has 2FA enabled or enforced? In the user management , check the 2 Factor Authentication status column. It will show one of three statuses: Disabled, Enabled, or Enforced. Does enabling multi-factor authentication affect SSO? Yes. Enabling multi-factor authentication will disable SSO if SSO is enabled on your account. Conclusion: Two-factor authentication in Recruit CRM helps protect your account and your organization by adding a secure verification step to the login process. Hope this helps! b: What this feature does and when to use it? The See All Emails feature allows Account Owners and users with the appropriate Custom Role permissions to view other users' mailboxes directly from the Recruit CRM Mailbox. This feature is useful when you want to: View another user's mailbox from within Recruit CRM. Monitor email conversations across your team. Search for a teammate's mailbox using their name or email address. Improve collaboration and visibility across your organization. ✉️ See your teammates' emails View a teammate's mailbox Navigate to Mailbox and click the arrow icon next to your mailbox. Select your mailbox or choose a teammate's mailbox from the list. Use the search bar to quickly find a teammate by their name or email address, if required. Grant mailbox access Note: This feature is available only for Account Owners and users assigned a Custom Role with the required permission. Custom Roles & Permissions are available on the Business Plan or higher. Navigate to User Management and open the Roles & Permissions tab . Create a new custom role by clicking New Role, or edit an existing role by clicking the three-dot menu and selecting Edit. Enable the Access to the complete Mailbox & Emails of all users permission. Scroll all the way down and click Save Role on the bottom right to apply your changes. Troubleshooting Problem: I cannot view another user's mailbox. Likely Cause: Your account does not have permission to access other users' mailboxes. What to Check: Verify whether you are an Account Owner or have been assigned a Custom Role with the All Users' Mailbox Access permission enabled. Resolution: Contact your Account Owner or admin to enable the required permission for your role. FAQ's 1. Who can view other users' mailboxes? Only Account Owners and users with a Custom Role that has the All Users' Mailbox Access permission enabled can view other users' mailboxes. 2. Can I search for a teammate's mailbox? Yes. You can use the search bar in the mailbox dropdown to search for teammates by their name or email address. Conclusion The See All Emails feature allows authorized users to access teammates' mailboxes while giving administrators control over mailbox permissions. This helps improve collaboration, visibility, and communication across your organization. b: Customize your Chrome extension to record the most relevant information for candidates, companies, and contacts! You can add more fields of your choice directly to the extension, in addition to the existing ones. Whether it's a default field or any of the custom fields, the Chrome extension can be aligned perfectly to suit your unique requirements. How to add custom fields to the Chrome extension? 1. Go to Admin Settings >> Data Customization >> Candidate Fields / Company Fields / Contact Fields to view a list of default and custom fields that can be displayed on your extension. 2. To show a field on the extension, simply check the corresponding checkbox under the ' Extension ' column, and uncheck it to hide the field. Note: The fields that are already available by default in the extension cannot be deselected. These default fields will appear as greyed out for easy identification. Additionally, you can select up to 15 fields that can be displayed on the Chrome extension. For candidates, the Work and Education History sections are available by default on the extension. How to reorder sections on the Chrome extension? You can change the order of sections on the Chrome extension by heading to the ' Settings ' tab (gear icon) on the Chrome extension and using the ' hamburger menu ' icon to drag them across the list. FAQs on selecting additional/custom fields in the Chrome extension What happens if I select more than 15 fields? Since we have set up the Chrome extension to display only 15 additional fields, the system will restrict you from selecting more than 15 checkboxes in the 'Extension' column within Admin Settings. Can I add file-type custom fields to the Chrome extension? Yes, you can add a file type custom field to appear on the Chrome extension. However, please note that the extension won't show a preview of the file due to technical constraints, you'll only be able to see the file name. How does the override data setting work with the new features? The override data settings do not affect the additional fields within the Chrome extension. These fields will always be overwritten, except for Current Organization and Skills. This design enables users to make updates to the data without constraints, particularly for custom fields where data isn't sourced from LinkedIn. t: SEO Settings in Recruit Craft
s: This article explains how to configure SEO settings for your Recruit Craft website and Career Pages
h: What this feature does and when to use it
What is SEO and why is it important?
Configure SEO Settings for a Website Page
Click here to know more about what to configure in the SEO Settings
The SEO Settings panel contains the following fields: 1. Route (URL Path)
2. Page Title
3. Page Description
4. Metadata
b: ✨ What this feature does and when to use it SEO (Search Engine Optimization) helps search engines like Google understand your website content and display it to people searching for relevant information. Recruit Craft allows you to configure SEO settings for individual website pages as well as Career Pages. These settings control how your pages appear in search engine results and when they are shared on social platforms. Using the SEO settings panel, you can configure: • Route (URL path) • Page Title • Page Description • Metadata • Thumbnail Image These settings help improve discoverability, create a better user experience, and increase the chances of attracting relevant candidates and clients to your website. Use this feature when: • You want your website or Career Page to rank better on search engines • You are creating a new website and want to optimize it from the beginning • You want pages shared on social platforms to display professional titles, descriptions, and images • You need different SEO settings for different pages on your website • You want candidates and clients to easily understand what a page is about before clicking it 🤔 What is SEO and why is it important? SEO stands for Search Engine Optimization. It is the process of helping search engines understand your website content so that your pages can appear in relevant search results. Good SEO can help: • Increase website visibility • Attract more candidates and clients • Improve click-through rates from search engines • Create more professional page previews when links are shared For example, if someone searches for "Recruitment jobs in London," well-configured SEO settings can help your Careers Page or Job Page appear higher in search results. 📋 Configure SEO Settings for a Website Page Follow these steps to configure SEO settings for a website page: Open your website project in Recruit Craft and navigate to the Pages section in the left sidebar. Click the three dots (⋮) next to the page that you want to configure the SEO settings for, and select SEO Settings, and the SEO Settings panel will open. Fill in the required SEO fields: • Route • Page Title • Page Description • Metadata • Thumbnail Image ​ Review all details carefully and ensure they accurately describe the page. ​ Click Save to apply the SEO settings. ​ The updated information will be used for search engines and social sharing previews. Click here to know more about what to configure in the SEO Settings The SEO Settings panel contains the following fields: 1. Route (URL Path) The Route determines the page URL and forms part of the link visitors use to access the page. ​ Example: Website URL: https://yourcompany.com Route: about-us Final URL: https://yourcompany.com/about-us ​ A clear and descriptive route helps both users and search engines understand what the page is about. ​ Best practices: • Use descriptive words • Keep URLs short and readable • Use lowercase letters • Separate words with hyphens ​ 📌 Important: • Duplicate page URLs are not allowed • Routes only support lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens 2. Page Title The Page Title is the main title associated with the page. It appears in browser tabs and is commonly used as the clickable headline in search engine results. A good page title helps search engines understand the page content and helps users decide whether to visit the page. ​ Example: Recruitment Jobs in London | ABC Recruitment ​ Best practices: • Clearly describe the page • Include relevant keywords • Keep it concise and easy to understand 3. Page Description The Page Description provides a short summary of the page content. Search engines often display this text below the page title in search results. A well-written description gives visitors a preview of what they can expect on the page and can encourage more clicks. Example: Explore the latest recruitment and staffing opportunities in London. Apply directly through ABC Recruitment. Best practices: • Summarize the page clearly • Include relevant keywords naturally • Encourage users to click 4. Metadata Metadata provides additional information about the page that helps search engines better understand and categorize its content. While metadata is not always directly visible to visitors, it can improve how search engines interpret and index your pages. Use metadata to provide additional context about the page and its purpose. 5. Thumbnail Image The Thumbnail Image is used when the page is shared on social platforms or appears in supported link previews. A relevant thumbnail helps create a more professional appearance and can increase engagement when the page is shared. Examples: • LinkedIn posts • Facebook shares • Messaging apps Use a high-quality image that represents the page content and aligns with your branding. ​ ​ 📋 Configure SEO Settings for a Career Page SEO settings for Career Pages follow the same process as website pages. ​ To update SEO settings for a Career Page: Open your Career Page project. Locate the page you want to update. Open SEO Settings by clicking the three dots (⋮) next to the page that you want to configure the SEO settings for. Configure the Route, Page Title, Page Description, Metadata, and Thumbnail Image. Save your changes. The SEO settings will be applied to the Career Page in the same way as standard website pages. ⚠️ Important Notes • SEO settings are configured separately for each page • Duplicate page URLs are not allowed • Routes only support lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens • Website pages and Career Pages follow the same SEO configuration process • SEO changes may take time to appear in search engine results • If you change the URL of a published page, Recruit Craft will display a warning because existing links may break ❓ FAQs Do I need to configure SEO settings for every page? No, but it is recommended for important pages such as Home, Careers, Jobs, About Us, and other key landing pages. Can different pages have different SEO settings? Yes. SEO settings are configured individually for each page. What happens if two pages use the same route? Recruit Craft does not allow duplicate page URLs. Each page must have a unique route. Will SEO changes appear immediately on Google? No. Search engines may take some time to crawl and update their search results. Do Career Pages use the same SEO settings? Yes. Career Pages follow the same SEO configuration process and support the same SEO fields as website pages. SEO settings help improve how your website and Career Pages appear in search engines and social sharing previews. By configuring clear routes, titles, descriptions, metadata, and thumbnail images for each page, you can make your content easier to discover and create a more professional experience for candidates and clients. t: Sequences within Recruit CRM
s: In this article, we will discuss the power of sequences for streamlined communication and task management within Recruit CRM.
h: How do sequences work?
What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
Understand sequence types and capabilities
Email Sequencing
SMS Sequencing
LinkedIn Message Sequencing
Task Sequencing
b: How do sequences work? The sequence is a powerful strategy that enables you to streamline your communication efforts and optimize task management. In this article, we will talk about the various sequence capabilities Recruit CRM offers. When a candidate or contact is enrolled, Recruit CRM begins executing the sequence from the first configured step. A sequence can include: • Emails • SMS messages • LinkedIn messages • Internal tasks Each step executes in sequence according to its configured timing and channel. The next step is triggered based on the delays and schedule defined within the sequence. This allows you to automate outreach, follow-ups, and internal actions without manually managing each interaction. If a step fails due to issues such as a disconnected email account, insufficient SMS credits, or invalid contact information, the enrollment may pause until the issue is resolved. A candidate or contact can only be actively enrolled in one sequence at a time. What this feature does and when to use it? Sequences in Recruit CRM help you automate communication and follow-ups across multiple channels such as email, SMS, LinkedIn, and internal tasks. Instead of manually reaching out at every step, you can set up a structured workflow that runs automatically over time. This ensures consistent outreach, better engagement, and fewer missed follow-ups while managing candidates or contacts at scale. You can use this feature when: • You want to automate candidate follow-ups after sourcing. • You want to Reactivate an existing talent pool. • Scale outreach with consistency. Please note : This is an exclusive feature which is available on Business plan and above. Users on the Pro plan/Free Trial can create only 1 sequence on their account at a time. Before you begin: • Ensure your email, SMS provider, and LinkedIn integrations (where applicable) are connected and active. • Confirm that you have the required permissions to access Admin Settings > Sequences if you plan to manage sequence configurations. • Make sure candidate and contact records have valid email addresses, phone numbers, and LinkedIn URLs (if used in sequences). • Check that your account has sufficient SMS credits if you are using SMS sequences . • Be aware that opted-out contacts (email/SMS) and candidates already in another sequence will not be enrolled again. Understand sequence types and capabilities Recruit CRM supports multiple types of sequencing that you can use individually or in combination: Email Sequencing Send a series of scheduled email templates to candidates and contacts over a defined period. This ensures consistent, timely, and personalized outreach, with emails going out one after another as configured. ​ ​ Click here to read more about Email Sequencing in Recruit CRM SMS Sequencing Create SMS sequences to automatically send timely text messages to candidates and contacts. This helps automate communication, improve engagement, and streamline your recruitment process. Click here to read more about SMS Sequencing in Recruit CRM LinkedIn Message Sequencing Create a sequence of LinkedIn messages to be sent to candidates and contacts at scheduled intervals. This keeps you in touch with prospects automatically, improving response rates and smoothing your recruitment workflow. Click here to read more about LinkedIn Sequencing in Recruit CRM Task Sequencing Go beyond external communication by creating task sequences. These automatically create and assign tasks on candidate and contact profiles, helping you manage follow-ups and internal actions consistently. Click here to read more about Task Sequencing in Recruit CRM You can combine email, SMS, LinkedIn, and task steps into a single workflow-style sequence that contains all or selected steps you need. Enrolling candidates or contacts in a sequence You can enroll records into a sequence either in bulk or individually, depending on your use case. Enrolling multiple candidates or contacts in a sequence in bulk 1. Open the Candidates or Contacts list page. You can also enroll records from the Jobs page, which will include all primary contacts associated with that job. 2. Select the records you want to enroll by clicking the checkbox next to each name. Once selected, click on Enroll in Sequence from the top bar. If the option is not visible, click on More to locate it. ​ 3. After selection, review the pop-up listing the candidates or contacts that will be enrolled. Records will be excluded if they: • Have opted out of email • Are already enrolled in another sequence • Do not have a valid email address. ​ 4. Click Continue to proceed to sequence selection, then choose the sequence you want to enroll the selected records in. You can use filters to narrow down sequences based on the owner or the types of steps they contain. ​ 5. Once selected, review all the steps in the sequence. Use the pencil icon next to any step to make changes. You can adjust the number of days between steps and set the preferred execution time for each step. ​ 6. b: How do sequences work? The sequence is a powerful strategy that enables you to streamline your communication efforts and optimize task management. In this article, we will talk about the various sequence capabilities Recruit CRM offers. When a candidate or contact is enrolled, Recruit CRM begins executing the sequence from the first configured step. A sequence can include: • Emails • SMS messages • LinkedIn messages • Internal tasks Each step executes in sequence according to its configured timing and channel. The next step is triggered based on the delays and schedule defined within the sequence. This allows you to automate outreach, follow-ups, and internal actions without manually managing each interaction. If a step fails due to issues such as a disconnected email account, insufficient SMS credits, or invalid contact information, the enrollment may pause until the issue is resolved. A candidate or contact can only be actively enrolled in one sequence at a time. What this feature does and when to use it? Sequences in Recruit CRM help you automate communication and follow-ups across multiple channels such as email, SMS, LinkedIn, and internal tasks. Instead of manually reaching out at every step, you can set up a structured workflow that runs automatically over time. This ensures consistent outreach, better engagement, and fewer missed follow-ups while managing candidates or contacts at scale. You can use this feature when: • You want to automate candidate follow-ups after sourcing. • You want to Reactivate an existing talent pool. • Scale outreach with consistency. t: Setting Up and Customizing Your Email Signature
s: Your email signature is an essential part of the emails, and here's how you can create one within Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Set Up Multiple Email Signatures
Set Up Different Signatures for Multiple Email Accounts
Troubleshooting
Problem: My email signature is not appearing in emails
Problem: My HTML signature is not displaying correctly
Conclusion
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Email Signature feature allows you to create and manage a signature that is automatically added to your outgoing emails. Your signature is applied across Recruit CRM email communications, including any email sequences, helping you maintain a professional and consistent brand presence. Use this feature when you want to: Maintain a consistent email signature across emails. Use different signatures for different connected email accounts. Set Up Multiple Email Signatures Click your profile picture in the top-right corner and open Email Settings . Navigate to the Email Signature section. Use the editor to build your signature, adding any contact details, branding elements, or formatting you'd like to include. If you already have a professionally designed HTML signature, switch to Code View and paste the HTML directly into the editor. Review the signature and save your changes. Once configured, your email signature is automatically added to outgoing emails sent from Recruit CRM, including emails sent through sequences. Set Up Different Signatures for Multiple Email Accounts On the Business Plan and above , you can set up two email signatures if you have connected two email accounts with Recruit CRM. Open the Email Signature settings and select the email account from the Set Email Signature for dropdown. Create or update the signature for that account. Save your changes. Recruit CRM automatically applies the appropriate signature based on the email account selected when sending an email. How are multiple email signatures used across Recruit CRM? When you have multiple email accounts connected, Recruit CRM automatically applies the signature associated with the email address being used. However, the Default Email ID signature will be used in the following areas: While sending automated emails via talent pool and job application form settings. Email Triggers. Standard Email Templates. To change which signature is used for these automated communications, set a different email address as your default from Email Settings by enabling the Mark as Default option. Troubleshooting Problem: My email signature is not appearing in emails Likely Cause: The signature may not have been saved correctly. What to Check: Verify that a signature has been created and saved. Also, confirm that you are sending the email from the account associated with the signature. Resolution: Save the signature again if needed and ensure the correct sender email address is selected before sending the email. Problem: My HTML signature is not displaying correctly Likely Cause: The HTML code may contain unsupported formatting or syntax errors. What to Check: Review the HTML code added through Code View and send a test email to verify how the signature appears to recipients. Resolution: Correct any issues in the HTML code, save the changes, and send another test email to confirm the formatting displays as expected. Conclusion By setting up and managing your signatures correctly, you can ensure the right branding and contact information are automatically included in both manual and automated emails. s: Learn how to manage Target Reports right from Recruit CRM.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
Setting Up a Target
Search, filter, and customize target list view
Viewing and Generating a Target Report
Export target reports:
Automated Emails When a Target is Achieved
Sharing, Embbeding, and Auto-Refreshing Target Reports
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The Target Reporting feature in Recruit CRM empowers you with advanced tools to set, monitor, and report on Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) . This feature allows users to create comprehensive target reports for company members, roles, teams, and individuals, providing detailed insights into performance against set targets. With customizable KPIs, reporting permissions, API support, and automation capabilities , you can effectively track goals and enhance performance management across teams. Targets have default statuses such as upcoming, active, or completed, and they automatically stop tracking after the end date unless you extend them. Before you begin Only account owners, admins, and custom roles with access to Target reports can view and create targets. Ensure you know which target type you want to set (individual, teams, roles, or company-wide). Decide the KPIs you want to track. The KPIs available in target reports are the same as those in the team performance report. Confirm the target frequency and the start and end dates for tracking. Decide whether you want email notifications sent to assignees when targets are completed. 🎯 Setting Up a Target Go to Admin Settings and click on Target Reports . Click on Create New Target . ​ Fill in the target details, including: Title Target type (individual, teams, roles, or company-wide) Assignee Timeline (frequency) Start date, End date KPIs and Target value For Frequency , choose how often the KPI is tracked (for example, weekly or monthly). ​ For Start and End Date , define when to begin and stop tracking. Targets automatically stop tracking after the end date, but you can extend a target by editing the end date. ​ For KPI selection , choose one or more KPIs (such as calls per week or meetings per month) and assign values. The KPIs available are the same as those in the team performance report. ​ To add more than one KPI to a single target report, click Add Another KPI . ​ Review the status behavior: targets will move through statuses such as upcoming, active, or completed based on dates and progress. ​ Click Create to save the target. ​ Search, filter, and customize target list view In the Target Reports list, use the search bar to search for targets by name. ​ Use filters to filter targets by frequency . ​ Click Show or Hide Column to customize which columns are visible in the list view. ​ 📊 Viewing and Generating a Target Report Go to the Reports section and open Target Reports . ​ In the target report view, track performance by monitoring teams, individuals, or roles against assigned KPIs within the set dates and frequency. ​ Review the chart where the red line represents the target set. ​ Use the report controls and filters in the target report to adjust what you are viewing (for example, entity type or date range). ​ In the chart, click on any bar to view the detailed entity data behind that result. The bar is clickable and opens more detailed data. ​ Use the additional interactive controls in the report to explore more details or switch between entities and KPIs. ​ From the target reports area, you can also create a new target from scratch if needed. ​ Export target reports: In the target report view, use the export controls to export the graphic as a PNG , JPG , or .SVG file. ​ Click the Export to CSV button to export the report data as a CSV file. ​ 📩 Automated Emails When a Target is Achieved You can notify Assigned Teams/Roles/Individuals when a target is completed. Please notice that the Account Owner and Target Creator also receive notifications. To achieve this, turn on the 'Send Email Notifications to Assignees' toggle in Target Reports inside the Reports section . Turn on the Send Email Notifications to Assignees toggle to enable automated emails when a target is completed. ​ When enabled, assignees or assigned teams, roles, or individuals will be notified when a target is completed. ​The account owner and the target creator also receive notifications. ​ 🔗 Sharing, Embbeding, and Auto-Refreshing Target Reports You can also share your report externally through a unique link. In the target report view, click Share Report . ​ In the sharing settings, enable the target report direct link to generate a unique external link for the report. ​ Use the same controls to disable the direct link when you no longer want the report to be accessible externally. ​ Turn on Auto-refresh to refresh the report data at predefined intervals that you set. ​ Copy the target report URL to share it externally, and use the preview option to see how the shared report will appear. ​ Troubleshooting Problem: KPIs you expect are not available when creating a target Likely cause: You are expecting KPIs that are not part of the team performance report. What to check: Review the KPIs available in the team performance report, as target report KPIs match this list. Resolution: Use one of the KPIs that exists in the team performance report, or adjust your reporting expectations to those available KPIs. FAQs Q1: What happens when a target reaches its end date? Targets automatically stop tracking after the end date. You can extend tracking by editing the target and updating the end date. Conclusion: Target reports in Recruit CRM give you a structured way to set KPIs, track performance visually, and share results with your team and stakeholders.
