s: Learn how to set up calling in Recruit CRM!
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to set up calling integration in Recruit CRM?
1. Add & verify your calling number:
Method 1: From the Profile section:
Method 2: While making your first call:
2. Try free call credits on any plan:
3. Buy calling credits:
Here's how you can buy calling credits 💰
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM's Calling feature, powered by Twilio , lets you call candidates and contacts directly from within the platform, eliminating the need to switch to an external calling application. Use this feature when: • You want to call candidates or contacts directly from Recruit CRM. • You need to use the built-in native dialer available on the Pro Plan and above. The Calling feature helps streamline your communication workflow by allowing you to place calls, optionally record conversations, and store call logs and notes within the candidate or contact record, ensuring all communication history remains centralized and easily accessible.The calling/auto-dialer feature is available on the Pro plan and above. Please Note The calling/auto-dialer feature is available on the Pro plan and above. IMPORTANT: Due to local guidelines, Twilio will no longer allow domestic outbound calls between +91 (Indian) numbers. International calls placed from Indian numbers will still be supported. Based on Twilio guidelines, the phone number verification method has been updated. To continue using calling services, please verify your phone number using the new verification process added here . 📞 How to set up calling integration in Recruit CRM? 1. Add & verify your calling number: There are two ways to add the calling number to the system: Method 1: From the Profile section: Navigate to your Profile section in Recruit CRM. Under the Phone field, enter the phone number you want to use for making calls. Save your profile to ensure the phone number is stored successfully. Once the phone number is added in Recruit CRM, open the candidate/contact profile. Click on the phone number of the candidate/contact, and the system will ask you to verify your number. Click on the 'Verify your number to make calls' option, then click on 'Proceed'. The system will show a pop-up containing the 6-digit verification code as shown below. You will receive an incoming call from Twilio to the number you added to verify the number. After answering the call, open the dialer section on your phone and enter the 6-digit code shown on the pop-up in Recruit CRM. Once added, the number will be verified. Method 2: While making your first call: Click on the candidate's/contact's phone number and, in the pop-up window, add the phone number (if not added from the Profile Settings ). Once added, click on 'Proceed', the system will show a pop-up containing the 6-digit verification code. You will receive an incoming call from Twilio to the number you have added. After answering the call, open the dialer section on your phone and enter the 6-digit code shown on the pop-up in Recruit CRM. Once added, the number will be verified. 2. Try free call credits on any plan: If you haven't used our calling service before, you can try it with free calling credits available on the Free plan - no upfront cost required! Pro Plan and Business Plan : Pro and Business Plan users can try the Calling feature using the free Recruit CRM Credits . Enterprise Plan : Users will receive the Calling credits included with their Recruit CRM subscription. To check if you have free calling credits: Go to Admin Settings -> Phone Calling & SMS settings . Look for the "Limited Free Credits Available" message, which indicates available credits for local calls (not international). Note: Free credits apply only to calling and do not include texting functionality. If you haven't used the entire free credit in previous calls, you can continue making calls until it’s fully used, provided the remaining balance is enough for at least one more minute of calling. Each free credit call will automatically disconnect once it reaches a 5-minute duration limit. 3. Buy calling credits: Now, to start making calls through Recruit CRM, you'll have to buy calling credits. ⬅️ Here's how you can buy calling credits 💰 To buy the credits, Navigate to the Admin settings -> Phone Calling and SMS settings Click on the green 'Buy Calling Credits' button: Add the credit amount by clicking on the " +" button, you can check the amount on the right side: Confirm the default payment method or add another card to make the payment. You can check the prices on Twilio by clicking on the link below: https://www.twilio.com/voice/pricing/us The actual cost paid by you is (Local Call Pricing + Browser/App Call Pricing + Recording Pricing (if applicable)) x 1.25 and this includes us storing the call for you as long as you use Recruit CRM 4. Calling a candidate/contact: Once your phone number has been verified and you have sufficient calling credits: Open the relevant Candidate or Contact record. Click on the person's phone number to initiate a call. The system will open a calling pop-up displaying the To and From phone numbers. Review these details to ensure they are correct. If you want to record the call, switch the Record Call option to Yes . Tick the consent checkbox to confirm that you have obtained or are providing the required consent for call recording. Click the green Call button to start the call. You will hear a calling tone while the call connects, and the recipient's phone will begin to ring. During the call, you can add call notes directly in the on-screen notes section. These notes will automatically be saved to the Notes & Calls section of the candidate or contact record. ​ After the call ends, a follow-up screen will appear where you can add additional call details, including the Call Type . Save the call details to store the complete call log on the candidate or contact record. Learn how to customize call types 🎧 Call recording permissions in Recruit CRM Call recording is controlled by your account admin and can be enabled or disabled per user or team. When enabled, you'll see a Record Call toggle in the calling pop-up, and you must confirm consent before recording starts. ​ See call recording permission settings 📋 How to transcribe calls in Recruit CRM? Recruit CRM can automatically generate a text transcript of recorded calls, saved alongside the call log on the candidate or contact record. This makes it easy to search past conversations without replaying the audio. ​ Learn how call transcription works 📲 How to use the native dialer to call from the system? In addition to calling from your browser, you can place calls using your system's native dialer connected through Recruit CRM. This routes the call through the same verified number and logs it to the candidate or contact record automatically. ​ Click here to learn to use your native dialler for calling! Troubleshooting Problem: Unable to place domestic outbound calls between +91 Indian numbers Likely cause : Twilio no longer allows domestic outbound calls between +91 Indian numbers. What to check : Confirm that both the caller and recipient numbers are +91 Indian numbers and that the call is domestic. Resolution: Use international calling where supported, or use an alternative method for domestic calls between +91 Indian numbers, as this restriction is enforced by Twilio and cannot be overridden in Recruit CRM. Problem: Call cannot be placed despite having credits Likely cause: Phone number might not be verified, credits might not be sufficient for at least one more minute, or Twilio restrictions may apply. What to check: Confirm your phone number is verified via the six-digit code process. Check the remaining balance and ensure it is enough for at least one minute of calling. Review Twilio limitations relevant to your country, especially for +91 Indian numbers. Resolution: Complete phone verification if not done. Top up calling credits if the balance is low. Adjust your calling strategy to comply with Twilio’s guidelines FAQs Which plans support calling in Recruit CRM? The calling feature is available on the Pro plan and above. Do I need to verify my phone number to use calling? Yes. Based on Twilio’s updated guidelines, you must verify your phone number using the new verification process, which involves receiving a Twilio call and entering a six-digit code shown in Recruit CRM. Are domestic calls between +91 Indian numbers supported? No. Due to local Twilio guidelines, Twilio will no longer allow domestic outbound calls between +91 Indian numbers. International calls placed from Indian numbers are still supported. Do free credits cover international calls or texting? No. Free credits are for local calls only and do not apply to international calls. Free credits also apply only to calling and do not include texting functionality. Conclusion: You can now set up Twilio-powered calling in Recruit CRM, verify your number, manage free and paid credits, and place calls to candidates and contacts directly from the platform. Buy calling credits: Now, to start making calls through Recruit CRM, you'll have to buy calling credits. ⬅️ Here's how you can buy calling credits 💰 To buy the credits, Navigate to the Admin settings -> Phone Calling and SMS settings Click on the green 'Buy Calling Credits' button: Add the credit amount by clicking on the " +" button, you can check the amount on the right side: Confirm the default payment method or add another card to make the payment. You can check the prices on Twilio by clicking on the link below: https://www.twilio.com/voice/pricing/us The actual cost paid by you is (Local Call Pricing + Browser/App Call Pricing + Recording Pricing (if applicable)) x 1.25 and this includes us storing the call for you as long as you use Recruit CRM 4. Calling a candidate/contact: Once the number is verified and credits are added, click on the phone number of a candidate/contact and the system will open a pop-up to make a phone call: You'll see the "To" and "From" numbers along with an option to record the call. If you wish to record a call, switch to YES, tick the consent box to confirm, and click on the green 'Call' button to start the call. You'll hear a calling tone and the phone will start ringing. You can take call notes on the screen, those will be added to the 'Notes & Calls' section on the record. Once the call is over, you'll get another screen to add more details about the call, including the Call Type. Click here to know how to customize the call type! 🎧 Call recording permissions in Recruit CRM Click here to learn about Call recording permissions 📋 How to transcribe calls in Recruit CRM? Click here to learn how to transcribe the calls 📲 How to use the native dialer to call from the system? Click here to learn to use your native dialler for calling! Troubleshooting Problem: Unable to place domestic outbound calls between +91 Indian numbers Likely cause : Twilio no longer allows domestic outbound calls between +91 Indian numbers. What to check : Confirm that both the caller and recipient numbers are +91 Indian numbers and that the call is domestic. Resolution: Use international calling where supported, or use an alternative method for domestic calls between +91 Indian numbers, as this restriction is enforced by Twilio and cannot be overridden in Recruit CRM. Problem: Call cannot be placed despite having credits Likely cause: Phone number might not be verified, credits might not be sufficient for at least one more minute, or Twilio restrictions may apply. What to check: Confirm your phone number is verified via the six-digit code process. Check the remaining balance and ensure it is enough for at least one minute of calling. Review Twilio limitations relevant to your country, especially for +91 Indian numbers. Resolution: Complete phone verification if not done. Top up calling credits if the balance is low. Adjust your calling strategy to comply with Twilio’s guidelines FAQs Q1: Which plans support calling in Recruit CRM? The calling feature is available on the Pro plan and above. Q2: Do I need to verify my phone number to use calling? Yes. Based on Twilio’s updated guidelines, you must verify your phone number using the new verification process, which involves receiving a Twilio call and entering a six-digit code shown in Recruit CRM. Q3: Are domestic calls between +91 Indian numbers supported? No. Due to local Twilio guidelines, Twilio will no longer allow domestic outbound calls between +91 Indian numbers. International calls placed from Indian numbers are still supported. Q4: Do free credits cover international calls or texting? No. Free credits are for local calls only and do not apply to international calls. Free credits also apply only to calling and do not include texting functionality. Conclusion: You can now set up Twilio-powered calling in Recruit CRM, verify your number, manage free and paid credits, and place calls to candidates and contacts directly from the platform. h: What this feature does and when to use it?

Troubleshooting

Conclusion:
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Profile section allows you to manage your personal Recruit CRM account settings, including your profile picture, registered email, time zone, time format, default currency, password, email reminders, daily email reports, email tracking, and browser notifications. This feature is useful when you want to: Set up your Recruit CRM profile for the first time. Update your registered email, password, or time zone. Manage email reminders, daily reports, email tracking, or browser notifications. How to Set Up Your Profile Open your Profile section: From any screen in Recruit CRM, click your avatar in the top-right corner and select Profile . Change your profile picture: In the Profile section, click the existing profile image on the left side and upload the picture you want to use for your Recruit CRM account. Change your registered email ID: Click the email section, remove your existing email address, and enter the new email address you want to use for your Recruit CRM account. Set your default time zone: Select your preferred time zone from the Time Zone dropdown and click Save Profile to apply the change. Choose your time format: Select either the 12-hour AM/PM or 24-hour format. Your selected format will be reflected wherever time is displayed or selected across Recruit CRM, including interviews and custom date/time fields. The same format will also be reflected in the mobile app. For example: In 12-hour format, times will appear as: 5:00 AM, 5:00 PM. In 24-hour format, times will appear as: 05:00, 17:00 (without AM/PM) Set your default currency: Select your preferred currency from the Default Currency dropdown. Note: You can also have a separate currency for each candidate and each job. You can change that by going inside the candidate's profile or inside that job. All Amount fields follow a standardized currency format: <Symbol><Amount> <Code> (e.g., $100 USD , ₹5,000 INR ). Amount values are also right-aligned across list views and tables for easier scanning. Note: This formatting does not apply to Contract Staffing/Timesheets . Change your account password: Click Change Password, enter your current password, and then enter your new password to update your account credentials. Click here to learn more. Manage email reminders and daily email reports: Turn off email reminders and the daily email report: If you don't want to receive email reminders for your tasks and appointments in Recruit CRM, here's how you can turn them off by disabling this toggle. You can also disable the daily email report, which is a report you'll receive every morning between 8-10 AM, essentially a list of all your website, job boards, and talent pool applications or Recruit CRM profile submissions from the last twenty-four hours. Click here to learn more about Email Reminders! Manage the email tracking pixel: This feature will help you manage your email tracking within Recruit CRM. If it is on, Recruit CRM will add a tracking pixel in your email body, and if it is off, then the system won't add a tracking pixel. If the emails that are sent from Recruit CRM are going to the spam or junk folder of your recipient, turn this tracking pixel off to avoid emails going to spam or junk. Enable browser notifications: You can also enable browser notifications for real-time updates without the need to be active on the web app. Note: Profile settings apply to your individual user account and do not change other users’ settings. Troubleshooting Problem: Emails sent from Recruit CRM are landing in recipients’ spam or junk folders. Likely cause: Email tracking pixel is turned on and being flagged by some email providers. What to check: Check the Email Tracking Pixel setting in your profile. Resolution path: Turn the tracking pixel off to avoid emails going to spam or junk. Conclusion: The Profile section lets you manage your personal Recruit CRM settings, preferences, and notifications in one place. Related Articles How Email Open Tracking Works in Recruit CRM? You can customize the page appearance, configure form fields, collect language and proficiency details, send automated emails, and embed the Talent Pool Page on your website. This feature is useful when you want to: Collect profiles from candidates who aren't applying for a specific job. Build and maintain a database of potential candidates. t: Share jobs with your hiring manager
s: Learn how to seamlessly share jobs/submit candidates from Recruit CRM with your hiring managers using the portal.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Share a job with your Hiring Manager
Troubleshooting
Problem: My Hiring Manager can't see the job or the candidates.
FAQs
1. Do I need to send the Online Candidate List every time I assign a new candidate?
2. How does the Hiring Manager access shared jobs?
Conclusion
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows you to share jobs and candidate pipelines with your Hiring Managers through the Hiring Manager Portal. You can control which candidates and fields are visible, and any future updates made in Recruit CRM are automatically reflected in the portal. This feature is useful when you want to: Share jobs with Hiring Managers. Control which candidates and candidate details are visible. Keep candidate updates synchronized in real time. Share a job with your Hiring Manager Navigate to Jobs and open the job you want to share. Under the Candidate Pipeline tab, set the visibility of the candidates you want to share and choose the candidate fields you want Hiring Managers to view, and click Submit to Client . Select the Online Candidate List and make sure the Enable Portal Link option is enabled. An email containing the Online Candidate List link will be generated. Send this email to your Hiring Manager. Use the Online Candidate List link received in the email to access the shared candidate list. From there, click View in Portal to open the Hiring Manager Portal. You'll land on the Timesheets tab by default. From there, navigate to the Jobs tab to view the shared jobs and their assigned candidates. Please note: The Hiring Manager only needs to receive this invitation once to sign up for the Hiring Manager Portal. However, for each new job you want to share, you'll need to enable the Portal Link and send the Online Candidate List email for that specific job. After the Hiring Manager has signed up, you don't need to send another invitation for future candidates. Simply assign new candidates to the job and turn their visibility on. They will automatically appear in the Hiring Manager Portal. Any hiring stage updates or remarks you add in Recruit CRM are synchronized automatically and become visible to the Hiring Manager in real time. Troubleshooting Problem: My Hiring Manager can't see the job or the candidates. Likely Cause: Candidate visibility hasn't been enabled, the Portal Link hasn't been activated, or the Hiring Manager hasn't accessed the portal through the shared Online Candidate List. What to Check: Verify that the required candidates have their visibility turned On, the Portal Link is enabled, and the Hiring Manager has clicked View in Portal from the Online Candidate List. Resolution: Enable candidate visibility, ensure the Online Candidate List has been shared, and ask the Hiring Manager to access the portal through the shared link. FAQs 1. Do I need to send the Online Candidate List every time I assign a new candidate? No. After the Hiring Manager has signed up using the initial invitation, newly visible candidates are automatically shared through the portal. 2. How does the Hiring Manager access shared jobs? The Hiring Manager should open the Online Candidate List email and click View in Portal . They'll land on the Timesheets tab by default. From there, navigate to the Jobs tab to view the shared jobs. Conclusion Sharing jobs through the Hiring Manager Portal gives Hiring Managers secure, real-time access to candidate pipelines while allowing you to control exactly what they can see. Once the initial invitation has been accepted, future candidates and updates are shared automatically, making collaboration faster and more efficient. t: Sharing a formatted CV With Clients
s: This article act as a guide to help you submit formatted CV's of candidates with Clients.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?

How to Create a Custom “Formatted CV” field? 📃
Show the formatted CV field on candidate profile pages

Troubleshooting

b: What does this feature do & when to use it? The formatted CV workflow lets you store and share a version of the candidate’s CV that uses your company’s formatting and this formatted CV can be shared with clients when you submit candidates. You can either use Recruit CRM’s native resume/CV formatting tool or upload externally formatted files into this custom field. You can use this feature when: When you want to send a candidate’s CV in your own company-branded format. When you want to keep a separate “formatted CV” file in Recruit CRM alongside the original resume. When you want clients to see only the formatted CV and not the original resume. When you regularly submit candidates to clients from jobs and need a consistent CV format. Before you begin: This feature (native resume/CV formatting tool) is available for Business plan users and above. You need access to Admin Settings to create custom candidate fields and configure which fields are shared with clients. Make sure you have your formatted CV files ready to upload if you are formatting resumes outside Recruit CRM. Decide whether you want clients to see only the formatted CV or both the formatted CV and the original resume. How to Create a Custom “Formatted CV” field? 📃 Go to Admin Settings . ​ Under Data Customization , click Candidate Fields . ​ On the right side, click the green New Custom Field button. ​ Name the new custom field (for example, “Formatted CV” or “Formatted Resume”). ​ Set the field type to File . ​ Click the Save Field button. ​ On the left side, ensure the visibility for the new “Formatted CV” field is set to On so that it is visible. ​ Show the formatted CV field on candidate profile pages In the profile section, identify any existing field you do not want to keep (for example, a field like “Locality”). ​ Click the pencil icon to the right of the field you want to replace. ​ Click the Replace Field button. ​ Choose the Select Field option. ​ From the list, select the “Formatted CV” (or similarly named) custom field you created earlier. ​ Click Replace to confirm. ​ The new formatted CV field will now replace the old field in the candidate profile layout. ​ Upload a formatted CV for a candidate On the candidate profile, locate the new formatted CV field. ​ Click the pencil icon to the right of the empty field. ​ Click Upload and upload the candidate’s CV or formatted resume file. ​ The layout change you made (replacing the old field with the formatted CV field) will reflect on all candidate profile pages, but the uploaded file itself is specific to each candidate. ​ Make the formatted CV field visible to clients Go to Admin Settings again. ​ Click Fields Shared with Clients . ​ Search for the custom “Formatted CV” field you created. ​ Tick the checkbox for Formatted CV so that this file is shared with clients. ​ (Optional) Untick the Resume checkbox if you do not want to share the candidate’s original resume with clients. ​ Click Save Settings to apply your changes. ​ Troubleshooting Problem: The formatted CV field does not appear on candidate profiles Likely cause: The field is not set to visible. What to check: In Admin Settings > Candidate Fields, confirm the “Formatted CV” field’s visibility is set to On . On a candidate profile, confirm you replaced an existing field with the formatted CV field. Resolution: Turn on visibility for the field and repeat the “Replace Field” steps to add it to the profile layout. Problem: The Upload option is not available on the formatted CV field Likely cause: The field type is not set to File . What to check: In Admin Settings > Candidate Fields, confirm the field type for the formatted CV field. Resolution: If the field is not a file field, create a new custom field with the File type and repeat the configuration steps. FAQs Do I need to be on a specific plan to use the native resume/CV formatting tool? Yes. The native resume or CV formatting tool is available for Business plan users and above. Does changing the candidate profile layout affect all candidates? Yes. When you replace a field with the formatted CV field in the profile layout, that layout change reflects on all candidate profile pages. Conclusion: You can now create, upload, and share formatted CVs with clients directly from Recruit CRM, giving you better control over how candidate information is presented. Conclusion:
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Recruit CRM lets you share jobs on social media and other external platforms to source candidates from different channels. You can either: Use one-click posting buttons for LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitter/X, or Xing. Copying the job application form link and paste it on any external platform of your choice or just emailing it to candidates. You can use this feature when: You want to quickly promote open jobs on LinkedIn, Facebook, Xing or Twitter/X using one-click posting. You need a shareable job application link for posting on other platforms or job boards. You want all applicants from social media and external channels to flow directly into Recruit CRM. Before you begin Make sure you have access to the Jobs list page in Recruit CRM. Ensure you are logged into the social media platform (LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitter/X or Xing) in your browser where you want to post the job. Confirm that your Job Application Form is already customized in Admin settings so that candidates see the correct fields when they apply. To change the default social media share image and text, you need access to Admin settings and the Public Job Page settings. One-click posting on Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, or Xing Go to your Jobs list page in Recruit CRM. ​ Click on the job that you want to share from the Jobs List Page. ​ Now, on the specific Job Details page, locate the three social media icons (LinkedIn, Facebook,Twitter/X and Xing) displayed on that job. Click the icon for the social media platform where you want to post the job. A ready-made post will open on that platform. ​ Review the pre-filled content and type any additional text you would like to add to your job listing, and click the Post (or equivalent) button on the social media platform to publish the job. Share a job using the job application URL Open the job in Recruit CRM for which you want to generate a shareable application link. ​ Click the Copy Job Application URL button to copy the application form link associated with that job. ​ Paste this link on any job board, social media platform, or website where you want to accept applications. ​ Optionally, paste the same link into an email if you want to invite specific candidates to apply. When candidates click this link, they will see the job application form you have customized in Admin settings and can submit their details directly. The candidate fills in the job application form you have configured in Admin settings. Once submitted, the candidate’s data is stored directly in the Recruit CRM database. Change the default social media share image and text Go to " Public Job Page Settings " in Admin Settings . ​ Click on the Social Media Sharing tab. ​ You can change the text inside the 2 boxes, that will appear on your post on Social Media. The format will be like - Apply To {Job Name} With {Company Name}, where {Job Name} & {Company Name} is dynamic and can’t be changed. The {Company Name} is the name of your company/agency, not the clients ​ Upload or select the image you want to use as the default social media share image (this image will be applied to all social media postings). ​ Save your changes. The image you upload in Recruit CRM will be used for all social media posts created from your jobs page, including when candidates themselves share a job from that page. ​ FAQs Q1: Whose company name appears in the social media post — ours or the client’s? The company name used in the social media post is your company or agency name, not the client’s name. Conclusion: Sharing jobs on social media with Recruit CRM is designed to be fast and flexible, whether you use one-click posting or the job application URL, while keeping all candidate data centralized in your account. t: Showing & Hiding data fields Across forms (Candidate/Company/Contact/Job) (New UI)
s: This article explains how to manage field visibility and layout in Recruit CRM for different record types.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Step-by-step instructions to manage field visibility
Where these changes appear
1. List Pages
2. Add/Edit Forms
3. Profile/Details Pages
Troubleshooting
FAQs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Recruit CRM allows you to control which fields are visible across different record types such as Candidates, Companies, Contacts, and Jobs. By managing field visibility and layout, you can: • Control which fields appear on list pages. • Decide which fields are shown in Add/Edit forms. • Manage which fields are visible on record detail pages. This helps you reduce clutter, simplify your interface, and ensure your team focuses only on the most relevant information. Use this feature when you want to: • Hide unused or irrelevant fields. • Ensure important fields are always visible. ​ 📋 Step-by-step instructions to manage field visibility Please note that only users with the appropriate permissions will be able to edit the column/field arrangement. Click here to learn more. Step 1: Navigate to the "Admin Settings" icon and click on the Record fields that you want to edit. Step 2: Locate the field you want to manage and use the toggle to control its visibility. Click Save once done to apply the changes. • Toggle ON → Field will be visible • Toggle OFF → Field will be hidden This setting applies across: • List pages • Add/Edit forms • Record detail pages Note: Column customization is user-specific, while field visibility is global. The selected field will now be shown or hidden across all relevant views. Where these changes appear 1. List Pages Field visibility controls whether a field exists in the system view. To control how it appears on the list page: Go to the relevant list page → click Show/Hide Columns • Select the fields you want to display • Rearrange columns based on your preference • Click Apply to save changes In the Hide/Show Columns page, searching for a field scrolls to and highlights the matching field(s), with a counter (e.g., 1/2) to jump between matches. You can still drag and drop to reorder columns while a search is active. 2. Add/Edit Forms Only fields marked as visible will appear in the Add/Edit form, and they will follow the same order as configured in Admin Settings . Please note that any required fields must be filled before saving the record. 3. Profile/Details Pages Fields with visibility turned on will appear on the record's details (profile) page, while hidden fields will not be shown. From the profile page, you can further arrange and choose which of these visible fields to display using the Customize Information Overview option. ​ You can rearrange all fields visible on each page (Candidates/Companies/Contacts/Jobs) in an order of your choice. Troubleshooting Problem: A field no longer appears on the list page. Likely cause: The field's visibility is turned off in Admin Settings or not selected in the Show/Hide Columns option. ​ What to check: Check the field’s visibility toggle in Admin Settings > Data Customization for the record type. Check the Show/Hide Columns settings on the list page. Resolution path: Turn the field’s visibility toggle on in Admin Settings. Reopen Show/Hide Columns , select the field, and click Apply . FAQs Does changing field visibility affect all users? Yes. Field visibility is global and applies across the account. ​ Do these changes delete any data? No. Hiding a field only removes it from view. The data remains stored. Who can manage field visibility? Only users with access to the Admin Settings and permission to access the Data Customization section can manage the field visibility. Is column customization the same as field visibility? No. • Field visibility → controlled in Admin Settings (global) • Column layout → controlled on list page or details page (user-specific) Conclusion: Managing field visibility helps you create a cleaner, more focused workspace in Recruit CRM. By showing only what matters, you can improve data quality, streamline workflows, and make it easier for your team to navigate and use the system effectively. Happy Recruiting! t: Showing & Hiding data fields Across forms (Candidate/Company/Contact/Job) from admin settings
s: This article will help you change the visibility of fields for your entire team in Recruit CRM.
b: Recruit CRM is designed to be extremely customizable and give you the ability to choose the fields you want to make visible inside the account. ​ Changes made in the visibility of data fields through "Admin Settings" will be reflected in Add/Edit Forms, Lists & Profile Page of Candidates/Companies/Contacts/Jobs. You can make changes in your data fields by following the steps below: Step 1: Click on the "Admin Settings" icon Step 2: Click on any button under the "Data Customisation" section Step 3: Toggle between the data fields of your choice set the visibility of fields as "ON" or "OFF" and mark the fields as " Required" or "Not Required." Step 4: You will be able to see all fields set to " visible" on your List Pages (Candidates/Companies/Contacts/Jobs). An example of the Candidate List Page is below: You'll see all the fields here which you made visible in Admin Settings . Then, you can select fields that you want to be seen on your List Pages. You can also rearrange the order of selected fields by dragging the fields Up or Down. These changes will also appear in "Application forms" and "Profile Pages" . ​ You can access all application forms just by clicking the " + " button at the top right. t: Signing up on the Hiring Manager Portal
s: This article explains how Hiring Managers can be invited to the Hiring Manager Portal (HMP), complete the signup process, manage their profile, and access jobs and timesheets.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Invite a Hiring Manager and sign up
Update your profile on HMP
Access timesheets and jobs
Troubleshooting
Problem: I can't see any timesheets after signing up.
FAQs
1. Do I need a company email address to sign up?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Hiring Manager Portal (HMP) provides Hiring Managers with secure access to the jobs, candidate pipelines, and timesheets shared with them by their recruiting agency. Hiring Managers can be invited either by the agency through Recruit CRM or by another Hiring Manager from within the portal. This feature is useful when you want to: Invite Hiring Managers to the Hiring Manager Portal. Complete the Hiring Manager signup process. Update your profile information. Access shared jobs and candidate pipelines. View and approve timesheets shared by your recruiter. Please note: Hiring Managers can be invited using any valid email address . There are no email domain restrictions. Invite a Hiring Manager and sign up Sign in to the Hiring Manager Portal and click the Hiring Managers icon from the left navigation menu. Click Invite Hiring Manager and enter the client's email address, and click Send Invite. Pro Tip: Use Add Another Email to invite multiple users at the same time. The client will receive an invitation email containing a signup link. After clicking the link, the client can complete the signup process using the same email address that received the invitation. Your email address and company will already be populated and cannot be changed during signup. Your account is created immediately, and no additional email verification is required. Update your profile on HMP After signing in, you can update your own profile information at any time. Log in to the Hiring Manager Portal. Click your Profile from the upper-right corner. Update your details and save the changes. You can also choose how time is displayed in the Client Portal. Under Time Format , select either the 12-hour or 24-hour format and click Save Profile. All timesheets will be displayed using the selected time format. Please note: If you change your email address to one that matches an existing Contact in Recruit CRM, the Client Portal Enabled tag will automatically appear on that contact record. Any jobs, candidates, or timesheets previously shared with your old email address will no longer be available. You can only edit your own profile. Each Hiring Manager is responsible for managing their own account. Access timesheets and jobs After signing in, you'll land on the Timesheets tab by default. Timesheets will appear only when all of the following conditions are met: Your portal email matches a Contact record in Recruit CRM. That Contact is associated with the relevant Contract or Contract-to-Permanent job. The Online Candidate list Link for that job has been enabled. When all three conditions are met, timesheets become available automatically. If the Online Link is later disabled, the timesheets are removed immediately. To access shared jobs: Open the Online Candidate List link shared with you and click ' View in Portal '. You'll land on the Timesheets tab first. From there, open the Jobs tab on the portal. Your shared jobs will now be visible. Troubleshooting Problem: I can't see any timesheets after signing up. Likely Cause: Your portal account hasn't been linked to the appropriate contact record, or the Online Link for the job hasn't been enabled. What to Check: Verify that your portal email matches the contact record associated with the relevant job and that the Online Link has been enabled. Resolution: Please contact your recruiting partner to ensure your email is linked to the correct contact record and that the Online Link is enabled. Once both requirements are met, your timesheets will automatically appear in the portal. FAQs 1. Do I need a company email address to sign up? No. The email domain restriction has been removed. You can sign up with any valid email address, even with Google.com , rediffmail.com , etc. 2. Can I change my email or company name while signing up? No. These two fields are pre-filled based on the invite and are locked during sign-up. You can update your other details freely. 3. I clicked 'View in Portal,' but I do not see jobs. Where are my jobs? When you click 'View in Portal' from the Online Candidate List link, you might on the Timesheets tab first. To see the jobs shared with you, go to the Jobs tab on the portal. The shared jobs will then be visible. 4. I was invited but haven't signed up yet, and I clicked 'View in Portal'. What happens? You will be taken to the Sign In page rather than the Sign Up page. New accounts can only be created through an invite, so ask your Agency Recruiter or existing Hiring Manager on the Portal- to Invite you as well. 5. Will I have to verify my email after signing up? No. Email verification has been removed. Your account is active as soon as you complete the sign-up form. Conclusion The Hiring Manager Portal makes it easy for Hiring Managers to collaborate with recruiters by providing secure access to shared jobs, candidate pipelines, and timesheets. Once invited and signed up, Hiring Managers can manage their own profile, review shared information, and stay updated throughout the recruitment process. t: Single Sign-On (SSO) Setup in Recruit CRM with Google, Azure, and Okta
s: Streamline your recruitment process with Recruit CRM's Single Sign-On integration.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin:
Step-by-step instructions
Enable Single Sign-On in Recruit CRM
Select your identity provider (IDP)
Set up SSO for your desired IDP:
Google
Okta
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Recruit CRM’s Single Sign-On (SSO) integration lets users access their Recruit CRM account using their existing login credentials from an external identity provider that supports the OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocol. Instead of managing separate Recruit CRM passwords, users authenticate once with an IDP such as Google, Microsoft Azure, or Okta. Recruit CRM then trusts that authentication and grants access to the corresponding user account. Use Single Sign-On in Recruit CRM when you want to: Centralize user authentication through an identity provider like Google, Microsoft Azure, or Okta. Enforce consistent security policies from your IDP across Recruit CRM access. Control which users can log in to Recruit CRM via IDP group membership. Before you begin: Please note: SSO is available only on the Business and Enterprise plans. Only users with access to Admin Settings and Account Management can configure SSO. You must have an existing identity provider (IDP) that supports OpenID Connect (OIDC), such as Google, Microsoft Azure, or Okta. You will need to create or configure an OIDC application in your IDP and obtain the credentials required by Recruit CRM. Enabling SSO will disable multi-factor authentication (MFA/2FA) if it is currently enabled on the account. Step-by-step instructions Enable Single Sign-On in Recruit CRM Log in to the Recruit CRM web app as an admin or account owner. Go to Admin Settings . Open Account Management settings. Locate the Single Sign-On option. Turn on the Single Sign-On toggle to enable SSO for your account. Select your identity provider (IDP) In the Single Sign-On configuration area, select your preferred identity provider (IDP) from the available options, such as Google or Microsoft Azure. Set up SSO for your desired IDP: Google 1. Navigate to Google Cloud Platform 2. From the navigation bar, click on 'APIs and Services' -> ' OAuth consent screen' ​ 3. On the OAuth consent screen , click on the 'Select a Project' dropdown and from there you can create and select your project as shown below: 4. Once you select the project, select the 'User Type' as Internal/External as per your preference and click on 'Create' : 5. Fill in the required information including the name of your app, support emails, authorized domain, etc. 6. Click on 'ADD & REMOVE SCOPES', select all the scopes, and click on the blue 'Update' button -> hit 'Save and Continue': 7. The next step is to click on the 'ADD USERS' button and add the users -> hit 'Save & Continue'. It will then show you the entire summary, click on 'Back to Dashboard': 8. Post this, the next step is to create the credentials. Follow the steps below to create them: In the Authorised Redirect URI section, paste the 'Redirect URI' that you've copied from the Recruit CRM's Account Management settings while setting up the SSO: 9. Once you create the credentials, you can access them by clicking on the name: Okta Getting the 'Client ID' and the 'Client Secret' 1. Create an account on Identity | Okta and click on 'Admin' on the top-right of the navbar: 2. It will redirect you to the Okta console. On the left panel of the console, click on Applications → Applications: 3. Click on "Create App Integration". A pop-up will appear, select the options as shown below and click on 'Next': 4. Under the 'Grant Type', enable the 'Client Credentials' and 'Refresh Token' options and enter the Redirect URL that you copied from our Recruit CRM web app. 5. Select 'Controlled access' as per your preference and click on 'Save'. 6. Once you save your changes, you will able to get the 'Client ID' and the 'Client Secret' as shown in the image below: Getting the Authorization URL and Access token URL 1. Navigate to Security → API on the left panel and then click on 'default': 2. You'll be redirected to the 'default' page, click on the 'Metadata URL': 3. Once you click on the 'Metadata URL', you can access the 'Authorization URL' and 'Access token URL': Adding users 1. Navigate to Directory → People and click on 'Add person': 2. Fill out the required form and click on 'Save': ​ Azure Getting the 'Client ID' 1. Create an account on Microsoft Azure Portal . 2. Select 'App Registrations' from the Menu/Search Bar: 3. Click on the 'New Registration' button. Following this, provide the necessary details including the name of the app, select the supported account types that meet your requirements, and add the Redirect URL copied from the Recruit CRM web application. 4. Click on 'Register' and you will get the 'Client ID' and 'Tenant ID': For Authorization UL and Access Token URL, you need to use this Tenant ID as: Authorization URL: https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant id}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize ​ Access Token URL: https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant id}/oauth2/v2.0/token Accessing the 'Client Secret' 1. Click on 'Add a certificate or secret' on the same page where you got your 'Client ID' and 'Tenant ID' : 2. Click on ' New client secret', fill in the 'Description' and select the option available in the 'Expires' dropdown as per your preference and click on 'Add': 3. Once you click on 'Add', you will get the 'Client Secret Value'. Granting Admin consent for default Directory 1. Navigate to 'Authentication' on the left side panel >> enable both the 'Access token' and 'ID token' and click on 'Save': 2. Next, navigate to 'API Permissions' located in the same left panel and click on 'Microsoft Graph (1)'. A new screen will appear where you'll find a list of checkboxes corresponding to various permissions. Please ensure all checkboxes are selected, indicating that you've granted the necessary permissions. Once done, proceed to click on 'Update Permissions' to confirm your selections. 3. After completing the permissions setup, proceed by clicking on 'Grant admin consent for Default Directory'. Upon clicking, a popup window will appear seeking confirmation. Click 'Yes' to grant the necessary admin consent. Adding users 1. To add users to this IDP, begin by clicking on 'Overview' on the left panel. Then, proceed to select 'Manage Application in local directory': 2. Click on 'Assign users and groups'. 3. Now, proceed by clicking on '+ Add user/group'. 4. A window will appear allowing you to select the users or groups you wish to add. Choose your peers from the list and click on 'Select'. Connect the IDP to Recruit CRM Return to the Recruit CRM Single Sign-On configuration screen. Paste the credentials you obtained from your IDP into the matching fields in Recruit CRM. Double-check that each value is copied correctly from your IDP to avoid connection errors. Click the Save button to apply the SSO configuration. Configure email and password login behavior After SSO is successfully set up, review the option that controls whether users are permitted to log in using email and password in addition to SSO. If you want to enforce SSO-only access for all users (except the account owner), uncheck the option to permit login using email and password. If you want to allow users to continue using email and password as a backup login method, check the option to permit login using email and password. Save your changes. Troubleshooting Problem: User cannot log in via SSO Likely cause: The user is not included in the relevant IDP group or the IDP configuration does not assign them to the Recruit CRM application. What to check: Verify in your IDP admin console that the user is a member of the group that has access to the Recruit CRM SSO application. Confirm that the user’s email address in the IDP matches their email in Recruit CRM. Resolution: Add the user to the correct IDP group or application assignment. Ask the user to try logging in again via SSO. FAQs Which identity providers can I use for SSO? Recruit CRM supports identity providers that use the OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocol, including Google , Microsoft Azure , and Okta . What happens to MFA/2FA when I enable SSO? When you enable SSO in Recruit CRM, any existing MFA/2FA configuration in Recruit CRM is disabled. If you require multi-factor authentication, you should enforce it at the identity provider level. ​ Can users still log in with email and password after SSO is enabled? Yes, but only if you enable the option to permit login using email and password . If this option is unchecked, users must log in via SSO. The account owner can always log in with email and password regardless of this setting. Conclusion: Single Sign-On in Recruit CRM lets you centralize authentication, simplify user logins, and control access through your existing identity provider. Once configured, you can manage who can sign in via IDP groups while keeping the account owner’s email and password access as a secure fallback. t: SMS Sequencing in Recruit CRM
s: This article will guide you on how to create SMS sequences to interact and enhance your engagement with candidates and contacts.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to create an SMS sequence
Enroll Contacts while pitching Candidates
1. Low SMS Balance Warning
2. Notifications for Sequence Pausing
3. Enrollment Criteria for SMS Sequences
4. SMS Sequence Analytics Limitations
FAQs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? SMS Sequences allow you to send a series of scheduled text messages to Candidates or Contacts over a defined period. You can combine SMS, Email, Task, and LinkedIn steps into a single sequence to automate follow-ups and improve engagement. This feature is useful when you want to: Automate SMS follow-ups with Candidates or Contacts. Combine SMS, Email, Task, and LinkedIn steps in a single sequence. Schedule messages for specific dates and times. Personalize messages using SMS templates. Build structured communication workflows. Please note: SMS Sequencing is available on the Business Plan and above . Users on the Free and Pro plans can create one sequence . Only Account Owners, Admins, or users with the required Sequences permissions can create sequences. SMS sequencing is available only in supported regions: USA, UK, Israel, Hong Kong, Canada, and Sweden . Recruit CRM uses Twilio to power SMS messaging. US customers must complete Twilio registration before sending SMS. UK customers must complete and receive approval for the required KYC before texting is enabled. Learn more about KYC here . SMS credits are required to send messages. Learn How To Buy Texting Credits How to create an SMS sequence Navigate to Admin Settings → CRM Process Customization → Sequences . Click Create Sequence . Select whether the sequence is for Candidates or Contacts . Enter a name for the sequence, add an SMS step, and choose an existing SMS template or create a new one. Please note: Messages longer than 160 characters are split into multiple segments and charged accordingly, as per Twilio guidelines . Specify when the SMS should be sent by selecting the number of days and the execution time. Setting the value to 0 sends the SMS on the same day the record is enrolled in the sequence. It is important to know exactly when the SMS will be sent in relation to the starting date of the sequence. To calculate this, you can use the following formula: Send Date = Start Date + Specified No. Of Days (Send SMS In) Here, "Start Date" represents the date when the sequence was initiated. "Specified Date" or "Send SMS In" is the number of days you have indicated for the SMS to be sent after the start of the sequence. The resulting "Send date" is the calculated date on which the SMS will be sent. For example : If you start the sequence on January 1st and specify that the SMS should be sent in 2 days, the Send Date would be calculated as follows: Send date= January 1st + 2 days =January 3rd. Enable the Opt-out/Unsubscribe text if required. This is recommended to comply with Twilio's messaging guidelines . Continue adding additional SMS, Email, Task, or LinkedIn steps as required. You can rearrange the sequence using drag-and-drop. Please note: A sequence can contain up to 40 steps , including a maximum of 10 SMS , 10 Email , 10 Task , and 10 LinkedIn steps. Set the execution day for each step (between 0 and 250 calendar or business days) and save the sequence. Please note: Tasks can be created on the same day as the sequence initiation by setting the day as "0". ​ When implementing a task on the 0th day, it's crucial to align the step timing with the previous steps or set it for a later time than the preceding step to ensure a seamless workflow. Once the sequence is created, enroll Candidates or Contacts into it. Refer to the Managing Sequences article to learn how to enroll and unenroll records from a sequence. Enroll Contacts while pitching Candidates When pitching Candidates to Contacts, you can immediately enroll the selected Contacts into a sequence. While pitching Candidates, click Enroll Selected Contacts to Sequence . After the email is sent or the Candidates are marked as pitched, you'll be redirected to enroll the selected Contacts into a sequence. Key points to note 1. Low SMS Balance Warning When the SMS credit balance approaches around 20 credits, a warning message will be displayed, prompting you to recharge. Failure to recharge will result in the sequence being paused. 2. Notifications for Sequence Pausing You will receive email and in-app notifications when the sequence is about to pause due to a low SMS balance. 3. Enrollment Criteria for SMS Sequences During enrollment, you can only enroll candidates or contacts who meet the following criteria: Not enrolled in another sequence. Have phone numbers on their profiles. Have not opted out of receiving SMS. Have a local number. For the US region, have given consent to receive SMS. 4. SMS Sequence Analytics Limitations In SMS sequencing, metrics like 'Open rate,' 'Reply rate,' and 'Unsubscribe rate' cannot be tracked. FAQs 1. What are the time slots/execution times of the sequences? SMS/Emails in a sequence are fired in 30-minute slots (e.g. 9:00 AM, 9:30 AM, etc.). Also, the timestamp is based on the timezone set in the user profile who initiated the enrolment . ​ Here's how a user can check their timezone: 2. How many prospects can be enrolled in a sequence at a time? The limit on the number of prospects that can be enrolled in a sequence depends on the number of users in the account. Each user can enroll up to 500 prospects in a sequence at a time. 3. Is there any limit on the number of candidates/contacts that a user can enroll in a sequence? A user can enroll up to 500 candidates/contacts in either 1 or across multiple sequences at any given point in time. Once a user reaches the maximum active + paused enrollments i.e. 500, they will not be able to enroll any further records until the active sequence(s) are completed or they manually unenroll some records. 4. How many steps can you have in a particular sequence? Add steps to the sequence as required, up to a maximum of 40 steps , which includes a maximum of 10 email steps, 10 task steps , 10 LinkedIn steps and 10 SMS steps. You can easily rearrange the sequence steps by using the drag-and-drop functionality. 5. What happens when a user edits a running sequence? If someone edits the sequence that is already running, then the changes will apply only to future enrollments. 6. How many sequences can be created on an account? In total, you can add up to 1000 sequences to a business plan account. However, on the Pro plan, you can test the feature with 1 sequence. 7. Can we add a candidate/contact to multiple sequences? No, each candidate/contact can only be a part of a single sequence at a time. 8. When does a prospect get unenrolled from the sequence? 1. Whenever someone replies to the SMS sequence , the sequence gets paused for that specific prospect and it gets unenrolled from the sequence. 2. If the candidate/contact chooses to opt out of the SMS they will get automatically unenrolled. 3. If you manually unenroll them from the sequence. Conclusion: SMS Sequences help automate follow-up communication by combining scheduled text messages with email, tasks, and LinkedIn steps. With flexible scheduling, SMS templates, and compliance features like opt-out messaging, you can create structured communication sequences while keeping Candidate and Contact engagement organized. t: Social Profile Links - Candidates/Companies/Contacts
s: Adding social profile links to your candidates, companies & contacts
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Before you begin:
Step-by-step instructions
From the edit form
View and access social profiles
From the record Preview
Create custom social profile fields
Control visibility of social profile fields
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Social profile links in Recruit CRM allow you to store and access multiple social media profiles directly within candidate, contact, and company records. You can open these profiles instantly, add custom platforms with your own icons, and control which fields are visible to your team, helping you keep records organized, relevant, and easy to navigate. You can use this feature when you want to: • Quickly access Social Media profiles from within a record. • Keep all relevant social links organized in one place. • Add custom social platforms to suit your unique requirements. ​ Before you begin: • You need access to candidate, contact, or company records. • Admin Settings access is required to create and manage custom social fields. Step-by-step instructions From the edit form 1. To add social profile links, open the specific record and click on the pencil icon to edit. ​ 2. This will open the Edit Record form for that record. In the edit form, scroll down to the Social Profile Links section. Here, you can paste the relevant URLs. By default, fields are available for platforms such as Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter, Xing, and GitHub . Once added, click Submit to save the changes. ​ ​ View and access social profiles From the record Preview To quickly view all social media links from the list page, click the Preview (eye icon) next to the record. This opens a preview of the profile, where all associated social profile links are visible. You can click any icon to directly open the corresponding social media profile in a new tab. ​ Create custom social profile fields You can create custom social profile fields with their own icons, in addition to the default ones provided by Recruit CRM. Go to Admin Settings → Data Customization and select record type (Candidate / Contact / Company) Click + New Custom Field ​ Enter field name (e.g. Telegram, Threads, etc) Set field type → Social Profile ​ Upload a logo to represent the platform. This logo appears as the icon on the record. If you need to download social media logos, you can use Brandfetch to find and download logos for different platforms. Click Save to create the field. Control visibility of social profile fields You can control which social profile fields are visible on the Edit form and profile view. For example, if you only want to see Xing and LinkedIn and hide Twitter, Facebook, or GitHub because they are not relevant, you can change their visibility. To adjust visibility: Go to Admin Settings → Data Customization and then select the required record type (Candidate, Contact, or Company) Scroll to the Social Profile Links section Toggle fields ON or OFF based on your preference Click Save to apply the changes ​ Fields that are turned off will no longer appear on the add or edit form. FAQs Can I add multiple social links to a record? Yes, you can add multiple links across different platforms. Who can create custom social fields? Only users with Account Owner and Admin access. Can I use any logo for custom fields? Yes, you can upload any relevant logo file. Do social links open in a new tab? Yes, clicking an icon opens the profile externally. Conclusion: Managing social profile links helps you keep records informative, accessible, and tailored to your workflow, so you can quickly understand and engage with candidates, contacts, and companies without leaving Recruit CRM. t: Submit candidates to contacts
s: You can submit candidates assigned to jobs and also receive interviewer feedback by sharing a link in a couple of clicks.
h: Setting the visibility of the candidates in your Hiring Pipeline
Selecting the fields that you want to share with the client
1. Online candidate list
2. Email grid with attachments
3. Executive Search Report
b: You don't have to shuffle between your CRM, ATS, or email to find and email details of your candidates to your clients. Recruit CRM lets you send candidates you have assigned to a job to your clients in less than 3 clicks and gives them space to quickly write feedback on each candidate. ​ The candidate won't receive any emails when you send their application to a contact. How to submit candidates to contacts? 1. Navigate to the Jobs list page and click on a specific job : 2. Set the visibility of the candidates and choose the fields that you want to share with the client. Setting the visibility of the candidates in your Hiring Pipeline You can set the visibility of all candidates to ON/OFF within the job. Visibility ON: This means the candidate is visible in the list shared with the client. Visibility OFF: This means the candidate is not shared with the client. If you have too many candidates in any of the hiring stages, you can change the visibility of all the candidates to ON/OFF in just one click. Selecting the fields that you want to share with the client You also need to make sure you share the right fields with the client. To do that, click on the "Fields Shared with Clients" button and select the fields that you want to share. These shared fields will only be limited to this job, if you want to select the fields shared with clients on an account level you need to go to Admin Settings --> Field Shared with Clients 3. Click on the Submit Candidates button under the 'Candidates Pipeline' tab. 3. You'll get three options: Online Candidate List Email With Attachments Executive Search Report ​ ​ For the Online Candidate List and the Email With Attachments, it's possible to set up a trigger that changes the candidate's hiring stage whenever the email is sent. You can learn more about this by clicking here 1. Online candidate list This will send a link to your hiring manager with the list of candidates. A list of candidates will be submitted to the concerned contact through email. Once you choose the "Online Candidate List" option, the system will create an email with the link that will have a list of candidates that you have made visible. You can click on the "Preview List" button to check all the fields and candidates are chosen correctly. Your email needs to be connected here to generate the shared link, or the preview list.
