t: Submit candidates to contacts (New UI)
s: This article explains how to submit candidates assigned to a job to your contacts in Recruit CRM and collect interviewer or client feedback through shared links and emails.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Submit Candidates to a Contact
Access the Candidate Pipeline
Configure Candidate Visibility
Configure Fields Shared with Clients
For a Specific Job
For All Jobs:
Submit Candidates
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Submit Candidates feature allows you to share candidates assigned to a job with clients, hiring managers, or other contacts directly from Recruit CRM. It provides a centralized way to present shortlisted candidates, collect structured feedback, and collaborate on hiring decisions. Using shared candidate lists or email submissions, you can control which candidates and candidate fields are visible to recipients, collect feedback in a structured format, and allow contacts to update candidate hiring stages directly. Use this feature when: • You want to send shortlisted candidates to a client or hiring manager directly from Recruit CRM. • You need an efficient way to collect candidate feedback without relying on lengthy email threads. • You want clients or interviewers to review candidates through a shared list or Kanban-style view. • You want contacts to update candidate hiring stages directly from the shared link. 📌 Note: Candidates do not receive any email or notification when their profiles are submitted to a contact through the Submit Candidates feature. Submit Candidates to a Contact Follow the steps below to access the Candidate Pipeline and share candidates with a client or hiring manager. Access the Candidate Pipeline Navigate to the Jobs list page and click on the job whose candidates you want to submit. You will be taken to the Job Details page. Scroll down to the Candidate Pipeline section, where you can view all candidates assigned to the job and manage candidate submissions. From here, you can configure candidate visibility, choose which fields to share, and submit candidates to your contacts. Configure Candidate Visibility Before submitting candidates, you must decide which candidates should be visible to the client. ​ Use the visibility toggle next to each candidate to control whether they will appear in the shared candidate list. • Visibility ON – The candidate will be visible to the client. • Visibility OFF – The candidate will not be included in the shared list. • Not Available – Candidates in the Applied stage cannot have their visibility updated. To update the visibility, please update the stage from 'Applied' to another hiring stage. ​ ​If you need to update the visibility of multiple candidates at once, click Set Candidate Visibility button at the top of the Candidate Pipeline tab and choose whether to turn visibility on or off for all candidates in the job. ​ Configure Fields Shared with Clients You can control which candidate information is visible to clients. For a Specific Job In the Candidate Pipeline, click Fields Shared & Kanban Customization . ​ Select the candidate fields you want clients to see for that particular job from the list on your right. These settings only apply to the selected job. For All Jobs: Navigate to Admin Settings → Fields Shared with Clients . Select the fields that should be shared with clients across the account. These settings become the default for all jobs. Submit Candidates Once visibility and shared fields have been configured: In the Candidate Pipeline , click Submit Candidates . Select one of the available submission methods: • Online Candidate List • Email with Attachments and Candidate Grid • Executive Search Report Note For Online Candidate List and Email with Attachments and Candidate Grid , you can configure an automation that updates the candidate's hiring stage when the submission email is sent. ​ Click here to learn more about it Online Candidate List This option sends an email containing a secure link to the selected contact. The shared link displays only: • Candidates whose visibility is turned on • Fields that have been configured for sharing ​ Before sending: Click Preview List to verify the candidates and fields that will be visible. Confirm everything appears correctly. Please note: A red dot badge appears on the Remark icon whenever the candidate's current hiring stage contains a remark added by the client. Click the Remark icon to view the remark. 📌 Note: Your email needs to be connected here to generate the shared link, or the preview list. ​ Here's how to connect your email if it's not connected: Connecting Your Email (Gmail) To Recruit CRM Using Nylas Connecting Your Outlook/Office365 Email To Recruit CRM Connecting IMAP Email to Recruit CRM Once the client opens the link, they can switch between: • List View • Kanban View From either view, clients can: • Review candidate profiles • Add feedback and remarks • Move candidates between hiring stages ​ Click here to know how to customize Kanban cards for clients ​ Control Which Hiring Stages Clients Can Use: You can control which hiring stages clients are allowed to use when reviewing candidates through the shared Online Candidate List. ​ To configure this: Navigate to Admin Settings → Hiring Pipeline . Locate the Master hiring pipeline at the top and click on edit and find the stage you want to make available to clients. Enable the Let Clients Use option for that stage. ​ Only stages with this option enabled will be available to clients when they move candidates between stages from the shared List or Kanban view. ​ Control CSV Export Permissions: You can also decide whether clients can download the shared candidate list as a CSV file. To configure this: Navigate to Admin Settings → Fields Shared with Clients . Scroll down to locate the Export to CSV toggle. Turn the toggle ON to allow clients to export the candidate list. Turn the toggle OFF to restrict exports and keep candidate information view-only within the shared portal. ​ Email with Attachments and Candidate Grid This option sends an email directly to the contact containing: • A candidate grid within the email body • Candidate attachments ​ 📌 Important: Only the first 20 candidates are included when using this option. Candidates are selected based on the most recently updated records. You can also use the Candidate Submission Agent to help draft your submission email. The Candidate Submission Agent uses AI to generate structured and professionally formatted candidate submission emails based on your configured instructions, branding preferences, and layouts. This helps create a more consistent client experience while reducing the time spent manually drafting submission emails. ​ Click here to know more about the Candidate Submission Agent Executive Search Report This option generates a professional report of candidates assigned to the job. When generating the report: • You can select up to 100 candidates at once • The report can be shared directly via email • The report can be downloaded as a PDF and shared manually This option is useful when presenting a larger group of candidates in a structured report format. Click here to learn how to generate the Executive Search Report Sort Candidates in the Candidate Pipeline The Candidate Pipeline also includes sorting options to help you organize and review candidates more efficiently. From the Candidate Pipeline tab, you can sort candidates by: • Name – Alphabetical order • Hiring Stage – Pipeline stage • Assigned On – Date assigned to the job • Updated On – Most recently updated candidates • Visibility – Visibility status ​ For each option, you can choose either: • Ascending order • Descending order This makes it easier to focus on the candidates most relevant to your workflow. Troubleshooting Problem: The Online Candidate List link cannot be generated or previewed. Likely cause: Email is not connected in Recruit CRM. What to check: Confirm your email account is connected in your Recruit CRM profile -> email settings. Resolution: Connect your email, then retry generating or previewing the Online Candidate List link. Problem: A candidate does not appear in the list shared with the client. Likely cause: Candidate visibility is turned off for that job. What to check: In the job’s Candidate Pipeline, verify the visibility toggle for that candidate. ​ Resolution: Turn visibility On for the candidate individually, or use Set Candidate's Visibility to apply visibility in bulk. Problem: The client cannot see certain candidate fields. Likely cause: Those fields are not selected in Fields Shared with Clients . ​ What to check: In Group Admin Settings > Fields Shared with Clients , review which fields are selected. In the specific job, check the Fields Shared and Kanban Customization tab. ​ Resolution: Select the required fields to Fields Shared with Clients globally or for the specific job, then resend or refresh the shared view. ​ Problem: Not all candidates are included when using Email with Attachments and Candidate Grid. Likely cause: This option is limited to the initial twenty candidates. ​ What to check: Confirm how many candidates are in the pipeline and which ones were most recently updated. ​ Resolution: Be aware only the first twenty, ordered by most recently updated, are sent. If needed, adjust which candidates are most recently updated or use another submiss

t: Summarise Data in Advanced Analytics
s: This article will guide you on how to summarize data to calculate averages, totals, and other metrics.
h: What is Summarization?
Step-by-step instructions on how to summarize data by a column in Advanced Analytics
Summarize a chart or a table:
How to pick the right chart for your summaries?
Summarize with custom expressions
Summarizing tips
Cumulative Summaries
Distinct values
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Summarizing data helps answer questions like "How much revenue was made each day last week?" by calculating averages, totals, and other key metrics. You'll reach for summarization any time you need a single number or a grouped comparison instead of raw rows. For example, total placements this quarter, average deal value by owner, or candidate counts by pipeline stage. It's the step to use when you've already got the right data in front of you and just need to roll it up into something you can read at a glance or turn into a chart. Click here to know more about how to a create chart (question) What is Summarization? Summarizing means combining data from multiple records together and producing a single number, like the “average of product ratings”. So you need to determine: The numerical metric that’s going to be used to combine value. For example, count, sum, or average The column whose values will be combined. For example, quantity, price, or rating (optionally) Breakouts . They determine the groups that the data is broken out by (or grouped ). For example, you can compute order quantity grouped/broken out by months. For example , in Advanced Analytics, you can find: Average of Deal Value: Average of Deal Value by Owner Name: Average Deal Value by Owner Name for each month: In all these cases, the metric is Average, and the column is Deal Value, but adding breakouts creates different summaries and charts. Step-by-step instructions on how to summarize data by a column in Advanced Analytics You can quickly summarize your data by clicking on a column header in a table. The available summary options depend on the column type (e.g., numerical, categorical, date). Summarize a chart or a table: There are multiple ways to add summaries in Advanced Analytics: 1. Using the Table View : Click on the column header to summarize by that column. 2. Using the "Summarize" Button: Click “Summarize” button (top-right corner) when viewing a table or chart. In the “Summarize by” block, select a metric (e.g., Sum, Count, Average). In the “Group by” block, choose how to categorize your data. Click “+” to add more breakouts (grouping levels). 3. Using the Query Builder: Add a Summarize block in the query builder and select metrics, columns, and breakouts. For more details, refer to Ask a question in the query builder . How to pick the right chart for your summaries? When you click “visualize” on a question with summaries, Advanced Analytics will automatically select a chart that it believes is the most appropriate for your result. For example, if you group by a time series column, Advanced Analytics will create a line chart. In most cases, the chart that Advanced Analytics picks will be the best option. You can change the chart type . Advanced Analytics charts have requirements on the number and the kind of breakouts you can use in summaries that feed into the chart: CHART TYPE BREAKOUT REQUIREMENTS BREAKOUTS ARE USED FOR Table No breakouts required Displays raw or summarised query results as rows and columns, no grouping needed Number, gauge, and progress charts Single number, no breakouts N/A Pie charts 1 breakout Color of segments Waterfall and funnel charts 1 breakout X-axis Maps 1 breakout by a column with geographical data Location Trend charts 1 breakout by a column with time series data Time period for comparison Line, bar, row, area, and combo charts 1 or 2 breakouts First breakout for the X-axis (or Y-axis for row charts), second breakout for color Pivot tables at least 2 breakouts Rows and columns Scatter plots 1 to 3 breakouts First breakout for the X-axis, second for color, and third for the bubble size Sankey charts 2 breakouts + 1 metric First breakout for source nodes, second breakout for target nodes; metric column determines the flow size between nodes Detail No breakouts Displays the full record for a single row, used for drilldown views Box plots 1 required breakout; optional 2nd breakout First breakout for the X-axis categories; optional second breakout creates colored series per category You can switch chart types (e.g., Pie → Bar) but some charts (e.g., Pivot Table) may have restrictions based on the number of breakouts used. Summarize with custom expressions If you need more complex summaries, such as calculating average or applying conditional logic, you can use Custom Expressions in Advanced Analytics. For example, summing up of deal values only when the weighted deal percentage is 33%: SumIf([Deal Value], [Weighed Deal Percentage] = 33) Check out our article on custom expressions to learn more. Summarizing tips Group by dates and times: You can group by date and time columns. Advanced Analytics automatically selects a granularity to group by: for example, for date columns, it will automatically group by months. groups date/time columns (e.g., by month). To change the granularity, click on the time period and select a different unit (day, week, quarter, etc.). Group by numeric variables: In Advanced Analytics, you can also group by numeric variables, like Deal Value. Advanced Analytics will bin the numerical variable for you, creating range-based “categories” for grouping: If you group by a numeric variable and select "Count" as the metric, Advanced Analytics will generate a histogram (a distribution chart) of this variable. Cumulative Summaries Advanced Analytics has two types of cumulative summaries: cumulative sum cumulative count For every record, they will return the sum or count of all values up to this record in the table.These summaries work a bit differently from other summaries because the data they return depends on the order of the data in your table. Let’s say you have a table with values by month. Cumulative sum will be computed like this: Month Value Cumulative sum July 5 5 November 4 5+4 = 9 March 2 5 + 4 + 2 = 11 But if the months ordering is changed (while values remain the same), then the cumulative sum is changed as well: Month Value Cumulative sum March 2 2 July 5 2 + 5 = 7 November 4 2 + 5 + 4 = 11 Distinct values Advanced Analytics “Distinct values” summary returns the number of unique values in a column. To see the distinct values themselves, you can create any summary with a breakout by that column instead. Example: Counting Distinct Deals per Owner If you want to see how many different deals each Owner has handled, use: 🔹 Distinct count of Deal Name grouped by Owner Name. This will give you a column with all the Owner Names, and a column with row counts for every Owner Name (you can hide the count column from the results): Note In SQL, you summarize by adding a function like COUNT into a SELECT statement — similarly to how you’d add a new column computed based on the values of other columns. In Advanced Analytics, these two operations are distinct: to add a new column, you can use a Custom column block, but to add an aggregation, you use a Summary block. Troubleshooting Problem: If the chart is blank or empty, with no error displayed. Likely cause: The query has not been summarized. Most visualizations require at least one aggregation (such as Count, Sum, or Average) and, in many cases, a grouping field. What to check: Verify that a Summarize step has been added. Ensure that at least one aggregation (for example, Count of, Sum of, or Average of) is selected. Resolution path: Add the required aggregation and grouping in the Summarize step, then rerun the query and visualize the results. Conclusion: Summarization turns raw records into meaningful metrics by combining a numerical measure, a target column, and optional breakouts, giving you totals, averages, counts, and more. With options like custom expressions, cumulative summaries, and distinct values, you can tailor summaries to answer even complex business questions. If you need help at any stage, feel free to reach out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance Hope this helps! t: Sync HubSpot Records with Recruit CRM Using Workflow Automation
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to connect HubSpot in Workflow Automation
How to connect your Recruit CRM account app in Workflow Automation
Overview of each step in the Recipe
Set up HubSpot → Recruit CRM automation
Step 1: Trigger a workflow when a new HubSpot record is created
Step 2: Search for the record in Recruit CRM
Step 3: Check whether a matching record exists
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The HubSpot integration in Workflow Automation allows records to be automatically synced between HubSpot and Recruit CRM. When a new contact, company, deal, or note is created in HubSpot, the workflow checks whether a matching record already exists in Recruit CRM. If a match is found, the existing record is updated. If no match is found, a new record is created. This helps reduce manual data entry and keep information consistent across both platforms. You can use this integration when you want to: Automatically create or update contacts in Recruit CRM from HubSpot. Automatically create or update companies in Recruit CRM from HubSpot. Automatically create or update deals in Recruit CRM from HubSpot. Automatically create or update notes in Recruit CRM from HubSpot. Keep HubSpot and Recruit CRM records synchronized. Set up separate workflows for different record types. The integration also supports syncing in the opposite direction, allowing records created in Recruit CRM to be automatically created or updated in HubSpot. Apps that are required to be connected for the recipe HubSpot Recruit CRM How to connect HubSpot in Workflow Automation 1. 1. Navigate to Admin Settings >>> Workflow Automation & Integrations . 2. Click on the Connections tab under the 'Workflows' section and click on the 'Create' button >>> 'Connection'. 3. Use the search bar to search for the HubSpot app and connect it by following the instructions and setting the necessary permissions. Once the app is successfully connected, you will see a message titled 'Connection Established'. When the required app is connected, you can select the connected account inside the related steps of the recipe. How to connect your Recruit CRM account app in Workflow Automation 1. Navigate to Admin Settings >>> Workflow Automation & Integrations . 2. Click on the Connections tab under the 'Workflows' section and click on the 'Create' button >>> 'Connection'. 3. Use the search bar to search for the Recruit CRM app and connect it by selecting it and entering the API key . Once the app is successfully connected, you will see a message titled 'Connection Established'. When the required app is connected, you can select the connected account inside the related steps of the recipe. ​ Overview of each step in the Recipe Set up HubSpot → Recruit CRM automation The HubSpot to Recruit CRM workflow follows the same basic pattern for contacts, companies, deals, and notes: New record in HubSpot → Search Recruit CRM → Check whether a match exists → Create or update the Recruit CRM record Step 1: Trigger a workflow when a new HubSpot record is created The workflow starts when a new record is created in HubSpot. Depending on the recipe, the record can be a: Contact Company Deal Note Step 2: Search for the record in Recruit CRM The workflow searches Recruit CRM for a matching record using relevant identifying information, such as an email address. This step checks whether the HubSpot record already exists in Recruit CRM before creating a new record. Step 3: Check whether a matching record exists An IF condition checks the result of the search. If no matching record is found, the workflow proceeds to create a new record in Recruit CRM. If a matching record is found, the workflow skips creation and updates the existing Recruit CRM record instead. Step 4: Create the record in Recruit CRM If no matching record exists, the workflow creates a new record in Recruit CRM using the information received from HubSpot. The relevant HubSpot fields are mapped to the corresponding Recruit CRM fields during this step. Step 5: Update an existing record If a matching record already exists, the workflow updates the existing Recruit CRM record with the latest information from HubSpot. This prevents duplicate records while keeping the information synchronized. You can refer to the image below to understand the flow of the recipe: ​ The same trigger, search, condition, and create/update logic applies to companies, deals, and notes . ​ Sync Recruit CRM records to HubSpot The integration also supports the reverse workflow. When a new record is created in Recruit CRM, it can be automatically created or updated in HubSpot. This allows the integration to support bidirectional synchronization between the two platforms. New record in Recruit CRM → Create or update the record in HubSpot Step 1: Trigger a workflow when a new Recruit CRM record is created The workflow starts when a new record is created in Recruit CRM. In the recipe, select the relevant Recruit CRM record type as the trigger. Step 2: Create or update the record in HubSpot (Custom) Once the trigger is set, add the Create or Update record in HubSpot (Custom) action. Before configuring the action, you will need to select and connect the appropriate HubSpot connection . If you are working with different HubSpot accounts or connections, make sure you select the correct connection for the workflow. This action uses the information from the newly created Recruit CRM record to either create a new record in HubSpot or update an existing one, depending on whether a matching record is found. Map the relevant Recruit CRM fields to their corresponding HubSpot fields to ensure the information is transferred correctly. Step 3: Save and test the workflow Once you have configured the trigger and field mappings, click Save and use the Test option to verify that the workflow works as expected. The workflow will then automatically send newly created Recruit CRM records to HubSpot based on the configuration. You can refer to the image below to understand the flow of the recipe: ​ ​ Conclusion The HubSpot integration in Workflow Automation helps keep contacts, companies, deals, and notes synchronized between HubSpot and Recruit CRM. By using the available recipes, matching existing records, and creating or updating records automatically, the workflow reduces manual data entry and helps maintain consistent information across both platforms. t: Task Sequencing in Recruit CRM: How to Create and Use Task Sequences
s: This article will guide you on how to create task sequence to streamline your workflow and enhance task management.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
Before you begin
Create a new sequence:
Configure step timing and behavior:
Enroll contacts into a sequence while pitching candidates:
FAQs
Conclusion:
b: What does this feature do & when to use it? Task sequencing is a powerful method to automatically set up tasks for your candidate and contact profiles in Recruit CRM, along with other follow-up steps (emails, LinkedIn steps, SMS steps). A sequence defines a series of steps and the number of days after the sequence start when each step should occur. Once a record is enrolled in a sequence, Recruit CRM creates the tasks according to the task steps you configured. You want to automatically set up tasks for candidate profiles. You want to automatically set up tasks for contact profiles. You need a structured, multi-step follow-up process using tasks, emails, LinkedIn steps, and SMS steps. You want consistent timing between outreach steps without manually creating each task. Before you begin Task sequencing is available as a Business plan and above. Users on Pro or Free plans can create only one sequence. Only account owners, admins, and users on custom roles with access to sequences can create task and email sequences. Decide whether you want to build the sequence for candidates or contacts before you start. Plan your steps (tasks, emails, LinkedIn steps, SMS steps) and their timing, including how many days after the sequence start each step should occur. Create a new sequence: Go to Admin Settings in Recruit CRM. Under CRM Process Customization , click on Sequences . Click on the Create Sequence button. Select either Candidates or Contacts as the record type for which you want to create the sequence. Enter the Sequence Title to name your sequence. Configure step timing and behavior: For each step, specify the number of days after the start of the sequence when that step should be set up. ​ Confirm the days you set for each task step, as this defines when the task will be due relative to the sequence start date. ​ Understand how timing is calculated: ​ Task due date = Start date + Specified number of days. ​ Start date is the date when the task sequence is initiated. ​ "Specified Date" is the number of days you have indicated for the task to be set up after the start of the sequence. ​ Add steps to the sequence as required, up to a maximum of 40 steps in total. ​Within those forty steps, you can include up to ten task steps, ten email steps, ten LinkedIn steps, and ten SMS steps. ​ Rearrange the order of sequence steps using the drag-and-drop functionality to match your desired workflow. ​ For each step, set a specific number of days for it to execute, choosing between a range of 1 to 250 calendar days or business days. ​ To create tasks on the same day the sequence is initiated, set the day value to 0 for that step. ​When using a step on day 0, align the timing carefully with any previous steps or schedule it for a later time than the preceding step to keep the workflow seamless. ​ Enroll contacts into a sequence while pitching candidates: When pitching candidates to contacts, complete the process of sending the email or marking the candidates as pitched. ​ After the successful completion of sending the email or marking candidates as pitched, you will be automatically redirected to a page where you can enroll those contacts into a sequence. ​ On the redirected page, follow the on-screen options to enroll the relevant contacts into your chosen sequence. ​ Once enrollment is complete, your configured steps will run according to the days and step types you have set in the sequence. ​ FAQs How is the task due date calculated in a sequence? The task due date is calculated as: Task due date = Start date + Specified number of days , where the start date is when the sequence is initiated. ​ "Specified Date" is the number of days you have indicated for the task to be set up after the start of the sequence. ​ Conclusion: Task sequencing in Recruit CRM helps you automate structured follow-up for candidates and contacts by defining clear steps and timing. Configure your sequences carefully, especially the day values for each step, and you will maintain a consistent, efficient workflow with minimal manual effort. t: Task Type Customization in Recruit CRM
s: This article explains how to customize task types in Recruit CRM so you can better categorize and manage your tasks.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?

Adding Task Types
Troubleshooting

b: What this feature does and when to use it? Task type customization lets you create and manage custom task types in Recruit CRM. You can add new task types, name them, and set one as the default. This helps you tag and categorize tasks in a way that matches your recruitment process, making it easier for you and your team to identify and manage different types of tasks. You can use this feature when: When you want to create custom task types that match your internal workflow. When your team needs clearer tagging and categorization of tasks. Before you begin: Only users with access to the admin settings on the Business plan and above can customize task types. On the Pro plan, only Account Owners and users with the admin role can perform task type customization. On the Business plan and above, you can also grant access to task type customization to team members with custom roles. Customize Task Types 1. Go to Admin Settings > Click on Task Type Customization under CRM Process Customization. 2. Click on the " Customize" button. 3. Click on Add New Status and add a name (up to 50 characters) for your task type. 4. You can make it your default task type by checking the box next to it. 5. You can also customize the default Task types by editing the corresponding Task type name to suit the one relevant to you. ​ 6. Hit the "Save Status" button. Please Note: The number of available task types is a total of 100, including 2 task types available in the system by default, 'Follow Up' and 'Interview Scheduling'. In addition, on the Business plan, you can grant access to the "Task Type Customization" option to your team members on custom roles as well. Here's how you can do this: ​ 1. Go to your User Management settings in the admin settings . 2. Go to the " Roles & Permissions " section and click on the pencil icon next to the role to which you want to grant access. 3. Now, scroll down turn ON the toggle for "Task Type Customization" and hit the " Save Role " button. Adding Task Types While adding a task, you will be able to select its type on the field 'Type': Also, on the Tasks & Meetings page, you'll be able to filter the tasks by Task Type: Additionally, under Reports , you can find the 'Task Type' KPI for the Team Performance Report and the Job Statistics Report . Troubleshooting Problem: You cannot see the Task Type Customization option in Admin Settings. Likely cause: Your user role or plan does not have permission to customize task types. What to check: Confirm that your account is on the Business plan or Pro plan. On the Pro plan, confirm that you are an Account Owner or have the Admin role. On the Business plan and above, confirm that your custom role has the task type customization toggle turned on. Resolution: Ask an Account Owner to either perform the customization or update your role permissions as described in the steps above. Problem: You cannot add more task types. Likely cause: You have reached the maximum limit of thirty task types (including the two default system task types). What to check: Count your existing task types to confirm if you have reached the total of thirty. Resolution: Remove or repurpose existing task types if you need to add new ones. FAQs How many task types can I create in Recruit CRM? You can have a total of thirty task types, including the two task types available in the system by default. What happens if I reach the task type limit? If you reach the total of thirty task types, you will not be able to add more until you remove or adjust existing task types. Conclusion: Customizing task types in Recruit CRM helps you better categorize and manage your tasks, giving your team clearer visibility into different types of tasks. t: Tasks, Meetings, and the Task Queue in Recruit CRM
s: Everything you need to manage tasks, meetings, and the task queue in one place.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Step-by-step instructions to navigate the Tasks and Meetings Page
1. Open the Tasks and Meetings page
2. Manage tasks
3. Process tasks using the Task Queue
4. Manage overdue tasks and perform bulk actions
5. Manage meetings
6. Perform bulk actions on meetings
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Tasks and Meetings Page: From one place, you can view, filter, sort, and manage tasks and meetings, process pending work using the Task Queue , perform bulk actions such as updating, completing, deleting, or exporting records, and keep track of overdue tasks. Use this feature when: You want to view and manage all your tasks and meetings from a single location. You need to work through pending tasks efficiently using the Task Queue . You want to filter and sort tasks or meetings to focus on your priorities for the day. You need to perform bulk actions, such as marking tasks as completed, updating, deleting, or exporting multiple records at once. You want to monitor and manage overdue tasks to ensure nothing is missed. Managing tasks and meetings efficiently plays an important role in staying on top of your daily workload. The following sections explain how to use the Tasks and Meetings page to organize and complete your work more effectively. Step-by-step instructions to navigate the Tasks and Meetings Page 1. Open the Tasks and Meetings page From the left navigation panel, click Tasks and Meetings . Use the dropdown in the top right corner to switch between the Tasks and Meetings views. ​ 2. Manage tasks Use the Quick View section to switch between All Tasks , Completed Tasks , and Incomplete Tasks . ​ You can choose between All Tasks, Completed Tasks, and Incomplete Tasks from the Quick View section. When you use the Tasks page for the first time, the system sets the Quick View to Incomplete tasks, with the Owner filter set to you, and the Due date filter set to today. If you change any filter, including the Quick View selection, that choice persists the next time you open the section, even after you log out and log back in. You can filter tasks based on the Owner, Collaborators, Status, Entity, Associations, Due Date, Added By, Added on, Related To, Updated By, and Updated On parameters. You can further refine the tasks by using the available filters to quickly find specific tasks based on: Owner Collaborators Status Entity Association Due date Added by and Added on Related To Updated by and Updated on ​ 3. Process tasks using the Task Queue Click Start Tasks in a Queue from the top right of the Tasks page to work through pending tasks without manually opening each record. ​ Within the Task Queue, you can: Switch between Candidate, Contact, Company, Job, and Deal tasks. Use the Progress dropdown to see all records in the queue. Navigate between records using the Previous and Next buttons. Reschedule the task Mark it as done ​ 4. Manage overdue tasks and perform bulk actions Any task that remains incomplete after its due date is automatically marked as Overdue . Since tasks are not completed automatically, they must be manually marked as complete either from the related record or directly from the Incomplete Tasks view on the Tasks and Meetings page. You can also perform bulk actions by selecting multiple tasks and using the toolbar to: Mark tasks as completed Update task details Delete tasks Export tasks 5. Manage meetings Switch to the Meetings view using the dropdown in the top right corner. Choose between List View and Calendar View , then use Quick View to display: All Meetings Upcoming Meetings Past Meetings Today's Meetings ​ By default, Recruit CRM displays your upcoming meetings. Use filters to narrow results based on: Owner Attendees Collaborators Meeting Type Entity Status Associations Scheduled Date Added by and Added on Related To Updated by and Updated on ​ Ensure your calendar is connected and synchronized so meetings appear correctly. 6. Perform bulk actions on meetings Select one or more meetings to perform bulk actions using the toolbar. You can: Update meeting details Delete meetings Export meetings ​ 7. Sort and view related records Use the Sort option to organize both tasks and meetings in ascending or descending order. Available sorting options include: Related To Owner Status Task or Meeting Type Added By and Added On Updated By and Updated On Due Date or Meeting Date Title Description ​ To view more information about a related record, click the Profile View icon beside the record name in the Related To column. A side panel opens with the record's details. 8. Filter tasks and meetings from the Dashboard Use the filtering options available on the Dashboard to quickly refine the tasks and meetings displayed. Filter Tasks by status and date. Filter Meetings by status, meeting type, and date. ​ Troubleshooting Problem: Tasks are missing from the Tasks page Likely cause : Filters or Quick View are hiding some tasks. What to check : Confirm whether Quick View is set to All, Completed, or Incomplete. Check filters such as owner, collaborators, status, entity, and due date. Resolution : Clear or adjust filters and switch Quick View to All to see a broader set of tasks. Problem: Overdue tasks are not marked as completed even after the due date passes Likely cause : Tasks are not automatically completed. What to check : Confirm whether you manually checked the checkbox beside the task name. Resolution : Open the record or use the Tasks and Meetings page, find the overdue task, and manually mark it as completed by checking the checkbox. Problem: Meetings do not appear in the Meetings section Likely cause : Calendar is not connected or not synced with Recruit CRM. What to check : Verify that your calendar is connected and syncing with Recruit CRM. Check filters and Quick View (such as upcoming or today’s meetings). Resolution: Connect and sync your calendar, then review the Meetings page again with appropriate filters. Problem: Bulk actions are not affecting the expected items Likely cause : Not all intended tasks or meetings are selected. What to check: Confirm which rows are selected before performing bulk update, bulk delete, or export. Resolution: Re-select the correct items and then click the relevant bulk action button (Mark as Completed, Update, Delete, or Export). FAQs Q1: What is the default view when I open the Tasks page for the first time? The default view shows incomplete tasks where you are set as the owner. Any filters you change will persist the next time you open the section. Q2: What is the default view when I open the Meetings page for the first time? The default view shows upcoming meetings where you are the default owner, and your chosen filters will be maintained in future sessions. Q3: Are tasks automatically marked as completed when the due date passes? No. Tasks are only marked as completed when you manually check the checkbox beside the task name or use bulk actions to mark them as completed. Q4: How does the task queue help me work faster? The task queue opens the profile pages linked to tasks and lets you move between records using previous and next buttons, so you do not need to manually open each task in a new tab. Q5: Can I export tasks and meetings? Yes. You can export both tasks and meetings by selecting them on their respective list pages and clicking the export arrow in the top header bar. Conclusion: Managing tasks, meetings, and the task queue from one central place in Recruit CRM helps you stay on top of your daily work, handle overdue items, and streamline bulk updates. If you need more help creating tasks or meetings, use the in-app hyperlinks provided on the dashboard and Tasks and Meetings pages for additional guidance. b: What this feature does and when to use it The Team Performance Report provides a comprehensive view of individual teammate and team performance across a wide range of KPIs (Key Performance Indicators). It helps you measure productivity, monitor hiring activities, compare performance across teammates and teams, and identify trends over a selected time period. 📌 Note: Reports for individual team members are available on all supported plans, while team-specific reports are available only on the Business Plan and above . ​ Use this feature when: • You want to compare the performance of individual recruiters or teammates. • You need to evaluate how different teams are performing against key recruitment KPIs. • You want a consolidated view of activities such as candidates added, notes created, calls logged, meetings scheduled, tasks completed, and emails sent. • You need to review historical performance across hiring stages within a specific date range. • You want to measure the effectiveness of email sequences, including enrollments, open rates, reply rates, and unsubscribe rates. Results are displayed through interactive charts and detailed tables, allowing you to drill down into the underlying records, perform Boolean searches, sort and filter data, and export reports for further analysis. Generate and Analyze the Team Performance Report 1. Open the Team Performance Report: Navigate to the Reports section from the left-hand navigation menu and open the Team Performance Report . 2. Select recruiters and teams: Choose the team members you want to include in the report from the Users dropdown. If you're on the Business Plan or above , you can also select one or more Teams from the Teams dropdown to generate team-level reports. 3. Select the KPIs: Open the KPI dropdown and select the metrics you want to analyze. The Team Performance Report supports a wide range of KPIs, including: All hiring stages within your Master Hiring Pipeline. Notes added to any record by your users (including note types) Tasks added Candidates, jobs, contacts and companies added Total call logs added to all records and to specifically candidates or contacts Candidate, contacts, and total meetings added (including meeting types) Candidates pitched Contact stages added to contacts Billable revenue and cash collected from related deals. Sent email conversations (This will include emails sent from RCRM, your connected native email account, and email sequences.) Email sequences: number of enrollments, sequences created, open rate, reply rate, and unsubscribe rate. Activity-Based vs. Stage-Based KPIs: When interpreting prescreen calls, note: "Prescreen": Logged phone calls categorized under Call Type in KPIs are activity-based and require filtering by Call Type: Prescreen to view details. "Prescreen": Also refers to a hiring stage in pipelines, with data exclusively visible in stage-based reports, not activity-focused ones. ​ ​ 4. Select the date range: Choose the required date range for the report. You can select one of the predefined ranges or specify a Custom Date Range by choosing the desired start and end dates. 5. Generate or save the report: Click Generate Report to run the report. If you plan to use the same report configuration again, click Save and Generate Report . This saves the report settings so you can quickly access and modify the report in the future. Once the report is generated, you'll see a bar chart displaying the selected KPIs based on the chosen recruiters, teams, and date range. View Detailed Records: Each bar in the chart is clickable. Click any bar (for example, Candidates Added ) to open a detailed list of the records associated with that KPI for the selected time period. ​ Within the detailed report, you can: • Review the underlying records. • Sort the data by clicking any column header. • Apply additional filters to narrow down the results. • Perform a Boolean Search to quickly locate specific records. • Export the filtered results as a CSV file. Export the Report: You can export the report in multiple ways: • Click Export Report to CSV above the chart to download the stage-wise summary table as a CSV file. • Click the Export icon in the top-right corner of the bar chart to download the chart as an image in PNG, JPG, or SVG format. • Click any bar in the chart to open the detailed candidate list for that stage, then select Export Report to CSV to download the detailed candidate report as a CSV file. ​ Important Notes: 📌 Historical Hiring Stage Data Hiring stage KPIs (such as Assigned or Placed ) are based on historical data . This means the report shows candidates who were in those hiring stages at some point during the selected date range, even if their current hiring stage has since changed. 📌 Activity-based vs. Stage-based KPIs Some KPI names may appear similar but represent different types of data. For example, Prescreen can refer to: • A Call Type , which is an activity-based KPI. To view these records, filter by Call Type: Prescreen . • A Hiring Stage , which is a stage-based KPI and is reported separately within the hiring stage metrics. Sent Email Conversations KPI: The Sent Email Conversations KPI has additional permissions and reporting considerations: • By default, only Account Owners can generate reports containing the Sent Email Conversations KPI. • On the Business Plan , you can grant access to this KPI through Custom Roles . • If a teammate has multiple connected email accounts (available on the Business Plan ), you can choose which connected email account to report on. 📌 Scheduling limitations When scheduling reports that include the Sent Email Conversations KPI: • This KPI only works in scheduled reports, and the report will be emailed to you from `support@recruitcrm.io`. •The maximum supported date range is 30 days . • Today's date cannot be selected , as email activity may still be syncing. • Scheduled reports begin from the following day . • Selecting a date range longer than 30 days will display an error. 📌 Saved report permissions If a saved or scheduled report contains only the Sent Email Conversations KPI, only Account Owners and users with the required custom permission can view it. If the report contains Sent Email Conversations along with other KPIs: • Users without permission can still open and run the report. • However, the Sent Email Conversations KPI will be omitted from their results. • If such a user edits and saves the report, the restricted KPI will be permanently removed from that saved report configuration. What to check: Confirm that the same KPIs are selected in the report as in any target or comparison report. Confirm that the date range in the report matches the date range you intend to analyze. Resolution: Adjust the KPI selection and date range so they match your intended parameters, then regenerate the report. Problem: Numbers for hiring stages look different from the current pipeline view Likely cause: Hiring stage data in the Team Performance Report is historical. What to check: Confirm that the date range used in the report includes periods when candidates may have been in different stages than they are now. Resolution: Interpret hiring stage KPIs as historical counts: if you see numbers related to any hiring stage assigned or placed, it means candidates were in that hiring stage during some point in the date range the report was generated for, and their current hiring stage may now be different. Users will not be able to use the texting feature until the KYC process is completed and approved by Twilio. You can fill in the KYC form inside Recruit CRM under Phone Calling & SMS settings. t: Texting Laws and Consent in Recruit CRM
s: This article will give you guidelines about what you'll need to consider before texting your candidates/clients.
h: Twilio's Messaging Policy
U.S. Carrier Penalties for Non-Compliant Messaging
T-Mobile penalties for non-compliant Messaging
Content Violation
Messaging Program Evasion
b: Recruit CRM allows users on the Pro plan and above to send text messages directly to Candidates and Contacts. To use this feature, you'll need to purchase messaging credits. Recruit CRM uses Twilio to power its texting functionality. Before sending any text messages, you are responsible for obtaining the recipient's consent and ensuring that your messages comply with Twilio's Messaging Policy and applicable carrier regulations. Please note: The texting feature is currently available only for the following countries: USA, UK, ISRAEL, HONG KONG, CANADA, & SWEDEN. It allows for sending messages within the country, international messaging is currently disabled. US-based clients first need to register with Twilio to start texting. Here's how you can do this Users in the UK are required to complete a KYC form in order to use the texting feature. Texting will only be available after the KYC form is submitted and approved. ➡️ Learn more about KYC here . Failed SMS will be chargeable and can be viewed in the message log under Phone Calling and SMS Settings. Twilio's Messaging Policy An important intent of this step is to make sure that messages are sent with the consent of the message recipient, and that those messages comply with applicable laws, communications industry guidelines or standards, and measures of fairness and decency. Twilio treats all messaging transmitted via Twilio’s platform as Application-to-Person (A2P) messaging. All A2P messages originating from Twilio are subject to this Messaging Policy, which covers rules and /or prohibitions regarding: Consent ( “opt-in”) ; Revocation of Consent (“opt-out”) ; Sender Identification ; Messaging Usage ; Filtering Evasion ; and Enforcement. This policy applies to all our customers who use our texting feature as we integrate texting with Twilio. U.S. Carrier Penalties for Non-Compliant Messaging U.S. carriers have created A2P messaging channels, such as shortcodes, Toll-Free numbers, and 10-digit long codes (A2P 10DLC) in order to give senders a sanctioned channel for messaging that will ensure consumers reliably receive wanted messages. A failure to comply with carrier requirements may be subject to carrier penalties. T-Mobile penalties for non-compliant Messaging Content Violation Content violating carrier policies – as reflected in Twilio's Acceptable Use Policy and/or Messaging Policy – includes spam, phishing, and SHAFT violations (Sex, Hate, Alcohol, Firearms, Tobacco). Fee: $10,000 per violation Messaging Program Evasion Using filtering evasion techniques, such as snowshoeing and recycling numbers (releasing/purchasing new numbers), to dilute number reputation. ​ Fee: $1,000 Fine This article has provided information about the law designed to help Recruit CRM's users better understand the legal issues surrounding texting. Legal information is not the same as legal advice, the application of the law to an individual's specific circumstances. Recruit CRM insists that you consult a lawyer if you want professional assurance that our information, and your interpretation of it, is accurate. Refer to this article for texting your candidates/contacts directly from RecruitCRM Related Articles Call Recording Laws and Consent Requirements in Recruit CRM Texting & WhatsApp Messaging Candidates/Contacts in RecruitCRM Obtaining consent for texting prospects (New UI) Texting Candidates/Contacts in RecruitCRM (New UI) US A2P 10DLC Registration & SMS Consent Configuration

s: This article explains what the Time to Hire Report does, how to generate it, and how to interpret its metrics and outputs.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Generate and Analyze the Time to Hire Report
Export the Report
Here is how the two metrics on the Time to Hire Report are calculated:
Troubleshooting
Problem: A hiring stage you expect to see is missing from the report
Problem: Export options do not appear
FAQs
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Time to Hire Report helps you measure the efficiency of your hiring process by showing how long it takes to fill jobs and how much time candidates spend at each stage of your hiring pipeline. Using this report, you can measure the average time it takes for the entire hiring process for different jobs! Time to Hire Report measures the time between the creation of a job to when the first candidate is placed and the average time to hire for all placements for the job. You can also measure the average time for each hiring stage in your hiring pipeline. These metrics will not only help you get an overview of the time to hire for individual jobs, but you can also compare the time taken to hire for different jobs and how long a candidate has spent in each hiring stage. The report presents the data through an interactive bar chart and a detailed table , allowing you to compare hiring timelines across selected jobs and hiring stages. You can click most bars in the chart to view the underlying candidate records, and export both the charts and report data for further analysis or sharing. Generate and Analyze the Time to Hire Report 1. Open the Time to Hire Report Navigate to the Reports section from the left-hand navigation menu and open the Time to Hire Report . ​ 2. Select the jobs Choose the job or jobs you want to include in the report. You can: • Use the Quick View filters to narrow down the list of jobs. • Perform the Add Filter or the Boolean Search to find specific jobs based on your search criteria. Once you've identified the required jobs, select them using the corresponding checkboxes, then click Select Jobs to confirm your selection. 3. Select the hiring stages (KPIs) Open the KPI dropdown and select the hiring stages you want to analyze in the report. These stages are used to calculate the average time candidates spend at each stage of your hiring pipeline. ​ 4. Generate or save the report Click Generate Report to run the report. If you want to reuse the same report configuration in the future, click Save and Generate Report . This saves the report settings while generating the report immediately. ​ Once the report is generated, you'll see: ​ 1. A bar chart displaying the average time taken for candidates to move through each selected hiring stage. All bars in the chart are clickable. Click any bar to view the list of candidates associated with that hiring stage for the selected jobs. ​ Within the detailed report, you can: • Review the underlying candidate records. • Sort the data by clicking any column header. • Customize the displayed information using Edit Columns . • Apply additional filters to narrow down the results. • Perform a Boolean Search to quickly locate specific candidates. • Export the filtered candidate list as a CSV file. ​ 📌 Please note: One of the bars in the chart represents an aggregate metric and is therefore not clickable . ​ 2. A detailed table below the chart displaying both the average time and the actual time taken for each hiring stage across the selected jobs, allowing you to compare hiring timelines and identify stages that may be causing delays. ​ Export the Report You can export the report in multiple ways: • Click the Export icon in the top-right corner of the bar chart to download the chart as a PNG, JPG, or SVG image. • Click Export Report to CSV in the table section to download the detailed Time to Hire report as a CSV file. • Click any bar in the chart to open the detailed candidate list for that KPI, then click Export Report to CSV to download the detailed report as a CSV file. ​ Here is how the two metrics on the Time to Hire Report are calculated: 1. Time for the first candidate to reach a specific stage = Date of specific Hiring Stage (Stage Date) - Date on which job was created 2. Average time for all candidates to reach a specific stage = Total time taken / Number of candidates in that Hiring Stage Total Time = [Date of Specific Hiring Stage (Stage Date) of first candidate - Date of Job Created] +[Date of Specific Hiring Stage (Stage Date) of second candidate - Date of Job Created] Troubleshooting Problem: A hiring stage you expect to see is missing from the report Likely cause: The stage was not selected as a KPI when configuring the report. What to check: In the Time to Hire Report setup, review which KPIs (hiring stages) are selected. Resolution: Re-run the report and ensure the required hiring stages are selected in the KPI list before generating. Problem: Export options do not appear Likely cause: You may not be clicking the correct menu icons on the graph or table. What to check: For the graph, look for the three lines icon on the top right corner. For the table, look for the Export Report to CSV button at the top corner of the table. Resolution: Click the appropriate icon and select the desired export format (PNG, JPG, SVG for graphs). FAQs How is “time for the first candidate to reach a specific stage” calculated? Time for the first candidate to reach a specific stage is calculated as: Date of specific hiring stage (stage date) − Date the job was created. This shows how long it took from job creation until the first candidate reached that stage. How is the “average time for all candidates to reach a specific stage” calculated? Average time for all candidates to reach a specific stage is: Total time taken ÷ Number of candidates in that hiring stage. The total time is the sum of each candidate’s time to reach that stage. How is “total time” defined in this report? Total time is calculated by adding together - [Date of Specific Hiring Stage (Stage Date) of first candidate - Date of Job Created] +[Date of Specific Hiring Stage (Stage Date) of second candidate - Date of Job Created] What does the Time to Hire Report measure at the job level? The Time to Hire Report measures: The time from job creation to when the first candidate is placed in that job. The average time to hire for all placements in that job. The average time spent in each hiring stage for that job. Can I save and reuse a Time to Hire Report setup? Yes. When generating the report, you can choose Save and Generate Report . This saves the report configuration, and you can later view and edit all saved reports instead of reconfiguring from scratch. Conclusion The Time to Hire Report in Recruit CRM gives you a clear view of how long it takes to fill jobs and how much time candidates spend in each hiring stage. By selecting the right jobs and KPIs, generating the report, and using the graph, table, and export options, you can track hiring speed, identify bottlenecks, and improve your recruitment process. If you need further help using or interpreting the Time to Hire Report, reach out to Recruit CRM support team. t: Timesheet Notifications & Email Reminders (Beta)
s: This article explains how automated email reminders, custom reminders, and real-time in-app notifications work for both Timesheets and Reimbursements, helping contractors, clients, and agency users stay informed throughout the approval process.
h: What does this feature do & when to use it?
How do Timesheet Notifications & Email Reminders work?
Automated Email Notifications
Custom Email Reminders
Email Templates for Timesheet Reminders
In-App Real-Time Notifications
Reimbursement Notifications & Attachments
Automated Email Notifications for Reimbursements
b: Note: Currently, this feature is in beta version and can be enabled upon request. Please feel free to reach out to your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. What does this feature do & when to use it? The Timesheet Notifications & Email Reminders feature helps keep contractors, clients, approvers, and agency users informed throughout the timesheet lifecycle. How do Timesheet Notifications & Email Reminders work? There are three types of notifications available for Timesheets to help contractors, clients, and you stay updated throughout the timesheet process: Automated Email Reminders , Custom Email Reminders , and Real-Time In-App Notifications . Each notification type serves a different purpose based on the user role and timesheet status. Automated Email Notifications Automated emails are system-generated notifications that are sent automatically when specific timesheet actions take place. Contractors receive these emails in real time when a timesheet is created for them, when the timesheet is approved by the Agency or Client, or when the timesheet is rejected by the Agency or Client. Each email includes a “View Timesheet” link, allowing contractors to directly access the relevant timesheet in the Contractor Portal. Contractor email notifications will not be sent if the contractor has been unassigned from the job, if the Contractor Portal is disabled, if the contractor does not have access to the Contractor Portal, or if the contractor is marked as Off-Limits. Note: Make sure the Contractor Portal is enabled for the contractor to receive email notifications Approvers receive automated reminder emails when timesheets with logged hours are submitted and are waiting for approval. A timesheet can be submitted by an Agency Recruiter, Client, or Contractor. A timesheet with zero logged hours can also be submitted, but it will not appear on the Approvers’ Review Timesheets page or trigger an automatic submission notification to approvers. The system checks for newly submitted timesheets every 4 hours starting from 00 UTC . An email reminder is sent only when submitted timesheets are found during that period. This includes newly submitted timesheets as well as timesheets that have been resubmitted after being rejected. The reminder email includes all timesheets that are currently awaiting approval for that approver, including older pending timesheets that have not yet been approved. Note — For clients to receive these notifications: Client Portal must exist Online link must be enabled When an approver opens the email and clicks the provided link, they are redirected to the relevant place to review the timesheets. Agency approvers are redirected to Recruit CRM, while Client approvers are redirected to the Client Portal. Custom Email Reminders Custom email reminders allow agency users to manually send reminder emails whenever follow-up is required. These reminders are sent immediately to the selected contractor or approver. Contractor reminders can be sent for timesheets that are in Open or Rejected status. Approver reminders can be sent for Submitted timesheets that are waiting for approval. This also includes zero-hour timesheets when a Custom Reminder is manually sent, even though these timesheets do not appear in the Approvers’ Review Timesheets page or trigger automatic submission notifications. ​ When a Custom Reminder is manually sent for a zero-hour timesheet, the approver receives the reminder and can review the timesheet. If multiple selected timesheets belong to the same recipient, Recruit CRM sends a single consolidated reminder email that includes all relevant timesheets requiring action. ​ ​ Email Templates for Timesheet Reminders Two new email templates are available under Standard Email Templates: Contractor Timesheet Reminder Email Template Approver Timesheet Reminder Email Template These templates automatically populate when sending a custom reminder. Important: Do not remove the {view_timesheet} link from the email template. This option allows recipients to directly access the relevant timesheet. Before sending a reminder email, Recruit CRM checks whether the required contractor or approver details are available. For contractors, reminder emails cannot be sent in the following cases: The contractor’s email ID is missing. The contractor has opted out of receiving emails. The contractor record has been deleted. The contractor has been unassigned from the job. The Contractor Portal does not exist. The Contractor Portal has been disabled. For approvers, reminder emails cannot be sent in the following cases: The approver’s email ID is missing. The approver has opted out of receiving emails. The approver record has been deleted. The timesheet has not been shared with the contact. The online link is disabled for the client. If any validation check fails, the system will display the reason why the reminder could not be sent. Once the issue is resolved, you can revalidate the details and send the reminder again. In-App Real-Time Notifications Real-time in-app notifications help contractors, clients, and approvers stay updated on important timesheet activities directly within their respective portals. These notifications are available in the Contractor Portal, Client Portal, and Agency Portal . When a user receives a notification, they can click on it to directly open the related timesheet page, where they can review the details or take the required action. Contractors receive notifications when important timesheet actions take place, such as when a timesheet is created for them, when their timesheet is approved by the Agency or Client, or when their timesheet is rejected. Approvers receive notifications when a timesheet with logged hours is submitted for approval. This applies whether the timesheet is submitted by the Contractor, Client, or Agency user. Zero-hour timesheets do not generate submission notifications for approvers. If multiple timesheets require the same type of notification, the system may group them into a single notification instead of creating separate notifications for each timesheet. Users can access all relevant timesheets directly from the notification. In-app notifications will not be generated if the required portal does not exist, the portal has been disabled, or the Client online link has been turned off. Reimbursement Notifications & Attachments Recruit CRM also sends notifications for reimbursements, helping contractors, agency users, and clients stay informed throughout the reimbursement approval process. Automated Email Notifications for Reimbursements Contractors receive automated email notifications in real time when a reimbursement is Approved or Rejected by an Agency or Client approver. These notifications are sent only if the contractor has access to the Contractor Portal . Clicking View Reimbursement in the email opens the reimbursement tab of the related timesheet in the Contractor Portal. Agency and Client approvers receive automated reminder emails when a reimbursement is Submitted for approval by a contractor or agency user. These reminder emails are generated every 4 hours and consolidate all pending reimbursement approvals for the same approver into a single email. If a reimbursement is reopened after a previous decision, it will be included in the next scheduled reminder email. Real-Time In-App Notifications for Reimbursements Real-time in-app notifications are also available for reimbursements. Contractors receive notifications when a reimbursement is Approved or Rejected , while Agency and Client approvers receive notifications when a reimbursement is Submitted for approval. Clicking a notification opens the reimbursement tab of the related timesheet, allowing users to review or take action immediately. FAQs Why didn't a contractor receive an automated email ? Possible reasons include: Contractor Portal is disabled Contractor Portal does not exist (they haven’t been Invited/ No sign Up) Contractor has been unassigned from the job Contractor is marked as Off-Limits Why can't I send a reminder for an approved timesheet? Approved timesheets are not eligible for reminder emails, since Timesheet Lifecycle is considered Complete upon Approval. What happens when I click a notification or email link? Depending on your Portal, you will be redirected to the relevant timesheet, approval page, or portal page associated with the notification, where you can perform the necessary Action. Do zero-hour timesheets trigger automatic notifications to approvers? No. Zero-hour timesheets do not appear on the Approvers’ Review Timesheets page or trigger automatic submission notifications. However, an approver can still review a zero-hour timesheet when an agency or client user sends a Custom Reminder manually. Conclusion With real-time notifications enabled, users can stay informed about important timesheet updates directly from their respective portals. These notifications help contractors
