b: What this feature does and when to use it? Pay and Bill Rule Templates allow you to standardize how contractor working hours, overtime, breaks, pay, and billing amounts are calculated in Recruit CRM. You can create reusable templates by defining a work schedule, choosing how breaks are handled, setting the treatment of additional hours, and adding custom rules based on shifts or working hours. This feature is useful when you want to: Standardize pay and bill calculations across contractors. Define regular working days and hours. Configure unpaid break hours that are automatically deducted from working hours. Configure overtime, shift-based, and time-range rules. Apply multipliers or fixed pay and bill rates. Create reusable templates for different contractor work schedules. Reduce manual calculations and maintain consistency across timesheets. Please note: This feature is currently available in Beta and can be enabled upon request. Please contact your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. Who can manage Pay and Bill Rule Templates? Account Owners , Admins , and users with custom roles that have access to Pay and Bill Templates can access Pay and Bill Template Settings . Users with Team Member and Restricted Team Member roles cannot access these settings. How to create a Pay and Bill Rule Template? Navigate to Admin Settings → Pay and Bill Settings → Pay and Bill Rule Template . Click Add Rule Template. Under Work Schedule , enter a name for the template and select the method you want to use for defining the contractor's work schedule. Set up the Work Schedule Choose one of the following methods to configure the contractor's work schedule. Work Start and End Time Select at least one working day and define the Start Time and End Time for each day. Unselected days are treated as days off. You can use Copy to All to apply the first day's schedule to all working days. The configured schedule is treated as Regular Hours and calculated at the standard 1× rate. Please note: The Start Time and End Time must be different, and 00:00 cannot be used as the End Time. Enter Work Hours Select the working days and enter the number of working hours for each day. You can use Copy to All to apply the first day's hours to all working days. Please note: You can enter up to 24 working hours per day, and the working hours cannot be 0. Configure unpaid break hours Use Unpaid break hours per day to define the break duration deducted from scheduled hours when calculating actual payable working hours and overtime thresholds. Please note: The break duration cannot exceed the scheduled working hours for a day. Example: If the work schedule is 9:00 AM–5:30 PM with a 30-minute excluded break , the actual working hours are 8 hours . If the contractor logs 9:00 AM–6:00 PM , the system calculates 1 hour of overtime . Please note: Overtime hours are displayed only when a custom overtime rule is configured. Configure Round Time Entry Use the Round time entries automatically toggle in the Rule Template to automatically round time entries based on a selected interval. You can choose from the following rounding intervals: 6 minutes 15 minutes 30 minutes You can also choose how the time entries should be rounded: Round Up: Rounds the time entry up to the next selected interval. Round Down: Rounds the time entry down to the previous selected interval. Nearest Interval: Rounds the time entry to whichever selected interval is closest. For example, if the selected interval is 15 minutes : With Round Up , 8:04 is rounded to 8:15. With Round Down , 8:14 is rounded to 8:00. With Nearest Interval , 8:04 is rounded to 8:00, while 8:06 is rounded to 8:15. For bulk entries, rounding is applied according to each contractor's individual timesheet settings. If contractors have different rounding configurations, each entry is rounded according to the settings configured for that contractor. Configure the standard rate for extra hours Use the Apply standard rate (1X) for extra hours toggle to control how hours outside the defined work schedule or custom rules are handled. Enabled: Extra hours are paid and billed at the standard 1× rate . Disabled: Only hours covered by the work schedule or custom rules are considered for pay and bill calculations. Any additional hours are not payable or billable. Add custom rules Custom rules allow you to configure shift-based, overtime, and time-based pay and bill calculations. Click Add Rule . Enter a name for the rule, select the applicable days, choose the Rule Type , and configure the required time range or threshold. The working days configured in the Work Schedule are selected by default. Define the pay and bill rates using either a Multiplier or a Fixed Rate . Fixed rates use the currency configured in the Timesheet Settings . Please note: The same time range cannot be applied to multiple rules on the same day. If logged time falls outside all configured rules, the Apply standard rate (1X) for extra hours setting determines whether those hours are paid and billed. You can click the Delete icon to remove a rule or Add Rule to create additional rules. Rule Type and description For Work Start and End Time Method: Rule Type Description Before shift You can apply a "Before Shift" rule on selected days, specifying a time range that occurs before the regular shift start time. ‘Before shift’ for the same day cannot be applied twice. A Before Shift rule cannot start at 00:00, as it is considered an invalid start time for this rule type. After shift You can apply an "After Shift" rule on selected days, specifying a time range that occurs after the regular shift start time. This is applicable only if the method is set to "Shift." ‘After shift’ for the same day cannot be applied twice. The After shift rule cannot start at 00:00, as it is considered an invalid start time for this rule type. Specific time range The Specific Range rule allows you to define a specific time window by specifying a start and end time, and applying a multiplier for that range. This rule can be applied to multiple ranges on the same day. Daily Overtime The Daily Overtime rule lets users decide after how many hours overtime should be paid on a given day. The threshold must be equal to or more than the regular working hours defined for that day. For example, if Monday’s regular hours are 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM (8 hours), then the Daily Overtime threshold must be at least 8. If it’s set below 8, the system will show an error. If the total hours worked on that day go beyond this threshold, the extra hours will be paid and billed (given that those hours are not covered by other rules). The Daily Working Hours rule can be applied twice for the same day to support multiple overtime thresholds. The same threshold (e.g., “above 8 hours”) cannot be applied more than once. Each rule must define a unique threshold. Weekly overtime The Weekly Overtime rule applies to all days in the week and is only available for weekly and biweekly timesheets. You can set a weekly threshold (e.g., 40 hours). If the total hours worked in a week go beyond this threshold, the extra hours will be counted as overtime (given those hours are not covered by other rules). The threshold must be equal to or more than the total regular hours in that week. If your work schedule is: Monday to Thursday: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM (8 hours/day) Friday: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM (7 hours) Then your total regular hours = (4 × 8) + (1 × 7) = 39 hours So, the weekly overtime threshold must be at least 39 hours . You cannot set the threshold lower than the total regular hours for the week. This rule cannot be applied twice. Breaks Breaks are excluded, they are subtracted from the working hours. This means the break duration will not be considered for pay or bill calculations. Breaks are always deducted from the time slot entered on the timesheet. ​ Example: Regular Hours: 9:00 to 17:00 After-Shift Rule: 17:00 to 18:00 Break Taken: 13:00 PM to 14:00 PM Time Logged on Timesheet: 9:00 to 18:00 In this case, the 1-hour break will be deducted from the regular hours (9:00 AM to 5:00 PM), not the after-shift time. So the system will calculate: Regular Time: 7 hours (after removing 1-hour break) After-Shift Time: 1 hour For the Enter Work hours Method: Rule Type Description Daily overtime The Daily Overtime functionality will work the same as the Shift Rule. The minimum hours, overtime multipliers, and all other related functionality will remain consistent with the shift rule behavior. Weekly overtime The Weekly Overtime functionality will work the same as the Shift Rule. The minimum hours, overtime multipliers, and all other related functionality will remain consistent with the shift rule behavior. This rule cannot be applied twice. Breaks As breaks are excluded, the break hours will be subtracted from the work hours Note: When rules are applied, the Specific Range rule is applied first, followed by Daily Overtime, and finally Weekly Overtime

t: Timesheets - Deals for Contract Staffing (Beta)
s: This article explains how Deals work for contract staffing, how candidates and jobs link, how timesheets work, and bulk actions you can take.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to associate a Job with a Deal?
How to associate additional candidates with a Deal?
How to enable timesheets from a Deal?
Enable timesheets individually
Enable timesheets in bulk
How to manage timesheets inside a Deal?
Add time sheets in bulk
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Deals in Recruit CRM help you manage contract placements by bringing associated jobs, candidates, and timesheets together in one place. You can link Contract and Contract to Permanent jobs to Deals, automatically associate placed candidates, enable timesheets, and manage timesheet activities directly from the Deal. This feature is useful when you want to: Track contract placements and associated contractors in one place. Link Contract or Contract to Permanent jobs with Deals. Automatically associate placed candidates with a Deal. Create and manage timesheets directly from a Deal. Perform bulk actions without opening each contractor's profile individually. Please note: This feature is currently available in Beta and can be enabled upon request. Please contact your Account Manager to have it enabled for your account. How to associate a Job with a Deal? Navigate to Deals , open the required Deal, and click the Pencil icon to edit it. Under Related With , select the Company . Once selected, the Contact field is automatically populated with the associated contact. Select the Job you want to associate with the Deal. Only jobs linked to the selected company will appear in the dropdown. Click Submit to save your changes. For Contract and Contract-to-Permanent jobs, all placed candidates associated with the linked job are automatically added to the Deal. Candidates aren't automatically associated with other job types. How to associate additional candidates with a Deal? You can manually add additional candidates to a Deal when needed. Open the Deal and click the Pencil icon. Under Related With , search for and select the candidate in the Candidate field, then click Submit . If the candidate is assigned to a job linked to the Deal, they will appear under that associated job. Otherwise, they will appear under Not Associated Candidates . How to enable timesheets from a Deal? You can enable timesheets for candidates directly from the Deal, either individually or in bulk. Please note: Timesheets can only be enabled for Contract and Contract-to-Permanent jobs. Enable timesheets individually Open the required Deal and expand the job under Related Candidates to view its associated candidates. Click the Timesheet icon for the required candidate. Configure the required timesheet settings, such as the pay rate, bill rate, and timesheet approver, then click Enable . Enable timesheets in bulk Under Related Candidates , select the required candidates or use the checkbox beside the job name to select all candidates associated with that job. Click Enable Timesheet . Configure the required timesheet settings and click Enable to enable timesheets for all selected candidates. Please note: Timesheets cannot be enabled for candidates under Not Associated Candidates because they aren't linked to a job. Bulk enablement is also unavailable when the selected candidates belong to different jobs. Which timesheets are visible in a Deal? Timesheets appear under the Deal's Timesheets section when the candidate has timesheets enabled, is linked to the Deal, and is assigned to a job that is also associated with the Deal. Timesheets for candidates under Not Associated Candidates aren't displayed in this section. How to manage timesheets inside a Deal? The Timesheets section allows you to create timesheets in bulk and manage existing timesheets directly from the Deal. Add time sheets in bulk Open the Timesheets section of the Deal and click + Add Timesheets . Select the Job , Candidates , and Timesheet Period . Only jobs associated with the Deal are available for selection. The first selected candidate is used as the reference for eligibility. Other candidates can be selected only when they have the same timesheet frequency, start of the week or month, duration, and matching timesheet rules. If a timesheet period has already been added for any selected contractor, that period will no longer be available for selection. Click Add to create the timesheets. View and manage individual timesheets Click the Timesheet Period to view the individual timesheets and perform actions such as adding time, submitting, approving, rejecting, or editing timesheets. Delete timesheets in bulk Select the required timesheets or use the bulk checkbox to select all available timesheets, then click Delete . Please note: Approved timesheets cannot be deleted. Troubleshooting Problem: I can't select a Timesheet Period. Likely Cause: A timesheet for that period has already been created for one of the selected contractors. What to Check: Review the existing timesheets for the selected contractors. Resolution: Select a Timesheet Period that hasn't already been added for any selected contractor. Problem: I can't delete a timesheet. Likely Cause: The timesheet has already been approved. What to Check: Review the current timesheet status. Resolution: Approved timesheets cannot be deleted. FAQs 1. Are placed candidates automatically associated with a Deal? Yes. Placed candidates are automatically associated when the linked Job Type is Contract or Contract to Permanent. 2. Which candidates can be selected when adding timesheets in bulk? Candidates must have matching timesheet frequency, start of the week or month, duration, and timesheet rules. The first selected candidate is used as the reference. Conclusion Deals for Contract Staffing provide a centralized way to manage contract jobs, candidates, and timesheets in Recruit CRM. By associating eligible jobs and contractors with Deals, you can enable timesheets, create timesheets in bulk, manage individual entries, and perform bulk actions more efficiently. t: Track the Source of Applicants from Multiple Platforms Using the Job Application URL/Talent Pool Page (New UI)
s: This article will tell you how you can track the source of your applicants who apply through the Job Application URL/Talent Pool Page that you share!
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Track Candidate Sources Using a Job Application URL
Track Candidate Sources Using a Talent Pool Page URL
Troubleshooting
Problem: The Source field is not showing the expected platform name for new candidates.
FAQs
Do I need separate URLs for each platform?
Will this update the Source field for candidates who already applied?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? This feature allows you to track where candidates are applying from when they use a Recruit CRM Job Application form or Talent Pool Page . By adding a simple source parameter to the URL before sharing it on external platforms, Recruit CRM automatically captures that source and stores it in the candidate's Source field when they apply. This makes it easy to identify which platforms and channels are driving applications, helping you measure the effectiveness of your recruitment efforts and make better sourcing decisions. Use this feature when: • You share Recruit CRM job application links on platforms such as LinkedIn, job boards, social media, or other external websites. • You want to track which platforms generate the most candidate applications. • You need to filter and report on candidates based on where they applied from. • You manage a talent pool page and want to measure the performance of different traffic sources and sharing channels. Track Candidate Sources Using a Job Application URL You can track where candidates are applying from by adding a source parameter to your job application URL before sharing it on external platforms. For example, if you want to track candidates applying through LinkedIn, you can modify the job application URL to capture LinkedIn as the source. Follow these steps: Open the job you want to share in Recruit CRM and copy the Job Application URL . Add ?source=LinkedIn to the end of the URL. ​ Example: Original URL: https://jobs.yourcompany.com/job/software-engineer Modified URL: https://jobs.yourcompany.com/job/software-engineer?source=LinkedIn ​ 3. Share the modified URL on LinkedIn along with your job post. 4. When a candidate applies through this link, Recruit CRM automatically records LinkedIn in the candidate's Source field. You can use the same approach for any platform by replacing the value after source= with the desired source name. Examples: • ?source=Facebook • ?source=Indeed • ?source=Website • ?source=Referral • ?source=Twitter Once applications start coming in, you can use Advanced Search in Recruit CRM to filter candidates by the Source field and analyze which platforms are generating the most applications. 📌 Please Note The parameter must use the word source in lowercase. For example, use ?source=LinkedIn and not ?Source=LinkedIn . Track Candidate Sources Using a Talent Pool Page URL If you want to track the source of candidates who join your database through a Talent Pool Page, you can use the same source-tracking method described above. Follow the steps below to add a source parameter to your Talent Pool Page URL before sharing it. 1. Navigate to Admin Settings and open the Talent Pool Page Settings , next click on the 'Integrate Talent Pool' tab and copy the Talent Pool Page Link. 2. Append the appropriate source parameter to the URL before sharing it. Example: https://jobs.yourcompany.com/talent-pool?source=LinkedIn 3. Share the modified URL on the desired platform. Candidates who submit their profiles through the modified Talent Pool Page URL will have the specified source captured automatically in Recruit CRM. Troubleshooting Problem: The Source field is not showing the expected platform name for new candidates. Likely cause: The URL parameter was not added correctly or source is not in lowercase. What to check: Confirm the URL contains ?source= followed by the platform name and verify that source is written exactly in lowercase (not Source or SOURCE ). Resolution: Correct the URL to use ?source=PlatformName with source in lowercase, then reshare the updated link. FAQs Do I need separate URLs for each platform? Yes. To distinguish between platforms, create a unique URL for each one by changing the value after ?source= and then share that specific link on that platform. Will this update the Source field for candidates who already applied? No. The Source parameter only applies to candidates who apply after you start using the modified URL. It does not retroactively update existing candidates. Where can I see and use the Source information? You can view the Source field on candidate records and use the Source field in Advanced Search to filter and track applications from a specific platform. Conclusion: Source tracking helps you understand where your candidates are coming from by capturing the platform or channel used to access your job application or Talent Pool links. By simply adding a source parameter to the URL before sharing it, you can accurately track candidate origins, measure the effectiveness of different sourcing channels, and use Recruit CRM's filtering and reporting capabilities to make more informed recruitment decisions. t: Tracking Placed Candidates in Recruit CRM
s: Learn how to create, filter, and manage placement records while avoiding duplicates in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Where to view placements
How to create Placements
Option 1: From the candidate profile
Option 2: From the Job Details page
Option 3: From the candidate List or Kanban view
Pre-filled placement fields
How to create custom fields for placements?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Placements feature in Recruit CRM helps you track candidates who have been successfully placed into specific jobs at specific companies. Each placement record brings together candidate, company, contact, job, and deal information in one place, making it easier to manage placements throughout the recruitment process. Use this feature when: You want to track candidates who have been successfully placed into jobs for specific companies. You need to create placements from candidate profiles, job pipelines, list views, or Kanban views with key details automatically pre-filled. You want to prevent duplicate placement records for the same candidate and job. You need to filter, group, search, or bulk manage placement records for reporting, invoicing, or day-to-day operations. You want to add custom fields to capture placement-specific information required by your recruitment process. With placements, Recruit CRM helps reduce manual work, maintain accurate placement records, and efficiently manage placement data using filters, grouping, custom fields, and bulk actions. 📋 Where to view placements You can see all your placements on the Placements list page: ✨ How to create Placements A placement is created when you update a candidate's hiring stage and select the Create Placement option. Option 1: From the candidate profile Open the relevant Candidate profile. Go to the Assigned Jobs tab to view all jobs assigned to the candidate. Click the candidate's current Hiring Stage for the relevant job. Select the appropriate hiring stage from the dropdown. Select the Create Placement checkbox. ​ Submit the stage update to create the placement. Option 2: From the Job Details page Open the relevant Job . Navigate to the Job Details page. Scroll down to the Candidate Pipeline . Click the candidate's current Hiring Stage . Select the appropriate hiring stage from the dropdown. Select the Create Placement checkbox. Save the stage update to create the placement. When marking a candidate as Placed, you will have an option to update the candidate's current organization and Job Title using the "Update Candidate's Current Organization and Job Title" checkbox. Checking it lets you edit the pre-filled job title (in case it needs to differ from the job's own title) before submitting, so both the candidate's organization and title update together in one step. Option 3: From the candidate List or Kanban view You can also create placements while updating hiring stages from the candidate List View or Kanban View within a job. From the List View Open the relevant job and click View All Candidates . Switch to List View , if required. Click the candidate's current Hiring Stage . Select the new hiring stage. Select the Create Placement checkbox. Save the update. From the Kanban View Open the relevant job and click on View All Candidates and switch to Kanban View . Drag and drop the candidate card to the appropriate hiring stage. In the confirmation dialog, ensure the Create Placement checkbox is selected. Confirm the stage change to create the placement. Pre-filled placement fields When a placement is created from a candidate profile or a job, Recruit CRM automatically populates the following fields in the placement form: Candidate Company Contact Job This reduces manual data entry and helps create placement records more quickly and accurately. 🛠️ How to create custom fields for placements? If your recruitment process requires additional placement information, you can create custom placement fields to capture it. Open Admin Settings . Under Data Customization , select Placement Fields . Add custom fields as needed to store additional placement details, such as placement terms, commission details, or internal notes. Turn on the Visible toggle for each custom field you want to display on the placement form. Once enabled, the selected custom fields will appear on the placement form whenever a new placement is created. Click here to learn how to add custom fields for placements! 🏷️ How to tag entities on placements You can tag different types of entities (like Users, Companies, or Jobs) using the Entity Type custom fields . Click here to learn how to create Entity type custom fields! 🔍 How to filter placements Use filters to quickly find placement records based on specific criteria. Open the Placements page. Click Add Filters . Select the field you want to filter by, such as: Candidate Company Contact Job Deal Placement ID Currency Created On Created By Configure the required filter conditions. Click Apply to view the matching placement records. ​ Applied filter fields appear as separate columns, making it easier to scan, sort, and manage placement records. You can also use Boolean Search in the search bar to find placements using keywords and logical operators such as AND , OR , and NOT . ​ Group placements The Group By option helps organize placement records based on related information. On the Placements page, click Group By . Select how you want to group the records: Jobs Deals Companies Contacts The placement list is automatically organized based on your selection, making it easier to review related placement records. ✅ How to identify if a placement already exists Recruit CRM helps prevent duplicate placement records by displaying a placement indicator. In the job pipeline, look for the Placement indicator. If a placement already exists for the candidate and job, the indicator appears as an active icon. If no placement exists, the indicator appears in gray . No duplicate entries are allowed for a placement. If you need to make changes, you can update the existing placement record instead of creating a new one. 📦 Bulk actions on placements Archiving placements Select the placements you want to archive. Then click on the Archive button: To view archived placements, click on the Quick View button → Archived : Exporting placements You can select the placements you want to export, then click on the Export button. After that, you can select the fields you want to export and click on the Export button to download them as a CSV file. Deleting placements After selecting the placements you want to delete, click on the Delete button. Confirm the deletion by clicking on the Delete button. Please note that this is an irreversible action. Creating Invoice After selecting the placements you want to create invoice for, Click on the Create Invoice button. Please note that placements from different companies/jobs can't be invoiced together in bulk. They can only be made for the same company/job. Bulk Updating Fields After selecting the placements you want to update the fields for, Click on the Update Fields button. Choose the field that you want to update and click on Update Field to save the changes. Customize Bulk Actions You can customize the bulk actions visible at the top of the placements list view. Click on More → Customize Bulk Actions. You can drag the fields to reorder the arrangement. 🔑 Role access for placements 1. By default, only the account owner and admins have access to view and create placements. ​ 2. On the business plan , you can grant access to view, create, edit and delete placements to users on custom roles as well. Troubleshooting Problem: I cannot see the Placements tab or any placements Likely cause: You do not have permission to view placements. What to check: Confirm your role and plan with Account owner. Resolution: An account owner or Admin should grant you access. On the Business plan, they can use custom roles to allow view access to placements. Problem: I changed a hiring stage but no placement was created Likely cause: The Create Placement checkbox was not ticked when updating the hiring stage. What to check: Review the last stage change and confirm whether the checkbox was selected. Resolution: Change the hiring stage again and ensure the Create Placement box is checked, or manually create a new placement from the candidate or job. Problem: My custom placement fields are not visible on the placement form Likely cause: The visibility toggle for the custom fields is turned off. What to check: In Admin settings → Data Customization → Placement Fields , verify that the toggle for each custom field is enabled. Resolution: Turn on the visibility toggle for any field you want to appear on the placement form. ❓FAQs Q1. What is the Entity Type field for? b: Placements help you keep track of candidates placed in specific jobs under specific companies. Recruit CRM makes this easier by giving you simple ways to filter, update, and avoid duplicate placements. 📋 Where to view placements You can see all your placements on the Placements list page: ⚙️ Customize your Placement list view You can customize the Placement list view by selecting which fields are displayed and arranging them in your preferred order. This helps you focus on the information that matters most to you. ​ Steps to customize the view: Click on the 'Show/Hide Columns' button at the top right corner of the page. ​ Select the fields you want to display and deselect the ones you don’t need. Arrange the fields in your preferred order by dragging and arranging the list. Click 'Apply' to save your changes. ​ ✨ How to create Placements Whenever you update a candidate’s hiring stage, you’ll get the option to create a Placement. Option 1: From within the candidate's profile: Go to the candidate's profile and click on the Assigned Jobs tab. This will have a list of jobs that the candidate has been assigned to: Click on the hiring stage of the candidate and you will get a drop-down menu of the stages you created like Shortlisted, Assigned, Rejected, and many more. After selecting the appropriate stage, ensure to select the 'Create Placement' checkbox for creating a placement: Option 2: From within Jobs ​Go to the Job details page and open the Candidate Pipeline tab. This will have a list of candidates assigned to the job: Click on the Hiring stage for the candidate - you will get a drop-down menu of the different stages like Shortlisted, Assigned, Rejected, and many more. You can select the appropriate stage, make sure to tick the 'Create Placement' checkbox for creating a placement: When marking a candidate as Placed, you will have an option to update the candidate's current organization and Job Title using the "Update Candidate's Current Organization and Job Title" checkbox. Checking it lets you edit the pre-filled job title (in case it needs to differ from the job's own title) before submitting, so both the candidate's organization and title update together in one step. You can also change the hiring stages on the “List view” and “Kanban view” of candidates within a job. To do that click on the blue "View All" button: Now on the List View, you can click on individual hiring stages and update it, and make sure to select the 'Create Placement' checkbox for creating a placement: On the Kanban board view, you can simply drag and drop the candidate across the hiring stages and select the 'Create Placement' checkbox for creating a placement. Note: The 'Create Placement' checkbox will remain disabled when you are updating the hiring stage of candidates in bulk. That's about it! ✍️ Pre-filling placement form fields When you create a new placement from a job or candidate profile, the system will automatically pre-fill the Candidate, Company Contact, and Job fields. This saves time and reduces manual work. 🛠️ How to create custom fields for placements? If you have specific requirements, you can include custom 'Placement' fields to store additional details as needed. This can be done from the Placement Fields page . Click here to learn how to add custom fields for placements! To make custom fields show on the Placement form, ensure to toggle them 'ON' as visible on the placement fields page . 🏷️ How to tag entities on placements You can tag different types of entities (like Users, Companies, or Jobs) using the Entity Type custom fields . Boolean Search You can use Boolean search to quickly find specific placements by applying keywords and conditions to narrow down your results. ​ Grouping Placements To make placement tracking more organized, you can use the Group By option to view placements based on related records. Steps to group placements: Click on Group By at the top right of the Placement list page. Select how you want to group placements (Jobs, Deals, Companies, or Contacts). The list will automatically organize placements into groups based on your selection, making it easier to review related records. ​ ✅ How to identify if a placement already exists A Green button is displayed when a placement has already been created, helping you avoid creating duplicates. t: Transferring ownership of records
s: This article will help you transfer ownership of records from active or deactivated users to other users on your team.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
How to transfer the ownership of records in Recruit CRM?
Troubleshooting
Problem: You are unable to access the transfer option.
FAQs
Can I transfer records from a deactivated user?
How can I quickly find a specific user to transfer records from?
What happens after I click Submit on the transfer screen?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Transfer Ownership feature allows you to transfer record ownership from one user to another within Recruit CRM. This helps ensure that important records are actively managed and assigned to the appropriate team member when users leave the organization, are deactivated, change roles, or when teams are being restructured. Use this feature when: • A team member leaves your organization and their records need to be reassigned. • A user is deactivated, and you want their records transferred to an active user. • You are restructuring teams and need to consolidate records under a different owner. • You want to maintain continuity and ensure all records have an active owner responsible for managing them. ↔️ How to transfer the ownership of records in Recruit CRM? Follow the steps below to transfer records from one user to another in Recruit CRM: Navigate to Admin Settings and under Account Management , click Users . Locate the user whose records you want to transfer. • You can scroll through the user list • Filter users by Active or Deactivated status • Use the search bar to quickly find a user by name Once you have found the user, click the Pencil option next to their profile. On the Edit User tab, click on the Transfer button at the bottom right corner of the tab. On the transfer screen, select the user who should become the new owner of the records. Review your selection and click Submit . Once the transfer is completed successfully, a confirmation message will be displayed. After the transfer is complete, all records owned by the original user will be reassigned to the selected user, ensuring continued ownership and management of those records. Troubleshooting Problem: You are unable to access the transfer option. Likely cause: You may not be in the correct section or may not have access to Admin Settings. What to check: •Confirm you are in Admin Settings > Users under Account Management . •Confirm you have the necessary access level to view and manage users. ​ Resolution: •Navigate to the correct area and locate the user again. •If you still cannot see the transfer option, contact your account owner or administrator for appropriate access. FAQs Can I transfer records from a deactivated user? Yes. You can filter users by activated or deactivated status and then transfer records from either type of user. How can I quickly find a specific user to transfer records from? Use the search bar on the Users page and type the user’s name, or apply filters based on their activated or deactivated status. What happens after I click Submit on the transfer screen? After you select the target user and click Submit , the records owned by the original user are reassigned to the user you selected. Do I need to reactivate a user to transfer their records? No. You can transfer records from users regardless of whether they are active or deactivated by using the status filters. Conclusion: Transferring ownership of records in Recruit CRM helps you manage team changes without losing track of important data. t: Troubleshooting Speed Issues with Recruit CRM.
s: This article will help you troubleshoot the speed issue
h: Perform the following troubleshooting steps when:
1. Clear your Application Storage
2. Clear your DNS cache
FAQs
Do I need any special permissions to follow these steps?
Do I need to reload the page after clearing site data?
Conclusion:
b: Perform the following troubleshooting steps when: Recruit CRM pages are taking a long time to load. You are not able to click on a button in Recruit CRM. Parts of the Recruit CRM interface stop responding. Recruit CRM data does not appear or only loads partially. 1. Clear your Application Storage 1. Right-click anywhere on the Recruit CRM page and select the option labeled “Inspect” from the context menu. ​ 2.In the developer tools panel that appears, click on the tab labeled “Application.” ​ 3. In the left-hand panel inside the Application tab, locate and click on “Storage.” In the main area on the right side, find the “Clear site data” button and click the “Clear site data” button. 4. Reload or refresh the Recruit CRM page in your browser. 2. Clear your DNS cache 1. For MacOS Launch the "Terminal" app on your Mac system. You can open it using Command + Space and type "Terminal" in the search bar Once the Terminal is open, enter the following command ​ sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder You'll be asked to enter the password, it is the same password that you use to login to your computer This will flush the DNS cache. You can now visit app.recruitcrm.io to get the latest DNS information. 2. For Windows: First, you need to click on the start button and select the CMD (command prompt) tool. This will launch a command prompt window. Inside it, you need to enter the following text: ​ ipconfig /flushdns Hit the Enter button to execute the command and Windows will flush the DNS cache. You can now resume visiting app.recruitcrm.io to fetch the updated DNS information. c. For Google Chrome Browser First, you need to enter the following address in your browser’s address bar and press enter on your keyboard. ​ chrome://net-internals/#dns This will load Chrome’s net internal settings page. From here you need to click on the ‘Clear host cache' button, and Chrome will clear up its DNS cache FAQs Do I need any special permissions to follow these steps? You only need access to your own browser and the ability to open the developer tools using the Inspect option. Do I need to reload the page after clearing site data? Yes. After you click the Clear site data button, you should reload or refresh the Recruit CRM website so it can load fresh data. Conclusion: Clearing application storage through your browser’s developer tools is a quick way to resolve many speed and responsiveness issues in Recruit CRM. If you still experience problems after following these steps, consider reaching out to Recruit CRM support for further assistance. t: Turning Off Email Reminders
s: This article explains how to turn off email reminders for tasks and meetings, and how to stop daily email reports in Recruit CRM.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Turn Off Email Reminders for Tasks and Meetings
Turn Off the Daily Email Report
Understanding the Daily Email Report:
FAQs
What is the daily email report in Recruit CRM?
Who receives the daily email report by default?
Do these settings affect other users’ reminders or reports?
b: What this feature does and when to use it? Notification Settings allow you to control which email notifications Recruit CRM sends to you. From your profile settings, you can choose whether to receive email reminders for tasks and meetings, as well as the daily applications report that summarizes applications received within the last 24 hours. When these settings are turned off, Recruit CRM stops sending the corresponding email notifications to your inbox while the underlying tasks, meetings, and application data remain available within the platform. Use this feature when: • You do not want to receive email reminders for tasks/meetings in Recruit CRM. • You do not want to receive the daily applications summary email. Turn Off Email Reminders for Tasks and Meetings If you no longer want to receive email reminders for your tasks, meetings, or both: Click your Profile icon in the top-right corner of Recruit CRM and select Profile . Locate the Notification Settings section on the right side of the page. Turn off the relevant toggle(s): • Tasks – Stops email reminders for tasks. • Meetings – Stops email reminders for scheduled meetings. You can disable either notification type individually or turn off both, depending on your preference. Turn Off the Daily Email Report The Daily Email Report is a report you'll receive every morning between 8-10 am, essentially a list of all your website, job boards, and talent pool applications/ Recruit CRM profile submissions from the last 24 hours. To stop receiving this report: Go to Profile → Notification Settings . Locate the Daily Email Report toggle. Turn the toggle OFF . Understanding the Daily Email Report: When enabled: Only the account owners and admins receive the daily email reports for ALL the website, job boards, and talent pool applicants when the toggle is turned ON from their respective profile settings. Users other than the account owner and admins will get the email reports for all the applicants that apply to the jobs they own OR are collaborator on. Once the toggle is turned off, Recruit CRM will stop sending the daily report email. FAQs What is the daily email report in Recruit CRM? The daily email report is an email sent every morning between 8 to 10 AM, listing all website, job board, and talent pool applications or Recruit CRM profile submissions from the last 24 hours. Who receives the daily email report by default? Account owners and admins receive daily email reports for all website, job board, and talent pool applicants when the toggle is turned on in their profile. Other users receive reports only for applicants to jobs they own or are collaborators on. Do these settings affect other users’ reminders or reports? No. The toggles in your profile’s Notification Settings affect only your own email reminders and daily email reports. Will turning off the daily email report delete any application data? No. Turning off the daily email report only stops the summary email. All applications remain available inside Recruit CRM. Conclusion: You can control your inbox by adjusting task reminders, meeting reminders, and the daily email report directly from your profile’s Notification Settings in Recruit CRM. Happy Recruiting! t: Understanding bulk email limits in Recruit CRM
s: This article explains how bulk email (email shot) limits work in Recruit CRM and how external email service provider restrictions affect your sending.
h: Limits on bulk emailing 🔍
How Recruit CRM sends bulk emails
Recommendations from Recruit CRM 🤔
FAQs
Why shouldn’t I send to all 500 recipients at once?
What batch size does Recruit CRM recommend for bulk emails?
How long should I wait between bulk email batches?
Conclusion:
b: Recruit CRM offers a bulk emailing/email shot option so you can send out bulk emails to your candidates/contacts in a single shot. Click here to learn how to bulk-email your candidates and contacts Limits on bulk emailing 🔍 While Recruit CRM allows you to send an email shot to 500 candidates/contacts at a time, it is important to understand that most email service providers (like Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, etc.) impose certain restrictions on the number or volume of emails that can be sent in a single batch AND/OR within a day . ​ Sending bulk emails beyond these limits may result in temporary account suspension and the classification of your emails as spam. Here are a few limits set by different email providers for your reference: Email limits in Google Workspace Sending limits on Outlook.com Limitation set by Sendgrid Limitations set by Mailchimp Limits on sending email in Yahoo Mail 📌 How Recruit CRM sends bulk emails To help improve email deliverability and reduce the risk of sender accounts being restricted, Recruit CRM sends bulk emails with a randomized delay of 5–10 seconds between each email instead of using a fixed interval. ​ This creates a more natural sending pattern, which helps prevent email providers such as Microsoft Outlook and Office 365 from identifying bulk email campaigns as automated activity. ​ ​ Please note: Because of this randomized delay, bulk email campaigns may take slightly longer to complete. However, this safeguard helps protect your account reputation and improves overall email deliverability. Recommendations from Recruit CRM 🤔 While you can choose up to 500 records at a time (in Recruit CRM) to email at once, it's not recommended to send emails to a large number of recipients all at once. ​ It's advisable to keep your email batches relatively small, typically no more than 30 to 50 emails at a time, based on the restrictions set by your email service providers. After sending each batch, we recommend waiting 20 to 30 minutes before sending the next batch. Recruit CRM also spaces individual emails within a bulk campaign using a randomized 5–10 second delay to create a more natural sending pattern and help improve email deliverability. This strategy can lower the risk of your email account being flagged by your service provider, thus reducing the chances of these emails landing in the spam folder of your candidates or contacts. 🤔FAQs Why shouldn’t I send to all 500 recipients at once? Most email service providers (like Gmail, Outlook, and Yahoo) have their own sending limits. Sending to a very large number of recipients in a single batch can trigger these limits, cause temporary account suspension, or lead to your emails being marked as spam. What batch size does Recruit CRM recommend for bulk emails? It is advisable to keep your email batches relatively small, typically no more than 30–50 emails at a time, based on the restrictions set by your email service provider. How long should I wait between bulk email batches? After sending each batch, it is recommended to wait for a 20–30 minute interval before sending the next set of emails. Conclusion: By understanding Recruit CRM’s bulk email capacity and your email provider’s limits, you can plan safe, effective email shots that reach candidates and contacts. Hope this helps! t: Understanding Recruit CRM Credits
s: Learn how Recruit CRM Credits work, including monthly credit allocation, supported features, credit consumption order, and plan-wise limits.
h: What this feature does:
Monthly Complimentary Credits
Where can Recruit CRM Credits be used?
How to check your Recruit CRM Credits
How are credits consumed?
Frequently Asked Questions
Which plans receive complimentary Recruit CRM Credits?
Which features use Recruit CRM Credits?
b: Please note: This feature is currently in Beta and will be gradually rolled out to all users. What this feature does: Recruit CRM Credits provide a shared credit balance that can be used across multiple credit-based features within Recruit CRM, including: • Data Enrichment. • Job Posting via VONQ. • Calling and SMS. • AI Job Candidate Matching • AI Sourcing • Job Change Alerts • Backdoor Hiring Alerts • AI Edits in the Resume Formatting Agent Depending on your subscription plan, you'll receive a monthly allocation of complimentary credits that can be used across supported features. This gives you the flexibility to use your monthly credits where they're most valuable for your recruitment workflow. Monthly Complimentary Credits Business and Pro plan users receive complimentary Recruit CRM Credits every month based on the number of purchased user licenses on your account. Plan Approximate Monthly Credit Value Pro Approximately 10% of your monthly subscription fee Business Approximately 15% of your monthly subscription fee 📌 Please note: The value of complimentary credits is calculated based on your subscription plan and the number of active user licenses on your account. ​ Where can Recruit CRM Credits be used? Your Recruit CRM Credits can be used across several features. The number of credits deducted depends on the feature and the action you perform. Data Enrichment: 1 to 5 credits, depending on the type of data enriched. Job Posting via VONQ: 25 credits per job posting. Calling and SMS: Credits are deducted based on the existing calling and SMS pricing. AI Sourcing: Filter-based search: 1 credit per results page (up to 100 results). Natural language search: 3 credits per results page (up to 100 results). Job-based search: 3 credits per results page (up to 100 results). AI Job Candidate Matching: Matching: 3 credits per results page (up to 100 results) Refining criteria: Re-running the search after refining the matching criteria consumes 3 credits again. Refreshing matches: 2 credits when the refresh finds new matching candidates. Job Change Alerts: 1 credit per update, charged when you accept the job change update. Backdoor Hiring Alerts: 5 credits per unlocked record from the Backdoor Hiring report. ​ How to check your Recruit CRM Credits Here is how you can access your Credits within Recruit CRM: Navigate to Admin Settings and click on Data Enrichment . ​ From this page, you can: • View your total available credits . • Track your credit usage . • Purchase additional credits whenever required. ​ 📌 Please note: Although Recruit CRM Credits can be used across multiple features, they are currently displayed and managed from the Data Enrichment section in Admin Settings . How are credits consumed? When you use a credit-based feature, Recruit CRM automatically consumes credits in the following order: Complimentary Recruit CRM Credits Purchased Subscription Credits Remaining Credits in your account This ensures your complimentary monthly allocation is always used first before any purchased credits. Frequently Asked Questions Which plans receive complimentary Recruit CRM Credits? Complimentary Recruit CRM Credits are currently available for Pro and Business plans. Which features use Recruit CRM Credits? Recruit CRM Credits can be used for: • Data Enrichment. • Job Posting via VONQ. • Calling and SMS. • AI Job Candidate Matching • AI Sourcing • Job Change Alerts • Backdoor Hiring Alerts Do my complimentary credits depend on the number of users? Yes. Complimentary credits are allocated per purchased user license , so your total monthly credit allocation increases with the number of users on your account. In what order are credits consumed? Recruit CRM first uses your complimentary monthly credits, followed by any purchased subscription credits, and then any remaining credits available in your account. Conclusion: Recruit CRM Credits provide a flexible way to use multiple AI, enrichment, communication, and job advertising features from a shared monthly credit balance. By understanding how credits are allocated and consumed, you can make the most of your available credits across the platform. t: Understanding the Reports and Statistics on the Dashboard
s: This article will help you understand how the different reports and statistics work on the dashboard.
h: What this feature does and when to use it?
Dashboard Reports & Statistics
1. Total Candidates Statistics
2. Total Deals Statistics
3. Total Job Statistics
4. Tasks & Meetings
5. Candidate Pipeline By Jobs
6. Candidate Pipeline By Company
b: What this feature does and when to use it? The Dashboard in Recruit CRM provides a centralized view of your recruitment activities through 11 interactive reports , giving you quick insights into your hiring pipeline, deals, jobs, tasks, meetings, and candidate activity. These reports help you monitor performance, identify trends, and stay on top of your recruitment process without having to generate individual reports. Use this guide when you want to: • Get a high-level overview of your candidate hiring pipeline. • Track deal stages, pipeline value, and overall sales performance. • Monitor the status of your open, closed, and active jobs. • Stay updated on upcoming or overdue tasks and meetings. • Analyze candidate pipelines by job, company, candidate owner, or assigned recruiter. Each dashboard report provides a different perspective on your recruitment data, helping you quickly assess performance and make informed decisions. This article gives an overview of all the dashboard reports available in Recruit CRM, explains what each report represents, and helps you understand how the displayed statistics are calculated. 📊 Dashboard Reports & Statistics 1. Total Candidates Statistics The Total Candidates Statistics card provides a comprehensive overview of the entire candidate hiring pipeline. Whenever you click on any particular stage you'll be redirected to a list of candidates currently present in that stage. You will also get an option to select any particular job status or generate a report for all job statuses. Additionally, this card also provides an overview of the total number of candidates present within the system as well as the total assigned and unassigned candidates. You can click on the 'All Unassigned' and 'All Assigned' numbers to get a comprehensive list of candidates under each of the categories. ​ All Unassigned = Total number of candidates that are not assigned to any jobs. ​ All Assigned = Total number of candidates in every hiring stage across all jobs You will also be able to see all assigned candidates in Kanban View for specific stages, across all jobs. The "All Assigned Candidates" list, accessed from the Dashboard, the "Owner" field - you can add it as a column, filter by it, and include it in CSV exports, just like on other candidate list pages. When you click on a stage statistic on the Dashboard (e.g., "Sourced"), select candidates from that filtered list, and open "Update Candidate Stage," the Stage field pre-fills with that stage and shows it highlighted in the dropdown, instead of showing a blank field. 2. Total Deals Statistics The Total Deals Statistics report displays all deal stages, pipeline amounts, and provides us with the status of each deal. In addition to viewing the overall statistics, recruiters can also generate reports specific to individual team members or teams, allowing for more targeted analysis. 3. Total Job Statistics The Total Job Statistics provides an overview of the total number of jobs present under different job statuses. This report is useful for tracking the status of open jobs and identifying which ones may require additional attention. By reviewing this report, recruiters can prioritize their workload and ensure that they are making progress on each job opening. 4. Tasks & Meetings The Tasks & Meetings section in the Dashboard offers a convenient and comprehensive overview of upcoming and backlogged tasks and meetings. It provides detailed information such as titles, descriptions, related records, attendees, owners, and collaborators, allowing users to quickly grasp the key details of their activities. You can quickly edit or delete entries right from the Dashboard, keeping your records accurate. Additionally, the 'Export to CSV' button enables users to export tasks and meeting data, for analysis or sharing with your team. ​ 5. Candidate Pipeline By Jobs The Candidate Pipeline By Jobs depicts all jobs and the number of candidates in different stages of the recruitment process for each job. ​ In addition to viewing the overall statistics, the recruiters will also get an option to select any particular job status or generate a report for all job statuses. Recruiters can also generate reports specific to individual team members or teams, allowing for more targeted analysis. 6. Candidate Pipeline By Company The Candidate Pipeline By Company report displays all companies along with candidates/applicants in different stages of the jobs associated with each company. Through this report, the recruiters can better understand the performance of each company and make adjustments as needed. 7. Candidate Pipeline By Candidate Owner The Candidate Pipeline by Candidate Owner shows all the candidates added by different owners who are in different stages of the recruitment process. This report is useful for tracking the performance of individual recruiters and identifying potential areas of improvement. Recruiters can also generate reports specific to individual team members or teams present within the system. 8. Candidate Pipeline By Recruiter Assigned The Candidate Pipeline By Recruiter Assigned report displays the number of candidates that each recruiter has assigned to any job. 9. Candidate Lifecycle Report You can refer to the article below to learn more about the Candidate Lifecycle Report. Candidate Lifecycle Report 10. Team Performance Report You can refer to the following article to learn more about the Team Performance Report. Team Performance Report 11. Target Report You can refer to the following article to know more about the Target Report. Target Report 🖌️ Customizing the Dashboard Recruit CRM offers a customizable dashboard that enables users to prioritize reports by simply dragging and dropping them into place. Additionally, users have the flexibility to select which reports are displayed and which can be hidden. You can also select to either show or hide the checklist from the dashboard. Troubleshooting Problem: Dashboard layout does not show preferred reports Likely cause : Some reports may be hidden or arranged lower on the page. What to check: Review dashboard customization options to see which reports are enabled. Check the current positioning of each report card. Resolution: Enable any hidden reports you need. Drag and drop report cards to prioritize the most important ones at the top of the dashboard. ​ FAQ 🎯 How Can I Filter Candidates by Hiring Stage? You can filter your database to view candidates based on their hiring stage. Here’s how you can do it: Navigate to the Dashboard in Recruit CRM. On the left-hand side select the candidate statistics you want to view using the dropdown (All Candidates, Your Candidates, or Teammates’ Candidates). ​ Below this section, you will find all default and custom hiring stages, along with the number of candidates in each stage. ​ Click on any hiring stage and you will be redirected to a new page that displays the complete list of candidates in that specific stage. ​ From the list page, you can perform additional actions such as sending emails, updating fields, exporting records, and more. ​ What does “All Unassigned” mean in Total Candidate Statistics? “All Unassigned” is the total number of candidates that are not assigned to any jobs in the system. What does “All Assigned” mean in Total Candidate Statistics? “All Assigned” is the total number of candidates in every hiring stage across all jobs. Clicking this number opens a comprehensive list of all assigned candidates. Can I choose which reports appear on my dashboard? Yes. Recruit CRM offers a customizable dashboard where you can select which reports to display or hide and reorder them using drag and drop. You can also choose to show or hide the checklist. Conclusion The Recruit CRM dashboard brings together key reports and statistics so you can understand and manage your recruitment pipeline, deals, jobs, and activities in one place. Use the reports, filters, and customization options described here to tailor the dashboard to your workflow and quickly act on the insights it provides. t: Updating or Changing Your Recruit CRM Subscription/Account Plan
s: This article will help you easily make changes to your subscription plan
h: Switching Between the Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans
How billing works when switching plans?
Switching from Monthly to Annual plan
Switch from annual to monthly billing
Switch some of your seats to annual billing
FAQs
Q1. Can I move from annual to monthly billing by myself?
Conclusion:
b: Recruit CRM's subscription management lets you update your plan, and seat configuration as your business needs change. Whether you're upgrading from Pro to Business or to Enterprise , switching from monthly to annual billing, or using a combination of both, these settings can be managed directly from your account. ​ Please note: On the Pro Plan , only the Account Owner can make subscription changes. On the Business and Enterprise plans, other users can be granted this permission through Custom Roles . The sections below cover the most common subscription changes and explain how to complete each one. Switching Between the Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans Log in to your Recruit CRM account. Go to Admin Settings > Plans & Billing . From the left navigation panel, select Plans . Review your current subscription plan and the available Pro , Business , and Enterprise plans. If required, use the toggle at the top of the page to switch between Monthly and Annual billing to compare the available pricing and plans. Select the plan you want to switch to and follow the on-screen prompts to complete the change. How billing works when switching plans? When switching to a different plan: Charges for the new plan are calculated on a pro rata basis for the remaining days in your current billing cycle. The full cost of the new plan is charged when your subscription renews in the next billing cycle. Please note: If you downgrade your subscription: Business → Pro: You must remove any teams , custom roles , and custom fields exceeding the 15 custom field limit supported by the Pro Plan. You must also reduce your Sequences and XML Feeds, Custom Hiring Pipelines to 1 each , as the Pro Plan supports only 1 Sequence , 1 XML Feed and 1 Custom Hiring Pipeline . If your account exceeds the new 10,000 records per user limit, purchase Additional Records Limit add-ons or delete excess records. ​ ​ Enterprise → Business: You must adjust your records to match the 20,000 records per user limit on the Business Plan. If your account exceeds the new limit, purchase Additional Records Limit add-ons or delete excess records. ​ ​ Enterprise → Pro: You must remove the unsupported teams , custom roles , custom fields exceeding the 15 custom field limit, extra custom hiring pipelines (Pro Plan supports 1 custom hiring pipeline ), extra Sequences (Pro Plan supports 1 sequence ), and reduce your XML Feeds to 1 , as the Pro Plan supports only 1 XML Feed . If your account exceeds the new 10,000 records per user limit, purchase Additional Records Limit add-ons or delete excess records. Recruit CRM will prompt you to complete these changes before the downgrade can be applied. Switching from Monthly to Annual plan Log in to your Recruit CRM account. Go to Admin Settings > Plans & Billing . From the left navigation panel, make sure you are on the View Current Plan tab, then select Edit Current Plan . Choose Annual as your preferred billing cycle. Review the updated pricing and billing details. Confirm the change to update your subscription. Switch from annual to monthly billing If you want to change your subscription from annual to monthly billing, contact the Recruit CRM Support team using either of the following methods: Use the chatbot within Recruit CRM. Email the Support team at support@recruitcrm.io . Include your account details and mention that you would like to switch from annual to monthly billing. The Support team will guide you through the process and make the necessary changes. Please note: Your request must be submitted before your annual subscription renewal date . Once your annual subscription has renewed and payment has been processed, the billing cycle cannot be changed until the next renewal period. Switch some of your seats to annual billing Just like the option to switch between Monthly and Annual, you can now choose to add some of the seats to Annual while keeping some in Monthly. Login to your Recruit CRM account > Admin Settings > Plans & Billing > View Current Plan > Click on Edit Current Plan: Once on the page, ensure that the billing plan is selected to Annual (right-hand side), and choose the division of the seats between Monthly and Annual : Once you have selected the seats and divided them between Monthly and Annual , click on the review order to move on to the next page and pay for the upgrade. After each of the steps mentioned, here's how you can make a payment: Scroll to the bottom of the page and click on the Review order option to check the amount and proceed further with the payment. On the next page, you'd be asked to put in a card detail if you do not have a card on file, or change it if you wish to; and proceed further with making a payment with the charge being applied on the current transaction being made (as shown in the below image). Click on the Update Plan and Pay button once confirmed. FAQs Q1. Can I move from annual to monthly billing by myself? No. To move from an annual billing plan to a monthly billing plan, you must contact Recruit CRM support via chatbot or email. The request must be made before your annual subscription renewal date. Conclusion: Updating your Recruit CRM subscription plan, whether changing plan levels, or splitting seats between monthly and annual is managed from your account with clear prompts and pro-rata billing. If anything is unclear or you need help with a specific change, reach out through the in-app chat box and the support team will guide you through the process. t: Upgrading Your Account
s: This article will help you understand how the "account upgrade" process works in Recruit CRM.
h: Upgrading from the free trial to a paid plan
Accessing your signed contract
Upgrading from Pro to Business Plan
Troubleshooting
Problem: Cannot start the upgrade from free trial to a paid plan.
Problem: Pricing does not match expectations when changing billing cycle.
Problem: Unable to complete the upgrade because the contract is not signed.
FAQs
b: Ready to move beyond the Recruit CRM free trial or upgrade your existing subscription? Recruit CRM makes it easy to upgrade your account, choose the plan that best fits your team's needs, and manage your billing preferences. Use this feature when: You are upgrading from a Free Trial to a paid Recruit CRM plan. You want to upgrade from the Pro Plan to the Business Plan . The sections below walk through the different upgrade scenarios and explain how to complete each one. ​ Upgrading from the free trial to a paid plan Verify your registered email address by completing the verification process in your Recruit CRM account. ​ Here is how you can verify your email Once your email has been verified, start the upgrade process by either: Clicking the Upgrade Your Account button at the top right of your screen, or Navigating to Admin Settings → Plans & Billing → Upgrade Your Account . Choose your preferred billing cycle by switching between Monthly and Annual . The pricing will automatically update based on your selection. Then select the subscription plan you want to purchase ( Pro , Business , or Enterprise ). Once the plan type is selected, configure your subscription by: Selecting the required number of licenses . Adding Additional Record Limits , if required, using the + and − buttons. You can also choose to purchase the subscription with a combination of annual and monthly licenses. This article will guide you through the steps. Once you've finalized your subscription structure, click Review Order from the right-hand panel. ​ On the payment page: Enter your payment details. (Recruit CRM accepts both debit and credit cards.) Save your billing information. Review your purchase details carefully. ​ Accept the Recruit CRM Terms of Service by selecting the confirmation checkbox. ​ Before completing your purchase, review the subscription agreement. All new Recruit CRM customers are required to sign the contract before the subscription can be activated. ​ Create your signature by choosing one of the available options: Draw your signature. Type your signature. Upload your signature. Click Create , then Save to complete and store the signed agreement. ​ Click Pay to complete your purchase and upgrade your account. ​ Please read the contract and terms of service carefully before proceeding to sign. Accessing your signed contract You'll be able to view and download the history of your signed agreements on the tab 'View Current Plan' and in the 'Invoice & Subscription Agreement History' tab. Upgrading from Pro to Business Plan Log in to your Recruit CRM account and go to Admin Settings > Plans & Billings . From the left navigation panel, select Plans . Choose the Business Plan as your new subscription. Review your order, including the updated plan details and charges. Proceed to checkout and complete the payment to finalize the upgrade. Note: You will only be charged a pro-rated amount that will be automatically calculated for the remaining period of your billing cycle. In line with our policies, we don't provide upfront discounts. However, you can save up to 20% by opting for our annual plan. See what's included in the Business Plan Troubleshooting Problem: Cannot start the upgrade from free trial to a paid plan. Likely cause: Registered email address is not verified. ​ What to check: Confirm that you have completed the email verification steps in Recruit CRM. ​ Resolution: Verify your email address first, then use the Upgrade Your Account button or go to Admin Settings → Plans and Billings to restart the upgrade process. Problem: Pricing does not match expectations when changing billing cycle. Likely cause: Billing toggle is set to the wrong cycle (monthly vs annual). ​ What to check: Confirm whether the toggle is set to monthly or annual and note that prices update automatically. ​ Resolution: Switch the toggle to the intended billing cycle and review the updated prices before proceeding. Problem: Unable to complete the upgrade because the contract is not signed. Likely cause: Terms of service and contract have not been accepted and signed. ​ What to check: Ensure you have checked the box to agree to the terms of service and completed the signature step. ​ Resolution: Open the contract, read the terms, draw, type, or upload your signature, click Create , then Save , and proceed to payment. FAQs Which payment methods are accepted for upgrading my Recruit CRM account? Recruit CRM accepts both debit and credit cards for subscription payments. Can I choose between monthly and annual billing? Yes. You can switch the billing toggle between monthly and annual, and the pricing will automatically adjust according to your selection. How am I charged when upgrading from Pro to Business mid-cycle? When you upgrade from Pro to Business, you are charged a prorated amount that is automatically calculated for the remaining period of your current billing cycle. Are there upfront discounts available on plans? In line with the stated policies, Recruit CRM does not provide upfront discounts. However, you can save up to 20% by opting for an annual plan. Conclusion: Upgrading your Recruit CRM account involves verifying your email, choosing the right plan and billing cycle, configuring licenses and record limits, completing payment, and signing the required contract. How to cancel your Advanced Analytics Subscription

b: Before you begin: Advanced Analytics is an Enterprise plan feature which can also be added at an additional cost to Pro or Business plan subscriptions. On the Enterprise plan, Advanced Analytics is available on an opt-in basis and is not enabled by default. So if you would like Advanced Analytics to be enabled for your account, please feel free to reach out to your Account Manager, and we will be happy to assist you. 💰How to purchase Advanced Analytics Subscription 1. Navigate to the Advanced Analytics tab in the Reports section. 2. Click the 'Buy Advanced Analytics' subscription button. 3. You can select the plan you want and click ' Buy Advanced Analytics' subscription. ⬆️ How to upgrade your Advanced Analytics Subscription (Monthly to Yearly) Note : Only users on the Annual Recruit CRM subscription will be able to upgrade from a monthly to a yearly Advanced Analytics subscription. 1. Navigate to the Advanced Analytics tab in the Reports section. 2. Click the Edit Subscription button. 3. In the pop-up window, select the Edit Subscription option. 4. Select the Annual option for Advanced Analytics and proceed to pay the prorated amount by clicking the Buy Advanced Analytics button. ⬇️ How to downgrade your Advanced Analytics Subscription You will not be able to downgrade to the monthly plan from the yearly plan within the app. Please contact us using the chatbot or email us at support@recruitcrm.io so we can assist you with it. ❌ How to cancel your Advanced Analytics Subscription 1. Click on the 'Edit Subscription' button under the Advanced Analytics tab 2. Then click on the 'Cancel Subscription' option. You can cancel your Advanced Analytics subscription anytime, and your access to Advanced Analytics and all custom reporting will be revoked after the subscription end date. Note: All the user data and reports will be preserved for 30 days only in Advanced Analytics and after 30 days, all data of the account will be removed completely. Users can resume/re-purchase the subscription within 30 days and you will be able to see all your previously saved reports. But once the data is removed, users would need to re-create any/all reports they were using on Advanced Analytics again. FAQs Can I upgrade from a monthly to a yearly Advanced Analytics subscription? Yes, but only if you are on an annual Recruit CRM subscription. Can I downgrade from a yearly to a monthly Advanced Analytics plan inside the app? No. You cannot downgrade from a yearly to a monthly Advanced Analytics plan within the app. You need to contact Recruit CRM via the chatbot or email support@recruitcrm.io for assistance. s: This guide explains how to collect SMS consent in Recruit CRM for US-based texting and how to configure it inside Recruit CRM.
h: Why A2P 10DLC Registration Is Required

Required Disclosures in Consent Language
Approved Methods and ways to Collect SMS Consent
