b: US carriers require clear, intentional consent before you can send text messages. If you’re sending SMS to US numbers through Recruit CRM (powered by Twilio ), you must complete A2P 10DLC registration and comply with carrier consent rules; otherwise, your campaigns may be rejected, delayed, or suspended to prevent spam and protect consumers. Why A2P 10DLC Registration Is Required US carriers regulate application-to-person (A2P) messaging under the 10DLC framework. Any business sending SMS messages for recruitment communication must: Register their messaging campaign Clearly describe how consent is collected Provide compliant consent language Ensure users actively opt in before receiving messages Recruit CRM supports compliant consent collection, but it must be properly configured before submitting your registration form. Why Consent Is Required Under A2P 10DLC Consent means a clear, affirmative action by the recipient indicating they agree to receive SMS messages from your company for a stated purpose. To prevent rejection, Recruit CRM requires clients to configure compliant consent before submitting A2P registration details. Required Disclosures in Consent Language Your company name Purpose of messaging (recruitment / hiring communication) cross mark Don’t include your own name/ any brand’s name) Purpose of messaging (recruitment / hiring communication) That messages may be automated That messages are sent using Recruit CRM Message frequency (or “Message frequency may vary”) “Message and data rates may apply” Opt-out instructions (Reply STOP) Help instructions (Reply HELP) Links to: ​ Recruit CRM SMS Terms of Service Recruit CRM Privacy Policy ​ Why Recruit CRM Legal Links Must Be Included Because SMS messages are sent through Recruit CRM, carriers require that recipients are shown: Recruit CRM SMS Terms of Service Recruit CRM Privacy Policy Approved Methods and ways to Collect SMS Consent Recruit CRM supports two compliant methods for collecting consent from candidates. 1. Email-Based Consent With email-based consent: The candidate receives an email requesting confirmation. The user must actively click to accept SMS communication. Consent is recorded before any SMS is sent. This method provides strong audit documentation and is recommended where possible. How to Configure Email Consent: Navigate to Admin Settings and Open SMS Opt-in Settings Click on pencil icon to Edit and enter your approved SMS consent text and click save. Ensure that the consent text includes all required regulatory disclosures. ​ Example Consent Text ​By agreeing, you consent to receive automated SMS messages from {{Company Name}} related to recruitment and hiring communication. Messages are sent using Recruit CRM. Message frequency may vary. Message and data rates may apply. You can reply STOP to opt out at any time or HELP for assistance. Recruit CRM’s SMS Terms of Service are available at Terms of service | Recruit CRM and Privacy Policy can be found at Privacy policy | Recruit CRM . ​ Replace {{Company Name}} with your company’s name. Please Note: You can adjust the text to match your brand’s tone, but all required disclosures must stay included. Also, make sure to include Recruit CRM’s Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy links exactly as shown in the example. Click here to know how to obtain email based consent 2. Web Form / Checkbox Consent You can also collect consent through: Job Application Forms Talent Pool Forms Profile Update Request Forms For this method to be compliant: The SMS consent checkbox must be unchecked by default The user must manually select the checkbox The consent wording must be clearly visible Consent must be recorded only after form submission ​ To Enable SMS Consent in Forms Go to Admin Settings → Job Application Form (you can also configure Talent Pool or Profile Update Request Forms; here we’re using Job Application Form as an example). ​ Scroll to the bottom, enable the SMS Consent checkbox, click the pencil icon to add your compliant checkbox consent text and save. ​ Example Checkbox consent text By agreeing, you consent to receive automated SMS messages from {{Company Name}} related to recruitment and hiring communication. Messages are sent using Recruit CRM. Message frequency may vary. Message and data rates may apply. You can reply STOP to opt out at any time or HELP for assistance. Recruit CRM’s SMS Terms of Service are available at Terms of service | Recruit CRM and Privacy Policy can be found at Privacy policy | Recruit CRM . ​ The consent text configured in your account must exactly match the wording submitted in the A2P registration form. Updating SMS Terms In addition to SMS consent text, you must configure SMS Terms within Recruit CRM. ​ To update SMS Terms Consent text : ​ Go to Admin Settings → Job Application Form then locate SMS Terms and enter your compliant SMS Terms content and click Save. ​ Example SMS Terms text SMS Terms – {{Company Name}} By providing your phone number and opting in, you agree to receive SMS messages from {{Company Name}} related to recruitment and hiring opportunities. These messages may include job alerts, interview scheduling, application updates, and other employment-related communication. Messages may be sent using automated technology through our recruitment platform, Recruit CRM. Message Frequency: Message frequency may vary depending on your application activity and communication needs. Message & Data Rates: Message and data rates may apply based on your mobile carrier plan. How We Use Your Information: Your phone number will be used solely for recruitment-related communication. We do not sell or share your mobile number with third parties for marketing purposes. Opt-Out Instructions: You can opt out at any time by replying STOP to any message. After opting out, you will no longer receive SMS messages from us. Help Instructions: Reply HELP for assistance. Contact Information: {{Company Name}} {{Support Email or Phone Number}} Messaging services are provided through Recruit CRM. Recruit CRM’s SMS Terms of Service are available at Terms of service | Recruit CRM and Privacy Policy can be found at Privacy policy | Recruit CRM . Your SMS Terms must include: Description of the messaging term (recruitment communication) Types of messages candidates will receive Message frequency disclosure “Message and data rates may apply” statement Instructions to reply STOP to opt out Instructions to reply HELP for assistance Your company contact information Confirmation that user data will not be sold Click here to know how to obtain consent through external pages Branding & Form Visibility Requirements When collecting SMS consent via forms: Your company name must be clearly displayed Your company logo should appear on the form The form URL should reflect your company name where possible Carriers review these details to verify that consent is being collected by a legitimate business entity. Consent via Sms (Not Recommended for US Campaigns) SMS Keyword Opt-In will be deprecated soon, as guided by Twilio . ​ Please Note: Collecting consent via SMS (for example, asking users via SMS to reply START) is no longer considered compliant. This method should not be used. You must collect SMS consent using: Email-based consent Web form / checkbox consent Completing the A2P Registration Google Form The A2P 10DLC Registration Google Form is a compliance form that collects your business and consent details for US texting approval. This form is required for submitting your SMS campaign for carrier review under A2P 10DLC regulations. You need to submit your: Business Details, Authorised Person details, Address Details, Brand Details and Consent RElated details in the form. ​​Campaigns are reviewed based on the information submitted in this form. If the details are incomplete or inconsistent, the campaign may be rejected. ​ How to fill the Consent Details in the Google form After completing all consent configuration inside the product, you must fill the A2P 10DLC registration Google Form. t: Use AI to find candidate matches in Recruit CRM
s: This article explains how to use candidate-to-candidate AI matching in Recruit CRM to quickly find similar candidates based on an ideal profile.
h: What This Feature Does and when to use it?
Understanding the Matching Algorithm:
Before You Begin:
Step-by-Step Instructions
Method 1: Launch Matching from a Candidate Profile
Method 2: Launch Matching from a Job Profile
Understanding AI Match Analysis
Click here to learn more about the actions that can be performed on Matched Candidates.
b: What This Feature Does and when to use it? AI candidate-to-candidate matching in Recruit CRM helps you find ideal candidate matches by analyzing a reference candidate’s profile and searching for similar candidates across your candidate database. Once you identify a strong-fit candidate for a role, you can use AI to discover more candidates with similar skills, experience, education, location, languages, job titles, and industry background. This feature is especially useful when you want to: • Find more candidates similar to a strong-fit candidate already identified for a role. • Discover candidates based on overall profile similarity rather than keywords alone. ​ Note: This is a Business and Enterprise plan exclusive feature. However, users on the Pro plan can view up to 2 candidate matches to have an overview of the feature. Understanding the Matching Algorithm: AI Matching in Recruit CRM uses AI capabilities to perform bimetric scoring, a two-way matching algorithm based on holistic profiles rather than a string of keywords, to generate the match rate between two candidate profiles. ​ The bimetric scoring uses details available on the candidate's resume such as skills, experience, education, location, language, job titles, industry, etc. Candidates are ranked on a scale from 0 to 100, where a higher score indicates a stronger match. Before You Begin: Resume requirement: As the AI utilizes data from candidate resumes to identify matches, this feature is only available for the candidate profiles that have a resume uploaded to the default resume field . Data completeness: The more complete the reference candidate's profile, the more accurate the matching algorithm will be. Profiles with detailed resume information, skills, experience, education, and location produce better match results. The system will return up to 50 candidate matches ranked by match score. A match score of 100 represents the closest match; 0 represents no match. Step-by-Step Instructions Method 1: Launch Matching from a Candidate Profile Open the candidate profile you have identified as an ideal fit for the role. ​ Look for the Find Candidate Matches option represented by a shining star icon ✦ at the top of the candidate profile. If the star icon is not directly visible, click the three dots icon (More options) in the actions area to view additional options. Then select Find Candidate Matches from the dropdown menu. ​ ​ The system will analyze the candidate's profile and display a list of similar candidates ranked by match score. ​ Once matching is complete, you will see a list of up to 50 candidates with their match scores. You can search within AI Matching results using the search bar without manually scrolling through the candidate list. You can search using: Candidate Name Current Job Title City By default, AI analyses and compares candidate profiles based on skills, experience, education, location, language, job titles, and industry to identify the most relevant matches. Method 2: Launch Matching from a Job Profile 1. Go to the relevant Job in Recruit CRM and open the Candidates Pipeline tab for that job. 2. Identify the ideal candidate within the job’s candidate list and click on the three dots next to that candidate’s name. 3. Choose Find Matching Candidates from the menu to view AI-generated matches based on that candidate’s profile. ​ Once matching is complete, you will see a list of up to 50 candidates with their match scores. Understanding AI Match Analysis AI Matching provides detailed reasoning behind each candidate match, helping recruiters understand why a candidate is considered a good fit. For every matched candidate, AI-generated insights are available across: Function – Shows how closely the candidate’s role and responsibilities align with the requirement. Skills – Shows how well the candidate’s skills match the required skills. Level – Shows how closely the candidate’s experience and seniority match the role. Trajectory – Shows how the candidate’s career progression aligns with the expected growth path. Domain – Shows the relevance of the candidate’s industry and domain experience. Location – Shows how well the candidate’s location and work preferences match the requirements. Each section includes a score and explanation, helping you quickly evaluate candidate strengths and gaps. You can also assign a candidate to the job directly from the Match Analysis panel without leaving the AI Matching screen. You can refresh AI Matching results to generate an updated list based on the latest available candidate information. Refresh is useful when new candidates are added, profiles are updated, or additional information becomes available after the previous matching run. When refreshed, AI Matching re-evaluates the data and updates the results based on the latest match scores. The Refresh option can be used once every 5 minutes for the candidate. You can quickly review multiple matched candidates using: Candidate selection from the results list Previous and Next buttons available in the Match Analysis panel When a candidate is selected, their Match Analysis is displayed automatically. Click here to learn more about the actions that can be performed on Matched Candidates. Once you have identified promising matches, you can take the following actions directly from the matches list after selecting the specific candidates: Assign to a job Request Updated Profile : Ask candidates to update and submit their latest information and documents. Send emails: Reach out to matched candidates with personalized or template-based mails. Add Notes : Add important comments or feedback about candidates for your team to review. Update Field : Change specific candidate details, such as skills, source. Enroll in a Sequence: Add candidates to an automated series of follow-up emails and tasks. Pitch to contacts: Submit matched candidates to client contacts for consideration. Add to hotlists: Create or manage lists of top candidates for future reference. Export : Download selected candidate records and data for reporting or offline use. You can provide feedback on AI-generated matches directly from the Match Analysis panel. Available feedback options are: Strong Match Weak Match Feedback can be submitted once per candidate match and helps improve future AI Matching experiences. Please Note: AI Matching supports multiple languages. Match analysis is generated in the same language as the source content used for matching, such as the candidate profile details. Troubleshooting Problem: The Candidate Matching button is greyed out and cannot be clicked. Likely cause: A resume is not attached to the candidate profile. ​ ​ What to check: Verify whether a resume file is attached in the candidate’s default resume field. ​ ​ Resolution path: Upload the candidate’s resume file, as the AI matching score is calculated based on the attached resume. FAQs Who can use candidate-to-candidate AI matching in Recruit CRM? Any user with access to candidate profiles and jobs can use AI matching, but the number of visible matches depends on your plan. Business and Enterprise users see up to 50 matches; Pro users see up to two. Will refreshing always produce new matches? No. Refreshing re-runs the matching process using the latest data. If no better or additional matches are identified, the existing results remain unchanged. Why did a candidate receive a high score even if they do not match every requirement? AI Matching evaluates multiple factors together. A candidate may score highly because they strongly match several important areas, even if they do not perfectly match every requirement. The Match Analysis panel explains the reasoning behind the score. Conclusion Candidate-to-candidate AI matching in Recruit CRM helps you quickly find and act on lookalike candidates based on an ideal profile, using rich resume data to drive accurate match scores. Use it from both candidate profiles and job records to build better shortlists, rediscover strong talent in your database, and streamline your outreach and placement workflows. t: Use the native dialer to call from the system
s: Learn how to use the native dialer functionality to make calls from Recruit CRM but using your own calling system.
h: What this feature does & when to use it?
Before you begin:
Step-by-step instructions
Changing the default native dialer of your computer
Open the Candidate or Contact Profile in the Mobile App
Download the mobile app now!
Troubleshooting
FAQs
b: What this feature does & when to use it? Calling using the native dialer in Recruit CRM lets you start a call from a candidate or contact profile and automatically open your default calling application or phone dialer. You can use this when: You want to call candidates or contacts using your existing calling tools (Zoom, Skype, Teams, etc.). You prefer to use your computer’s or phone’s default dialer. Before you begin: Please note: Make sure your computer has a default calling application set (for example, Zoom, Skype, or Microsoft Teams). Ensure your browser is allowed to open external applications (check pop-up and protocol handling permissions). On mobile, confirm that the Recruit CRM mobile app is installed and you are logged in. Verify that candidate or contact records have valid phone numbers saved. Default calling behavior (which app opens) is controlled by your device or operating system, not by Recruit CRM. Step-by-step instructions 1. Open the Candidate or Contact Profile on the Web Within the candidate or contact profile, locate their phone number. Click on the Open Native Caller button displayed next to the phone number. 2. Confirm Opening the Native Calling Application After you click the Open Native Caller option, your browser will display a pop-up asking you to confirm opening the native calling application set as default in your computer settings (for example, Zoom.us, Skype, Teams, etc.). Click Open in the browser pop-up to proceed. 3. Place the Call in Your Default Calling System Once confirmed, you will be redirected out of Recruit CRM and taken to your computer’s default calling system. Complete and manage the call directly within that calling application. Changing the default native dialer of your computer Learn How to change the default native dialer on Mac? Learn How to change the default calling app on Windows and Android? Open the Candidate or Contact Profile in the Mobile App Open any candidate or contact profile in the Recruit CRM app on your phone and click on the phone button. In the candidate or contact profile on your phone, tap the Phone button, then tap the Open Native Dialer button at the bottom of your screen. Your phone will redirect you to its default calling window, where you can start calling your candidates or contacts using your device’s native dialer. Download the mobile app now! Download on iPhone Download on iPad Download on Android Troubleshooting Problem: The native caller does not open when I click the button. Likely cause: Browser is blocking the protocol or pop-up. What to check: Browser pop-up settings and protocol handler permissions (for example, for zoom.us , skype , or tel links). Resolution path: Allow the browser to open external apps and retry clicking Open Native Caller . Problem: The wrong calling app opens from the web. Likely cause: Incorrect default calling application set on your computer. What to check: System default app settings for calling or link handling. Resolution path: Change your system default calling app (for example, set Zoom or Skype as default) and then use Open Native Caller again. FAQs Can I choose a different calling app each time? Your browser and operating system will typically use the default calling application you have set. To change it, adjust your system or browser defaults. Is the internet required to use the native dialer? For VoIP tools like Zoom, Skype, or Teams, you need an internet connection. For your phone’s native dialer, you need normal mobile network coverage. Conclusion : Using the native dialer in Recruit CRM lets you start calls quickly from candidate and contact profiles while continuing to use your preferred calling tools on the web and mobile. t: Using Mentions to Notify Teammates in Recruit CRM
s: Mention your teammates on a note to give them an email notification with a link to that record.
h: What this feature does?
When to use this feature?
How to mention a teammate in Recruit CRM
Mention a teammate on a record
Troubleshooting
Problem: A mentioned teammate does not receive the email notification.
Problem: A tagged user cannot see the note in Recruit CRM after being mentioned.
Problem: A user on the account cannot mention teams.
b: What this feature does? Need to quickly loop in a teammate on a record? Use mentions to notify them instantly and avoid back-and-forth. The Mention feature in Recruit CRM lets you tag teammates or teams directly in notes on the records. When you mention someone, they receive an email notification that includes a direct link to the record where you added the note. When to use this feature? You can use this feature when: You want to quickly alert a teammate about an update on a candidate, company, contact, or job record. You need a direct link to a specific record included in an email notification. How to mention a teammate in Recruit CRM Mention a teammate on a record Open the relevant candidate, company, contact, or job record where you want to collaborate. ​ Go to the Notes section of the record. Type your note and enter the @ symbol to start a mention. ​ Select the teammate you want to mention from the available options. Click + Add Note to save the note with the mention attached. ​ The mentioned teammate will receive an email notification containing a link to the record. ​ The teammate can click the View Mention button in the email to open the specific record in Recruit CRM. Please note If you are on the Business plan or above , you can mention teams in notes by typing @ and selecting the relevant team. You can mention any team, even if you are not a member of that team. When you mention a teammate or team, Recruit CRM sends an email notification with a link to the record where the mention was added. If it is the recipient's first mention email, they may need to check their Spam/Junk folder and mark it as Not Spam to ensure future mention notifications reach their inbox. Recipients can reply directly to the mention email to start an email thread with the person who mentioned them, or click View Mention to open the relevant record in Recruit CRM. A mention does not change the tagged user's existing record permissions . The tagged user can view the note in Recruit CRM only if their role has View Everything access. If the tagged user does not have the required access, they may still receive the mention email but may not be able to view the note or record in Recruit CRM. Troubleshooting Problem: A mentioned teammate does not receive the email notification. Likely cause: The email was filtered into spam or junk. ​ What to check: Ask the teammate to look for the mention email in their spam or junk folder. ​ Resolution: The teammate should mark the mention email as not spam so future mention notifications appear directly in their inbox. Problem: A tagged user cannot see the note in Recruit CRM after being mentioned. Likely cause: Their role does not have “view everything” access. ​ What to check: Confirm the user’s role and its access level, specifically whether “view everything” access is enabled. ​ Resolution: An Account Owner should adjust the role to have “view everything” access if appropriate, so the tagged user can view the note. Problem: A user on the account cannot mention teams. Likely cause: The account is not on the business plan or above. ​ What to check: Verify the current plan and confirm whether it is the business plan or above. ​ Resolution: Upgrade to the business plan or above if team mentions are required. FAQs Q1: Where can I use mentions in Recruit CRM? You can use mentions in the notes section of any record such as candidate, company, contact, or job. Q2: What happens when I mention a teammate in a note? The mentioned teammate receives an email notification that includes a link to the specific record where the note with the mention was added. Q3: Can I mention teams as well as individual teammates? Yes. If you are on the business plan and above, you can mention teams in notes, and you can mention any team even if you do not belong to that team. Q4: How can a mentioned teammate respond to a mention email? They can reply directly to the email to start an email thread with the teammate who mentioned them, or click the “View Mention” button in the email to open the record in Recruit CRM. Q5: How do I make sure mention emails do not go to spam? The first time a teammate receives a mention email, they may need to mark it as not spam in their email client. After that, future mention notifications should appear in the inbox. Conclusion: Mentions in notes help your team collaborate faster in Recruit CRM by sending targeted email notifications that link directly to specific records, while respecting role-based visibility and plan-specific options. If you need further help using mentions for your workflow, contact your Recruit CRM support for additional guidance. Error Handler: If something fails within the Monitor block, then this step is triggered. b: With this automation, every new job created in Recruit CRM can be shared on LinkedIn. Apps that are required to be connected for the recipe: 1. Recruit CRM 2. LinkedIn 3. Google Drive 🔗 How to connect your Recruit CRM app in Workflow Automation 1. Navigate to Admin Settings >>> Workflow Automation & Integrations . 2. Click on the Connections tab under the 'Workflows' section and click on the 'Create' button >>> 'Connection'. 3. Use the search bar to search for the Recruit CRM app and connect it by selecting it and entering the API key . Once the app is successfully connected, you will be able to see a message as 'Connection Established'. 🔗 How to connect your LinkedIn account in Workflow Automation 1. Navigate to Admin Settings >>> Workflow Automation & Integrations . 2. Click on the Connections tab under the 'Workflows' section and click on the 'Create' button >>> 'Connection'. 3. Use the search bar to search for the Cognito Forms app and connect it by selecting it and signing in. 4. Allow the required permissions and click on Continue. Once the app is successfully connected, you will be able to see a message as 'Connection Established'. 🔗 How to connect your Google Drive account in Workflow Automation 1. Navigate to Admin Settings >>> Workflow Automation & Integrations . 2. Click on the Connections tab under the 'Workflows' section and click on the 'Create' button >>> 'Connection'. 3. Use the search bar to search for the Google Drive app and connect it by selecting it and then Sign in with Google. 4. Allow the required permissions and click on Continue. Once the app is successfully connected, you will be able to see a message as 'Connection Established'. 📋 Overview of each step in the Recipe for sharing new jobs on LinkedIn 1. Trigger: New Job Created in Recruit CRM: This is the starting point of the automation. It gets triggered whenever a new job is created within Recruit CRM. 2. Actions: Monitor step : It helps in monitoring the following actions for errors. This makes the automation more reliable. IF Condition: Checks whether the condition specified is satisfied, and : ​ If yes, it continues to the next step, which is to first initialize the image upload on LinkedIn using your company ID to prepare for posting. ​ Then it downloads the image file (e.g., job banner) from Google Drive to generate an Image URN and share the job post with the image on your LinkedIn company page. ​ If no, then no further action is taken. Error Handler: If something fails within the Monitor block, then this step is triggered. The Retry Logic ensures that if the errors match those specified (429, 500–504), it retries the monitored actions up to 3 times. If the error continues after 3 retries, or if the error doesn’t match the handled types, the automation stops. That's it! I hope this helps.
